suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Residential or Smart TV IP address issues DNS query for proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io, bright-sdk.com or connects to 3.33.193.183 or 15.197.193.114. High-fidelity indicator for proxy network enrollment.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Smart TV App Setup Wizard with Hidden Permission Nesting
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes obfuscation mechanism: consent 'buried in TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' Defense-evasion step is the *delivery method* for initial access—pipeline classified only T1071 (generic protocol), missing T1036.008 (match legitimate appearance) and UI-based social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV app setup wizard or EULA flow contains permission request (network proxy, VPN, raw network) that appears after initial 'Agree' prompt, uses visual de-emphasis (small text, low contrast), or requires non-standard navigation input (arrow-key combinations, remote button sequences) rather than direct touch/click confirmation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repo Compromise via Suspicious Commit Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories'—this is the core attack vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for GitHub compromise or commit-based malware injection, which is the delivery mechanism for supply-chain worms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub commit logs for structural anomalies: commits adding/modifying .github/workflows, package.json, or build manifests by new or inactive contributors; commits from newly-rotated SSH keys; commit payloads containing encoded or obfuscated scripts typical of worm propagation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Repository Coordinated Compromise Aggregation
suggestion.rationale: Exactly 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories compromised in coordinated attack—this is a distinctive scale signal. Pipeline produced no aggregation rule to detect when multiple repos in a single organization are compromised within a narrow time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when ≥5 repositories in the same GitHub organization exhibit simultaneous anomalies: unusual commits, new SSH key deployments, branch protection rule modifications, or secret rotation—all within 48 hours, indicating coordinated worm propagation.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm File Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names the threat 'Miasma Worm' but pipeline extracted zero file hashes, malware signatures, or behavioral indicators. This is the foundational IOC extraction failure—worm samples should be hashed and detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once Miasma samples are procured, generate hash-based detections for known worm binaries. Supplement with behavioral rules: recursive repo cloning from a single process, self-modification of build scripts, execution of unsigned binaries from .git directories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Poisoning via Build System Injection
suggestion.rationale: Worm targeting GitHub repos implies exploitation of CI/CD pipelines to poison downstream artifacts (packages, containers). Article describes compromise of 73 repos but pipeline generated no detection for build-system injection or artifact pollution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD job logs for: new workflow steps absent from source code (step injection), downloads of unsigned/untrusted binaries during build, execution of scripts from non-standard paths, build artifacts with modified metadata that don't match committed source.

suggestion.title: Recursive Repository Compromise Detection (Worm Propagation)
suggestion.rationale: A 'worm' by definition self-propagates. Article does not detail propagation mechanism but pipeline should have inferred that compromised repos may clone sibling repos and re-inject the worm. No lateral-movement or propagation detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repository clone-and-commit cycles: repository A performs unexpected git clone of repository B in the same organization, followed immediately by a commit push back to A or forward to a third repository. Flag recursive patterns (A→B→C, B→A) within <1 hour windows.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Repo Metadata Modification (Bypass of Code Review)
suggestion.rationale: Worms targeting GitHub often disable branch protections, bypass code review, or modify repository secrets. Article mentions widespread compromise but pipeline generated no detection for defensive-control circumvention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository setting changes: branch protection rules disabled, required code reviewers removed, webhooks added to external hosts, deploy keys created, or organization members removed—especially by users who have not performed these actions historically.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Mass Disable Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' after compromise. Pipeline missed detection of rapid/bulk repository deletion or disabling, a signature impact of repository takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Multiple repositories disabled or deleted within a short time window (< 1 hour) by a single actor or from a single source IP. Monitor GitHub GraphQL/REST API calls to `deleteRepository` or `updateRepository(archived=true)` operations. Alert on >5 repo state changes by non-admin accounts or unusual automation tokens.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions Action Workflow Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Azure Functions Action' as directly compromised. Pipeline missed GitHub Action file modifications (workflow YAML, JavaScript action entrypoint) or suspicious execution within the action namespace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Commits to `.github/workflows/*` or `action.yml` in the azure-functions-action repository not authored by maintainers, or workflow execution logs showing unexpected commands, environment variable exfiltration, or network calls to non-Microsoft domains. Track webhook events on this repository.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Injection via Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'AI Coding Agents' as the attack vehicle. Pipeline missed detection of injected commands or malicious code funneling through agent dependencies into AI model inference or code generation pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection of unexpected dependencies or code injected into package.json, requirements.txt, or pyproject.toml linked to AI agent libraries (e.g., LangChain, AutoGPT). Monitor for agent runtime execution of code not in the approved baseline. Alert on agent API calls to external command execution or script invocation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack implies compromised packages or dependencies. Pipeline missed IOCs for tampered package manifests, version downgrades, or pre-release publication of legitimate packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories (npm, PyPI, NuGet) for unexpected version releases, yanked/re-published versions, or metadata changes (author, maintainer, signed signatures removed) on packages known to be in the Microsoft ecosystem or AI agent dependencies. Alert on version rollbacks or non-semantic versioning jumps.

suggestion.title: Miasma Malware Artifact Detection in Repository Contents
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Miasma Worm' as the threat. Pipeline failed to extract malware signatures, hashes, code patterns, or behavioral indicators associated with this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan repository commit history for known Miasma worm signatures (if available from threat intel feeds), obfuscated code patterns, or embedded binary payloads. Monitor for repository commits containing file hashes or C2 domains associated with Miasma. Cross-reference with YARA rules or malware samples from incident response reports.

suggestion.title: Automated Agent Execution of Injected Payloads
suggestion.rationale: AI coding agents are the stated target. Pipeline missed detection of agent-initiated code execution, file writes, or privilege escalation triggered by crafted prompts or compromised action dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AI agent processes spawning unusual child processes (bash, PowerShell, curl, git) or writing files to unexpected directories. Monitor for agent API calls that invoke code execution without user authorization. Alert on agent environment variable exfiltration or outbound connections from agent processes to non-whitelisted domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' — installation of the malicious package is the primary attack surface. Zero detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip or Python package manager execution with arguments containing 'durabletask' package name. Escalate on installation of specific compromised versions. Correlate with environment expectations (should not appear in prod without business justification).

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Compromised Package Import
suggestion.rationale: Article signals 'compromised' package status implying malicious payload. No detection framework for execution phase following package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning, code injection, or network I/O initiated by Python interpreter after durabletask import. Baseline legitimate library behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Package Integrity Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain detections should include pre-execution verification checks. No hash, signature, or checksum validation detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed pip signature verification, package hash mismatches, checksum validation errors, or file metadata inconsistencies during durabletask installation.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Organizations using durabletask as a transitive (indirect) dependency face risk without explicit package listing. Pipeline missed dependency-chain analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query application manifests (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.py) to identify where durabletask is a transitive dependency. Flag installations of parent packages that pull compromised versions automatically.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise C2 and Data Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises enable downstream attack phases. Article's 'compromised' status implies malicious payload, but post-exploitation detections absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious outbound connections from hosts with confirmed durabletask installation. Flag C2 beaconing patterns, data exfiltration indicators, and deviations from baseline communication profiles.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent file modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability affects 'cgroups v1 release_agent feature'—this is the exploitation vector. Modification of release_agent files is abnormal and indicative of privilege-escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/[pid]/cgroup. Flag writes from unprivileged users (UID > 1000). Cross-reference with process spawning to identify payload execution.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged user namespace + cgroup operation sequence
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 exploitation requires unprivileged user namespace creation (unshare/clone) followed by cgroup manipulation. The article states attackers 'leverage' this flaw from unprivileged context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) or clone(CLONE_NEWUSER) syscalls from non-root users with subsequent cgroup file operations within 5 seconds. High-confidence indicator of CVE-2022-0492 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected code execution via cgroup release_agent trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks'—release_agent executes commands when cgroups are released. Detection must identify process spawning with cgroup-related ancestry or event hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned with parent=release_agent handler or process creation events triggered by cgroup subsystem events. Flag if parent process does not exist on disk (signature of cgroup-triggered execution).

suggestion.title: Access to unprivileged_userns_clone or kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone sysctls
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 exploitation pathway often begins by checking or modifying kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone setting. Article's mention of 'unprivileged' attackers implies this reconnaissance step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads/writes to /proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone from non-root users, especially followed by unshare() syscalls. Low false-positive risk in production systems.

suggestion.title: Bulk Password Reset Requests to Instagram Web Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow.' Pre-June-6 exploitation of this publicly documented vulnerability should be detectable via unusual request volume and patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag spikes in POST requests to /accounts/password/reset/ endpoints pre-June-6-2026 from non-standard ASNs or bot-like user-agents. Correlate with account-access anomalies 24-48 hours post-request.

suggestion.title: Email Address Enumeration via Exposed Password Reset Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed unredacted email addresses associated with user accounts.' Attackers enumerate Instagram user emails by probing the flaw, enabling downstream credential-stuffing attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential password-reset requests with username/email variations returning 200-response patterns that leak valid email addresses. Threshold >100 reqs/minute from single source.

suggestion.title: Phone Number Disclosure via Account Recovery Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed...phone numbers associated with user accounts.' Password reset endpoint returned obfuscated recovery phone numbers; mass scraping possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for systematic enumeration of /accounts/password/reset/ responses revealing partial phone format (e.g., +1-***-***-1234). Alert on >50 unique account enum attempts per hour.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Using Exposed Instagram Email-Phone Pairs
suggestion.rationale: Article: exposed 'email addresses and phone numbers' create a correlated dataset for targeted credential abuse. Post-June-6, monitor for abuse of the leaked contact pairs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-June-6: detect login failures using known-breached credential pairs filtered to emails/phones disclosed by the Instagram flaw. Correlate with external breach databases (Have I Been Pwned).

suggestion.title: Account Takeover of High-Profile Instagram Users Post-Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'high-profile individuals such as Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and model Georgina Rodriguez' had contact info exposed. These named targets will face intensive credential-recovery and ATO attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >2 failed login/recovery attempts within 1 hour on verified high-profile accounts post-June-6. Flag any successful recovery SMS/email confirmation from out-of-region IPs.

suggestion.title: Malformed Media File Execution in FFmpeg
suggestion.rationale: Article: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — zero-days in multimedia libraries manifest as remote code execution when processing attacker-controlled files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FFmpeg process execution with suspicious file arguments (corrupted headers, unusual magic bytes, oversized metadata). Correlate with process crashes, abnormal memory allocation, or unexpected child processes. Baseline FFmpeg behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Drive-by Download Exploitation via Malicious Media
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' — browser rendering of crafted media files is a canonical initial-access vector for 0-day chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of media files (.mp4, .mov, .mkv, .webm, .webp) from untrusted sources (emails, malicious sites). Correlate with browser crashes, abnormal memory access, or post-compromise indicators within 1 hour of download.

suggestion.title: Phishing with FFmpeg-Exploiting Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — high-volume zero-day availability incentivizes email-based weaponization of crafted media files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email attachments with video/image MIME types sent to users with outdated FFmpeg or Chrome (inventory correlation). Detect post-delivery execution of file decompression, media rendering, or codec libraries.

suggestion.title: Memory Corruption Exploitation (Heap/Stack/Use-After-Free)
suggestion.rationale: Article context: 21 + 429 vulnerability count suggests widespread memory-safety bugs in multimedia/browser parsers—canonical ROP, heap spray, ASLR bypass indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg/Chrome memory for ROP gadget sequences, heap spray patterns, or stack pivot instructions. Correlate with control-flow guard (CFG) violations, DEP exceptions, or out-of-bounds memory access. Analyze crash dumps for shellcode markers.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Version Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article: '429 Chrome Patches' and FFmpeg zero-days — detection must prioritize identifying unpatched instances across enterprise before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain real-time inventory of Chrome and FFmpeg versions. Flag systems running versions released before the zero-day disclosure window. Correlate version age with lateral-movement attempts or exploit-kit C2 beaconing to prioritize urgent patching.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Fuzzing & Crash-Database Uploads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI Agent Uncovers' zero-days — implies automated fuzzing reconnaissance and crash reporting as part of threat-actor discovery arsenal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect local fuzzing harnesses (parallel FFmpeg/Chrome invocations, rapid temp file creation, memory dumps). Alert on uploads to crash aggregators (OSS-Fuzz, ClusterFuzz, vendor bug-trackers). Baseline multimedia codec behavior and flag reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited' vulnerability; no detection use case provided despite high severity and KEV status indicating adversary activity in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U listening ports for abnormal traffic patterns: sudden spike in connection count, rapid request rate from single or distributed sources, and simultaneous connection failures. Correlate with service CPU/memory exhaustion in performance logs.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Port Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires discovery of running Serv-U instances; no reconnaissance detection despite active-threat context of article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential connection attempts to Serv-U default service ports (22, 3389, or vendor-specific), failed connection attempts from single source across port range, or service fingerprinting queries.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Availability Collapse
suggestion.rationale: DoS attack goal is service unavailability; no operational detection for availability degradation, error spikes, or dropped connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained elevation in Serv-U service error rates, connection rejections, or timeout events. Detect sudden drops in successful transaction count or service uptime metrics correlated with inbound traffic surge.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable SolarWinds Serv-U Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes version-specific DoS flaw; pipeline missed asset discovery logic to identify vulnerable installations for remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Serv-U process/service startup with executable path, version string, or build number in process telemetry. Match against CISA KEV-listed vulnerable version range to identify unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states flaw is 'actively exploited' — pipeline must detect HTTP/HTTPS POST/GET attempts to Cisco SD-WAN Manager vulnerable endpoints (typically /api/v1/* or /admin/* paths with malformed input triggering the CVE condition)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager (port 443 typical) with suspicious URI patterns, error codes 500/502, or POST payloads containing template injection/serialization gadgets. Track response times and error rates as exploitation attempts often trigger exceptions.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Post-Compromise Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Once inside manager via CVE-2026-20245, attacker gains control of policy distribution — article implies active exploitation suggests post-compromise discovery of connected branch sites and policy configuration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated API queries from compromised manager to enumerate connected WAN endpoints, policy templates, or credential stores. Look for unusual account activity (system service accounts reading config files, querying AD/LDAP for device inventory).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SD-WAN Policy Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes manager compromise — attacker can inject malicious routing policies or QoS rules into all connected branch devices, enabling lateral movement across the SD-WAN fabric
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual policy distribution events (config push to all devices simultaneously, policies targeting internal subnets instead of WAN traffic, policy timestamps misaligned with admin activity). Flag rapid policy churn on branch devices.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SD-WAN Manager Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Manager compromise likely grants access to stored credentials for managed WAN devices, routers, and firewall appliances — article's 'no patch available' window invites full credential harvest
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor manager processes for access to credential storage (config files, vaults, database queries). Look for large data transfers from manager to external IPs shortly after exploitation indicators. Track OS process dumps or memory extraction tools.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation suggests attacker maintains persistence — manager can be weaponized as a C2 node issuing commands to all branch sites or exfiltrating telemetry
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections from manager to non-Cisco domains, periodic callbacks with fixed intervals, or DNS queries for dynamic C2 infrastructure. Baseline manager's normal outbound traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SD-WAN Manager Tunnel Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Manager controls encrypted WAN tunnels — compromised manager can redirect traffic destined for branches to attacker infrastructure, enabling large-scale data exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor manager for unusual tunnel configuration changes (adding attacker-controlled endpoints, disabling encryption on sensitive routes). Look for asymmetric traffic patterns (large inbound to manager, large outbound to non-business destinations).

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation with 'diksimarina' Username
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers create rogue admin account named 'diksimarina': 'The attacker submits a value... followed by a PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account with the username 'diksimarina'.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation logs and database records for accounts with username 'diksimarina' or variants. Alert on admin-level user creation without prior administrative action or API call. Check wp_usermeta for recent additions of users with administrator role from unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Form Submission to Complex Calculation Feature with Quote Injection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described: attacker 'submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement.' Detect malicious payload patterns in form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Everest Forms Complex Calculation endpoint (vulnerable plugin ≤1.9.12). Flag form submissions containing single quote followed by PHP keywords (wp_, eval, etc.). Look for payloads starting with single quote in calculation field parameters.

suggestion.title: wp_insert_user() Execution from Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation method explicitly states: 'the injected PHP code is executed, and the malicious administrator account is created' via wp_insert_user(). Log execution of WordPress user-creation functions from non-admin code paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress function call logs for wp_insert_user() invocations originating from plugin code (non-core paths). Alert on user creation calls from form processing, calculation, or eval contexts. Correlate with HTTP requests to form endpoints.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation from Attacker IP Ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies primary attack sources: '202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26, and recommends defenders block them.' Correlate admin account creation timing with these sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track requests to Everest Forms endpoints from IP addresses 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26. Alert when these IPs trigger Complex Calculation form submissions or when admin account creation events occur within 60 seconds of requests from these sources.

suggestion.title: PHP eval() Invocation from Plugin with User-Controlled Input
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'the resulting code using PHP's 'eval()' function. Although user input is passed through a 'sanitize_text_field()' function, which does not escape single quotes.' Detect eval() execution with unsanitized input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP execution logs and application instrumentation for eval() calls originating from Everest Forms plugin context. Alert on eval() with variables containing form input data. Cross-reference with requests containing special characters (quotes, semicolons) in calculation parameters.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Installation on Smart TV Outside Official Store
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs Into...' — indicates sideloaded or unofficial distribution. No detection exists for out-of-band app installation on tvOS/Android TV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installation events on Android TV devices or app installations on tvOS outside the official app store. Track installation sources and validate against known-good deployment vectors. Smart TV app stores have limited legitimate sideload scenarios.

suggestion.title: High-Volume HTTP Requests from Smart TV to Non-Content Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states apps are 'Web-Scraping Proxies' — indicates sustained, structured outbound HTTP traffic. Title mentions scraping content for AI, implying bulk data extraction rather than user-initiated browsing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TVs initiating high request counts (>500/hour) to non-CDN, non-media domains typical of web scraping. Look for GET-heavy patterns, low response size variance, and IP geolocation mismatches (TV in EU requesting from US-only services at bot-like regularity).

suggestion.title: Background Service Execution in Foreground-Only Free Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article implies apps run silently as 'proxies' without user awareness — detection gap for persistent background execution in apps that declare no background-service permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Android TV, monitor for apps spawning service processes or threads without matching manifest permissions. On tvOS, detect apps with scheduled/recurring background tasks after installation. Correlate with app not actively in foreground.

suggestion.title: Outbound SOCKS Proxy or HTTP Tunnel Traffic from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly labels TVs as 'Proxies for AI' — attackers will tunnel traffic through compromised TVs to obfuscate scraping origin. No detection for proxy-protocol signatures originating from TV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound SOCKS5/HTTP CONNECT tunneling from TV to external relays. Look for repeated 2-way tunneling on high port ranges, bidirectional data symmetry, and geo-mismatch between TV location and tunnel destination.

suggestion.title: App-to-C2 Beaconing from Smart TV After Silent Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers need command channel to activate scraping and exfiltrate results. Article does not name C2 domains, but detection should fire on behavioral anomalies (regular check-ins to attacker infrastructure).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic DNS queries or HTTP POST requests from TV to non-media, non-ISP domains in predictable intervals (every 5–60 minutes). Correlate with recent app installations and elevated outbound data volume.

suggestion.title: Bulk Web Content Staging in TV Local Storage After App Installation
suggestion.rationale: Scraped content must be staged locally before exfil. Article does not detail storage paths, but detection should flag abnormal local-disk growth in app sandboxes on resource-constrained TV devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid growth of files in app-writable directories (/data/data/<app>/cache, /sdcard/Android/data, or equivalent tvOS paths) following free-app installation. Baseline: TV apps typically use <100 MB; scraper caches will reach GBs within days.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to Bright Data proxy domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 11 IOCs tied to Bright Data infrastructure used for device enrollment: 'proxyjs.brdtnet.com', 'proxyjs.luminatinet.com', 'clientsdk.bright-sdk.com', etc. Devices tunneling traffic through these endpoints are the primary compromise signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries to bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io and network connections to 3.33.193.183 or 15.197.193.114 originating from smart TV devices. Establish baseline for expected endpoints; flag deviations. Proxy protocol signatures in TLS/SSL certs confirm enrollment.

suggestion.title: Free smart TV app installation followed by proxy C2 traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku...have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices.' Initial access is via trojanized app on official app store; execution and C2 follow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate free app installation events on smart TV platforms with subsequent connections to Bright Data infrastructure within minutes. Identify app package names and versions known to embed proxy logic. Flag installation → C2 connection chain as compromise.

suggestion.title: Anomalous sustained outbound bandwidth and connection count on smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes web-scraping activity ('scrape web data for AI training') sustained in background. Device will exhibit elevated egress volume and persistent outbound state inconsistent with normal TV usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline per-device egress bandwidth and established connection count over typical viewing patterns. Alert when smart TV sustains outbound traffic > 2σ above baseline, especially to non-CDN, non-user-facing IP space. Correlate timing with app execution and C2 domains.

suggestion.title: TV app permissions granted outside visible user interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article: consent dialog 'buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' Users unaware permissions are being requested and granted. Permission grants occur during non-interactive execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network/proxy permission grants to apps not in active foreground during grant. Flag permission dialogs rendered off-screen or in non-standard navigation flow. Cross-check app execution state and user input telemetry at time of permission.

suggestion.title: Bright Data residential proxy service activity from consumer networks
suggestion.rationale: Bright Data (luminati.io, brdtnet.com) is commercial proxy provider. Use of infrastructure by consumer smart TV represents resource hijacking and abuse from known malicious proxy provider.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from non-enterprise, consumer, or residential device types to bright-sdk.com, luminati.io, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com. Monitor for protocol patterns consistent with Bright Data SDK traffic (HTTP CONNECT tunneling, proxy-specific user-agents). Recommend network-layer block rules.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Compromise - Suspicious Commit Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories'—worm propagation and repo compromise imply unusual commit patterns, branch creation, or code push activity that should be flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual commit frequency, branch creation velocity, or code modifications in high-value Microsoft GitHub repositories. Flag commits from new or anomalous user accounts, especially those pushing binary or obfuscated payloads. Correlate with Microsoft Defender telemetry for unsigned or untrusted code execution.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation in Supply-Chain Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly identifies 'Miasma Worm'—worms self-replicate; expect lateral movement across forked repos, downstream consumers, or linked projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for evidence of rapid repo cloning, forking, or automated code distribution from affected Microsoft repositories to downstream dependencies or developer machines. Monitor for file write patterns consistent with worm replication (iterating directory trees, creating copies with minor variations).

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attacker successfully pushed malicious code to 73 repos; requires credential compromise or token theft against Microsoft/GitHub admin accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub PAT or OAuth token misuse: unusual IP ranges, off-hours logins, bulk repo modifications, or cross-organizational access patterns. Correlate failed GitHub auth attempts preceding successful commits. Cross-reference with Entra ID sign-in risk signals.

suggestion.title: Downstream Consumer Infection Vector Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain worm targeting 73 Microsoft repos implies secondary infections of consumers who depend on or sync these repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track clone/pull operations of the 73 affected repos across internal networks and third-party customers. Correlate repo sync operations with suspicious process execution (unsigned binaries, script interpreters launching unexpected commands, C2 callbacks). Alert on known Miasma hash signatures.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash & Artifact Detection - Miasma Family
suggestion.rationale: No hash IOCs provided despite 'Miasma Worm' naming; pipeline should surface sample hashes, file paths, registry keys, or command patterns associated with Miasma.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create hash-based detections for known Miasma samples and alert on execution from unexpected locations (temp, user profile, System32 disguises). Flag process launches with Miasma-associated command-line arguments or parent-child process chains (e.g., git.exe spawning cmd.exe with encoded payloads).

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Supply Chain Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Azure Functions Action and 72 other repositories disabled after supply chain attack targeting AI Coding Agents'—pipeline extracted zero indicators for detecting malicious code injection into GitHub Actions. Supply chain compromise is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to popular GitHub Actions, especially those named after cloud platforms (Azure Functions Action). Flag commits that introduce code with suspicious patterns (credential exfiltration, code execution, repo manipulation) into action YAMLs or entry scripts. Baseline action contributors and flag new or dormant accounts committing to actions with >1000 users.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Disablement Event Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '72 Other Repositories Disabled'—indicates coordinated impact phase. Pipeline failed to map this to detection logic for mass admin actions or cascading failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cluster of repository disable/archive events within short timeframe (e.g., >10 repos disabled in <1 hour) especially if triggered by single compromised action or service account. Correlate with concurrent failed Actions runs or unusual API patterns from previously-trusted accounts.

suggestion.title: Malware Signature - Miasma Worm Distribution via Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article names the threat 'Miasma Worm'—pipeline produced empty IOCs. At minimum, worm name, known distribution hashes, or command patterns from public writeups should be catalogued.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Develop signature for Miasma worm artifacts: known code patterns, obfuscation markers, or command sequences observed in compromised Actions workflows. Monitor for Actions jobs that execute unsigned/unverified binaries or contact known malware C2 domains identified in threat intel.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Privilege Escalation via Compromised Action
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'targeting AI Coding Agents'—suggests elevated context or credentials flowing through Actions. Pipeline missed detection for agents receiving elevated GitHub tokens or API credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Actions workflows triggered by or targeting AI agents (check job names/env vars for agent identifiers) that request elevated scopes, read GITHUB_TOKEN secrets, or export credentials to environment. Detect exfiltration of secrets to external endpoints during agent execution.

suggestion.title: Unusual GitHub Actions Dependency Pull Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often inject malicious dependencies. Article hints at infrastructure compromise but pipeline extracted no detection logic for suspicious package/dependency downloads during action runs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Actions workflows for unexpected or unsigned package downloads from PyPI, npm, or private registries during runs. Flag jobs that pull dependencies with names similar to legitimate libraries (typosquatting) or from newly-registered accounts.

suggestion.title: Batch Repository Configuration Change by Compromised Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Disabling 72 repositories implies bulk actions—likely via compromised automation account or token. Article doesn't specify mechanism but pipeline should detect patterns of mass config changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single API caller or service account making batch repository configuration changes (disable, visibility change, settings modification) in short timeframe. Correlate with unusual IP addresses, geolocation changes, or timing inconsistent with normal admin schedules.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates durabletask package was compromised on PyPI—a supply chain attack vector. Detection should flag installation of packages from PyPI with unusual hashes, unexpected versions, or installation on systems that don't match organizational baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip install commands executed against PyPI repositories for 'durabletask' package; correlate version numbers against known-good baseline; alert on installation of versions outside organization's pinned/approved range. Cross-check against threat intel feeds for known-malicious package versions and hashes.

suggestion.title: Execution of Code from Compromised PyPI Package (durabletask)
suggestion.rationale: Once installed, the compromised durabletask package would execute malicious code on import/execution. Detection should identify unusual child processes, network connections, or file writes originating from Python interpreters after durabletask import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python interpreter (python.exe, python3) for unusual child process spawning, unexpected network connections, or file modifications to sensitive paths following durabletask package import or during application startup. Baseline normal behavior of applications that legitimately depend on durabletask.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Compromised Dependency in Application Startup
suggestion.rationale: Malicious durabletask package would execute each time an application imports it—creating a form of persistence. Detection should identify applications that consistently load the malicious package at startup or during scheduled execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated execution of Python-based applications that import durabletask; track module load events for the durabletask package; correlate with scheduled tasks or service startups that trigger application initialization. Alert on unexpected module versions or unsigned modules loaded by trusted applications.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Python Process (Post-Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Compromised PyPI packages typically establish outbound command-and-control after code execution. Detection should identify network traffic from Python interpreters to known-malicious domains or unusual external endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections initiated by python.exe/python3 processes; flag connections to non-standard ports, known C2 domains (via threat intel), or geographically anomalous destinations. Correlate DNS queries from Python processes; alert on queries to newly-registered domains or known malicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft or Data Exfiltration via Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises often steal credentials or exfiltrate data. Detection should identify unusual file access patterns, registry queries for credentials, or large data transfers originating from Python processes running the compromised package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes for queries to credential storage locations (HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows Credential Manager, .ssh directories, environment variable reads); flag access to sensitive files (secrets, .env, config files); correlate with unusual outbound data transfers or archive/compression operations.

suggestion.title: Organizational Inventory of durabletask Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Organizations need to rapidly identify which applications/services depend on durabletask to assess exposure. Detection should catalog package dependencies and alert on vulnerable versions across the environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan application source code, dependency manifests (requirements.txt, setup.py, Pipfile), and runtime package lists (pip freeze) to enumerate all instances of durabletask; correlate versions against advisory; prioritize remediation based on exposure (public-facing apps vs. internal tools) and network trust zones.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent File Write from Unprivileged Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' CVE-2022-0492 is exploited by writing to /proc/*/cgroup and release_agent files; this is the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write syscalls to /sys/fs/cgroup/**/release_agent or successful opens with O_WRONLY flag from non-root processes. Correlate with process execution in container/unprivileged context. Baseline: release_agent writes should only come from privileged daemons (systemd, container runtime).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Cgroups Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article describes improper authentication allowing attackers unspecified actions; CVE-2022-0492 impact is privilege escalation. No privilege escalation technique (T1548, T1068) was mapped despite this being the vulnerability's purpose.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawning children with elevated UID (non-root → root), new capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE), or cgroup namespace transitions. Correlate with earlier cgroup controller access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Cgroup Hierarchy Traversal from Container
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of cgroups v1 release_agent typically involves escaping container isolation by accessing parent cgroup hierarchies (/../../../ patterns). Article context implies containerized or isolated execution environments are vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container/process logs for reads/writes to parent cgroup paths (e.g., /../../) or attempts to access host cgroup namespaces from container contexts. Detect attempts to list or modify cgroup.procs across hierarchy boundaries.

suggestion.title: Kernel Oops/Warning Correlated with Cgroups Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts of CVE-2022-0492 may leave footprints in kernel logs before or after successful escalation. No kernel-level detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate kernel oops, BUG_ON, or WARNING messages in kern.log with preceding cgroup-related syscalls (open, write, release_agent access). Kernel panic immediately after cgroup release_agent write suggests failed exploitation or system instability.

suggestion.title: Known CVE-2022-0492 PoC Tool Execution Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'being actively leveraged in real-world attacks.' Threat actors are using exploitation tools; no scanning or tool-usage detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of known CVE-2022-0492 PoC patterns (e.g., cgroup_escape, CVE-2022-0492-exploit scripts, cgroupfs-related memory mapping/mmap calls). Flag suspicious Python/Bash scripts that write to /sys/fs/cgroup/ or /proc/*/cgroup in sequences matching documented exploits.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Controller State Change Without Admin Authorization
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may modify cgroup controllers (freezer, memory, devices, cpu) to escape constraints. Article's 'improper authentication' category suggests auth/access control bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to cgroup controller files (cgroup.procs, memory.limit_in_bytes, freezer.state) from non-privileged users. Alert if unprivileged process writes to tasks file or moves itself into a new cgroup under parent hierarchy.

suggestion.title: Instagram Password Reset Exploitation - Bulk PII Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' that 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers.' Detection should cover attempts to extract multiple records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Instagram password reset endpoint for requests returning high volumes of PII (email/phone combinations). Baseline normal reset frequency per user; flag IPs/accounts making bulk resets in short time windows or across unrelated accounts.

suggestion.title: Instagram Password Reset Abuse - Credential Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Password reset mechanism is a credential access vector. Article demonstrates flaw exposes credential-tied PII; post-fix, monitor for exploitation attempts against formerly-vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate password reset requests with subsequent authentication events. Flag patterns where resets are followed by account property changes (recovery email update, 2FA disablement) or logins from new IPs within 15 min of reset request.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Targeting High-Profile Instagram Users
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exposure of 'high-profile individuals such as Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and model Georgina Rodriguez.' Collected email/phone data increases phishing risk targeting these individuals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exposed email/phone lists from incident with inbound phishing campaigns. Flag emails/SMS to known-exposed addresses referencing Instagram, account recovery, or security verification within days of disclosure.

suggestion.title: Credential Validation Against Exposed Instagram Contacts
suggestion.rationale: Exposed emails and phone numbers enable downstream credential stuffing. Monitor authentication systems for attempts using leaked Instagram account identifiers post-incident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline failed login attempts against Instagram and cross-platform services post-incident. Flag sharp increase in failures for exposed email/phone combinations, especially from non-residential IPs or impossible-travel patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect FFmpeg exploitation via crafted video files
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — clear execution path via video processing is missing from pipeline output. No UC created for monitoring video file handling anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg process crashes, memory violations, or spawning child processes (indicator of code injection) when processing video files from untrusted sources. Correlate with suspicious file access patterns (temp dirs, system dirs) that indicate post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Monitor Chrome zero-day exploitation attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' — no detection UC for Chrome-specific exploitation despite high vulnerability surface area and widespread deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome process crashes, sandbox escapes (chrome.exe spawning unexpected child processes with SYSTEM/ADMIN privileges), or unusual memory allocation patterns. Correlate with recent updates to identify lag between patch release and exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Track vulnerability disclosure and patch deployment velocity
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes large-scale disclosure ('21 Zero-Days', '429 Bugs') — pipeline missed detection UC for organizational patch readiness and exposure tracking during high-velocity disclosure cycles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alerts for unpatched FFmpeg/Chrome instances post-disclosure. Track time-to-patch metrics and identify systems remaining vulnerable >72h after patch availability. Cross-reference with network telemetry for suspicious inbound connections to vulnerable hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect proof-of-concept code execution and staged payloads
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability research releases often trigger immediate POC development — pipeline omitted UC for detecting downloaded exploit code, malicious samples, or staged payload delivery targeting these vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of POC exploits (GitHub/Pastebin repos mentioning CVE + FFmpeg/Chrome), suspicious document attachments embedding video payloads, or lateral tool movement. Correlate file names/hashes with known exploit tracking databases.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Actively Exploited... DoS Flaw' with KEV catalog status. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for attempts to trigger the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized requests to Serv-U service endpoints (default ports 22, 135, 445, 3389, or configured alt ports). Flag rapid connection attempts, fuzzing patterns, or requests with abnormal header counts/sizes targeting Serv-U process or listening sockets.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Availability Disruption
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'DoS Flaw' as the attack vector. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection for service unavailability post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Serv-U process crashes, restarts, or unresponsive socket listeners post-request surge. Correlate connection count spikes, memory exhaustion, or CPU saturation on Serv-U host with client-side connection timeouts.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Traffic to Serv-U Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: DoS exploits typically manifest as traffic anomalies. Article states active exploitation but pipeline generated no network-based detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical connection patterns to Serv-U service ports. Alert on sustained connection count > 2 sigma, packet-per-connection ratio anomalies, or connections from unexpected geographies. Flag if source IPs match known attack infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-XXXX Serv-U Vulnerability Scanner Activity
suggestion.rationale: KEV catalog implies active weaponization; pipeline should have extracted CVE ID and signature for reconnaissance/PoC tool activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nessus, Qualys, or automated exploit framework requests matching the Serv-U vulnerability signature. Detect version-enumeration attempts via banner grabbing or HTTP fingerprinting against Serv-U endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Flaw Actively Exploited'. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite explicit mention of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20245 exploit signatures (likely input validation bypass or RCE gadget chains). Alert on unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or network egress from manager instances post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited' — absence of defensive action suggests attackers may maintain access or establish persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful CVE-2026-20245 exploitation attempts with anomalous outbound connections from affected SD-WAN Manager instances to external C2 infrastructure. Flag long-lived connections to rare or newly-seen destinations in threat-intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Credential Theft or Configuration Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation of management plane vulnerability typically preceded by information discovery and credential access. No use cases generated despite 'actively exploited' severity suggesting ongoing post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for enumeration of local user accounts, queries to Active Directory or LDAP post-exploitation, and attempts to read sensitive config files (/etc/shadow equivalents, database credentials). Detect bulk file reads targeting backup or config directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Injection in Form Field Submission
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement' and uses '// comment marker' to bypass remaining code. This injection pattern is directly observable in form POST data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Everest Forms Complex Calculation endpoints for payloads containing leading single-quote followed by PHP function names (wp_insert_user, strlen, substr, etc.) and comment sequences (//, #). Correlation with IPs 202.56.2[.]126 or 209.146.60.26 is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: eval() Execution with User-Controlled Form Input
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'executes the resulting code using PHP's eval() function' where the code is constructed from user form fields. This is the core execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on eval() calls in PHP where arguments contain unescaped user-supplied form field values from Everest Forms. Correlate eval() warnings/execution with preceding POST to form submission endpoint and check for single-quote escape patterns.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation via wp_insert_user() Outside Admin UI
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injected PHP code is executed, and the malicious administrator account is created' via direct 'wp_insert_user() call to create a new administrator account with the username diksimarina'. This is programmatic account creation, not admin-panel-driven.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on wp_insert_user() calls or WordPress user_login='diksimarina' table inserts combined with user_role containing 'administrator' that originate from non-admin HTTP requests. Absence of admin UI audit logs for user creation is strong signal.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the vulnerability is 'without authentication to execute arbitrary code' and can result in admin account creation via form submission. This is unauthenticated persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate new administrator user creation in WordPress logs with absence of: (1) login events from that username, (2) password reset notifications, (3) user creation from /wp-admin/user-new.php. New admin accounts with suspicious usernames appearing within seconds of form submissions are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Complex Calculation Feature Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack vector: 'vulnerability is in the plugin's Complex Calculation feature, which accepts values submitted through form fields.' This specific feature in versions ≤1.9.12 is the only attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on POST requests to Everest Forms Complex Calculation endpoints (check plugin code for calc feature endpoints) where payload contains single-quote, PHP keywords, and/or comment syntax. Validate Everest Forms version is ≤1.9.12 to confirm exploitability. Alert on volume > 5 attempts/day.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Source IP Blocking - Known Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article provides two source IPs: '202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26' with 'exploitation started on April 13, with the firewall blocking over 29,300 attempts.' These are campaign-specific, validated indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement network-level blocks and alert on any inbound traffic from 202.56.2[.]126 or 209.146.60.26 to WordPress instances running Everest Forms. Alert even on blocked/WAF-rejected requests to validate protection is working. Correlation with Everest Forms error logs confirms exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Installation of Unsigned or Sideloaded Applications on Smart TV Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article title signals 'free apps' as the attack vector. Phrase: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs Into...' indicates initial access via application installation outside official channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package installation events from non-official app stores or sideloading mechanisms on smart TV devices. Monitor for installation of applications with suspicious metadata (mismatched signatures, unsigned binaries, or apps requesting excessive network permissions).

suggestion.title: Detect High-Volume Outbound HTTPS Connections from Smart TV Devices to Unclassified Domains
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: devices become 'web-scraping proxies.' Article directly describes scraping activity that must egress data. Phrase: 'web-scraping proxies for AI' indicates bulk outbound requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for TV device egress. Alert when a TV makes >500 unique HTTPS connections per hour to domains not in whitelist, or when outbound request rate from a TV device exceeds 100 req/min. Correlate with User-Agent strings indicative of headless/automated clients.

suggestion.title: Detect Unusual Data Exfiltration Volume from TV Devices to External C2
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires bidirectional communication and large data transfers to transmit scraped web content. Phrase: 'turning Smart TVs into...proxies' implies data movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor total egress bytes per TV device. Alert when a TV device transmits >1GB per day to a single external endpoint, or when egress volume exceeds 10x baseline. Flag connections to known proxy or anonymization infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Permission Escalation or Network Capability Requests in Smart TV Apps
suggestion.rationale: Malicious apps must request permissions to access network and storage. Attack requires app to bypass sandboxing and access full network stack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on app manifest permission requests for unrestricted network access, storage access, or system service invocation on TV devices. Correlate with app signing certificates that are self-signed or from untrusted CAs.

suggestion.title: Detect Web Scraping Behavioral Patterns (Rapid Page Fetches, User-Agent Spoofing)
suggestion.rationale: Scraping apps exhibit distinct behavioral signatures: rapid sequential requests, non-standard User-Agents, deep crawls of single domains. Article explicitly describes 'web-scraping' functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns: >10 requests/second to same domain, identical User-Agent across disparate source IPs (indicating botnet), sequential fetching of directory structures, or requests to robots.txt followed by systematic crawl. Flag headless browser signatures (Puppeteer, Selenium, etc.).

suggestion.title: Detect Communication from TV Devices to Known AI Training Data Aggregation or Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltrated data flows to attacker infrastructure. Phrase: 'for AI' indicates data flows to attacker-controlled aggregation points or known bad infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference TV device outbound connections against threat intelligence feeds for known malicious C2 domains, data aggregation services, and proxies. Alert on DNS queries from TV devices to dynamic DNS providers or newly-registered domains. Monitor for use of uncommon ports (8888, 3128, 9999) associated with proxy tunneling.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Installation: Proxy-Trojan
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku...have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices'—app installation is the entry point but no installation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV app store logs for installation of applications matching known proxy-trojan signatures (brdtnet, luminati, bright-sdk variants). Flag installations that succeed despite lacking documented publisher or containing suspicious permissions requests for network access.

suggestion.title: Deceptive Consent Dialog: Hidden Proxy Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—the obfuscation mechanism for enrollment is a T1036 masquerading technique but went undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag TV app UI events or permission dialogs that appear outside standard system patterns, or permission grants logged with minimal user interaction time. Track settings changes (esp. proxy/network settings) made within seconds of app install or without explicit menu navigation.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Network Egress Volume from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article states apps 'scrape web data for AI training'—this scraping activity generates detectably unusual egress patterns not yet translated into a use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV network telemetry for sustained outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to diverse, non-entertainment domains. Baseline expected domains per device model; flag systematic requests to unusual TLDs or rapid domain cycling consistent with web scraping. High packet-loss or multi-threaded connection patterns are indicators.

suggestion.title: Proxy Service Client Registration and Heartbeat
suggestion.rationale: Devices must enroll and maintain enrollment in the proxy network—registration calls and periodic heartbeats to control domains are detectable but not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from smart TV to known proxy service control domains (proxyjs.*, clientsdk.*, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, bright-sdk.com). Focus on DNS queries and TLS certificate subject patterns; proxy clients often use predictable enrollment URLs and periodic callback intervals.

suggestion.title: Proxy App Persistence: Auto-Launch and Update Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article implies apps 'remain enrolled' across device reboots and updates—persistence mechanisms warrant detection but were not included in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TV boot-up telemetry and app lifecycle logs for proxy apps auto-launching without user interaction. Flag modifications to app auto-start settings, service registrations, or scheduled tasks that enable proxy process execution. Detect update bypass techniques (e.g., app-version downgrades or signature disablement).

suggestion.title: Smart TV Proxy App: Network Signature (User-Agent Anomalies)
suggestion.rationale: Proxy clients typically exhibit distinctive User-Agent strings and HTTP header patterns not seen in standard TV apps—these signatures enable direct identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract User-Agent strings and HTTP headers from TV network traffic; flag those containing proxy-sdk identifiers (Bright, Luminati, BrightData libraries) or generic/missing UA headers inconsistent with legitimate Samsung/LG apps. Correlate with known proxy client fingerprints from threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Action Referencing Unverified Publisher
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'Azure Functions Action'—implies attack disguised legitimate action or injected malicious variant; 'Miasma Worm Hits Microsoft Again' signals known actor reusing tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflows referencing GitHub actions from unverified publishers that resemble official Microsoft/Azure action names (e.g., 'azure-*', 'microsoft-*' by non-microsoft orgs). Flag unpinned or wildcard version references (v1.* vs v1.2.3). Cross-reference against GitHub's official verified publisher list.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Disablement or Archival in Short Timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack'—attacker achieved control to mass-disable repos, indicating credential compromise or RBAC exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 repository disabling/archival events within 30-minute window by single service principal, PAT, or user. Correlate with unusual API token creation, geographic anomalies, or off-hours activity. Cross-check token scope against least-privilege baseline.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in .github/workflows File
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack on 'AI Coding Agents' implies payload delivery via workflow file modification—attacker injects malicious build steps to compromise agent runtimes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits modifying .github/workflows/*.yml with suspicious patterns: external docker image pulls from ECR/registries outside organization, curl/wget calls to non-allowlisted domains, env variable exfiltration (echo $GITHUB_TOKEN), or obfuscated bash/PowerShell. Flag commits from newly-created or dormant accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Service Principal or PAT Usage Against Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Disabling '72 other repositories' requires escalated automation credentials; article implies Miasma actor obtained legitimate CI/CD service principal or personal access token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service principal or PAT activity deviating from baseline: access to repositories outside normal scope, rapid-fire repository modification/deletion calls, or sign-ins from unexpected IP ranges. Correlate with recent token issuance or secret rotation.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Secrets via GitHub Actions Log Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD compromise grants access to environment secrets (tokens, API keys, SSH keys); Miasma attack likely harvests credentials for lateral movement into dependent systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan published GitHub Actions logs for patterns of secret exposure: base64-encoded strings, common credential formats (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY), or POST requests to external domains. Flag workflows using `run: echo ${{ secrets.* }}` or dynamic variable expansion in commands.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted or Lookalike GitHub Action from Malicious Publisher
suggestion.rationale: 'Azure Functions Action' prominence in attack title suggests actor distributed trojanized variant under official-sounding name to trick developers into adopting Miasma payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify GitHub actions with names differing by 1-2 characters from official Microsoft/Azure actions but from non-verified publishers (e.g., 'azure-function-action' vs 'azure-functions-action'). Alert if action has been added to workflows in bulk across unrelated organizations or has obfuscated action.yml inputs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious durabletask Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack.' No use case for detecting installation of this specific compromised package was generated despite it being the central IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip install/download commands targeting durabletask package. Flag installations from affected versions or non-PyPI sources. Correlate package installation events with process creation and network activity. Compare installed package hashes against security advisory checksums.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises commonly execute malicious code during setup.py or import-time hooks. Article indicates package compromise but no use case addresses detection of execution triggered by installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate pip install or python setup.py invocations with unexpected child process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget). Alert on network connections originating from Python interpreter during package installation. Monitor for file writes outside site-packages directories during install phase.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Runtime Behavior from Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Once installed, compromised package will exhibit malicious behavior at import or runtime. Article references durabletask compromise but no use case for detecting anomalous runtime behavior was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline behavior for legitimate durabletask usage in Azure Functions and serverless environments. Alert on deviations: unexpected API calls, data access outside normal patterns, credential access, or outbound network connections from Python processes importing durabletask.

suggestion.title: Package Integrity and Checksum Verification Failures
suggestion.rationale: Detecting package tampering is critical in supply chain compromises. Article explicitly indicates package compromise but no use case for integrity verification or checksum mismatch detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package verification tools (pip, checksumming utilities, code signing verification) for failures on durabletask. Alert when downloaded package hashes diverge from known-good values. Correlate failed integrity checks with subsequent indicators of compromise.

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 release_agent Code Execution Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the flaw 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature' and is 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks.' This is the core attack vector and was not detected. No rule exists to alert on release_agent path writes or execution of payloads triggered by release events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/cgroup symlink injection attempts. Correlate with unexpected process spawning during cgroups resource-limit triggers. Monitor for shell or binary execution with parent PID of cgroups kernel subsystem.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged User Privilege Escalation via Kernel Exploit CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article warns flaw 'may allow attackers' to escalate privileges. Pipeline generated no post-exploitation signature. Should detect non-root process transitions to root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability acquisition via cgroups v1 vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes where uid/gid transitions from unprivileged to 0 occur following cgroups-related system calls (open, write on /sys/fs/cgroup). Cross-reference with known KEV catalog date (2026-06-07) to baseline pre-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Container Breakout via cgroups v1 Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 commonly exploited for container escape. Pipeline did not generate container-specific detection despite cgroups being core to container isolation. Article context implies container environments are primary target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor containerized processes accessing /sys/fs/cgroup v1 paths, executing cgroup-manipulation tools (cgexec, cgset), or spawning processes with host-level capabilities. Alert on cgroup v1 configured in container runtimes running on patched kernel versions.

suggestion.title: Systems Still Running Vulnerable cgroups v1 (Kernel Reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' Systems on cgroups v1 are anomalous (v2 is default since ~Linux 5.8); identifying these is recon-phase intelligence for vulnerability scanning and prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory systems where cgroups v1 is enabled via /proc/cgroups parsing or kernel command-line inspection. Flag systems with kernel version < 5.8 OR cgroups=cgroup1 in boot params. Cross-reference against asset database to identify legacy systems requiring patching.

suggestion.title: Kernel CVE-2022-0492 PoC or Exploit Tool Staging
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV warning implies exploit tooling is likely circulating or actively deployed. Pipeline did not generate detection for PoC scripts, exploit binaries, or tool staging common to privilege-escalation playbooks (e.g., cgroup exploit scripts on disk, LKML patch application attempts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on download or write of files matching CVE-2022-0492 exploit signatures (cgroup-bomb.c, CVE-2022-0492.py, etc.). Monitor for exploitation frameworks (Metasploit, pwncat) with cgroups modules loaded. Flag LKML patch application or kernel module compilation targeting this vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Password Reset Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow.' Detection of anomalous access to password reset endpoints (high frequency, sequential user enumeration, unusual parameters) is the primary defensive indicator for this vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password reset endpoints for unusual request patterns: high frequency from single source, sequential user ID enumeration, unusual User-Agent strings, or requests with unexpected parameter values. Alert on response-code discrepancies or timing artifacts that leak valid vs. invalid account information.

suggestion.title: PII Disclosure in Password Reset Responses
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers.' Detection at the application/WAF layer catches information disclosure in endpoint responses before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect password reset endpoint responses for PII patterns (phone numbers, email addresses) in error messages, recovery text, or redirect parameters. Baseline normal response signatures and alert on deviations that expose contact info.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Targeting Exposed Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Once email addresses are public—'high-profile individuals such as Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg'—phishing campaigns using these enumerated targets become immediate follow-up attacks. Detect spikes in inbound email to disclosed accounts post-disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike detection on inbound phishing emails to accounts known to be in Instagram's user base, with account recovery or password reset themes. Correlate timing with vulnerability disclosure date (June 6, 2026) and established Instagram user accounts.

suggestion.title: SIM Swap Attacks Following Phone Number Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Exposure of 'phone numbers associated with user accounts' creates immediate SIM swap risk, especially against high-profile targets. Phone carrier alerts and MFA bypass patterns are key indicators of account takeover attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SIM swap indicators (carrier reports, unusual device registration) with accounts known affected. Alert on MFA delivery failures immediately before successful authentication, unusual device/location during login, or session activity inconsistent with account profile.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Against Enumerated Accounts
suggestion.rationale: With email/phone pairs now public and enumerated via the 'password reset flow' vulnerability, attackers can execute credential stuffing against verified real accounts. The vulnerability also validates which accounts exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for coordinated login failures followed by successful logins using accounts linked to exposed email addresses.
