Track password reset attempts immediately preceding credential stuffing. Watch for automated patterns: many attempts from same source in short timeframe against enumerated account set.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Zero-Day Exploitation via Malformed Media File
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for FFmpeg exploitation despite explicit disclosure of 21 vulnerabilities, a clear attack surface for initial compromise via malicious video/audio processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg process creation with suspicious command-line flags, memory access patterns, or parent processes (email clients, browsers). Correlate with unusual file access to media libraries or temporary codec processing. FFmpeg exploitation often chains to remote code execution via crafted containers.

suggestion.title: Chrome Vulnerability Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs.' Pipeline failed to map any Chrome-specific exploitation vectors despite 429 patches indicating widespread vulnerability landscape requiring active defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome sandbox escape indicators (child processes with SYSTEM/admin privileges), suspicious V8 engine memory access, or Chrome process injection via DLL/code-cave techniques. Correlate with drive-by download detection and malicious script execution.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Version Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses specific vulnerability counts (21 for FFmpeg, 429 for Chrome) but pipeline extracted no version indicators, affected ranges, or patch recommendations for asset remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FFmpeg and Chrome installations via WMI/registry. Extract version strings and compare against pre-patch version baselines referenced in this disclosure. Flag unpatched instances for immediate remediation priority given zero-day status.

suggestion.title: Memory Corruption in FFmpeg Codec Processing
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day category typically involves memory safety (buffer overflow, use-after-free). Article does not provide technical details, but 21 simultaneous zero-days suggest systematic vulnerability class (e.g., codec parsing) warranting heap/stack monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg process for suspicious memory allocation patterns, heap spray indicators, or rapid allocation/deallocation cycles typical of exploitation. Flag abnormal memory pages transitioning to executable state during media file processing.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Unexpected Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Serv-U as targeted product in active exploitation; 'actively exploited' establishes threat hunters need real-time visibility on process spawning. Expected detection gap for Serv-U.exe or sftpd.exe with anomalous parents, arguments, or execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Serv-U daemons (sftpd.exe, Serv-U.exe) are spawned from non-standard parents, with suspicious CLI flags (e.g., /listen on non-standard ports), or with privilege elevation. Baseline normal service startup and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Connection Rate to Serv-U Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'DoS flaw'; DoS impact requires detecting traffic volume anomalies. Phrase 'actively exploited' means defenders need immediate detection. Missed detection for connection floods, incomplete handshakes, or protocol violations on typical Serv-U ports (21, 22, 23).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Threshold on inbound connections to Serv-U listening ports; flag >500 connections in 60s from single source or >100 failed auth attempts. Detect incomplete TCP handshakes (SYN floods) or malformed FTP/SSH commands.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Restart Cascade
suggestion.rationale: DoS attacks terminate target services; 'DoS flaw' in article establishes impact is availability loss. Missing detection for repeated Serv-U process termination, event log service-failure entries, or rapid restarts indicating crash loop under attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Serv-U processes terminate unexpectedly (not by admin action) or restart >2 times in 10 minutes. Correlate with preceding spike in inbound traffic or failed connection logs.

suggestion.title: Known Serv-U CVE Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites CISA KEV catalog inclusion for 'actively exploited' vulnerability; pipeline should map to published CVE details and exploitation indicators. Missing: IDS/IPS signatures, HTTP/FTP payload patterns, or proof-of-concept detection rules for the specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate or ingest signature set for the identified SolarWinds Serv-U CVE (not specified in truncated article). Monitor for malicious request patterns (e.g., oversized commands, path traversal, code injection syntax) targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Serv-U Account
suggestion.rationale: Successfully exploited Serv-U often grants file-transfer access; article's 'actively exploited' status suggests post-exploitation activity follows. Missing: detection of unusual FTP/SFTP login anomalies, file transfer bursts to unexpected destinations, or lateral-move indicators from Serv-U host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed Serv-U login attempts followed by success from new source IP; detect bulk file transfers to non-whitelisted destinations; monitor for unusual privilege or group membership changes on Serv-U host post-login.

suggestion.title: CVE Publication / CISA KEV Reconnaissance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability was added to CISA KEV catalog—recon phase where threat actors scan for vulnerable instances. Missing: detection of scanning tools (Shodan queries, mass-scan traffic), CVE-specific scan patterns, or vulnerability assessment tooling targeting Serv-U.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound scans for Serv-U fingerprinting (banner-grab on port 21/22/23, HTTP OPTIONS requests, default-credential attempts). Flag scanning tools like masscan, Shodan CLI, or automated vulnerability scanners targeting the organization's external-facing Serv-U instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20245 Flaw Actively Exploited' — the primary attack vector must be detected. No use case was generated to catch exploitation in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager listening endpoints for HTTP requests targeting known vulnerable code paths. Alert on successful authentication immediately following exploit-pattern URI sequences (e.g., path traversal, injection vectors typical of unpatched SD-WAN flaws).

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized Admin Access Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation but does not indicate mitigation; post-compromise credential theft or privilege escalation is highly probable. No use case monitors for admin authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication failures to Cisco vManage admin console (port 8443 typical) followed within seconds by successful authentication from same source IP, or successful logins from IPs never seen in past 90 days.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution via SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies command execution capability post-compromise. Article provides no detail, but standard post-exploit playbook would spawn shell or script interpreters. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any child process spawned by Cisco SD-WAN Manager/vManager service (java process, nginx) running /bin/bash, /bin/sh, powershell, cmd.exe, or script interpreters. Correlate with CVE-2026-20245 exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: Configuration / Credential Exfiltration from SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: No patch available increases attacker incentive to steal network topology, device credentials, and WAN link configurations for lateral movement or persistent access. Pipeline completely missed exfiltration signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk reads from SD-WAN config directories (/etc/vmanage, /opt/viptela/etc) followed by unusual outbound TLS/DNS/HTTP traffic to non-whitelisted destinations. Alert on config files appearing in /tmp or being read by non-manager processes.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation on SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation with no available patch creates strong incentive for persistence. No use case detects backdoors, cron jobs, or service modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new cron jobs, systemd services, or sudoers entries created after exploitation timeline. Flag any executable installed in /etc/init.d, /usr/lib/systemd/system, or /var/spool/cron by non-admin user accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager to Branch Devices
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN managers centrally control branch edge devices; article emphasizes manager compromise but pipeline missed lateral movement phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected SSH, NETCONF, or proprietary management protocol traffic from vManager to branch edge devices (vEdge, cEdge appliances) outside change windows. Flag high-volume config pushes or firmware updates initiated from compromised manager.

suggestion.title: Suspicious persistent outbound proxy traffic from smart TV device
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states TVs are 'turned into web-scraping proxies'—core attack vector is undetected. Exfiltration via TV's internet connection to attacker infrastructure is the payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV device (AndroidTV, WebOS, Tizen user-agents) initiating sustained outbound HTTPS/HTTP sessions to non-ISP, non-CDN IPs with cumulative data transfer >1GB/week. Baseline comparison: normal TV behavior is streaming + OS updates only (<100MB/week). Alert if traffic occurs during off-peak hours (midnight–6am) or coincides with free-app installation.

suggestion.title: Free app installation with deceptive network-permission scope
suggestion.rationale: Attack begins with 'free apps' distribution per article headline. Pipeline missed initial-access detection—apps with legitimate purpose (game, utility) requesting unrestricted network access warrant alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Application installation on smart TV platform where declared functionality does not justify requested permissions. Example: 'Weather app' requesting persistent background-process execution and unrestricted outbound access. Monitor app metadata (manifest permissions vs. declared purpose) and flag mismatches. Cross-reference app signer certificate and publisher against known malware authors.

suggestion.title: Bulk HTTP scraping pattern from smart TV to news/aggregation domains
suggestion.rationale: Core attack is web scraping. Article states apps 'scraping for AI'—this is the collection phase. No detection drafted for high-volume automated requests to content sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV device making >100 HTTP HEAD/GET requests per hour to known content-aggregation sites (news: cnn.com, bbc.com; social: medium.com; repositories: github.com; archives). Request pattern: short response times, no user-agent variation, sequential domain enumeration, no session cookies. Distinguish from legitimate streaming by examining request rate and target domain category.

suggestion.title: Smart TV proxy relay to AI training infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies scraping 'for AI'—detection should target C2 domains or infrastructure serving this purpose. Pipeline produced zero C2-phase logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV establishing persistent outbound tunnel or forwarding traffic to known AI data-scraping-as-a-service platforms or LLM-training-data aggregators. Maintain IOC list of C2 domain patterns (e.g., proxy forwarding services, data-broker APIs, unattributed scraping infrastructure). Alert on DNS queries or TLS SNI matching known malicious C2.

suggestion.title: App persistence and auto-update after device reboot
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious behavior happening 'quietly'—malware persistence is implied. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection. Rogue apps re-launching after termination or updating silently would confirm ongoing compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Free app automatically relaunching after process kill or device reboot without explicit user action. Monitor process spawn behavior: does app appear in startup traces with no corresponding UI trigger? Cross-reference app auto-update events with network exfiltration spikes. Alert if app process respawns >3 times in 24 hours after user termination.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Smart TV App Installation with Hidden Proxy Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku' are the vector. Pipeline missed initial-access phase entirely. Delivery is deceptive app store distribution targeting TV platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag apps installed on smart TVs (Tizen/webOS/Roku OS) that request network or persistent storage permissions while appearing as utility/media apps. Alert on apps not signed by vendor, or with SDK dependencies matching proxy infrastructure (bright, luminati, brdtnet).

suggestion.title: Network C2 Connections to Residential Proxy Enrollment Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists domains: proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, bright-sdk.com. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite being clearly named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS/TLS connections from smart TV source IPs to {proxyjs,clientsdk}.{brdtnet,luminatinet,bright-sdk}.com or brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io. Flag persistent sessions (>1hr) and any outbound traffic spikes from residential TV IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Deceptive Consent Dialog Buried in Remote Navigation Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation' — explicit defense-evasion masquerading technique to hide malicious intent from user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TV apps for rapid arrow-key event sequences that trigger hidden dialogs. Flag permission grants that occur without observable user dwell-time on consent screen, or consent granted via non-obvious navigation paths (e.g., buried in Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics).

suggestion.title: Persistent Background Service for Proxy Network Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'continuous enrollment into a commercial residential proxy network.' Persistence layer must exist on device to re-enroll and survive reboots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on background services or scheduled tasks created by free-app packages on smart TVs with names or executables matching proxy/SDK patterns (brightsdk, luminati, brdtnet). Monitor for low-frequency wake schedules and network-only capabilities.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Web Scraping and Proxy Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'scrape web data for AI training' via 'residential proxy network.' Pipeline missed exfiltration phase entirely despite being central to threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TV devices making 100+ HTTP/HTTPS requests per hour to arbitrary third-party domains, collecting responses without user-initiated browsing. Correlate with outbound traffic to C2 infrastructure. Validate against normal TV usage patterns (streaming services, weather APIs, firmware updates).

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Unauthorized Commit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories were compromised by Miasma Worm; pipeline generated zero detections. Core attack vector is malicious code injection into repos—must detect commits from compromised or unauthorized accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits to Microsoft-owned repositories from newly-provisioned service accounts, accounts with recent credential resets, or accounts authenticating from unusual geographies. Prioritize commits touching .github/workflows/, build scripts, or CI/CD configuration files.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Replication - Recursive Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Miasma Worm explicitly indicates self-replicating malware; pipeline supplied no execution-phase detections for process chains or recursive spawning behavior typical of worm propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent-child process pairs with identical or near-identical command lines spawned in rapid succession, processes executing from .git directories or temporary paths, or high branching-factor process trees from a single source.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across GitHub Repositories via Shared Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of 73 repositories implies either shared credential theft or propagation across organizational boundaries; no lateral-movement detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git clone operations on multiple repositories by the same user/token in short time windows, SSH key material exfiltration from developer workstations, or repository access from bot-like service accounts from non-standard IP ranges.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Tampering - Build Artifact Contamination
suggestion.rationale: Worm injection into GitHub repos necessarily infects CI/CD build outputs and published artifacts; pipeline detected zero persistence or artifact-modification signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml), new pipeline steps downloading unverified dependencies, unexpected artifact registry pushes with unsigned or mismatched SHAs, or build logs containing network exfiltration commands.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Account Compromise - Malicious Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Access to 73 Microsoft-owned repos requires compromised or stolen personal access tokens/SSH keys; no credential-access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub/Azure DevOps personal access tokens or SSH keys issued from non-corporate IPs, failed multi-factor authentication attempts preceding successful logins, or API authentication patterns consistent with credential-stuffing or replay attacks.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Administrative Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' — coordinated disabling across multiple distinct repos signals account compromise or admin privilege abuse. Must detect mass state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single principal disables or transfers ownership of >10 repositories within 60 minutes, or audit logs show repository deletion/archival across disparate organizations in single session.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifically names 'Azure Functions Action' — supply chain attacks on CI/CD must detect modifications to .github/workflows and action.yml with new secret exfiltration, credential dumping, or privilege escalation steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits modifying workflow files that introduce new step runners, add `secrets:` context to step outputs, modify runner environment to export credentials, or inject shell commands with exfil patterns.

suggestion.title: Compromised Package in AI/Coding Agent Ecosystem
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'AI Coding Agents' via supply chain — detect new package versions with unexpected maintainers, added binary dependencies, or sudden code entropy spikes in npm/PyPI/pip indexes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package versions with author/owner changes, newly-injected transitive dependencies from untrusted sources, or statistical code anomalies (entropy, byte distribution) relative to prior versions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Commits to Release Branches
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires code injection into 73 repos — detect commits to main/release branches from actors outside historical committer set, or commits bypassing branch protection policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when commits land on protected/release branches from newly-provisioned or dormant accounts, or when commit author differs from GitHub account committing (sign mismatch), or when branch protections are temporarily disabled before merge.

suggestion.title: Mass GitHub/Azure API Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover 73 target repositories — detect reconnaissance via bulk repository metadata queries, organization membership enumeration, or Azure Functions endpoint probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume GitHub API calls (list repos, org members, collaborators) from single IP/principal, or Azure REST API probing Functions endpoints and IAM permissions from untrusted source within short window.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm Persistence via Forked Repository
suggestion.rationale: Named threat actor in title — establish persistence baseline: detect forks of compromised repos, stars/watches from newly-created accounts, or background pull requests containing reconnaissance commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repositories being forked immediately after compromise, or pull requests with generic/templated descriptions that modify build config (CI/CD trigger injection), or repository stars from bulk newly-created bot accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised 'durabletask' PyPI package; pipeline missed baseline detection for suspicious package installations or version anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install / python -m pip / poetry add for: (1) known-compromised package names (durabletask), (2) unusual version jumps or re-released versions of dormant packages, (3) rapid successive package installations from single source. Correlate with network callbacks to verify delivery.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Imported Python Package
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package executes malicious code on import; pipeline missed detection for unexpected child processes or network connections spawned by python/pip
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect subprocess spawning or outbound network connections from python.exe or pip processes immediately after package installation. Flag curl/wget/powershell child processes or DNS queries to non-standard domains initiated within 5 seconds of 'import <package>'.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Attacker-Controlled C2 via Compromised Package
suggestion.rationale: Malicious durabletask payload would establish command-and-control callbacks; pipeline missed detection for unusual outbound connections or credential theft patterns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS or HTTP POST traffic originating from python processes to newly-registered or low-reputation domains, especially those with high entropy (base64-like) in SNI or request body. Cross-reference against current package installation timeline.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Repository Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack involves uploading malicious version to PyPI; pipeline missed detection for package version anomalies, sudden author changes, or file integrity violations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest PyPI metadata API logs; alert on: (1) version jumps or pre-release versions published to stable branch, (2) unexpected .so/.pyd/.pyc binaries in pure-Python package, (3) author/maintainer changes without prior repository activity, (4) rapid version republication after deletion.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Compromised Package in Build Environments
suggestion.rationale: If durabletask installed in CI/CD (GitHub Actions, Jenkins), malicious code runs with build environment privileges; pipeline missed detection for build-context credential/secret access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD logs, detect python package imports followed by file access to .ssh/, .aws/, ~/.netrc, or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables. Flag subprocess execution of git commands with unusual arguments (push to external repo, clone with embedded credentials).

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 DD-WRT Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware is delivered by exploiting CVE-2021-27137, a buffer overflow vulnerability caused by insufficient user input...can be leveraged without authentication.' No exploitation detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to DD-WRT admin interfaces (/cgi-bin endpoints common in router admin) with abnormally large Content-Length payloads or payload containing repeated byte patterns typical of buffer overflow attempts. Flag specifically against known vulnerable DD-WRT versions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Hidden Binary Creation in /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, /dev/shm/.sys
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware copies itself to hidden locations such as /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, and /dev/shm/.sys, and then creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes.' Persistence mechanism entirely unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation with leading dot in /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm followed by chmod +x within 1 minute. Correlate with immediate cron -e or crontab file modifications, or subsequent shell startup file writes (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .profile).

suggestion.title: Cron Job Creation with 15-Minute Relaunch Interval
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes.' Scheduled task persistence not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect crontab modifications (cron -e, /etc/cron.d, /etc/cron.hourly writes) containing */15 interval patterns pointing to hidden directories or /dev/shm. Especially suspicious if cron task executes without parent interactive shell session.

suggestion.title: Multi-Port SSH/Telnet Brute Force Scanning Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'downloads a Python script...uses worker threads to randomly scan internet-facing systems on common ports like 22 (SSH), 23 (Telnet), 80/443 (HTTP/HTTPS), 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888...attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials.' Lateral movement scanning not mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed SSH/Telnet login attempts from single source across multiple target hosts within rolling 10-minute window. Alert when same source probes ports 22, 23, 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888 sequentially (characteristic of multi-port scanner). Flag credential patterns typical of weak default creds (admin/admin, root/root, root/<blank>).

suggestion.title: Termination and Persistence Removal of Competing Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'C0XMO actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients...and terminates them...by deleting binaries and removing their persistence mechanisms, including cron jobs, init scripts, system services, and shell profile entries.' Defense evasion activity not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a newly-spawned process issues kill/pkill/rm commands against known malware binaries (mirai, tsunami, qbot, Gafgyt variants) or deletes files from /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, /etc/cron.d directories in rapid succession (10+ delete operations within 30 seconds).

suggestion.title: Custom Multi-Stage C2 Handshake with Magic Strings
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'connects to a hardcoded command-and-control (C2) address using a custom multi-stage handshake that includes magic strings and shared secrets.' C2 communication pattern not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained connections to hardcoded IPs with multi-stage connection pattern: initial connection, short silence, then rapid burst of small payloads (characteristic of handshake negotiation). Alert on connections with unusual/non-standard ports combined with encrypted payload containing repeated fixed-length headers (magic string markers).

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'cgroups v1 release_agent feature' as the exploitable mechanism. Pipeline generated no detection for this specific technique despite it being the core attack vector mentioned in threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /etc/cgroup files with shell metacharacters; flag execution of system commands spawned via cgroup release_agent callbacks. Track privilege boundary transitions from user namespaces to host uid=0.

suggestion.title: Linux kernel exploitation—CVE-2022-0492 attack surface
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks 'actively leveraged' this kernel flaw but pipeline emitted zero kill-chain phases. Privilege escalation from container or unprivileged user context is the core attack behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid uid/gid transitions or anomalous capability changes (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE granted to unprivileged process). Flag processes opening /proc/sys/kernel paths or accessing cgroup pseudofiles from containers.

suggestion.title: Container escape or namespace breakout detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE context ('cgroups v1 ... may allow attackers') strongly implies container-to-host escape. No use case covered this critical attack outcome despite being implicit in the vulnerability description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes originating from container namespaces (pid/net/user) that subsequently execute host-level commands, access host filesystems outside mount boundaries, or spawn children with elevated capabilities.

suggestion.title: Instagram Password Reset Endpoint Abuse - Bulk Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' suggests publicly accessible endpoint; no mention of access controls. Attackers probing or testing endpoint before patch deployment would appear as spike in requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline password reset endpoint request volume per IP/geo. Alert on single source generating >5% of daily traffic to endpoint, or requests from datacenter IPs associated with scanning tools. Monitor for requests missing valid session cookies or user context.

suggestion.title: Unredacted PII in Password Reset HTTP Response
suggestion.rationale: Core finding: 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers' — password reset endpoint returning full email/phone in response body instead of masked format indicates application-layer information disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP 200 responses from password reset endpoints for presence of unredacted email (user@domain.com pattern) or phone (±10-digit number). Alert if response contains >1 email/phone field in plaintext. Correlate with request patterns suggesting enumeration.

suggestion.title: Post-Disclosure Account Takeover via Exposed Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies email/phone exposure for 'high-profile individuals' (Zuckerberg, Rodriguez); exposed identity + password reset token creates account compromise window pre-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After June 6 2026, correlate password reset events on exposed accounts with successful subsequent logins from IPs/geos never seen for those accounts. Flag reset+login <2hr apart. Secondary: detect credential stuffing on test accounts using format (exposed-email@instagram.com, dictionary-passwords).

suggestion.title: Rapid Patching Rollout - Version Jump Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emergency hotfix within hours' — Instagram likely incremented API version or deployed code blocking unredacted PII in responses. Observable via version headers or 400 errors on old client requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Instagram API version headers (e.g., X-API-Version, User-Agent strings) for sudden increments June 6-7 2026. Detect requests returning 400/403 due to missing/invalid response fields post-hotfix. Cross-reference with deployment logs for password-reset related changes.

suggestion.title: RMM Tool Installation via Impersonated IT Support
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'trick the target into installing remote monitoring and management tools such as AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps, thereby granting them initial access'—this post-compromise persistence is directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps installers following Teams/Zoom/Quick Assist remote session activity. Flag installations with unusual parent processes or from temporary directories.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Typosquatting Internal IT Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'phishing domains tied to the campaign that impersonate internal IT portals using naming patterns such as <organization>-itdesk[.]com <organization>-it[.]com <organization>-helpdesk[.]com'—domain registration patterns are detectable via WHOIS/DNS enrichment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic to domains matching pattern [organization-name]-(itdesk|it|helpdesk)[.]com that resolve to non-internal IP space. Cross-reference against legitimate internal IT domains to identify spoofs.

suggestion.title: Privnote Self-Destructing Message Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'use privnote[.]com, a self-destructing messaging service, to share installation links and commands with targets' and 'this tactic helps reduce forensic artifacts'—unusual for legitimate IT operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS to privnote[.]com from user endpoints during or immediately after remote access sessions. Alert on any sharing of technical installation/configuration links via ephemeral messaging services.

suggestion.title: Bulk Sensitive Document Targeting from Compromised Session
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Once inside a network, the group searches for sensitive legal and financial documents, including contracts, tax records, Social Security numbers, and merger or acquisition files' from 'document management platforms and cloud storage repositories'—rapid, focused collection is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequential bulk access to document repositories (SharePoint, OneDrive, file shares) targeting legal/financial documents (contracts, tax, M&A plans, SSN records) from a single session within compressed timeframe (< 2 hours), particularly from compromised RDP/Zoom sessions.

suggestion.title: WinSCP and Rclone Execution for Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'WinSCP or Rclone' as exfiltration tools—these utilities are strongly indicative of data theft intent and rarely appear in legitimate enterprise operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any execution of WinSCP.exe or rclone.exe, especially following document access anomalies or compromised remote sessions. Flag process invocations with cloud storage or SFTP endpoints in command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Fast-Flux DNS Rotation for Leak Site Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article reports attacker infrastructure uses 'fast-flux infrastructure' with 'residential IP addresses across multiple countries and ISPs' to protect 'business-data-leaks[.]com' leak site—fast-flux rotation patterns are detectable via passive DNS analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains with anomalously high NXDOMAIN rates followed by rapid IP rotation across residential IP ranges spanning multiple geographies. Flag queries to domains with 'leak', 'data-leak', 'business-data' keywords regardless of observed resolution success rate.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Process Crash or Excessive Resource Consumption
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Actively Exploited SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Flaw'—DoS attacks manifest as service crashes, restarts, or resource exhaustion. Pipeline generated zero Impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ServUAgent.exe or Serv-U service terminating unexpectedly, rapid sequential restarts within 5 minutes, or CPU spikes >80% correlated with network connection flood from external IPs to Serv-U listening ports (22, 115, 3074).

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited.' Pipeline missed Initial Access detection for exploitation attempts via HTTP/SSH to Serv-U endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known vulnerable Serv-U URI patterns, SSH protocol handshakes followed by abnormal command sequences, or multiple failed authentication attempts against Serv-U SFTP/SSH from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable SolarWinds Serv-U Version Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA Adds...to KEV Catalog'—this marks elevation to government-tracked active exploitation. Pipeline missed detection for inventory drift against patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On endpoints running Serv-U: enumerate installed version via process command-line (/version flag), registry keys (HKLM\Software\SolarWinds\Serv-U), or file version metadata, then cross-reference against CISA KEV catalog. Alert if running version is known-vulnerable.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager—CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Actively Exploited' with 'No Patch Available'—establishes real-time threat. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite explicit exploitation claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints matching CVE-2026-20245 payload signatures or known PoC patterns. Alert on requests with abnormal POST bodies, path traversal indicators, or command injection patterns targeting the Manager's REST API.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager—Post-Exploitation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Actively exploited vulnerability in network management plane suggests remote code execution or privilege escalation. Article omission of exploitation mechanism does not negate likelihood of command execution post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unexpected process spawning from Manager service accounts or unusual shell invocation (bash, sh, powershell) from the SD-WAN Manager process tree. Cross-correlate with authentication logs to detect lateral movement from the compromised Manager instance.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager—External Remote Services Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager is an internet-facing control-plane node; exploitation likely targets or abuses its management interface. Article establishes 'actively exploited' status, implying attacker is already establishing access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track external IP connections to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager admin interfaces; correlate with failed authentication attempts. Alert on credential additions to the Manager during or shortly after exploitation windows (especially if no patch available—attacker may lock in access).

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager—Asset and Version Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'No Patch Available'—defenders must identify affected instances by version/build. Pipeline should have flagged need for inventory enumeration before detection can be scoped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances for version/build numbers to identify which are running unpatched builds vulnerable to CVE-2026-20245. Correlate with external access logs to prioritize instances reachable from the internet.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager—Network Segmentation Bypass via Manager Compromise
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager controls overlay network policies and routing; compromise allows attacker to pivot to managed branch/remote sites. Article's 'actively exploited' claim implies post-exploitation phase likely underway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious policy changes or tunnel routing modifications initiated from the Manager console, especially if triggered by non-standard administrator accounts or outside change windows. Monitor for new overlay tunnels to untrusted destinations.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager—Management-Plane Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager holds topology, routing, and device configuration data. Actively exploited vulnerability creates risk of stolen network intelligence. Pipeline missed collection-phase implications.
log_sources: Cisco SD-WAN Manager database audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API queries to the Cisco SD-WAN Manager database (device inventory, topology, policy tables). Alert on large outbound data transfers from the Manager instance to external IPs or object-storage URIs (S3, Azure Blob, etc.) that do not match legitimate backup/reporting patterns.

suggestion.title: WordPress admin account creation via form injection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active wild exploitation: 'The attacker submits a value for a text field...followed by a PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account.' Telemetry shows username 'diksimarina' as known exploitation artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_insert_user() calls with role='administrator' or cap_administrator, especially during or shortly after HTTP POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints. Look for unexpected admin account creation within 5 minutes of form submission from external IPs. Hunt specifically for username 'diksimarina' and variants.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Complex Calculation eval() injection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism stated: 'Complex Calculation feature...accepts values submitted through form fields and inserts them into a PHP code string...executes the resulting code using PHP's eval() function.' Attack vector: 'attacker can close the intended string, inject arbitrary PHP code, and comment out the remaining generated code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form POST submissions to Everest Forms calculation endpoints containing unescaped single quotes followed by PHP syntax (function names, keywords, // comment markers). Flag payloads like: ' followed by wp_, sys_, exec, eval. Correlate with eval() execution in PHP logs or subsequent database writes creating admin records.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Everest Forms Pro version detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'affects versions 1.9.12 and earlier' and patch released March 18. Active exploitation confirmed starting April 13 with 29,300+ blocked attempts. Unpatched instances are directly exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan WordPress plugin directories for Everest Forms Pro version ≤1.9.12. Cross-reference with web access logs for POST requests to form processing endpoints from untrusted sources. Any unpatched instance receiving form traffic post-April-2026 warrants immediate investigation.

suggestion.title: Known malicious account 'diksimarina' hunt
suggestion.rationale: Wordfence telemetry documented this exact username created during active exploitation. Article: 'username diksimarina' and 'review log files and administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search WordPress user tables and admin logs for username 'diksimarina' or simple variants. Check creation timestamp, last login, capabilities, and actions. Any match is confirmed compromise indicator requiring full forensic response including backdoor sweep.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms source IP blocking (202.56.2.126, 209.146.60.26)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two primary exploitation sources: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26' and recommends defenders block them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26 at perimeter and WAF. Hunt historical logs for any HTTP/HTTPS requests from these sources to WordPress domains, especially to form endpoints. Correlate with injection payloads and admin-creation events for attack confirmation.

suggestion.title: PHP string escape bypass in form field values
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'user input is passed through sanitize_text_field() function, which does not escape single quotes (\') or other characters that influence PHP syntax. As a result, an attacker can close the intended string, inject arbitrary PHP code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form field values containing single quotes adjacent to PHP keywords, function calls, or control structures. Specific pattern: ' followed by whitespace and (wp_, mysql_, exec, system, eval, include, require, array, if, foreach, etc.). Medium-confidence alert; escalate to high if followed by database modification or file write events.

suggestion.title: Trojanized App Installation and Persistence on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs'—initial access via compromised app distribution (supply chain). Pipeline produced zero IOCs and no initial-access phase despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV devices for app installations from non-standard sources (sideload, untrusted app store, unsigned packages). Correlate app installation events with subsequent network callbacks to C2 infrastructure or unexpected outbound connections initiated by the TV process within 10 minutes post-install.

suggestion.title: Web-Scraping Proxy Activity from Residential IP
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: 'Web-Scraping Proxies for AI'—detection of proxy botnet behavior (exfiltration of content). Pipeline failed to map the command-and-control or exfiltration phases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on smart TV devices generating >100 HTTP requests/hour to diverse external domains with high request velocity. Flag GET requests retrieving large HTML payloads or structured data (JSON, XML) from news, academic, or copyright-protected content sites. Correlate patterns with known AI training data repositories or scraping targets.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Command-and-Control Beaconing from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article implies coordinated, ongoing proxy operation ('quietly')—requires C2 channel to inject targets and retrieve results. Pipeline produced zero kill-chain phases; C2 reconstruction is missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect regular, interval-based outbound connections from smart TV to fixed IPs or registered domains not associated with firmware updates, OEM services, or CDNs. Flag DNS queries for newly registered or low-reputation domains from TV device. Alert on small-payload exchanges (beaconing pattern) in off-hours or outside normal usage windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Update or Package Installation on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized apps persist via update mechanisms; article's 'quietly' implies long-term operation requiring persistence. Pipeline did not surface persistence techniques (T1547.*, T1195.002).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for app update packages from non-OEM sources or repositories. Flag updates that decompress secondary executables, modify network settings, or create hidden services. Detect app updates executing with unusual privileges or modifying system binaries outside the expected app sandbox.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Data Exfiltration via Residential Device
suggestion.rationale: Adversary objective is scraping 'for AI' (bulk data theft using residential IPs to evade reputation blocks). Impact phase—large-volume unauthorized data transfer—was not captured in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when smart TV device outbound bandwidth increases 5x+ above baseline within 24 hours. Flag sustained HTTP/HTTPS traffic (>500 KB/hour) to non-CDN, non-media-streaming destinations. Correlate with app installation events and cross-reference target domains against copyright-protected content sites, academic repositories, or AI training datasets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Installation on Smart TV Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states free apps on Samsung, LG, Roku 'quietly enrolling millions of living room devices'—initial access is through app store downloads; pipeline missed the installation event as a detection hook.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for app installations on smart TVs from publishers without established reputation. Correlate with subsequent outbound connections to proxy domains. Alert on apps requesting network permissions that don't match their declared function.

suggestion.title: Connections to Bright Data / Proxy Infrastructure Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 11 specific IOCs (proxyjs.brdtnet.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, luminati.io, etc.) that are the direct control infrastructure; standard IOC-driven hunt completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries and connections from any device to bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io and subdomains proxyjs.*, clientsdk.*. Flag devices connecting to multiple proxy domains within short timeframe as likely proxy network enrollment.

suggestion.title: Persistent Outbound Traffic Anomaly on Residential Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes devices being enrolled to 'scrape web data for AI training'—sustained exfiltration traffic from a device typically used for streaming is the measurable impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for normal smart TV traffic (streaming, app updates, DNS). Alert on sustained outbound traffic that deviates significantly from baseline or shows patterns consistent with being rerouted through proxy infrastructure (e.g., connections to residential IP ranges, repeated connections to same proxy domain with varying payloads).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Hidden Consent Dialogs in Smart TV Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically states consent 'buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—masquerading/UI deception is the evasion tactic used to obscure permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit app permission requests for network access from apps that don't require it (non-streaming, non-communication). Monitor for permission elevation patterns (app requests broad permissions, then requests expanded permissions in minor update). Flag apps with network permissions that become active only after app update completes.

suggestion.title: App Update Triggering Unexpected Network Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article suggests 'free apps' deploy the proxy enrollment silently, likely after installation or update; detect when app updates are followed immediately by new persistent network connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate app update events on smart TVs with subsequent establishment of new persistent outbound connections. Alert on apps that establish connections to proxy infrastructure domains within 5-60 seconds of update completion, especially if those connections exhibit heartbeat/check-in patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Bulk Repository Commits by Non-Developer Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 73 repositories were compromised. Miasma worm 'hits' these repositories—implies unauthorized code injection. 'Supply chain attack' indicates commits/pull requests from attacker-controlled or compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk commit/PR merges to production repositories from non-whitelisted accounts, commits introducing build scripts with network calls (curl/wget/powershell), or commits bypassing branch protection in compressed timeframe.

suggestion.title: Git Post-Checkout Hook Execution on Developer Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Developers cloning 73 infected repositories trigger malicious hooks. Worms self-replicate through initialization scripts in .git directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Bash/PowerShell process spawning from .git/hooks directories, Git hook file modifications post-clone, or unexpected child processes from git.exe at repository clone completion.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Artifact in CI/CD Pipeline Output
suggestion.rationale: GitHub supply chain attack implies automated builds. Malware injected into repositories flows into release artifacts (binaries, packages, containers) consumed by downstream users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or anomalously-signed artifacts published from automated builds, build manifests introducing new external dependencies, or GitHub Actions workflows modified to exfiltrate secrets/keys.

suggestion.title: Service Account Access to Multiple Repositories in Compressed Timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Attacker likely abuses CI/CD credentials or service accounts to access/modify 73 repositories. Bulk access pattern deviates from legitimate automation baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate access to >10 repositories by single service account within 1 hour; flag if source IP, timestamp, or access pattern deviates from historical baseline for that account.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Direct Push to Protected Branches Without PR Review
suggestion.rationale: Worm bypassing code review to inject malware into 73 repositories. Direct pushes to main/master by unexpected actors evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful force-pushes to protected branches, direct commits bypassing branch protection rules, or commits merged without required reviewer approval when baseline shows 100% PR enforcement.

suggestion.title: Repository Clone Activity from Atypical Network Locations
suggestion.rationale: Miasma worm propagation implies external infrastructure cloning infected repos at scale. Bulk clones from ASNs/geolocations inconsistent with Microsoft/developer patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency git clone operations from single source IP targeting multiple Microsoft repositories, clones from datacenter/cloud ASNs inconsistent with expected developer geography, or clones preceded by failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Repository Mass Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' and Azure Functions Action compromised. Pipeline missed the coordinated repository tampering pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk repository settings changes (disabling actions, workflows, branch protections) within short time window across multiple repos by single account or token. Correlate with unusual OAuth token issuance or compromised PAT usage.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack targeting 'AI Coding Agents' via GitHub Actions implies workflow/action modification. Article mentions Azure Functions Action specifically—this is execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits modifying .github/workflows/ files in public repos or published GitHub Actions that add new secrets, environment vars, or script execution. Flag additions of curl/powershell download-and-execute patterns targeting external domains.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm Artifact Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names threat as 'Miasma Worm'—this is a known malware family. Pipeline failed to extract indicators or suggest file/process monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Miasma worm signatures in downloaded artifacts, compiled binaries in build caches, or suspicious DLL/executable files in GitHub runner environments. Cross-reference with malware intelligence feeds and hash-based detection.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Public Repository Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies worm targeting 'AI Coding Agents' via public packages/actions. No UC for detecting malicious dependencies added to lock files or manifest poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected additions or version bumps in dependency manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod) in high-profile repos. Flag dependencies with newly-created publishers or unusual publish velocity. Correlate with OAuth token anomalies.

suggestion.title: AI Tool Integration Abuse via Compromised Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'targeting AI Coding Agents'—suggests credential theft for GitHub Copilot, IDE integrations, or automation tools. Pipeline missed credential-access detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth token issuance to unusual client IPs/user agents (non-IDE), bulk PAT creation, or token usage anomalies (e.g., tokens issued for GitHub Copilot suddenly accessing private repos). Cross-reference with suspicious Git clone/push patterns.

suggestion.title: Build Artifact Exfiltration via GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack implies data exfil. Article title does not detail exfil but repo disabling suggests attack cleanup. No UC for detecting outbound transfers of build secrets or source code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unencrypted HTTPS POST/PUT to non-standard domains from GitHub Actions runners, especially with large payloads or multipart form uploads. Flag exfil of secrets, source code, or .env files. Monitor for GitHub Actions secrets being logged or written to external services.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Installation — Known Malicious Package Name or Version
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' — establishes affected package and attack vector. Detections must flag installations of durabletask alongside other known-compromised package names from threat intel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install / pip list / requirements.txt parsing for package names matching known-compromised PyPI packages (durabletask, etc.). Alert on installations without corresponding SBOM entry or matching threat-intel feeds. Flag version pinning mismatches.

suggestion.title: PyPI Account Compromise — Unauthorized Package Publish Event
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack implies attacker gained package maintainer credentials. Article describes package 'compromised' — detections needed for unauthorized publish events to PyPI registry from unexpected IPs, geolocations, or API tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI publish API logs for: (1) version uploads from new IP/geolocation, (2) publishes outside maintainer's normal schedule/timezone, (3) new or previously-unseen API tokens performing publish, (4) failed authentication attempts preceding successful publish.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Suspicious Process Execution from Python Package Path
suggestion.rationale: Compromised PyPI packages execute malicious code during import/installation. Article establishes package compromise — detections needed for unexpected child processes spawned from site-packages or .local/lib directories immediately after pip install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by python.exe with parent path containing 'site-packages', '.local/lib', or pip cache directories. Flag unexpected spawns (curl, wget, powershell, cmd) within 60s of pip install completion. Alert on LOLBin invocations from package directories.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Hash or Checksum Mismatch — Transitive Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions package compromise; supply-chain attacks often inject malicious versions. Detections needed for installed package hashes mismatching expected SBOMs, requirements-lock files, or threat-intel feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package hashes (pip show, pip freeze) against locked requirements files and threat-intel feeds of known-malicious package hashes. Alert on hash mismatches, missing dependencies, or unexpected version substitutions during pip install.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Network Exfiltration or C2 Beaconing from Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages establish backdoors or stealers. Article describes compromise — detections needed for post-install network anomalies (DNS, HTTP/HTTPS to unknown domains, suspicious data exfiltration patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections from python.exe processes within 5 minutes of pip install to non-whitelisted external domains. Flag DNS queries for known C2 domains or suspicious subdomains. Alert on data exfiltration patterns (large outbound transfers, encrypted tunnels to unknown IPs).

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Injection — Unexpected Package in Dependency Tree
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises often poison transitive dependencies (packages that durabletask depends on). Article establishes package compromise — detections needed for unexpected versions or new packages appearing in pip freeze output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse pip freeze output and cross-reference against known upstream lockfiles (Pipfile.lock, poetry.lock). Alert on transitive dependencies with unexpected versions, orphaned packages, or mismatches with upstream manifests. Flag version pinning anomalies.

suggestion.title: Scanning for DD-WRT and IoT vulnerabilities on internet-facing ports
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The scanner then uses worker threads to randomly scan internet-facing systems on common ports like 22 (SSH), 23 (Telnet), 80/443 (HTTP/HTTPS), 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888, and others.' This is the reconnaissance phase before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single-source high-volume connection attempts across multiple ports (22, 23, 80, 443, 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888) within short time window, especially originating from known German IP ranges or with botnet-typical user-agents. Successful scanning typically precedes exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 exploitation attempts against DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'C0XMO botnet malware is delivered by exploiting CVE-2021-27137, a buffer overflow vulnerability caused by insufficient user input. It can be leveraged without authentication and leads to executing arbitrary code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to DD-WRT admin interfaces containing buffer overflow payloads or oversized parameters in known vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with immediate subsequent high-entropy payloads or shell commands in request bodies.

suggestion.title: SSH and Telnet brute-force attacks with credential stuffing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After finding a target, the malware attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials, detects the CPU architecture, and deploys a compatible C0XMO binary.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/Telnet login failures from single source against multiple accounts or devices within 5-minute window. Look for password attempts using common weak credentials (admin/admin, root/root). Combine with successful login immediately after brute-force series.

suggestion.title: Suspicious persistence mechanisms: hidden cron jobs and shell startup modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once it gains access to a device, the malware copies itself to hidden locations such as '/tmp/.sys,' '/var/tmp/.sys,' and '/dev/shm/.sys,' and then creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes. Also, shell startup files are modified to enable automatic execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron job creation with 15-minute intervals, especially in .sys or hidden directories. Alert on modifications to shell startup files (.bashrc, .profile, .zshrc) adding execution of binaries from /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm. Correlate with new file creation in those hidden paths.

suggestion.title: Detection of rival botnet and security tool termination
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'C0XMO actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients on the host, as well as red-team tools, programming tools, and network services that may interfere with its operation, and terminates them. It does so by deleting binaries and removing their persistence mechanisms.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk process termination of known botnet binaries, security scanners (nmap), or penetration testing tools (Metasploit) from a single process within 2 minutes. Correlate with immediate removal of cron jobs and init scripts for those same binaries.

suggestion.title: Python scanning framework deployment with network reconnaissance packages
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'For wider distribution, C0XMO downloads a Python script that installs additional packages such as 'requests,' 'paramiko,' and 'beautifulsoup4,' which are required for network scanning and communication, and for running activities over SSH and telnet protocols.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python execution with pip/conda installing paramiko (SSH library), beautifulsoup4 (HTML parsing), and requests (HTTP library) sequentially. Correlate with prior network scanning activity and subsequent SSH/Telnet connection attempts. High confidence when combined with hidden file creation.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Privilege Escalation via cgroups v1 release_agent
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2022-0492 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature' and categorizes it as 'improper authentication' enabling privilege escalation; pipeline generated zero use cases for this core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to cgroups v1 release_agent paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /sys/fs/cgroup/*/notify_on_release). Alert on process privilege transitions that correlate with cgroup subsystem access, or execution of child processes spawned from release_agent callbacks with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Exploitation Signature — Kernel cgroups Handler Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'actively leveraged' exploitation but pipeline identified no behavioral or signature-based detections; missing hunting logic for actual exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation patterns: unauthorized writes to release_agent config files by non-root processes, kernel audit failures (audit_log entries for cgroup2_restricted operations), or spawning of shell/binary execution from within cgroup namespace boundaries—all indicative of CVE-2022-0492 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance — cgroups v1 Vulnerability Probing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must enumerate kernel cgroup version and feature support; article identifies cgroups v1 as the vulnerable configuration but pipeline detected zero reconnaissance-phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process activity reading cgroup capability indicators: /proc/cgroups enumeration, /sys/fs/cgroup directory listing with unusual frequency, or execution of 'cat /proc/cmdline | grep cgroup' patterns. Flag systematic probing of cgroup version (v1 vs v2) on systems running vulnerable kernel versions.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Password Reset Endpoint Request Volume
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' enabled unauthorized data access. Exploit would require multiple requests to the reset endpoint; detecting bulk/anomalous reset requests could catch ongoing exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious password reset endpoint patterns: request volume >95th percentile for a 5-minute window, requests lacking typical user context (no referrer, non-human user-agent, scripted patterns), or >3 distinct password reset attempts for same account within 1 hour. Normal password resets are low-velocity and user-initiated.

suggestion.title: Sensitive PII in Password Reset Response Body
suggestion.rationale: Article details the flaw 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers'—indicating the vulnerable endpoint returned excessive PII in response payloads. Detection must flag when authentication endpoints leak personally identifiable data in responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password reset, account recovery, and credential verification endpoints for responses containing unredacted PII fields (phone numbers, full email addresses, birthdates). Expected behavior returns opaque tokens or confirmation-only responses. Any response body matching regex for full-format phone/email from reset endpoints is a data exposure indicator.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Account Recovery Completion
suggestion.rationale: Logic bugs in password reset flows often allow attackers to reset accounts for users they don't own. Article mentions high-profile targets were affected; detect successful password resets from anomalous request sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag password reset completion (successful reset confirmation) when preceded by atypical reset requests: originating from IP not previously associated with account, from unusual geography relative to user's baseline, or completed without user email confirmation received. Correlate with subsequent login from new device within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Precursor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'These emails do not contain malicious links or attachments and instead serve as a precursor for follow-up phone calls.' Pipeline missed detection for benign invoice-themed phishing designed to trigger outbound calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect invoice-themed emails from external consumer accounts followed by outbound calls within minutes. Monitor for caller ID spoofing or caller claiming to be corporate IT. Correlate email sender domain with absence of internal infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Tool Installation via Remote Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'During these sessions, the threat actors trick the target into installing remote monitoring and management tools such as AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps.' Pipeline missed execution chain from Teams/Zoom/Quick Assist parent to these tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps installation or execution with parent process being remote session tool (Teams, Zoom, Quick Assist, mstsc.exe). Flag unsigned or unsigned-by-vendor installation. Monitor for command-line silent install parameters.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Document Repository Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once inside a network, the group searches for sensitive legal and financial documents...The attackers commonly target document management platforms and cloud storage repositories.' Pipeline missed detection for bulk file system scanning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume file enumeration on document management platforms (ShareFile, SharePoint, Box, etc.) and cloud storage (OneDrive, Google Drive) within hours of network access. Flag searches for keywords: 'contract', 'acquisition', 'merger', 'tax', 'SSN'. Correlate with newly-installed remote access tools.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via WinSCP or Rclone
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attackers commonly target document management platforms and cloud storage repositories before exfiltrating the data using tools such as WinSCP or Rclone.' Pipeline missed both tool execution and exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WinSCP.exe or rclone.exe execution, especially with command-line arguments for remote server configuration or credential passing. Correlate with large outbound file transfers to non-corporate cloud providers or unknown IP addresses. Monitor for batch-mode or automation flags.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Registration for Impersonated IT Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Mandiant also discovered phishing domains tied to the campaign that impersonate internal IT portals using naming patterns such as: <organization>-itdesk[.]com, <organization>-it[.]com, <organization>-helpdesk[.]com.' Pipeline extracted zero domain-based IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS lookups and HTTP requests to newly-registered domains matching patterns: *-itdesk[.]com, *-it[.]com, *-helpdesk[.]com where domain does not match known internal IT infrastructure. Cross-check WHOIS age (< 30 days). Alert on SSL certificate mismatches to legitimate issuer.

suggestion.title: Fast-Flux DNS Infrastructure Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Resecurity said the group's "business-data-leaks[.]com" leak site and related infrastructure rely on residential proxy networks...across Latin America, Eastern Europe, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Asia.' Pipeline missed infrastructure-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single domain resolving to multiple IP addresses within short time window. Flag if resolved IPs are geographically diverse (multiple countries/regions), in residential IP ranges, or belong to different ASNs. Alert on rotations faster than typical CDN patterns. business-data-leaks[.]com should be blocked/monitored.

suggestion.title: Execution of Vulnerable FFmpeg Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg'—implies code-execution bugs exploitable via media files or direct invocation. Attackers will attempt to trigger vulnerable codec/filter combinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ffmpeg.exe or ffmpeg process creation with suspicious arguments (e.g., demux filters, unusual codecs, or -vf/-af chains known to trigger buffer overflows). Correlate with file-write and network-exfil events immediately following process termination with high CPU/memory usage.

suggestion.title: Chrome Crash Spikes from Unpatched Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'—implies widespread pre-patch crash-inducing bugs. Spike in Chrome crashes (WER, Event ID 1000) before patch date is an indicator of active exploitation or testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >3σ deviation in chrome.exe or msedge.exe crashes within a 1-hour window, especially if clustered to specific executable versions predating the patch date. Correlate with tab/extension load events to narrow exploit vector.

suggestion.title: Scanning for Vulnerable Software Versions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability disclosure creates a known-bad version window. Attackers or defenders alike will scan for hosts running FFmpeg <[patched version] or Chrome <[patched version].
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries or commands that enumerate software versions (e.g., 'wmic datafile where name contains ffmpeg', 'Get-ItemProperty' for Chrome version, port 5985/5986 WMI scans). Suspicious if from non-admin or external IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Media File Delivery Pre-Patch
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days exploit media parsing. Article mentions 21 zero-days, implying multiple attack surfaces. Expect targeted delivery of weaponized media files (MP4, MKV, WAV) during the patch-gap window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on media file delivery (.mp4, .mkv, .wav, .flac) from untrusted senders or unusual sources, especially if saved to %TEMP% or executable directories. Correlate with immediate ffmpeg invocation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Activity After FFmpeg/Chrome Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of client-side bugs (FFmpeg, Chrome) enables code execution in the context of the media player or browser process. Expect child-process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or network C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by ffmpeg.exe, chrome.exe, or edge.exe (especially with unusual parent-child relationships). Flag network connections to non-whitelisted C2 ranges initiated from these processes within seconds of process start.

suggestion.title: Patch-Gap Detection: Unpatched Chrome/FFmpeg Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states Chrome patched 429 bugs and FFmpeg has 21 zero-days. Defensive baseline: identify all hosts still running pre-patch versions after advisory date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily scan of Chrome (chrome.exe --version, registry: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Google\Chrome\Version) and FFmpeg installs (ffmpeg.exe -version, registry paths) against known-vulnerable versions. Flag any host with version < [patched build] more than 14 days post-advisory.

suggestion.title: Detect SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation via Network Volumetrics
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly identifies 'DoS Flaw' as actively exploited threat; pipeline generated zero network-based DoS detection use cases despite volumetric attacks being the canonical exploitation vector for denial-of-service vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic targeting Serv-U listening ports (22, 121, 135–139, 445 typical) for sustained traffic spikes, connection-per-second anomalies, or flood patterns (SYN floods, UDP floods). Alert on packet rates exceeding baseline by >3σ or malformed/fragmented packets within exploit windows.

suggestion.title: Monitor Serv-U Process Availability & Crash Patterns
suggestion.rationale: DoS vulnerability inherently targets service denial; title establishes 'actively exploited' status. Pipeline missed process-level impact detection (unexpected terminations, resource exhaustion, restart loops).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Serv-U process uptime and resource consumption. Alert on sudden process terminations, restart counts exceeding 3 within 5 minutes, sustained CPU >80%, memory leak patterns, or file-handle exhaustion. Correlate with DoS traffic for confidence.

suggestion.title: Detect Application-Layer Exploitation of Serv-U Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article signals actively exploited vulnerability; pipeline generated no application-layer detection logic. Full article likely contains CVE, version, and payload details for targeted IDS/IPS/WAF rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE ID disclosed in full article, create network signatures matching known exploit payloads. Monitor Serv-U access logs for anomalous HTTP methods, oversized requests, malformed protocol frames, path traversal sequences, or command injection attempts targeting vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Slowloris & Protocol-Layer DoS Against Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'DoS Flaw' but pipeline generated zero low-and-slow attack detection. Slowloris and HTTP/protocol-layer exploitation are common DoS vectors for file-transfer services not captured in volumetric-only signatures.
