suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained incomplete connections (half-open TCP handshakes, slow TLS negotiation), partial HTTP requests held open indefinitely, or keep-alive abuse. Alert on connection counts from single source far exceeding legitimate client patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Cisco SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20245 Flaw Actively Exploited' — this is the core attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface even a minimal detection for exploitation attempts against this known-exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager admin interfaces targeting known CVE-2026-20245 payload paths. Track suspicious authentication attempts or session initialization failures preceding successful connections. Correlate with external IP sources known for scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager controls network routing and policy; article context (no patch, active exploitation) implies attackers gain persistence via config manipulation. Pipeline did not propose monitoring for post-exploitation persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of new administrative users, privilege escalation of existing accounts, or out-of-band configuration changes to SD-WAN policies without corresponding change tickets. Monitor for configuration file exports or backups being staged for exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Compromised SD-WAN Manager (network backbone device) is a high-value pivot point for lateral movement across branch networks. Article implies active compromise; pipeline did not propose detection for post-exploitation lateral movement abuse of network access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager for initiating unexpected outbound connections to internal subnets outside its normal administrative scope. Flag attempts to establish tunnels or routes to previously unreachable network segments. Correlate with failed authentication attempts on internal assets.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Service Exploitation via Public-Facing Interface
suggestion.rationale: Title states vulnerability is 'Actively Exploited' and 'No Patch Available,' implying defenders must detect exploitation signatures. Pipeline did not propose behaviors or payloads to hunt for.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Cisco SD-WAN Manager web server access logs and application logs. Search for malformed request payloads, command injection patterns, or XML/JSON parser anomalies typical of deserialization attacks. Flag processes spawned by the SD-WAN Manager service with unexpected parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Installation on IoT / Smart TV Device
suggestion.rationale: Article mechanism: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs'—implies initial access via application deployment. Pipeline generated zero detection for unauthorized app installs or non-standard package sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV and IoT device package managers for apps installed from non-official app stores, apps with unusual permission requests (system calls, broad network access), or installation outside normal OTA update windows. Baseline allowed applications and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Elevated Outbound Connections from Smart TV Device
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'Web-Scraping Proxies' requires sustained high-volume outbound HTTP traffic. Pipeline failed to generate detection for anomalous smart TV egress patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline outbound connection count and destination diversity per smart TV. Alert on sustained elevation in request volume, spike in distinct external IPs contacted, or patterns consistent with scraping: rapid sequential requests, non-media destination domains (e.g., ecommerce, news, research sites), absence of interactive think-time between requests.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Device Relaying Traffic as Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'proxies'—detection should identify when device forwards third-party traffic rather than originating requests itself. Mismatched User-Agent, request headers, or timing signatures vs. device capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect proxy-like behavior: HTTP requests originating from smart TV IP with external User-Agent and browser fingerprints inconsistent with the device OS or model. Look for high-velocity identical requests (templated scraping) distributed across multiple external targets but routed through single internal smart TV IP.

suggestion.title: Bulk HTTP Scraping Behavior from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism is explicit: 'Web-Scraping.' Pipeline did not suggest detection for automated scraping signatures: rapid sequential requests to domains, robot.txt access, crawl patterns, stateless request sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on request sequences from smart TV matching scraping behavior: GET requests to /robots.txt followed by crawl of site structure; rapid requests to same domain (>10 per second); identical or low-variance User-Agent over hours; no interactive delays (human-like think-time); sequential resource enumeration (page?id=1, page?id=2). Use volume and entropy baselines per external domain.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Communication from Infected Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Scraped data must exfiltrate to 'AI' operators per article. Pipeline generated zero detection for outbound C2 channels, data aggregation endpoints, or operator infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains/IPs operated by threat actor for command-and-control. Monitor smart TV DNS queries and connections to these infrastructure endpoints. Detect encrypted tunnels (TLS to non-standard ports), payload compression, or covert channels used to evade inspection and exfiltrate scraped datasets.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance and Content Scraping Targeting High-Value Domains
suggestion.rationale: 'Scraping for AI' implies targeting specific high-value content (research, proprietary, paywalled). Pipeline should detect reconnaissance: DNS enumeration, HEAD requests, 403/401 probing followed by bypass attempts or credential spray.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance activity from smart TV IPs: DNS queries for target domains before HTTP access, rapid HEAD/OPTIONS requests to multiple paths on target domain, response codes suggesting authentication bypass (301/302 chains), or requests with manipulated headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP) to spoof origin. Correlate with outbound data flows to indicate exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Suspicious App Installation — Proxy Ecosystem
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku...have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices into a commercial residential proxy network.' Initial access vector requires detection of proxy-related or unsigned apps installing on smart TV platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of apps related to proxy services (luminati, bright-data, brdtnet domains in app manifests/stores) or unsigned/third-party app installs on Samsung/LG/Roku devices. Flag rapid app installs or installs immediately post-device-firmware-update.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Network Connections to Known Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes devices 'scrape web data for AI training' via enrollment into 'commercial residential proxy network' operating through domains like proxyjs.brdtnet.com, luminati.io, bright-sdk.com. Exfiltration vector requires network IOC detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network connections from smart TV devices or TV-specific processes to known proxy service domains (luminati.io, bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, proxyjs.*, clientsdk.* subdomains). Correlate with absence of user-initiated VPN/proxy settings. Context: high volume sustained connections to these IPs despite lack of device-side proxy configuration suggest unauthorized proxy enrollment.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Background Process or Network Activity Outside User Intent
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes apps 'quietly enrolling' and 'secretly turning' devices into proxies, suggesting hidden background persistence. Devices act as proxies 'all through a consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation,' indicating user cannot easily disable activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect smart TV app processes maintaining network activity (DNS queries, HTTP/HTTPS connections to proxy infrastructure) during inactive user sessions (no remote input, screen off, or app backgrounded). Flag file modifications in app config directories that enable auto-start behavior or network connectivity permissions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Data Volume from Smart TV Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'scraping web data for AI training' via enrolled devices. Impact is continuous unauthorized data exfiltration through proxy network, measurable as abnormal bandwidth consumption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical outbound traffic volume and pattern for smart TV devices by make/model/firmware. Alert on sustained outbound bandwidth consumption 2-3× baseline, especially if correlated with connections to proxy infrastructure domains or during non-viewing hours. Scraping typically manifests as high HTTP/HTTPS request volume with short response latencies.

suggestion.title: Deceptive Consent Dialog Exploitation on Smart TV Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Attack relies on 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation,' exploiting UX constraints of smart TV interfaces to hide enrollment into proxy service. Platform-specific attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV app manifests and runtime telemetry for overly complex permission dialogs, permission requests with confusing or abbreviated explanations, or permissions buried under multiple navigation layers. Cross-reference apps requiring 'Network' and 'Device ID' permissions simultaneously with no obvious user-facing use case for both.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Commit to GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes worm targeting 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories—no detection for malicious commits introduced to repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for commits introducing suspicious code patterns: encoded payloads, command execution, lateral movement enumeration, or persistence mechanisms. Correlate commits from new/unknown accounts or at unusual times with repository access logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub API Token Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise implies account or token abuse; no detection for abnormal GitHub API calls or token misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls from non-organizational IP ranges, mass repository enumeration, unexpected personal access token creation, or token authentication from previously unseen locations. Cross-reference against VPN/proxy baseline.

suggestion.title: Repository Access from Anomalous Source
suggestion.rationale: Worm targeting 73 repos implies attacker repo access; no detection for out-of-baseline access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository access logs for login from non-corporate IP ranges, impossible-travel logins, or bulk repository cloning/access. Alert if single account or IP accesses >5 Microsoft-owned repositories in short time window.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution via Downloaded GitHub Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm distribution; no detection for execution of downloaded/cloned payloads from repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with parent git.exe or similar clone tools, execution of scripts/binaries from .git directories, or process command lines referencing GitHub URLs or repository names. Monitor for wscript.exe, powershell.exe, or cmd.exe spawned from downloaded artifacts.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Takeover via Suspicious Auth Events
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack on Microsoft repos implies developer account compromise; no detection for auth anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed followed by successful GitHub authentication, 2FA bypass attempts, new device/location login, PAT creation by unusual accounts, or session hijacking patterns. Correlate with Azure AD/Entra login anomalies for Microsoft-affiliated accounts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Repository Push
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often exfiltrate sensitive data; no detection for unusual repository push activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large/unusual commits to repositories (size anomaly), commits containing credential patterns (keys, tokens, passwords), or pushes to repositories outside Microsoft's org baseline. Monitor for deletion of audit logs or repository settings changes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Disabling or Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' following compromise—pipeline missed clear impact detection for mass repository state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single principal disables or deletes >10 repositories within 1 hour, especially when preceded by unusual GitHub Actions execution or Azure service principal activity.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Action Execution from Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is GitHub Actions—'Azure Functions Action' specifically mentioned as compromised artifact injecting payload into dependent repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflow jobs that invoke external actions with unexpected network calls, fetch payloads, or deploy to Azure infrastructure without documented authorization.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions Deployment from Unexpected Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Azure Functions Action'—malware leverages GitHub Actions to deploy code to Azure Functions runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure Functions deployments triggered by GitHub Actions workflows; alert on deployments with unusual source IPs, missing change documentation, or non-standard authentication paths.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Poisoning: Dependency or Action Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply chain attack infecting 72+ repositories—infrastructure suggesting injected dependencies or compromised action YAML manifests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare workflow YAMLs, package manifests across repositories for unexpected new step additions, suspicious action versions, or newly-referenced external registries not in baseline.

suggestion.title: Malware Artifact Detection: Miasma Worm
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Miasma Worm' as the malware family—should trigger malware signature and behavioral detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create Yara/SIGMA rules for Miasma indicators; monitor for file I/O, process creation, or registry artifacts matching Miasma signatures, especially in CI/CD runner environments.

suggestion.title: Service Principal or Token Creation Outside Provisioning Windows
suggestion.rationale: Attackers likely persisted via new Azure service principals or GitHub PATs to maintain access to disabled repositories and Azure infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service principal creation in Azure, managed identity assumption role changes, or new GitHub personal access tokens created outside change-control windows or with non-standard expiry.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation from Non-Authenticated Source
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' — the attack vector is installation of the malicious package. Any victim installing the compromised version is initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install commands and Python package imports for 'durabletask'. Flag installation of versions released around compromise date. Correlate package installation with subsequent unexpected child process spawning or network connections.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawned by Python Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages execute malicious code on import/use. Article describes package injection — should trigger on suspicious subprocess execution from python.exe or python3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget) spawned by python.exe within 5 seconds of package import or Python script execution. Prioritize if parent is running in user temp directories or site-packages.

suggestion.title: Network Outbound Connections from Python Process to Suspicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware typically establishes C2 communication. Should detect outbound network activity from Python interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from python.exe/python3 to IPs not in org whitelist, especially: newly-registered domains (<30 days), non-HTTPS ports from Python, or IPs resolved from free DynDNS services.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Written to Python Site-Packages Directory
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise modifies or injects files into installed package locations. Should trigger on unexpected modifications to site-packages/durabletask/.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification in Python site-packages directories, especially: .pyc/.pyo compiled bytecode, .so/.pyd binary extensions, or __pycache__ outside normal install windows. Flag if timestamp precedes known package release date.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Eval/Exec from Imported Package
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages often use dynamic code execution primitives. Should detect Python eval(), exec(), or __import__() called with suspicious arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If EDR supports Python hooking: alert on eval/exec/compile called with base64-encoded or obfuscated strings. If not: flag python -c arguments containing unusual imports or shell command execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Compromised Package Version Installed on Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title states specific package 'durabletask' was compromised. Version tracking of installed packages is foundational supply-chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically enumerate installed Python packages via 'pip list' or site-packages inventory. Match against known-compromised versions from threat feeds (CVE/GHSA advisories for durabletask). Alert if compromised version found on any endpoint.

suggestion.title: Malware Copies Self to Hidden Temporary Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'copies itself to hidden locations such as /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, and /dev/shm/.sys' — direct persistence indicator with no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of files with dotted names (.sys) or paths in /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm combined with executable permissions and root/system ownership. High confidence if followed by cron job creation or shell startup file modification.

suggestion.title: Cron Job Creation with 15-Minute Relaunch Interval
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes' — explicit persistence mechanism completely missed despite being trivially detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor crontab modifications and /etc/cron.d/ file creation. Alert on cron entries with */15 pattern (every 15 minutes) or similar short intervals, especially executing hidden binaries in /tmp or /var/tmp. Cross-correlate with suspicious process creation and shell script execution.

suggestion.title: Malware Process Enumerates and Terminates Rival Botnets and Security Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients on the host, as well as red-team tools, programming tools, and network services' and 'terminates them' — defense evasion via selective process killing completely absent from detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of /proc (ps, cat /proc/[pid]/exe) followed by selective killing of known security tools, development tools, or botnet identifiers using kill/pkill/killall. High severity if from non-standard service, followed by process termination events, and correlated with file creation in hidden paths.

suggestion.title: SSH and Telnet Brute-Force Credential Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents scanner 'attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials' with functions for 'SSH/telenet login' — no detection use case for ports 22 and 23 credential attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 10+ failed SSH/Telnet authentication attempts from single source IP or process within 60 seconds. Elevated severity if from internal network, non-standard service account, or correlated with network scanning and process enumeration activity.

suggestion.title: Network Scanning on Multiple Well-Known Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies scanner 'randomly scan internet-facing systems on common ports like 22 (SSH), 23 (Telnet), 80/443 (HTTP/HTTPS), 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888, and others' — no detection for port sweep behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process opening multiple connections to sequential IP addresses on known service ports (22, 23, 80, 443, 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888) within short timeframe (>50 connections in 5 min). Anomaly if from non-network-admin process or suspicious parent executable. High confidence combined with process enumeration.

suggestion.title: Python Execution Installing Botnet Scanner Dependencies (paramiko, beautifulsoup4, requests)
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'downloads a Python script that installs additional packages such as requests, paramiko, and beautifulsoup4' for network scanning — execution of Python with botnet-associated libraries generating zero detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python execution (python/python3) with pip install or import statements for paramiko (SSH automation), beautifulsoup4 (web scraping), and requests (HTTP client) together. High severity if from /tmp, unusual parent process, or correlated with network scanning, process enumeration, and hidden file creation.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent file modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'cgroups v1 release_agent feature'—exploitation involves writing malicious commands to release_agent files under /sys/fs/cgroup/. Critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent. Alert on modifications from non-root processes. Correlate with subsequent command execution to identify exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Kernel privilege escalation—suspicious cgroup syscall sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively leveraged'—need behavioral detection for cgroup manipulation patterns preceding privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged processes executing rapid cgroup-related syscalls (mount, write to cgroup interfaces) followed by privilege escalation to root. Flag transition patterns typical of CVE-2022-0492 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Container escape—host access from containerized process
suggestion.rationale: Cgroups v1 vulnerabilities are primary container-to-host escape vectors. Article does not explicitly mention containers but this is the dominant attack surface for this CVE in production.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container-spawned processes accessing /sys/fs/cgroup or host filesystem. Alert when container process crosses namespace boundaries or spawns host-level child processes.

suggestion.title: Persistence—release_agent-based command execution
suggestion.rationale: Release_agent files execute automatically when cgroups release. Attackers weaponize this for persistence but article does not detail this vector—detection necessary for real-world attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect release_agent files containing executable payloads or suspicious script paths. Alert on unexpected process spawning from cgroup release events or release_agent pointing to known backdoor signatures.

suggestion.title: Password Reset Request Spike / Account Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' — attackers can enumerate which email/phone combinations exist and may generate unusual request volumes to discover valid accounts before the fix.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password reset endpoint for abnormal request rates, high cardinality in submitted email/phone identifiers, or requests from a single source targeting many different accounts. Baseline normal reset traffic and alert on 3-5x spikes or requests with atypical parameter patterns.

suggestion.title: Unredacted PII in Authentication Response
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers' in the reset flow — password reset responses should never contain full contact information. Detect responses that leak PII that should be masked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect password reset endpoint responses for full email addresses or 10-digit phone numbers in plaintext. Establish baseline of responses that contain any PII and alert on deviations from expected masking patterns (e.g., standard should show ****.****@example.com).

suggestion.title: Account Access Anomaly Post-Password-Reset
suggestion.rationale: If attackers enumerate valid accounts via the flaw and harvest contact info, they will attempt login shortly after. Article notes high-profile accounts were exposed, making account takeover a credible follow-on attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate password reset requests with successful login events in a <30-minute window from anomalous geolocations, devices, or IPs not previously associated with the account. Prioritize resets for known VIP/high-value accounts.

suggestion.title: Exploit of Public-Facing Web Application / Password Reset Logic Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' — this is a direct T1190 exploitation scenario where the web app's authentication mechanism is bypassed to leak PII.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password reset endpoint for request sequences that violate state-machine assumptions: e.g., submitting reset step N without completing step N-1, reusing reset tokens, or submitting invalid/malformed parameters that bypass validation logic. Baseline expected request paths and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: PII Gathering via Credential Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw 'exposes user emails and phone numbers' — this directly enables T1589 (Gather Victim Identity Information) for reconnaissance, phishing, or social engineering follow-up attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-disclosure, monitor for phishing campaigns or SMS messages targeting email/phone combinations harvested from the Instagram flaw. Correlate exposed account identifiers with inbound phishing/smishing attempts. Watch for bulk email enumeration or verification queries.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Remote Code Execution Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg'—implies RCE / arbitrary code execution surface. Pipeline generated zero kill-chain phases and zero use cases despite this being the core attack vector. T1190/T1203 exploitation techniques entirely absent from output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg process spawning with suspicious arguments (e.g., filter chains, codec invocation), child process spawning (shell/cmd), or file write operations outside expected directories. Detect attempts to feed malformed or oversized media files that trigger parser crashes or memory corruption.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Exploitation via Patched Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'—signals widespread pre-patch exploitation window. Zero browser exploitation use cases generated. T1203 (Exploitation for Client Execution) canonical for browser vulns, not mapped in kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Chrome child process spawning (especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe), unusual memory access patterns, or tab crashes preceded by malicious script execution. Detect attempts to delay or disable auto-update mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Attack via Malicious Media Delivery
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days + Chrome patches indicate convergence on media processing attack surface. Article frames AI discovery (suggesting active researcher disclosure) but no initial-access or delivery use cases. T1566.001 (phishing attachment), T1189 (drive-by download) not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of media files (MP4, WAV, AVI, etc.) from atypical sources, especially within 7 days post-patch release. Monitor for file creation in temp directories followed by FFmpeg/Chrome invocation. Correlate with email phishing indicators if delivery vector mentioned.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Actively Exploited SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Flaw' — no detection logic for exploitation vectors against this product was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U service ports (22, 3074) for malformed requests, payload anomalies, or CVE-specific exploit signatures. Flag connection attempts containing known DoS payload patterns or version-specific vulnerability exploits.

suggestion.title: Denial of Service Attack Impact on Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies this as a 'DoS Flaw'—detection for impact phase (service unavailability, resource exhaustion) was omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process availability, network connection counts, and service responsiveness. Alert on sudden service crashes, elevated connection rates exceeding baseline, or sustained unresponsiveness consistent with DoS impact.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Process Anomalies After Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: DoS exploitation causes service degradation or crashes—post-exploitation process behavior baseline missing from detection output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish Serv-U process baseline (CPU, memory, crash frequency). Alert on repeated process terminations, abnormal memory spikes, or high CPU sustained >threshold during exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-20245 is 'actively exploited'; this is the primary attack vector and must be detected at application layer. No use case was generated despite being the headline threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager web interfaces for requests matching known CVE-2026-20245 exploit signatures, parameter injection attempts, and payload patterns consistent with exploitation of the vulnerable endpoint.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20245 exploitation grant remote code execution on manager appliance; article states actively exploited, implying attackers execute commands post-breach to establish foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual processes spawned from SD-WAN Manager service (Java/Tomcat context), shell interpreter execution, reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, ifconfig), or reverse shell connections.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Lateral Movement via Policy Injection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised manager orchestrates WAN policies across branch devices; attackers can inject policies to pivot to managed infrastructure and establish persistence across the SD-WAN fabric.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager API logs for policy deployment commands to branch devices outside change windows. Correlate with authentication anomalies on branch appliances following policy pushes from compromised manager.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Credential and Encryption Key Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Manager appliances store branch device credentials, symmetric encryption keys, and WAN topology secrets; article emphasizes active exploitation, suggesting attacker motive for credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk exports of SD-WAN configuration databases, enumeration of vault/key storage APIs, access to credential stores, or extraction of encryption material from manager persistent storage.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Command-and-Control Persistence and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Successful breach of network management platform enables persistent C2 channel and exfiltration of WAN topology, policies, and operational intelligence across managed branch network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from SD-WAN Manager to external IPs outside approved management ranges. Track DNS queries for C2 domains and large data transfers exfiltrating configuration or topology data.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Everest Forms Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account'. Detection should trigger on admin account creation events immediately following form submissions to vulnerable plugin endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for wp_insert_user() function invocations in WordPress execution logs or database logs within the Everest Forms plugin context, particularly those creating users with role='administrator'. Correlate timing with HTTP form submissions to vulnerable endpoints. Flag any account creation with username patterns observed in exploitation (diksimarina, variants).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Injection in Form Submission Fields
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability is in Complex Calculation feature where 'user input is passed through sanitize_text_field() function, which does not escape single quotes (') or other characters that influence PHP syntax'. Attackers inject code by submitting 'values that begin with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on form submissions to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms-pro/ endpoints containing payload patterns: leading single quote followed by PHP function calls (wp_insert_user, system, exec, shell_exec, eval), especially with closing comment markers (// or #). Baseline: legitimate form data should not contain PHP keywords.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts from Known Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two primary source IPs: '202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26' and states 'Wordfence's report provides several offending IP addresses' with Wordfence blocking 'over 29,300 attempts' starting April 13, 2026.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block inbound traffic from IPs 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26. Alert on HTTP requests from these sources to any WordPress Everest Forms endpoints. Track attack volume and payload variations per source IP to identify infrastructure reuse or expansion.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Everest Forms Pro Plugin Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The security issue affects versions 1.9.12 and earlier' and 'the Everest Forms developer released a patch...on March 18'. Plugin version enumeration enables proactive blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan WordPress sites for Everest Forms Pro plugin presence and version via HTTP response headers, readme.txt parsing, or database queries. Flag any version ≤1.9.12 as exploitable. Alert on first-seen vulnerable plugin versions or downgrades.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Account Creation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Wordfence report states the attacker 'calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account with the username 'diksimarina''. Article recommends defenders 'review administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (via database audit logs, wp-admin API logs, or Wordfence alerts) for new admin-role accounts. Flag any created during or immediately after form submission peaks. Specifically alert on creation of usernames matching known attacker patterns (diksimarina, similar entropy/style).

suggestion.title: eval() Function Calls in Everest Forms Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states the plugin 'executes the resulting code using PHP's 'eval()' function'. Detection should identify eval() invocations with unsanitized or attacker-controlled input passed directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument or monitor PHP execution within Everest Forms plugin (especially Complex Calculation feature) to detect eval() calls. Baseline: legitimate eval() usage should be minimal/predictable. Alert on eval() with variables derived from HTTP request parameters (GET, POST, headers).

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTPS Egress to Non-Whitelisted Hosts from Smart TV Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article states apps act as 'web-scraping proxies'—requires sustained outbound HTTPS connections to scraping targets. Pipeline did not map exfiltration/C&C behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained HTTPS traffic from Smart TV streaming/media apps to non-CDN, non-ISP-affiliated destination IPs, especially with connection patterns consistent with proxy behavior (rapid sequential connects to diverse targets, repeated connections to same IP across multiple days).

suggestion.title: App Installation from Third-Party or Unsigned Sources on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector requires distributing malicious 'free apps'—pipeline missed initial-access detections for out-of-band app delivery or compromised app-store apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag app installations on Smart TVs sourced from unofficial app stores, sideload vectors, or apps with unsigned/mismatched publisher certificates. Alert on media apps requesting excessive network/system permissions relative to functional baseline.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Automated HTTP Requests from Single Smart TV to News/Content Sites
suggestion.rationale: Core attack is 'web-scraping'—requires bulk HTTP requests to public content. Pipeline did not detect collection-phase indicators (T1005).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained, high-frequency HTTP GET requests from a single Smart TV to news aggregators, e-commerce, or media sites with characteristics inconsistent with user browsing (identical User-Agent across thousands of requests, requests without typical browser headers, sequential page-index traversal, off-hours timing).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Streaming/Media Application Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Malicious apps must spawn shell, curl, python, or node.js processes to execute scraping logic. Pipeline did not map execution-phase behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes (curl, wget, bash, python, node.js) spawned by media app executables, especially with command-line arguments indicating web requests or file I/O. Baseline legitimate subprocesses per app and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Sudden Traffic Pattern Shift Indicating Proxy Conversion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Smart TVs 'turned into proxies'—this behavioral shift should be detectable via traffic volume/destination diversity anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline outbound traffic from Smart TVs (typically CDN/streaming-service destinations). Alert on sudden shift to unrelated destination IP diversity, burst connection counts unrelated to user-triggered events, or connection timing inconsistent with video playback.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Permission Grants and Dormant UI with Active Network I/O
suggestion.rationale: Malicious apps must request network access and may remain backgrounded with minimal UI activity while scraping. Pipeline did not surface permission-based or dormancy indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect apps granted network/system permissions post-install without corresponding user interaction (no app launch events, no UI rendering). Correlate permission grants with subsequent sustained network I/O and absence of expected app functionality logs.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Proxy Infrastructure Domains and IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free apps...have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices into a commercial residential proxy network.' IOCs listed: proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io, bright-sdk.com, 3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114. Pipeline failed to generate this use case despite the article recommending it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify smart TV devices or residential IPs establishing connections to known proxy infrastructure domains and IPs. Flag persistent outbound connections on typical proxy ports (80, 443, 8080, 3128). Correlate DNS queries to proxy domains with subsequent network traffic to establish beaconing patterns.

suggestion.title: Smart TV App Installation with Proxy-Related Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku...quietly enrolling...devices.' This is supply-chain initial access. Pipeline missed detection of malicious app installation phase with network permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor installation of free apps on smart TV platforms with elevated network permissions. Detect apps requesting 'Network & Internet' or 'System Proxy' permissions without clear functional justification. Flag rapid adoption of same app across multiple households in short time window.

suggestion.title: Deceptive Consent Dialog Preceding Network Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' Pipeline missed the social-engineering vector — detection of deliberate UX obfuscation preceding proxy enrollment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid remote-control navigation sequences (bypassing or obscuring menu navigation) on smart TV with immediate subsequent DNS/proxy requests to infrastructure domains. Detect navigation patterns inconsistent with typical user behavior (too fast, non-random arrow sequences).

suggestion.title: Persistent Proxy Beaconing from Smart TV Device
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'devices...into a commercial residential proxy network used to scrape web data.' Pipeline missed persistence detection — apps maintaining long-lived C2 connections post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV apps initiating periodic outbound connections to proxy infrastructure domains with consistent timing and payload size. Detect beaconing patterns (e.g., connection attempt every 30-60 seconds) from residential device IPs to brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, bright-sdk.com on proxy-typical ports.

suggestion.title: Residential IP Address Proxy Abuse Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'scrape web data for AI training all through...dialog...enrolled...into a commercial residential proxy network.' Pipeline missed detection of the exfiltration phase — traffic patterns consistent with residential proxy abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Residential device IPs making rapid sequential requests to diverse unrelated domains, elevated request volume inconsistent with TV usage patterns, or User-Agent strings indicating automated scraping. Detect reverse-proxy behavior (inbound requests proxied through residential IP) originating from smart TV devices.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Utility App with Hidden Proxy Functionality
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free apps' with hidden enrollment mechanism. Pipeline missed defense-evasion detection of benign-looking apps executing proxy services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apps with innocuous names/icons (Weather, Clock, Clock, Utilities) that declare proxy, network bridging, or HTTP client capabilities in manifest. Detect silent apps (no user interaction for hours) followed by sudden outbound network activity to proxy domains on proxy ports.

suggestion.title: Repository Bulk Disable or Deletion After Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' following compromise—bulk disablement is a post-exploitation action indicative of attacker cleanup or defensive remediation. Pipeline missed this impact pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid, sequential repository disable/delete events affecting multiple repositories in a single organization within a narrow timeframe. Alert if >5 repos disabled in <1 hour by a single account, especially if account is service-linked or previously dormant.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Injection into High-Value Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Azure Functions Action' compromise—this is workflow manipulation. Detection must catch unauthorized .github/workflows modifications that introduce new steps or exfiltration logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new or modified .github/workflows/*.yml files in high-value repositories (Microsoft orgs, AI/ML projects) that add previously-unseen external action calls (especially to unvetted registries), invoke shell commands downloading from unusual domains, or execute environment variable exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Stolen PAT or OAuth Token Used for Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack targeting 'AI Coding Agents' implies credential compromise. Article does not explicitly name the attack vector, but compromising service accounts or developer credentials is the most probable initial access for bulk repository manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Personal Access Token or OAuth token usage from unusual geographies, unusual times of day, or IPs not previously associated with the account. Flag token creation immediately followed by bulk repository access or modification events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Commit or Push to Critical Supply Chain Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromise of Microsoft's own 'Azure Functions Action' repository—this is a commit/push attack on a production artifact. Pipeline should flag commits injecting malicious code into action.yml or wrapper scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits to action.yml, package.json, or lib/index.js in action repositories that modify download URLs, add inline shell/Python execution, or obfuscate code. Flag commits from newly-provisioned or previously-inactive accounts committing to protected branches without PR review.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack: Widespread Simultaneous Targeting of AI/ML Tooling Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack 'targeting AI Coding Agents'—this is a coordinated supply-chain campaign. Pipeline should reconstruct the scope: 73 repositories, unified attack vector, common victim profile (AI agent frameworks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate repository compromise events across multiple orgs targeting repositories tagged with AI, ML, automation, or agent keywords. Alert if >3 such repositories are compromised within 24 hours with overlapping attacker account infrastructure (same IP, API key, commit email domain).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration or Exposure of Source Code via GitHub Release or Download Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on coding agents often exfiltrate source or inject backdoors into published artifacts (releases, npm packages, PyPI). Article does not detail the exfiltration mechanism, but this is a critical missing detection for understanding impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new release artifacts published to npm, PyPI, or GitHub Releases from compromised repositories. Flag if release creation follows unauthorized push/commit events, if artifact size dramatically increases, or if artifact is downloaded from unusual external IPs immediately after publication.

suggestion.title: PyPI Supply Chain Compromise – Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' establishes the attack vector; a supply chain compromise is useless if we cannot detect when the malicious package is installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip install, import, or requirement file updates targeting durabletask. Alert on installation of affected versions; correlate with parent process identity and execution context to establish install source.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Imported Package
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'compromised' package; injected malware would execute commands post-import. Expected payload behavior not detailed in provided article body but typical for PyPI compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from Python interpreter or durabletask module import, especially curl/wget/PowerShell/cmd.exe or scripts written to temp directories. Establish baseline of legitimate children first.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via Supply Chain Package
suggestion.rationale: High-severity compromises typically include data exfiltration; article context suggests credential harvesting but specifics not visible in truncated body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python processes accessing credential stores (Windows Credential Manager, browser profiles, ~/.ssh), environment variables, or cloud API endpoints. Correlate timing with durabletask import.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Communication from Python/durabletask
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain payloads establish C2 or data exfiltration channels; article does not detail domains/IPs, indicating pipeline failed to extract them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual outbound connections from Python processes using durabletask to non-standard ports, newly registered domains, or IP ranges associated with threat infrastructure. Baseline legitimate outbound traffic first.

suggestion.title: Package Version Anomaly – Yanked or Out-of-Sequence Release
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often inject versions with gaps in release history or reuse of old version numbers. Article title confirms compromise but version details missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip logs and PyPI metadata for unexpected version installations of durabletask—especially yanked releases, versions with abnormal gaps from previous releases, or versions that re-appear after withdrawal. Cross-reference against known-good version timeline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 DD-WRT Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states C0XMO 'was delivered by exploiting CVE-2021-27137, a buffer overflow vulnerability caused by insufficient user input...leads to executing arbitrary code.' This is the primary attack vector and requires no inference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to internet-facing DD-WRT instances containing large stack payloads or shellcode patterns. Correlate with unexpected spawning of high-privilege processes on router/HTTPD after exploit attempt.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Persistence via 15-Minute Cron Relaunch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes' after copying binaries to hidden paths. The specific 15-minute interval and hidden directory patterns are detectable behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new cron entries (crontab, /etc/cron.d) pointing to executables in /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, or /dev/shm/.sys with recurring 15-minute intervals. Cross-reference with file creation events for binaries in those directories.

suggestion.title: Rival Malware and Red-Team Tool Eradication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes C0XMO 'actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients, red-team tools, programming tools' and 'terminates them by deleting binaries and removing their persistence mechanisms, including cron jobs, init scripts, system services, and shell profile entries.' This is a distinct hostile-takeover behavioral pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid mass process terminations (3+ in 5 minutes) coupled with aggressive binary deletions from /tmp, /var, /dev/shm, followed by deletion of init.d scripts and cron jobs referencing those processes. Signature indicates malware self-preservation behavior.

suggestion.title: Python-Based Network Reconnaissance and Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: Article describes C0XMO downloading 'a Python script that installs additional packages such as requests, paramiko, beautifulsoup4' and uses 'worker threads to randomly scan internet-facing systems on common ports like 22, 23, 80/443, 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888' then 'attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials.' Port enumeration and tool chain are observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound scanning traffic from compromised host to bulk port list (22, 23, 80, 443, 7547, 8080+) across large IP ranges. Alert on Python process spawning with paramiko/beautifulsoup4, followed by SSH/Telnet authentication failures from same source in short time window.

suggestion.title: Shell Startup Modification for Malware Auto-Launch
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'shell startup files are modified to enable automatic execution' as secondary persistence mechanism complementing cron-based relaunch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to .bashrc, .bash_profile, .zshrc, /etc/profile, /etc/profile.d/ for injected commands spawning hidden executables or invoking scripts from /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, /dev/shm/.sys.

suggestion.title: Custom Multi-Stage C2 Handshake with Magic Strings
suggestion.rationale: Article describes C2 connection via 'custom multi-stage handshake that includes magic strings and shared secrets,' distinct from standard botnet C2 protocols and supporting 19 DDoS attack methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections from compromised IoT/router to rare external IPs using non-standard protocol. Analyze packet payloads for binary magic string sequences and multi-stage handshake patterns deviating from SSH/HTTP/DNS baselines.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature'—release_agent is the exploitation vector for code execution. Pipeline generated no behavioral detection for writes to this critical file.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes/modifications to cgroup release_agent paths (e.g., /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent, /proc/*/cgroup) from unprivileged processes. Flag executable binary placement in /tmp or /var/tmp immediately followed by cgroups pointer updates. Monitor for notify_on_release handler registration from non-root contexts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Cgroups Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article warns the vulnerability 'may allow attackers' to exploit cgroups—implicit privilege-escalation or container-escape capability. No use case captures the escalation pattern despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In containerized environments, detect unprivileged processes accessing cgroup subsystem followed by execve() with uid=0 or capability changes. Flag unshare(CLONE_NEWCGROUP) syscalls from container-spawned processes. Monitor for cgroup2 downgrade attempts or cgroup_attach syscalls from unexpected contexts.

suggestion.title: System Inventory — Vulnerable Linux Kernel with Cgroups v1
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks' but pipeline generated no hunt for exposed systems. Prerequisite detection is required to identify systems with CVE-2022-0492 exposure and establish baseline vulnerability surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query systems for kernel version < 5.13 with cgroups v1 enabled (no cgroups2 mount, or controllers in v1 hierarchy). Flag systems where reported kernel version via /proc/version differs from actual uname output. Correlate inventory with network exposure and container runtime presence.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection — Cgroups Release Agent Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active real-world exploitation but pipeline has no signature for the specific attack—writing shell commands or binaries to release_agent and triggering via cgroup destruction. This is the actual exploitation step missing from all generated use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file write operations that insert shell commands or executable references into cgroups v1 release_agent files. Monitor for process-creation chains where a non-root process writes to release_agent followed by destruction of a cgroup in the same hierarchy. Detect base64-encoded payloads or variable expansion in release_agent file content.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Password Reset Endpoint Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' exposed PII. An attacker exploiting this would trigger repeated requests to extract email/phone data. This access pattern is the primary indicator of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Instagram password reset endpoint for anomalous request patterns during vulnerability window (June 6, 2026 until hotfix deployment). Alert on >5 requests/min from single source, requests with account-enumeration payloads, or automated extraction patterns inconsistent with legitimate password resets.

suggestion.title: Phishing Targeting Exposed Instagram User Emails
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exposed 'unredacted email addresses' including high-profile individuals (CEO, celebrities). Downstream attackers would immediately weaponize this list for targeted credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exposed Instagram user email addresses (published June 6, 2026) with inbound phishing campaigns. Alert on spearphishing delivering fake Instagram login pages or OAuth-credential harvesters to known-exposed addresses, especially targeting high-profile accounts.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via SIM Swap on Exposed Phone Numbers
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'phone numbers' exposed for high-profile users including 'Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg'. Attackers would exploit exposed phone numbers for SIM-swap account takeover, triggering authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For phone numbers exposed June 6, 2026, monitor accounts for MFA delivery failures, new device registrations, or authentication from impossible locations. Alert on account access immediately following authentication anomalies tied to exposed phone-based 2FA.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Zero-Day Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg.' FFmpeg is widely deployed in media pipelines; zero-day window prior to patch is active exploit risk. Detection must monitor execution of FFmpeg with untrusted input (downloaded, streamed, or shared media).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FFmpeg process spawned with file arguments referencing downloads, temp directories, or network shares; or FFmpeg making outbound connections to non-standard ports. Baseline normal transcoding and alert on deviations, especially post-disclosure before widespread patching.

suggestion.title: Chrome Unpatched Version Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article states '429 Bugs' patched in Chrome release. Enterprise systems remain vulnerable until patch deployment. Detection must identify endpoints running pre-patch Chrome versions and correlate with active exploitation signals (web browsing, crash dumps).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: SoftwareInventory query: Chrome version < [disclosed patch version] AND (endpoint shows browser activity OR network connections to known exploit-hosting IPs). Flag for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Media Processing Untrusted-Input Execution
suggestion.rationale: Both FFmpeg and Chrome handle media from untrusted sources. Article scope (widespread zero-days) suggests media-processing supply chain is high-risk. Detection should flag process chains where media utilities spawn shells or network connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor parent process: web browser or file manager spawns ffmpeg/ffprobe/chrome with media file, followed by child process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, nc.exe). Correlate file-system writes to suspicious directories post-media-processing.

suggestion.title: Fuzzing Framework Execution on Non-Dev Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'AI Agent Uncovers' zero-days implies automated fuzzing/discovery. If threat actors replicate this capability on internal networks, detection must flag fuzzing frameworks (AFL, LibFuzzer, honggfuzz) on production/non-security-research systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execution of known fuzzing binaries or crash-analysis tools (gdb, afl-triage) outside whitelisted security labs. Monitor for systematic media-file mutations, crash dumps, or high-entropy input generation—signs of active vulnerability discovery.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw is 'actively exploited' — requires detection for exploitation attempts targeting vulnerable Serv-U instances. No use case provided despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U service ports (22, 3822) for abnormal access patterns, payload delivery, or exploitation signatures. Correlate with recent version fingerprinting or vulnerability scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Denial of Service Attack Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'DoS Flaw' as the vulnerability type — no detection use case created for DoS attack patterns targeting or resulting from exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect volumetric or protocol-based DoS patterns against Serv-U endpoints: sustained high-volume connections, TCP SYN floods, malformed packets, or connection exhaustion targeting service ports.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Serv-U Service Inventory and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: For active exploitation to occur, instances must be discovered and identified. Pipeline missed detection for Serv-U service presence and version enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Serv-U processes with vulnerable version strings. Detect port scanning or service enumeration targeting ports 22, 3822 combined with FTP service discovery behavior.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Unexpected Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation activity following successful DoS or remote code execution — article indicates active exploitation likely extends beyond simple DoS impacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from Serv-U service context: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32, or other execution utilities. Correlate with network connections from service account context.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Actively Exploited' — scanning and probing patterns should be monitored. Detection gap for initial-access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager (default port 8443) for HTTP requests with suspicious path traversal, injection, or authentication bypass patterns. Alert on unexpected status codes (500, 403) followed by reconnaissance-like GET requests from the same source IP. Cross-reference User-Agent strings against known exploit frameworks.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution Indicators on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation with no patch implies confirmed breaches. 'No Patch Available' extends dwell time. Missing detection for command execution post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Cisco SD-WAN Manager service accounts (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe from tomcat/cisco processes). Flag network connections from SD-WAN Manager to unusual external ports or domains. Monitor for file writes to web-accessible directories or system binaries.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager controls network routing policy; successful exploit likely enables network pivoting. Article does not address detection of lateral movement post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected network flows originating from the SD-WAN Manager host to internal infrastructure (e.g., domain controllers, backup systems, adjacent subnets). Flag changes to SD-WAN routing policies that redirect traffic outside normal baselines. Alert on SSH or RDP connections from the manager to systems it should not access.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Fingerprinting CVE-2026-20245
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation indicates attackers are actively scanning for vulnerable instances. Pipeline missed reconnaissance detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans targeting Cisco SD-WAN Manager (8443, 8444, and management IPs). Flag HTTP requests to known vulnerable endpoint paths (e.g., API routes or config pages) that return version strings or error messages. Correlate multiple probe attempts from the same source across different target IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Changes to SD-WAN Policies
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation likely followed by persistence through policy modification. Article omits detection for configuration tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to SD-WAN configuration files (typically in /opt/cisco-sdwan or Windows registry equivalents) outside change-control windows. Monitor audit logs for user account creation within the manager's local admin groups. Flag unexpected REST API calls to management endpoints that modify device policies.

suggestion.title: WordPress Administrator Account Creation via wp_insert_user()
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'attacker submits a value...followed by a PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account with the username diksimarina.' Defenders instructed to 'review administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress database for wp_insert_user() function calls or wp_users table insertions with role='administrator' outside normal admin panel workflows. Alert on usernames matching known malicious patterns (e.g., 'diksimarina'). Flag any administrator account creation within 5 seconds of form submission requests from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Injection via Unescaped Form Field Input
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sanitize_text_field() does not escape single quotes or other characters that influence PHP syntax. As a result, an attacker can close the intended string, inject arbitrary PHP code, and comment out the remaining generated code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints for payloads where form field values contain single quote (') immediately followed by PHP keywords/functions (wp_insert_user, system, eval, exec, echo, etc.). Alert on payloads containing comment markers (//) or (#) within calculation field values. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Complex Calculation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability: 'Complex Calculation feature, which accepts values submitted through form fields and inserts them into a PHP code string. Then, it executes the resulting code using PHP's eval() function.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to WordPress form endpoints where Complex Calculation features are active. Alert on submissions containing eval() syntax, PHP statements, string-escape sequences, or syntax-altering characters (single quotes, semicolons, comment markers). Establish baseline; Wordfence documented 29,300+ attempts indicating strong signal value.

suggestion.title: Attack Traffic from CVE-2026-3300 Exploit Source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26, and recommends defenders block them.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block inbound traffic from 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26 at network boundary. Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests from these IPs to WordPress form endpoints, /wp-admin/, or REST API routes. Flag successful (HTTP 200-299) or error (HTTP 400-500) responses to requests from these sources.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Everest Forms Pro Version ≤1.9.12 Installed
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability affects versions 1.9.12 and earlier.' Patch released March 18; exploitation began April 13. Unpatched version detection enables both preventive and forensic timelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan WordPress plugin files for Everest Forms Pro version ≤1.9.12 (check readme.txt or plugin header). Alert on plugin activation or source code modification post-install. Cross-reference suspicious activity timestamps with March 18 patch release to identify unpatched exposure windows.

suggestion.title: SmartTV Unauthorized Outbound Proxy Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes TVs being used as web-scraping proxies. Should detect abnormal egress from TV devices (high volume, non-streaming traffic, rapid domain changes) suggesting proxy abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV devices for unusual outbound traffic patterns: sustained high-bandwidth connections to non-media domains, rapid connection chaining to multiple IPs/domains within short timeframe, or traffic to known proxy/scraper infrastructure. Baseline legitimate TV traffic (streaming, updates, NTP) and alert on significant deviation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Installation on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is malicious apps on smart TVs. Should detect installation of apps from untrusted sources or apps with suspicious permission requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track app installations on smart TV devices, focusing on sideloaded or non-official app store apps. Alert on apps requesting network access during initial install or during passive idle periods, or apps spawning child processes that establish network connections without user interaction.

suggestion.title: SmartTV Process Executing Web Scraping Activity
suggestion.rationale: Scraped content must be downloaded/parsed. Should detect unusual process behavior on TV devices (curl, wget, Python, Node.js spawning with scraping patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of scripting engines (Python, curl, wget, node) or web-scraping libraries on smart TV devices where such tools are not baseline. Alert on command lines containing URL patterns, HTML parsers, or file I/O indicating data collection.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism on Smart TV Device
suggestion.rationale: Malicious app must persist across reboots. Should detect unusual startup configurations or scheduled tasks on TV systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions to TV system startup folders, .sh/.bat files in boot directories, cron jobs, or registry modifications that would re-execute the malicious app on device restart. Compare against baseline permitted TV auto-start applications.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to residential proxy service infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies proxy enrollment domains (proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com) and IPs (3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114). Standard IOC-driven command-and-control hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and TCP/UDP connections from smart TV devices (Samsung/LG/Roku) to known proxy service domains. Identify enrollment events through first-contact patterns and sustained connection volume anomalies.

suggestion.title: Smart TV app-initiated proxy network enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes enrollment mechanism 'through a consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—deceptive UI leading to enrollment. Should detect when free apps trigger proxy infrastructure contact coincident with user consent interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate app install/update events with outbound connection to proxy domains within 2–5 minutes. Flag as enrollment via social engineering rather than legitimate application functionality.

suggestion.title: Smart TV network baseline deviation—residential proxy relay signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'millions of living room devices' silently enrolled for continuous 'scraping web data.' Detect abnormal outbound traffic volume, byte asymmetry, or destination diversity inconsistent with typical TV usage patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-TV outbound traffic baseline. Alert on sustained byte-out volume > 2 standard deviations, elevated unique destination count, or byte-out/byte-in asymmetry indicating proxy relay activity.

suggestion.title: Proxy SDK library detection in smart TV app packages
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'free apps' on Samsung/LG/Roku stores shipping enrollment capability. Reverse-engineering reveals embedded proxy client libraries (Bright SDK, Luminati). Detect via static binary analysis or app package scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .apk/.tpk app packages for Bright SDK, Luminati client, or BrightData library signatures (string patterns: 'proxyjs', 'luminati', 'bright-sdk'). Flag presence as supply-chain compromise or malicious publisher.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated permission-grant sequences in TV app UI
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—permission grant hidden in complex, non-standard menu navigation. Detect through abnormal UI event sequences preceding permission grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TV app permission-grant events preceded by unusually long or convoluted remote-key input sequences (>15 arrow/OK presses) or navigation to hidden/non-standard menus. Flag as social engineering via UI obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Publisher-level supply chain compromise—bulk proxy enrollment distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes coordinated enrollment across millions via free apps, implying either publisher compromise or intentional malicious publisher. Multiple apps from same publisher contacting proxy infrastructure suggests systematic distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference app publishers on Samsung Galaxy Store, LG Content Store, and Roku Channel Store with proxy network IOCs. Flag publishers with 3+ distinct apps all initiating proxy infrastructure contacts as likely compromised or malicious.

suggestion.title: GitHub Mass Repository Modification by Miasma Worm
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes: 'Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories'. This is direct supply-chain code execution vector with observable commit/push patterns. Pipeline generated zero detections for this primary attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, anomalous commits across 50+ repositories within short time window, unusual commit authorship patterns, or commits containing known worm signatures or obfuscated payloads. Correlate GitHub account activity spikes with branch protection rule modifications or unusual merge approvals.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise - Miasma Worm Injection
suggestion.rationale: Compromising 73 Microsoft repositories requires GitHub credential theft or token abuse. Article implies account compromise but pipeline missed GitHub IAM abuse detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API authentication from unusual geolocations, impossible-travel logins, creation of new OAuth applications/PATs, or API tokens being used from non-standard clients. Correlate with subsequent mass-commit activity.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Ingestion - Miasma-Compromised Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets '73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories' which are likely libraries/dependencies. Downstream consumers ingesting compromised packages is the impact. Pipeline missing impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor organization's package managers and artifact repositories for pulls/installs from known-compromised Microsoft repositories post-incident. Correlate package version anomalies (unexpected version jumps, pre-release installs, unsigned packages) with Miasma incident timeline.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Replication via GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Malware named 'Miasma Worm' indicates self-propagating/replicating behavior. No detections generated for automated propagation via GitHub Actions or similar CI/CD hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows or repository hooks that automatically create new commits, fork repositories, or trigger workflows in other repositories without explicit user interaction. Monitor for cyclic workflow patterns or workflows executing malicious scripts.

suggestion.title: Detection of Miasma Worm IOC - Malware Name and Known Hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names threat: 'Miasma Worm'. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should ingest malware name and repository file hashes into blocklists/watchlists immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create watchlist for 'Miasma Worm' malware family name. Extract and hash all commits/artifacts from 73 affected Microsoft repositories and alert on any file matches in organization endpoints or package caches. Monitor for references to Miasma in code, comments, or configuration.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions GitHub Action Tampering Detection
