suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for IKEv1 VPN authentication attempts and anomalies in your environment. Alert on deviations: sudden increases in failed-then-successful auth patterns, IKEv1 connections from previously unseen ASNs, or geographic clustering of connection sources inconsistent with legitimate traffic.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23631 Redis Lua RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-23631 as enabling 'post-authentication remote code execution' allowing attackers to 'gain full control of a Redis host' via Lua scripting engines. No use case generated despite being the core vulnerability and a named, trackable IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EVAL, EVALSHA, or SCRIPT LOAD commands received on Redis 6.x/7.x instances (vulnerable versions), especially from non-standard clients or from authenticated sessions originating outside administrative IP allowlist. Flag Lua scripts containing shell command invocation patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Post-Authentication Redis Access Followed by Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires prior authentication. Article states attackers 'gain full control of a Redis host' post-exploitation, implying attacker must first obtain valid credentials. Detection must cover authentication anomalies preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Redis client authentication patterns by source IP, application identity, and port. Alert on authentication from unusual geography, non-standard Redis clients (tool-based rather than app-based), or auth events immediately preceding suspicious script execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Lua Script Injection via Redis Scripting Engines
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'two such engines: the older scripting engine and the newer [...].' Detection should distinguish between legitimate admin script execution and attacker-crafted payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor script length, entropy, and content heuristics. Lua scripts >10KB, scripts containing os.execute, io.popen, require('socket'), or patterns obfuscating intent warrant investigation. Compare against historical admin script baselines.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration via Redis Lua
suggestion.rationale: Full host compromise enables lateral movement and data theft. Article implies 'full control' outcome, suggesting attacker may exfiltrate sensitive data or establish persistence through the Lua engine.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual outbound network connections initiated from Redis process after Lua script execution. Monitor for large data transfers from Redis instances to external IPs, or Lua scripts opening raw sockets (socket.tcp, etc.) and transferring data.

suggestion.title: HTS Tool Exploit - Unverified Email Password Reset Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts,' allowing reset-link generation for accounts attackers didn't own. This is the vulnerability vector enabling the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS password-reset requests where supplied email does not match account registration. Stack requests by source IP/session and alert on >5 mismatched email reset attempts or >20 across 24h. Cross-correlate with failed account ownership verification steps.

suggestion.title: 2FA Bypass via Stolen Password Reset Links
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'they obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in and hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.' Login should require 2FA; reset-link logins bypassed this check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login events where authentication method is 'password-reset-link' AND 2FA challenge was skipped or not presented. Cross-reference password-reset timestamp from HTS with login attempt within 5 minutes; alert if 2FA-required flag is false.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account Compromise Detection - Impossible Travel Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gained access to >20,000 accounts with email/phone, posts, DMs, activity history. Exfiltration would require logins from unexpected geolocations. Article notes: 'accounts have been secured to prevent any continued unauthorized access'—suggests rapid re-access post-discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each account, detect login from a new geolocation >1000 km from previous login within 30 minutes. Given 20,000 affected accounts, baseline this cohort separately and alert on >5 accounts with impossible-travel within 1 hour of breach discovery window (late May 2026).

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Tool Abuse - Rate Spike and Success Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: Meta 'disabled the HTS AI-powered support system and all password reset links it had generated.' This implies high volume of reset-link generation. Normal account recovery is low-frequency; bulk resets are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS password-reset request rate per hour; baseline pre-attack period. Alert on sustained rate increase >10x or >100 resets/hour from single source, batch, or API key. Correlate with low email-verification success rate (<20%) to identify bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Compromised Account Data Exfiltration - Bulk Content Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists accessed data: 'direct messages and communications, social media posts and content (photos, videos, stories), account activity and interaction history.' Attackers exfiltrate this post-takeover via API or scraping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For compromised accounts (identified post-breach), detect bulk downloads: >50 DMs accessed, >100 media items fetched, or full-account-export API calls within 1 hour of account takeover window. Alert if export requests come from non-standard clients or IP ranges inconsistent with account history.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Package Installation from Untrusted Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'PyPI Packages Deploy Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers'—supply-chain compromise via package manager is the attack vector. No use case generated despite this being initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip/pip3 install commands with suspicious flags (--index-url, --extra-index-url, --no-deps) pointing to non-PyPI hosts, or installation of packages with typosquatting names. Cross-reference package names against PyPI advisory feeds and upstream threat intelligence.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Memory Access from Python Interpreter Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'cross-platform memory scrapers'—this implies direct memory access patterns (ptrace, /proc/mem, etc.). No collection-phase use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python processes (python, python3) opening handles to other processes' memory regions or invoking ptrace/process_vm_readv. Baseline legitimate memory introspection tools (debuggers, profilers) to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Python Process Loading Suspicious Native Libraries or Exploiting ctypes/cffi
suggestion.rationale: Memory scrapers require native-code execution; article's reference to 'cross-platform' suggests use of Python's ctypes or compiled extensions. No execution/privilege escalation use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python interpreter loading unexpected .so/.dll/.dylib files from temp directories, /dev/shm, or non-standard library paths. Flag ctypes.CDLL() or cffi invocations with dynamic argument construction.

suggestion.title: AI/ML-Based Security Tool Evasion via Obfuscated Payload Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'AI Analyst Misdirection'—suggests deliberate techniques to evade automated analysis. No defense-evasion use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python payloads with intentional polymorphic variable naming, obfuscated imports, or decoy functionality designed to confuse static/dynamic analysis. Flag packages with suspiciously high entropy in strings or heavy use of exec/eval with base64-encoded arguments.

suggestion.title: Detection of Wiper or Destructive Payload Installation via Package Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Wiper Deterrent'—implies either wiper payload delivery or anti-wiper evasion. No impact/impact-evasion use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor setup.py/pyproject.toml post-install hooks and entry points for invocation of shell commands, particularly those touching system directories or disk operations (dd, rm -rf, shred, cipher). Cross-reference with known wiper signature databases.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Name Typosquatting and Dependency Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often use lookalike names. Article describes PyPI compromise but no typosquatting or dependency-confusion detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a curated list of high-value Python packages and monitor pip/pip3 install logs for similarly-named variants (e.g., 'requets' vs 'requests'). Alert on successful installation of packages from private/alternative indices that have the same name as public packages.

suggestion.title: Credential Usage Post-Vishing Report
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates vishing campaign targeting employees; no UC detects credential compromise aftermath. Article phrase: 'Vishing and Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication failures followed by anomalous successful logins (unusual geolocation, time, device) within 48 hours of reported social engineering incidents. Flag accounts with logins from VPN/proxy after credential phishing reported to SOC. Cross-reference with HR reports of vishing calls.

suggestion.title: Physical Access Anomalies and System Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states physical intrusions; typical detections cover cyber only. No UC for post-physical-access behavior (credential harvesting devices, USB drops, workstation compromise). Article phrase: 'Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate badge-access or CCTV anomalies (tailgating, off-hours access to sensitive areas) with subsequent lateral-movement or data-access signals on network 12-36 hours later. Flag USB device insertions, especially on high-value hosts in sensitive locations.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Staging and Exfiltration Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'Data Theft Extortion'; no UC detects file aggregation, compression, or movement to staging servers typical of extortion campaigns. Article phrase: 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual file read patterns (especially PII-adjacent: HR files, financial reports, customer databases) followed by compression (.7z, .rar, .zip) or uploads to public cloud storage (Mega, Mediafire) or attacker-controlled domains. Alert on high-volume outbound traffic from normally quiet accounts.

suggestion.title: Log Deletion and Forensic Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Extortion campaigns typically cover tracks post-exfiltration. No UC detects log clearing or disabling audit trails common to UNC-class actors. Phrase: 'extortion' implies dwell time and cleanup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion or clearing of Security event logs (Event ID 1102), PowerShell history, command-line history, or wevtutil clear-log calls. Monitor for disabling of auditing via GPO or registry changes to disable Sysmon, Windows Defender, or MDE.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Org Chart Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Vishing campaigns typically follow reconnaissance identifying targets; pipeline missed initial-access reconnaissance phase. Article context implies targeted selection of victims. Phrase: 'Vishing and Physical Intrusions' implies prior targeting intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attacker infrastructure (identified domains/IPs) reconnaissance of target org: LinkedIn scraping, company-website crawling, Google dorking patterns, or social-media enumeration. Flag external mail-forwarding rule creation or inactive-account reactivation preceding vishing calls.

suggestion.title: Voice Call Pattern Anomalies and Pretexting
suggestion.rationale: Vishing is the primary attack vector; zero UCs detect phone-based social engineering. Article: 'Vishing and Physical Intrusions' — no behavioral detection for unusual call patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate employee-reported vishing attempts with inbound call metadata: spoofed caller ID, calls to multiple employees in sequence, calls outside business hours, routing through VOIP proxy. Cross-reference with failed MFA/login attempts during or immediately after call windows.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: UniFi OS Server Vulnerable to CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910/33000/34911
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists five CVEs affecting UniFi OS Server management platform. Pipeline correctly identified the hunt type in Recommended Hunts section but failed to emit it in generated use cases output. This is foundational—organizations must inventory affected versions first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset databases for UniFi OS Server versions matching CVE-2026-34908/34909/34910/33000/34911 version ranges. Correlate with network discovery to locate internet-facing or accessible instances. Flag unpatched systems for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker can gain full root access...without a single credential' and 'one unauthenticated request into a complete system takeover.' Exploit attempts should be the primary behavioral detection but pipeline generated no execution-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi OS Server endpoints (port 8443, 443 typical) for HTTP requests lacking authentication context that trigger backend errors, execute system operations, or match known exploit patterns from the CVE chain. Baseline legitimate admin requests; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root Following RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'complete system takeover' and 'full root access'—this is the outcome of privilege escalation, yet pipeline captured zero privilege escalation techniques (should include T1548, T1134 variants). Post-exploitation behavioral detection is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of elevated-privilege processes (root/SYSTEM) from UniFi Java service or web worker processes. Flag child processes (bash, sh, python, curl) executing with administrative rights in the absence of credential submission events or sudo audit logs.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command Execution on UniFi OS Server
suggestion.rationale: Article implies command execution as the mechanism for 'complete system takeover' but pipeline has no execution-phase detections. This is the observable manifestation of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell interpreter invocations (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) spawned from the UniFi OS process context. Baseline legitimate operations; flag deviations such as outbound network commands, credential dumping, or installation of persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised UniFi OS Server
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'management platform for the UniFi family' — a compromised management node is a pivot point to managed network devices (APs, switches, gateways). Pipeline omitted lateral movement risk despite multi-device attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from the compromised UniFi OS Server to internal network ranges (VLAN subnets, AP clusters, gateway devices) using non-standard ports or protocols that deviate from baseline management traffic. Flag file-copy operations or reverse-shell initiation to managed infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Persistence Installation on UniFi OS Server
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of impact to 'thousands of organizations,' implying attackers will establish persistence for sustained access. Pipeline generated zero persistence-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of new user accounts, cron/systemd services, or startup scripts on UniFi OS Server post-exploitation. Flag modifications to Java startup parameters, application configuration files, or initialization hooks that enable backdoor re-entry or privilege escalation on reboot.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM BSD Variant Deployment on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states BSD variant of BRICKSTORM deployed on Linux appliances. Pipeline extracted no IOC or technique despite this being the central claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unusual process execution patterns consistent with BRICKSTORM behavior (shellcode execution, kernel module loading) on Linux systems. Cross-reference with BSD/Unix-like process signatures. Monitor for atypical system calls associated with cross-platform malware.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo Infrastructure Targeting Linux Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies VerdantBamboo as the actor conducting deployment campaign. Pipeline surfaced no actor attribution or associated IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify VerdantBamboo C2 infrastructure and delivery mechanisms targeting Linux appliance management interfaces. Monitor for phishing or supply-chain compromise vectors targeting organizations running vulnerable appliances.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Malware Variant Deployment Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes BSD variant running on Linux—unusual cross-platform behavior suggesting advanced development or variant family reuse. No UC generated despite this technical anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BRICKSTORM variants compiled for multiple OS targets (BSD, Linux) in organization. Flag unexpected OS-specific binaries for same malware family. Monitor for OS-masquerading behavior where Linux binaries mimic BSD system calls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 DD-WRT Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states C0XMO was 'delivered by exploiting CVE-2021-27137, a buffer overflow vulnerability caused by insufficient user input...without authentication and leads to executing arbitrary code.' This is the primary initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT router access logs and network traffic for exploitation attempts: HTTP requests with buffer overflow payloads, suspicious Content-Length values, or process crashes correlated with inbound connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Cron Job Persistence to Hidden Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes.' Explicit persistence via cron pointing to /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, /dev/shm/.sys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cron job creation/modification referencing hidden system directories (.*/.sys patterns) or 15-minute execution intervals. Cross-correlate with new file creation in those same paths.

suggestion.title: Shell Configuration File Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'shell startup files are modified to enable automatic execution.' Standard Linux persistence via ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, /etc/profile.d.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write events to ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, /etc/profile*, and startup script directories that append commands sourcing /tmp, /var/tmp, or /dev/shm paths.

suggestion.title: Bulk Process Termination of Competitor Botnets
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients...and terminates them...deleting binaries and removing their persistence mechanisms.' This cleanup pattern is distinct threat behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequences (5+ terminations in <60s) of known IoT malware processes (Mirai, Gafgyt, etc.) from a single parent, followed by bulk binary deletion, especially from /tmp or /var/tmp.

suggestion.title: SSH/Telnet Brute Force Lateral Movement Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials.' Multiple failed auctions followed by successful lateral movement is the kill-chain signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH/Telnet auth logs: 50+ failed attempts from single source to different user accounts on same host, followed by successful login. Correlate with paramiko/requests process execution.

suggestion.title: Multi-Port Network Scanning for Target Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses worker threads to randomly scan internet-facing systems on common ports like 22, 23, 80/443, 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888.' High-volume discovery scanning precedes infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single internal source initiating connection attempts to 100+ unique external IPs on ports {22,23,80,443,7547,8080,8443,8888} in <10 min window. Signature: SYN+RST patterns (timeout scans).

suggestion.title: Monitor for Instagram Password Reset Flow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'critical logic bug' exposing 'unredacted email addresses and phone numbers' via password reset endpoint. No use case generated despite clear credential_access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk or rapid sequential password reset requests from same source IP/User-Agent targeting high-profile account handles. Monitor for exfiltration patterns (unexpected data downloads, exports) following successful reset-info retrieval.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Exposed Recovery Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Exposed phone numbers and emails enable SIM-swap, email takeover, and MFA bypass. Article identifies 'Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and model Georgina Rodriguez' as confirmed victims—high-value targets for coordinated account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new MFA device enrollment, geolocation anomalies, or session token generation from unexpected geographies within 48 hours of password reset activity on accounts with confirmed exposure.

suggestion.title: Sensitive PII Exposure in Web Application Responses
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: 'logic bug' returning unredacted credentials in password reset flow. Generic hunting signal for similar vulnerabilities exposing emails, phone, or recovery tokens in cleartext responses or error pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses containing full email, phone number, or unencrypted credential recovery tokens in cleartext. Flag account recovery endpoints returning more than obfuscated/hashed identity hints.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Email—Invoice Themed from Consumer Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'invoice-themed phishing emails from consumer email accounts. These emails do not contain malicious links or attachments and instead serve as a precursor for follow-up phone calls.' This attack vector is distinct and requires detection of benign-looking emails followed by phone calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with invoice/billing themes from external consumer domains (gmail.com, yahoo.com) sent to legal organizations with no attachments or links. Correlate with inbound calls within 1-4 hours. Monitor for caller spoofing and VoIP origination.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Software Installation After Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details: 'convinces employees to join remote support sessions...installing remote monitoring and management tools such as AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps, thereby granting them initial access.' RMM installation is the critical execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation for anydesk*.exe, zoho*.exe, bomgar*.exe, superops*.exe when preceded within 30 minutes by Teams/Zoom/Quick Assist session initiation. Monitor for unsigned binaries or installation to temp/downloads directories during remote sessions.

suggestion.title: Bulk Sensitive Document Collection Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'searches for sensitive legal and financial documents, including contracts, tax records, Social Security numbers, and merger or acquisition files...commonly target document management platforms and cloud storage repositories.' Post-compromise data discovery is distinct from exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint/OneDrive/Box for bulk sequential file opens matching legal keywords (contract, merger, acquisition, due diligence, tax return, SSN). Alert on >10 distinct sensitive files opened by single user outside business hours or immediately following RMM tool installation.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via WinSCP and Rclone
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exfiltrating the data using tools such as WinSCP or Rclone.' These tools are legitimate but highly suspicious for bulk data movement when installed post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of winscp.exe or rclone.exe from non-standard paths or during off-hours. Monitor for large outbound transfers (>50 MB) to cloud storage IPs (AWS S3, OneDrive, Google Drive) within 5 minutes of process execution.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Registration—Organization IT Support Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article details phishing domains: '<organization>-itdesk[.]com', '<organization>-it[.]com', '<organization>-helpdesk[.]com'. These patterns enable proactive domain monitoring and takedown coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registrations and DNS activity for newly created domains matching [org-name]-itdesk.*, [org-name]-it.*, [org-name]-helpdesk.*. Alert on privacy registrar use or fast-flux infrastructure with multiple rapid IP rollovers.

suggestion.title: Extortion Email Detection—Ransom Demands with Threat Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'ransom demands often arriving within 30 minutes of the attackers leaving...declare they will call and email target employees and external clients directly...explicitly emphasize that the leak will compromise client trust, invite substantial regulatory fines.' Timing and messaging are distinctive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor incoming email for extortion demands with 3-day deadline, threats to contact clients/regulators, or mentions of legal/regulatory fines. Alert when received within 1 hour of bulk exfiltration event or RMM tool removal.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Phishing Email Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Title 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume' directly establishes high-volume phishing as the attack vector. No detection UC generated for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid, large-scale email distribution from external domains targeting organizational domains. Baseline normal phishing email volume by domain and flag anomalous spikes. Correlate high-volume phishing with reports of compromise, credential validation failures, or downstream lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Monitor Failed Login Attempts Following Phishing Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article context 'crushing SOCs with alert volume' implies credential compromise as downstream effect of phishing success; no credential-access phase in kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After phishing campaigns, expect spike in password-spraying attempts (credential validation) from compromised accounts. Detect sustained failed login attempts from users who clicked recent phishing links, grouped by target user and source IP.

suggestion.title: Alert Tuning: Suppress Benign Failed Credential Events
suggestion.rationale: Article title states goal is 'reduce Tier 1 overload'—directly implies need for alert-fatigue reduction and context-aware suppression rules for failed logins in high-churn environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Suppress failed-login alerts for known service accounts, scheduled maintenance windows, and users with documented high-failure-rate patterns (e.g., cached-credential expiry). Whitelist internal test domains and developer environments to reduce false-positive volume hitting Tier 1.

suggestion.title: Detect AI-Assisted Social Engineering Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'AI Phishing'—indicates use of generative models to craft phishing text. No detection for linguistic or metadata anomalies that distinguish AI-assisted from human-written emails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with statistical outliers in linguistic entropy, grammatical consistency, sender-domain reputation delta, or unusual signature/disclaimer patterns typical of LLM-generated content. Correlate with known generative-model output signatures (e.g., formulaic tone, hallucinated compliance info).

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass in Check Point VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'password bypass in IKEv1 setups'—core attack vector. Pipeline missed credential_access kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 Phase-1 negotiations for authentication bypasses: successful Phase-2 tunnel negotiation without Phase-1 PSK validation log entry, or Phase-2 initiation immediately following failed Phase-1 attempts. Alert on IKEv1 renegotiations completing in sub-second timeframes or repeated identical proposals despite auth failures.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Remote Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title states flaw is 'exploited'—successful credential bypass should result in VPN access establishment (initial_access phase). Pipeline generated zero initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Check Point VPN connections from unexpected geolocations, connection patterns deviating from user baseline, or sessions established during off-hours. Correlate VPN auth success with downstream internal reconnaissance or lateral movement attempts (SMB probe, RDP enumeration, SSH attempts) within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN IKEv1 Weak Encryption or Downgrade Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: IKEv1 cryptographic weaknesses (e.g., DES, null-cipher, weak DH groups) are common attack surface. No defense_evasion or protocol-downgrade detection suggested by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IKEv1 Phase-1 negotiations using deprecated encryption (DES, 3DES), absent integrity protection, or DH group ≤1024 bits. Flag IKEv1 proposals that omit authentication methods or allow NULL encryption. Baseline hardened configurations and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Default or Shared Pre-Shared Key Reuse
suggestion.rationale: IKEv1-based exploits frequently target default PSKs or shared credentials. No IOC extraction means default PSK patterns, CVE IDs, or affected product versions were missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful IKEv1 authentication using known weak PSK values (e.g., 'password', 'admin', or industry test vectors documented in CVE PoC). Monitor for repeated PSK reuse across disparate peer addresses or time windows. Cross-reference against Check Point default credential advisories.

suggestion.title: VPN Gateway Configuration Tampering Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful credential bypass often precedes persistence actions (policy modification, rogue user creation, tunnel configuration backdoors). Pipeline failed to generate persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to IKEv1 PSK, authentication policy, IPSec encryption settings, or user access controls. Correlate config changes with non-admin user logins, service account activity, or sessions flagged as compromised. Monitor for addition of rogue Phase-1 proposals or backup PSK entries.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Phase-2 Tunnel Establishment Without Successful Phase-1 Auth
suggestion.rationale: Core bypass mechanic: tunnel established despite failed authentication. Pipeline identified zero protocol-level anomalies or authentication-sequence violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IPSec SA establishment (Phase-2) without corresponding successful Phase-1 IKE_SA formation or PSK validation. Alert on tunnel negotiation completion in abnormally short timeframes (<200ms), suggesting authentication bypass. Monitor for Phase-2 Quick-Mode payloads without valid Phase-1 parent SA.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - CVE-2026-23631 Vulnerable Redis Instances
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline's own recommendations section lists this template but failed to generate output. Article fixes dangerous RCE in Redis—detection must flag vulnerable versions pre-May 2026
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Redis instances by version. Flag all versions released before May 2026 (per article's patching timeline) as vulnerable to CVE-2026-23631. Cross-reference with network exposure and recent authentication logs to prioritize assets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Lua Script Execution in Redis
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes exploitation via 'powerful server-side Lua engines, allowing administrators to run custom logic directly in the database'—behavioral baseline needed for script execution anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor EVAL/EVALSHA commands in Redis logs. Establish baseline of legitimate script names/hashes from administrative maintenance windows. Alert on: (a) unknown script hashes, (b) execution outside scheduled windows, (c) Lua functions invoking os.execute or similar shell primitives.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Privilege Escalation via Lua Script
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'post-authentication RCE'—detection must correlate auth success with immediate privilege-escalating script operations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create correlation rule: Redis AUTH success → EVAL command within 5 minutes. Flag when non-admin credentials immediately execute scripts. Inspect script payloads for process spawning, file writes, or system calls.

suggestion.title: Redis Process Child Process Spawning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article promises 'complete control to Host Server'—OS-level command execution is the exploitation endpoint. Phrase 'run custom logic directly in the database' implies code execution escaping Redis sandbox
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any child process spawned by Redis daemon (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell, python, etc.). Redis should never legitimately spawn shell interpreters. Treat any such activity as confirmed exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Discord token cache access by non-Discord process
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Discord Tokens' in title and threat profile. Browser-generic cookie detection misses Discord's distinct token storage in AppData\Local\Discord\Cache and LocalAppData\Discord. Discord tokens enable account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes other than Discord.exe reading/copying files in Discord's Cache and Code Cache subdirectories. Monitor for handles to token-bearing files (e.g., discord_log_0.log contains authentication state). Exclude Discord auto-update and profile-sync processes.

suggestion.title: Mass Password Reset Requests from Support-Tier Recovery Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'obtained password reset links' via HTS and 'Meta disabled... all password reset links it had generated' — directly describes volumetric exploitation of account recovery endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account-recovery endpoints for abnormal request volume and velocity. Baseline daily reset issuance by support tool; alert when single source exceeds historical mean by >5x. Correlate successful password resets with login success within 15 minutes from non-established geoip/device.

suggestion.title: Email Verification Bypass in Account Recovery Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts' — the vulnerability is email verification step being skipped or unvalidated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag password reset requests where email-verification step is skipped, returns success without out-of-band confirmation, or accepts email addresses not registered to the target account. Monitor for requests missing email domain validation or confirmation-link click logs.

suggestion.title: Successful Login Immediately Post-Password-Reset from Anomalous Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in and hijack accounts' — indicates immediate post-reset login from attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login within 30 minutes of account password reset where the login originates from IP/device/geolocation not seen for that account in prior 90 days. Escalate on 5+ accounts sharing attacker IP/ASN post-reset in 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Two-Factor Authentication Disabling on Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers 'hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled' — indicates either 2FA disabling post-compromise or accounts specifically targeted with no 2FA configured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 2FA removal/disable actions on accounts that authenticated from new device/IP in prior 24h. Alert on 2FA toggle within 5 minutes of first anomalous login. Cross-reference with password-reset activity within same 30-minute window.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Tool Public-Facing Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability in the company's High Touch Support (HTS) tool, an AI-assisted support system' — describes direct exploitation of publicly-exposed account recovery endpoint (T1190).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS and similar account-recovery API endpoints for request patterns indicating authentication-check bypass: requests with unregistered email addresses, missing email-verification headers, or null/undefined verification parameters. Flag bulk requests to diverse accounts from single source IP.

suggestion.title: Bulk Mandatory Security Checkpoint Enrollment Post-Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: Meta 'enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint' — indicates detection/remediation event useful for tracking incident timeline and response scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create rule detecting bulk account security-checkpoint enrollment (>100 accounts in <1 hour). When detected, correlate enrollment timestamps backward to identify incident window and forward to identify account takeover attempts. Use for threat-hunt 'time of initial compromise' anchoring.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malicious packages deployed via PyPI; pipeline produced zero IOCs from supply chain vector. Title: 'Graph ML PyPI Packages Deploy...'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/conda install commands and subprocess creation immediately after. Flag if installation of unfamiliar or typosquatted packages precedes memory access, outbound C2, or script execution. Correlate package hash against known-malicious PyPI versions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Memory Access from Python Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cross-platform memory scrapers' as primary payload; title explicitly names memory scraping as attack step. No detection generated despite clear collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python process creation with unusual parent processes, elevated privileges, or suspicious command-line patterns (e.g., ctypes, pymem, win32api, mmap). Correlate with process tokens, memory dump tools, or access to /proc/[pid]/mem on Linux.

suggestion.title: Python Execution with Defense Evasion Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Title cites 'AI analyst misdirection' as explicit payload—suggests obfuscation, environment detection, or anti-analysis. Pipeline missed defense-evasion kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python execution with indicators of obfuscation (UPX-packed bytecode, base64 decoding, dynamic module imports) or evasion (checks for debuggers via __import__('sys').gettrace(), environment variable checks, process name spoofing). Signature misdirection patterns: imports of legitimate libraries but unusual symbol access.

suggestion.title: Wiper Preparation or Anti-Forensics Activity from Python
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'wiper deterrent' as payload component; suggests impact or anti-forensics capability. Zero IOCs or detection rules generated for this critical stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes opening raw disk devices (/dev/sd*, \\Device\\HarddiskVolume*), writing to boot sectors, or deleting event logs / file system journals. Flag sys.modules imports of ctypes accessing kernel functions. Detect shadow copy deletion or recycling bin clearing triggered from Python context.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Communication from PyPI-Installed Package
suggestion.rationale: Misdirection tooling and memory scrapers require exfiltration channel; title implies multi-stage C2 capability. No network-based detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate PyPI package outbound activity. Flag Python processes resolving or connecting to non-CDN, non-PyPI hosts post-install, especially if C2 domain registration is recent or uses fast-flux. Inspect DNS queries from pip/poetry processes for DGA-like patterns or unusual TLDs.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Exploitation via Graph ML Libraries
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Graph ML PyPI Packages'—suggests targeted package name or dependency abuse. Pipeline should have flagged known-malicious package names or namespace-confusion attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query PyPI API or mirror logs for packages matching 'graph-ml*', 'graphml*', or similar with recent creation dates and zero download history before spike. Cross-reference with requirements.txt, setup.py, and Pipfile in development environments. Alert if package maintainer account has no prior package releases or account was compromised.

suggestion.title: Vishing callback detected: Non-IT user downloads and executes RMM tool post-contact
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Using Vishing and RMM Tools'. Opens with 'phone calls, screen-sharing tricks, and remote monitoring software'. Pipeline generated zero detections for vishing initiation or victim callback. Detection gap: victim receives inbound call, is socially engineered, downloads/executes RMM within hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-IT user executes RMM installer (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk, ScreenConnect) within 4 hours of: (a) inbound call to desk phone, or (b) unsolicited Teams/Slack DM requesting 'remote support', or (c) executable downloaded from attacker domain or free file-hosting service with low organizational prevalence.

suggestion.title: Screen-sharing tool deployment for initial reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'screen-sharing tricks' as attack vector. Pipeline missed detections for screen-share applications (GoToMeeting, Zoom, Cisco Webex, Chrome Remote Desktop, TeamViewer's viewer-only modes) deployed outside IT baseline—distinct from persistent RMM tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag installation of web-based or quick-launch screen-share tools (Teams, Zoom, Webex, GoToMeeting, Chrome RDP, AnyViewer) by end-users without IT approval, especially when followed by file/system access attempts.

suggestion.title: Pre-exfil staging: Bulk compression or rclone sync before RMM callback
suggestion.rationale: Article states actors 'exfiltrate data' via RMM. No behavioral hunts for pre-exfil staging (compressing sensitive files or syncing to attacker-controlled cloud storage prior to RMM handoff).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk .zip/.7z/.tar.gz creation or rclone/Cyberduck process execution targeting Legal/, Contracts/, Financial/ directories, especially when immediately followed by RMM tool launch or outbound connections to attacker IPs.

suggestion.title: RMM-mediated exfiltration to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists business-data-leaks.com and 7 IPs as IOC infrastructure, but pipeline output shows zero IOCs and zero IOC→technique→detection mappings. No hunt for outbound RMM traffic to these specific C2 destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on outbound connections from RMM process (AnyDesk.exe, TeamViewer.exe, ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe, RustDesk.exe) to IOC IPs (192.236.147.131, 192.236.147.138, 193.141.60.212, 192.236.154.158, 192.236.146.173, 174.169.162.62, 64.94.84.97) or domain business-data-leaks.com.

suggestion.title: Anomalous RMM session behavior: Extended duration, high data transfer, non-business hours
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hands-on-keyboard' exfil via RMM but pipeline generated no behavioral anomaly hunts for session duration, data volume, or timing indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when RMM session (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, RustDesk) duration exceeds 4 hours outside business hours, transfers >1 GB, or accesses sensitive file shares (\Legal\, \Contracts\, \Financials\).

suggestion.title: Inbound Vishing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Used Vishing' as attack vector; zero detection rule generated for voice-based social engineering. Article phrase: 'UNC3753 Used Vishing and Physical Intrusions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clustered inbound calls to help desk, executive staff, or technical personnel requesting credentials, system access, or sensitive data. Correlate call patterns with authentication anomalies, credential resets, and email compromise attempts within 24 hours of call spikes.

suggestion.title: Physical Security Anomalies Preceding Data Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Physical Intrusions' implying on-site access; no detection for badge anomalies, unauthorized facility access, or surveillance. Article phrase: 'Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected badge access to sensitive areas during off-hours, badge cloning attempts, or access by inactive/terminated employee IDs. Correlate facility access anomalies with concurrent social engineering reports or data exfiltration alerts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous High-Volume Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly involves 'Data Theft' but no exfiltration detection generated. This is the core attack objective. Article phrase: 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound transfers exceeding baseline user/department patterns, especially to non-whitelisted external IPs or low-reputation domains. Flag transfers disguised as backup traffic or administrative activity, particularly correlated with vishing incidents or physical access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Ransom Demand / Extortion Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign labeled 'Extortion Campaign' but pipeline generated no detection for ransom artifacts or threatening communications. Article phrase: 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for common ransom note filenames (DECRYPT_ME, README, RANSOM), cryptocurrency wallet addresses, threat actor contact details, or specific extortion messaging. Monitor shared drives and email for appearance of these artifacts post-exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Physical Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Physical intrusions imply on-site system access, but no detection for subsequent privilege escalation or lateral movement. Article phrase: 'Physical Intrusions...Data Theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Following physical security incidents, monitor for credential dumping (lsass.exe access, registry queries), pass-the-hash attempts, remote access protocols (RDP, WMI, PsExec), and lateral port scanning from previously-clean workstations.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Targeting Executive / IT Personnel
suggestion.rationale: Vishing success requires convincing impersonation but no detection for credential requests via phone posing as IT/vendor. Article phrase: 'Used Vishing.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate help-desk password-reset requests or multi-factor authentication resets with prior vishing reports or call center queue spikes. Flag successful authentication from anomalous geographies/IPs within 4 hours of such requests.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Server Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'one unauthenticated request into a complete system takeover'—directly describes network-based RCE exploitation. Pipeline generated zero hunts despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to UniFi OS Server (default ports 443, 8443) from untrusted sources. Flag requests containing RCE payloads, command injection patterns, or POST/GET to known-vulnerable API endpoints. Correlate against CVE-2026-34908+ exploitation signatures. Baseline normal UniFi administrative traffic and alert on anomalous request structure from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from UniFi Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful RCE achieving 'root access'—exploited code would spawn shells or payload processes from the UniFi daemon. Pipeline missed post-exploitation process behavior entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is UniFi OS daemon (unifi, unifi-controller process) and child is shell interpreter (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /bin/dash) or payload tool (curl, wget, nc, python, perl). Flag command lines containing reverse-shell patterns, base64 decoding, or network callbacks from these contexts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'gains full root access'—this is the final impact. Pipeline failed to suggest privilege-escalation-focused detections despite it being the direct outcome of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation from UniFi service account to root/uid 0. Flag successful sudo/su/setuid transitions, setcap abuse, or kernel exploit indicators. Track parent-child relationships where low-privilege process spawns high-privilege shell. Alert on unexpected escalation paths in UniFi-related process trees.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory Scan - UniFi OS Server Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Five CVE-IDs listed in article require version-scoped asset hunting. Pipeline extracted CVE list in body but produced zero structured IOCs and zero asset-exposure use case (standard first hunt for multi-CVE advisory).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset inventory for UniFi OS Server instances. Cross-reference installed versions against CVE-2026-34908, CVE-2026-34909, CVE-2026-34910, CVE-2026-33000, CVE-2026-34911 to identify vulnerable deployments. Use port fingerprinting (443, 8443) and HTTP header analysis to detect UniFi instances; correlate with patch status. Flag all affected systems as immediate recon targets for threat hunters.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Command & Control Signaling from UniFi Host
suggestion.rationale: Root-compromised management platform is ideal for lateral movement staging and persistence. Article implies 'complete system takeover' but pipeline missed C2 and exfiltration-signaling detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate UniFi egress (NTP, vendor updates, configured API calls). Alert on unexpected outbound connections from UniFi host to non-whitelisted IPs, especially high ports (>10000) or C2-like patterns (DGA domains, fast-flux IPs, known botnet infrastructure). Monitor DNS from UniFi host for dynamic domain registrations or suspicious TLD patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised UniFi OS Server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes management platform compromise—natural pivot point for network-wide attack. Pipeline generated zero hunts for lateral movement despite UniFi's privileged network position (manages network infrastructure).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance activity originating from UniFi host (scanning, enumeration, credential harvesting). Flag SSH/RDP/WinRM connections from UniFi server to other infrastructure. Alert on payload delivery (wget, curl, scp) to secondary targets. Track tools commonly used for lateral movement (smbexec, psexec, wmiexec) executed from UniFi process tree or spawned by root shells on that host.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Process Execution from Appliance Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is deployed on Linux appliances. No execution-phase detection provided despite 'deploys' being the core action verb.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with BRICKSTORM indicators (hash, name patterns, parent process from system daemons or SSH sessions). Alert on unusual process spawning from appliance management ports (SSH, web UI, SNMP). Cross-correlate with network beaconing from the same source.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Installation Post-BRICKSTORM Deployment
suggestion.rationale: BSD and Linux rootkits achieve stealth persistence via kernel extensions. Article describes deployment but provides no detection for persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect insertion of unsigned kernel modules post-compromise via auditd syscall logs (init_module, finit_module). Monitor /lib/modules and /sys/module for unexpected entries. Flag any modprobe or insmod execution from non-root service contexts.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM C2 Beacon from Linux Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Malware requires command channel. Article implies ongoing compromise but supplies no network-based detection for C2 communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify anomalous outbound connections from Linux appliances (appliance internal subnet to external). Profile for periodic beaconing, consistent port/protocol, or DNS queries to newly registered domains. Correlate timing and destination IP against known BRICKSTORM infrastructure.

suggestion.title: BSD Variant BRICKSTORM Binary Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly calls out 'BSD variant' of BRICKSTORM, implying cross-compiled or BSD-native build. No binary or artifact detection for BSD-specific samples.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-match known BRICKSTORM BSD ELF samples. Inspect binary headers for BSD-specific ELF flags or linked BSD C libraries (libc BSD variants). Detect suspicious use of BSD-specific system calls (pledge, unveil) via process tracing where available on hybrid systems.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo Attribution Signal Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article names VerdantBamboo as the actor but provides no detection logic to attribute follow-on activity. Missing behavioral/infrastructure clustering use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate indicators associated with VerdantBamboo: malware samples, C2 IPs/domains, file signatures, and delivery vectors. When BRICKSTORM is detected or suspected, expand search to correlated infrastructure. Detect initial access attempts from VerdantBamboo-attributed phishing, watering holes, or supply-chain compromise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Configuration Changes on Linux Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Deployed malware must modify appliance config or boot sequence to persist. Article implies tampering but no detection covers config modification attack steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to cron (/etc/cron.d, /etc/crontab), init scripts (/etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system), and boot config (/etc/rc.local, /etc/grub.d). Flag file modifications with timestamps correlating to BRICKSTORM execution. Alert on rapid mass-writes to these paths.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Volume Spike (Mail Alert Flood)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume'—implies high-volume phishing emails triggering alerts. No UC generated despite clear operational indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained email alert volume spikes from phishing detection engines. Baseline legitimate mail volume per sender/domain and alert when AI-driven phishing campaigns cause 5x+ increase in flagged messages within 1h windows. Correlate with user report rates to filter signal from noise.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Link Detection (Evasion Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'AI Phishing'—implies ML-generated content designed to evade detection. No UC addresses the technical characteristics of AI-generated phishing URLs or body text patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AI-generated phishing by flagging emails with high entropy URLs, non-standard domain registration patterns (bulk registrations), and text cadence anomalies (e.g., unusual pronoun usage, repetitive filler phrases common in LLM output). Correlate with ML classifiers trained on synthetic vs. human-authored phishing samples.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Exposed Instance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the vulnerability affects 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190 — KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets). Attackers must first identify or gain access to a publicly exposed LiteLLM service. Pipeline missed the discovery phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan network for LiteLLM instances by identifying services on standard Python/web ports (5000, 8000, 8080) with LiteLLM signatures in HTTP banners, SSL certificates, or response headers. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unaccounted or orphaned deployments.

suggestion.title: Authentication to LiteLLM Followed by Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' can execute commands. Core attack is auth + command execution. Pipeline generated no detection pairing these events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication events to LiteLLM services (HTTP 200 POST to /api/*, successful API token validation) immediately followed by process creation (cmd.exe, bash, PowerShell, python -c) spawned from the LiteLLM process context. Baseline legitimate requests and child processes; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Pattern Matching in LiteLLM Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'command injection'—the attack vector is malicious input to the API. Pipeline should detect injection metacharacters or executable keywords in request bodies targeting LiteLLM endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST bodies to LiteLLM endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, backticks, `$()`, `<<EOF`), command keywords (exec, system, os.popen, subprocess), or script interpreters (bash, sh, powershell, cmd, python). Flag requests with multiple injection signals in a single payload.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege API Key Spawning Unexpected Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns that 'holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' can exploit. Detection should flag when a read-only or scoped key is used to trigger system commands—violating its intended scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API authentication logs (key ID, scope/role, timestamp) with process-creation logs from the LiteLLM service context. Alert when a key classified as read-only, low-privilege, or belonging to a test/development tier initiates process execution or file-write operations.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Performing Lateral Movement or Data Access
suggestion.rationale: After command injection succeeds, attacker gains execution in the service context. Article describes 'arbitrary commands on the host'—pipeline should detect post-exploitation activity (outbound connections, credential access, lateral movement) sourced from the compromised service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections, file access, and process spawning from the LiteLLM service account/process for anomalies: unexpected outbound IPs/ports, access to sensitive file shares, spawning of reconnaissance or lateral-movement tools (psexec, mimikatz, ssh), or credential dumping utilities.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable LiteLLM Version Deployed Post-Patch-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date '2026-06-22'. Pipeline should generate a compliance/tracking detection for versions deployed after the deadline or rollbacks to pre-patched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory LiteLLM installations and their versions. Alert on any deployments, updates, or rollbacks to versions prior to CVE-2026-42271's patch release (versions released before 2026-06-22). Track remediation status per host through the patch deadline and flag non-compliant assets.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Critical Check Point VPN Flaw Exploited to Bypass Passwords in IKEv1 Setups' — the vulnerability is an authentication bypass. Pipeline must detect attempt patterns consistent with CVE exploitation against IKEv1 negotiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IKEv1 Phase-1 negotiation anomalies: repeated aggressive mode requests, unusual DH group combinations, or authentication success without valid credentials. Flag Check Point VPN gateways receiving exploit-consistent request patterns.

suggestion.title: Successful VPN Authentication After Credential-Less Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is password bypass. Pipeline must correlate failed traditional auth attempts immediately followed by successful VPN tunnel establishment without matching credential submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN user sessions where auth-failure events (wrong password, account locked, etc.) precede successful tunnel establishment within sub-minute intervals, or where tunnel success occurs without corresponding pre-shared-key validation logs.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Lateral Movement from Check Point Compromises
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw 'Exploited' — this is active-breach context. Successful VPN bypass immediately enables lateral movement. Detection must correlate VPN auth anomalies with internal reconnaissance or lateral-movement activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN clients establishing unusual internal-network connections (port scans, RDP/SSH pivots, enum of unrelated subnets) within minutes of authentication via the vulnerable IKEv1 vector. Correlate VPN session GUIDs with outbound reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Gateway Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Check Point VPN as vulnerable platform. Pipeline must flag IKEv1-specific protocol anomalies and exploitation signatures at the gateway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point gateways for IKEv1 Aggressive Mode floods, crafted payloads with oversized transforms, or repeated Quick Mode requests from single source IP. Flag any deviation from normal IKEv1 handshake state machine.

suggestion.title: Mass VPN Connection Anomalies on Check Point Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability exploited in the wild typically triggers spike in exploit attempts. Pipeline must detect volumetric or behavioral surge in VPN auth events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of VPN authentication success/failure rates per gateway and alert on >3σ deviation. Detect single source IPs generating >50 IKEv1 negotiation attempts in 5min window, or geographically anomalous VPN client distributions.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Service Restart or Failover Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts may trigger gateway instability or admin response. Pipeline must surface operational anomalies that correlate with active exploitation windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Check Point VPN gateway restarts, service crashes, or high-availability failovers during or immediately after surge in IKEv1 authentication anomalies. Correlate with exploit attempt timelines.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via URI Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version' and 'attackers can bypass authentication and reach backend services' by crafting requests that 'appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi OS ingress for requests to '/api/auth/validate-sso/' or similar paths that exhibit decode/normalize behavior differences between validation and routing. Establish baseline of legitimate auth paths and alert on deviations. Detect requests bypassing the authentication validation component by comparing raw-form exempt paths with normalized-form protected routes.

suggestion.title: Command Injection via Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command' and explicitly recommends monitoring 'ucs/update/latest_package' endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to 'ucs/update/latest_package' endpoint for shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), `, &&, ||) and encoded variants in payloads. Correlate with suspicious child process creation under 'ucs-update' parent. Flag requests from unauthenticated sources or bypassing normal auth session validation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'injected commands do not initially run as root' but 'affected service account's sudo privileges make privilege escalation trivial' and 'execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sudo invocation by service accounts without password prompts, TTY allocation, or normal privilege-elevation indicators. Track sudoers modifications granting passwordless sudo to service accounts. Alert on unexpected binaries executed via sudo from non-interactive service contexts (e.g., ucs-update spawning shell, compiler, or system utilities).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Processes Under ucs-update Parent
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'suspicious child processes under 'ucs-update'' as a recommended detection indicator for the exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate child processes spawned by ucs-update (package utilities, extractors). Alert on unexpected process names, shell interpreters (bash, sh, python), or utilities unrelated to package management. Prioritize detection of indicators suggesting successful command injection (reverse shells, exfiltration tools, privilege escalation utilities).

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation via CVE-2026-34909
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-34909 as 'a path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system' chained with auth bypass to reach vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi OS HTTP requests for path traversal patterns (../, ..\, Unicode/URL encoding variants). Alert on attempts to read system configuration, /etc/sudoers, or files outside web root. Correlate path traversal probing with subsequent authentication bypass or endpoint access attempts on same target.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Rebase Merge Enabled by Non-Admin User
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This is the direct trigger for RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs API calls or web logs for MERGE settings changes (specifically rebase merge enablement) by authenticated non-owner users, or by repo owners immediately after repo creation. Flag rapid rebase toggle changes in default-configured instances.

suggestion.title: Account Creation on Gogs with Open Registration Enabled
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false)' and 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account.' This is the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account creation events on Gogs instances with open registration. Baseline normal user count and flag bulk or rapid account registration. Alert on accounts created from suspicious ASNs or immediately followed by repo creation.

suggestion.title: Rapid Gogs Repository Creation Followed by Merge Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Exploit chain described as: 'create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' then 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle.' Sequential behavior indicates exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account creation → repo creation → merge settings modification within short time window (minutes) by same user. Particularly suspicious if user has no prior commit activity or if repo remains empty.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gogs Version Identification (0.14.2 or 0.15.0-dev)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions: 'affects all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev.' Patch available in 0.14.3. Version detection is primary mitigation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate exposed Gogs instances via fingerprinting (HTTP headers, /api/v1 responses, page structure) and identify versions. Flag any instances running 0.14.2, 0.15.0-dev, or unpatched variants. Cross-reference with Shodan/Shadowserver for internet exposure.

suggestion.title: Multiple Private Repository Access via Merge Operation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'read any repository (including private repos).' Merge operations provide access to private repo contents—detect abnormal multi-repo read patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single-user access to multiple private repositories through merge operations in short timeframe. Alert on users viewing/merging code from repos they have no explicit grant to. Track private repo access anomalies per user baseline.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Patterns in Gogs Merge() Code Path
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights: 'this flaw is very similar to other argument-injection flaws' and 'affects a different code path (Merge()).' Signature-based detection on merge function calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs process execution logs for command-line argument injections in merge operations. Alert on shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons) in merge-related arguments. Track Go runtime errors or panics originating from merge code paths.

suggestion.title: Email with DoubleClick Redirect to Malicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states campaign 'using Google's own DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims toward a fileless .NET loader.' This is the initial access vector; no detection rule was generated despite it being the primary attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links that redirect through doubleclick.net infrastructure to the IOCs (fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, bth.startthewave.org, pengajian.muliastudy.com, andrefelipedonascime1778799406970.2241107.meusitehostgator.com.br, catalogo.castrouria.com, xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net). Alert on multi-hop redirect chains masquerading as legitimate ads.

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Loader Memory Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the payload as 'fileless .NET loader'—code executing in memory without disk writes. This is a core evasion technique, yet pipeline generated no detection rule despite listing T1027 as a technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .NET runtime processes (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, msbuild.exe, regsvcs.exe) executing Assembly.Load, LoadAssembly, or Invoke-Expression followed by in-memory code execution. Correlate parent processes receiving DoubleClick-redirect emails with child .NET execution.

suggestion.title: Injection from CLR-Hosted Process
suggestion.rationale: Fileless loaders typically inject payloads into secondary processes for execution. Article's truncated description '...runs [...]' indicates runtime behavior consistent with process injection patterns common in .NET-based malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .NET processes spawning system processes (svchost.exe, rundll32.exe, wininit.exe) with direct process handle requests or remote thread creation. Alert on cross-process memory writes from CLR-hosted processes.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to Malicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline identified T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) as a technique but generated zero network detection rules. Article lists 7 command domains; no IOC-driven hunt was generated despite this being a high-confidence C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS or HTTP/HTTPS connections to fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, bth.startthewave.org, pengajian.muliastudy.com, andrefelipedonascime1778799406970.2241107.meusitehostgator.com.br, catalogo.castrouria.com, xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net from hosts that recently processed emails or executed .NET assemblies.

suggestion.title: Hash-Based Detection of Known Loader Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 5 SHA256 hashes for the fileless loader; pipeline extracted zero. Despite listing 'file hash IOC(s)' in recommended hunts, no detection rule was generated and no hashes appear in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match process or file hashes against: d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5, c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6, c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18, f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348, e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd. Flag any match as likely fileless loader execution.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan Command-and-Control Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'can take full control of an infected machine'—a core RAT capability. No detection hypothesis addresses remote command-and-control channel establishment or callback patterns to C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from user-mode processes to article IOC IPs/domains. Flag persistent callback intervals, reverse-shell spawning (cmd.exe/powershell.exe with network I/O), and execution of known remote-access tools (mstsc.exe, TeamViewer clients). Correlate with file access patterns to wallet/browser directories to confirm infection chain.

suggestion.title: Discord Application Token Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Discord Tokens' as specific exfiltration target. Generic browser cookie detection (UC_BROWSER_STEALER) misses Discord's app-specific token storage in %APPDATA%\Discord. Requires dedicated hunt to catch Discord-targeting harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor non-Discord processes reading Discord Local Storage and Cache directories. Flag rapid sequential file access to Discord token locations followed by outbound connections to article C2 domains within 60 seconds. Correlate with suspicious parent processes or temp directory execution.

suggestion.title: Wallet File Enumeration and Discovery Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Malware must discover wallet files before stealing them. Article describes 'wide reach,' implying active reconnaissance. T1083 is mapped but no execution-layer detection for wallet directory enumeration patterns during discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential enumeration of 3+ distinct crypto wallet directories (%APPDATA%\Ethereum, %APPDATA%\Bitcoin, %APPDATA%\Exodus, etc.) by single process within 10-second window. Flag processes checking multiple wallet keystores in succession, indicating active reconnaissance rather than incidental or user-initiated access.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Staging and Execution from Temp Directories
suggestion.rationale: T1027 is mapped but no execution-phase detection suggested. Infostealer droppers typically stage executables in %TEMP%, Downloads, or AppData\Local\Temp. Article distributed 'through underground channels' implies delivery mechanism evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution from %TEMP%, %TMP%, Downloads, or AppData\Local\Temp with randomized/obfuscated names (<12 chars, non-dictionary words). Correlate with unsigned or invalid digital signatures and anomalous parent processes (explorer.exe, svchost.exe spawning user-mode executables).

suggestion.title: Account Enumeration — Discord Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article targets Discord tokens, implying enumeration of Discord accounts/servers on victim. T1087 (Account Discovery) relevant but missing. Should detect automated Discord credential queries or API enumeration attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process access to Discord user profile data, session files, or credential storage. Flag repeated reads of Discord configuration files or outbound API calls to Discord endpoints from non-Discord processes. Correlate with file access to wallet/browser credential stores to confirm infostealer activity chain.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Linking to Passkey-Themed Credential Harvesters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states group uses 'social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials.' Domains passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com are clearly credential-harvesting landing pages. Missing T1566.002 (Phishing: Spearphishing Link) detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt email gateways for messages to enterprise cloud-storage users containing URLs to passkey*/deploypasskey domains. Correlate with cloud-storage login attempts (failed or successful) and HTTP POST events to those domains within 24h of message delivery.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission and Exfiltration to Pink IPs/Domains
