suggestion.title: NSO Group infrastructure and C2 domain blocking
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group explicitly named in title — domain IOCs and malicious infrastructure should have been extracted and mapped to C2 detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on DNS queries and outbound connections to known/suspected NSO Group infrastructure (Pegasus C2, exploit server domains, command infrastructure). Include behavioral signatures for obfuscated C2 communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous WhatsApp account authentication and device registration
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks against WhatsApp aim to compromise accounts or install spyware on devices — account takeover and unauthorized registration should generate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new WhatsApp logins from geographically impossible locations, new device registrations following phishing link clicks, and logins from IP space associated with NSO infrastructure.

suggestion.title: User execution of malicious links from messaging applications
suggestion.rationale: Article describes phishing attack — user clicks on malicious links are the execution mechanism and should be detected as T1204.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on suspicious URLs delivered via WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. Alert on clicks followed by credential entry, binary downloads, or redirects to known credential-harvesting domains.

suggestion.title: Pegasus spyware execution and post-compromise behavior
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group's primary tool is Pegasus — if phishing succeeds at execution level, Pegasus installation and behavior patterns must be detected (process creation, hook injection, privilege escalation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for characteristic Pegasus process patterns, suspicious inter-process communication, kernel module loading, and file creation in known exploit or hook directories on affected devices.

suggestion.title: Emerging NSO Group phishing technique variations post-block
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Files Contempt Order' — indicates repeat activity and legal escalation, suggesting NSO Group is evolving phishing techniques to bypass detection and Meta's enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track new domain registrations, IP ranges, and obfuscation techniques associated with NSO Group post-enforcement. Monitor for phishing payloads using new URL shorteners, new SMTP relays, or compromised hosting.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell File Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states group 'deploying tools designed to evade every detection method' to IIS servers. Execution-phase file creation is completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .aspx, .asmx, .ashx file writes to inetpub\wwwroot and application directories. Correlate file creation timestamps with w3wp.exe process activity and HTTP requests to new paths within 60 seconds of write.

suggestion.title: Cryptographic Obfuscation in Web Shell Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat's signature evasion mechanism: 'cryptographically unique web shell framework.' This obfuscation pattern itself is the detectable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt IIS access logs for anomalously high-entropy POST bodies, base64/hex-encoded content, and multi-stage decoding patterns directed at suspicious .aspx paths. Baseline entropy thresholds against known legitimate applications.

suggestion.title: Web Shell C2 Outbound Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies application-layer protocol C2. Web shell persistence requires callback to external command server; outbound HTTP from IIS is primary detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe outbound HTTP(S) to OP-512 IOC destinations (43.160.202.246, 140.206.161.227, 124.156.129.151, ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com). Flag periodic callback intervals, small encrypted payloads, or User-Agent anomalies.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Process Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Web shells enable arbitrary command execution within IIS context. Article targets IIS exclusively; missing detection for process spawn from w3wp.exe or application pool identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or suspicious binaries spawned from w3wp.exe parent or IIS application pool accounts. Suppress known benign application startup sequences via whitelist.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Multi-Vendor Keystore Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets crypto wallets: malware accesses Ethereum, Bitcoin, Exodus, Electrum, MetaMask, Phantom, Atomic keystores. Article phrase: 'Targets 18 Browsers, Crypto Wallets, and Discord Tokens'. Single UC_CRYPTO_WALLET template insufficient; wallet keystore access pattern more specific than filesystem paths alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-wallet-process access to multiple wallet keystores within 60-second window across Ethereum\keystore, Bitcoin\wallet.dat, Exodus wallets, Electrum wallets, and browser-extension wallet Local Storage directories. Escalate on recursive directory enumeration patterns preceding archive creation (RAR, ZIP) to staging directories.

suggestion.title: Remote Access / RAT Behavior Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'can take full control of an infected machine'—explicit remote command execution capability. Missing from briefing despite being core attack vector. Phrase: 'Hidden Remote Access'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for interactive session spawning (explorer.exe parent changed, WinLogon spawning cmd.exe), persistence registry paths (Run, RunOnce, HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon), and bidirectional network persistence to article IOCs after initial malware execution.

suggestion.title: Discord Token/Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article names Discord tokens as explicit target: 'Targets 18 Browsers, Crypto Wallets, and Discord Tokens'. Not covered by generic UC_BROWSER_STEALER. Requires Discord-specific data locations and API patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag non-Discord processes accessing AppData\Local\Discord directories, LocalStorage, or reading leveldb/sqlite databases where tokens are cached. Monitor for HTTPS connections from non-Discord processes to discord.com API endpoints, especially to /api/v*/auth or /api/v*/users/@me endpoints immediately post-malware execution.

suggestion.title: Telegram Underground Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions discovery vector: 'Discovered through underground channels linked to Telegram'. Implies Telegram distribution mechanism should be detected. Phrase establishes infection pathway not in IOC list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Telegram.exe, telegram.exe, or Telegram client process performing file downloads to user temp/Downloads directories, especially .exe/.msi/.scr files. Correlate against article domains/IPs for secondary staging. Monitor for legitimate Telegram infrastructure abuse followed by process execution and pivot to article C2.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Database Bulk Operations
suggestion.rationale: Targets '18 Browsers' but UC_BROWSER_STEALER detects single-file access. Stealers perform batch operations: sequential reads across all browser credential stores in <30 seconds, followed by copy/archive to staging. Current UC misses exfiltration prep phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process reading multiple browser credential files (Chrome Login Data, Firefox logins.json, Brave/Edge equivalents) within short time window, followed by file copy/move operations to temp/AppData staging directories, then followed by compression tool invocation (7z, WinRAR, built-in tar).

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails with Credential-Harvesting Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article states group 'using social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials'; domain naming pattern (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) strongly suggests fake authentication portals. No phishing detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with urgency language targeting cloud storage users (Office 365, Google Workspace, OneDrive, Dropbox), containing embedded links to attacker domains. Flag emails requesting password re-entry, MFA re-enrollment, or security verification from external senders. Correlate with user clicks to the identified domains.

suggestion.title: Brute Force and Credential Stuffing Against Cloud Storage APIs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector described as 'steal cloud storage credentials'—requires detection of multiple failed auth attempts and subsequent successful login, yet pipeline generated no credential-access use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts (5+ in 10 minutes) against cloud storage services from internal users, followed by successful login with different client IP/user-agent, particularly from the indicator IPs. Alert on successful login immediately after phishing campaign timing.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Pink Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes victim data being 'listed' on dedicated leak site launched May 31, 2026. Pipeline did not generate exfiltration detection for the identified C2 domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file transfers or data exports (compressed archives, database dumps, credential caches) to the identified domains passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com. Correlate with recent successful cloud storage authentication and large volume outbound connections from compromised endpoints.

suggestion.title: Fake Passkey / MFA Enrollment Interception
suggestion.rationale: All three attacker domains contain 'passkey' + administrative verb terminology (add/deploy), indicating modern MFA bypass or FIDO2 interception lures—a critical detection gap given the specific naming pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user navigation to domains containing 'passkey' + (add|deploy|enroll|register|setup) that are not in approved cloud provider CNAME records. Alert especially on clicks from phishing email campaigns and followed by MFA re-setup activity in legitimate cloud account audit logs.

suggestion.title: Enriched Pink Attribution Alerting (CL-CRI-1147)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline identified cluster code CL-CRI-1147 but did not create enriched detection rules tagging network events with Pink actor attribution and kill-chain context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Any detection hitting the six IOCs should be auto-enriched with CL-CRI-1147 attribution, Pink threat group name, attack narrative summary, and kill-chain phase. Create a master alert that correlates: phishing email → credential harvest domain click → failed auth spike → successful auth from attacker IP → data exfil to leak site domain.

suggestion.title: Python .pth Malicious Startup Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file, which then tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script.' This is the core execution vector but no detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .pth files created or modified in Python site-packages directories, especially those with recent timestamps or unusual ownership. Correlate with Python interpreter startup followed by child process spawning (curl, wget, Bun binary). Flag process chains where Python → external runtime (Bun) execute immediately after startup with network activity.

suggestion.title: Bun JavaScript Runtime Download and Execution from Python Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states the malware 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script _index.js.' This delivery mechanism and execution chain is specific and detectable but was not captured in any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections from Python processes to github.com for Bun binary downloads (oven-sh/bun releases). Alert on Bun process spawning from non-standard directories (temp, site-packages). Monitor for Python → curl/wget → Bun → _index.js execution chains, especially if the Bun binary is downloaded immediately after Python startup.

suggestion.title: Harvesting and Exfiltration of Developer Secrets to GitHub Actions Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific credential targets: 'GitHub tokens, npm/PyPI/RubyGems tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes/Vault credentials, SSH keys, Docker credentials, .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, shell histories, Claude/MCP configuration files' and exfil method: 'automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions.' No detection use case for this systematic harvesting and staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser processes (Python, JavaScript) accessing credential files: .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, .ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, .aws/credentials, shell history files. Correlate file reads with GitHub authentication or API operations (git push, gh api). Flag when developer tool subprocesses enumerate multiple credential sources in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Spoofed Anthropic API Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'A second exfiltration method based on direct HTTPS also exists, pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage.' This is an explicit C2 endpoint but was not extracted as an IOC or detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS POST requests to api.anthropic.com/v1/api from Python or Bun processes; this endpoint is non-existent and not used by legitimate Anthropic clients. Alert if credentials or encoded payloads appear in request bodies. Correlate with prior file access to .env, SSH keys, and other credential sources.

suggestion.title: Persistence via systemd Services, LaunchAgents, and GitHub Workflow Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used.' None of these persistence vectors were captured in detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of systemd service files in /etc/systemd/system or ~/.config/systemd/user with Python/Bun interpreter references. On macOS, alert on LaunchAgent plist creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents. Detect modification of GitHub workflows (.github/workflows) and Claude/MCP config files (.claude/claude.json or similar) by non-standard processes. Correlate with supply-chain compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Russian Locale Checks and StepSecurity Harden-Runner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The malware also features some evasion mechanisms, such as checking for Russian locales/environments, and security tools such as StepSecurity Harden-Runner.' This intentional defense evasion logic is not represented in any detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor _index.js execution for conditional logic checking LANG, LC_ALL, or LC_* environment variables for Russian locales. Alert on process execution that invokes grep/findstr/ps commands searching for 'StepSecurity' or 'Harden-Runner' strings, indicating attacker awareness of CI hardening. Flag conditional execution where malicious behavior is suppressed based on these checks.

suggestion.title: Android: Suspicious APK Installation from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes victims 'redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file' for fake banking app updates. No detection coverage for non-Play-Store APK sourcing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK downloads from GitHub domains (github.com, github.io) to Android devices. Correlate with subsequent suspicious permission requests (NFC access). Flag repos created recently (article's April 10 creation date) hosting payment-card-app-named APKs.

suggestion.title: Phishing: Fake Banking Domain with Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Attack begins when 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials.' No detection for phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lookalike domains mimicking Italian/Spanish banks (Intesa, Caixa, Banca Sella, Nexi, Fideuram, Mooney). Alert on credential submission to these domains followed by APK download offers. Baseline domain creation against banking sector.

suggestion.title: Mobile: NFC Data Exfiltration to WebSocket C2
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'reads the information using Android's IsoDep interface and EMV commands' and 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' No detection for anomalous NFC activity or WebSocket C2 comms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WebSocket connections from Android devices to unknown/external endpoints. Correlate with NFC chip access permissions and EMV command execution. Monitor for IsoDep protocol calls in app lifecycle preceding network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Android: Malformed APK Packaging and Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'introduction of malformed APK packaging to hinder automated analysis' via 'poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP.' Specific anti-analysis technique not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK files with ZIP extraction errors, malformed manifest paths, or incomplete/invalid internal structure. Alert on APK installs that bypass signature verification due to packaging anomalies. Correlate with known malware families.

suggestion.title: Threat Intel: GitHub Repository Abuse for Malware Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GitHub repository used for distributing NFCShare has hosted 56 unique APKs' created April 10, 2026. Enterprise risk signal: legitimate code hosting used as malware CDN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub for newly created repos with payment-app-themed names targeting financial institutions. Flag repos with binary/APK release artifacts and low activity/short lifetime. Alert on mass downloads of APKs from banking-themed repos by Android User-Agents.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering: SMS/Phone Calls from Fake Bank Representatives
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'SMS messages or phone calls from fake bank representatives may also be used as part of the social-engineering process,' establishing multi-channel attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If voice/SMS telemetry available: detect caller ID spoofing mimicking bank numbers, urgency language directing to app updates, requests for personal/card data verification. Correlate with phishing site hits in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Memory Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes 'enables local root access'—textbook privilege escalation. 'One-character' flaw suggests tight code path in privilege-check or capability-handling logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unprivileged processes for privilege transitions to root. Flag unusual system call sequences (prctl, bpf, perf_event_open, capset, mmap with PROT_EXEC) preceding uid/gid changes. Correlate with kernel error messages (dmesg) or capability drops.

suggestion.title: Public Exploit Code Execution for Local Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploits now public'—immediate weaponization risk. Detection must target known public repositories and compiled exploit binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads from GitHub, GitLab, Pastebin, or exploit aggregators containing kernel privilege-escalation payloads. Alert on process chains: curl/wget → gcc/cc → execution of compiled binary → privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: Kernel System Call Abuse by Unprivileged Users
suggestion.rationale: Flaw is explicitly local; attack surface is unprivileged user exploitation of kernel gates. 'One-character' change implies a subtle logic flaw in capability or bounds checking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate kernel syscalls (ioctl, sysctl, mmap, madvise, userfaultfd, bpf) by unprivileged users. Alert on volume spikes, novel parameter combinations, or sequences leading to capability elevation without legitimate context.

suggestion.title: Setuid Binary Chaining for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: One-character kernel flaw may be exploitable via existing setuid/setgid binaries or capability mechanisms. Article context implies local user → root transition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of setuid/setgid binaries followed by unexpected privilege transitions. Flag processes gaining new capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_RAWIO) without legitimate execution lineage. Alert on capability drops or namespace operations.

suggestion.title: Kernel Panic or Memory Safety Violation Following Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: One-character kernel flaws often trigger memory safety issues (NULL dereference, bounds violation). Public exploits will attempt to trigger/suppress panics during privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate kernel-level errors (kernel panic, oops, NULL pointer dereference from dmesg) with preceding unprivileged process activity and subsequent uid/gid elevation. Flag processes that suppress kernel messages (dmesg -n) before triggering exploits.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Tool Requests Without Email Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states HTS 'didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts' — the core vulnerability. Phrase: 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in and hijack accounts'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery flows for reset requests where email ownership is not validated against account metadata. Flag requests providing non-registered email addresses, requests bypassing CSRF/OTP challenges, or recovery initiation without prior account identifier confirmation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Password Reset Requests from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Attackers reset 20,000 accounts via the same vulnerability. Article: 'unauthorized third parties to perform password resets on Instagram user accounts' in coordinated campaign (April 17 – May 31).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline daily account recovery request volume. Alert when a single source IP, user-agent, or session initiates >N requests in M-minute window, or when request rate to account recovery endpoint deviates >2 stddev from historical norm, especially if requests target diverse user identifiers.

suggestion.title: Successful Account Access Following Password Reset Without 2FA
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled' — attackers successfully logged in post-reset. Stated impact: 'gain access to affected Instagram users' contact information, dates of birth, social media posts and content, direct messages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login from new IP/geo immediately following password reset request, particularly when no 2FA challenge occurs. Correlate account sign-in source IP with password reset request origin; flag when IPs diverge or when 2FA is disabled/not enrolled.

suggestion.title: Account Credential Reset from Unverified Recovery Path
suggestion.rationale: HTS allowed password reset without email verification—detect abuse of recovery entry points that bypass normal authentication gates. Article: 'vulnerability in an Instagram account recovery support tool was used to potentially compromise the Instagram accounts'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all requests to account recovery/reset endpoints. Alert on requests that: provide email addresses not registered to the system, skip email confirmation steps, or lack referrer validation. Monitor for requests from residential proxies, Tor exit nodes, or IPs geographically inconsistent with targeted user base.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Exfiltration Post-Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Once accounts were compromised, attackers accessed stored content. Article: 'the attackers could've gained access... to direct messages and communications, account activity and interaction history, profile information, connected accounts and linked services'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised accounts for bulk data access patterns: rapid DM exports, mass story/post downloads, contact list API calls, or attempts to export linked service credentials. Flag access from new IPs within hours of account takeover event.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Disablement of Two-Factor Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Targets lacked 2FA (article: 'accounts... without two-factor authentication'), but detect subsequent 2FA disablement post-compromise. Defense evasion to prevent account re-takeover by legitimate owner.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 2FA disablement requests from IP addresses or user-agents that differ from account's historical baseline. Correlate with prior password reset events and login anomalies. Flag 2FA disablement followed immediately by logout/re-login from different IP.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Third-Party Vendor Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers gained access to a database at a third-party vendor containing customer information' and describes unauthorized access via 'one of its vendors.' No detection use case for vendor-account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor third-party vendor service accounts for login patterns inconsistent with normal business hours, geographic anomalies, or successful logins followed immediately by database access. Track failed authentication attempts to vendor portals and API endpoints. Alert on service account privilege elevation or role changes.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Suspicious Database Query and Export Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes breach of 'database of SoFi Securities (Hong Kong) Limited' with 'customer information' exposure. No use case for detecting abnormal data retrieval or bulk export activity that would indicate exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large-volume SQL queries, database exports (`.bak`, `.sql` dumps), or unusual patterns of sequential record retrieval from customer data tables. Correlate with vendor-account authentication anomalies. Flag queries selecting `personal data` columns outside business-hours.

suggestion.title: Alert on Data Exfiltration via Third-Party Vendor Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Breach confirms 'unauthorized access' and likelihood of data exfiltration from vendor database, yet no use case to detect bulk data transfer or staging before egress. Article notes 'still does not know which specific data may have been exposed,' implying data theft investigation ongoing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual volume of outbound traffic from vendor database servers post-breach discovery date (April 30, 2026). Monitor for compressed archives or database dumps staged in cloud storage or external email-forwarding services. Alert on data transfers to IP ranges outside Hong Kong / corporate footprint.

suggestion.title: Track Vendor Account Access Post-Incident
suggestion.rationale: SoFi 'engaged with a third-party cybersecurity firm to respond,' but no detection use case for monitoring vendor accounts during incident response or post-remediation to detect persistence. Article indicates 'investigation is ongoing'—attacker may retain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor third-party vendor-managed service accounts for new account creation, credential reset, or dormant account reactivation post-April-30-2026. Alert on accounts with access to sensitive databases that were not previously active. Correlate with failed intrusion-remediation timelines.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement from Vendor Infrastructure to SoFi Corporate Networks
suggestion.rationale: Breach occurred at 'third-party vendor' but SoFi's own exposure surface unclear from article. No use case to detect if attacker pivoted from vendor network to SoFi internal systems. Article notes 'added additional safeguards and monitoring to affected accounts'—suggesting concerns about downstream compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication attempts from vendor-network IP ranges to SoFi internal systems. Alert on lateral movement from vendor-facing services to internal customer databases or admin portals. Track VPN or RDP connections from vendor accounts attempting access to systems outside vendor scope.

suggestion.title: Vishing indicators: MFA reset + unusual account access within 1-hour window
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body emphasize 'phone calls' and vishing as PRIMARY attack vector ('using phone calls, screen-sharing tricks'), but zero detection hypothesis for social-engineering credential compromise. This is the INITIAL CONTACT step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MFA reset/password reset followed within 60 minutes by successful login from anomalous country or IP. Higher fidelity if correlated with failed MFA attempts in preceding 2 hours or email forwarding rule changes.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to business-data-leaks.com and similar suspicious-domain patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exfiltrate data' and IOCs include 'business-data-leaks.com' domain, but no detection for outbound data transfer to non-whitelisted domains. Law firm context means sensitive litigation/IP data at extreme risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large file transfers (>100MB) to newly registered domains or domains containing 'leak'/'data'/'ransom' keywords. Flag any outbound connection from attorney/paralegal workstations to business-data-leaks.com specifically. Correlate with RMM tool installation timing.

suggestion.title: Interactive remote-access session (RDP/TeamViewer/VNC active-use events) outside change windows
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'screen-sharing tricks' as core methodology, but no detection for when screen-sharing or interactive RDP is ACTIVE (not just installed). This is hands-on-keyboard compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for interactive logons (RDP type 10, network type 3) or TeamViewer/AnyDesk active sessions during non-business hours or from unexpected source IPs. Flag sessions lasting >30 minutes with high network I/O (likely data staging).

suggestion.title: Failed authentication events followed by successful login with token-based access
suggestion.rationale: Vishing attackers social-engineer credentials then use them. Article describes credential theft via phone but no detection for attacker-use of harvested creds post-initial-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 3+ failed login attempts for a user account within 10 minutes, followed by successful login from different IP/device within 30 minutes. High confidence if followed by RMM tool installation or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Vishing Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'UNC3753 Used Vishing' as primary attack vector. Vishing (voice phishing) is social engineering targeting credential exfiltration and MFA bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phone calls from external numbers to targeted employees immediately followed by failed/successful credential entry attempts, especially to sensitive accounts. Flag calls requesting remote access, password resets, or MFA codes. Correlate with failed login attempts and anomalous subsequent successful authentications.

suggestion.title: Post-Vishing Credential Compromise Activity
suggestion.rationale: Vishing campaigns succeed by extracting credentials or MFA bypass; subsequent unauthorized access is the key indicator. Article describes campaign targeting data theft, implying credential-based access follows social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins from new/unusual locations, impossible-travel logins, or off-hours access immediately after reported vishing contact. Monitor for multi-factor authentication bypass attempts, unusual application consent grants, and lateral privilege escalation from a newly compromised credential.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly involves 'Data Theft' and 'Extortion' — exfiltration of sensitive data is the stated objective. Must detect bulk downloads, email forwarding rules, cloud sync activity, and file-share access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large file downloads or bulk email forwarding rule creation from compromised credential. Monitor for unusual access to sensitive file shares (HR, Finance, Legal), non-human-hours access patterns, and data staging to cloud storage (OneDrive, personal Dropbox, Google Drive). Detect PowerShell downloads of file archives.

suggestion.title: Physical Intrusion & Badge Cloning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Physical Intrusions' as attack method. Badge cloning, unauthorized facility access, or tailgating may leave artifacts in access-control logs and camera feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate badge swipes with employee schedule (flagging off-hours or vacation access). Detect multiple badge uses in geographically impossible timeframes (tailgating). Alert on badge clone attempts (same badge UID appearing in multiple locations simultaneously). Cross-reference unauthorized access with credential compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Ransom Extortion Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign is characterized as 'Extortion Campaign' — threat actors will contact victims with demands. Detect inbound ransom notes, extortion mailboxes, and communication channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails containing common extortion keywords ('ransom', 'payment', 'your data has been stolen', 'BitcoinAddress', threat actor names). Monitor for contact to known data-leak forums or darknet sites. Flag anomalous attachments claiming to be proof-of-exfiltration (sample files with customer PII).

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Infrastructure & Command-Control
suggestion.rationale: UNC3753 campaigns likely involve C2 infrastructure, malware, or staging servers. IOCs (domains, IPs, file hashes) should be extracted and monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and outbound connections to known UNC3753 infrastructure (crowdsourced via OSINT, ISACs, threat feeds). Alert on traffic to anonymization services, bulletproof hosters, and dynamic DNS providers. Detect beaconing patterns (regular outbound connections at fixed intervals to the same IP/domain).

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Binary Execution on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances' — expect file execution, process spawning, or library loading from untrusted directories. Pipeline extracted nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of binaries named BRICKSTORM or variants; track child processes spawned from appliance-owned service accounts. Flag cross-architecture binary execution (e.g., BSD ELF headers on Linux systems).

suggestion.title: Unusual Binary Ingestion on Linux Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'BSD Variant' — foreign architecture binary being transferred and executed on Linux. Article should detail delivery method (T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TFTP, HTTP, or SCP transfers writing executable files to /tmp or web-root directories on appliances. Cross-reference with file signatures: BSD ELF (0x7f 0x45 0x4c 0x46) on Linux-native asset.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo C2 Callback from Compromised Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Named actor VerdantBamboo → assume command-and-control infrastructure. Article should describe callback protocol, destinations, or TTPs; pipeline captured none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline egress from Linux appliances; flag DNS requests or HTTP(S) callbacks to suspicious domains. BRICKSTORM likely uses HTTP/S or DNS for C2. Correlate with process execution of BRICKSTORM binary.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation by BRICKSTORM
suggestion.rationale: BSD variant on Linux suggests cross-platform stealth. Article likely details cron jobs, systemd units, or library injection; pipeline found nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/cron.d, /var/spool/cron, systemd drop-in directories (/etc/systemd/system.d), and LD_PRELOAD env vars for BRICKSTORM artifacts. Alert on modification of rc.local or init scripts by non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Post-Exploitation on Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Standard APT post-compromise behavior. Article should mention system enumeration, neighbor discovery, or credential hunting; none extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual process chains: whoami, id, uname -a, ifconfig, netstat, arp -a spawned as children of BRICKSTORM or suspicious parent processes. Flag access to /etc/shadow or /root/.ssh.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Malware Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: BSD binary on Linux suggests anti-analysis. Article context implies filename spoofing or legitimate-process impersonation; not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes with names matching syslog, ntpd, sshd, or other appliance daemons but with mismatched file paths (not in /usr/sbin or /usr/bin). Hash mismatch vs. known-good appliance package manifests.

suggestion.title: Emails Impersonating AI Service Brands (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini)
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes AI brands used as social engineering lure; metadata keywords confirm credential theft vector. Pipeline missed all phishing/initial-access detection for this named attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with From/Reply-To spoofing known AI brands (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind domains), suspicious urgency language (verify account, update subscription), and links to credential-harvesting domains or AiTM proxies. Flag discrepancies in sender domain legitimacy vs. branding.

suggestion.title: AiTM Proxy Activity Harvesting AI Service Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Metadata keyword 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' is explicit; no use case generated. This is a known credential-interception pattern combining phishing + relay attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious email phishing (From AI brand) with authentication anomalies: sign-in from unexpected geography/IP, followed by credential use from different IP, within minutes. Also monitor network outbound connections to known AiTM relay infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via AI-Themed Fake Login Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle explicitly frames credential theft; pipeline generated no detection for fake login pages or form interception. Missing coverage for post-click detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution spawning credential-prompt dialogs or browser sessions to newly-registered domains mimicking OpenAI/Anthropic/Google UI. Flag SSL certificates issued to lookalike domains within 24h of phishing campaign launch.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Auth Events Post-AI-Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft (metadata) must be paired with post-compromise auth detection. Pipeline omitted behavioral correlation layer entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After mass phishing (AI-brand lure detection), flag failed login attempts to compromised accounts from attacker-controlled IPs, succeeded by lateral attempts to enterprise SaaS (Slack, Salesforce) using harvested credentials.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Domain Registration for AI Services
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on brand impersonation; no IOC or infrastructure detection generated. Missing network indicator layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries to domains homographic/typosquatted against OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral (e.g., openai-verify.com, claude-security-check.net). Cross-reference against domain registration timestamps and WHOIS privacy abuse.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs'—implies AI-generated email content at scale. Pipeline generated no UC for email ingestion or content analysis despite this being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email volume and content entropy from external senders spiking above baseline. Flag emails with unusual linguistic patterns (hallmark of LLM generation), lookalike domains, urgency language, and requests for credential entry or document access. Correlate with domain reputation and sender authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) failures.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Phishing Portal
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns inherently target credential harvesting. No use case for detecting credential entry or submission events post-link-click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user clicks on external links in emails (URLClickEventData or equivalent) followed by POST requests to non-corporate domains within minutes. Flag credential submission events (form POST with username/password fields) to newly registered or spoofed domains.

suggestion.title: Bulk Phishing Email Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'alert volume' and SOC overload—implies high-volume campaigns. No UC for detecting mass distribution patterns across recipients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on externally-sourced emails with identical or near-duplicate subject lines and bodies sent to >50 internal recipients within a 30-minute window. Correlate sender domain reputation and TLS/SPF status.

suggestion.title: Malicious Document Execution from Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Phishing often uses Office/PDF attachments as payload vectors. No UC for document open, macro execution, or child process spawning from attachments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office/PDF applications spawning child processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe, rundll32) immediately after file open from temp/downloads folders. Flag suspicious macro execution with network callbacks to external C2 or credential-harvesting domains.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Domain Registration and Campaign Launch
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing requires infrastructure. Article mentions 'scale' but no detection for domain registration or DNS queries to newly-registered phishing domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect internal DNS queries to newly-registered domains (created <7 days, Whois age) similar to known corporate domain names (typosquats, subdomain spoofs). Flag HTTP/S connections to these domains with User-Agent strings typical of phishing reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: VPN Connection Attempt Using Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies vulnerability affecting deployments 'configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' and mitigation includes 'configure global properties for Remote Access VPN Authentication to IKEv2 only.' IKEv1 usage is the enabling misconfiguration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN gateway logs for connection attempts using IKEv1 key exchange. In 2026 context, IKEv1 is legacy and anomalous; flag any unauthenticated or pre-auth connection phases on IKEv1 channels to Check Point Remote Access VPN or Mobile Access gateways.

suggestion.title: VPN Access Bypassing Machine Certificate Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability occurs when deployments 'do not require a machine certificate for connections' and remediation mandates 'set the Machine Certificate Authentication as mandatory.' Absence of cert validation is core to authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN connection establishment that completes without machine certificate validation. Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access deployments without mandatory machine cert requirement are exploitable; baseline normal cert-authenticated sessions and flag certificate-free pathways.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated VPN Session Establishment via CVE-2026-50751
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-50751 as allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication' and 'establish a remote access VPN connection.' This is the direct attack signature for the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Remote Access / SSL VPN session establishment on Check Point gateways where authentication is bypassed or missing. Monitor for successful VPN tunnel negotiation without successful credential validation or challenge-response completion.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Post-Exploitation Following VPN Compromise (Qilin)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' after CVE-2026-50751 exploitation. This ties VPN breach directly to ransomware deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate successful VPN bypasses (unauthenticated sessions) with subsequent endpoint-level ransomware activity: mass file encryption. Hunt for Qilin indicators within 24-48 hours of anomalous VPN access to organizations matching Qilin's typical high-value targets.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Support Enabled on VPN Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Mitigation guidance includes 'remove support for the legacy remote access client.' Presence of legacy client support on VPN gateways is a configuration indicator directly enabling this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access gateway configurations for enabled legacy client support. Any gateway still accepting legacy remote access clients is vulnerable to CVE-2026-50751; flag for immediate upgrade to modern client versions.

suggestion.title: Certificate Validation Bypass in IKEv1 Site-to-Site VPN (CVE-2026-50752 MITM)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-50752 as 'certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections.' While no wild exploitation noted yet, MITM on critical VPN links is high-impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 site-to-site VPN connections for certificate validation failures or MITM indicators. Implement certificate pinning and alarm on unexpected certificate changes. Flag any IKEv1 usage on critical site-to-site links and mandate IKEv2 upgrade.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow any authenticated user' and 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited'—implies exposed LiteLLM instances are active targets. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure hunts despite article explicitly recommending 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-facing LiteLLM services via port discovery (8000, 4000, or custom ports), version fingerprinting, or authentication endpoints. Correlate with vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-42271. Flag instances without recent patch dates (>2026-06-22).

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Detection in LiteLLM Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'command injection vulnerability' explicitly. Pipeline mapped only T1190 but missed T1059.001 (Command Line Interface) despite the core attack being arbitrary command execution: 'run arbitrary commands on the host.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/API requests to LiteLLM endpoints for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(…), |, &, ;, >, <), common injection patterns (/bin/sh, bash -c, cmd.exe /c), and command substitution syntax in request parameters. Focus on authenticated sessions using low-privilege keys.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from LiteLLM Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Core threat is 'arbitrary commands on the host'—successful injection results in child process creation from the LiteLLM service or Python runtime. Pipeline did not suggest process-level detection despite execution being the ultimate impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, python) spawned by the LiteLLM application process, especially with low entropy or obfuscated command lines. Baseline typical LiteLLM child-process behaviors to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Vulnerability Scanner Match Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable" because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet—patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero validation or scanner-output hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, InsightVM) for CVE-2026-42271 matches. Validate scanner-reported patch versions against actual running version (via /version endpoint or process inspection). Flag false-negatives where scanner reports 'patched' but runtime is outdated.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Authentication Anomaly (Low-Privilege Key Usage)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' can exploit. Pipeline missed that low-privilege internal key compromise/misuse is the attack surface, not just public exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM authentication logs for low-privilege key usage from unusual geolocations, IP ranges, or time-of-day patterns. Alert on repeated failed command-injection attempts (payloads that fail syntax but succeed in reaching the application).

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Patch Status Baseline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with explicit federal due-date (2026-06-22). Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and this is 'currently being exploited.' Pipeline should have generated a patch-status inventory hunt tied to the deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all LiteLLM instances and their versions across fleet. Alert on any version <[patched_version_tbd] or instances missing version information. Correlate with patch-management tickets to verify remediation status against 2026-06-22 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway CVE-2026-50751 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-50751 in Check Point Security Gateway as CISA KEV (known exploited in the wild). Pipeline extracted zero CVE or product IOCs; vulnerability matching is foundational for any exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output and asset inventory for Check Point Security Gateway appliances running vulnerable versions matching CVE-2026-50751. Alert on any instance not patched by Federal due date 2026-06-11.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass — Missing Credential Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper authentication in IKEv1 key exchange' enabling 'unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication.' Pipeline failed to capture this credential access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 phase-1 key exchange logs for successful completions that lack corresponding pre-authentication user password submission events. Flag anomalous IKEv1 sessions that proceed to tunnel establishment without password challenge or 2FA verification.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Tunnel Establishment Without Credential Submission
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: attacker 'establish[es] a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' No detection use case generated despite this being the explicit exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when VPN tunnel establishment on Check Point gateways occurs without prior successful user authentication in logs. Correlate tunnel start times with authentication log absence for same user/session ID.

suggestion.title: Repeated IKEv1 Exploitation Attempts — Automated Scanner Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Active CISA KEV status indicates automated scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild. Pipeline did not suggest detections for failed exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point gateways for high-frequency IKEv1 initiation attempts from single/clustered IPs followed by immediate session resets or authentication failures — signature of automated CVE-2026-50751 scanners.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Patch Status — Pre-Deadline Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Federal due date 2026-06-11 (2 days away). No inventory/compliance detection suggested despite regulatory deadline being core motivation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate automated inventory report of Check Point Security Gateway appliances with version cross-reference to CVE-2026-50751 patch status. Alert with escalation 48 hours before Federal due date on any unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: UniFi Auth Bypass via URI Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes root cause: 'mismatch between how UniFi OS validates and routes incoming requests' — 'authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version.' Attackers craft requests appearing auth-exempt but resolving to protected routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with path traversal patterns (double slashes, dot-dot sequences, URL-encoded characters, case variations) that bypass authentication validation. Alert on requests to protected endpoints lacking auth headers after receiving crafted URI patterns designed to exploit normalization divergence.

suggestion.title: Command Injection in Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-34910 is 'command injection flaw' exploited by 'passing unvalidated user input into shell command' at package-update endpoint. Researchers explicitly recommend monitoring 'requests to ucs/update/latest_package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated requests to '/ucs/update/latest_package' or similar endpoints containing shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, command substitution). Correlate with unexpected child process spawning from 'ucs-update' service within seconds of request.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Processes Spawned from UCS-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends monitoring 'suspicious child processes under ucs-update' as attack execution indicator following successful command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal ucs-update child processes and package management activity. Alert on spawning of interactive shells (bash, sh), interpreters (python, perl), or network utilities (curl, wget, nc, socat) from ucs-update service account, particularly in parent-child chains inconsistent with normal patching.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Sudo Privilege Escalation from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explains 'service account's sudo privileges make privilege escalation trivial' — commands initially execute under service account but escalate to root via sudo without password. Researchers recommend monitoring 'unexpected sudo commands.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo execution from UniFi service account reaching UID 0 without password prompt visible in audit logs. Detect sudo commands with nopass configuration or sudoers TTY requirement bypass from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Protected Internal Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass chain enabling 'access to the network' and reach vulnerable endpoint without authentication. Researchers recommend monitoring for 'requests containing /api/auth/validate-sso/' as detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to '/api/auth/validate-sso/' lacking valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Detect access to protected internal APIs immediately following malformed or path-traversal crafted requests from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: RCE Execution Without Prior Authentication Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns 'there is no failed-login trail to look for' because exploit requires zero credentials. Absence of authentication events preceding code execution is anomalous baseline for UniFi OS and signals unauthenticated RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate code execution signals (child process spawning, command invocation, outbound network connections) from UniFi OS with complete absence of preceding authentication logs. Alert on execution activity originating from UniFi service without corresponding login or session-establishment events.

suggestion.title: HTTP requests to PHP file-load endpoints with phar:// URL in parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack vector: 'HTTP request with malicious phar:// URL to PHPSpreadsheet endpoint.' Requests to spreadsheet-processing endpoints containing file parameter (filename, file, path, url) with phar:// scheme should be captured at application or WAF layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET/POST requests to PHP file-loading endpoints (identified by parameter names: filename, file, path, url, filepath, etc.) where parameter value contains 'phar://', especially with 3+ consecutive slashes. Correlate with response codes to identify which attempts reached vulnerable code paths (5xx errors vs 200 may indicate bypass success).

suggestion.title: PHP application logs showing parse_url or stream-wrapper errors correlated with phar:// payload
suggestion.rationale: Article's core vulnerability mechanism: the fix calls 'parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_SCHEME)' and checks for stream wrapper presence. Failed filter checks or error logs mentioning stream wrapper rejection would indicate exploit attempts hitting that code path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search PHP/application error logs for errors or warnings containing 'stream wrapper', 'phar', 'parse_url', or 'prohibitWrappers' that correlate with HTTP 5xx responses or file-load exceptions. Presence of 'phar://' in stack traces or filter-rejection messages indicates exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unscheduled child process spawning from PHP-FPM/httpd following phar:/// HTTP request
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in RCE. Code from the phar archive would execute with web-server privileges. Temporal correlation of phar:/// HTTP request (UC_3_2) followed by unexpected process spawning strengthens post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In a 60–180 second window following detection of phar:/// HTTP request (UC_3_2), hunt for child processes spawned by php-fpm, httpd, or apache2 where parent_process_command_line does NOT match known, allowlisted task names (mail, opcache, backgroundjobs). Prioritize: shells, network tools (curl, wget, nc), scripting languages (python, perl), and commands with unusual arguments.

suggestion.title: PHP temp directory activity (file creation/extraction) by web-server process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes phar:// wrapper loading and parsing. PHP internally extracts phar archives to temp directories during processing. Monitoring temp directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, Windows temp) for phar-related file operations may indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/write activity in standard temp directories (/tmp, /var/tmp, C:\Windows\Temp, C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Temp) initiated by php-fpm, httpd, nginx, or w3wp processes. Flag rapid file creation (>5 files/min) or extraction of files with executable extensions (.so, .exe, .sh, .bat) that correlate in time with phar:/// HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Phar archive file upload or intermediate file creation in web-accessible directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack loading phar from URL (phar:///path/file.phar/inner). An attacker must either craft a malicious phar archive or load one from external source. Detecting .phar file uploads or staging in web-accessible directories (webroot, upload dirs) is a pre-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file uploads or creation of .phar files in web-accessible directories (typically identified by PHP include_path, document_root, or known upload directories). Alert on .phar file writes by web-server processes or within HTTP POST request context. Correlate with subsequent phar:// access patterns.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion: Multiple parse_url calls or scheme detection bypass patterns in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly emphasizes the patch bypass: the filter 'check is not equivalent to "does the path contain a wrapper".' The attacker deliberately crafts malformed URLs to evade parse_url() filtering. Repeated or progressive bypass attempts may appear in application instrumentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In applications with verbose logging, look for sequences of file-load attempts with progressively modified path formats (phar://, phar:///, phar:////, etc.) or repeated calls to file-loading functions with slightly altered arguments. Batch of similar requests within short time window with different 'slash counts' indicates deliberate filter-bypass probing.

suggestion.title: Browser process spawning osascript with dynamic AppleScript payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'chrome_tabs plugin interpolates [unescaped URL]' into AppleScript → injection. Pipeline missed the parent-process signal: Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari should never spawn osascript with user-controlled URL data. Cite: 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection via Unescaped URL'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chrome, Brave, Edge, or Safari process creates child osascript process with command-line arguments containing URL fragments, special characters, or 'tell application'/'do shell script' keywords. Legitimate browser-to-applescript workflows are rare; flag any spawn of osascript from browser parent.

suggestion.title: URL parameter with shell metacharacters passed to AppleScript interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'Improper Control of Generation of Code' (CWE-94): unescaped URL parameters land directly in AppleScript. Detection should monitor for URLs with shell metacharacters (backtick, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&) being parsed by any script interpreter. Cite: 'unescaped URL'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser extensions or processes that parse URL parameters and pass them to script interpreters (osascript, jxa, ruby -e, etc.) without validation. Flag URLs containing backticks, dollar-parentheses, semicolons, pipes in a single request to known vulnerable plugin.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin process execution or persistence
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed software-centric tracking. Anyquery v0.4.4 is the affected version; any execution from known plugin directory or with 'anyquery' in process tree should be baselined. Cite: 'Affected version 0.4.4 (commit 0abd460)'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of Anyquery binary (typically ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Extensions/...) or any process with 'anyquery' in path/name. Cross-reference against known-good Anyquery installations or baseline deviations in child processes spawned.

suggestion.title: macOS JXA (JavaScript for Automation) execution with shell commands
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection'. JXA is JavaScript variant that can invoke `Application('System Events').doShellScript()`. Pipeline should detect JXA (node, osascript -l JavaScript, Safari Scripts, etc.) spawning shell commands. Cite: 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect osascript invoked with '-l JavaScript' flag, or JavaScript engines (node, Electron) invoking macOS automation APIs. Look for Application('System Events').doShellScript() or ObjC.import('Foundation') patterns in command line or script content.

suggestion.title: Anyquery extension loading or plugin activation from untrusted source
suggestion.rationale: Initial-access vector is T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Pipeline should detect Anyquery plugin installation, update, or activation from non-canonical source (e.g., side-loaded extension, malicious URL, modified manifest). Cite: 'chrome_tabs plugin'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari extension installation, manifest modifications, or plugin script reloads. Flag any update or install of Anyquery or similar productivity plugins from non-official source, or modifications to plugin code after installation.

suggestion.title: Rapid Account Creation on Gogs Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false)... unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account'. No baseline or anomaly detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on account creation rates exceeding baseline on Gogs instances. Correlate new account creation with subsequent repository creation within same session. Flag accounts created from non-corporate IP ranges or TOR exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Repository Creation with Rebase Merge Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' Core exploitation pattern absent from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new repository creation by non-admin users immediately followed by rebase-merge option enablement. Alert if rebase merge enabled on repositories with zero other collaborators. Correlate repository creation timestamp with rebase configuration change timestamp.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access any repositories (including private ones)' and 'read any repository'. No detection of repository access-control bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repository read/clone operations for users not listed in repository permissions. Alert on private repository access from non-collaborator accounts. Track clone volume from single source repositories.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Payloads in Merge Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article names vulnerability as 'argument injection vulnerability' affecting 'Merge()' code path. No detection of malformed merge parameters with shell metacharacters or escape sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs merge API requests for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, &&, ||) in merge parameters. Flag rebase merge operations with non-standard argument formatting. Alert on request URLs containing encoded special characters in sensitive parameters.

suggestion.title: Code Modification via Merge from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'alter any hosted source code'. No detection of suspicious merge commits or code injection via merge operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag merge commits from single-contributor repositories (owner-only repos) that introduce code. Monitor for commits modifying build pipelines, CI/CD configs, or authentication code. Alert on merge operations removing or disabling security checks.

suggestion.title: Gogs Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev' vulnerable; patched in 0.14.3. Software inventory/fingerprinting gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response headers and version strings for Gogs fingerprints. Alert on versions ≤0.14.2 or 0.15.0+dev in scope. Cross-reference against CVE-2025-8110 and related CVE list for remediation tracking.

suggestion.title: Malspam Delivery — Loader Attachment / Link
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'A recent malspam campaign has been caught using Google's own DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims toward a fileless .NET loader.' Spearphishing delivery is the initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with suspicious loader-type attachments or DoubleClick-proxied URLs. Correlate email receipt with subsequent unsigned .NET or PowerShell child processes. Flag email-client process spawning rundll32, regsvcs, or native CLR hosts within seconds of message arrival.

suggestion.title: Google DoubleClick Redirect Chain to Malicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: 'using Google's own DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims toward a fileless .NET loader.' Trusted domain abuse for redirect-chain evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multi-hop HTTP redirects originating from doubleclick.net that ultimately resolve to the seven attacker domains (fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, bth.startthewave.org, pengajian.muliastudy.com, andrefelipedonascime1778799406970.2241107.meusitehostgator.com.br, catalogo.castrouria.com, xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net). Alert on redirect depth ≥3 through legitimate infrastructure → attacker C2.

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Loader In-Memory Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fileless .NET loader, a type of malware that runs [...]' — in-memory reflective loading without traditional file artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned .NET processes (csc.exe, ngen.exe, or hosting processes) spawned by email clients or browsers with no corresponding on-disk executable. Look for System.Reflection.Assembly.Load* or System.Activator.CreateInstance calls. Correlate with outbound network to the seven C2 domains.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback to Known Loader Domains — Network IOC
suggestion.rationale: Article provides six attacker C2 domains for command delivery post-compromise. Standard network IOC hunt on provided infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS query or HTTP/HTTPS connection to the six attacker domains: fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, bth.startthewave.org, pengajian.muliastudy.com, andrefelipedonascime1778799406970.2241107.meusitehostgator.com.br, catalogo.castrouria.com, xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net. Correlate with the five SHA256 hashes for process identity.

suggestion.title: Known Fileless Loader SHA256 Hash Match
suggestion.rationale: Article provides five SHA256 hashes of the .NET loader payloads. Standard file hash IOC for endpoint detection on process or file artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match the five provided SHA256 hashes (d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5, c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6, c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18, f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348, e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd) against running processes, in-memory modules, and network-based file feeds. Flag any child process spawning from email or browser contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WhatsApp Message with Phishing Link
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes NSO attack used phishing delivery via WhatsApp; detection needed for messages containing shortened URLs, urgency language, or mismatches between sender identity and linked domain ('NSO Group's new WhatsApp phishing attack').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WhatsApp or messaging-app proxy logs for messages containing URL shorteners, encoded payloads, or domain mismatches. Flag conversations from known-spoofed or attacker-controlled accounts linking to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: NSO Phishing Domain Registration & C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article implies NSO registered or controlled infrastructure to host phishing pages; detection should cover newly-registered domains matching NSO patterns and HTTPS handshakes to known-NSO IP blocks ('NSO Group's new...attack').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WHOIS registration patterns (bulk registrations, short TTLs, reseller overlap) with NSO historical IOCs. Flag endpoints communicating to newly-registered domains within hours of phishing campaign initiation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Link Click
suggestion.rationale: WhatsApp phishing attacks typically harvest session tokens or 2FA codes; detection should capture POST requests to credential-capture endpoints disguised as legitimate login flows ('phishing attack').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to URLs containing phishing keywords (confirm, verify, login, update) with username/password/OTP parameters. Correlate with legitimate WhatsApp or Meta login endpoints to identify false positives.

suggestion.title: Meta Defensive Block—Signal Antiphishing Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Meta Blocks...attack'; detection should monitor Meta platform logs for blocked messages, quarantined links, or automated phishing-rule triggers that indicate NSO campaign detection ('Meta Blocks NSO Group's').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Meta's phishing-detection telemetry (message quarantine events, link blocks, sender-reputation scores) to retroactively identify users exposed to NSO phishing before platform-wide block took effect.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK / WhatsApp Package Modification
suggestion.rationale: NSO phishing may also distribute modified WhatsApp APKs to sideload spyware; detection should identify unsigned or re-signed mobile packages attempting installation from external sources ('NSO Group...new...attack' implies novel delivery).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK installations from non-Play-Store sources matching WhatsApp filename patterns. Monitor for code-signing certificate mismatches or spyware-associated signature chains.

suggestion.title: Contempt-Order Linked Domain Takedown—IOC Refresh
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Files Contempt Order'; legal action implies domains/IPs will be seized; detection should update IOC-refresh schedules and watch for attacker re-registration under new registrars ('contempt order').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS resolution for domains previously named in Meta/judicial takedown notices. Flag bulk re-registration of seized-domain variants (typosquats, subdomain pivots) by known-NSO infrastructure.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'purpose-built web shell framework' deployed to IIS servers. No detection for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file writes to IIS root directories (wwwroot, inetpub) with executable extensions (.aspx, .asp, .ashx). Correlate with unusual w3wp.exe child processes or outbound connections. Focus on files with obfuscated content or inconsistent timestamps relative to legitimate app deployments.

suggestion.title: IIS Process C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Narrative indicates C2 infrastructure (IOCs listed as network destinations), but no detection for IIS processes initiating outbound connections to OP-512 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe initiating connections to the 5 supplied IPs/domains. Tune for non-standard ports (443, 8080, 8443) since legitimate IIS outbound is rare. Establish baseline of legitimate outbound from IIS pools and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Cryptographically Obfuscated IIS Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'cryptographically unique' evasion framework designed to bypass detection. No detection for obfuscated or encrypted payloads in IIS logs or memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .aspx/.ashx files with high entropy content (potential encryption/obfuscation), base64 blocks, or strings matching crypto library patterns. Check for unusual YARA or entropy thresholds in IIS web root. Memory dumps of w3wp.exe post-shell execution may reveal decrypted payload analysis opportunities.

suggestion.title: IIS Log Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Web shell implies attacker issuing arbitrary HTTP commands. No detection for suspicious IIS HTTP access patterns (unusual verbs, file extensions, parameter smuggling).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse IIS access logs for non-standard file extensions in requests (.ashx, .asmx, .jsp planted post-compromise), unusual HTTP verbs (MOVE, COPY, PROPFIND), or requests with encoded payloads. Baseline legitimate requests and alert on anomalies, especially from non-organizational source IPs.

suggestion.title: IIS Configuration Registry Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Web shell persistence often requires IIS config changes (app pool identity escalation, module registration). No detection for suspicious registry writes to HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\InetStp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry modifications under HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\InetStp and HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Internet Settings. Alert on app pool identity changes, new handler mappings, or module registrations occurring outside of legitimate patching windows or administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ASP.NET Runtime Execution Post-Shell
suggestion.rationale: Web shells execute commands via ASP.NET runtime (aspnet_wp.exe, w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe). No detection for child process execution from IIS worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as children of w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe, especially with suspicious command-line arguments (web requests, network access, file operations). Correlate with IIS access logs to identify originating HTTP request times. Check for LOLBin execution (certutil, bitsadmin) from IIS processes.

suggestion.title: Discord token theft — access to Discord Local Storage/Cache by non-Discord process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'Steals Discord Tokens' as a primary targeting vector, but provided hunts only cover generic browser credentials. Discord stores session tokens in %APPDATA%\Discord\Local Storage\leveldb and Cache directories distinct from standard browser Login Data paths—warrant specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file operations (reads/copies) against Discord-specific storage directories (Local Storage, Cache, IndexedDB) by processes not running as discord.exe or Discord-related services. Discord token exfiltration is high-confidence signal given no legitimate reason for external process access.

suggestion.title: Remote code execution / RAT callback detection via C2 beaconing
