Payload inspection should match password/token/wallet data patterns (Base64 'password':', 'token':', 'seed phrase' keywords).

suggestion.title: Phishing emails with cloud credential-theft themes targeting enterprise users
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the group uses 'social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials.' This is textbook T1566 spearphishing, yet no email-based phishing hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound emails with cloud-account themes (password reset, verification request, sign-in alert) from external senders to enterprise users. Correlate with sender domain reputation and any URLs pointing to attacker-controlled domains from IOC set.

suggestion.title: Unusual cloud storage account login from attacker-controlled infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials will be used to access cloud storage from the attacker-controlled IPs listed in article IOCs. No hunt for compromised-credential usage was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins to OneDrive/Dropbox/SharePoint accounts from the IOC IPs (185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66) or correlate failed + successful auth from new geolocation post-phishing send.

suggestion.title: Bulk cloud storage data exfiltration post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'listed several initial victims' suggesting stolen data is staged for extortion. No cloud-egress anomaly hunt was generated despite clear exfiltration intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk download/export activity in cloud storage accounts, unusual sharing grants, or downloads to external domains, especially from formerly dormant accounts or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance enumeration of cloud storage content post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Extortion groups systematically map victim environments before exfil to identify high-value data. Article structure implies selective targeting ('already listed several initial victims'), suggesting reconnaissance occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of folders, file searches, or permission-inspection queries in cloud storage immediately following a new login from unfamiliar IP or user agent.

suggestion.title: Cloud storage account modifications and persistence mechanisms post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attackers stealing high-value data often establish secondary access (add forwarding rules, secondary accounts, backup methods). No persistence-mechanism hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for new secondary email accounts added to cloud-storage account recovery options, new app registrations/OAuth grants to third-party services, or unexpected sharing permissions granted to external domains.

suggestion.title: Credential validation against domain infrastructure from IOC set
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three 'passkey'-themed domains (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) suggesting credential-harvesting landing pages. No hunt for users accessing these domains was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enterprise user HTTP/DNS traffic to the three passkey-themed IOC domains. Correlate any hits with phishing email sends and subsequent cloud-storage anomalies from same user account.

suggestion.title: Python .pth File Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file' and recommends 'look for Python packages containing executable .pth startup hooks'. This is the core initial-execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .pth files in Python site-packages directories being created or modified, followed by Python interpreter invocations. Correlate file creation by package-install processes with subsequent Python execution chains.

suggestion.title: Bun JavaScript Runtime Download from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script' and recommends 'unexpected downloads of the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub'. Distinguishes this attack from standard Python malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python or child processes downloading Bun binaries from GitHub release URLs (github.com/oven-sh/bun). Flag downloads of unfamiliar JavaScript runtimes followed by script execution.

suggestion.title: Process Chain: Python → Bun → _index.js Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'process chains where Python launches Bun to execute _index.js'. Direct attack flow recommendation from the researchers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent-child chains: Python → curl/wget → Bun executable → JavaScript. Monitor for Bun executing scripts from /tmp, current directory, or obfuscated filenames.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions'. Primary exfiltration channel specific to developer environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid GitHub API calls: repository creation → workflow file commits → push operations. Correlate with environment variable exports or secret refs in .github/workflows YAML files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Anthropic API Endpoint HTTPS Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage'. Unusual C2 disguise exploiting tool legitimacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS POST/PUT requests to api.anthropic.com/v1/api from non-SDK clients or with non-Anthropic User-Agents. Cross-reference with Python/Bun process execution timing.

suggestion.title: Persistence via systemd and LaunchAgent Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used'. Multiple persistence vectors requiring distinct detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of systemd unit files in /etc/systemd/system and /usr/lib/systemd/system. On macOS, track .plist file creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/. Flag writes to .github/workflows/ and Claude MCP config directories by non-IDE processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Banking APK Downloaded from GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '56 unique APKs that impersonated mobile apps for banks primarily from Italy and Spain' hosted on a GitHub repository 'since April 10'. Detection should flag APK downloads from GitHub URLs using legitimate banking app names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads of .apk files matching banking app name patterns (e.g., *Carte.apk, *CaixaBank*, *Banca*) from GitHub repositories. Flag GitHub repos created within 90 days of download or with typosquatted names. Correlate with visits to phishing sites impersonating banks.

suggestion.title: NFC Card Data Harvesting via Fake Verification Screen
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware using 'fake verification screen to place the cards near the mobile device's NFC chip' and reads 'card number, type, expiry date, and 4-digit PIN'. Direct credential exfiltration via NFC should generate detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag apps with NFC read permissions (android.permission.NFC) that trigger multiple NFC EMV command sequences via IsoDep interface within short time windows. Alert when apps request both NFC permissions and credential input capabilities (keyboard overlay, dialog boxes) in the same session.

suggestion.title: Malformed APK Packaging for Static Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states newer samples include 'poisoned/malformed file paths within the ZIP' causing extraction tools to 'wrongly interpret internal relative paths as filesystem paths and trigger errors'. This is deliberate defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze APK files for malformed ZIP metadata including invalid path structures, non-standard directory ordering, or encoding anomalies. Flag APKs that generate errors during extraction by standard tools but remain executable as indicators of obfuscation intent.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Exfiltration of Payment Card Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel'. WebSocket-based C2 used for stolen financial data is a distinct detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebSocket connections from banking apps or apps with NFC permissions to external hosts on non-standard ports. Flag WebSocket traffic exfiltrating structured data matching card metadata patterns (16-digit numbers, expiry dates, 4-digit codes).

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Redirect to Malicious APK Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain: 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials. Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository'. Site-to-app-download redirect is the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domains with homoglyph/typosquatting similarity to legitimate banks (edit distance <3) that redirect users to APK downloads outside official app stores. Correlate phishing domain visits with subsequent APK installations on same device.

suggestion.title: Banking App Installation with Anomalous Signature or NFC+Credential Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article documents APK installation where 'new variants of NFCShare Android malware are being distributed as fake updates for legitimate banking apps'. Signature mismatch + unusual permission combo flags suspicious banking apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag banking app installations where APK signature issuer or hash does not match official publisher records. Alert on banking apps requesting NFC permissions combined with INPUT_METHOD, CLIPBOARD_READ, or record audio permissions, as legitimate apps rarely need all three.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Load Post-Exploit Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploits Now Public' for local-root kernel flaw. Attackers will load malicious modules or trigger kernel code paths; no detection proposed for insmod/modprobe execution or unsigned module loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod/modprobe execution from unprivileged contexts, kernel module load audit events, or signature validation failures in /lib/modules. Correlate timing with prior suspicious process activity.

suggestion.title: Privilege Elevation Detection via Vulnerable Kernel Version
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Local Root Access' via kernel flaw. Should detect uid/gid elevation anomalies on vulnerable kernel versions matching vuln scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected uid/gid for each process; flag elevation of non-setuid binaries. Correlate elevated-privilege child processes with parent execution from low-privilege accounts on vulnerable kernel versions.

suggestion.title: Kernel Panic / Oops Correlation with Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits commonly trigger crashes, faults, or oops messages. Article describes kernel-level vulnerability; should detect dmesg segfaults, null-pointer dereferences, or stack traces as post-exploitation evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest kernel logs for seg-fault/null-ptr/stack-smash signatures. Correlate crash timestamp with preceding suspicious process execution or network inbound on the host.

suggestion.title: Execution of Public Kernel Exploit PoC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploits Now Public'. PoC binaries or shell scripts will match file hashes or behavioral patterns (direct execution, script interpretation, privilege escalation syscalls).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-sig known kernel exploit PoCs once CVE is identified. Detect execution of binaries named *exploit*, kernel-vuln*, or shell scripts downloading/compiling kernel PoCs.

suggestion.title: Runtime Kernel Exploit Compilation (gcc/clang in /tmp)
suggestion.rationale: Public exploits are source; attackers compile in-place on target. Article signals public PoC; should flag compiler execution by unprivileged users, especially in /tmp or download directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on gcc/clang/ld execution by non-root accounts in /tmp, /dev/shm, or $HOME. Correlate with prior wget/curl or web-browser activity and /proc/sys/kernel/* modifications.

suggestion.title: Bulk Password Reset Requests via Account Recovery Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'exploited a flaw in the company's High Touch Support (HTS) tool...obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in.' No detection proposed despite attackers performing resets at scale. Phrase: 'exploited the fact that HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery tool (HTS or equivalent) for elevated password reset request volume from single source IP, for password resets on accounts with mismatched or unverified email domains, or for resets issued without matching the registered account contact. Baseline per user/per IP and alert on 3+ resets in 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Password Reset Bypass of 2FA
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled' via password reset. This is a post-compromise detection gap. Phrase: 'password reset links that allowed them to log in...without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful login to account immediately after forced password reset if 2FA is not enforced post-reset, or if login source IP differs from historical norm. Correlate password-reset event to login event within 5 minutes with mismatched geo/device.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Connected Accounts and Linked Services Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gained access to 'other connected accounts and linked services' post-takeover. No detection for lateral movement via account linking suggested. Phrase: 'attackers could've gained access to...other connected accounts and linked services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in to linked/connected accounts (Facebook, WhatsApp, Threads, etc.) using credentials obtained from compromised Instagram account. Alert on logins to linked services from IP addresses previously associated with the HTS abuse or password-reset activity.

suggestion.title: Mass Data Exfiltration from Compromised Social Media Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates sensitive data accessible post-compromise: 'direct messages and communications, social media posts and content (photos, videos, stories), account activity and interaction history.' No detection for bulk data access or download patterns. Phrase: 'the attackers could've gained access to affected Instagram users' contact information...direct messages and communications, account activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume API calls to retrieve DMs, posts, photos, or story history from newly compromised accounts. Alert on accounts accessing significantly more messages/media than baseline within 1-hour post-compromise window, or on exports/downloads of account data shortly after unauthorized login.

suggestion.title: HTS Tool Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific attack vector: unverified email addresses in HTS recovery flow. No detection rule for abuse of the HTS service itself. Phrase: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts, they obtained password reset links.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS/account-recovery endpoints for requests where supplied email address does not appear in account records, requests for password resets on non-existent accounts, or requests where email domain/pattern does not match registered account owner domain. Alert on multiple failed verification checks followed by successful reset.

suggestion.title: Mandatory Security Checkpoint Bypass or Delayed Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article states Meta 'enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint.' Detection should flag accounts that bypass or skip re-authentication checkpoints post-compromise. Phrase: 'enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint and asked all affected users to reset their passwords again.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to flagged/checkpoint-enrolled accounts that bypass re-authentication steps, skip 2FA enrollment, or resume normal activity without completing mandatory security re-verification. Alert if checkpoint-flagged account is accessed from different geo/device than the initiating takeover IP within 72 hours.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Access From Third-Party Vendor Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers gained access to a database at a third-party vendor containing customer information.' Core collection phase—pipeline omitted detection for abnormal query patterns, bulk exports, or data extraction from vendor databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor database systems for deviation from baseline query patterns: unexpected SELECT volume on customer PII tables, bulk data exports outside business hours, queries from unusual service accounts, or high-volume exfiltration. Alert on compression of database files followed by outbound transfer.

suggestion.title: Compromised Vendor Credentials or Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential compromise as attack vector: 'unauthorized access to a database.' Pipeline failed to surface T1078 (Valid Accounts) or detection scenarios for vendor system account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline vendor system access patterns; alert on anomalous authentication (new IPs, unusual hours, failed attempts followed by success). Monitor for rapid privilege escalation immediately after credential use. Flag lateral movement within vendor network post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Unmonitored Bulk Data Transfer From Vendor Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: discovery on 'April 30, 2026' after 'unauthorized access to a database'—exfiltration predates detection. Pipeline missed outbound data transfer detection from vendor systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound transfers from vendor database systems exceeding baseline volume. Detect archive files (tar, zip) created from database directories. Monitor egress to untrusted IP ranges or cloud accounts. Flag unusual port usage for data exfiltration (non-standard DB ports, HTTP/HTTPS for large payloads).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation at Third-Party Vendor Prior to Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of database with customer PII implies lateral movement or privilege escalation within vendor environment. Article states breach was discovered post-incident; pipeline omitted privilege escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed logins with vendor systems followed by successful privileged access. Detect rapid creation of admin accounts or service account privilege grants. Monitor for RDP/SSH lateral movement chains across vendor infrastructure targeting database servers.

suggestion.title: Inadequate Logging or Detection Delay at Third-Party Vendor
suggestion.rationale: Article: SoFi 'discovered the incident on April 30, 2026' after 'unauthorized access'—temporal gap indicates unmonitored access. Breach existed before detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for disabled audit logging on vendor database systems, deletion of security event logs, or audit log tampering. Alert on gaps in vendor-supplied logs or timestamps. Audit vendor's logging configuration: missing database activity monitoring, no MFA on database access, overly permissive service account credentials.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Phone Call (Vishing) – Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack chain begins with 'using phone calls' and 'vishing.' First-stage attack vector is completely undetected by pipeline despite being named in headline and body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logon spikes or compromised credential indicators correlating with incoming call center metadata (if available) or unusual caller interaction reports. Look for successful logons from new source IPs within hours of failed authentication clusters from same endpoint.

suggestion.title: RMM Tool Deployed by Non-IT User
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote monitoring software to break into corporate systems.' Core execution phase but pipeline generated zero UCs despite multiple RMM vendors (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ScreenConnect, Splashtop) being common in this threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt RMM installation (process execution, file writes, registry persistence) by non-administrative user accounts. Spike confidence when RMM process spawns within 1 hour of fresh credential use or when parent process is browser or shell (not MSI/installer).

suggestion.title: Screen-Sharing Application Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'screen-sharing tricks' as attack method. No detection rule generated for screen-sharing tools despite being named attack vector alongside RMM and vishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect screen-sharing tool launch (Chrome Remote Desktop, Quick Assist, AnyDesk screen-share mode) by non-admin user without prior IT ticket. Flag if followed by lateral file access to sensitive shares or preceded by unusual logon patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Known Malicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'steal sensitive files' with explicit sink domain 'business-data-leaks.com.' Attack objective is clear but no exfil-phase detection generated. Pipeline failed to extract all 8 IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from file operations (7z.exe, WinRAR, PowerShell compression) or RMM child processes to exfil domain (business-data-leaks.com) and associated IPs (192.236.147.131, 192.236.147.138, 193.141.60.212, 192.236.154.158, 192.236.146.173, 174.169.162.62, 64.94.84.97). High confidence if within 24 hours of RMM execution.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-RMM Foothold
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of 'sensitive files' implies need for elevated access. Attack chain (vishing → RMM → exfil) requires privilege escalation step to access protected data. No detection suggested despite clear logical requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UAC bypass techniques (fodhelper.exe elevation, EventViewer UAC bypass, COM object hijacking) or token impersonation (RunAs, Impersonate) spawned from or within RMM process context. Flag suspicious elevation attempts by RMM-spawned child processes.

suggestion.title: Vishing Attempt – Credential or Information Harvest
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'UNC3753 Used Vishing and Physical Intrusions' — vishing (voice phishing) is the stated initial-access vector. Pipeline did not surface any detection for social engineering phone campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for caller ID spoofing, unusual external PSTN calls to executive or IT staff, and employee reports of unsolicited callers posing as vendors, IT support, or service providers. Correlate with password reset attempts, MFA device registrations, or lateral movement within 24h of reported call.

suggestion.title: Physical Intrusion Indicators – Unauthorized Facility Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Physical Intrusions' as part of attack methodology. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for badge/CCTV anomalies or after-hours facility access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on after-hours badge swipes in critical server rooms, data centers, or executive floors; credential sharing among access control logs; or tailgating events (multiple people on single badge swipe). Cross-reference with network logins from previously unseen locations in the same facility.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration – High-Volume Transfer to External Storage
suggestion.rationale: Campaign objective is 'Data Theft' and 'Extortion' — implies large-scale data staging and exfiltration. Pipeline did not surface detection for collection or exfiltration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous outbound data transfers: (1) top users by volume in network logs, (2) connections to cloud storage or file-sharing domains from previously clean assets, (3) SMB/NFS reads of sensitive file shares followed by immediate compression/archiving, (4) DLP block or alerting on PII/financial data exports. Baseline expected user transfer patterns; flag 5–10× normal volume in a 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: Extortion Demand Communication – Post-Breach Threat Actor Contact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign' — threat actors contact victim post-breach with payment demands. Pipeline should surface detection for inbound threat communications or dark-web postings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails for common extortion keywords ('data breach,' 'ransom,' 'proof of access') and IOCs matching breach context (internal employee names, systems, or data snippets). Correlate with threat-intel feeds and dark-web paste sites mentioning the organization name or sector. Flag emails from newly registered domains or free email providers with urgency language.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Access – Interactive Logon from Unexpected Locations
suggestion.rationale: Once vishing or physical intrusion grants initial foothold, threat actors perform discovery and lateral movement. Article mentions 'data theft' campaign but does not detail second-stage activity. This is a critical blind spot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logons from harvested credentials: (1) user accounts logging in from new geography or AS number post-incident, (2) administrative tools (RDP, PSExec, PsRemote) executed by non-IT users, (3) pass-the-hash indicators (NTLM relay, Kerberoasting), (4) lateral traversal to file servers or sensitive systems by newly compromised accounts. Establish baseline per user; alert on deviations within 48h of suspected vishing success.

suggestion.title: Discovery Behavior – Recon Tools and File Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors conducting data theft must discover high-value targets (PII, financial records, trade secrets). Pipeline did not suggest detection for recon activity such as directory enumeration or sensitive-file searches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of discovery tools (net.exe, dsquery, dir, findstr, robocopy) by non-IT accounts; searches for files matching patterns (*.xlsx, *.pdf, PII keywords); enumeration of shares (net view \\\\*); or queries to Active Directory for user attributes. Correlate with newly enabled accounts or credential-use events in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from System Binaries on Linux Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware deployment on Linux appliances; expected behavior is shell/interpreter spawning from unexpected parents. Phrase: 'Deploys BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances' implies execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sh, bash, or perl spawned as child of system services, network daemons, or package managers on Linux appliances. BRICKSTORM variants typically establish interactive shell access post-exploitation. Baseline normal children for each parent process and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Connections from Appliance Management Services
suggestion.rationale: Malware deployment on appliances suggests C2 exfiltration or remote access. Article context implies network-based attack delivery or callback. Detection gap for C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from appliance management interfaces (SSH, SNMP, syslog daemons) to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially on non-standard ports or to known malware C2 infrastructure. Correlate with process creation events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write/Persistence in /etc or /opt Directories
suggestion.rationale: Malware deployed on appliances typically persists via cron jobs, init scripts, or rc.d entries. Article implies sustained presence, not one-off execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or modification in /etc/cron.d, /etc/init.d, /opt, or /lib/systemd by non-privileged processes or during abnormal time windows. Cross-correlate with process creation from those same parent processes within minutes.

suggestion.title: BSD Binary Artifacts on Non-BSD Linux Systems
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances'—BSD binaries (ELF with BSD headers, BSD libc calls) are anomalous on standard Linux. Detection gap for OS-mismatched payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan executable binaries on Linux appliances for BSD-specific ELF headers, BSD system call conventions, or mismatched libc imports. Flag as suspicious if ELF file claims BSD target but is executing on Linux kernel. Correlate with file delivery source.

suggestion.title: Malware Family Signature Detection: BRICKSTORM Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Malware family name is in title but no behavioral or signature detection suggested. Missing core malware-specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy YARA/Sigma rules for BRICKSTORM file signatures and behavioral patterns (mutex names, registry keys, network beacons, code injection). Monitor for process hollowing, code cave injection, or entropy spikes indicative of packed/obfuscated payloads. Cross-reference with public threat intel.

suggestion.title: Python process spawning shells after pip install
suggestion.rationale: Article: '23 PyPI packages' with 'obfuscated' code executing on import targeting 'MCP developers'; malicious packages automatically run code at install/import time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter (python.exe, python3) spawning cmd/powershell/bash within 5 seconds of pip install command or package import. Correlate parent-child relationship and timeline. Filter against baseline development environments using legitimate testing frameworks.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to getsession/git-tanstack C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'filev2.getsession.org', 'getsession.org', 'git-tanstack.com' as attacker infrastructure for exfiltration/command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections to getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org, or git-tanstack.com from developer machines. Correlate source process to identify if Python or pip initiated the connection. High confidence indicator of Shai-Hulud malware execution.

suggestion.title: File hash detection for malicious PyPI artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 6 high-fidelity hashes (ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c, 2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96, 12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b, e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497, 833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4, b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation/execution events against provided hash IOCs. Immediate high-confidence alert on match. Enrichment: determine if file arrived via pip package staging directory (/site-packages, .egg, .whl).

suggestion.title: Suspicious package name similarity to legitimate MCP libraries
suggestion.rationale: Article: supply chain attack 'targeting MCP developers' with 'malicious PyPI packages'; typosquatting/lookalike package names are standard supply chain delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install commands for package names with high Levenshtein distance to known legitimate MCP/development libraries (tanstack, msgpack, etc). Flag installations from new/uncommon package indices. Correlate against OSINT lists of known typosquatted names.

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration from Python process to attacker IP 83.142.209.194
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '83.142.209.194' as attacker infrastructure; malicious packages will exfiltrate developer credentials/data to this IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any outbound connection from Python/pip processes to 83.142.209.194. Correlate with recent pip install operations. Inspect network payload for base64-encoded or obfuscated credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI-Branded Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes threat actors using 'AI brands as bait' — implies malicious domain registration mimicking OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, etc. No detection surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations containing AI brand keywords (openai, chatgpt, anthropic, deepseek, copilot) registered within last 30 days, especially with high edit distance from legitimate domains. Correlate with spam-campaign infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Impersonating AI Service Providers
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: threat actors use AI brand names in social engineering — implies phishing campaigns. Article keywords include credential theft but pipeline extracted zero phishing-specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with subject/body containing AI brand names (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) + urgent credential-refresh language + links to newly-registered domains not in whitelist. Correlate sender domain reputation.

suggestion.title: AiTM Proxy Detection for AI Service Logins
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' but zero detection use cases exist. AiTM requires detecting session-hijacking indicators post-credential-capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-ins to AI service providers (OpenAI, Anthropic APIs, ChatGPT, etc.) from novel geographic locations within hours of phishing-email send-time, or from IPs flagged as proxy/VPN infrastructure, especially with impossible-travel violations.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass Signals in AI-Service Account Access
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks typically replay captured credentials + MFA tokens. Article focuses on credential theft but pipeline missed detection for token-reuse patterns in high-value AI accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful sign-ins to AI-service accounts (OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, etc.) where MFA challenge was satisfied but no standard MFA device fingerprint present; flag when same user's sign-in from different device within 15 minutes.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stuffing Against AI Platform APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes credential theft as attack objective via AI-brand phishing. Follow-on is automated testing of stolen credentials against known AI platform login endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume failed sign-in attempts to AI platform endpoints (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, huggingface.co) from single source IP within 1-hour window; especially if interleaved with successful sign-ins using valid credentials post-phishing window.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of API Keys from AI Service Dashboards
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials grant access to API key dashboards. Article does not describe post-compromise actions but this is the natural follow-on from credential theft against AI services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API key generation, exposure, or download events in AI service dashboards (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, etc.) shortly after suspicious sign-in activity; flag if keys are accessed from dashboard then immediately queried via API from external IP.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Phishing Email Batch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly identifies 'alert volume' and 'SOC overload' from phishing; pipeline must detect bulk email patterns indicative of mass phishing campaigns rather than isolated messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails arriving in high batches (>100 messages in 1hr to distinct recipients) with identical or near-identical sender domains, subject lines, body hashes, or URL patterns. Flag if sender domain reputation is newly registered or spoofed. Escalate if payload hash matches known phishing clusters.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Content Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on 'AI Phishing'; detection must identify linguistic/structural markers of LLM-generated emails (e.g., templated greetings, high entropy subject variance, hallucinated company references) that differ from targeted spear-phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Score email body text for LLM fingerprints: unusual grammatical constructs, lack of specific personalization, generic urgency phrasing, repetitive templated blocks. Correlate with sender domain age, IP geolocation shifts, and mass distribution. Higher AI-score + batch distribution = phishing.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Gateway Overload / Alert Fatigue Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'crushing SOCs with alert volume'; detection must alert on abnormal surge in phishing-tagged messages or gateway rejections that indicate organized campaign pressure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateway inbound volume, phishing-tag rate, and queue depth. Alert on 2x+ surge in 30min windows. Correlate with SOC alert queue depth and MTTL (mean time to label). If phishing alerts exceed 500/hr for >2 hrs, escalate as organized campaign signature.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Link Click-Through
suggestion.rationale: Mass phishing at scale aims to harvest credentials; detection must track user interaction (clicks, form submission) with phishing URLs, especially for users with high-risk profiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users clicking links in flagged phishing emails, especially within 30 seconds of receipt. Correlate with subsequent logon anomalies (failed logins, unusual geo/device, credential spray patterns). If >5% of recipients click phishing link, assume account compromise risk imminent.

suggestion.title: Email Authentication Bypass (SPF/DKIM/DMARC Failures)
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses phishing campaigns at scale; effective campaigns exploit email auth gaps. Detection must flag emails bypassing or spoofing authentication frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails failing SPF, DKIM, or DMARC validation that masquerade as internal domains or trusted partners. High volume of auth-failures from single source IP + high phishing tag rate = organized spoofing campaign.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access VPN Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs... and establish a remote access VPN connection.' This is the core exploitation vector yet no detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Remote Access VPN or Mobile Access session establishment from previously unseen external IPs without corresponding authentication logs (failed or successful credential submission). Flag sessions using IKEv1 key exchange where no machine certificate was presented. Correlate against known vulnerable configurations: legacy client support enabled and/or machine certificate requirement disabled.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Key Exchange Without Machine Certificate Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'affects only deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol, with security gateways that accept legacy Remote Access clients and do not require a machine certificate for connections.' Mitigation requires mandatory cert configuration; absence of this control indicates exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access gateway configurations to identify systems with IKEv1 enabled and machine certificate authentication disabled or optional. Alert on any IKEv1 session lacking certificate-based authentication. Monitor configuration changes that disable certificate requirements.

suggestion.title: Certificate Validation Bypass in Site-to-Site VPN (CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-50752 'affects certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections.' Pipeline extracted neither vulnerability nor detection for MITM risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site VPN tunnels using IKEv1 for certificate validation anomalies: mismatched subject names, unexpected issuer chains, or certificate pinning failures. Flag IKEv1-negotiated tunnels that lack mutual authentication or where one endpoint uses self-signed certificates. Correlate with unencrypted lateral movement observed in network telemetry post-tunnel establishment.

suggestion.title: Qilin Post-Compromise Activity Following VPN Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' yet pipeline extracted zero indicators or detections for Qilin gang activity, reconnaissance patterns, or ransomware deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24–48 hours of successful VPN breach (identified by IOC or timeline), hunt for Qilin malware samples, credential dumping tools (mimikatz, lsass.exe dumps), directory enumeration activity, and data exfiltration to known C2 infrastructure. Monitor for ransom note creation (qilin_readme.txt patterns) and bulk file encryption (high-entropy writes). Correlate VPN access source IPs with subsequent lateral movement destinations.

suggestion.title: Legacy VPN Client Protocol Negotiation (IKEv1 in Modern VPN)
suggestion.rationale: Check Point advisory recommends 'configure global properties for Remote Access VPN Authentication to IKEv2 only' as mitigation. Continued IKEv1 usage represents anomalous vulnerability indicator where IKEv2 is the secure standard.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of VPN gateway IKE protocol usage; IKEv1 should be rare or absent post-remediation. Alert on any IKEv1 key exchange proposal or successful negotiation. Correlate IKEv1 sessions with exploitation timeline (May 7 – early June 2026) and known vulnerable gateway configurations. Flag any rollback from IKEv2 to IKEv1 post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Exploit Signature (CVE-2026-50751 / CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Check Point 'advised customers to... enable IPS and download the signatures.' Specific exploitation signatures for these CVEs should be monitored in IPS/IDS logs. Pipeline extracted neither CVE identifier nor recommended detection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable and alert on Check Point IPS signatures for CVE-2026-50751 and CVE-2026-50752. Monitor IPS/IDS logs for exploitation attempts against Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access gateways. Correlate signature detections with vulnerability assessment results (vulnerable IKEv1 + no mandatory cert configuration) to filter false positives.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states 'CVE: CVE-2026-42271' as the detection target. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for BerriAI LiteLLM instances (product discovery, version fingerprinting) exposed to internet-accessible endpoints. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-42271 to identify unpatched assets requiring remediation by 2026-06-22 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution via LiteLLM Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...to run arbitrary commands on the host.' This is the execution phase of the kill chain; pipeline mapped no execution techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes or command-line invocations spawned by LiteLLM parent process or service user. Baseline normal LiteLLM operations; flag deviations (shells, script interpreters, system utilities) that indicate command injection exploitation.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Key Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' as attack precondition, implying use of valid credentials to trigger the injection. Pipeline failed to map this authentication-to-execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate low-privilege internal API key usage (auth logs) with subsequent unusual process execution or command activity in LiteLLM context. Detect anomalous elevation from low-privilege key holder to system command execution.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing LiteLLM Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' and CISA KEV entries are observed exploited in the wild, implying exposed instances are actively targeted. Pipeline failed to surface asset-exposure patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify BerriAI LiteLLM services accessible from external networks via port scanning, cloud asset inventory, DNS enumeration, or WAF logs. Prioritize instances matching federal patch deadline (2026-06-22).

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass — Check Point Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication'; directly describes exploitation technique absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Security Gateway IKE protocol logs for Phase 1 exchanges lacking valid pre-shared-key validation, multiple failed authentication attempts on UDP 500, or IKEv1 negotiation completion without corresponding authenticated user session. Flag rapid IKEv1 initiations from external IPs followed by VPN session creation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access VPN Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password'—core exploitation outcome, absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN tunnel establishment on Check Point gateways where IKEv1 Phase 2 completes but no corresponding user authentication event (RADIUS, LDAP, local DB) is logged within authentication timeout window. Flag sessions that skip or bypass normal pre-shared-key/password validation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Check Point Security Gateway Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline failed to generate exposure detection use case despite vulnerability impact being exploitation of exposed assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network reconnaissance data and external scanning logs for publicly routable IP addresses responding to IKEv1 probes on UDP 500. Cross-reference discovered Check Point gateways against internal asset inventory to identify internet-facing instances. Prioritize scanning results showing IKEv1 responses from external scanners post-2026-06-08.

suggestion.title: Check Point CVE-2026-50751 Exploitation Attempts — IKE Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability in 'IKEv1 key exchange'; pipeline must detect protocol-level exploitation patterns (malformed IKE packets, replay attacks, weak crypto negotiation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or anomalous IKEv1 packets on Check Point gateways: Phase 1 exchanges using known-weak cryptographic proposals, multiple rapid retransmissions, or replayed IV/nonces. Alert on IKEv1 exchanges from untrusted sources that negotiate authentication methods inconsistent with policy or trigger crypto validation failures.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised VPN Access — Post-Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes establishing VPN connection bypassing password; once access granted, attacker can move laterally into internal network—detection gap for post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For VPN sessions lacking proper user authentication (matched by session ID to IKEv1 anomalies), flag subsequent internal network reconnaissance (DNS queries to AD, SMB/RDP probes, port scans) originating from the VPN tunnel. Correlate unauthenticated VPN session timing with anomalous internal traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Check Point Gateway Patch Status Verification — CVE-2026-50751
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due date 2026-06-11; pipeline omitted asset inventory correlation (vulnerable versions) and patch state hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate publicly exposed Check Point gateways (from asset-exposure hunt) against vulnerability scanner results and banner-grab version detection. Flag any gateway with IKEv1 enabled and OS/firmware version matching known vulnerable ranges (pre-patch versions for CVE-2026-50751). Verify patch application timestamp against federal due date.

suggestion.title: Auth Bypass via URI Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers can bypass authentication and reach backend services...by crafting requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization.' Core initial access step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests where raw URI path differs from normalized routing path, particularly targeting auth-exempt endpoints that resolve to protected API routes after normalization. Baseline /api/auth/validate-sso/ traffic and alert on anomalous routing to update endpoints.

suggestion.title: Command Injection via Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands on the system.' Endpoint is ucs/update/latest_package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET to ucs/update/latest_package for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, backticks, $(), $(command)). Correlate with unexpected child process spawning under ucs-update parent; pipe command injection indicators with process creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning Under ucs-update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'defenders can also look for...suspicious child processes under ucs-update.' Direct post-execution indicator of command injection success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by ucs-update (typically limited to package/update binaries). Alert on unexpected interpreters (sh, bash, python, perl), network tools (curl, nc, wget, socat), or non-standard binaries as children of ucs-update process.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries, making escalation to root trivial.' Attack reaches root with no credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo command execution by UniFi service account (normally unprivileged). Flag passwordless sudo invocations and sudo execution paths deviating from normal update operations. Correlate with ucs-update child process creation for attack chain validation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Protected UniFi API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'By crafting requests...attackers can bypass authentication and reach backend services that should not be publicly accessible.' Violates expected authentication posture on protected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal authenticated/unauthenticated access by endpoint. Alert on requests to protected API routes (/api/*, /ucs/*) from external/untrusted networks lacking valid auth tokens or session cookies. Flag requests to protected endpoints with auth bypass payloads.

suggestion.title: HTTP multipart file upload of .xlsx/.xls spreadsheet to web-exposed endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability triggered by PHPSpreadsheet parsing user-supplied spreadsheet files; no detection covers the delivery vector (file upload). Article: 'CVE-2026-34084 was patched by the helper File::prohibitWrappers' implies user uploads feed the vulnerable code path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests with multipart/form-data encoding and filename patterns matching .xlsx, .xls, or application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet MIME to endpoints known to invoke PHPSpreadsheet (e.g., /import, /upload, /parse). Correlate with subsequent phar:// access patterns.

suggestion.title: File path containing phar:// scheme with 3+ consecutive slashes post-colon (parse_url bypass signature)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes the bypass mechanism: 'When the input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner with three or more slashes after the scheme'. This is the specific bypassed pattern not covered by generic phar:// detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for regex pattern in file-handling logs/parameters: (phar|php|data|expect):///{2,} (two or more additional slashes beyond //) which bypasses parse_url($path, PHP_URL_SCHEME) length checks. Flag with CVE-2026-45034.

suggestion.title: PHP stream-wrapper or phar extraction warnings in application/PHP error logs from user-controlled input
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'File::prohibitWrappers' patch that inspects parse_url results; successful bypass of this check would cause PHP to attempt stream-wrapper invocation, generating warnings/errors before or concurrent with code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PHP warnings mentioning 'phar://', 'stream wrapper', 'parse_url', 'allow_url_include', or 'fopen' with preceding HTTP requests containing phar:// patterns. Focus on errors where the source is traceable to user input (filename parameter, upload, request body).

suggestion.title: Spreadsheet library or phar:// stream processing in web-server application context outside maintenance windows
suggestion.rationale: Article implies legitimate PHPSpreadsheet usage is expected; this hunt separates benign parsing (during scheduled imports) from opportunistic exploitation (off-hours, suspicious source IP, unusual file source).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for PHPSpreadsheet or phar-processing library calls outside documented batch-processing windows. Enrich with context: source IP, user account, file origin (upload vs. retrieval), file size, and phar:// pattern presence.

suggestion.title: Browser plugin process spawning osascript with interpolated arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'chrome_tabs plugin interpolates' unescaped URLs into AppleScript code. No hunt addresses the injection point itself: plugin render process launching osascript with embedded variable expansion or command substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect chrome/brave/edge/safari render processes or plugin-associated threads spawning osascript with command lines containing $() command substitution, backticks, or $ variable expansion. Correlate with known plugin names or file paths containing 'anyquery'.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin spawning shell interpreter after AppleScript execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'do shell script' command execution within injected AppleScript. Hunt missing for the resulting shell command execution: Anyquery or associated plugin process spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash with unexpected arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Anyquery executable or chrome/brave/edge/safari plugin processes spawning shell interpreters with parent process anomalies or with command arguments that suggest AppleScript-mediated execution (nested quoting, escaped special characters).

suggestion.title: Nebula credential harvesting from host config files (T1552.004)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'API trusts the bearer token' and references private key exposure via T1552.004, but no UC detects exfiltration of certificate/key material from `/etc/nebula/` or config endpoints. Missing detection for `GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}/certificate` or file-level reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for GET requests to `/api/v1/hosts/*/certificate` or `/api/v1/operators/*/certificate` returning 200 followed by file reads of config directories (nebula.conf, cert files). Correlate HTTP source with subsequent SSH/SFTP exfil from the same host.

suggestion.title: Nebula cloud service enumeration beyond operators roster (T1526, T1087)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1526 and T1087 but UC_3_3 only covers `/api/v1/operators` and `/api/v1/operators/*/api-keys`. Missing enumeration of `/api/v1/networks`, `/api/v1/hosts`, `/api/v1/lighthouse` endpoints which expose CA topology and resource inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance bursts against nested API endpoints (networks, hosts, groups, lighthouse). Alert on user making >10 GET requests across ≥5 distinct resource types in <2 minutes, indicating systematic service enumeration.

suggestion.title: Nebula host certificate abuse for tunnel hijacking (T1550.001 + lateral movement)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions T1550.001 (alternate auth tokens) and T1069.003 (permission discovery). After UC_3_2 reenroll succeeds, attacker holds valid host certificate for lateral movement. Missing detection of certificate re-use from anomalous source IPs post-reenroll.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-reenroll, track when the same certificate (extracted from successful enroll response) authenticates Nebula tunnel connections from different source IP than the reenroll originator. Flag certificate reuse within 24h from >2 source IPs as lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Nebula stored data manipulation via config/firewall injection (T1565.001)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1565.001 but UC_3_4 only detects firewall PUT. Missing detection for indirect data corruption: operator certificate injection, lighthouse hostname spoofing, or network route hijacking via config mutation endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH/PUT requests to `/api/v1/networks/{id}/settings` or `/api/v1/operators/{id}/settings` with payloads modifying routing, DNS, or certificate pinning fields. Correlate with UC_3_3 reconnaissance to identify attacker progressively mapping and mutating the overlay network.

suggestion.title: Nebula resource hijacking via multi-operator API key accumulation (T1496)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1496 but no UC detects attackers collecting API keys from multiple operators to exhaust compute resources or redirect traffic. UC_3_1 catches one key mint; missing detection for accumulation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single source successfully minting API keys for ≥3 distinct operators within 10 minutes (POST /api/v1/operators/*/api-keys returning 200/201 for different operator IDs). This signals credential hoarding for resource takeover.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Creation by Newly Provisioned or Low-Privilege Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' and 'Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner.' This is the second exploit step, immediately following account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs API/web logs for repository creation by accounts provisioned within the same session or within short time windows (minutes to hours). Alert when new account creation is immediately followed by repository creation, particularly if repositories are subsequently configured with rebase merging enabled.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rebase Merge Configuration Enablement on User-Owned Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This configuration change is the prerequisite that activates the vulnerable code path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gogs repository settings modifications that enable rebase merge functionality (the vulnerable code path targeted in PR #8301), particularly on repositories created shortly after account provisioning. Correlate with subsequent merge operations on the same repository.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Patterns in Gogs Merge() Function Invocations
suggestion.rationale: Core exploit vector: 'argument injection vulnerability' affecting 'the Merge() code path.' Article notes it 'affects a different code path (Merge()) that was never addressed' and references four related CVEs (CVE-2024-39933, CVE-2024-39932, CVE-2026-26194, CVE-2024-39930) with similar injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs merge/rebase request logs for command-injection signatures in commit metadata, branch names, or merge message fields. Watch for shell metacharacters, escape sequences, or unusual argument delimiters. Correlate merge operations with system-level command execution if Gogs runs with shell integration or elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gogs Version Identification (0.14.0–0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev Pre-Patch)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'affects all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev' with patch in version 0.14.3 released June 7. ShadowServer tracks 2,300+ internet-exposed Gogs instances; this is a clear version-based indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Gogs instances via version banner detection in HTTP responses (Server headers, /api/v1/version endpoints, or login page source). Flag instances running versions 0.14.0–0.14.2 or 0.15.0+dev as vulnerable. Prioritize internet-facing instances enumerated in Shodan/ShadowServer feeds.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Repository Access Following Merge-Triggered RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gain ability to 'access any repositories (including private ones)' and 'read any repository (including private repos)' as direct impact of the RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repository access by users lacking explicit permissions, especially private repositories. Alert on access patterns that deviate from baseline per account. Correlate private repository access with prior merge/rebase operations or detected exploit attempts on the same instance.

suggestion.title: Credential and Source Code Exfiltration via Post-Exploitation Gogs Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies impacts: 'steal credentials' and 'alter any hosted source code.' RCE grants full repository access, enabling harvesting of credentials from .env files, secrets, keys, or configuration files committed to repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE, monitor Gogs process and logs for bulk repository exports, access to sensitive file patterns (.env, secrets.*, *.key, *.pem, .git/config), or repository contents piped to external destinations. Alert on out-of-process credential or source code exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Malspam delivery with DoubleClick redirect pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malspam campaign' using 'Google DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims' — this is initial-access phishing. Pipeline lists no T1566 mapping and generated no delivery-stage hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails with redirects through doubleclick.net or similar ad-serving domains. Look for SPF/DKIM failures combined with high-trust sender spoofing. Correlate with VirusTotal submissions of suspicious URLs in email bodies.

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET loader in-memory execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fileless .NET loader' running memory-resident malware — pipeline missed process-injection signature (T1134) and .NET inline execution (T1059.003). No hunt generated for memory-based execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe, csc.exe, or msbuild.exe spawning without command-line arguments or with obfuscated arguments. Look for process injection signals: OpenProcess → VirtualAllocEx → WriteProcessMemory chains. Monitor CLR/.NET runtime loading in unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: Trusted infrastructure abuse (Google DoubleClick masquerade)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes actors 'hiding behind a name that most systems trust without question' and using 'Google's own DoubleClick' infrastructure—this is T1036 (Masquerading) / T1199 (Trusted Relationship). Pipeline maps only T1071/T1027, missing evasion intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network flows to doubleclick.net, adservice.google.com, and known Google ad-serving IPs originating from non-advertising contexts. Alert if these trusted domains are followed by connections to extracted IOC domains (fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, etc.).

suggestion.title: SHA256 hash match on fileless loader payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 5 SHA256 hashes explicitly for the .NET loader binaries. Pipeline generated no hash-matching hunt despite article listing this as a recommended detection template (install phase, High confidence).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any file or process hash matching: d5b7247c497788cf0031ceb06e3df77a45fef59f1e49633dc7159816d64759b5, c61b1941cf756eb7551f7c661743802362728b785adc22e860d269713dfb01a6, c356aff1a01c2b0da472e584c8e3c8f875b9a24280435d42836a77b19f5a8c18, f1c3ebe78bd8c38559bf3cfcc9a9fa37d221e31780774a3787e26160a61f5348, or e91fb249aa97be5c7931e430781167edfe7ba804720b5f643e6ab70b7e6e74dd across all file systems and process memory.

suggestion.title: C2 callback to extracted command domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 7 C2/staging domains. Pipeline generated no network-detection use case despite article explicitly recommending 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt (C2 phase, High confidence).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or network connections to fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, bth.startthewave.org, pengajian.muliastudy.com, andrefelipedonascime1778799406970.2241107.meusitehostgator.com.br, catalogo.castrouria.com, xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net. Correlate with suspicious process lineage (email client → rundll32/powershell → network connection).

suggestion.title: NSO Group WhatsApp Phishing Link Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack'—phishing is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite title clearly establishing this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WhatsApp-themed URLs and messaging patterns historically associated with NSO campaigns. Flag messages impersonating WhatsApp support or containing shortened URLs redirecting to credential-harvesting pages. Cross-reference sender domains against NSO infrastructure indicators from prior campaigns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WhatsApp Account Compromise Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks on messaging platforms succeed when credentials are harvested; article title implies NSO's objective likely included account access. Zero use cases for post-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login anomalies on WhatsApp Business or Meta account infrastructure: failed login attempts from unusual geos, rapid re-authentication after credential reset, or API calls from non-standard clients shortly after phishing message delivery.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies NSO Group by name—a known spyware vendor with documented infrastructure footprint. Pipeline surfaced no actor-specific detections or IOC correlation with prior NSO operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate any domains or IPs referenced in this phishing campaign against VirusTotal, Shodan, and historical NSO infrastructure lists from Amnesty, Citizen Lab, or Lookout threat reports. Flag DNS queries or connections to domains registered at same registrar/nameserver as prior NSO C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'purpose-built web shell framework' targeting IIS; no detection for unusual child processes spawned by w3wp.exe. Article phrase: 'purpose-built web shell framework targeting Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or IIS application pool processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, or other shell interpreters. Establish baseline of normal child processes per application and flag deviations. Correlate with recent IIS configuration changes or file uploads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation in IIS Directories
suggestion.rationale: Web shell persistence mechanism but no hunt for artifacts. Article: 'web shell framework.' Typical indicators: .aspx, .jspx, .ashx, or obfuscated extensions written to wwwroot or bin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor C:\inetpub\wwwroot, C:\inetpub\logs, and IIS application directories for file creation/modification with .aspx, .jspx, .ashx, .jsp, or double-extension variants (e.g., .aspx.txt). Flag writes by non-administrative accounts or outside maintenance windows. Cross-reference with application deployment manifests.

suggestion.title: ASP.NET Handler (.ashx) C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Domain IOC 'ashx.lhlsjcb.com' explicitly contains .ashx suffix, indicating ASP.NET handler abuse for C2. No use case targets handler files or domains with this pattern. Article IOC: 'ashx.lhlsjcb.com.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for ASP.NET .ashx files in web directories; correlate file metadata with outbound connections. Analyze IIS W3SVC logs for POST requests to suspicious .ashx paths with large response payloads (exfiltration) or periodic request patterns (C2 beaconing). Flag anomalous User-Agent strings or binary payloads.

suggestion.title: IIS-Originated Outbound C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Web shells establish reverse channels; article emphasizes evasion suggesting active C2. No hunt for periodic outbound connections from IIS processes. Article phrase: 'evade every detection method that works against similar China-linked actors' implies adversarial C2 protocol design.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate IIS outbound traffic (Windows Update, logging services, patch servers). Alert on w3wp.exe connections to rare external IPs, non-standard ports without legitimate business context, or geolocations inconsistent with deployment. Apply frequency analysis to detect periodic beaconing intervals.

suggestion.title: IIS Access Log Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Initial web shell upload or reconnaissance would appear in IIS logs. No detection for HTTP exploitation signatures (PUT/DELETE methods, file upload to hidden paths, exploitation framework payloads). Article: 'targeting Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze W3SVC logs for anomalous HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE on production servers), 5xx errors followed by 2xx success (exploitation + upload confirmation), requests to non-existent paths outside public directories, or User-Agent strings matching known exploitation frameworks (e.g., Metasploit, Empire, Mimikatz variants).

suggestion.title: Phishing for Cloud Storage Credentials via Lookalike Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'using social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials.' Attacker domains (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) are obvious brand-impersonation phishing kit infrastructure. No credential-phishing detection was generated despite being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user clicks to attacker-controlled domains containing cloud-storage keywords (passkey*, deploy*) within 5 minutes of spearphishing email delivery. Flag POST requests to these domains with credential-like payloads (email, password, API token patterns). Correlate with legitimate cloud-provider login immediately after to confirm compromise.

suggestion.title: Network Traffic to Attacker Infrastructure (C2/Exfil)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dedicated data leak site on May 31, 2026' with victims already listed. No network-based hunt for connections to attacker IPs (185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66) or command-and-control traffic was generated, despite these being core IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from enterprise hosts to the three attacker IPs or three attacker domains. Prioritize connections from cloud-storage admin accounts, API clients, or batch-upload tools. Correlate with user credential compromise timeline from phishing email.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Cloud Data Exfiltration After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states credentials were stolen to access 'sensitive data' in cloud storage. No detection for bulk data downloads, API enumeration, or large transfers from compromised cloud accounts was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud-storage account audit logs for: (1) login from unexpected IP after phishing campaign, (2) rapid file enumeration or bulk download API calls within minutes, (3) data transfer to external recipient or sync service. Alert if volume exceeds user's historical baseline by 10x.

suggestion.title: Victim Notification & Extortion Threat Messaging
suggestion.rationale: Article describes extortion group with active leak site listing victims. No detection for extortion emails, ransom demands, or leak-site victim announcements was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails from attacker-controlled domains or free-remailer services threatening data publication and demanding ransom. Scan inbound email for links to newly registered domains matching attacker infrastructure (whois lookup). Flag external OSINT mentions of company name on known extortion/leak sites.

suggestion.title: Domain Registration and Passive DNS Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attacker domains follow deliberate naming pattern (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) suggesting brand-hijack campaign infrastructure. No OSINT or DNS-infrastructure-discovery detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries from enterprise to attacker domains before they appear in external threat feeds. Cross-reference domain registration dates, registrars, and WHOIS privacy services. Identify other domains in same registrant cluster using passive-DNS and threat-intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Python .pth file execution with external process launch
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious artifacts included a *-setup.pth file...Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file, which then tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub.' Defenders explicitly instructed to 'look for Python packages containing executable .pth startup hooks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes spawning Bun or other external runtimes immediately after import of a package with .pth files in site-packages. Monitor for site-packages/.pth files with executable payloads or unusual file extension patterns (*-setup.pth).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Bun runtime download from GitHub during Python execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub' and 'unexpected downloads of the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub, and process chains where Python launches Bun to execute _index.js' in defender guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python processes initiating HTTPS downloads of Bun binaries from GitHub releases. Flag process chains: Python → curl/wget → Bun execution, especially from developer workstations or CI environments where Bun is not a standard dependency.

suggestion.title: Credential file access from Python package import context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targeted a broad range of developer secrets that included...GitHub tokens...npm, PyPI, RubyGems, JFrog publishing tokens, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes...SSH keys, Docker credentials, .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, Shell histories, Claude/MCP configuration files.' These are actively harvested in import-time execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads from Python processes targeting credential stores (.env, .npmrc, .pypirc, ~/.ssh, ~/.docker, shell history files, Kubernetes config, cloud credentials). Unusual timing: reads during package install or pytest/CI runs when no legitimate code reasons exist.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions workflow creation by malware for secret exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The primary data exfiltration method is similar to past Shai-Hulud operations, using automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions.' Pipeline missed workflow-based exfil detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect programmatic creation of GitHub workflows or repositories by developer accounts that don't match historical patterns. Monitor for workflow jobs that write environment variables, secrets, or file contents to repositories. Alert on base64-encoded or hex-encoded secrets being committed.

suggestion.title: Persistence via systemd service or macOS LaunchAgent from Python context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of /etc/systemd/system/*.service files or ~/.config/systemd/user/ services initiated by Python processes or package managers. On macOS, alert on LaunchAgent plist creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents from non-system sources. Include Claude/MCP config file modifications.

suggestion.title: HTTPS exfiltration to spoofed Anthropic API endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A second exfiltration method based on direct HTTPS also exists, pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage.' Concrete IOC and detection opportunity missed.
