suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on outbound HTTPS to api.anthropic.com from non-browser processes, especially Python/Node.js contexts. Verify legitimate Anthropic SDK calls use correct certificate pinning. Monitor for POST requests to /v1/api with large payloads or unusual timing outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Impersonating Bank Redirects to GitHub APK
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials. Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file.' Clear initial access chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing domains impersonating Italian/Spanish banks followed by redirects to GitHub raw content URLs ending in .apk. Flag credential entry on lookalike banking domains (typosquatting, homograph variants). Cross-reference suspicious GitHub repos against known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Installation Masquerading as Legitimate Banking App
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 9 APKs: 'Intesa Carte.apk, Sella Carte.apk, Banca Sella Carte.apk, Nexi Carte.apk...' all impersonating legitimate Italian/Spanish banking apps. These bypass Google Play Store validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK installations from GitHub or unknown sources with file names matching legitimate banking apps (Intesa, Banca Sella, Nexi, CaixaBank variants). Alert on installations lacking Play Store cryptographic signatures. Detonate APKs with suspicious NFC/payment permissions from non-banking package authors.

suggestion.title: NFC Card Reader with Fake Verification Screen
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After tricking victims with a fake verification screen to place the cards near the mobile device's near-field communication (NFC) chip, NFCShare reads the information using Android's IsoDep interface and EMV commands.' This is explicit payment card collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect apps with NFC/payment permissions displaying credential/card entry screens not from legitimate banking app package names. Alert on multiple successive NFC card reads (scanning multiple cards). Flag APK requesting EMV/IsoDep interface for non-payment purposes.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Exfiltration of Payment Card Data
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel' carrying 'card number, type, expiry date, and a 4-digit PIN.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained WebSocket connections from devices running suspicious banking apps to non-standard ports or newly registered IP addresses. Flag WebSocket sessions transmitting card-like data patterns (16-19 digits, expiry dates, 4-digit PINs) from mobile devices. Correlate against payment card breach intelligence feeds.

suggestion.title: Malformed APK Packaging to Evade Static Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'introduction of malformed APK packaging to hinder automated analysis...newer samples include poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP, causing some extraction tools to wrongly interpret internal relative paths as filesystem paths and trigger errors.' This is defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APKs with malformed ZIP internal structure, poisoned relative paths, or non-standard packaging that fails standard extraction tools. Use binary analysis on raw APK files rather than relying on standard tooling. Cross-reference malformed APK hashes with NFCShare signatures.

suggestion.title: SMS/Phone Social Engineering from Fake Bank Representatives
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'SMS messages or phone calls from fake bank representatives may also be used as part of the social-engineering process' to direct users to download malicious app updates. Attack vector mentioned as observed in similar campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SMS/voice calls impersonating Italian/Spanish banks with subsequent malicious app installs from GitHub. Flag messages directing app updates outside of Play Store. Alert on spoofed caller IDs matching known banking fraud campaigns. Cross-reference message content with phishing URLs from simultaneous campaigns.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation via Linux Kernel One-Character Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states the attack vector: 'One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access.' This is a clear privilege_escalation kill-chain entry. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts where unprivileged processes issue setuid(), seteuid(), or related syscalls, or where processes transition to euid=0. Flag kernel log warnings or BUG_ON messages corresponding to the identified flaw. Correlate failed privilege attempts with process execution of public exploit code.

suggestion.title: Execution of Public Linux Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Exploits Now Public'—attackers will download and run them. Pipeline missed the execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of C compiler (gcc, cc, clang) in temporary directories (/tmp, /dev/shm) or unusual locations. Flag wget/curl downloads from exploit repositories (github.com raw content, exploit-db, pastebin) followed by immediate compilation. Detect bash/sh processes executing downloaded scripts that subsequently spawn privilege-escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Kernel Anomaly After Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: A one-character kernel flaw may cause instability during or after exploitation. Article does not detail impact, but kernel panics or crashes are common side-effects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel logs for panic messages, NULL pointer dereference messages, or BUG_ON() triggers. Correlate system reboots or unclean shutdowns with anomalous privilege-escalation attempts occurring shortly before. Alert on kernel warnings or out-of-memory errors in temporal proximity to suspicious syscall sequences.

suggestion.title: Repeated Failed Privilege Escalation Preceding Root Shell
suggestion.rationale: Attackers probe privilege boundaries before exploiting. Article describes new, unpatched vector—initial attempts will fail until exploit is used.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for failed privilege escalation attempts (sudo denials, su failures, capability misses). Alert on statistically significant increases in failed attempts from a single user/process, followed by privilege escalation success without an intervening sudo or su entry. Flag privilege escalation success immediately following kernel error messages or unusual syscall sequences.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Kernel Memory Protection Bypass
suggestion.rationale: A one-character flaw typically indicates a logic error in bounds checking or memory protection. Pipeline missed memory access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel audit logs for mmap() calls with MAP_FIXED or PROT_EXEC flags from unprivileged processes attempting to map kernel memory. Flag brk() system calls that alter process memory beyond expected heap boundaries. Detect segmentation faults or page-fault exceptions followed immediately by privilege-escalation syscalls.

suggestion.title: HTS Password Reset Sent for Non-Associated Email
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts' — password resets issued to emails not tied to the target account is the core exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS password reset issuance where the email address provided is not in the Instagram account's registered contact information. Detect when reset links are generated for accounts via email addresses that fail verification checks. High volume of such mismatches within a time window indicates systematic exploitation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account Password Resets via Support Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Over 20,000 Instagram users had their accounts hijacked' via HTS — indicates volume attack. Detection should flag when a single IP/session resets passwords for many distinct accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when password reset requests originate from a single source (IP, session, API key) and target multiple distinct Instagram accounts within a short timeframe (e.g., >5 resets in 1 hour). Correlate with failed email verification.

suggestion.title: Account Access Without 2FA Re-Enrollment Post-Reset
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'log in and hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled' — compromised accounts accessed immediately after password reset without 2FA protection re-engagement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login events to Instagram accounts within 1-5 minutes of a password reset via HTS, where the accessing IP differs from the account's historical login locations and 2FA is not re-enabled or re-verified. Flag especially if the account was previously protected by 2FA.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Tool Disabled or Throttled
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After discovering the incident, the company disabled the HTS AI-powered support system and all password reset links' — indicates need to detect when support systems are forcibly disabled due to abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emergency disabling of account recovery services, mass revocation of issued reset links, and mandatory re-authentication enforcement on bulk account sets. These are post-breach containment signals indicating a detected compromise wave.

suggestion.title: Data Access Post-Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers could access: 'contact information, dates of birth, social media posts and content, direct messages and communications, account activity and interaction history' — post-takeover data exfiltration or browsing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data access patterns on accounts post-password-reset: bulk downloads of DMs/posts, rapid enumeration of connected accounts, profile changes, or data export requests from new geolocations. Cross-reference with accounts enrolled in post-incident security checkpoints.

suggestion.title: Mass Credential Reset and Mandatory Re-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Meta also enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint and asked all affected users to reset their passwords again' — detection of incident response at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mass enrollment of accounts into mandatory security checkpoints or forced password reset campaigns. When >1,000 accounts are simultaneously flagged for re-authentication and password reset, correlate with HTS anomalies and potential account takeover incidents.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Vendor Account Lateral Movement to Database
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers gained access to a database...via one of its vendors.' Pipeline missed the core kill-chain jump from vendor system to customer database via credential compromise or abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database query execution from third-party vendor service accounts or IP ranges. Flag privilege escalation chains originating from external vendor integrations. Detect authentication events using vendor-provisioned credentials from unusual locations or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Dump or Mass Export
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers gained access to a database...containing customer information' with scope still unknown. Need detection for exfiltration-phase data staging regardless of volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk SELECT queries or database backup/export operations on the SoFi Securities database, especially from vendor-associated accounts or tools. Detect unusual data volumes exiting the database layer to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Vendor Integration Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthorized access to a database...via one of its vendors.' Pipeline has no use case for anomalous behavior on third-party service accounts before they pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline behavior for all third-party vendor service accounts (login times, query patterns, IP ranges, data accessed). Alert on deviations: off-hours logins, account enumeration queries, access to sensitive customer tables, or connections from unexpected networks.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Vendor Credential Abuse Timeline Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article discovery date: April 30, 2026. Pipeline missed detection use case for credential reuse across systems post-vendor-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication events: if vendor system compromise is confirmed, immediately search for those compromised credentials used against downstream systems (SoFi databases, email systems, cloud tenants). Flag any use of vendor-provisioned secrets outside the vendor's normal context.

suggestion.title: Customer Database Schema Reconnaissance Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article: scope of exposed data unknown. Attacker must have performed discovery to identify high-value tables (customer PII, financial records).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database for INFORMATION_SCHEMA or system catalog queries from vendor service accounts. Detect sp_tables, DESCRIBE, SHOW TABLES, or metadata enumeration activity before the actual data exfiltration occurs.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Customer Data Access Pattern Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article warns customers to 'monitor financial accounts for suspicious activity' implying ongoing access risk. Pipeline missed detection for continued unauthorized access post-discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate third-party data access patterns. Alert on queries accessing customer PII (names, emails, phone, addresses) or financial records (account balances, transaction history) outside normal batch job windows, or from unexpected query tools.

suggestion.title: Vishing Indicators — External Call Followed by RMM Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack begins with 'phone calls, screen-sharing tricks' via vishing. Pipeline missed entire initial-access vector. No detections for reconnaissance calls, credential harvesting attempts, or social engineering pretexts leading to RMM install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate external phone calls (from PSTN logs or UC logs if available) with rapid subsequent RMM tool installation or legitimate remote-assistance tool activation (Quick Assist, RDP, TeamViewer) within minutes on the same user endpoint. Flag calls from outside corporate phone list immediately preceding unusual process execution or RMM install.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to business-data-leaks.com
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exfiltrate data' and lists business-data-leaks.com as IOC—likely the exfil staging domain. Pipeline extracted domain but generated no hunt for exfil-specific network traffic to this destination. Missing T1041, T1048 coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to business-data-leaks.com, network connections to business-data-leaks.com on ports 80/443/8080/8443, and file transfers >100MB outbound to this domain. Correlate with data classified as sensitive (law firm files, contracts, client data) copied to staging paths immediately prior.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Installed RMM Tool
suggestion.rationale: After RMM installation, attacker uses tool to move laterally and exfil. Article says group 'exfiltrate data' post-compromise but no hunt for RMM-spawned lateral-movement commands (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe via RMM parent process).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe, wmic.exe, tasklist.exe spawned as child processes of RMM tools (AnyDesk.exe parent, TeamViewer.exe parent, etc). Alert on network reconnaissance (ipconfig, nslookup) and remote share enumeration (net view, net use) originating from RMM process lineage.

suggestion.title: Concurrent RDP and RMM Sessions on Law Firm Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article targets law firms where legitimate RDP is common. Post-vishing compromise, attacker likely opens RMM channel alongside or after RDP. Missing detection for anomalous session multiplexing or session type pairs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on events where RDP session logon is immediately followed (within 5 min) by RMM tool process execution from the same user account. Flag cases where RDP source IP differs from user's normal location AND RMM install follows. Establish baseline RDP+RMM pairs for your organization and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Out-of-Path RMM Executable Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often deploy RMM via malware dropper or unsigned executable. Article doesn't specify delivery method but UC_RMM_TOOLS detection is process-name-only (would miss renamed/spoofed binaries). Missing cryptographic signature and file-path anomaly checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RMM executables (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, etc.) lacking valid Authenticode signatures, installed to user-writable paths (AppData, Temp, Downloads) instead of Program Files, or spawned by parent processes typically associated with malware delivery (explorer.exe from Downloads, cmd.exe, powershell.exe with suspicious arguments, mshta.exe, wscript.exe).

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Compromised User Context
suggestion.rationale: Vishing attack likely harvests or reuses victim credentials. After RMM install, attacker operates as compromised user or lateral moves. Pipeline missed T1078 (Valid Accounts) and credential-access indicators. No hunt for unusual authentication patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed login attempts followed by RMM installation (suggests credential validation). Flag Sign-in events with unusual geographic location, time-of-day, or device immediately preceding or following RMM process detection. Alert on password-reset or MFA-bypass attempts correlated with RMM presence.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Targeting Corporate Users
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Vishing' as initial compromise vector. No detection use case was generated for voice phishing attacks or anomalous outbound phone calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound calls to high-value targets (CFO, IT admins) followed within 24 hours by unusual login activity, device adds, or multi-factor authentication changes. Correlate call metadata with downstream authentication event anomalies.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise Post-Vishing
suggestion.rationale: Vishing implicitly leads to credential capture and reuse, but no detection for compromised credential replay or lateral movement following phishing was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts from new/unusual geographies within hours of vishing attack surface. Flag successful logins from previously unseen IP ranges, especially followed by privileged access or mailbox delegation changes.

suggestion.title: Physical Intrusion and Network Access
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Physical Intrusions' but no detection use case maps intrusion to network compromise, badge access, or unauthorized device connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new MAC addresses or device enrollments correlated with badge access anomalies or after-hours building access. Flag connections from devices with no asset management records joining corporate networks.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'Data Theft' but pipeline did not generate any detection for large data transfers, uncommon file access patterns, or exfiltration to external storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk downloads of sensitive files by recently compromised accounts, especially if followed by uploads to consumer cloud storage (AWS, Azure, etc.). Flag data volume anomalies >10x baseline for user+host tuple.

suggestion.title: Extortion/Ransom Demand Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'Extortion Campaign' but no detection use case maps extortion tactics (ransom notes, threat emails, payment demands) to security observables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation/modification of .txt or .html files with keywords ('ransom', 'bitcoin', 'payment', 'encrypted', 'restore') in sensitive directories. Alert on mass file encryption or .desktop file changes combined with suspicious email sent externally.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Malware Execution on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly names 'BRICKSTORM' deployment on Linux Appliances—malware family execution is baseline detection. No use case generated despite explicit malware name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BRICKSTORM process spawning on Linux systems, including variants and renamed copies. Correlate with known malware signatures and behavioral patterns (file writes to /tmp, /var, or persistence directories; network outreach after execution).

suggestion.title: Linux Appliance Compromise via BRICKSTORM Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'Linux Appliances'—suggests initial compromise vector or supply chain delivery. No kill-chain phase or initial-access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized binary placement or execution on Linux appliances following network anomalies or exploits. Look for unsigned/unexpected process execution from /opt, /usr/local, or appliance-specific directories; correlate with CVE activity targeting appliance types.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Malware deployment implies C2 beaconing; article mentions VerdantBamboo-attributed malware but pipeline captured zero network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from compromised Linux appliances to known/suspected BRICKSTORM C2 infrastructure. Flag DNS queries to malware-related domains; inspect for binary protocol anomalies (non-standard ports, unmatched TLS SNI, suspicious SSL certificates).

suggestion.title: BSD-to-Linux Cross-Platform Malware Adaptation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'BSD variant' executed on Linux—suggests cross-platform compiled or portable malware. No technical pivot on platform adaptation or build artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of BSD-compiled binaries on Linux systems or Linux binaries with BSD compilation artifacts. Monitor for ELF binaries with mismatched architecture flags, portable/static linking patterns, or unusual libc dependency chains indicating cross-platform builds.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-BRICKSTORM Installation
suggestion.rationale: Linux appliance compromise typically followed by privilege elevation or persistence; article does not articulate post-execution actions, but deployment scenario implies escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-BRICKSTORM deployment, monitor for escalation attempts: sudo/setuid abuse, cron job injection, kernel module loading, or capset modifications. Cross-correlate process lineage from BRICKSTORM spawned processes to privilege-escalation syscalls or UID changes.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg RCE Exploitation via Characteristic 183-byte Malicious Packet
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'critical RCE-capable heap buffer overflow reachable with a single 183-byte network packet'—a rare, highly specific attack vector that should be a primary hunting signature for network-reachable FFmpeg services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic for 183-byte (or near-identical byte-count) suspicious payloads directed at services running FFmpeg: media processors, streaming platforms, surveillance endpoints, cloud media services. Correlate with abnormal process termination (exit code indicating memory violation) within seconds.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Termination of Media Processing Services post-Suspicious Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Heap buffer overflows crash processes. Article's RCE exploit mechanism will manifest as abnormal service termination. Link network activity detection to process monitoring for higher-fidelity correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect media processing services (FFmpeg, ffprobe, media frameworks) terminating with exception codes indicative of memory violations (access violation, segmentation fault). Alert on instances with prior ingestion of untrusted media or network activity from non-allowlisted sources within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FFmpeg Process Inventory and Exploit Surface Area Mapping
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 9 specific CVE-2026-39xxx vulnerabilities affecting FFmpeg across 'browsers, streaming platforms, surveillance systems, and cloud infrastructure'—disparate deployment contexts requiring unified inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Discover and catalog all FFmpeg process executions and library loads across infrastructure. Map to known-vulnerable versions against CVE-2026-39210–39218. Prioritize public-facing streaming and surveillance endpoints. Alert on any network-accessible exposure of vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Media Upload/Ingestion Attack Surface Monitoring for Critical Services
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes FFmpeg powers 'surveillance systems' and 'streaming platforms' as high-impact targets. These services accept untrusted media input—the attack entry point—and should be monitored for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public-facing media ingestion endpoints (upload APIs, stream ingest, file processing queues) for suspicious file submissions: malformed containers, oversized payloads, or crafted byte sequences consistent with heap-corruption exploits. Alert on correlation with downstream media-processing service crashes.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption and Memory Exploitation Patterns in FFmpeg Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'heap buffer overflow' as exploitation mechanism. Memory corruption patterns are detectable at process/kernel instrumentation layer and correlate strongly with post-exploitation RCE activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg and dependent media processing libraries for abnormal memory allocation/deallocation sequences and heap fragmentation patterns preceding the overflow trigger. Flag processes executing untrusted media files followed by suspicious memory-access violations or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Out-of-Bounds Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'out-of-bounds read and write weakness in the Chrome V8 JavaScript engine' and 'heap corruption'—memory corruption indicators must signal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome processes with heap corruption events, buffer overflows in V8 heap, or ACCESS_VIOLATION exceptions tied to JavaScript JIT contexts. Correlate exception patterns with known V8 gadget-chain signatures.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass in Chrome Sandbox Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploit 'could also be exploited to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR'—entropy-reduction and address-leak attempts must be tracked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect address-space leakage gadgets in V8 bytecode (information-disclosure patterns), /proc/self/maps reads on Linux, or memory-layout predictions preceding RCE in same process. Alert on ASLR-defeat chains followed by code execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTML Delivery to Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote attackers can exploit via crafted HTML pages'—initial delivery vector of exploit payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user navigation to low-reputation or newly-registered domains with subsequent Chrome process exceptions or memory-corruption events within 10 seconds. Flag HTML responses with obfuscated or polyglot JavaScript targeting V8 internals.

suggestion.title: Chrome Browser Crash Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploitation 'could also trigger a crash'—unplanned termination is an indirect exploitation signal when tied to web activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome process crashes (exit codes indicating heap corruption or access violations) within 5 minutes of visiting untrusted URLs. Spike detection on fleet-wide crash rates post-patch-release indicates active pre-patch exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Chrome Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions 149.0.7827.102+ (Windows/Linux), 149.0.7827.103 (Mac)—older versions are confirmed-vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous inventory of Chrome versions. Flag any instance <149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or <149.0.7827.103 (Mac). Escalate unpatched systems for emergency patching; correlate with exploit-kit C2 beaconing or drive-by-delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Sandbox Escape Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enable...further code execution via another weakness'—sandbox escape or privilege escalation activity outside Chrome process boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by Chrome executing system binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) immediately after heap-corruption events. Flag process injection from Chrome context to system services or elevated-privilege processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw is 'exploited in the wild' — pipeline must detect CVE-specific payloads and exploitation signatures
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to LiteLLM endpoints for known exploit patterns matching CVE-2026-42271. Detect unusual request parameters, POST payloads, or headers targeting vulnerable code paths. Alert on requests from non-allowlisted client IPs or user agents.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated LiteLLM API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated RCE' — pipeline should detect authorization bypass or missing credential validation on restricted endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API calls to LiteLLM services lacking valid Authorization headers, API keys, or valid JWT tokens. Monitor for repeated 401/403→200 patterns or direct access to admin endpoints without credentials. Correlate with failed auth events.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'chains to unauthenticated RCE' — must detect shell spawning and arbitrary command execution once exploited
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child process creation from LiteLLM process (python litellm, node wrapper). Flag cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh spawned with suspicious arguments, environment variables, or network connectivity. Establish baseline for legitimate operations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound Connections from Compromised LiteLLM Host
suggestion.rationale: In-the-wild exploitation 'chains to RCE' — attacker-controlled code execution enables C2 callbacks and data exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish whitelist of legitimate LiteLLM egress (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure endpoints). Flag unexpected DNS queries, IP connections, or protocols. Monitor for high-volume outbound traffic, encrypted tunnels, or connections to known malware C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Configuration or Credentials Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: RCE provides file access to config files and secrets — should detect reading of .env, API keys, or configuration stores
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to LiteLLM config directories (.env, config.yaml, secrets files) from unexpected processes or contexts. Monitor for reads of environment variables, reads of cloud credential stores, or exfiltration of API key files.

suggestion.title: Network beacons from Python to article C2 domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 3 specific C2 infrastructure domains (filev2.getsession.org, getsession.org, git-tanstack.com). Malicious PyPI packages will beacon to these IPs/domains during execution and exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Python.exe or pip.exe initiating outbound connections to getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org, or git-tanstack.com. Focus on non-standard ports, encrypted tunnels, and connections from user workstations rather than build systems.

suggestion.title: Executable file hashes from malicious PyPI artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 6 file hashes (SHA256, SHA1, MD5) belonging to malicious package contents. Direct hash matching against artifact caches and downloaded files during PyPI package extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File hash match for ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c, 2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96, or other hashes listed during pip install, package extraction, or process execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python subprocess spawning during package installation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malicious packages execute arbitrary code during install: 'malicious PyPI package-version artifacts' launching unusual children via T1059.004 (Python scripting).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: python.exe or pip.exe spawning network utilities (curl, wget, powershell), command shells, or system binaries during active package import or setup.py execution. Baseline legitimate build tools and exclude CI/CD runners.

suggestion.title: PyPI package version metadata anomalies and typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '23 newly discovered malicious PyPI package-version artifacts' and '37 packages' previously compromised. Detection should flag suspicious version uploads, abandoned projects with new versions, or packages impersonating real libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: New package versions from unusual authors, packages with minimal downloads suddenly updated, versions targeting specific libraries (mcp, tanstack, etc. variants), or versions uploaded from infrastructure tied to C2 domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45321 exploitation or vulnerability scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-45321 as the vulnerability backing this campaign. Hunt for exploitation attempts, proof-of-concept usage, or systems running vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-45321 exploit patterns, systems patching or disabling this CVE, or proof-of-concept tools referencing this CVE ID in command-line arguments or payloads.

suggestion.title: MCP tool dependency chain compromise detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically targets 'MCP Developers.' Hunt for suspicious dependency chains in MCP-related tools and any malicious transitive dependencies injected into popular MCP libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: pip install or import statements for MCP tools pulling in suspicious or newly-added transitive dependencies, or lock files (requirements.txt, poetry.lock) showing unexpected package versions.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with AI brand domain impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'AI brands as bait' in social engineering attacks. Pipeline should detect emails claiming to be from ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc., but originating from domains that mimic these brands or are completely spoofed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails with sender addresses or subject lines claiming AI service identity (ChatGPT, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft Copilot) where domain is not from legitimate provider. Look for typosquatting (chatgpt-verify.com, openai-login.net) and urgency language ('verify account,' 'confirm access').

suggestion.title: Login attempt to spoofed AI service URL
suggestion.rationale: Schema metadata flags 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' as attack vector. Article describes credential theft via fake login pages mimicking legitimate AI services. Pipeline should alert on authentication attempts to URLs matching spoofed AI brand patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to domains containing AI brand keywords (chatgpt, claude, copilot, openai) combined with URI paths matching authentication patterns (/login, /signin, /auth, /verify) where domain reputation is low or domain is newly registered. Correlate with failed/successful credential submission.

suggestion.title: AiTM proxy traffic pattern for credential interception
suggestion.rationale: Schema explicitly flags AiTM attacks. Pipeline should detect the proxy-in-the-middle network signature: client → attacker-controlled proxy → legitimate service, characterized by token forwarding or session hijacking indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful authentication from IP X followed immediately by requests to sensitive resources from IP Y (attacker exfiltrating access), unusual user-agent strings on auth endpoints, or certificate warnings suppressed on first login. Correlate proxy certificate issuance with legitimate AI brand domains in HTTPS traffic.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to non-Microsoft/non-OpenAI domain
suggestion.rationale: Article theme (credential theft via phishing) directly implies form-based credential capture. Pipeline should flag HTTPS POST containing credential-like data to domains impersonating AI services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS POST requests to suspicious domains with POST body containing credential patterns (username, password, email, session tokens) where destination domain has low reputation, high domain edit distance from legitimate AI brand, or was registered within 7 days.

suggestion.title: Multi-factor auth bypass or token theft post-phishing
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses credential theft paired with MFA evasion or token interception, pipeline should surface detections for MFA prompt bombing, push notification acceptance from unusual contexts, or token replay from attacker IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multiple failed authentication attempts followed by successful sign-in from attacker IP within minutes, MFA approval from anomalous geoIP, or rare OAuth/SAML token exchange to AI service APIs followed by lateral movement to non-AI-service resources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious redirect chain from AI brand phishing email
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering phishing campaigns often use redirect chains to evade link scanners. Pipeline should detect emails with links that pass through shorteners or attacker infrastructure before reaching spoofed login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email clicks on shortened URLs or legitimate-service-hosted links (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.) that redirect to newly-registered domains containing AI brand keywords. Flag redirect chains longer than 2 hops or chains that resolve to HTTPS with self-signed/recently-issued certificates.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection - Suspicious Sender & Domain Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'AI Phishing' as the attack vector. This is initial access; no email-based detections were generated despite phishing being the stated attack method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with sender-display-name mismatches to envelope-sender domain, homograph/typosquatting domains mimicking legitimate senders, suspicious TLDs, and unusual reply-to headers. AI-generated phishing may exhibit statistical anomalies in language models detectable via entropy or NLP scoring.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Credential Compromise - Impossible Travel & Unusual Auth
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns harvest credentials leading to account compromise. Article context (SOC alert volume) implies successful breaks. No detection for post-breach sign-in anomalies or lateral movement was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sign-in attempts from geographically impossible locations or uncharacteristic timezones within 5-30 min of phishing-email delivery. Alert on legacy authentication (BasicAuth, IMAP, POP3) or non-browser clients immediately post-phishing from previously desktop-only users.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Click & Credential-Form Submission Chain
suggestion.rationale: Phishing redirects to credential-harvesting pages. Article discusses campaign volume; no detection for click→form-submission chains to attacker infrastructure was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email-gateway phishing-link detections (Safe Links, SEG sandbox) with downstream form submissions to attacker-controlled domains or IP space, especially over HTTPS with self-signed certs or domain-age <90 days.

suggestion.title: Email Account Persistence - Forwarding Rules & Mailbox Delegation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised email accounts from phishing attacks commonly implant forwarding rules or mailbox permissions for persistence. No post-compromise persistence detection was proposed despite credential-access being the natural follow-on.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Inbox rule creation immediately post-phishing, especially rules forwarding to external SMTP or conditional rules masking suspicious patterns. Alert on delegated-access grants (SendAs, SendOnBehalf) or MailboxPermission changes to non-human principals.

suggestion.title: Alert Fatigue Suppression - Bulk Phishing Campaign Deduplication
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly addresses 'alert volume crushing SOCs' and 'Tier 1 overload.' Zero tuning or aggregation use cases were proposed despite operational focus on reducing false-positive burden.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate identical or near-identical phishing emails (same sender domain, subject template, link) into single incident alerts rather than per-recipient alerts. Suppress low-confidence phishing alerts for domains already in threat feeds; escalate only first-seen sender domains or novel credential-harvesting patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Unauthenticated VPN Access Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs' — primary attack vector. No detection generated despite explicit authentication bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 VPN handshakes from external sources that complete without valid credential submission or machine certificate validation. Alert on successful session establishment where authentication logs show bypass or missing validation steps.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Negotiation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability requires 'deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' — legacy protocol presence is the vulnerability precondition. No detection for protocol version anomalies or enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any VPN negotiation of IKEv1 instead of IKEv2. IKEv1 should be decommissioned; its presence is a vulnerability indicator and suggests potential CVE-2026-50751 targeting.

suggestion.title: Missing Machine Certificate Requirement on VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies flaw affects deployments 'that do not require a machine certificate for connections' — this misconfiguration is necessary for exploitation. No detection for certificate validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN sessions established without machine certificate validation. Monitor for policy changes that disable mandatory certificate requirements or whitelist unauthenticated IKEv1 clients.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Lateral Movement by Qilin Ransomware Affiliate
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' after VPN breach. No detection for lateral movement or ransomware deployment following authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful CVE-2026-50751 exploitation with subsequent mass file encryption, ransom note creation, and multi-host lateral movement (RDP/SMB). Detect Qilin indicators: encryption of .exe, .doc, .pdf, simultaneous encryption across multiple systems within hours of VPN access.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Vulnerable Configuration State
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies precise misconfiguration: IKEv1 + legacy remote access client support + no machine cert mandatory. No detection for vulnerable configuration inventory or patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Check Point appliance configurations for simultaneous presence of IKEv1 support, deprecated remote-access-client acceptance flag, and disabled machine certificate requirement. Correlate with patched status for CVE-2026-50751 and CVE-2026-50752.

suggestion.title: Site-to-Site VPN MITM via CVE-2026-50752 Certificate Validation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses second vulnerability: 'CVE-2026-50752...certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1' exploitable for MITM on site-to-site VPN. Distinct attack surface with no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site IKEv1 tunnels for certificate validation errors, unexpected peer certificate changes, or sessions where cert validation was bypassed. Alert on asymmetric traffic patterns or unexpected gateway IP changes within established tunnels.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable LiteLLM Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states to 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-42271. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure use case despite the article explicitly directing readers to the template at `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure` and the threat model being public-facing exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for vulnerability scanner hits on BerriAI LiteLLM or CVE-2026-42271 across the fleet. Cross-correlate with network exposure data to identify instances accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on any exposed LiteLLM service responding to HTTP requests on typical API ports (5000, 8000, 8080).

suggestion.title: Suspicious API Activity from Low-Privilege Keys
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the vulnerability affects 'holders of low-privilege internal-user keys'—credential-based access vector. No use case generated for detecting unusual API activity or privilege escalation from such accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls from low-privilege or service-account API keys that normally have restricted access patterns. Flag anomalies: calls to unusual endpoints, parameter injection attempts, or privilege escalation patterns within the same session. Baseline normal API usage per key and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Command Execution via LiteLLM Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... arbitrary commands on the host.' Pipeline did not generate a detection for process execution anomalies spawned by the LiteLLM process or API handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by LiteLLM (python.exe, litellm service, API handler processes). Flag unexpected process creation, especially shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or utilities suggesting data exfiltration or persistence (curl, wget, ssh, cron). Correlate with prior suspicious API calls.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Arbitrary Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'run arbitrary commands on the host' without restriction on command class. Attackers will likely establish persistence; no detection generated for this post-exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After command execution anomalies, search for persistence mechanisms: scheduled task creation, cron job additions, service registration, or startup folder modifications initiated from LiteLLM process context. Also monitor for unexpected binaries or scripts written to system directories.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point IKEv1 key exchange logs for sessions marked as unauthenticated but establishing tunnel. Detect VPN authentications where pre-shared key validation fails but IKEv1 Phase 2 proceeds. Alert on connections from external/non-whitelisted IPs that skip password/certificate authentication steps.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Session Without Credential Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allowing VPN session 'without a valid user password.' Detect sessions established despite failed or missing credential verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN session initiation events with authentication failure logs. Alert when a session_created event has no corresponding successful_authentication event within 2 minutes, or authentication_result=failed/skipped but connection_established=true.

suggestion.title: Check Point IKEv1 Phase 1/Phase 2 Negotiation Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is specifically in 'IKEv1 key exchange.' Detect malformed or bypassed negotiation sequences at the protocol level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 Phase 1 completion with missing/null authentication payloads. Alert on Phase 1 Main Mode succeeding without valid ID payload. Detect Phase 2 Quick Mode initiation when Phase 1 authentication status is unauthenticated. Flag Aggressive Mode negotiations with invalid/empty shared secret.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Affected Asset Inventory and Patch Gap
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch deadline 2026-06-11. Article recommends immediate vulnerability scan: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Identify unpatched Check Point gateways.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Check Point Security Gateway version < patched build. Identify instances in DMZ/exposed subnets. Calculate days_since_deadline for compliance reporting. Alert on unpatched systems with inbound VPN traffic from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Remote Attacker VPN Access from Non-Authenticated Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote attacker' and 'exposed assets.' T1190 implies public-facing exposure. Detect external IPs gaining VPN access without credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile baseline VPN source IPs and credentials. Alert on external IPs establishing VPN tunnels with authentication_status=unauthenticated or auth_method=none. Correlate with GeoIP to flag non-standard geography. Flag repeated attempts from same source IP after authentication failures.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 Encryption/Authentication Downgrade
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass implies negotiation manipulation. Detect if vulnerable gateways accept weak/null encryption or missing authentication payloads in IKEv1 negotiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 negotiation logs for cipher/hash downgrades mid-session. Alert when encryption_algorithm=NULL or auth_algorithm=NONE is negotiated. Detect Phase 1 proposals with missing auth method (DH+encryption only, no signature). Flag Main Mode completions with identity_type=none.

suggestion.title: UniFi Authentication Bypass via URI Normalization
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version'—describes the core auth bypass enabling the chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to /api/auth/validate-sso/ originating from unauthenticated sources. Flag when raw request URI encoding or path traversal patterns normalize to protected backend routes (e.g., double-encoded slashes, semicolon-delimited parameters, or /../ sequences that collapse after normalization).

suggestion.title: UniFi Package Update Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ucs/update/latest_package endpoint for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(, backticks, >, <) in request parameters. Alert on payloads attempting command substitution or piping.

suggestion.title: UniFi Unauthorized Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access...making escalation to root trivial.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo command invocations from the UniFi service account (ucs-update or similar) without corresponding password prompts or failed authentication events. Monitor for sudo execution of system binaries (passwd, visudo, systemctl, etc.).

suggestion.title: UniFi Path Traversal File Disclosure (CVE-2026-34909)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-34909 as 'path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system' used to bypass auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests containing path traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e, ..\, encoded variants) targeting UniFi API endpoints. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses to detect successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from UniFi Update Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'defenders can also look for...suspicious child processes under ucs-update'—indicates process execution as a post-exploitation detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by ucs-update or unifi services that are not normally expected (shells, compilers, network utilities). Flag interactive process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe) from the service account.

suggestion.title: UniFi Improper Access Control Bypass (CVE-2026-34908)
suggestion.rationale: Article: CVE-2026-34908 is 'improper access control flaw that can allow unauthorized changes to vulnerable systems'—initial foothold to protected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated requests to internal management endpoints that should require authentication. Baseline known-good auth routes and alert when non-auth endpoints are accessed by unauthenticated sources or in sequences that suggest enum/bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Creation or Modification by Web-Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1505.003 (Web Shell) in MITRE techniques but no detection hunt covers it. Exploitation of PHPSpreadsheet RCE directly enables web shell staging for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5 files created or modified by web-server processes (php-fpm, apache, nginx, w3wp). Filter for atypical file paths outside document root or uploads directories to reduce FP from legitimate uploads.

suggestion.title: Spreadsheet File (.xlsx / .xls) Upload Followed by Phar Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: T1204.002 'User Execution: Malicious File' is listed but not operationalized. Article describes parsing of uploaded spreadsheets; attacker uploads malicious .xlsx then triggers phar:// handler. No UC detects the upload-then-exploit sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate upload of .xlsx / .xls file to web application with subsequent HTTP request containing phar:// pattern within 60s, originating from same source IP. If missing correlation data, hunt for .xlsx creation in web server's upload directory followed by process execution from web-server parent.

suggestion.title: Stream Wrapper Parse Bypass in Application Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vulnerability mechanism: `parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_SCHEME)` bypass when input is `phar:///path/file.phar/inner`. Application-level logs or debug output may record the malformed URI or the check failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt application/web-server logs for URIs matching the bypass pattern (phar with 3+ slashes after scheme, e.g., 'phar:///'), parse_url errors, or wrapper rejection failures. Look for repeated attempts with scheme variations suggesting trial-and-error exploitation.

suggestion.title: Browser extension spawning osascript outside system automation context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'chrome_tabs plugin (and equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari variants)' injecting code into AppleScript. Detection should monitor for non-standard Chrome/Brave/Safari/Edge processes spawning osascript—this parent-child relationship is suspicious and narrows the kill chain to the actual delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on osascript spawned directly by browser processes (Chrome, Brave, Safari, Edge). Filter out legitimate system automation. The plugin context means osascript should not be invoked from the browser binary itself—this indicates the vulnerability is being weaponized.

suggestion.title: Unescaped URL string in AppleScript/JXA command line
suggestion.rationale: Article title and vulnerability description emphasize 'Unescaped URL' as the core mechanism: 'interpolates a … \[URL\] … without escaping.' Detection should hunt for osascript commands containing raw URL patterns (http://, https://, etc.) in the process command line, indicating user input flowed directly into script code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for osascript or jxa-equivalent command lines containing unescaped URL strings (e.g., 'http://' or 'https://' in the process command). The presence of a URL string within an osascript execution context suggests the vulnerability (direct URL interpolation into code) is in play.

suggestion.title: User clicks malicious URL → browser window opened via AppleScript
suggestion.rationale: Kill chain starts with T1204.001 (User Execution: Malicious Link) or T1204.002 (Malicious File). Article states vulnerability is triggered when 'user opens' the link. Detection should correlate URL clicks (browser history, web proxies, if available) with subsequent osascript execution to show the trigger event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user URL navigation to malicious domains with immediate osascript execution. Even without network telemetry, look for osascript processes launched within seconds of browser window becoming active, indicating the link-to-execution window.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin or JXA-enabled browser process execution anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is plugin-specific (chrome_tabs plugin). Detection should monitor for the vulnerable plugin being loaded or the vulnerable version of Anyquery being invoked. Article identifies affected version 0.4.4 (commit 0abd460).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Anyquery 0.4.4 or earlier being loaded by browser. Monitor for suspicious JXA script execution patterns originating from the browser extension directory (typically ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Extensions/ on macOS or equivalent for Brave/Edge).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Account Creation on Default-Configured Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false)' and explicitly states 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account.' This is the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs user registration events for bulk/rapid account creation, especially paired with immediate repository creation. Flag accounts created from non-standard IP ranges or ASNs targeting Gogs instances. Baseline normal signup rates per instance.

suggestion.title: Repository Creation by Non-Privileged User on Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner' and attacker exploits this to set up malicious repo context. Repo creation is the scaffolding for the merge-based exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs application logs for repository creation by newly-registered users or accounts without prior repository activity history. Correlate with account creation timestamps; flag repo creation within 24 hours of account signup.

suggestion.title: Rebase Merge Configuration Change in Gogs Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' and this setting is required to execute the exploit. Rebase enablement is the final pre-exploitation configuration step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs repository settings audit logs for toggling of rebase merge options. Prioritize alerts when rebase is enabled on newly-created repositories or immediately before merge operations with suspicious timing patterns.

suggestion.title: Merge Operation with Argument Injection in Gogs Merge() Path
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the flaw as 'argument injection vulnerability' in 'Merge()' code path. The exploit is triggered during a merge operation that processes unsanitized arguments, allowing command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Git merge operations spawning unexpected child processes (shell, interpreters) from Gogs service context. Flag merge commands with embedded shell metacharacters, backticks, variable expansion, or process substitution in repository-provided data. Inspect git-http-backend process arguments for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Gogs Merge Argument Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can allow attackers to compromise Internet-facing instances' and 'steal credentials, move laterally to other systems on the network, and alter any hosted source code.' RCE is the impact of the argument injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution within Gogs service security context (uid/gid running git-http-backend or Gogs). Flag execution of shells, interpreters, or system utilities spawned by Git operations. Correlate with suspicious file modifications to repository contents, particularly outside of standard push/pull paths.

suggestion.title: Malspam with Redirect Chain via Legitimate Ad Network
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malspam campaign' using 'Google's own DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims.' No hunt for phishing emails with redirect chains or suspicious DoubleClick/Google domain traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links to doubleclick.net or similar ad networks that redirect to non-ad destinations. Monitor for user clicks on such links followed by downloads or process execution. Flag redirect chains where the landing domain is non-canonical (dynamic, regional TLDs, newly registered).

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Loader Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'fileless .NET loader' — the delivery mechanism is described but no hunt for in-memory .NET execution, reflective loading, or PowerShell-based assembly injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or CLR execution launching .NET assemblies from memory (parent: powershell.exe, parent: rundll32.exe with suspicious command-line flags like -nop, -w hidden, System.Reflection.Assembly.Load, etc.). Also hunt for process hollowing into legitimate .NET executables (svchost, lsass child processes).

suggestion.title: Suspicious .NET Child Process from Non-Standard Parent
suggestion.rationale: Fileless loaders typically spawn .NET processes from unusual parents (cmd.exe, cscript.exe, notepad.exe). Article does not describe the loader's execution context, but this is a standard IOC for this attack class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET runtime processes (AppLaunch.exe, csc.exe, or managed CLR hosts) spawned by command-line interpreters, script hosts, or unusual parents. Include environment variable anomalies (COMSPEC substitution, CLR hosting flags set in parent environment).

suggestion.title: Email Link Click to Domain Enumeration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires user to click malspam link, traverse DoubleClick redirect, and land on C2 domain. No hunt for the email-to-C2 funnel or suspicious outbound connection timing relative to email delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email delivery times with outbound network connections to extracted domains within 10 minutes of click. Flag cases where C2 domain contact occurs without prior DoubleClick traversal logs (suggesting email-only delivery or bypass).

suggestion.title: Abuse of High-Trust Redirect Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights that attackers exploited DoubleClick because 'most systems trust without question.' Pipeline should suggest hunts for redirect chains through trusted domains. Not mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect redirect chains where the first hop is a high-trust domain (google.com, doubleclick.net, microsoft.com) but the landing page is newly registered, geolocation-mismatched, or contains malware signatures. Flag single-click traversals (no legitimate ad delays, tracking, or secondary hops).

suggestion.title: Registry/WMI Activity Following .NET Loader Execution
suggestion.rationale: Fileless loaders typically register for persistence or enumerate system info after execution. Article does not specify but is a known post-execution pattern for this malware class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for registry modifications or WMI queries (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_Processor) shortly after .NET process creation. Cross-reference with C2 domain connections to identify reconnaissance → beaconing sequences.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Phishing Link Detection via Meta Blocklist
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Meta Blocks NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack.' Pipeline produced no use case for detecting blocked or suspicious WhatsApp-based phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks on or access to domains flagged in Meta's published blocklist for this NSO campaign. Correlate with WhatsApp-branded phishing emails or messages containing shortened URLs or direct links. Alert on first-time domain registration patterns matching NSO's historical infrastructure.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Threat Actor Activity Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'NSO Group' as the threat actor. Pipeline produced empty threat-actor list and no kill-chain phases, missing actor attribution entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag reconnaissance or phishing attempts originating from known NSO Group C2 infrastructure, hosting providers, or domain registrar patterns. Correlate with historical NSO campaigns (Pegasus, Black Cube, etc.) for command-and-control callback signatures and delivery infrastructure reuse.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via WhatsApp Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks targeting WhatsApp users typically pivot to credential theft. Article mentions 'phishing attack' but pipeline generated no use case for harvesting endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to credential-harvesting pages that mimic WhatsApp login flows, account recovery pages, or session-verification forms. Monitor for bulk redirects from phishing URLs to attacker-controlled form endpoints and subsequent credential validation requests.

suggestion.title: Meta Legal/Policy Response Infrastructure Signaling
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Files Contempt Order'—a legal escalation indicating formalized tracking. Pipeline missed detection for Meta's own enforcement infrastructure (blocklists, legal notices).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid domain/infrastructure pivot by NSO in response to Meta's published blocklist or legal notification. Flag newly registered domains with TLD/registrar patterns matching blocked NSO infrastructure. Correlate registration timestamps with Meta's published action dates.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Deployment via ASPX/ASHX Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'deploying tools' and 'web shell framework' targeting IIS—explicit execution and persistence mechanism. Pipeline generated no use cases despite clear detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS directories for new ASPX/ASHX files with suspicious entropy or obfuscated naming. Correlate file creation with w3wp.exe child processes executing arbitrary code. Alert on large base64 payloads in HTTP POST bodies targeting web root paths.

suggestion.title: IIS Server Initial Access via Public-Facing Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'targeting Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers' as attack vector; strongly indicates exploitation of exposed IIS instances. No initial_access phase detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for anomalous HTTP requests to IIS servers that precede shell creation (500 errors, parameter fuzzing, known CVE signatures). Baseline normal IIS access patterns and alert on deviations from TLS/HTTP version norms or suspicious User-Agent strings.

suggestion.title: Cryptographically Unique Web Shell Defense Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'cryptographically unique Web Shell Framework' designed to 'evade every detection method'—explicit defense evasion via obfuscation. Pipeline maps only T1071, missing T1027 and T1140.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan ASPX/ASHX files for polymorphic characteristics: high Shannon entropy, inline reflection/System.Reflection usage, suspicious string deobfuscation calls. Build entropy baselines for legitimate app dlls vs payload-bearing shells. Monitor for renamed/obfuscated web.config alterations.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command & Control via Covert HTTP Channels
suggestion.rationale: Web shell frameworks inherently establish C2; article's framework explicitly designed for evasion, implying obfuscated parameter encoding or hidden protocol indicators not flagged by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to ASPX handlers for unusual parameter counts, excessive length, or binary-looking content in Query/Form fields. Baseline legitimate web app traffic and alert on requests with high compression ratios or repeated XOR/XE operations in payloads.

suggestion.title: Data Collection and Staging via IIS Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Web shell frameworks typically enable local file enumeration and ex-filtration. Article mentions 'framework' but no detection for data access/staging phase—common post-execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for w3wp.exe or aspnet_wp.exe processes accessing sensitive directories (SAM, SYSVOL, User profiles). Monitor for unusual file copies or tar/zip operations initiated by IIS worker processes. Alert on script-initiated ADSI queries or Registry reads via COM interop.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to OP-512 C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 5 IOCs for C2/staging infrastructure. Pipeline shows empty IOC output and zero network IOC-driven hunts despite 'Recommended hunts' section in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS-hosted applications and system processes for outbound connections to: 43.160.202.246, 140.206.161.227, 124.156.129.151, ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com. Correlate C2 contact with web shell file creation timestamps. Alert on DNS queries to those domains from web-server-tied process contexts.

suggestion.title: Discord token extraction from Code Cache / Local Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly claims 'targets Discord tokens' but no hunt covers Discord-specific theft. Discord stores tokens in %AppData%\Discord\Code Cache and leveldb; article narrative covers this gap entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Non-Discord.exe processes reading or copying files from %AppData%\Discord\Code Cache, Cache, or Local Storage. Include parent process metadata and command line to distinguish malware from legitimate tools.

suggestion.title: RAT callback detection: sustained connections to C2 domains/IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'takes full control of infected machine' — explicit RAT capability. Lists 2 IPs and 5 domains but zero hunt for C2 beaconing or command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound connections from non-browser, non-system processes to article IOCs (45.138.16.107, 85.239.155.68, lucidstealer.one, iloveyoulucid.space, ghdfhfjhfg.webhop.me, 0kt.one, storedonutsmp.net). Prioritize beaconing patterns (regular intervals, consistent sizes).

suggestion.title: Suspicious parent-child process chains: unknown process spawning wallet/browser applications
suggestion.rationale: No execution-context hunt. Lucid Stealer must spawn credential-harvesting child processes; missing this breaks IR investigation and parent attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Low-prevalence or suspicious parent processes launching chrome.exe, firefox.exe, electrum.exe, or Bitcoin.exe as children. Escalate if parent originated in %Temp%, %AppData%\Local\Temp, or non-standard application paths.

suggestion.title: Browser extension persistence injection or credential-manager hook registration
suggestion.rationale: Stealing from '18 browsers' implies persistence via extension injection or API hooking. No persistence detection included in article hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Registry modifications to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or new files in %AppData%\Local\{Chrome,Edge,Firefox}\User Data\Extensions without corresponding browser update events.

suggestion.title: Credential-store enumeration via process memory access (LSASS, browser processes)
suggestion.rationale: Before harvesting, stealer must enumerate and locate credentials. No API-level or behavioral detection for reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Suspicious process issuing CreateRemoteThread or ReadProcessMemory calls targeting lsass.exe, chrome.exe, or other credential stores. Sequence of EnumProcesses followed by memory reads from unknown processes.

suggestion.title: Credential aggregation staging in temporary directories before exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Stealer typically stages stolen data in temp directories. Article mentions 'remote access' for exfil but no staging detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Rapid sequential file creation (.txt, .json, .sqlite, .db) in %Temp% or %AppData%\Local\Temp by unknown processes, followed by deletion and outbound network activity within minutes.

suggestion.title: Network connections to Pink infrastructure (IOC hunt)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 6 high-fidelity IOCs: 185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66, passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com. Pipeline's IOC extraction returned empty object. Article itself recommends this as priority hunt (phase: c2, High confidence). Pipeline failed to generate even this baseline use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS queries, TCP/UDP connections, or HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Pink's known domains or IPs. High-confidence indicator; block on first sighting.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to Pink phishing domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials.' Domain names (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) are linguistic indicators of credential-harvesting forms. Should detect password/MFA entry to these external sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST submissions containing password-like data (entropy > X, >8 chars alphanumeric) destined for Pink's domains. Correlate with phishing email receipt within 1-2 hours prior.

suggestion.title: Anomalous password resets post-phishing email
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'social engineering tactics' to harvest credentials. Typical attack pattern involves impersonation email triggering forced password reset or credential challenge. Article does not detail exact method, but this is standard initial-access vector for credential-theft groups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag password changes or MFA enrollments on high-value accounts (cloud storage, email, privileged) within 2 hours of suspicious emails purporting to be from IT/cloud-provider support. Cross-reference sender domain reputation and known phishing keywords.

suggestion.title: Bulk data exfiltration post-credential compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'launched its dedicated data leak site on May 31, 2026' and 'has already listed several initial victims.' Indicates successful credential compromise and mass data theft. Should detect anomalous downloads/uploads to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume downloads from cloud-storage accounts (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, SharePoint) to Pink's IPs/domains or to free file-hosting (mega.nz, tresorit, protonmail). Timeline correlation with detected credential harvest.

suggestion.title: Account takeover from Pink-attributed IPs
suggestion.rationale: The three Pink IPs (185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66) are infrastructure for credential use post-harvest. Should detect logins from these sources to stolen accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cloud-account logins originating from the three Pink-attributed IPs, especially if account is in geographic region misaligned with user baseline or if preceded by detected credential harvest within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Extortion/ransom communication from Pink operators
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Pink as 'extortion group' with operational data-leak site. Impact phase involves ransom demands. Article: 'has already listed several initial victims'—these victims will receive extortion threats.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails from Pink operators (compromised email accounts, throw-away domains, Tor proxies) threatening disclosure of stolen data or demanding payment. Flag emails naming victim organization, referencing confidential projects, or linking to the operational leak site.

suggestion.title: Python Package with Malicious .pth Startup Hook
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file, which then tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub.' Core execution mechanism, zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .pth files created in site-packages during package install. Flag .pth files containing shell commands, downloads, or invoking unrelated runtimes (e.g., Bun). This is abnormal—.pth files should only import Python modules.

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Download from GitHub by Python Process
