Flag apps that request card PIN entry without legitimate authentication context or that trigger NFC scans during unverified 'security verification' screens. Baseline: PIN entry for NFC transactions is extremely rare and should be rare per bank.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Exploitation – Abnormal Privilege Escalation from Unprivileged Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'enables local root access'; pipeline generated no detection for privilege escalation. Must detect non-root→root transitions, especially when preceded by unusual process activity or syscall anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a process spawns a child with UID 0 after running as unprivileged user, with no credential-acquisition events (setuid, sudo, su). Correlate with failed syscalls or suspicious ioctl/mmap activity in parent process prior to escalation.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Module Loading or Dynamic Kernel Code Modification
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits frequently load modules or modify kernel memory post-compromise; 'exploits now public' implies attackers will attempt in-the-wild exploitation. No detection UC for kernel module loading or /sys/module modifications generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect insmod, modprobe, or direct writes to /sys/module/ from non-root contexts. Alert on kernel module loads outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate with preceding failed privilege escalation attempts or unusual ioctl syscalls.

suggestion.title: Detection of Vulnerable Kernel Version Execution
suggestion.rationale: 'One-character' flaw indicates a specific, easily-identified vulnerable binary. Pipeline should map kernel version/hash signatures to detect systems running exploitable releases before compromise occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain hash/version signature inventory for vulnerable Linux kernel releases. Alert on execution of /boot/vmlinuz or uname calls on systems matching vulnerable signatures. Baseline by environment and alert on any mismatch.

suggestion.title: Suspicious System Call Sequences Indicative of Kernel Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits trigger recognizable syscall chains (mmap, mprotect, prctl, ioctl, clone with specific flags). No detection for abnormal syscall patterns preceding privilege escalation was generated despite article focus on technical exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes generating rapid sequences of mmap→mprotect or high-volume ioctl calls on /dev/* or /sys/* interfaces. Flag prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0) or CAP_* operations from userland. Escalate if followed by uid/gid change.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Command Execution Following Failed Privilege Escalation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes public exploits; attackers will attempt root-level commands post-compromise. Pipeline generated no impact-phase detection for root command execution following privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning with UID 0 from a parent that previously ran as non-root, especially if parent is a known exploit vector (suid binary, Python, Java, container runtime). Correlate with file system access to /root, /etc/shadow, /boot post-escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Password Reset via Account Recovery Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'obtained password reset links' by exploiting HTS failure to 'verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' Core attack vector; no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect password reset requests to HTS tool where submitted email does not match registered account contact, or verification step is bypassed. Spike on failed verification attempts followed by successful resets indicates exploitation of validation gap.

suggestion.title: Mass Account Takeover via Shared Account Recovery Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'over 20,000 Instagram accounts stolen' through single exploited mechanism (HTS). Attack is explicitly at-scale; pipeline generated no volume-based compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained waves of successful password resets followed by logins from new geographies/devices across 50+ accounts within 24h via same recovery pathway. Correlate with known vulnerable authentication mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Post-Takeover Bulk Data Exfiltration from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'could've gained access to...direct messages and communications, photos, videos, stories, account activity.' No detection use case addresses collection/exfiltration phase post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk retrieval of user-generated content (DMs, photos, videos, stories) from recently-reset or anomalously-accessed accounts. Flag where data access velocity and scope exceed baseline after account takeover is detected.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Followed by Unauthorized Recovery Tool Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack sequence: account lockout, then recovery tool invocation for password reset. No detection use case generated for this telltale lockout→recovery→compromise chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequence of account lockout followed within minutes by password reset via support/recovery tools, then login from new IP/device. Distinguish legitimate recovery (user self-service, support-assisted) from attacker-initiated via access patterns and correlation with known compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Email Verification Bypass in Account Recovery Flows
suggestion.rationale: Article: HTS 'didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' Pipeline missed the validation/authentication bypass vector—not just password reset, but broken verification logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery/password reset logs for requests where email verification is skipped, failed verification is overridden, or email-to-account validation logic returns false-positive approval. Baseline normal recovery flow and alert on deviations in auth validation gates.

suggestion.title: Vendor-Provisioned Database Credential Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states breach occurred 'via one of its vendors' with 'unauthorized access to a database.' Pipeline generated no detection use case for monitoring vendor-supplied service accounts for anomalous access patterns, time-of-day deviations, or unexpected geographic sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database logons using vendor-provisioned service accounts occurring outside documented maintenance windows, originating from unexpected geographies or IP ranges, or showing clusters of failed attempts followed by successful access. Cross-reference with vendor communication about expected access patterns and baselines.

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer PII Database Query Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes breach of customer database with 'personal information' exposure. Company warns of 'personal data' involvement but provided no scope. Pipeline failed to generate detection logic for large SELECT queries or bulk export operations against customer PII tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries returning large result sets spanning multiple customer records (names, emails, account identifiers, KYC data), particularly when originating from vendor-accessible accounts or unexpected sources. Flag use of backup and export utilities against production customer tables outside normal administrative maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Vendor Account Privilege Escalation to Production Data
suggestion.rationale: Vendor credentials were leveraged to access 'SoFi Securities (Hong Kong) Limited' customer database beyond expected operational scope. Pipeline did not generate use cases for detecting unauthorized privilege expansion or scope violations by compromised vendor accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for permission or role assignments granted to vendor-supplied accounts that expand access to production customer data tables. Flag vendor credentials accessing resources outside their documented operational scope, especially deviations from historical baseline access patterns.

suggestion.title: Vishing Campaign Detection - Targeted Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'vishing' as primary attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface any detection use case for voice-based social engineering. Phrase: 'UNC3753 Used Vishing...in U.S. Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume unsolicited phone calls to employee groups targeting credentials or access information. Correlate with failed login attempts, password reset requests, or MFA bypass attempts in hours following reported vishing calls. Track callers impersonating IT, vendor support, or executive personnel requesting access details.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Physical Access & Facility Intrusion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'physical intrusions' as attack method but pipeline generated zero detection. Physical access is the initial compromise vector enabling downstream credential and data theft. Phrase: 'Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on after-hours or weekend badge access for users not on approved maintenance/on-call schedule. Flag tailgating events (multiple personnel entering on single badge swipe) and unusual access to secure/data centers. Cross-reference badge timelines with security camera footage for unrecognized personnel or vehicles.

suggestion.title: Post-Intrusion Credential Extraction & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Data theft campaign implies post-intrusion credential harvesting. Pipeline missed detection for credential dumping tools (mimikatz, LSASS access) or network sniffing following physical compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LSASS memory access, credential dumping tools, or network packet sniffing immediately following physical intrusion timelines. Monitor for unusual process launches with SYSTEM privileges correlated to facility access events. Alert on unusual WMI/RPC activity indicative of lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Staging & Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'data theft extortion campaign' requiring data collection and bulk exfil, but pipeline suggested zero detection for compression, archiving, or data movement. Phrase: 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file compression (7zip, WinRAR, tar, zip) in sensitive data directories. Alert on large data transfers to non-corporate IP ranges, foreign countries, or free cloud storage services. Monitor for uploads to paste sites, threat-actor infrastructure, or anonymous file hosting.

suggestion.title: Ransom Demand & Extortion Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'extortion campaign' as objective but pipeline generated zero detection for ransom notes, leak site threats, or threat-actor contact channels. Critical post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search endpoints for ransom/threat note artifacts (README.txt, DECRYPT_ME.html, RESTORE_FILES.txt). Monitor inbound email for extortion demands claiming stolen data possession. Track web traffic to known threat-actor leak sites, paste services, or Tor/I2P infrastructure claiming to host exfiltrated data.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo BRICKSTORM Linux Appliance Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names threat actor VerdantBamboo deploying BRICKSTORM variant on Linux. Pipeline extracted neither. This is the primary incident narrative and should be the anchor detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious binary execution on Linux appliances following network delivery. Look for BRICKSTORM process hashes, filenames, or command-line signatures. Correlate with delivery vectors (phishing, supply-chain compromise) within 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Binary Cross-Platform Detection (Linux)
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates a BSD variant deployed on Linux—suggests malware family is portable/cross-platform. Pipeline must detect the malware family artifact regardless of OS variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BRICKSTORM variants by file hashing, strings matching known samples, or behavioral artifacts (unusual network egress, process injection attempts). Establish baseline for Linux appliance process behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Linux Appliance Persistence Mechanism (Post-Deployment)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployment but not persistence mechanisms. Typical APT malware establishes persistence via cron jobs, systemd services, or kernel modules. Pipeline should anticipate this attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/cron.d, /etc/crontab, /etc/systemd/system, and kernel module loading post-BRICKSTORM execution. Flag unsigned systemd units or cron entries executing from unusual paths (tmp, /dev/shm, non-standard lib directories).

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM C2 Beaconing (Linux Appliance)
suggestion.rationale: Deployed malware must establish command-and-control. Article does not detail C2 infrastructure; pipeline should generate hypothesis-driven detection for C2 patterns on hardened appliances (unusual outbound, DNS tunneling, HTTP POST to suspicious domains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Linux appliances to unknown or newly-registered domains post-BRICKSTORM execution. Flag DNS exfiltration patterns, suspicious HTTP User-Agents, or encrypted tunnel protocols (DNS-over-HTTPS) from appliance subnets.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo Delivery Chain (Phishing / Supply-Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies VerdantBamboo delivered malware but mechanism unstated. Common vectors: phishing, watering hole, supply-chain. Pipeline should generate broad detections for typical initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with malicious attachments or links from threat-intel feeds associated with VerdantBamboo. Monitor for suspicious downloads to Linux appliance users (Office macros, archives, shell scripts). Cross-reference with known VerdantBamboo C2 IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: Network-based FFmpeg RCE detection — 183-byte exploit packet signature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'single 183-byte network packet' triggers heap buffer overflow RCE. Pipeline provided zero network detections despite this being the explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network traffic to endpoints running FFmpeg (browsers, media servers, CDN, surveillance) for anomalously-sized packets (160–200 bytes) on media ports (1935 RTMP, 80/443 HLS/DASH/HTTP). Correlate packet spike with immediate destination-host process anomalies or crashes.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg RCE post-exploitation process behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE outcome but pipeline has no detection for code execution indicators post-exploitation. Missing behavioral alerts for shell spawning, unexpected child processes, or outbound connections following media process compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FFmpeg, ffprobe, ffserver, or embedded media processes spawn unexpected children (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash, /bin/sh, nc, curl). Flag if parent is a media file, RTMP stream handler, or Chromium renderer. Include parent network context in alert metadata.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg supply-chain compromise or malicious binary distribution
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg embedded in browsers, streaming platforms, cloud infrastructure creates mass distribution surface. Article notes widespread deployment but pipeline has zero supply-chain detection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg binary creation outside trusted package managers (apt, brew, choco, MSI). Detect unsigned or incorrectly-signed FFmpeg binaries. Alert on FFmpeg loads from non-standard paths (temp, AppData, /tmp). Cross-correlate suspicious binary with subsequent process spawning or network activity.

suggestion.title: Detect heap buffer overflow exploitation or crash-before-RCE patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'heap buffer overflow' as specific RCE mechanism. Pipeline abstracted away exploit type; should detect memory corruption indicators, application crashes, or ASLR bypasses preceding code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg and media-processing applications for crashes with heap corruption signatures (Windows: HEAP_CORRUPTION, access violations on freed memory; Linux: segmentation faults, double-free patterns). Flag crash events followed by successful code execution in same or child process within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Detect FFmpeg RCE exploitation attempts via network scanning or fuzzing probes
suggestion.rationale: Once zero-days are public, attackers probe for vulnerable instances. Pipeline provides no reconnaissance or probe-detection for exploitation attempts targeting media endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to media endpoints (RTMP 1935, HLS/DASH on 80/443) for malformed headers, binary payloads where text expected, or rapid sequential requests of varying sizes (scanning pattern). Correlate probe attempts with downstream exploitation attempts or CVE-specific scanner fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE credential access and lateral movement from compromised media services
suggestion.rationale: Article implies RCE but provides no detection for post-exploitation objectives. In widespread deployments, FFmpeg compromise is stepping stone to credential theft or domain escalation, not end goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FFmpeg or media-service child processes accessing credential stores (LSASS.exe, /etc/shadow), spawning dumping tools (mimikatz, hashdump), or establishing lateral connections to file shares, registry, or LDAP. Focus on privilege elevation from unprivileged media-service user context to SYSTEM or domain accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect IKEv1 VPN Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw...to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection'. Core attack vector; zero detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN logs for IKEv1 key exchange from sources without valid machine certificates. Flag successful authentication immediately following failed certificate validation. Alert if Machine Certificate Verification = False on IKEv1 sessions.

suggestion.title: Detect Legacy Remote Access Client Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires accepting 'legacy Remote Access clients' and Check Point advises to 'remove support for the legacy remote access client'. No detection for deprecated client versions generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN connections from deprecated/legacy remote access client versions. Cross-reference client-version or user-agent fields against known-legacy signatures. Escalate matches on systems with IKEv1 enabled.

suggestion.title: Detect Machine Certificate Requirement Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate'. Pipeline should have detected missing/disabled certificate enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Check Point Mobile Access/Remote Access VPN configurations to verify machine-certificate authentication is mandatory. Alert on any config change disabling or downgrading certificate requirement enforcement.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-VPN Lateral Movement Following IKEv1 Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate'. Pipeline should correlate VPN compromise with immediate internal reconnaissance and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For VPN sessions established via IKEv1 without valid machine certificate, monitor target host for lateral movement within 10 minutes: SMB enumeration, process/account discovery, credential dumping, file transfer to shares. Escalate as ransomware staging indicator.

suggestion.title: Detect Qilin Ransomware Staging Post-VPN Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article links exploitation directly to Qilin RaaS with 'confirmed post-compromise activity' and 'over 400 victims'. Should trigger Qilin-specific encryption and staging IOC detection on affected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On hosts accessed via compromised IKEv1 VPN, monitor for Qilin RaaS staging patterns: batch encryption scripts, rclone/7zip execution, shadow copy deletion commands, AV/backup service disablement via registry, and file encryption with Qilin-associated extensions.

suggestion.title: Compromised Government Account Accessing Messaging Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers used a hijacked user account to breach Tchap' and attacker 'social engineered a valid account on the education shard (matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr)'—signals account compromise via social engineering followed by unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Tchap/Matrix accounts from unusual geographies, impossible travel time, or user agents deviating from baseline, especially if immediately followed by bulk data queries. Flag accounts that transition from idle to high-activity post-login without expected user interaction patterns.

suggestion.title: Mass Account and Message Enumeration on Matrix-Based Service
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages and information on over 73,000 accounts, including email addresses, organization information, meeting links'—indicates systematic account discovery and message enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential API calls querying user account metadata or message listing endpoints; threshold on account enumeration by iterating user IDs or searching across public rooms. Single account generating 73k+ account lookups in days is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Authenticated But Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Attacker exfiltrated 'over 13.5GB of documents and media files' and article notes 'every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token'—indicates abuse of compromised credentials to bulk-download files at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data volume anomalies for authenticated users—compare daily download/transfer bytes against user baseline. 13.5GB exfiltration should trigger volume-threshold alerts. Flag bulk media ID enumeration followed by file downloads (pattern: scrape message IDs → extract media URLs → download all).

suggestion.title: Hardcoded LDAP Credentials Leaked in PowerShell Script
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gained access to 'hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director'—classic credential exposure in script.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts containing LDAP connection strings, passwords, or credential literals. Monitor for LDAP authentication attempts using credentials sourced from script paths or recently exposed/reviewed scripts. Alert on LDAP bind attempts from unexpected service accounts or IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Cross-Shard Lateral Movement in Federated Messaging Platform
suggestion.rationale: Attacker stated 'Everything below is what that one account could reach, other shards will have more'—implies awareness of multiple Matrix shards and potential for lateral movement between education, tax, and other government organization shards.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single accounts authenticating across multiple Matrix shards in rapid succession. Flag federation/homeserver traversal attempts. Detect requests to other shards using credentials sourced from education shard compromise.

suggestion.title: Authentication-Bypass File Access Pattern on Matrix Media Server
suggestion.rationale: Attacker noted 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token. The media IDs come from the messages. Once you have a message with a media URL you can pull the file freely'—describes access control flaw where files accessible without proper authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file download requests (by media ID) lacking valid bearer tokens or session identifiers. Alert on bulk file ID enumeration followed by downloads across multiple shards from single session. Track unauthorized media server access from compromised account IDs.

suggestion.title: V8 Engine Out-of-Bounds Memory Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'out-of-bounds read and write weakness in the Chrome V8 JavaScript engine' and 'heap corruption, exposing sensitive information or triggering a crash'—core exploitation indicator the pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome processes for abnormal memory access patterns, V8 engine exceptions, or unexpected heap allocations during HTMLparsing. Browser crashes immediately following navigation to untrusted domains may indicate exploitation attempts. Correlate with ASLR bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass Attempt Detection in Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploit to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR, making it easier to achieve code execution'—a specific post-exploitation technique that should trigger detection infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome/Chromium processes executing memory disclosure probes or information-gathering syscalls prior to process injection or code caves. Look for patterns consistent with ASLR entropy reduction or gadget chain construction.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTML Delivery via Browser Sandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attackers can exploit via crafted HTML pages'—the initial attack surface is untrusted HTML rendering, directly tied to T1566/T1190 techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of HTML payloads crafted to trigger V8 engine heap corruption. Monitor for sudden spikes in browser failures or crashes linked to specific domains or email campaigns. Inspect Content-Disposition headers and HTML object/embed tags for suspicious encoding.

suggestion.title: Sandbox Escape and Post-Exploitation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article notes threat: 'arbitrary code inside the web browser's sandbox' and ability to access 'data beyond the memory buffer'—indicates sandbox escape leading to elevated execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation behavior: Chrome spawning child processes with unusual privileges, writing to unexpected directories, or executing LOLBins. Alert on Chrome reading/writing files outside expected temp/profile directories or attempting to interact with system services.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Patch Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions (149.0.7827.102/103)—unpatched Chrome instances remain vulnerable and are high-risk assets requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Chrome versions across endpoints daily. Alert on deployment of outdated builds (pre-149.0.7827.102/103) post-patch date. Correlate with suspicious browser activity from unpatched systems to identify active exploitation.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 19 malicious PyPI packages that 'auto-run' a credential stealer. Pipeline missed detection for setup.py or post-install script execution that reaches beyond the package directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python package manager (pip/poetry) installation events followed by subprocess spawning commands outside standard library paths, especially those attempting to read credential files or establish network connections. Correlate pip install events with unexpected child processes within seconds.

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Credential File Access Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Payload is specifically a 'Bun credential stealer.' Pipeline should detect file-read events on Bun credential stores (~/.bun/, bunfig.toml with tokens) following suspicious Python package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access patterns targeting Bun configuration or credential locations from Python interpreter processes or child processes spawned during package installation. Flag reads to ~/.bun/install/cache, bunfig.toml, or npm-equivalent token files within 10 minutes of pip install.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration Over HTTP/HTTPS from Unexpected Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states stealer is designed to exfiltrate credentials. Pipeline missed C2 communication detection: HTTP POST/PUT requests containing structured data (JSON with creds) from Python subprocesses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP(S) requests initiated by Python processes or their children during/immediately after package installation, especially to low-reputation or unregistered domains. Flag requests containing credential patterns (tokens, API keys, base64-encoded auth headers).

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain: Malicious PyPI Package Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'PyPI attack' and '19 packages poisoned.' Pipeline failed to reconstruct initial access via compromised package repository.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install/poetry add commands targeting PyPI (pypi.org, test.pypi.org) for package names matching known malicious releases. Cross-reference package version numbers with threat feeds of poisoned package versions. Alert on installation of specific versions outside normal dependency ranges.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Exfiltration via setup.py Execution
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned packages likely use setup.py to execute malicious code. Stealer may target environment variables containing tokens (NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY). Pipeline missed detection for subprocess calls accessing env vars.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python setup.py execution spawning subprocesses that enumerate or read environment variables, especially when those subprocess calls are immediately followed by network egress or file-write events to /tmp or temp directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 LiteLLM Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild'—pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no kill-chain phases despite the title establishing a known, weaponized vulnerability with active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to LiteLLM instances with CVE-2026-42271 exploitation patterns. Establish baseline of legitimate LiteLLM API endpoints and flag anomalous parameter injection, path traversal, or authentication-bypass signatures in request payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Execution via LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—pipeline produced no execution-phase detections despite explicit reference to remote code execution without authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM process trees for unexpected child process spawning, shell invocation, or system command execution following CVE-2026-42271 exploitation indicators. Alert on process launch from LiteLLM service account with SYSTEM or unexpected privilege level.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass to LiteLLM API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Unauthenticated RCE' indicating auth-bypass component; pipeline missed credential-access and defense-evasion detection opportunities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests to LiteLLM endpoints that bypass standard authentication headers or session validation. Flag requests with missing or invalid Authorization tokens that successfully reach protected endpoints, or suspicious token injection patterns.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Abuse Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE chains establish command execution—pipeline failed to generate post-exploitation detection use cases for lateral movement or persistence via compromised LiteLLM instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large volumes of outbound connections from LiteLLM processes to non-standard ports or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate unusual data exfiltration patterns or reverse-shell indicators with LiteLLM process execution.

suggestion.title: RPC Endpoint Mapper Port 135 Enumeration and Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Remote Procedure Call (RPC) is a protocol that allows functions residing in a separate process...exploited by threat actors for lateral movement,' yet no UC monitors RPC port 135—the core attack surface—for enumeration, failed binds, or exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound and outbound port 135 connections from non-service processes (rule out svchost.exe, services.exe). Detect rapid connection attempts from single source to multiple targets (RPC enumeration sweep). Alert on failed RPC endpoint binds followed by successful connection and process execution (exploitation post-reconnaissance).

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping and LSASS Access post-RPC Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'credential theft' as attack objective but no UC detects credential-harvesting tooling or LSASS access that typically follows RPC-based lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of credential dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump, secretsdump.py) and suspicious file/registry access to SAM hive, Security hive, and NTDS.dit. Monitor for LSASS access from non-standard callers and correlate with prior RPC or lateral-movement tool execution to build attack-chain timeline.

suggestion.title: Service Creation and Configuration via RPC
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'privilege escalation' as outcome of RPC exploitation but no UC detects service creation/modification—the primary persistence and privilege-escalation vector triggered remotely via RPC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on remote service creation events (sc.exe, net.exe /remote, WMI Win32_Service.Create) sourced from RPC/port 135 traffic or lateral-movement tooling. Flag service modifications with suspicious binaries, display names, or run-as identities. Correlate with prior lateral-movement and credential-access activities.

suggestion.title: WMI/COM Remote Code Execution and Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: WMI and COM are primary RPC consumers for remote execution (article mentions 'Service Execution' T1569.002) but no UC monitors anomalous WMI process creation or COM object instantiation from remote sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WmiPrvSE.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe (WMI process execution). Alert on wmic.exe with /node: parameter (remote target), Invoke-WmiMethod calls from untrusted parent processes, or Win32_Process.Create method calls. Correlate WMI execution with prior RPC port 135 activity or lateral-movement tool execution.

suggestion.title: RPC Authentication Failures and Login Anomalies Prior to Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RPC exploitation but no UC detects probing, enumeration, and failed authentication attempts that precede successful compromise—key indicators of active RPC attack reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate spikes in failed RPC-related logons (Event 4625 targeting services or service accounts) with successful lateral-movement or service creation events. Detect rapid authentication failures followed by sudden success (exploitation after credential guessing). Flag authentication failures to high-value targets (domain controllers, SQL servers) sourced from unusual internal IPs.

suggestion.title: High-Precision Timing API in Untrusted Scripts
suggestion.rationale: FROST exploits browser timing APIs (likely performance.now(), High Resolution Time API) to measure SSD access latencies. The article states websites can trigger this, implying JavaScript execution; detect scripts accessing timing APIs with sub-millisecond precision.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript code calling high-precision timing functions (performance.now, performance.getEntries) within tight loops or correlate timing measurements with SSD I/O patterns. Flag unusual frequency of timing queries or access from cross-origin frames.

suggestion.title: Inferred App/Site Access via Timing Side-Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article describes tracking 'what sites and apps you open' via SSD timing variations. This is collection of user behavior; detect anomalous timing patterns in storage subsystem or statistical analysis of access latencies that could reveal system state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated I/O access patterns where latency is being measured or correlated with user action (app launch, website navigation). Establish baseline for normal SSD latencies and flag scripts performing statistical analysis of deviations.

suggestion.title: Covert Channel Exfiltration via SSD Timing Modulation
suggestion.rationale: Once browsing/app usage is inferred from timing, data must be exfiltrated; the article implies this occurs 'via SSD timing,' suggesting the attack leverages timing differences to encode or leak information.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect correlated JavaScript timing measurements and network events (XHR, fetch) occurring in synchronous bursts; timing data encoded into request headers, body, or DNS queries could represent covert exfiltration of inferred app/site names.

suggestion.title: Browser Feature Abuse for System State Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: FROST infers app/site presence by analyzing SSD timing—a form of system discovery. Detect queries or probes of browser APIs that leak system state (cache timing, resource timing, paint timing APIs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript console or DevTools for repeated invocations of PerformanceObserver, ResourceTiming, or paint-timing APIs; correlate with attempts to measure latency variance across repeated same-origin requests.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI/Package Artifact Installation — IOC Hash Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 6 file hashes (SHA256×2, SHA1×2, MD5×2) as 'high-fidelity' IOCs from compromised packages; zero detection proposed. Phrase: '23 newly discovered malicious PyPI package-version artifacts.' Must hunt for these specific artifacts on endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when files matching the 6 provided hashes (ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c, 2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96, etc.) appear in site-packages, __pycache__, or .whl archives. Correlate with recent pip install, pip show, or Python version check commands.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to Actor Domains — Network IOC Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 3 C2 domains (filev2.getsession.org, getsession.org, git-tanstack.com); article briefing references 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' template but pipeline extracted zero. Malicious packages will beacon post-install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt DNS or HTTP/HTTPS traffic from non-internet-facing hosts to {filev2.getsession.org, getsession.org, git-tanstack.com}. Raise confidence if originating from python.exe, pip.exe, or a process chain starting with recent pip install. Correlate with presence of IOC hashes.

suggestion.title: Python Package Runtime Subprocess Execution — Post-Import Payload Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply-chain compromise with implicit code execution on import/install. Phrase: 'malicious PyPI package-version artifacts' implies __main__.py or setup.py payloads. Current UC watches for installer.exe children; missing Python interpreter context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe or pip.exe spawning shell interpreters (cmd, powershell, bash) with inline script arguments (-c, -Command, -nop) or outbound pipes. Flag if preceded by pip install within 1 hour or if process command line contains base64/zlib patterns suggesting obfuscated payload.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/Encoded Payload in Installed Python Modules — T1027 Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as a technique; zero detection for obfuscated code patterns in packages. Malicious packages likely embed encoded/compressed payloads to evade signature and static analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .py files and __pycache__/.pyc bytecode in site-packages for base64 blocks, zlib/gzip magic numbers, hex-escaped strings, or suspicious exec/eval calls. Alert if detected in packages matching article SHA256 hashes or installed via pip within detection window.

suggestion.title: MCP Developer Targeting — Dependency Chain Abuse for Claude/Anthropic Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Target MCP Developers.' No detection for MCP-specific SDK packages (claude-sdk, anthropic, mcp, mcp-client, etc.) being installed from compromised sources or with unusual versions. Threat is specifically aimed at this developer cohort.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install/list events for packages with names mimicking or depending on claude, anthropic, mcp, mcp-client, or related SDKs. Flag unusual version numbers, install from non-PyPI URLs, or successful install of any of the 23 named compromised packages. Correlate with developer/data-scientist user accounts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Package Repository or Mirror Usage — Repository Spoofing/Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Mini Shai-Hulud, Miasma, and Hades' clusters spanning 471 artifacts across npm and PyPI. Attackers likely abused or spoofed package repositories. Detect configuration of non-canonical PyPI sources or mirrors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pip configuration changes (pip.conf, .pypirc modifications) pointing to non-canonical mirrors or URLs. Hunt for pip install --index-url or --extra-index-url flags referencing domains other than pypi.org, test.pypi.org, or known corporate mirrors. Alert if found on MCP developer machines.

suggestion.title: High-volume phishing campaign detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly establishes phishing as the attack vector overwhelming SOCs: 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous spikes in phishing-tagged emails from unique sender domains within short time windows. Correlate user-reported phishing volume with baseline and alert when 25%+ above normal. Flag campaigns using AI-generated content signals (unusual grammar variations in subject, unusual word substitutions).

suggestion.title: AI-generated phishing email fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'AI Phishing' as distinct threat: 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs' — pipeline missed techniques for detecting LLM-generated content anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect structural patterns typical of LLM-generated phishing: repeated opening phrases, unnatural pronoun shifts mid-email, inconsistent urgency escalation, token-level repetition patterns. Correlate with payload analysis for synthetic urgency markers ('immediate action required', 'verify account now').

suggestion.title: SOC alert fatigue evasion tactics
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes threat context: attackers are deliberately generating high alert volume to exhaust Tier 1 triage capacity, enabling low-risk-scored emails to slip through — no use case created for this secondary tactic
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag campaigns mixing obviously-malicious and obviously-benign emails in same sender domain to bloat alert queues. Monitor for suspicious reduction in phishing detection rate after bulk low-risk email injection. Detect campaigns with deliberately mixed payload risk scores designed to overwhelm prioritization rules.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated VPN Session Establishment via IKEv1 Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs' via CVE-2026-50751; confirmed exploitation across dozen organizations in early June. Core attack vector with zero UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when VPN session successfully authenticates via IKEv1 on deployments still accepting legacy remote access clients without machine certificates. Baseline healthy behavior: IKEv2 dominant, machine certs enforced. Flag anomaly: IKEv1 Phase 1 completion followed immediately by VPN_AUTH_SUCCESS without preceding IKEv1 Phase 2 failure/retry pattern.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Negotiation Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' and explicitly recommends configuring IKEv2-only post-patching. Continued IKEv1 negotiation after June 8 indicates unpatched or misconfigured gateways.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create historical baseline of IKEv1 usage pre-June 8, 2026. Post-patch, alert on any IKEv1 Phase 1 negotiation initiation from untrusted external networks. Expected trend: IKEv1 usage should drop to zero post-remediation. Anomaly: continued IKEv1 acceptance indicates unpatched systems or active attacker reuse.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Connection Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires 'security gateways that accept legacy Remote Access clients.' Detection of deprecated client profiles post-remediation indicates either attacker recon or unpatched internal systems continuing vulnerable patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and baseline legacy Check Point remote access client User-Agent strings and version identifiers from VPN logs pre-June 8. Post-remediation, alert on any connection attempt matching deprecated client profiles, which should be zero on patched systems. High-confidence indicator: legacy client + IKEv1 + no machine cert = exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Execution Post-VPN-Compromise Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate.' Establishes behavioral chain: VPN exploit → ransomware deployment. Critical for impact-phase detection linking VPN anomalies to encryption activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN authentication anomalies (esp. IKEv1 exploitation patterns, unauthenticated successful sessions) with downstream ransomware indicators: bulk file encryption, .qilin/.agenda ransom notes, cryptographic process execution. Temporal window: 4–72 hours post-VPN compromise. Qilin-specific: monitor for Synnovis, Lee Enterprises, Nissan, Asahi–sector behavioral patterns; look for victim-org TTPs after VPN breach.

suggestion.title: Certificate Validation Bypass in Site-to-Site VPN (MITM)
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-50752 explicitly 'affects certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections.' No exploitation observed yet, but requires proactive detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site VPN Phase 1 for certificate chain anomalies: self-signed certs substituted for expected CAs, mismatched subject Distinguished Names, unexpected intermediate certificate injection, signature validation failures. Alert on same VPN tunnel ID with multiple distinct peer certificates over time (indicates MITM interception). IKEv1-specific: this protocol lacks modern cert pinning; any cert deviation is suspicious.

suggestion.title: External VPN Connection Spike Aligned to Exploitation Window
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes exploitation timeline: 'attacks began on May 7, surged in early June.' Behavioral anomaly detection on connection rate changes during active-exploitation window (May 7–June 8) from previously unknown external sources indicates active CVE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of VPN connection rates and unique source IP diversity pre-May 7, 2026. Alert on statistically significant increase in VPN connection attempts from new external IPs during May 7–June 8 window. Confirm exploitation: filter to IKEv1 + legacy client + no machine cert. Secondary signal: geographic anomaly (Qilin victims: Japan, US, Australia, UK suggest wide targeting; flag unexpected country/ASN sources).

suggestion.title: Detect Unpatched LiteLLM Instances via Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references template at _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure. Federal patch due date 2026-06-22 establishes business criticality. Pipeline generated no UC for this canonical hunt despite being the primary control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-42271 or LiteLLM version fingerprints against vendor patch advisory. Alert on instances older than patched baseline. Prioritize assets with internet-routable exposure or public DNS records. Federal agencies face compliance date; enterprise orgs face breach risk.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary Command Execution via LiteLLM Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'run arbitrary commands on the host' via command injection. Execution phase entirely absent from pipeline despite explicit capability description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by LiteLLM service parent (litellm daemon, Python process, container). Alert on shell interpreters (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe) spawned by parent process not in baseline. Flag encoded commands or suspicious interpreter flags.

suggestion.title: Detect Low-Privilege API Key Usage with Elevated Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly threatens 'any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands.' Pipeline missed privilege escalation vector tied to credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API key or service-account authentication events with subsequent command execution. Flag when API keys tagged as 'read-only' or 'internal' initiate process creation or shell commands. Baseline expected usage per key scope; alert on privilege-misalignment.

suggestion.title: Detect Internet-Exposed LiteLLM Service Instances
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) implies exposure to untrusted networks. Article states KEV is 'currently being exploited'—exposure hunting is foundational initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network segmentation logs and firewall rules for LiteLLM service (ports commonly 8000, 8080, 5000, or vendor-specific) listening on WAN-facing interfaces or DMZ subnets. Cross-reference against asset inventory for 'internal' or 'dev' instances. Alert on any LiteLLM in PCI, HIPAA, or compliance-scoped zones reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement and Reconnaissance from Compromised LiteLLM Host
suggestion.rationale: RCE capability ('run arbitrary commands on the host') establishes platform for follow-on actions. Article focuses on entry; pipeline missed downstream lateral-movement and exfiltration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from compromised LiteLLM host to internal infrastructure (database ports 3306, 5432, 1433; LDAP/Kerberos; file shares). Alert on tool downloads (psexec, PuTTY, curl, wget) and reconnaissance commands (net group, dsquery, ipconfig, whoami, systeminfo). Establish baseline for legitimate LiteLLM C2 or integration traffic.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects public-facing VPN infrastructure via 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190). Need immediate inventory of exposed Check Point gateways listening on UDP/500 (IKEv1) and HTTPS console ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound connections to UDP/500 or Check Point management HTTPS ports (typically 443, 8443) from unexpected source IPs. Baseline your Check Point gateways' external exposure to audit patch status against CVE-2026-50751.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 SA Negotiation Without Prior Authentication Success
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Vulnerability allows IKEv1 key exchange to complete without corresponding authentication event (RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS success).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate IKEv1 logs (SA established, AUTH complete) against authentication server logs (RADIUS, LDAP, TACACS). Flag IKEv1 sessions where Phase 2 SA negotiation succeeds but no corresponding user authentication event in logs within ±30 seconds. On vulnerable gateways, this signal becomes anomalously frequent.

suggestion.title: Successful VPN Logins from Novel/Anomalous IP Addresses
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker' establishing valid VPN sessions. Expected adversary behavior: mass testing of IKEv1 from scanning infrastructure or botnet IPs, succeeding on vulnerable Check Points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline VPN connection success by source IP geolocation, ASN, and historical pattern. Alert on new/rare IPs successfully completing IKEv1 Phase 1 and Phase 2, especially if the IP is known to other SOCs or appears in threat feeds as scanner/botnet.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Handshake Spike and Brute-Force Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes improper IKEv1 authentication. Vulnerability makes the exchange bypassable, creating opportunity for brute-force or fuzzing attempts. Expect volume anomaly if adversaries attempt mass exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spike in IKEv1 Phase 1 initiation attempts (Main or Aggressive mode) without corresponding Phase 2 completion. Compare baseline IKEv1 volume per source IP; flag IPs with >10 Phase 1 attempts in 5 minutes but <30% Phase 2 success (suggests fuzzing or brute-force prior to exploitation).

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Lateral Movement and Suspicious Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Once inside via unauthorized VPN access, expect command & control, lateral movement, or exfiltration. Need detection for activity sourced from successful unauthenticated VPN sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful VPN sessions (especially those without matching auth-server confirmation) with downstream activity: DNS tunneling, C2 beacon communication, port scanning from the VPN IP, or suspicious SMB/RDP to internal hosts. Baseline expected post-VPN behavior and alert on deviations from known-good remote-work patterns.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Log Ingestion / CVE-2026-50751 Vulnerability Status
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-11.' Need operational detection to ensure logs are flowing from Check Point gateways and confirm patch status across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Check Point Security Gateways in inventory for CVE-2026-50751 remediation status. Confirm log ingestion is active from each gateway (SmartLog, audit logs) and baseline IKEv1 traffic patterns pre-patch. After patch deadline, flag any gateway still reporting as unpatched or with IKEv1 anomalies as high-priority for remediation team.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Request Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'By crafting requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization, attackers can bypass authentication and reach backend services that should not be publicly accessible.' This is the foundational attack enabling all downstream exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests where the raw HTTP request URI differs from the normalized/canonical form after Nginx processing. Specifically monitor for paths claiming auth-exempt status in raw form (e.g., /api/auth/validate-sso/) that resolve to protected internal endpoints after normalization. Correlate with subsequent unauthenticated access to restricted API functions.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal in Authenticated Endpoint Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-34909 as 'a path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system,' used to discover vulnerable code paths post-auth-bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e/, etc.) in API parameters targeting endpoints reached via the auth-bypass chain. Look for file reads from unusual directories (system config, /etc, application internals) through API endpoints. Correlate with requests to /api/auth/validate-sso/ in preceding logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Injection in ucs/update/latest_package Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands on the system.' Endpoint explicitly named: ucs/update/latest_package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to /ucs/update/latest_package containing shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) in body parameters. Correlate with immediate child process creation (sh, bash, curl, wget) under the ucs-update service. Alert on any deviation from expected parameter format.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries, making escalation to root trivial.' This is the escalation mechanism converting RCE into root compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo invocations from ucs-update process or its children that complete without password prompts (zero-delay sudo execution, exit code 0). Monitor sudoers file for passwordless sudo entries for the ucs-update account. Track any process UID elevation from non-root to root (UID 0) originating from service account context.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Processes Under ucs-update Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article defensive guidance: 'monitor requests to ucs/update/latest_package, suspicious child processes under ucs-update, and unexpected sudo commands.' Post-injection indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by ucs-update (expected: package managers, system utilities). Alert on anomalous children: interactive shells (sh, bash, zsh), network utilities (nc, curl, wget, socat), or reverse shells. Enforce mandatory parent-child process integrity: if ucs-update spawns processes, those children must execute within defined security contexts.

suggestion.title: Chained Detection Pattern: /api/auth/validate-sso/ → ucs/update/latest_package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicit defender guidance: 'defenders can also look for requests containing /api/auth/validate-sso/ and monitor requests to ucs/update/latest_package.` These two endpoints constitute the attack chain signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create sequence detection: flag any source IP issuing requests to /api/auth/validate-sso/ (especially from external/untrusted networks) followed by requests to /ucs/update/latest_package within 30 seconds. Apply HIGH alert if these requests lack proper authentication tokens or session cookies, or if the auth path appears to receive normalized routing (2nd request reaches backend despite appearing to target exempt endpoint in 1st request).

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet file-load method calls with phar:// wrapper in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via filename parameter passed to PHPSpreadsheet loader—application logs or web framework instrumentation would show load() or similar method calls with phar:// wrapper.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP/application logs for PHPSpreadsheet file loading operations (load, read, parse methods) where the filename parameter contains phar:// scheme. Also detect exceptions from parse_url or File::prohibitWrappers if framework logs the rejection.

suggestion.title: Multiple phar:// URL requests to PHPSpreadsheet endpoints from single source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a specific bypass pattern (three+ slashes)—attackers probing or attempting exploitation would send multiple requests. Threshold-based detection identifies scanning behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if a single source IP sends >3 HTTP requests containing phar:// variants within 10 minutes to any web endpoint known to process file uploads or spreadsheet imports.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-34084 patch version gap analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-45034 is a bypass of the CVE-2026-34084 patch—vulnerable versions are those with the incomplete prohibitWrappers check. Identify hosts running PHPSpreadsheet versions vulnerable to both CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous asset hunt: identify hosts running PHPSpreadsheet versions between (initial vulnerable version) and (version containing parse_url fix) or confirm presence of File::prohibitWrappers function with incomplete validation logic via SAST/DAST.

suggestion.title: Encoded phar:// variants in HTTP requests (case/encoding evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article shows attackers bypass the scheme check via slash-count manipulation (phar:///...). Attackers may also try case variations (PHAR://, PhAr://) or double-encoding (phar%253A%252F%252F) to evade pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phar:// pattern with case-insensitive regex, handle URL double-encoding chains, and check for hex-encoding (%70%61%72) or unicode variants. Alert on any form attempting to obfuscate the phar scheme.

suggestion.title: osascript with nested tell blocks and do shell script injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: URL is 'interpolated' into AppleScript with mismatched tell-block nesting allowing code escape. This is the core technical signature (UC_13_2 in article), yet pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect osascript invocation with multiple 'tell application' blocks and 'do shell script' in same command line, or when parent is Anyquery. The nested tell structure is the injection escape pattern.

suggestion.title: seturl.js execution and filesystem modification
suggestion.rationale: Article names seturl.js as the vulnerable component in chrome_tabs plugin (UC_13_1); pipeline provided zero file artifacts or executable hunts despite this being the exact attack point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt seturl.js process execution or file creation/modification events, correlating with Anyquery or Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari processes. Direct artifact from the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47252 asset exposure matching Anyquery ≤0.4.4
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable version (0.4.4, commit 0abd460); standard vulnerability matching is missing. Should query software inventory for installations on macOS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset-centric hunt: locate Anyquery version 0.4.4 (0abd460) or earlier on macOS; correlate with users visiting untrusted URLs in Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari to detect exposure.

suggestion.title: Browser process spawning osascript with URL-derived arguments
suggestion.rationale: Root cause is unescaped URL interpolation into AppleScript. Generic behavioral signature: watch for Chrome/Safari/Brave injecting URL content into script interpreter arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes (Chrome, Brave, Edge, Safari) spawning osascript or jxa with unusual command-line arguments or environment variables containing URL-like strings; correlation between visited URL and subsequent script invocation.

suggestion.title: API Token Scope Bypass — cross-operator resource access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'API trusts the bearer token alone for authorisation; per-CA ownership is enforced only in the Web layer' — core vulnerability is an operator-scoped token succeeding on non-owned operator resources. No current UC detects this scope-bypass pattern directly (UCs detect *outcomes*, not the auth-bypass itself). Should flag: same user/token accessing /api/v1/operators/{X}/... for multiple distinct operator IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User with bearer token successfully POSTs/PUTs to /api/v1/operators/{different_ids}/* or /api/v1/networks/{different_ids}/* where {different_ids} span >1 distinct operator namespace. Authorization bypass signature: 200/201/204 without corresponding Web UI grant (loadAccessibleCA would deny).

suggestion.title: Enrollment Token/Key Material Leakage in API Responses
suggestion.rationale: UC_12_2 covers the reenroll→enroll sequence for detection, but article's mention of 'host identity hijack' and T1552.004 (Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys) suggest API responses contain enrollment tokens/certificates. No UC explicitly hunts for key material in response payloads or token reuse across different hosts post-reenroll.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll returns 200 with response body containing Base64/PEM enrollment token or certificate. Same token or derived certificate appears in subsequent POST /api/v1/enroll from different source IP or user within 60s (lateral movement / token reuse).

suggestion.title: Network Service Enumeration via API Discovery Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1526 (Cloud Service Discovery) and T1087 (Account Discovery) are listed but UC_12_3 focuses on 'enumeration burst' behaviorally. Missing: explicit detection of sequential GET requests discovering network/firewall/host inventory that precedes actual exploitation. Phrase: 'CA-management endpoints in internal/api/cas.go' implies discoverable service topology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User issues 5+ unique GET requests to /api/v1/networks, /api/v1/hosts, /api/v1/operators endpoints (enumeration pattern) followed within 5min by state-change POST to one of those resources. Indicates recon→exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Non-Admin Operator Mutation via Under-Protected API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: UC_12_5 catches disable/enable/revocation, but article's core narrative is that 'most endpoints' in /api/v1/* lack ownership checks. Missing: explicit detection of a user with operator-user role (not admin) successfully calling admin-only mutations like operator.disable, api-key.delete on *other* operators' resources—the authorization bypass itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User with role 'operator' or 'user' (not 'admin') POSTs to /api/v1/operators/{target}/disable or DELETEs /api/v1/operators/{target}/api-keys/*, receives 200/204, and {target} is not their own operator_id (role-privilege boundary crossed).

suggestion.title: New User Creates Repository Immediately (Gogs Account-Repo Creation Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Since Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default...an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance.' This is the entry point for the exploit chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a newly created Gogs user creates a repository within minutes of account creation. Baseline typical user-repo creation delay and flag anomalies, particularly with rebase merge enabled in repo settings.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Rebase Merge Configuration Change (Gogs Merge Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This is the execution point for the argument injection vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs repository settings changes for rebase-merge enablement by low-privilege or newly created users. Pair with merge operation logs to detect subsequent exploit execution patterns in Git command parameters.

suggestion.title: Private Repository Access by Newly Created Account (Gogs Lateral Movement)
suggestion.rationale: Article states the exploit allows attackers to 'read any repository (including private repos), steal credentials, move laterally to other systems on the network, and alter any hosted source code.' Detection should capture early access to sensitive repos by suspicious accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when accounts created in the past 24 hours access private repositories they don't own, particularly if coupled with clone/pull operations on high-value or credential-containing repositories.

suggestion.title: Gogs Argument Injection in Merge Operations (Exploit Execution Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'argument injection vulnerability' in Merge() function: 'this flaw is very similar to other argument-injection flaws...but it affects a different code path (Merge()) that was never addressed.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect Gogs merge operation logs and underlying Git process invocations for malformed or suspicious argument patterns typical of command injection (escaped quotes, backticks, semicolons, pipe operators in merge metadata fields).

suggestion.title: Gogs Server Version Detection (Unpatched Instance Fingerprinting)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'affects all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev' and 'Rapid7 recommends that all Gogs users upgrade immediately' to 0.14.3 released June 7. Version enumeration is baseline hardening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Gogs server instances via version banner in HTTP responses or API endpoints. Flag instances running versions ≤0.14.2 or 0.15.0+dev. Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to prioritize patching.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploitation Workflow (Account→Repo→Merge→RCE Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes end-to-end exploit sequence: 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository...Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner. From there, enabling rebase merging is a single toggle.' This is a compound kill-chain event chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gogs events across a 1-2 hour window: new user creation + repo creation by same user + rebase merge enable + merge operation with suspicious Git arguments or output. Flag multi-stage sequences as likely exploitation.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Phishing Link Engagement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack'—need detection for user interaction with malicious links distributed via WhatsApp messaging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WhatsApp messaging logs for suspicious URLs and correlate click events with subsequent device behavior (unexpected process spawning, permission grants, enrollment anomalies). Alert on links resolving to known NSO/Pegasus infrastructure.

suggestion.title: NSO Pegasus C2 Communication Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group operates Pegasus spyware requiring command-and-control channels; baseline detection for Pegasus C2 HTTP/HTTPS/DNS patterns is essential for NSO threat hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTPS connections or DNS queries matching known Pegasus C2 infrastructure (specific TLS certificate patterns, HTTP User-Agent strings, behavioral connection patterns). Correlate with post-phishing timeline.

suggestion.title: Pegasus Surveillance Capability Activation (Screen/Audio Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Successful Pegasus exploitation activates surveillance modules T1113 (Screen Capture) and T1123 (Audio Capture); post-phishing system should show behavioral markers of these capabilities activating.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-WhatsApp-phishing-interaction, detect suspicious process creation for screen recording, audio capture, or keystroke logging. Alert on Pegasus-signature process names or unusual access to frame buffers, audio devices, or input streams.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Campaign Indicators via WhatsApp Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeted phishing via WhatsApp (not mass phishing); detection should correlate message metadata, sender patterns, and shortened URLs with NSO spearphishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WhatsApp message sender reputation, message timing, and URL shortener domains with known NSO phishing campaigns. Flag messages with obfuscated links or sender impersonation attempts.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Script File Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'purpose-built web shell framework' as primary attack mechanism but pipeline generated zero persistence detections. Phrase: 'purpose-built web shell framework'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS web root directories (C:\inetpub\wwwroot, app-specific paths) for suspicious .aspx, .ashx, .asmx file creation. Alert on script files with mismatched creation times, unusual ownership (service account vs. app identity), or suspicious embedded entropy. Correlate file writes with IIS application pool process activity.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Command Execution from IIS Worker
suggestion.rationale: Web shell framework deployed to execute commands; article emphasizes execution capability but zero execution-chain detection suggested. Phrase: 'purpose-built...designed to evade every detection method'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or IIS application pool identities spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, csc.exe, or other shell interpreters. Baseline legitimate IIS activity and flag command-line arguments containing obfuscated syntax, Base64 encoding, or file operations outside web application context.

suggestion.title: Cryptographic Obfuscation in IIS Web Files
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states web shell is 'cryptographically unique' and designed to 'evade every detection method.' Defense-evasion via obfuscation not mapped to detection. Phrase: 'cryptographically unique...designed to evade every detection method'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .aspx/.ashx files in web roots for high entropy, Base64/hex-encoded content, obfuscated method names, or embedded cryptographic signatures. Monitor IIS request logs for suspicious character sequences, mixed-case encoding patterns, or unusual %XX URL-encoded payloads in POST/GET parameters targeting script handlers.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from IIS to Article C2 IOCs
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 5 C2 IOCs (43.160.202.246, 140.206.161.227, 124.156.129.151, ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com) but pipeline generated zero network hunt. Missing command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from w3wp.exe or IIS service accounts to the five article IOCs or to non-standard/non-business ports. Flag connections to external IP space that don't correlate with known backend database/SaaS dependencies. Analyze HTTP request headers in IIS logs for suspicious User-Agent strings or encoded command payloads.

suggestion.title: Python .pth File Execution from Site-Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious artifacts included a '*-setup.pth' file' and 'a compromised wheel can turn an otherwise passive dependency install into a delayed execution trigger: the next Python, pip, test run, notebook kernel, CI job, or package-management command that starts Python may process the malicious .pth'. Core execution primitive completely unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .pth file creation in Python site-packages directories with suspicious or obfuscated content, especially during or shortly after pip install. Monitor for Python process execution immediately following site-packages .pth write. Alert on .pth files that execute external commands or download binaries.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Bun JavaScript Runtime Download from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Defenders should look for...unexpected downloads of the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub'. This is mentioned as a core detection vector but not mapped to any UC or technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect any curl/wget/powershell process spawned from Python context downloading from github.com/oven-sh/bun or similar Bun distribution points, especially from CI/CD or developer workstations not known to develop in Bun. Alert on Bun binary execution from temporary directories within minutes of download.

suggestion.title: Process Chain: Python Parent Spawning Bun to Execute _index.js
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights: 'Defenders should look for process chains where Python launches Bun to execute _index.js'. This explicit detection signature is both highly specific and highly indicative of this attack family but received zero UC coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent=python* spawning child=bun/Bun with command line containing '_index.js'. This process hierarchy is abnormal for legitimate workloads and strongly indicates supply-chain compromise. Escalate if _index.js is in /tmp, site-packages, or other non-standard locations.

suggestion.title: Enumeration and Access of Multi-Type Developer Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'targeted a broad range of developer secrets that included the following: GitHub tokens...npm, PyPI, RubyGems, JFrog publishing tokens...AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, and Vault credentials...SSH keys...Docker credentials...[and] .env, .npmrc, .pypirc'. No UC detects systematic credential file access from Python/Bun processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python or Bun processes reading sequentially from credential-bearing files: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.aws/*, ~/.azure/*, .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, *-setup.pth, MCP config directories. Alert on cross-file access patterns (reading 3+ different credential types in <1 minute) from a single process tree as indicative of credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Creation via Compromised Actions Workflow for Data Exfiltration
