suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'primary data exfiltration method is similar to past Shai-Hulud operations, using automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions'. This organizational-level observable describing automated repo creation during compromise is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls creating new repositories from CI/CD runner IPs or automation accounts, especially outside normal development hours. Flag if repository names match exfiltration patterns (*-secrets, *-exfil, *-backup) or if pushed data contains base64-encoded credentials, hex patterns matching SSH keys, or AWS key formats.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Anthropic API Endpoint for HTTPS Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'second exfiltration method based on direct HTTPS also exists, pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage'. This specific masqueraded endpoint used for credential exfiltration should alert on command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS requests for api.anthropic.com or similar Anthropic-branded domains from development machines or CI runners, especially if organization does not legitimate use Anthropic API. Flag any HTTP/HTTPS POST to this domain with credential-like payloads (base64, JWT patterns, JSON with token/secret fields). Treat as fallback exfiltration channel.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Banking App APK Downloads from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file.' Nine APK samples named for Italian and Spanish banks (Intesa Carte.apk, Sella Carte.apk, Nexi Carte.apk, Fideuram Carte.apk, Mooney Carte.apk, CaixaBank.apk variants) were hosted starting April 10.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK file downloads or installations from GitHub with names matching banking app patterns (*Carte.apk, CaixaBank*, Intesa*, Nexi*, Fideuram*, Mooney*). Correlate with user clicking phishing links impersonating financial institution login portals.

suggestion.title: Android NFC + Network Permissions in Untrusted Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware requesting NFC access via fake verification screens, then 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' Simultaneous NFC and internet permissions is inherently suspicious on Android.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Android apps requesting android.permission.NFC combined with android.permission.INTERNET, especially if they initiate WebSocket connections or abnormal HTTPS traffic. Baseline against known legitimate banking apps; NFCShare impersonations will lack legitimate signing certificates.

suggestion.title: Malformed APK ZIP Archive Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'newer samples include poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP, causing some extraction tools to wrongly interpret internal relative paths as filesystem paths and trigger errors.' This anti-analysis evasion is novel and should alert security tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK files (ZIP archives) with malformed or path-traversal-style internal file paths (e.g., '../../../evil.dex') that fail standard extraction, or trigger ZIP validation warnings. This indicates intentional obfuscation to evade static analysis.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Bulk APK Uploads (Multiple Banking App Names)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Since its creation on April 10, the GitHub repository used for distributing NFCShare has hosted 56 unique APKs' impersonating multiple banks. Repository pivot on April 10 creation with rapid malware proliferation is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub for repositories created in April 2026 containing multiple APK commits with banking app names (Intesa, Sella, Nexi, Fideuram, Mooney, CaixaBank, Banca Sella). Flag accounts with high-velocity APK uploads (56 samples over 2 months) and no legitimate development history.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Communication from Mobile Banking Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' No C2 detection pattern for WebSocket-based exfiltration of payment card data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket (ws://, wss://) connections from processes named after banking apps (Intesa*, CaixaBank*, etc.) to external IPs, especially if connections follow NFC-read activity patterns. Cross-reference IP/domain reputation for hosting multiple malware variants.

suggestion.title: Phishing-to-Malicious-APK Redirect Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials. Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository.' This two-stage chain (phishing + app update upsell) is the social engineering vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing domains impersonating Italian/Spanish financial institutions (Intesa, Sella, Nexi, Fideuram, Mooney, CaixaBank) with HTTP 302 redirects to GitHub repositories containing APK downloads. Timeline anchor: repo creation April 10, 2026; attacks observed from May 14, 2026.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Escalates to UID 0 Without sudo/su Wrapper
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'enables Local Root Access.' Successful exploitation should produce processes spawned by non-root parent running as UID 0—direct indicator of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process with UID=0 where parent process UID > 0 and parent is not sudo, su, systemd-run, or other known privilege elevation wrapper. Baseline legitimate suid binaries (ping, passwd) and system daemons to reduce false positives. Trigger: shell processes (bash, sh, zsh, dash) spawned as UID 0 from user context.

suggestion.title: Kernel Memory Access Via /proc or /dev Interface
suggestion.rationale: One-character kernel flaws typically require reading/writing kernel memory. Article describes exploitation of kernel code path—likely requires /proc/*/mem, /dev/mem, or eBPF-based memory manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor attempts to open /proc/*/mem, /dev/mem, /dev/kmem, or /sys/kernel/debug/* by non-root processes or unexpected processes. Cross-reference with process ancestry and file descriptor abuse patterns. Expected FP: kernel debuggers, valgrind, perf.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Load or Unsigned Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits may load malicious modules or execute code via eBPF/kprobes. Title 'one-character flaw' suggests targeted kernel path—detection via module instrumentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on insmod, modprobe, or programmatic module loading (syscall: init_module, finit_module) from non-root context or at unusual times. Correlate with previous privilege boundary checks. Monitor for unsigned or out-of-tree module signatures.

suggestion.title: Kernel Oops, Segfault, or Capability Boundary Violation in Logs Before Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel flaws often trigger BUG_ON(), assertions, or segmentation faults during exploitation attempts. Single-character bugs suggest specific code path trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate kernel log warnings (dmesg, /var/log/kern.log, audit logs) for capability boundary violations, segmentation faults, or BUG_ON messages with subsequent UID=0 process creation within 1-5 second window. Flag as exploit preparation + successful escalation chain.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Tool or Payload Execution Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploits Now Public'—public exploit tools will have consistent command-line signatures, argument patterns, or file drop locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE number is extracted, hunt for: (1) process creation with suspicious argument patterns (hardcoded offsets, /proc argument access), (2) known exploit tool names (e.g., CVE-XXXX-XXXX.c, poc.bin), (3) compilation of exploit code from /tmp or /dev/shm, (4) curl/wget download followed by immediate execution.

suggestion.title: Multiple Password Resets from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 20,000+ accounts hijacked via HTS password resets. Article: 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in and hijack accounts without two-factor authentication.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for this bulk pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when a single source (IP, user agent, session ID) requests password resets for 5+ distinct accounts within 1 hour. Correlate with lack of prior account relationship. High-fidelity if targets span different user groups or departments.

suggestion.title: Account Access Post-Unexpected Password Reset
suggestion.rationale: Attack sequence: reset password → immediate login via reset link. Article: 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in and hijack accounts.' Pipeline missed the authentication anomaly post-reset.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate password-reset events with successful login from different geography/IP within 15 minutes. Trigger alert if login originates from country user has never accessed account from, or if reset disabled prior 2FA enrollment.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Tool Abuse - Unverified Email in Reset Flow
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: HTS didn't validate email ownership. Article: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts, they obtained password reset links.' Pipeline missed validation-bypass pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for password-reset tokens issued without successful email-verification completion. Flag cases where reset link is clicked from IP that never submitted the recovery request. Detect if reset initiated with unverified/secondary email address on account.

suggestion.title: 2FA-Disabled Accounts with Unauthorized Login
suggestion.rationale: Attackers specifically targeted accounts lacking 2FA. Article: 'hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.' Pipeline failed to model this targeting pattern and post-compromise access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on login to accounts where 2FA was previously enrolled but is now disabled. Cross-correlate with account-recovery audit logs. Elevate severity if login follows bulk password-reset operation or originates from anomalous location.

suggestion.title: Coordinated Bulk Account Takeover Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 20,000+ accounts compromised in coordinated attack. Article: 'over 20,000 Instagram users had their accounts hijacked in a recent incident.' Pipeline missed detection of coordinated account compromise wave.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate login events: if 20+ accounts from same organization log in from identical anomalous IP post-password-reset within 2-hour window, trigger high-confidence alert. Correlate with account-recovery tool audit logs to establish causal link.

suggestion.title: Rapid Account Recovery Requests - Enumeration or Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: Attack required generating reset links for thousands of accounts. Article: 'vulnerability in an AI-assisted account recovery system...was exploited by unauthorized third parties to perform password resets on Instagram user accounts.' Pipeline missed enumeration/brute-force detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >10 password-reset requests per minute from single IP to account-recovery tool. Flag attempts using unverified contact methods (secondary email, recovery phone). Correlate request volume with reset-success rate to identify systematic exploitation vs. legitimate bulk support.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Access via Compromised Third-Party Vendor Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers gained access to a database at a third-party vendor' yet no detection use case targets third-party credential compromise or lateral movement from vendor systems into client infrastructure. This is a supply-chain attack pattern requiring distinct detection signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database access events from service accounts associated with third-party vendor integrations, particularly with logon failures preceding successful access, or access outside normal business hours from the vendor's IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Database Export to Exfiltration Path
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'database...containing customer information' was accessed; no use case detects the exfiltration phase. Query for abnormal volume exports, backup-to-external-location patterns, or bulk SELECT statements on customer tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on queries exporting >1000 customer records from SoFi Securities databases in single session, unscheduled data dumps to temp locations, or database backup files copied to cloud storage or external SMB shares.

suggestion.title: Database Access from Unusual Geographic Context
suggestion.rationale: Breach occurred at Hong Kong subsidiary; detection should flag access from geographies inconsistent with normal operations or from VPN/proxy exit nodes atypical for vendor staff.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database logins from IP geolocation mismatched to user's baseline (e.g., London-based vendor staff suddenly accessing from China), or access chains through rotating residential proxies.

suggestion.title: Detection Lag on Vendor System Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'discovered the incident on April 30, 2026'—no timeline given for actual compromise date. Use case should establish baselining to detect dwell time gaps when vendor account activity goes silent or shifts, suggesting account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for vendor service account login cadence and alert on 72+ hour gaps followed by resumed activity from new IP/device, or rapid privilege escalation immediately after account reactivation.

suggestion.title: Credential Reuse Across SoFi Infrastructure Post-Vendor Breach
suggestion.rationale: Once vendor credentials compromise is discovered, the attack may pivot; no use case covers lateral movement from vendor integration points into SoFi's internal Hong Kong infrastructure using harvested or reused credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service account or vendor-issued credentials being used to authenticate to non-vendor SoFi systems, particularly from the vendor's IP block or with failed attempts preceding success, indicating credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Vishing Call Detection via Phone Metadata & Caller Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'vishing' as attack vector ('UNC3753 Used Vishing and Physical Intrusions'). Pipeline missed initial-access detection for voice-based social engineering. Should alert on calls impersonating trusted entities with high-context pretexting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound calls from spoofed/newly-registered caller IDs targeting employees in finance or operations roles within 48h of registration. Correlate call metadata (duration, frequency, caller lookup failure) with subsequent credential submission to VPN/OWA logs.

suggestion.title: Physical Access Correlation with Data Exfiltration Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Physical Intrusions' paired with 'Data Theft'. Pipeline missed the correlation detection—physical badge swipes or CCTV ingress should trigger heightened monitoring for concurrent file access/network egress anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After-hours badge access to sensitive data centers correlates with elevated SMB/API calls to cloud storage or USB device mount events, or large encrypted file staging in temp directories. High severity if access is new employee or contractor with no prior exfiltration baseline.

suggestion.title: Ransom Demand & Extortion Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign described as 'Data Theft Extortion'—pipeline silent on impact phase. Should surface ransom notes, threatening emails, or bulk data-sample publication attempts. Cite: 'Extortion Campaign' in title implies demand delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing typical ransom-note phrasing ('your data has been encrypted,' 'contact us for decryption key') sent to org domain or board members. Cross-ref with OSINT feeds for org data dumps on dark web. High severity if sample files (confidential docs, customer PII) posted publicly with proof of exfil.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvest Post-Vishing via Web Form or Clone
suggestion.rationale: Vishing typically funnels targets to fake login portals; article fails to articulate the downstream credential-capture step but it is implicit ('vishing' → access → theft chain). Pipeline missed T1598 credential-interception detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After vishing calls, monitor for new phishing URLs registered to look-alike domains (typosquatting). Alert on employee credentials submitted to non-corporate IPs within 2h of call. Cross-check AD sign-in logs for impossible-travel or unusual geolocation + credential-stuffing patterns post-call.

suggestion.title: Insider or Compromised Employee Data Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Physical intrusion + vishing suggest targeted employees may be insiders or heavily compromised. Pipeline missed detection for abnormal file-access patterns (policy violation, bulk-read, cross-org access).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user accessing files outside their department, pulling full lists of employee/customer databases, or systematically enumerating directory-service objects (LDAP queries) after vishing compromise. High severity if user is contractor, recently-hired, or has active security exception.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'VerdantBamboo Deploys BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances'—direct attestation of malware execution as primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of BRICKSTORM payload processes on Linux appliance hosts. Flag process execution from temporary directories, script interpreters invoking remote payloads, and unusual child processes spawned by network service daemons or management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Appliance Management Interface Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies deployment 'on Linux Appliances'—indicates initial access via remote management protocols (SSH, HTTPS) to appliance control planes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/HTTPS connections to appliance management IPs from untrusted networks. Flag failed-then-successful authentication patterns, geographically anomalous management logins, and credential reuse across appliance fleet.

suggestion.title: Linux Boot/Init System Persistence Establishment
suggestion.rationale: BSD variant malware typically persists via firmware or init-level hooks; cross-platform nature implies bootkit or systemd-level persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/init.d, systemd service directories, GRUB parameters, and kernel module loading for unauthorized modifications. Flag service unit creation by unprivileged processes, binary suid changes, and bootloader config alterations on appliance hosts.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM C2 Egress Detection
suggestion.rationale: Successful malware deployment presumes active C2 communication; article [CRIT] severity indicates live attacker control requiring network-based indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections from compromised appliances to C2 infrastructure. Monitor for DNS queries to attacker-controlled domains, non-standard port usage on appliance egress, TLS certificate anomalies, and beaconing patterns inconsistent with legitimate appliance protocols.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg RCE — Suspicious Small Network Packet to Media Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'critical RCE-capable heap buffer overflow reachable with a single 183-byte network packet.' Pipeline did not generate detection for this specific attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ingress packets to known FFmpeg services (web frontends, streaming endpoints, surveillance systems) with payload size 170–200 bytes (accounting for headers). Correlate packet timing against FFmpeg process CPU spikes. High specificity if source is non-whitelisted external IP.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Process Unexpected Child Execution Post-Packet
suggestion.rationale: Successful heap buffer overflow RCE would manifest as arbitrary code execution; article states 'Enables Remote Code Execution Attacks.' Pipeline missed post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FFmpeg process spawning unexpected child processes (bash, powershell, curl, wget) within 5 seconds of receiving suspicious network traffic. Baseline expected children (demux, filter, encode subprocess families); alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Vulnerable Version In-Use Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 21 0-day vulns in FFmpeg and notes widespread deployment across 'browsers, streaming platforms, surveillance systems, and cloud infrastructure.' Pipeline did not generate inventory/discovery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate running FFmpeg processes and version strings from process command-line args, library load events, and HTTP User-Agent headers. Correlate against CVE-2026-39210..39218 patch availability. Alert if vulnerable version detected in production segment.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Connections from FFmpeg Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE success would enable attacker to pivot from compromised FFmpeg host; article emphasizes media processing criticality in cloud/streaming infrastructure. Pipeline did not suggest post-compromise C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound destinations from FFmpeg processes (CDN pulls, origin fetches, logging endpoints). Alert on new outbound IP/domain connections, especially on non-standard ports or to residential/suspicious ASNs, shortly after 183-byte ingress packet detected.

suggestion.title: Cross-Stack FFmpeg Exploitation Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states FFmpeg powers 'browsers, streaming platforms, surveillance systems, and cloud infrastructure'—multi-layer attack surface. Pipeline did not suggest multi-source correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 183-byte packet detections across web-tier WAF logs, streaming platform load balancers, surveillance system network ingress, and cloud egress. Single isolated hit may be noise; multiple hits across infrastructure types within 1-hour window indicates coordinated exploitation campaign.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Buffer Overflow Crash Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'heap buffer overflow'; this specific memory corruption often leaves forensic markers. Pipeline did not generate crash/segfault detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg process crashes with high-severity error codes (segmentation fault, access violation, heap corruption messages). Correlate crash timing with suspicious network traffic. Collect crash dumps for post-incident forensics; heap overflow patterns may persist in dump metadata.

suggestion.title: Chrome Process Execution from Suspicious Parent or with RWX Memory Regions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Zero-Day CVE-2026-11645 Exploited in the Wild'—confirms active code execution phase. V8 exploitation typically spawns child processes or modifies memory permissions for shellcode execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chrome/Chromium process creates child processes with no parent context justification, or chrome.exe/v8 runtime shows VirtualAlloc→VirtualProtect→CreateRemoteThread pattern. Execution from unusual working directory or with anomalous environment variables may indicate exploit-stage launcher.

suggestion.title: Chrome Sandbox Escape via Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Full-chain client-side exploits typically chain code execution in sandbox with privilege escalation ('Patch Now' urgency suggests kernel or system-level impact risk).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chrome/renderer process attempts to load unsigned drivers, access kernel handles (e.g., \Device\* object access), or spawn SYSTEM-level child processes. Monitor for DLL injection or token elevation attempts from browser context.

suggestion.title: V8 Heap Exploitation Memory Patterns
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-11645 targets Chrome V8 engine; exploitation typically involves heap grooming, overflow, or corruption (WRITE-WHAT-WHERE pattern).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for chrome.exe VirtualAlloc patterns showing repeated small allocations followed by VirtualProtect changing PAGE_READWRITE to PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE in rapid succession. Heap corruption exploits often exhibit distinct allocation/reprotection cadence.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Execution via V8 Exploit Payload
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation starts with malicious JavaScript received via drive-by or phishing; V8 flaw triggers code execution from within JIT-compiled JS context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound HTTP/HTTPS responses with obfuscated or anomalous JavaScript arriving at Chrome process; correlate with process execution anomalies within 100ms. Monitor for heap spray patterns (repeated ArrayBuffer allocations) which often precede exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Authentication Bypass Attempt (IKEv1)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw...to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' Core attack vector explicitly documented but no detection case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated VPN connection attempts on Check Point Mobile Access or Remote Access gateways using IKEv1 protocol. Alert on successful session establishment without valid machine certificate or legacy client authentication. Filter for connections to systems configured with deprecated IKEv1 key exchange.

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Post-VPN Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate.' Explicitly links ransomware actor to this VPN breach but no detection case captures post-exploitation Qilin IOCs or behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful VPN compromise, detect Qilin ransomware process execution, file encryption activity (mass file modifications with .qilin extension if applicable), and lateral movement patterns consistent with RaaS operations. Correlate VPN authentication bypass timeline with subsequent endpoint encryption events.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Activity on Modern IKEv2 Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol...that accept legacy Remote Access clients.' Detection gap: monitoring for clients using outdated protocols when IKEv2 should be enforced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IKEv1 protocol negotiation on Check Point gateways configured to enforce IKEv2 only. Flag legacy Remote Access client connections by user agent or handshake signature. Baseline normal client versions and alert on deprecated or unusual versions attempting connection.

suggestion.title: Check Point Gateway Without Machine Certificate Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate for connections' - configuration detection. Identifies misconfigured gateways vulnerable to the exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Check Point VPN gateway configurations to identify instances where Machine Certificate Authentication is not mandatory. Flag any gateway still accepting Remote Access clients without certificate-based authentication. Correlate with IKEv1 protocol usage to identify highest-risk endpoints.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering to Account Hijacking Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'social engineered a valid account on the education shard' and gained 'access to the platform following a social engineering attack.' No detection heuristics generated for credential compromise via phishing or pretexting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sign-in patterns inconsistent with account baseline post-social engineering campaigns targeting government sector. Flag impossible travel (sign-in from geographically distant location within short window). Cross-correlate with internal security awareness training completion to identify high-risk accounts.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded LDAP Credential Exposure via Configuration Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director.' Credentials exposed in version control or shared file systems enable account hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search PowerShell scripts in shared repositories, email, and file shares for regex patterns matching LDAP connection strings with embedded credentials (e.g., 'LDAP://.*password=.*', 'uid=.*pwd='). Alert on script distribution outside normal change-management workflows.

suggestion.title: Bulk Message Exfiltration from Messaging Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages and information on over 73,000 accounts.' This represents anomalous query volume against a messaging service not typical of legitimate usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate message query patterns by user and service account. Alert on single account executing >10k message queries in <1 hour window, or queries for messages outside user's typical chat rooms/teams. Monitor for sequential bulk account metadata lookups (T1087 - Account Discovery).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or Token-less File Download Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article reports attacker state 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token.' This is an authentication bypass enabling mass file exfiltration: '13.5GB of documents and media files.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file download endpoints for requests lacking or with invalid authentication tokens. Alert on automated sequential file downloads (inferred from file IDs in messages). Correlate large aggregated download volumes (>1GB in <1 hour) with single user/IP. Look for repeated 200 responses on endpoints that should require valid bearer tokens.

suggestion.title: Cross-Shard Infrastructure Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor demonstrates knowledge of platform's sharded architecture ('matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr' and claims 'other shards will have more'), suggesting active reconnaissance of infrastructure topology post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or HTTP requests to multiple shard endpoints from a single user account (especially education.tchap, health.tchap, etc.). Alert if previously-dormant account suddenly accesses infrastructure metadata endpoints or requests redirect information for services outside their organization.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Legitimate Credentials Across Administrative Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Attacker accessed 'education shard' and claimed ability to access 'every file' regardless of shard segregation. Post-compromise lateral movement using the hijacked account to enumerate and access restricted resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a user account accesses administrative functions or cross-shard services not aligned with their job role or previous behavior. Flag access to internal management APIs (media serving, configuration) from a standard user account. Monitor for permission escalation immediately following a sign-in from anomalous location.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Heap Corruption Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTML pages' causing 'heap corruption' and 'out-of-bounds read and write weakness.' No detection hypothesis offered despite explicit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome process crashes immediately following navigation to untrusted/newly-visited domains, correlate with V8 engine error codes. Detect unusual memory access patterns (out-of-bounds writes) or abnormal heap fragmentation in browser renderer processes post-page-load.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass Detection Post-Browser Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could also be exploited to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR, making it easier to achieve code execution via another weakness.' Chain to secondary RCE not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, flag sequences where ASLR entropy is leaked or bypassed (base address disclosure followed by calculated offset writes). Correlate Chrome renderer crashes with subsequent unsigned code injection attempts in child processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Patch Adoption Lag
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'update was available immediately' but 'could take days or weeks to reach all Chrome users.' Unpatched systems remain exploitable; versions 149.0.7827.102/103 are the patched baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome browsers with version < 149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or < 149.0.7827.103 (macOS) in production. Cross-correlate with visits to attacker-controlled or compromised HTML hosts (when attribution becomes available).

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation: Prior CVE Series Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article catalogs five 2026 zero-days and eight from 2025, all exploited in attacks. Pattern: V8 bugs (CVE-2026-3910, CVE-2026-11645) vs. graphics layer (CVE-2026-3909 Skia, CVE-2026-5281 WebGPU). Detection should fingerprint engine-specific exploit patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Group Chrome crashes by root-cause subsystem (V8, Skia, WebGPU, Dawn). Detect repeated crashes in the same engine module from the same source domain within minutes (indicates exploitation scanning or multi-stage attack).

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Out-of-Bounds Memory Read
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'can expose sensitive information' via 'out-of-bounds memory' access post-heap-corruption. No detection for data exfiltration to attacker-controlled destination post-browser-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual memory-reading syscalls (process_vm_readv, ReadProcessMemory equivalents) issued by Chrome renderer. Correlate with outbound HTTP/DNS to low-reputation or newly-registered domains within 60 seconds of crash recovery.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Engine Sandbox Breakout Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execute arbitrary code inside the web browser's sandbox.' Sandbox escape followed by child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash) from browser context is a strong indicator of post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or unexpected process spawns with Chrome or V8 engine as direct/indirect parent. Flag particularly: system shells, script interpreters, or credential-access tools spawned from renderer process (audit via parent process token/job object).

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation from Known-Bad Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: '19 Packages Poisoned'—pipeline must detect installations of the 19 malicious package names or suspicious PyPI index sources. This is the initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pip/poetry/uv install commands targeting the 19 identified poisoned package names. Flag installations from non-standard PyPI mirrors or index URLs. Alert on successful imports of confirmed-malicious packages in Python environments.

suggestion.title: Malicious Setup.py or Import Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'auto-run'—implies setup.py execution hooks or __init__.py payload injection triggered on installation/import, not on explicit function call.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect setup.py execution with unusual subprocess calls, network connections, or spawned processes. Monitor for __init__.py files in site-packages being created/modified with suspicious patterns (base64 strings, eval, dynamic imports). Flag Python processes with elevated privilege or unusual parent processes during package installation.

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Spawning from Python Environment with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Bun Credential Stealer'—malware binary needs execution context and target credential files. Detect Bun spawning from pip/setup context with immediate access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or password managers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Bun executable (bun, bun.exe) spawned from Python interpreter, setup.py context, or site-packages directory. Monitor for file reads on ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud, or /var/lib/gems password manager files immediately after Bun execution. Flag credential access from unexpected user context during package installation window.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials from Bun Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Credential Stealer'—implies data exfiltration to attacker C2. Detect outbound connections from Bun processes with credential data (base64-encoded or plaintext tokens).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections initiated by Bun or Python processes during package installation. Flag POST requests with suspicious payloads to non-standard domains. Monitor for DNS queries from installation context. Correlate file-read events (credential access) with immediate network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Encoded Malicious Code in setup.py or Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned PyPI packages hide payloads via base64/gzip encoding, string concatenation, or dynamically downloaded secondary stages to evade static inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect setup.py containing base64-encoded strings, eval(), exec(), __import__() with obfuscated module names. Flag pip install commands piping through base64 -d, gunzip, or other decoders. Alert on setup.py downloading secondary payloads via curl/wget to /tmp or process memory.

suggestion.title: Python Process Spawning Unusual Binaries or Shell Commands
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer capability requires subprocess execution; article context implies setup.py or import hook spawning Bun or shell commands to access credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes (python, python3) spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or Bun with unusual arguments or cwd in site-packages. Flag subprocess.Popen, os.system, or exec() calls with arguments involving /home, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or other credential paths. Alert on parent-child process chains: pip → setup.py → Bun → shell.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated LiteLLM API Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE' — pipeline missed baseline detection for unauthorized access to LiteLLM endpoints prior to RCE trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/GET requests to LiteLLM API endpoints (typical paths: /api/chat, /api/completions, /models) lacking valid API key or authentication headers, especially with model override parameters in body or URL. Alert on 401→successful requests to same endpoint within seconds (auth bypass attempt).

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from LiteLLM Python Worker
suggestion.rationale: RCE in LiteLLM (Python library) necessarily involves process execution; article describes 'chains to unauthenticated RCE' — pipeline must detect command execution spawned from LLM inference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by python.exe or litellm processes (via parent image name) with command lines containing: eval, exec, subprocess.call, os.system, or shell metacharacters. Flag especially if initiated within milliseconds of suspicious HTTP POST to LiteLLM endpoint.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / Model Override in LiteLLM Requests
suggestion.rationale: RCE via LiteLLM likely exploits parameter injection in model routing or prompt templating — article says 'chains to RCE' implying a specific vulnerability. Pipeline should detect suspicious request bodies targeting model selection or system prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LiteLLM API requests containing: 'model_override', 'system_prompt', 'jailbreak', '__import__', 'exec(', or raw Python builtins in the message/prompt fields. Flag requests with base64 or obfuscated payloads in parameters that resolve to code execution attempts.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM API Key or Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation 'in the wild' implies compromise of credentials or tokens; article context suggests threat actors may harvest API keys to maintain access or pivot internally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on exfiltration of LiteLLM config files (litellm_config.json, .env variants), API key files, or stdout containing 'sk-' or 'litellm-key-' tokens. Cross-correlate with unusual outbound HTTPS to non-whitelisted domains from application servers.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command-and-Control via LiteLLM Inference
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved, attacker may use the compromised LiteLLM instance as a C2 relay or for lateral movement; pipeline must detect abnormal LLM request patterns consistent with attacker queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LiteLLM completion/chat requests with abnormal frequency (>100 req/min from single source), requests containing system enumeration keywords (whoami, ifconfig, dir, ps), or encoding indicators (base64, hex, gzip). Correlate with process execution logs and DNS exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: RPC Endpoint Mapper Enumeration and Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states RPC is 'long exploited by threat actors' for lateral movement. Attackers probe RPC endpoints (port 135) before exploitation. No detection for this reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes connecting to RPC endpoint mapper (port 135) on local or remote systems, or tools enumerating RPC interfaces (epmapper queries, RpcStringBindingCompose API, repeated GetMasterBindingHandle calls).

suggestion.title: DCOM Object Instantiation for Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RPC-based lateral movement. DCOM (Distributed Component Object Model) is RPC-based and widely abused for LM without credentials. Phrase: 'core Windows protocol long exploited by threat actors for lateral movement.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious COM object instantiation from non-standard parents: MMC20.Application, Excel.Application, Word.Application, or Scriptlet.TypeLib activation. Monitor for indirect WMI execution (cmd.exe → wmiPrvSE.exe via COM) or CoGetInstanceFromFile with UNC paths.

suggestion.title: Remote LSASS Access and Credential Dumping via RPC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'credential theft' as attack objective. RPC enables remote LSASS dumping, secretsdump attacks, and registry-based credential exfiltration. No credential access detection present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on remote registry queries for SAM/SYSTEM (reg.exe with \\target\\HKLM\\SAM), MiniDump API calls on lsass.exe from non-System parents, or remote WMI process creation targeting credential-bearing processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious RPC Service Control for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies service execution (T1569.002) via RPC. Missing detection for abnormal Remote Service Control Manager (svcctl) calls to lateral movement targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect svcctl.exe or services.exe initiating RPC to unexpected targets, or non-system processes calling OpenSCManagerA/W with remote server parameter. Flag service creation/start on remote systems via RPC (ServiceMain function calls to non-localhost).

suggestion.title: UAC Bypass and Privilege Escalation via RPC/COM Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'privilege escalation' as outcome. RPC-based privilege escalation via COM object elevation (EventViewer COM object, Windows.UI.Composition) or RunAs service abuse is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CreateProcessAsUserA/W called from non-admin network-accessible services, RunAs service instantiation from user-controlled RPC calls, or suspicious COM object elevation patterns (low integrity → high integrity via COM activation).

suggestion.title: Suspicious High-Resolution Timer Measurement via JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes timing measurements as the core attack vector: 'websites track what sites and apps you open via SSD Timing'. Browsers implementing Web Workers and high-resolution clocks are the execution path; detection should flag sustained performance.now() or similar timing queries in script context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag JavaScript contexts (inline or Worker threads) issuing >10 high-resolution timer calls (performance.now(), rdtsc equivalents) within <1 second, especially if interleaved with forced garbage collection or memory allocation patterns. Correlate with background tabs or iframes with no user interaction.

suggestion.title: SSD Access Timing Pattern Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: FROST exploits 'SSD Timing' variations: 'Lets Websites Track What Sites and Apps You Open via SSD Timing'. Legitimate user activity has predictable I/O patterns; malicious timing probes produce artificial, regular access sequences to measure cache/NAND latency deltas.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process or browser subprocess generating >100 storage I/O requests in <5 seconds with microsecond-scale timing precision measurements logged, especially patterns that repeat across file offsets without application semantics (e.g., repeated seeks to same blocks).

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin Timing Inference via Performance API Leakage
suggestion.rationale: Attack enables 'Websites Track What Sites and Apps You Open'—inferring visited apps requires exfiltrating timing deltas cross-origin. Detection target: JavaScript measuring response times to requests to third-party domains (e.g., timing user's cached login tokens vs. first-access latency).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag JavaScript code that compares fetch() or XHR timing for requests to multiple distinct domains in sequence (e.g., facebook.com, slack.com, linkedin.com) within same browsing context, or uses Resource Timing API to extract cross-origin latency deltas. Payload: timing delta variance suggests cache hit (user visited site recently).

suggestion.title: Web Worker Timing Probes Against Local System Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: SSD timing attack requires baseline measurement of victim hardware. Article implies probing 'what sites and apps you open'—prerequisite is fingerprinting SSD vs. HDD, cache hierarchies, CPU clock. Web Workers allow low-level timing without blocking UI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Web Worker spawning followed by repeated allocations of large memory buffers (>50 MB) with microsecond-scale timing measurements. Pattern: allocate→measure latency→free→repeat. Indicates cache-line flush + reload probing to infer cache depth and SSD speed.

suggestion.title: Abnormal IFrame Timing Instrumentation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Websites embedding tracking code use IFrames for isolation. Article describes tracking 'via SSD Timing'—an IFrame must repeatedly measure its own I/O and exfiltrate timing deltas, either via postMessage or indirect side-channels (SVG timing, CSS paint events).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IFrame JavaScript contexts (crossOrigin-blocked from parent) that call performance.timing, performance.measure(), or similar APIs >50 times per minute, or that spawn Worker threads to avoid timing jitter. Secondary signal: timing data exfiltrated via timing-based covert channel (e.g., delayed postMessage or SVG load times).

suggestion.title: Weedhack File Hash Detection - Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: 30 high-fidelity SHA256 hashes provided in indicators section; should be the primary detection lever for this known-malware campaign. Article states active since January 2026, indicating these hashes are current signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or file creation matching any of the 30 SHA256 IOCs associated with Weedhack. Prioritize Minecraft launcher directory (Program Files/Launcher, AppData/Roaming/.minecraft) and parent processes spawning from game directories or mods folders.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Minecraft Launcher Modification or Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploiting their interest in game modifications' and 'hijack accounts.' Mods are loaded by the launcher; detection should flag unsigned or unexpected child processes from launcher, or launcher itself spawning credential-access utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor javaw.exe or launcher.exe spawning unusual child processes (powershell, cmd, certutil, curl, etc.) or accessing Windows credential stores. Alert on .minecraft or mods directory being written to by non-launcher processes.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from Minecraft Launcher or Game Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal credentials' and 'drain cryptocurrency wallets.' Minecraft stores OAuth tokens and wallet metadata locally; detection should flag credential dumping or access to credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing %APPDATA%\.minecraft\launcher_accounts.json, launcher_profiles.json, or wallet-related files with read+delete patterns. Flag LSASS or credential manager access from Minecraft-related child processes.

suggestion.title: Account Hijacking via Unusual Interactive Logon from Game Directory Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijack accounts.' Account takeover implies either credential stuffing, token theft, or brute-force—detection should flag unusual authentication activity from Minecraft launcher context or lateral account access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Minecraft process execution with unusual logon events (failed+success patterns, cross-geo, impossible travel) or SMB/RDP sessions from the same endpoint. Flag rapid repeated authentication failures against cloud gaming services or launcher APIs from the infected host.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain / Compromised Mod Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'distributed via malicious mods' (implied from 'interest in game modifications'). The delivery mechanism is compromised software; detection should flag unauthorized mod repository access or unsigned/untrusted mod installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic from Minecraft processes to known malware-hosting or untrusted mod repository domains. Alert on .jar or .zip file downloads into mods folder from non-official Minecraft launcher sources. Flag installations of mods from GitHub releases or Discord that match Weedhack operator infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Launcher Autostart or Injected Mod Loading
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates ongoing campaign since January 2026, implying persistence mechanism beyond single session. Minecraft mods persist across launcher restarts; detection should flag unauthorized mod folder modifications or launcher registry persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM/HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer or launcher startup registry keys for unauthorized entries. Alert on modifications to %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods\, mods.json, or loader config files after Weedhack hash execution. Track launcher scheduled tasks or Run key persistence.

suggestion.title: LLM Inference Engine Spawning Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'self-replicating AI worm that operates entirely on local, open-weight models'—implying worm code is generated or executed via LLM inference. Detect when Python LLM frameworks spawn unusual child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent is a Python LLM inference script (HuggingFace Transformers, Ollama, vLLM, etc.). Flag child processes with unusual arguments or from unexpected directories. Correlate inference logs with process creation timing to identify model-output-driven execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Model Weight or Adapter File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm could persist by injecting into model weights or LoRA adapters. Article: 'operates entirely on local, open-weight models' suggests direct model artifact manipulation for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement file integrity monitoring on model directories (.cache/huggingface, adapter paths with .safetensors/.ggml/.bin files). Flag unauthorized writes outside scheduled update windows. Cross-reference with inference process ownership to detect injection attacks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LLM Prompt Injection or Code Generation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Worm must generate and execute payloads via the LLM. Detect when model outputs contain executable code. Article implies model 'generates' replication logic—monitor inference I/O for code/shell patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and analyze LLM prompt completions for code-like patterns (bash/PowerShell/Python syntax, subprocess calls). Correlate with immediate process creation or file writes. Flag prompts requesting system commands, credential formats, or prompt injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Cross-Model or Cross-Environment Propagation via Shared Cache
suggestion.rationale: Open-weight models share caches and repositories. Self-replicating worm could spread by copying poisoned models. Article: 'operates entirely on local, open-weight models' implies propagation across multiple local instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual model file copies between inference environments or unauthorized huggingface-cli downloads. Flag model replicas appearing in unexpected directories or accessed from unusual processes. Track model version/hash changes to detect tampering.

suggestion.title: Inference Engine Resource Exhaustion or Anomalous Scheduling
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm spawning many inference calls would consume GPU/CPU. Article describes autonomously operating worm—expect sustained resource spikes and unusual inference task scheduling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inference engine resource utilization for sustained GPU/CPU spikes or unexpected inference API call rates. Flag cases where inference processes spawn many child instances or repeatedly load the same model. Correlate with user activity to identify autonomous worm-like behavior.

suggestion.title: Model Repository or Version Control Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Worm could persist by committing poisoned model versions to local or remote repositories. Article mentions 'open-weight models'—watch for unusual commits or model version changes indicating tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git operations on local model repositories for unauthorized commits or model weight modifications. Flag suspicious huggingface-hub library calls. Baseline expected model version changes and detect deviations; verify commit authorship aligns with expected maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Archive Extraction to Suspicious Temp Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw is exploited to 'deploy stealers'—implies malicious archives are opened by users, triggering extraction. No UC covers anomalous archive handling. Phrase: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited...to Deploy'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR.exe spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) or extracting files to %temp%, %appdata%, or ProgramData. Flag if extraction is followed immediately by execution of dropped binaries.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Process Execution Post-Archive
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'stealers' are deployed; article likely describes credential-theft malware execution. No detection for stealer behavioral patterns. Phrase: 'Deploy Stealers'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or rare executables querying credential storage (DPAPI, SAM hive reads, browser vault access via vaultcli.exe/rundll32.exe keymgr.dll). Alert on process creation from %temp% or user AppData combined with registry access to HKLM\SAM or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Protected Storage.

suggestion.title: WinRAR CVE Exploitation—Suspicious Archive Properties
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific WinRAR vulnerability (likely path-traversal or RCE in archive handling). Should detect archives with path-traversal payloads or suspicious embedded executables. Phrase: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WinRAR processing archives containing files with path-traversal patterns (../, ..\) in entry names, or mixed content (text + executable). Correlate with WinRAR process spawning network communication or child processes immediately after archive open.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from WinRAR-Spawned Process
suggestion.rationale: Stealers exfiltrate data; article implies live C2 infrastructure. No detection for post-exploitation network communication. Phrase: 'Deploy Stealers in Ukraine'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rare or unsigned child processes of WinRAR (or from %temp%) establishing outbound connections to non-common ports (443, 80, 8080, 9999, etc.) with high-entropy hostnames or non-FQDN IP destinations. Correlate with credential-access process execution.

suggestion.title: Ukraine-Targeted Spear-Phishing Archive Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Ukraine targeting; phishing is the likely initial delivery vector for malicious archives. No UC for Ukraine-geo or language-based phishing markers. Phrase: 'in Ukraine'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails to .ua domains or Ukrainian government/critical infrastructure entities with .rar/.zip attachments, especially if sender spoofs Ukrainian entities or uses borrowed legitimate-looking Ukrainian infrastructure. Correlate attachment metadata (creation date, internal paths with Cyrillic) with known Ukraine-targeting campaigns.

suggestion.title: Lookalike AI Brand Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords establish threat actors impersonating AI brands; 'AI brands as bait' implies fake domains/sites but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Microsoft article likely details fake ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registrations and DNS resolutions for subdomains or homoglyphs of AI brand names (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot variants). Flag domains registered recently, lacking SSL history, or resolving to infrastructure absent from AI vendor IP ranges. Correlate with phishing report volume.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Impersonating AI Services
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references social engineering and credential theft via AI brand impersonation; keywords mention 'credential theft' but zero email-based detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails purporting to come from AI vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft AI services) requesting credential revalidation, urgent account verification, or security alerts. Flag messages with high-reputation-spoofing indicators (lookalike sender, missing SPF/DKIM) containing links to suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Capture via Fake AI Login Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords 'Adversary-in-the-Middle' and 'Credential theft' establish credential harvesting; no detection hypothesis provided for fake login flows or HTTP POST events to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user clicks on suspicious AI-branded links with subsequent HTTP POST requests to non-Microsoft/non-OpenAI infrastructure (low-reputation, newly registered IPs). Monitor for browser automation or credential-stuffing tool signatures (Selenium, Puppeteer, curl patterns) accessing fake login pages.

suggestion.title: AiTM Proxy Deployment and Credential Relay
suggestion.rationale: Article keyword explicitly cites 'Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM)' but pipeline generated no detection logic for proxy interception, session tokens, or relay attacks against AI service credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AiTM proxy deployments (Evilginx2, Modlishka signatures) via parent-child process chains (Python/Node.js spawning HTTP proxy libraries) or suspicious network listener binds on common phishing proxy ports (8080, 9090, 8443). Monitor for credential exfiltration to attacker-controlled IPs post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI Tool Binary Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Social-engineering campaigns often distribute trojanized 'AI tools'; article likely discusses malware delivery but pipeline missed detection for suspicious AI-branded executable downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of executables/installers claiming to be AI tools (ChatGPT-installer.exe, Claude-setup.msi) from non-official sources or with mismatched signatures. Monitor for unsigned binaries with AI-brand filenames spawning suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, PowerShell, net.exe, reg.exe).

suggestion.title: Bulk Email with External URLs to Suspicious/Unregistered Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'AI Phishing' campaigns 'crushing SOCs with alert volume'—implies mass email campaigns with phishing links, a primary vector in modern phishing attacks described in the article premise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails sent in bulk from internal or compromised external accounts to multiple recipients, containing hyperlinks to newly registered domains, dynamic DNS, or domains with low reputation history. Correlate sender profile (newly created, dormant account reactivation) with recipients outside trusted distribution lists.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Authentication Followed by Success from Anomalous Location
suggestion.rationale: Article describes phishing campaigns likely harvesting credentials; pattern of failed logins (user entering wrong password on phishing form) followed by successful login from foreign IP/geolocation is canonical post-phishing compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify user accounts with 3+ failed authentication attempts within 5 minutes (phishing form entry errors), followed by successful login within 30 minutes from IP in different country/ASN than historical baseline. Escalate if followed by sensitive resource access (email forwarding, mailbox rules, OneDrive sync).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Forwarding Rules or Delegation Created Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Business Email Compromise aftermath of credential harvesting via phishing; attackers immediately create forwarding rules to maintain persistence and data exfiltration channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of email forwarding rules, inbox rules with external recipients, or delegate mailbox access within 1 hour of successful authentication from new location. Flag if rule routes sensitive keywords (invoice, payment, urgent, wire transfer) or applies to all incoming mail.

suggestion.title: Attachment Execution from Recently Opened Email Link
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing discussed in article likely includes attachment delivery or multi-stage downloads; need detection linking email click to subsequent file execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user click on external URL (captured in email gateway logs) with subsequent file creation/execution within 5 minutes in %TEMP% or %AppData%, especially macro-enabled Office documents, .exe, .scr, or script interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe with unusual arguments).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Sending Rate from User Account Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised account via phishing may be used to relay further phishing campaigns or spam; volume spike detection is standard SOC response to 'crushing alert volume' mentioned in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound email volume spike >5x user's 30-day daily average within a 1-hour window. Correlate with email template similarity (repeated subject/body), external-only recipients, or presence of URL shorteners and suspicious attachment types.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass or Disable Event Following Phishing Alert
suggestion.rationale: Advanced phishing campaigns often include MFA prompt injection or social engineering to disable MFA; article's 'AI Phishing' theme suggests sophisticated tactics beyond simple credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MFA disable requests, MFA method deletions, or repeated MFA denials followed by successful authentication from the same session. Investigate if preceded by phishing email or suspicious portal login attempt.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated IKEv1 VPN Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs, or Spark firewalls'—core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IKEv1 key exchange initiation from external sources without corresponding successful authentication. Flag connections where authentication is bypassed or skipped entirely in IKEv1 protocol negotiation.

suggestion.title: Deprecated Remote Access Client Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'security gateways that accept legacy Remote Access clients' as attack surface. Deprecated clients represent unpatched attack vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify and block connections from legacy/deprecated remote access client versions. Monitor for client version strings associated with unsupported software.

suggestion.title: Machine Certificate Validation Bypass on IKEv1
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacks target deployments 'do not require a machine certificate for connections'—certificate validation is disabled, enabling auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IKEv1 connections where machine certificate validation is skipped or fails. Detect policy changes disabling certificate requirements for remote access.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Ransomware Execution Following VPN Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate'—ransomware deployment occurs after initial VPN access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN authentication events with subsequent ransomware execution patterns (file encryption activity, ransom note creation, encryption binary execution). Detect behavioral markers of Qilin payload activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement and Data Collection Post-VPN Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Qilin's confirmed post-compromise activity following VPN breach, implying reconnaissance and data staging before encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SMB/RDP traffic originating from compromised VPN session to internal assets. Flag high-volume data access to file shares, mass enumeration of network shares, and lateral tool deployment.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-42271 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Detects unpatched LiteLLM instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any host with vulnerability scanner evidence of CVE-2026-42271 (CVE ID match in Qualys, Nessus, Tenable, or built-in patch-scan logs). Prioritize results with install date before 2026-06-22 (federal deadline) and externally accessible network exposure.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Authenticated Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands on the host.' Detects post-authentication exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On hosts running LiteLLM: detect process creation or command execution immediately following (within seconds) successful authentication to the LiteLLM service. Look for process parents that are unusual for a web API service, or command payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, backticks) in requests logged by LiteLLM.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege User Key Abuse for Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privilege internal-user keys' can trigger the vulnerability. Detects misuse of standard API credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a service account or low-privilege API key used by LiteLLM authentication logs unusual command execution (shell invocations, code compilation, network utilities) within 60 seconds of that key being used. Baseline normal LiteLLM operations first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from LiteLLM Host
suggestion.rationale: Article: arbitrary commands can be executed on 'the host.' If LiteLLM is compromised, lateral movement is the next phase. Detects attacker pivoting from exploited LiteLLM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected network connections or lateral movement (RDP, SSH, WMI, PsExec) originating from a host where LiteLLM is installed and a CVE-2026-42271 exploitation has been observed. Cross-correlate process creation on the LiteLLM host with remote access events.

suggestion.title: Check Point CVE-2026-50751 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' as canonical approach and references template substitution. Pipeline generated no use cases at all despite clear directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Check Point Security Gateway instances (product version Check_Point_Security_Gateway_*) exposed to internet with inbound IKEv1 (UDP 500) or IPSec (UDP 4500). Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-50751; flag unpatched or unapplied updates as of federal due date 2026-06-11.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass — VPN Connection Post-Failed Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'bypass user authentication and establish VPN connection without valid user password.' This auth-to-access pattern is directly detectable in gateway logs but pipeline generated no credential-access or lateral-movement use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IKEv1 key-exchange initiations (Phase 1) followed by SA establishment without corresponding successful authentication log entry. Flag sessions where VPN tunnel establishes despite null or invalid credential submission to auth backend.

suggestion.title: Repeated IKEv1 Key Exchange Anomalies from Unauthenticated Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote attacker' exploiting 'IKEv1 key exchange.' Pipeline missed protocol-level exploitation pattern—high-volume or repeated IKEv1 Phase 1 + Phase 2 completions from single source without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Count IKEv1 Phase 1 exchanges per source IP across 15-minute windows. Alert if single source completes Phase 1 → Phase 2 → SA establishment (indicating successful bypass) OR if >5 Phase 1 attempts detected (exploitation attempt fingerprint).

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Remote VPN Access Without MFA
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass of 'user authentication' for 'remote access VPN.' Vulnerable systems will allow VPN tunnel without secondary authentication factors. Detection should flag successful VPN sessions lacking MFA audit trail against baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify VPN tunnel establishments (successful SA negotiation in gateway logs) where corresponding MFA challenge/success is absent in MFA system logs or shows >5 minute gap. Compare against baseline of MFA-gated sessions.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Authentication Bypass via URI Normalization
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version of the same URI. By crafting requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization, attackers can bypass authentication.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with path encoding anomalies (double-encoding, case variation, directory traversal sequences) targeting '/api/auth/validate-sso/' that normalize to protected routes. Flag discrepancies between raw and normalized URI interpretation.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Unauthenticated Command Injection via Package Update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands.' Detection guidance: 'monitor requests to 'ucs/update/latest_package.''
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to 'ucs/update/latest_package' endpoint containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, ||, $, backticks, command substitution) in parameters. Alert on requests from sources that have not authenticated or do not have legitimate update roles.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Privilege Escalation via Service Account Sudo
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries, making escalation to root trivial.' Detection guidance: 'monitor...unexpected sudo commands.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo command execution spawned by ucs-update service or its children. Alert on any sudo invocation without a preceding authenticated user session, from non-interactive contexts, or with arguments to binaries not normally used in legitimate updates.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Suspicious Child Process Execution from ucs-update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'monitor...suspicious child processes under 'ucs-update.'' Successful exploitation triggers shell or command execution as a child of the legitimate ucs-update process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate child processes spawned by ucs-update (typically package-management binaries). Alert on unexpected child processes: interactive shells (bash, sh, dash), script interpreters (python, perl, ruby), or processes with shell metacharacters in command line.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Unauthenticated Access to Auth Validation Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'defenders can also look for requests containing '/api/auth/validate-sso/' and monitor requests to 'ucs/update/latest_package,'' which are the infection vectors for the unauthenticated RCE chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to '/api/auth/validate-sso/' from external or untrusted networks, particularly with path manipulation indicators or from hosts that have not completed a legitimate authentication flow. Baseline normal SSO validation patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet phar:/// three-slash wrapper bypass in HTTP request
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability as triggered by input form 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' with three or more slashes. This is the core exploitation vector: 'When the input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner with three or more slashes after the scheme...'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests containing phar:// followed by three or more consecutive slashes. The patch-bypass specifically exploits parse_url() behavior when the wrapper path is malformed with excessive slashes. Monitor both literal (phar:///) and URL-encoded variants (phar%3A%2F%2F%2F).

suggestion.title: Web-server process spawning shell or network tool child process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE capability through phar exploitation. Post-exploitation would manifest as web server processes (php-fpm, apache, nginx) spawning shells, scripting interpreters, or network utilities: 'Command and Scripting Interpreter (T1059), Unix Shell (T1059.004), PowerShell (T1059.001).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate on parent process name in (php-fpm, php, apache2, httpd, nginx, w3wp) spawning child processes in (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget). Exclude known administrative processes and expected cron/backup utilities.

suggestion.title: Phar archive file creation or modification initiated by web-server process
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability involves phar archive handling; successful exploitation should leave adversary-controlled phar files on disk. Technique references include T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer) and T1505.003 (Web Shell).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification where initiating process matches web-server names and filename matches *.phar extension or contains 'phar' in path. Cross-check file ownership and permissions for anomalies relative to baseline.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory detection: PHPSpreadsheet version vulnerable to CVE-2026-45034 or CVE-2026-34084
suggestion.rationale: Article references asset exposure detection. Inventory-based hunts should flag hosts running affected PHPSpreadsheet builds, especially those exposed via public-facing web applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset and vulnerability management systems for installed PHPSpreadsheet versions matching affected ranges for CVE-2026-45034 or CVE-2026-34084. Correlate against web application assets and internet-facing indicators to prioritize exposure.

suggestion.title: Browser spawning osascript with remote URL context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is in 'chrome_tabs plugin' interpolating unescaped URL into AppleScript, and lists T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File). The initial access is URL-driven; should detect browser processes launching osascript immediately after network activity to suspicious domains or with URL-derived arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Chrome, Brave, Edge, or Safari spawning osascript. Flag if parent is browser plugin path, or if ProcessCommandLine contains AppleScript keywords within seconds of the parent process making outbound network connections. Suspicious pattern: URL fetched → osascript invoked with shell-metacharacter payloads.

suggestion.title: AppleScript 'do shell script' invocation from Chrome-based plugins
