suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit and inventory all Remote Access VPN, Mobile Access, and Spark firewall deployments accepting IKEv1 negotiation. Alert on any new IKEv1-enabled tunnels post-patch release and prioritize for immediate IKEv2 migration or legacy client blocking.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN-Breach Ransomware Deployment (Qilin)
suggestion.rationale: Article directly links initial breach to ransomware: 'confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate'. VPN compromise enables lateral movement and data encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24–72 hours of anomalous VPN authentication or session events, monitor for file encryption patterns, ransom note creation, mass file access from VPN-connected endpoints to internal shares, and command-and-control domains associated with Qilin.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Middle Vulnerability on Site-to-Site VPN (CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies second vulnerability: 'CVE-2026-50752...affects certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections'.
log_sources: network packet captures of key exchange
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site VPN tunnels using IKEv1 for certificate validation failures or peer-identity mismatches. Alert on IPSec Phase-2 negotiations where presented certificates deviate from expected gateway fingerprints or trusted CA chains.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and threat profile states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'. Detecting publicly accessible LiteLLM instances is the first step to exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for CVE-2026-42271 vulnerable LiteLLM instances exposed on internet-facing ports (typically 8000, 4000, or custom API ports). Correlate vulnerability scanner results with network exposure data; flag instances accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor for version strings matching vulnerable LiteLLM releases in HTTP response headers and API documentation endpoints.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'command injection vulnerability that could allow any authenticated user...to run arbitrary commands on the host'. This is the exploitation phase and must be detectable via API request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to LiteLLM API endpoints (proxy logs, WAF logs) for shell metacharacters and command injection payloads in request bodies (backticks, $(), |, &, ;, >, <, pipe chains). Correlate with successful responses followed immediately by unexpected process spawning on the backend host. Flag requests from low-privilege API keys triggering host-level commands.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Key Used for Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands'. Abnormal command execution by low-privilege credential is a privilege-escalation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of command types and privileges associated with each LiteLLM API key tier. Alert when low-privilege keys issue commands outside their typical scope (e.g., system administration, package installation, credential access). Correlate API key identity with subsequent process creation events on the host using contextual linking (request ID, session ID, or timing proximity).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Host Activity via LiteLLM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'run arbitrary commands on the host'—successful exploitation will spawn unexpected processes. Host-level detection post-compromise is critical given this is KEV (active exploitation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from LiteLLM service parent processes (litellm, python litellm runtime, node litellm if applicable). Flag child processes with high entropy command lines, network connectivity attempts, credential scraping (grep /etc/passwd, cat .ssh), or reverse shells. Correlate temporal proximity to LiteLLM API requests with unusual payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article stresses: 'patch lag is the silent killer' and includes federal due-date 2026-06-22. Compliance-driven detection for unpatched instances is mandatory for regulated environments and aligns with CISA KEV intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for LiteLLM versions < patched build. Flag instances where patch is overdue relative to 2026-06-22 federal deadline. Prioritize systems exposed to internet or hosting sensitive data. Automate remediation workflow or escalate to change management if patching is delayed beyond acceptable grace period.

suggestion.title: Check Point IKEv1 Exploit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange' as the attack surface. Must detect anomalous IKEv1 protocol exchanges or malformed key material consistent with CVE-2026-50751 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IKEv1 MAIN or AGGRESSIVE mode exchanges on Check Point gateways that deviate from RFC 2409 protocol flow (missing authentication payloads, truncated exchanges, reuse of nonces). Flag when IKE SA establishment completes without successful IPsec phase-2 credentials.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Must detect successful tunnel establishment without credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN authentication logs and tunnel state transitions. Alert when a session reaches authenticated/connected state without a corresponding successful authentication event in auth logs, or when connection time-to-auth is below normal baseline.

suggestion.title: Exposed Check Point Security Gateway Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation of exposed instances. Article states CVE is 'currently being exploited in the wild'—attackers must first locate vulnerable gateways. Asset discovery is the prerequisite phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vuln scanner data for Check Point Security Gateway instances (by banner or product ID) reachable on UDP 500 or VPN management ports. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify systems older than CVE-2026-50751 release date (2026-06-08). Flag any gaps between discovery date and remediation date vs. federal due date 2026-06-11.

suggestion.title: Failed VPN Authentication Spike from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article references attacker bypassing authentication 'without a valid user password.' On systems where exploit fails or is rejected, this manifests as failed auth spikes preceding or concurrent with exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-source-IP baseline for failed VPN authentication attempts. Alert on sudden 5x+ spike or >10 failures in 5 minutes, especially from external/unknown IPs. Correlate with successful connections from same source immediately after failure burst to identify exploitation success.

suggestion.title: URI normalization bypass to protected endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'By crafting requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization, attackers can bypass authentication.' This is the core bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to `/api/auth/validate-sso/` that contain URI obfuscation techniques (double-encoded slashes, path traversal sequences, case variations) followed by access to normally protected endpoints without prior authentication events. Flag requests that normalize differently in the auth component vs. routing layer.

suggestion.title: Command injection via unauthenticated package-update endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands on the system.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/PUT requests to `ucs/update/latest_package` containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks, command substitution) or command keywords. Correlate with unexpected child processes spawned under the ucs-update service.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via passwordless sudo from service account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'The injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries, making escalation to root trivial.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo command execution from the UniFi service account outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on any sudo invocation targeting sensitive binaries (bash, sh, cat, chmod) or system utilities that could enable persistence or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Suspicious child process spawning from ucs-update
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends: 'monitor requests to... suspicious child processes under 'ucs-update.'` Baseline normal children and flag anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected child processes spawned by the ucs-update service. Alert on anomalies, especially network tools (curl, wget, nc, bash), unknown binaries, or processes that themselves spawn additional children.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to protected endpoints with no auth trail
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'The chain reaches root with no credentials and no user interaction, so there is no failed-login trail to look for.' Absence of auth events prior to protected endpoint access is itself anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate HTTP 200/success responses on protected API endpoints against authentication logs. Flag successful requests to protected endpoints that have no preceding authentication event in the session or from the source IP within the previous 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Multiple malformed auth-bypass requests within short window
suggestion.rationale: While Bishop Fox released a safe detection script, actual exploitation attempts will involve repeated requests with URI normalization tricks. Article notes researchers 'did not share the full details or a working proof of concept' but defenders can detect the pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of requests from the same source to `/api/auth/validate-sso/` variations or `ucs/update/latest_package` within 60 seconds using unusual URI patterns (encoded characters, multiple slashes, path traversal attempts). Five or more such requests in 60 seconds warrants escalation.

suggestion.title: PHP stream-wrapper bypass via parse_url() integer-length check evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article core detail: 'parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_SCHEME)... is_string($scheme) && strlen($scheme) > 1' is bypassed when input is 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' (3+ slashes). Detection should target the specific bypass pattern. Article: 'When the input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner with three or more slashes after the scheme'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP request parameters containing stream-wrapper URIs with 3+ consecutive forward slashes immediately after the scheme name (phar:///, php:///, data:///, expect:///). Correlate requests to PHP-based web applications with subsequent web-process shell spawning or unexpected file reads.

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet load() called with untrusted file-path parameter containing wrapper
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector requires PHPSpreadsheet's file-loading method to receive attacker-controlled input. Should detect when PHPSpreadsheet processes files via wrapper schemes instead of direct filesystem paths. Article: 'CVE-2026-34084 was patched by the helper File::prohibitWrappers'—this implies load() accepts file paths and lacks input validation pre-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If PHPSpreadsheet is instrumented or logged: flag any File::load() or Spreadsheet->load() call with argument containing phar://, php://, data://, expect://, or other stream-wrapper schemes. Correlate with HTTP parameters to identify external input flow into load().

suggestion.title: Phar archive extraction or code execution within PHP process
suggestion.rationale: Once phar:// bypass succeeds, attacker loads a malicious phar archive. Detection should capture phar mounting, extraction, or execution within PHP/web-server context. Article: 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' syntax suggests archive interior access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process opening/reading .phar files followed immediately by execution of child processes or network connections. Or detect file creation within /tmp/ or cache directories with non-standard ownership immediately after phar:// access.

suggestion.title: Chained: HTTP request with wrapper + web-process shell spawning (exploit evidence)
suggestion.rationale: Full kill-chain: HTTP request with phar:/// → PHP parse_url bypass → RCE → child shell execution. Requires correlation of web logs + process logs. Article implies this is the attack flow but pipeline generated no correlation rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Web datamodel requests containing phar:/// or related wrappers with Endpoint.Processes showing shell (bash/sh/powershell) or wget/curl spawned by php/apache/nginx within 2 seconds of request. High-confidence RCE signal if correlation is strict.

suggestion.title: Expect:// or data:// wrapper usage attempt (alternative bypass vectors)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists expect:// and data:// in the same class of wrappers filtered by the patched check. If phar:/// bypass is successful, attacker may also test other wrappers. Should hunt all variants. Article: 'reject stream wrappers such as phar://, php://, data:// or expect://'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for expect://, data://, or php:// scheme usage in HTTP request parameters to PHP endpoints. Treat as lower-confidence variant of phar:/// but still suspicious in production. Correlate with application errors or exceptions.

suggestion.title: osascript invoked with nested mismatched tell blocks + do shell script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'AppleScript breakout pattern' where attacker injects code into osascript causing mismatched tell-block structure that triggers shell escape. Article states vulnerability allows 'Code Injection via Unescaped URL' → osascript execution. Example SPL in article hunts for `tell application` appearing 2+ times in single command, which is the canonical injection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Malicious actor crafts URL containing AppleScript payload with nested tell blocks. Plugin renders URL unescaped into osascript command. Detection: osascript process spawned with ProcessCommandLine containing multiple `tell application` directives (≥2 opens) plus `do shell script`, indicating escape from script context into shell.

suggestion.title: Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari plugin parameter injection — seturl.js activity
suggestion.rationale: Article names `seturl.js` as the vulnerable file in recommended hunts section. No pipeline extraction of this filename IOC. seturl.js likely the URL handler responsible for interpolating unescaped input into AppleScript context. Should hunt for seturl.js process spawn or file modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect seturl.js spawning osascript with suspicious arguments, or file creation/modification of seturl.js outside expected plugin directories. Attacker may inject polyglot URL payloads through browser plugin manager or crafted links.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin loaded with remote code execution intent — process lineage
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in 'chrome_tabs plugin (and equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari variants)' within Anyquery extension. Root cause is plugin URL handler not escaping input. Should correlate plugin load events with subsequent osascript execution under same user session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process chain: browser (Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari) → Anyquery plugin context → osascript with injection payload. May appear as browser parent spawning intermediate process (plugin engine) then osascript. User interaction required (clicking link) but attack is one-click.

suggestion.title: JXA script injection — OSAKit/JavaScript bridge with shell escape
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection'. CVE affects both AppleScript AND JavaScript for Automation (JXA). JXA variant would use `Application('System Events').execute('shell command')` or ObjC bridge to escape sandbox. Pipeline missed the JXA dimension entirely despite it being in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: JXA injection payloads use `new ($.NSTask)()` or Application('System Events') to spawn shell. Detect osascript with language=JXA (-l JavaScript) combined with shell-escape patterns ($.NSTask, new ObjC proxies, system process invocation).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47252 asset inventory — Anyquery 0.4.4 installed
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected version 0.4.4 (commit 0abd460) of julien040/anyquery repository. Pipeline output shows zero IOCs including zero version/product identifiers. Asset exposure hunt should enumerate any macOS endpoints with Anyquery 0.4.4 or earlier installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset hunt: find macOS endpoints with Anyquery plugin installed (check ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Extensions or equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari paths). Cross-reference version against 0.4.4 threshold. Flag for urgent patching or plugin disablement.

suggestion.title: Gogs Account Creation on Internet-Facing Instance with Default Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account' and 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false).' External account registration on unpatched Gogs is the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new user registrations on internet-exposed Gogs instances (ports 3000, 3001 typical) when configuration DISABLE_REGISTRATION is false. Alert on rapid sequential registrations or registration from non-organizational ASNs.

suggestion.title: Repository Creation with Rebase Merge Enabled by Low-Privilege User
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' and 'the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction.' Pre-enabled rebase merge on new repos by non-owners is prerequisite for RCE chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repository creation events where rebase-before-merge is enabled in settings by non-admin users, especially within minutes of account creation. Correlate with subsequent commit/merge activities.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Patterns in Gogs Merge Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'argument injection vulnerability' affecting 'Merge() code path' and notes parallel to CVE-2024-39933, CVE-2024-39932, etc. RCE achieved through malformed arguments to git merge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by Gogs (gitea/gogs service account) during merge operations. Alert on git/shell processes with suspicious command-line patterns: unclosed quotes, shell metacharacters (|;`$), command substitution, or flags absent in benign rebase/merge workflows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Repository Access by Recently Created Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'read any repository (including private repos)' is direct impact. Post-RCE, initial exploit account accesses private repos it has no permissions for.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when user accounts access/clone private repositories not in their explicit permission list. Flag rapid sequential private repo access by accounts created in last 24h. Cross-reference Gogs permission matrix against access logs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Push to Repository by Non-Owner
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'alter any hosted source code' is stated impact. Commits by unprivileged accounts to repositories they do not own/maintain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect push/commit events where committer lacks write permissions on target repo per Gogs ACL. Alert on code changes to critical/production repositories (if registered). Flag commits from recently created accounts to any repo.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Lateral Movement Network Activity from Gogs Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'move laterally to other systems on the network' after compromise. Outbound connections from Gogs process to internal systems indicate post-exploitation reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by Gogs service process to internal IP space, especially to SSH (22), RDP (3389), SMB (445), or LDAP (389). Alert on unexpected DNS queries from Gogs process. Flag new child process spawns from Gogs service account with network capabilities.

suggestion.title: NSO-Attributed WhatsApp Phishing URL Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack'—pipeline produced zero IOCs or detections. Should detect spearphishing URLs delivered via WhatsApp targeting credential harvesting or malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious URLs shared via WhatsApp messages that redirect to credential-capture pages or fake Meta/WhatsApp login panels. Correlate against threat-intel feeds for NSO-attributed infrastructure. Monitor for link shortener abuse (bit.ly, tinyurl) masking final destination.

suggestion.title: Meta Enforcement Action Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Meta Blocks NSO Group' and 'Files Contempt Order'—indicates Meta published blocklists or IOCs. Pipeline should ingest published Meta security advisories for phishing URLs/domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Meta's published IOC feeds (if public) or Meta Security blog posts. Track domains/IPs listed in court filings. Flag any internal user access attempts to Meta-blocked phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake WhatsApp Login
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attack against WhatsApp users implies fake login pages. Pipeline missed behavioral detection for credential-capture traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests containing credential fields (password, 2FA code, session token) to non-WhatsApp/non-Meta domains. Correlate user-agents claiming WhatsApp mobile client. Flag repeated failed login attempts followed by successful logins from new geolocations.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Infrastructure Reuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group (Pegasus operator) has known C2 infrastructure. Article implies new campaign but pipeline missed actor attribution linkage—should cross-reference against historical NSO IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference any extracted IOCs against VirusTotal/AlienVault/OSINT NSO Pegasus infrastructure databases. Flag domains sharing ASN, SSL cert issuer, or DNS registrar patterns with prior NSO campaigns.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Post-Phishing Success
suggestion.rationale: Successful phishing of WhatsApp/Meta users enables account compromise. Pipeline missed post-compromise detection despite 'attack' phrasing implying exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logins to Meta/WhatsApp accounts from IPs/geolocations inconsistent with user baseline (VPN, proxy indicators). Flag bulk contact list exports, message archive downloads, or session token harvesting post-phishing window.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Client Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: NSO Pegasus historically exploits WhatsApp for device compromise (0-day calls, media processing). Pipeline should hunt for exploitation indicators beyond phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process spawning from WhatsApp application context (whasapp.exe, WhatsApp child processes). Flag unexpected kernel driver loads, memory mapping, or unsigned system modifications coinciding with WhatsApp media received events.

suggestion.title: Python package with executable .pth startup hook
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malicious artifacts included a "*-setup.pth" file' and 'a compromised wheel can turn an otherwise passive dependency install into a delayed execution trigger.' This is the initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python packages containing executable .pth files, especially setup.pth or *-setup.pth patterns in site-packages. Correlate with subsequent process creation events when Python interpreter starts, as .pth file execution is implicit during import/startup.

suggestion.title: Python launching Bun JavaScript runtime to execute _index.js
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script' and 'Python launches Bun to execute _index.js.' This is the delayed execution trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation chains where python.exe/python3 spawns bun or similar JavaScript runtime processes. Flag unexpected downloads of Bun from GitHub URLs (github.com/oven-sh/bun). Monitor for _index.js process arguments or child processes.

suggestion.title: Enumeration and harvesting of developer credential files
suggestion.rationale: Article lists targeted files: '.env, .npmrc, .pypirc' and 'GitHub tokens...SSH keys Docker credentials...Shell histories Claude/MCP configuration files.' This is a clear credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process activity that enumerates or reads .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, .ssh directories, Docker config files, and shell history. Flag reads of SSH keys, API credential files, or cloud configuration files in bulk or unusual contexts (e.g., from Python child processes).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to masqueraded Anthropic API endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'direct HTTPS...pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage.' False Anthropic endpoint is attacker-controlled C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS connections to api.anthropic.com with /v1/api or similar paths when origin is not known Anthropic client software or legitimate API callers. Cross-reference with known legitimate Anthropic IP/domain infrastructure. Flag POST requests with JSON payloads containing credential-like strings.

suggestion.title: Persistence via systemd service or macOS LaunchAgent creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of systemd service files in /etc/systemd/system or ~/.config/systemd/user with unusual ExecStart containing Python, Bun, or script references. On macOS, alert on new LaunchAgent plists in ~/Library/LaunchAgents with similar payloads. Also track unexpected modifications to ~/.github/workflows or ~/.config/claude/ directories.

suggestion.title: Shai-Hulud campaign: PyPI/supply-chain package trojanization
suggestion.rationale: Article attribution: 'Socket is tracking it alongside previous attacks, with the list of malicious artifacts attributed to Shai-Hulud activities now showing 453 items.' Campaign name and scope should trigger threat-hunting and YARA rules across artifact repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate installed PyPI packages against public Shai-Hulud indicators-of-compromise list (maintained by Socket and CISA). Monitor for installation of bioinformatics/scientific packages with anomalous build metadata, missing/modified source, or mismatched hashes. Maintain inventory of all Python packages in use and validate against known-good checksums.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Distribution via GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file.' Repository created April 10, 2026 with 56 unique APKs. Directly actionable indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Mobile devices downloading .apk files from github.com URLs rather than official app stores (Google Play). Correlate with process execution by package installers and establish C2 connection patterns. Monitor GitHub for repositories with banking-app-impersonating APKs.

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Impersonating Banking Institution with Malware Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials.' Campaigns target Italian banks (Intesa, Sella, Nexi, Fideuram, Mooney) and Spanish banks (CaixaBank) starting May 14, 2026.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Domains with lookalike/typosquat names of targeted European banking institutions. Monitor for credential harvesting pages followed by redirect chains to external APK hosts (particularly GitHub). Look for certificate mismatches or newly registered domains in banking verticals.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NFC Card Data Acquisition by Non-Banking Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware reads the information using Android's IsoDep interface and EMV commands' to steal 'card number, type, expiry date, and a 4-digit PIN entered by the victim.' This behavior is unique to legitimate payment terminals; mobile apps performing this are highly anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Applications not in official banking whitelist requesting NFC permissions or calling IsoDep/EMV command sequences. Alert on apps prompting users to 'place card near device' outside of legitimate banking workflows. Flag PIN entry within 60 seconds of NFC read event.

suggestion.title: Malformed APK Packaging for Static Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malformed APK packaging to hinder automated analysis' and 'poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP, causing some extraction tools to wrongly interpret internal relative paths as filesystem paths and trigger errors.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: APK files with malformed ZIP structures, path traversal sequences in manifest entries (e.g., '../../../'), or inconsistent offset/size metadata that break standard extraction tools but remain installable on Android devices. These evade sandbox and SIEM automation.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Exfiltration of Payment Card Data to Attacker C2
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' Payment card data (PAN, expiry, PIN) is the exfil payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) from apps not in banking whitelist, especially apps masquerading as banking apps. Monitor WebSocket frame content for patterns matching credit card numbers (16-digit sequences), expiry dates (MM/YY), and 4-digit PINs. Correlate with preceding NFC activity.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Banking App Update Prompt Redirecting to Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file.' Legitimate banking app updates are delivered via official app stores; external redirects are social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Phishing notifications (email, SMS, fake browser popups, in-app messages) prompting app updates with redirects to non-official distribution sources (GitHub, personal domains, suspicious hosts). Correlate notification origins with redirect destinations and final download locations.

suggestion.title: AI Brand Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering.' Core attack: emails impersonating ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or other AI brands to harvest credentials. Pipeline generated zero phishing UCs despite this being the primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with spoofed AI vendor display names (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft Copilot) combined with urgency language, verification requests, or account-security pretexts. Flag sender domains that typosquat legitimate AI vendor domains.

suggestion.title: AiTM Proxy Detection via Credential Relay
suggestion.rationale: Schema explicitly mentions 'Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM)' attacks; pipeline produced no detection for this technique. AiTM proxies intercept and relay credentials in real-time, bypassing MFA. This is the operational core of modern phishing-kit infrastructure and entirely unaddressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MFA challenges (conditional-access step-up auth) where tokens are validated but the subsequent authentication originates from a different IP/country/user-agent within seconds. This indicates real-time credential interception.

suggestion.title: Fake AI Service Credential Capture Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via AI brand bait requires attacker-hosted login pages or account-verification forms. Article discusses credential theft; no UC covers detection of phishing infrastructure (typosquat domains, SSL cert anomalies, page fingerprints).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains impersonating AI vendors (openai.com variants, anthropic.com homoglyphs, look-alike registrations). Flag newly-registered domains WHOIS-correlated with known phishing registrars. Cross-correlate with mail flow for mass phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Schema signals 'Credential theft'; AiTM attacks are worthless without defeating MFA. Article context implies modern phishing kit deployments, yet no UC for detecting MFA token relay or real-time authentication relay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MFA validation events followed by successful sign-in from geographically impossible locations or different user agents within 30 seconds. Alert on step-up auth (conditional access) triggered during unusual network conditions then immediately satisfied.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise AI Account Abuse and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials are stolen, threat actors access legitimate AI services (ChatGPT accounts, Copilot instances) for lateral privilege escalation or to exfiltrate sensitive data uploaded to chat histories. No UC addresses post-breach AI service abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous usage of cloud AI services: bulk uploads to ChatGPT/Copilot, unusual API token usage, API calls from unfamiliar geolocations, or mass retrieval of conversation histories. Correlate with known-compromised email accounts and malware beacon timestamps.

suggestion.title: Malicious Browser Extension Deployment via AI Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering with AI brand bait can extend to malicious browser extensions ('AI assistant helper'). Article covers execution mechanisms implicitly (how credentials lead to code execution) but pipeline generated no detection for extension-based persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser extension installation directories for unexpected extensions with AI-themed names. Flag extensions installed from non-official Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons URLs. Correlate suspicious extension presence with phishing campaign timeframes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 VPN Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be exploited by unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs, or Spark firewalls.' This is the primary attack vector and requires alerting on exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point VPN logs for unauthenticated session establishment attempts, failed authentication sequences followed by successful access, or IKEv1 session creation without valid credentials. Correlate with anomalous source IPs or geography for Qilin-attributed infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Legacy IKEv1 Protocol Usage on VPN Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'only deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' are vulnerable. Detecting active IKEv1 usage identifies at-risk systems that should be migrated to IKEv2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN gateway configurations advertising or accepting IKEv1 key exchange. Track IKEv1 session establishments over time—spikes may indicate active exploitation, especially if paired with unauthenticated or machine-certificate-absent connections.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Lateral Movement and Ransomware Preparation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate,' indicating actor pivots internally after VPN breach. Need detection for lateral movement and ransomware staging indicators following VPN access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal post-VPN activity, then alert on anomalies: process discovery tools (tasklist, Get-Process), network reconnaissance (nslookup, net view), lateral movement utilities (PsExec, WMI calls), and file enumeration from accounts or hosts with fresh VPN session origin. Tune for Qilin's known staging patterns.

suggestion.title: Certificate Validation Failures in Site-to-Site VPN (CVE-2026-50752 MITM)
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses second vulnerability affecting 'certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange' enabling MITM attacks. Although not yet exploited in wild, requires detection for site-to-site VPN integrity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for certificate validation errors, certificate subject mismatches, or self-signed certificates accepted on site-to-site VPN tunnels using IKEv1. Alert on unexpected certificate issuer changes or pinning violations on production VPN links.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Configuration Changes (Legacy Client Removal)
suggestion.rationale: Check Point recommends 'remove support for the legacy remote access client, configure global properties for Remote Access VPN Authentication to IKEv2 only.' Detect rollback or non-compliant configuration that re-enables vulnerable settings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration changes that re-enable legacy Remote Access client support, downgrade IKEv2-only enforcement, or disable Machine Certificate Authentication on VPN gateways. Correlate changes with unauthorized admin logins or API calls.

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Post-Breach Indicators (Victim Profiling & TTPs)
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms Qilin involvement in at least one CVE-2026-50751 incident and lists victim profile (Yangfeng, Nissan, Asahi, Lee Enterprises, Synnovis, Court Services Victoria). Use known Qilin staging and encryption behaviors post-VPN compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-VPN compromise, monitor for Qilin's known reconnaissance tools, batch file deployment for encryption staging, and command-line patterns matching documented Qilin playbook. Alert on bulk file encryption, registry modifications for persistence, or data exfiltration to known Qilin C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: BerriAI LiteLLM Internet-Facing Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry...observed exploited in the wild,' implying attackers are finding and targeting exposed LiteLLM instances. This detection hunt is the canonical first line of defense per article's own guidance: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound traffic to ports commonly used by LiteLLM (HTTP/HTTPS), combined with vulnerability scanner results confirming CVE-2026-42271 is not patched. Flag any instance reachable from untrusted networks (WAN, VPN without MFA).

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly: Low-Privilege API Key Abuse Against LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands.' Detection should flag when low-privilege keys (e.g., read-only, limited-scope API tokens) attempt operations that require elevated capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM API logs for requests from low-privilege credentials attempting command execution, system calls, or operations outside their declared scope. Correlate API key metadata (privilege level) with action performed.

suggestion.title: Command Injection: Arbitrary Shell Execution Post-LiteLLM Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Core of the vulnerability: 'run arbitrary commands on the host.' Detection must hunt for injection patterns in LiteLLM requests (parameter tampering, shell metacharacters) and monitor for unexpected process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline process creation from LiteLLM service account (normally none or only expected children). Alert on: new process creation under LiteLLM, interactive shell spawning, or command-line arguments containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks) in LiteLLM request payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution via Low-Privilege Context
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability allows command execution 'on the host' via low-privilege user keys. Detection should flag when commands run under unexpected privilege levels or from unexpected service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawn from the LiteLLM service account, particularly system administration tools (powershell, cmd, bash, sudo, curl, wget) or reverse-shell indicators. Cross-reference with LiteLLM authentication logs to confirm the initiating request.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Reconnaissance Activity Post-LiteLLM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once arbitrary command execution is achieved, adversaries typically enumerate the host and network. Article implies active exploitation, so post-exploitation discovery should be hunted alongside the injection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5 minutes of first command injection detection, hunt for reconnaissance commands: whoami, net user, ipconfig, systeminfo, dir, ls -la, or port-scanning tools executed under the LiteLLM service context or from a spawned child process.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated remote attacker' can 'establish a remote access VPN connection'—first detection is identifying internet-facing gateways on standard IKE ports (UDP 500, 4500).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound UDP traffic on ports 500 and 4500 to internal Check Point Security Gateway assets. Correlate with asset inventory to identify internet-routable instances. Perform version banner grab if available to confirm unpatched builds against CVE-2026-50751.

suggestion.title: Successful VPN Authentication Without Credential Submission
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication'—detection must flag successful VPN sessions where credential validation succeeded but no corresponding user authentication (password/MFA) event appears in Check Point AAA logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify IKEv1 phase-2 completions and successful VPN authentication where PSK/certificate validation succeeded but no matching username/password submission or MFA challenge appears in Check Point user-auth logs within 5-minute window prior.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Key Exchange Authentication Bypass Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly in 'IKEv1 key exchange' authentication—detection should flag IKEv1 sequences that complete authentication without proper auth payloads or with authentication payload failures preceding success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 exchanges (IKE_SA_INIT, IKE_AUTH phases) for abnormal sequencing: IKE_AUTH completion without auth_payload, or authentication payloads rejected followed immediately by successful phase-2 negotiation from same source IP. Requires Check Point debug logs or packet-level IKE protocol analysis.

suggestion.title: VPN Connections from Novel Source IPs Post-Patch-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patch due 2026-06-11 and notes 'known ransomware use'—after deadline, any successful VPN initiation from historically-unseen IP to unpatched gateways is exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate VPN source IPs. Post 2026-06-11, flag first-ever successful authentications from IPs lacking 90-day prior history. Cross-correlate source IP reputation (Shodan, AbuseIPDB, proxy/datacenter listings) and geoip against ransomware threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Patch Compliance by CVE-2026-50751
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status and patch due-date imply federal audit requirements—detection should inventory unpatched instances and raise compliance alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7) for CVE-2026-50751 findings on Check Point Security Gateway appliances. For any unpatched system accessible from internet-routable network segment (verify via port-scan, firewall logs UDP 500/4500), raise CRIT ticket with 48-hour remediation SLA relative to patch-due date 2026-06-11.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Unauthenticated Endpoint Access via URI Normalization Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'mismatch between how UniFi OS validates and routes incoming requests' where authentication checks the raw URI but Nginx normalizes it, allowing bypass to reach protected endpoints — requests to `/api/auth/validate-sso/` mentioned as explicit monitoring target
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to `/api/auth/validate-sso/` endpoint that lack authentication tokens or originate from non-whitelisted sources. Monitor for URI encoding anomalies and double-encoding patterns that might normalize to protected routes. Baseline legitimate authentication flows and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Command Injection in UniFi ucs-update Package Endpoint (CVE-2026-34910)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-34910 'enables command injection' with 'unvalidated user input into a shell command' targeting the `ucs/update/latest_package` endpoint — explicitly listed for monitoring
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to `ucs/update/latest_package` for shell metacharacters (backticks, `$()`, pipes, semicolons, redirects) in parameters. Alert on injection payloads like `; whoami`, `| /bin/bash`, or environment variable expansion. Correlate with unexpected child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo from ucs-update Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'service account's sudo privileges make privilege escalation trivial' and 'passwordless sudo access to several system binaries' — directly enables root escalation post-command-injection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sudoers execution from `ucs-update` service account. Alert on ANY sudo invocation from this account (passwordless sudo should never execute in normal operations). Cross-reference with parent process and timestamp to correlate with command injection attempts. Flag transitions from non-root to root context.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Creation from ucs-update Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'suspicious child processes under `ucs-update`' as a detection indicator defenders should monitor
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal child processes spawned by ucs-update (typically only legitimate package manager utilities). Alert on unexpected processes: interactive shells (bash, sh, zsh), network utilities (nc, curl, wget), or process launchers (python, perl). Monitor process tree depth and command-line arguments for injection signatures.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation via UniFi API (CVE-2026-34909)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-34909 as 'path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system' — used in exploitation chain before command injection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API requests for path traversal encoding patterns: `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, `....//`, and absolute path references in file/config parameters. Alert on requests attempting to read system files outside UniFi application directories (/etc, /proc, /sys, /home). Correlate with subsequent command injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Root Shell Access on UniFi OS
suggestion.rationale: Article states final impact is 'root shell on the target' obtained 'without authentication' and notes 'no failed-login trail to look for' makes retrospective detection difficult — requires forward-deployed monitoring
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, search for root-context processes spawned from unprivileged ucs-update service. Flag shell sessions established without corresponding authentication logs. Monitor for unexpected changes to system files (/etc/passwd, sudoers, system binaries, cron jobs) with root ownership. Detect inconsistencies in process ancestry (root shell with non-root grandparent).

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet wrapper-check errors in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in File::prohibitWrappers() where parse_url() logic is bypassed. When exploit succeeds, the application may log schema-validation failures, wrapper rejection errors, or file-not-found exceptions. Article phrase: 'parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_SCHEME)' and 'check is not equivalent to "does the path contain a wrapper"'—errors during this check would be logged by the framework.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application error logs for keywords matching wrapper bypass patterns: 'phar', 'wrapper', 'prohibit', 'scheme', or exceptions from PHPSpreadsheet classes during file load. Correlate with HTTP requests containing phar:// patterns on same timestamp. This catches exploitation logged by the vulnerable library before RCE occurs.

suggestion.title: Web-server process DNS/network egress post phar:/// request
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer) but no network-level detection exists. Post-exploitation, attacker executes commands and needs tools (UC_28_3 detects curl/wget spawning only at process level). Network IOCs—DNS queries for malware C2, HTTP GET to suspicious hosts—should correlate with phar:/// requests. Article phrase: 'T1105 — Ingress Tool Transfer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS queries or HTTP connections from web-server process IP to external/suspicious destinations within 5 minutes of phar:/// HTTP request observed in web access logs. Focus on rare ASNs, known malware hosting infrastructure, or non-standard ports (8080, 9090, 4444).

suggestion.title: New executable or script files in web-accessible directories after phar:/// request
suggestion.rationale: Successful Phar loading and RCE likely results in artifacts (webshell, backdoor, config file) planted into web root. UC_28_4 looks for .phar files but misses post-exploitation payloads. Article describes arbitrary code execution via the wrapper: attacker plants files. Detectable via baseline deviation in web directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline /var/www, webroot, document-root directories. Alert on new executable or script files (.php, .jsp, .aspx, .exe, .sh, .bat) or suspicious non-standard extensions created by web-server processes (php-fpm, apache, nginx, w3wp) within 10 minutes of phar:/// HTTP requests in access logs. Exclude scheduled tasks, package managers, and deployment tooling.

suggestion.title: Browser-to-AppleScript Code Injection via URL Parameter Escape Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the plugin 'interpolates a [URL] without escaping' into AppleScript. No detection addresses the initial browser→osascript call with unescaped user-controlled input from active tab URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari spawning osascript with command-line arguments containing URL-like structures, fragments, or special characters typical of web URLs (colons, slashes, percent-encoding). Correlate parent process to active browser tabs or recent URL history when available. Flag if osascript invocation occurs without corresponding user AppleScript editor process.

suggestion.title: Anyquery Chrome Extension → osascript Process Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability is in 'chrome_tabs plugin (and equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari variants)'. Pipeline should detect the specific plugin-to-osascript process chain rather than generic AppleScript breakout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trace browser process spawning osascript where the initiating process or loaded modules match known Anyquery extension paths (julien040/anyquery, ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Extensions/*anyquery*). Alert on version 0.4.4 or earlier in plugin manifest.

suggestion.title: Shell Escape from AppleScript 'do shell script' with Web-Origin Command Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload uses 'do shell script' breakout. Detection should isolate shell commands spawned from osascript where the command arguments originate from unescaped URL or web-sourced input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /bin/sh or /bin/bash child processes of osascript (or chrome processes invoking osascript). Flag when shell command line contains URL schemes, query parameters, fragment identifiers, or web-typical special characters. Correlate back to browser parent and active tab to confirm web origin.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — API token exfiltration via unauthorized /api-keys GET enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'API trusts the bearer token for authorisation' and enables listing all API keys for any operator via GET /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys. This is the *credential access* phase preceding UC_25_1 (key creation). Missing explicit hunt for attackers dumping existing keys before creating new ones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /api/v1/operators/*/api-keys with 200 response followed immediately by POST to same endpoint. Indicates reconnaissance (listing existing keys) before privilege escalation (minting new ones). Expected latency: <5 minutes between discovery and exploitation.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — lateral movement via stolen enrollment credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes reenroll/enroll chain for 'cross-tenant host identity hijack.' Host certificates issued via /enroll can be used to join another tenant's network. Missing hunt for certificate issuance to unexpected sources or lateral movement after reenroll.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /api/v1/enroll responses containing certificate data with subsequent network connections from that host to unexpected network segments. Certificate serial or hostname mismatch to tenant ownership is strong indicator of hijacked identity.

suggestion.title: Gogs New User Account Registration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' due to DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false. Account creation is the attack's entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs audit logs for new user registration events. Alert on account creation immediately followed by repository creation (within minutes). Flag registrations with throwaway email patterns or multiple accounts from same IP.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rapid Repository Creation by New User
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner. From there, enabling rebase merging is a single toggle.' Correlating new account with immediate repo creation and rebase enablement indicates exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account creation with repository creation within <5 minutes. Alert on empty or minimal-commit repos created by accounts <7 days old. Flag if rebase merge enabled immediately after repo creation.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rebase Merge Enabled on New Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This is a required prerequisite for the merge-path argument injection attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repository settings changes for enabling 'Rebase before merging'. Alert on rebase enablement by non-admin users, especially on repos <1 day old or created by account <7 days old.

suggestion.title: Gogs Merge Operation Argument Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'argument injection vulnerability' affecting 'different code path (Merge()) that was never addressed.' The merge operation is the direct RCE attack vector, exploitable through crafted commit/branch metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor merge operation logs for shell metacharacters (;|&$`\) in commit messages, branch names, or author fields. Alert on merge failures followed by process execution. Correlate merge attempts with Gogs process spawning unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Gogs Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromise the targeted server, read any repository, steal credentials, move laterally.' Successful argument injection triggers RCE via Git merge operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent=git/Gogs service. Alert on unexpected child processes: shells (/bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe), network tools (curl, wget, nc), credential dumpers. Baseline expected Gogs-spawned processes and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Source Code Repository Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'alter any hosted source code' is the impact phase. Attackers modify code post-RCE for persistence, supply-chain attacks, or credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits from accounts <7 days old to critical branches (main, master, release). Alert on bulk commits, commits modifying CI/CD configs, authentication code, or build scripts. Flag commits with suspicious branch/tag names containing payloads.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Phishing Link Click Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'WhatsApp Phishing Attack'—the delivery vector. No detection was proposed for message-borne malicious links or shortened URLs characteristic of Pegasus phishing campaigns targeting WhatsApp users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user clicks on shortened or obfuscated URLs within WhatsApp messages followed by redirect to credential-harvesting pages or suspicious TLDs. Correlate with subsequent authentication anomalies or multi-factor authentication bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: NSO Group / Pegasus C2 Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group is explicitly named in the title as the attacker. Pipeline should enumerate known Pegasus C2 domains, IP ranges, and malware signatures associated with NSO's infrastructure for network-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections to NSO-attributed domains (Pegasus C2), including known infrastructure from prior Pegasus exposures. Escalate if the same endpoint also initiated clicks on WhatsApp phishing links within the same session.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article references Meta filing a contempt order, implying successful account compromise. Detection gap for behavioral post-exploitation signals such as sign-in anomalies, recovery option changes, or message forwarding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After phishing link interaction, detect new device/geography sign-in, disabled MFA, password changes, recovery email modifications, or rapid auth retries. Correlate with the original WhatsApp phishing delivery timestamp to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Meta Account Data Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful phishing implies attacker access to target's messages, contacts, and account metadata. Article context suggests intelligence gathering rather than encryption/ransom, indicating collection phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised accounts for bulk message export, contact list downloads, chat history export, profile changes, or auto-forwarding rules. Track unusual API calls to Meta/WhatsApp that correlate with phishing success window.

suggestion.title: Python .pth Startup Hook Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file' and defenders must 'look for Python packages containing executable .pth startup hooks'; this is the direct execution trigger for the malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python interpreter invocations that load site-packages directories recently modified by pip installs. Alert on execution of .pth files with obfuscated or external-reference payloads, particularly *-setup.pth patterns from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Bun JavaScript Runtime Download from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub' and recommends hunting for 'unexpected downloads of the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub'; Bun is staging for JavaScript payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS to github.com targeting Bun releases/binaries initiated by Python, pip, or shell processes. Correlate with preceding package installation events and alert if Bun binary is subsequently executed from /tmp or user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Python-Spawned Bun Process Executing _index.js
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns: 'process chains where Python launches Bun to execute _index.js' indicates execution of the obfuscated payload; this is the key post-download behavioral indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent-child process trees: Python (or python3) spawning Bun with command-line arguments referencing _index.js or other JavaScript files. Flag any such chains on developer workstations or CI/CD environments as anomalous.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service Persistence via PyPI Package
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux'; malware writes service files to establish boot-time re-execution independent of .pth hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system and /usr/lib/systemd/system for new .service or .timer unit files created during or immediately after Python package installations. Alert on ExecStart directives containing shell metacharacters, downloaded binaries, or references to /tmp or hidden directories.

suggestion.title: GitHub Automated Secret Exfiltration via Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies primary exfiltration: 'using automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions'; attacker creates repos and pushes harvested credentials via workflow execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub API calls creating new repositories from CI/CD contexts, followed by commits/pushes containing base64-encoded or unencrypted credential patterns (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.). Alert if repository visibility is public or pushed to external accounts.

suggestion.title: Camouflaged Credential Exfiltration to Fake Anthropic Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes secondary exfiltration: 'direct HTTPS also exists, pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage'; malware masquerades as legitimate API traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS POST/PUT requests to api.anthropic.com/v1/api from non-whitelisted internal networks or CI systems. Inspect request bodies for base64-encoded credential material, shell history content, or SSH key formats; flag even if disguised as API payloads.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Distribution via GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'hosted on GitHub repository' and victims 'redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file.' This is the primary initial-access vector; pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK downloads from GitHub URLs, especially newly created repositories (April 10 creation date noted). Alert on files with names matching legitimate banking apps: 'Intesa Carte', 'Banca Sella', 'CaixaBank', 'Fideuram', 'Nexi', 'Mooney'. Correlate with preceding phishing-domain visits.

suggestion.title: NFC Card Data Capture via Social-Engineered Verification Screen
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack: 'tricking victims with a fake verification screen to place the cards near the mobile device's NFC chip, NFCShare reads the information using Android's IsoDep interface and EMV commands.' This collection behavior is completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious Android NFC API calls (IsoDep interface, EMV command execution) from recently installed or spoofed banking applications. Flag instances where NFC read operations are preceded by fake credential/verification UI patterns. Monitor for extraction of card number, expiry, and PIN in a single session.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Exfiltration of Stolen Payment Card Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'exfiltrates [card data] to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' Pipeline completely missed this C2 and exfiltration indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket connections (ws://, wss://) initiated by recently installed or unnamed applications, particularly masquerading as banking apps. Correlate suspicious WebSocket traffic with preceding NFC read operations and fake verification screen display. Flag connections to undocumented or low-reputation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Installation of Spoofed Banking Applications from Non-Play-Store Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 56 APK variants impersonating real banks: 'Intesa Carte.apk, Sella Carte.apk, Banca Sella Carte.apk, Nexi Carte.apk, Fideuram Carte.apk, Mooney Carte.apk, CaixaBank.apk, CaixaBankNfc.apk, CaixaReactivaTarjeta.apk.' App-spoofing detection is entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of APK files with filenames matching known legitimate Italian/Spanish banking apps (Intesa, Sella, CaixaBank, Fideuram, Nexi, Mooney) installed outside Google Play Store. Compare package names and signatures to legitimate versions. Flag installations following phishing-site visits.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Malformed APK Packaging Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes evasion: 'malformed APK packaging to hinder automated analysis...poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP.' This defense-evasion indicator was not surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed APK extraction attempts using standard tools (unzip, 7z, apktool) on ZipSlip-style or corrupted archive structures. Flag processes attempting archive recovery or anomalous path handling during APK unpacking. Alert on archive integrity violations with low entropy payloads.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Impersonating European Banking Institutions
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials.' SMS/phone impersonation also noted. This social-engineering entry point should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing domains imitating Italian/Spanish banks (Intesa, Sella, CaixaBank, Fideuram, Nexi, Mooney). Monitor for bulk SMS campaigns offering app updates. Flag URLs redirecting to GitHub raw content endpoints. Correlate with credential entry forms and subsequent APK download requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Active Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-11645 is 'exploited in the wild' targeting Chrome V8; no corresponding detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network requests to known malicious domains hosting CVE-2026-11645 exploits. Correlate with Chrome process execution showing abnormal child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned during or immediately after suspicious V8 memory access patterns.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Engine Crash-Loop and Anomalous Recovery
suggestion.rationale: V8 exploits typically trigger repeated browser crashes during memory spray/layout leak phases. Article indicates active exploitation, implying attacker is conducting reconnaissance via V8.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid Chrome process termination (crash) followed by immediate restart in <5 second cycles, especially when correlated with network requests to external C2 infrastructure or command execution from chrome.exe context.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chrome Inventory Flagging
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Patch Now'; detection coverage requires identifying Chrome instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-11645 before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Chrome/Chromium version inventory; flag versions prior to the patched build. Escalate alerts for unpatched instances with network access to known exploit-hosting domains or high-exposure user roles.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Chrome Child Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: V8 code-execution vulnerabilities are stepping stones to OS-level command execution. Article describes 'exploited in the wild' implying post-exploitation activity likely follows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of system utilities (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe) spawned as children of Chrome/Chromium processes, especially with uncommon arguments (e.g., curl, wget, net.exe commands).

suggestion.title: Browser Update Blocking or Disabled Auto-Update Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attackers targeting zero-days often disable browser auto-update to maintain window of vulnerability. Article's 'patch now' urgency suggests defenders must detect update blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for disabling or blocking of Chrome auto-update mechanisms (registry edits, service disables, policy GPO changes). Flag systems where Chrome version remains unchanged for >30 days post-CVE disclosure.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-50751) to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' This is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection rules monitoring for auth bypass patterns on affected gateways.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Mobile Access/Remote Access VPN logs for successful authentication events on IKEv1 sessions without corresponding machine certificates. Alert on rapid failed-to-success auth transitions and unauthenticated connection establishments that bypass standard credential requirements.

suggestion.title: Qilin Post-Compromise Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate,' indicating lateral movement and execution following initial VPN access. Pipeline should detect Qilin-specific behavioral signatures post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic and process execution for Qilin staging behaviors post-VPN establishment: suspicious PowerShell/cmd execution from VPN-connected IPs, lateral movement attempts to file shares, and reconnaissance activity (net discovery, AD enumeration).

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Usage on Production VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol,' creating a clear segmentation signal for at-risk infrastructure that should be inventoried and monitored separately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Check Point VPN gateway initiating IKEv1 key exchanges in 2026+. Generate inventory of all IKEv1-enabled instances. Monitor for CVE-2026-50751 exploitation signatures in IKE phase-1 handshake logs (malformed payloads, unusual negotiation patterns).

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Unauthenticated Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path described as allowing 'Unauthenticated remote attackers' to 'establish a remote access VPN connection.' Detection must discriminate legitimate auth flows from bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN tunnel establishment with zero authentication steps or missing mandatory cert validation. Alert on connections that skip pre-shared key exchange or machine certificate verification on gateways configured to require legacy Remote Access clients.

suggestion.title: Qilin RaaS Infrastructure Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Qilin as the threat actor, active since August 2022 with 400+ claimed victims. Command-and-control infrastructure associated with Qilin should be monitored post-initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Qilin-attributed C2 domains/IPs (from threat feeds, dark web leak site analysis) with egress traffic from compromised VPN users. Alert on DNS resolutions and HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Qilin staging servers from breached internal networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Detected by Vulnerability Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry stating 'currently being exploited in the wild.' Pipeline must flag when CVE-2026-11645 appears in scanner results as a high-priority incident. Directly from: 'CISA KEV entry...added CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result reporting CVE-2026-11645 affecting Chromium, Chrome, Edge, or Opera. Correlate scan date against patch-due date (2026-06-23) to prioritize unpatched assets. Even if patch management shows compliant versions, confirm absence of patch bypass or rollback.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTML Page Delivery / Browser Exploit Kit Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described: 'crafted HTML page' as the delivery mechanism for RCE. Pipeline must detect HTML-based exploitation attempts. From: 'remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious HTML downloads or email attachments targeting Chromium-based browsers, especially .html or .htm files from untrusted sources. Monitor for GET/POST to known exploit kit C2 domains attempting to deliver HTML-based V8 exploits. Flag HTML files that trigger browser crashes or high memory usage post-delivery.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Abnormal Behavior / Sandbox Escape Indicators
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability enables 'execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox'—the sandbox containment is the first barrier, so detection of code breakout is critical. From: 'out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability...execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Chrome/Edge/Opera with unexpected privilege escalation (e.g., system LUID, SeDebugPrivilege). Flag parent-child relationships where browser process spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scrpting engines. Alert on unusual memory access patterns (VirtualAlloc with EXECUTE_READWRITE on browser heap) or suspicious kernel-mode transitions from renderer process.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Check: Chromium / Chrome / Edge / Opera Versions vs. CVE-2026-11645
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch compliance: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-23' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Detection use case must track deployed browser versions against this CVE. From: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-23' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all endpoints for Chrome/Edge/Opera version ≤ unpatched threshold for CVE-2026-11645. Cross-reference against patch-due date (2026-06-23). Flag any system reporting a vulnerable version 30+ days post-due-date as critical non-compliance. Validate patches via file hash or version string, not just installer logs (patch rollbacks exist).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Page Hosting / Potential Exploit-Kit Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: The attack requires a web-accessible 'crafted HTML page,' implying either compromised infrastructure or adversary-controlled hosting. Detection must identify attacker-controlled or compromised sites attempting V8 exploitation. From: 'remote attacker...via a crafted HTML page' and 'could affect multiple web browsers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for web traffic to known exploit-kit domains or newly-registered domains with high V8 keyword matches. Flag any external URL accessed by browser processes immediately following failed patch verification. Cross-reference URL reputation feeds and domain-age against exploit-kit infrastructure profiles.

suggestion.title: Chromium Source Code / V8 Engine Local Debugging / Development Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may stage local proof-of-concept development or reverse-engineer the V8 engine to craft HTML triggers. Detect internal attempts to access or compile V8 components. From: 'out-of-bounds read and write' implies attackers likely iterated on memory layout weaponization locally before deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious access to Chromium source code, V8 GitHub repositories, or public proof-of-concept repos for CVE-2026-11645 from non-development hosts. Flag compilation of V8 or Chromium from unexpected directories. Monitor for gdb/lldb or IDA Pro targeting browser processes on development machines.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Vulnerability Presence Hunt
