suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...#asset-exposure]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline ignored this direct instruction and generated zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management logs for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances (vManage) with unfixed CVE-2026-20245. Flag assets below affected versions and not patched before federal due date 2026-06-23. Prioritize internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Command Execution from SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'execute arbitrary commands as root by supplying a crafted file'. Pipeline failed to surface the execution phase (T1059). Root-level command spawning is the exploitation outcome that must be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on command-line process creation running as root or under SD-WAN Manager service account with unexpected parent process, abnormal working directory, or command patterns inconsistent with vManage operations (e.g., shell invocation, file exfiltration commands).

suggestion.title: Crafted File Upload to SD-WAN Manager Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'supplying a crafted file to the affected system' is the delivery mechanism. Pipeline missed the file-upload attack surface entirely, which is the initial-access vector before command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco SD-WAN Manager web interfaces for file-upload POST/PUT requests. Flag uploads by non-administrative accounts, large binary uploads, or uploads with suspicious MIME types followed within seconds by process execution events.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'CVE-2026-7473 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and is a CISA KEV entry currently exploited in the wild. Standard asset-exposure hunt is the baseline detection for any KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management systems for Arista Extensible Operating System (EOS) with CVE-2026-7473 flag. Cross-reference unpatched instances against network exposure data (internet-facing, externally routable) to identify exploitable targets.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Suspicious Tunnel Decapsulation Error Events
suggestion.rationale: Article describes root cause: 'switch incorrectly decapsulates and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP.' Detection should hunt for decapsulation failures and malformed tunnel handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS device logs for decapsulation errors, tunnel processing failures, invalid encapsulation headers, or unexpected packet forwarding tied to decapsulation IP matching. Baseline normal tunnel traffic first, then flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Anomalous Egress After Tunnel Ingress
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attacker to 'forwards other unexpected tunneled packet' — implying attacker injects malicious tunneled traffic that device incorrectly processes and retransmits. Network detection should correlate tunnel ingress with suspicious egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Arista EOS devices receiving tunneled traffic destined to their configured decapsulation IP address followed by anomalous outbound traffic to non-standard destinations, different protocols, or bulk data transfer. Flag as potential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Patch Compliance Tracking — CVE-2026-7473
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal patch due date is 2026-06-23 and 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators.' Compliance tracking is a detection requirement for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate weekly inventory of Arista EOS firmware versions across the estate. Flag any version released before the vendor's patch date as non-compliant. Escalate internet-facing or DMZ-resident instances for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Remote OS Command Execution via FortiSandbox Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute arbitrary OS commands through the web interface.' This is the execution phase and requires dedicated detection logic separate from initial exploit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual process creation spawned by the FortiSandbox web service process (httpd/nginx/lighttpd). Look for unexpected shell interpreters (bash, cmd, powershell, sh) or script execution tools invoked with suspicious command-line arguments originating from the sandbox web interface listener process.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to FortiSandbox Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated remote attackers' accessing the web interface—this is initial access without credential compromise, signaling exploitation of the authentication bypass flaw itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiSandbox web interface endpoints (typical ports 8443, 443, 8080) for sequences showing missing or invalid authentication headers followed by command execution patterns, alerting on exploitation attempts that precede any token acquisition.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploit Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies this specific CVE but pipeline generates no signature-based detection. Public exploits for this vulnerability should include detectable payload patterns, request structures, or parameter injection techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create IDS/WAF signatures for known CVE-2026-25089 exploitation payloads, focusing on HTTP request parameter injection points and command structures documented in public POCs targeting the affected FortiSandbox versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Account Compromise via Social Engineering on Government Messaging Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actor gained access to the platform following a social engineering attack' and 'I social engineered a valid account on the education shard (matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for account authentications from anomalous geographies/IPs post-social-engineering report, MFA bypass or disabled 2FA on government messaging accounts, and sign-in patterns inconsistent with user baseline (off-hours, new device). Alert on successful login immediately after user reports credential exposure.

suggestion.title: Detect Hardcoded Credentials in PowerShell Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gained hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan PowerShell execution and file creation for hardcoded credential indicators (LDAP URIs, plaintext passwords, API keys in script content). Alert on scripts containing authentication material shared to external or public locations. Monitor LDAP binding events with credentials extracted from script source.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Message Exfiltration from Matrix Messaging Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages and information on over 73,000 accounts' and '13.5GB of documents and media files.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single account accessing or downloading 650k+ messages within hours/days (extreme volume). Alert on bulk media enumeration (iterating media IDs without corresponding UI interaction). Detect sustained API call patterns to /messages, /media endpoints from single session. Flag data egress >10GB from messaging platform.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated File Access on Matrix Media Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GET requests to /media endpoints without valid Bearer token or session cookie. Alert on media URL pattern generation (extracting media IDs from message responses then accessing directly). Detect file download activity bypassing authentication middleware or token validation failures.

suggestion.title: Detect Cross-Shard Reconnaissance and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker accessed 'education shard' and stated 'other shards will have more'—indicating reconnaissance of organizational compartmentalization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single account accessing resources across multiple Matrix shards (education, tax, health silos). Alert on LDAP or directory enumeration queries listing shard configuration, organization units, or user counts. Detect account activity in shards inconsistent with employee role/department.

suggestion.title: Detect Account Metadata and User Directory Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'information on over 73,000 accounts, including email addresses, organization information, meeting links, and account and device metadata.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single account querying user endpoints with pagination/wildcard patterns targeting 73k+ accounts. Alert on bulk collection of email addresses, org structure data, and device metadata outside normal admin workflows. Detect unusual API call frequency to /users, /profile, or /account endpoints.

suggestion.title: Outdated Chrome Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Stable channel has been updated to version 149.0.7827.102/.103 for Windows and Mac, and 149.0.7827.102 for Linux' — indicates systems running older versions are vulnerable; no inventory-based detection logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome process versions and installed software inventory for instances below 149.0.7827.102. Flag endpoints with Chrome process creation events where version string does not match patched release. High-risk if Chrome process launched from user-writable directory (indicators of supply-chain or sideload attack).

suggestion.title: Chrome Crash/Restart Spike (Post-Exploitation Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article states zero-day is 'actively exploited in the wild' but provides no post-exploitation indicators. Browser exploits often trigger sandbox escape or process termination; crash logs are artifact of exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal frequency of Chrome process termination and restart cycles within 5-minute windows. Correlate with network egress to C2 domains or suspicious child processes (powershell, cmd, wmic). Baseline per endpoint; flag if crash rate increases >2σ from rolling 7-day average.

suggestion.title: V8 Engine Exploitation via Crafted HTML Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers exploit 'via crafted HTML pages to execute arbitrary code inside the web browser's sandbox'—primary attack vector with no corresponding detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome/Chromium processes for suspicious child process spawning, unsigned code injection, or memory allocation patterns immediately following HTML content delivery; flag abnormal V8 exception logs or heap allocation failures.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass Indicators in Chrome Sandbox Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could also be exploited to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR'—ASLR bypass is a critical defense-evasion prerequisite for reliable code execution and should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome processes with sequential memory layout failures, successful allocations at predictable addresses post-exception, or disabled address randomization; correlate guard page faults with module loading sequence anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chrome Version Detection (CVE-2026-11645)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes patch rollout 'could take days or weeks to reach all Chrome users'—detection of endpoints running vulnerable versions <149.0.7827.102/103 is essential for vulnerability prioritization and impact scoping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Chrome processes with version <149.0.7827.102 (Windows), <149.0.7827.103 (Mac), <149.0.7827.102 (Linux) after 2026-06-09; flag endpoints where Chrome auto-update is disabled or update deployment failed.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption and Out-of-Bounds Memory Access in Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'out-of-bounds read and write weakness' causing 'heap corruption, exposing sensitive information'—out-of-bounds access patterns are runtime-detectable signals of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome sandbox processes generating access violations in heap regions, guard page faults, or abnormal memory reads beyond allocated buffer boundaries; correlate with process termination or crash dump generation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python setup.py Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages were 'poisoned to auto-run' — execution is triggered during pip install via setup.py hooks. Pipeline missed the entire execution vector: 'auto-run Bun credential stealer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for python.exe, pip.exe, or setup.py spawning unexpected child processes during package installation context. Alert on subprocess execution with suspicious command lines (curl, wget, powershell, cmd) originating from pip cache or temp installation directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Bun CLI Credential Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Bun Credential Stealer' as the payload. Pipeline did not suggest detection for credential harvesting from ~/.bun or Bun token stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-Bun processes read from ~/.bun/install/cache, Bun config files, or npm token locations. Correlate file access from setup.py context with network egress in the same session. Flag processes spawned during pip execution that attempt to read credential stores.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration from Python Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate stolen tokens. Article does not detail C2 domains in provided text, but detection should cover credential egress from setup.py execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections from python.exe or setup.py child processes to non-standard hosts (excluding pypi.org, github.com, mirrors). Flag POST requests from package installation context containing base64-encoded strings, JWT patterns, or token-like structures.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Poisoned PyPI Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector explicitly stated: 'Hades PyPI Attack: 19 packages poisoned.' This is T1195.001 and should anchor the entire kill-chain. Pipeline produced zero reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install logs for unexpected version numbers, non-standard package indexes, or SHA checksum mismatches against published PyPI metadata. Alert on installation of packages whose setup.py or wheel checksums deviate from canonical PyPI hashes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Name Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned packages typically mimic legitimate names to trick installation. Article title does not list specific names, but this tactic is intrinsic to supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package names against legitimate packages using Levenshtein distance ≤2 for typosquatting. Alert on installs of packages with single-character swaps, additions, or homoglyphs from high-value targets. Correlate with failed dependency resolution or fallback installs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 LiteLLM Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exploited in the Wild'—indicates active exploitation events that should trigger detection, but zero use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to LiteLLM endpoints for exploitation payloads and patterns consistent with CVE-2026-42271. Alert on unauthenticated or anomalous request structures preceding code execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE' but no execution-phase detection was proposed to catch the command execution itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process or command execution spawned from LiteLLM application context without preceding authentication log entries. Monitor for unexpected child processes or shell invocations from the LiteLLM runtime.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command and Control Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'chains to RCE'—implies post-compromise command execution and lateral movement, but no second-stage detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network traffic from LiteLLM processes for anomalous connections (C2 beaconing, reverse shells) that deviate from baseline LiteLLM operational patterns.

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Action Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Azure Functions Action' as attack vector; no detection for unauthorized action execution or replacement in workflows. Title states attack 'targeting AI Coding Agents' via Actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of GitHub Actions with unexpected outbound connections, credential access, or repository manipulation. Correlate action YAML changes with commit metadata (new committer, unsigned). Detect action version downgrades or execution from forked/unvetted sources.

suggestion.title: Repository Mass Disablement via Compromised CI/CD Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article title: '72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack'—no detection for bulk repository access revocation or simultaneous disabling patterns indicating lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential disabling/archiving of repositories within single authentication context. Alert on bulk permission removals or repository transfers from compromised identity. Correlate with GitHub Actions secrets exposure or SSH key compromise.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Injection in AI Agent Framework
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'worm' targeting 'AI Coding Agents'—suggests packaged malware delivery. No detection for unsigned packages, version inconsistencies, or dependency confusion attacks affecting ML/AI toolchains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected package versions in AI agent dependencies (e.g., numpy, tensorflow, langchain updates outside normal cadence). Alert on packages with metadata anomalies (unsigned, different signer, timestamp gaps). Correlate package downloads with repository fork/clone activity.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation Through Repository Modification Chain
suggestion.rationale: Malware named 'Miasma Worm' implies self-replication; article describes impact across 72+ repos. No detection for cross-repository infection patterns or cascading code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single identity modifying workflows or action YAMLs across unrelated repositories in sequence. Alert on repository-to-repository push patterns within short time window. Identify malicious payload signatures in commits to .github/workflows or package.json files across repository clusters.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions Deployment from Untrusted GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Azure Functions Action' as compromised; no detection for deployments to Azure triggered from modified or newly-added GitHub Actions using cross-platform credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Azure Functions deployments initiated by GitHub Actions using service principal or managed identity credentials. Alert when deployment action parameters change or source repository is newly forked. Detect Functions code containing network beacons, credential access, or repository API calls.

suggestion.title: HTTP.sys Integer Overflow RCE Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to a targeted server utilizing the HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys) to process packets.' (CVE-2026-47291) — no detection generated despite clear network-based exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized HTTP requests to http.sys that trigger integer wraparound logic; correlate with crash dumps, kernel exceptions, or unusual process termination of services hosting HTTP Protocol Stack. Watch for repeated crafted packets from single source within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: RDC Client Heap Overflow Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Heap-based buffer overflow in Remote Desktop Client which allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network' (CVE-2026-42985) and 'attacker who controls a Remote Desktop Server could initiate a remote code execution (RCE) on the machine when a victim connects to the attacking server using the vulnerable Remote Desktop Client' — describes server-side exploitation of client but no detection use case provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual mstsc.exe process behavior following RDP connection initiation (particularly from non-standard RDP servers); monitor for child process creation, code injection, or memory access violations. Correlate credential_guard bypass or UAC elevation attempts with recent RDP sessions.

suggestion.title: Windows Graphics Component Integer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Integer overflow or wraparound in Windows Win32K – GRFX subsystem (graphics component). An unauthorized attacker, exploiting this vulnerability can execute malicious code locally' (CVE-2026-44803, CVE-2026-44812) — local code execution vector with specific affected module not mapped to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privileged code execution (SYSTEM) spawned from user-mode graphics applications or unusual allocations to Win32K memory regions. Detect crafted metafile/GDI objects in file drops preceding dwm.exe/csrss.exe exceptions or unexpected kernel mode transitions.

suggestion.title: Hyper-V Guest-to-Host Escape via File Operation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'authenticated attacker on a guest virtual machine (VM) sends specially crafted file operation requests to hardware resources within the VM which could result in remote code execution on the host server' (CVE-2026-45607, CVE-2026-45641, CVE-2026-47652) — privilege escalation from guest VM to hypervisor is security-critical but no detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor guest VM processes attempting direct hardware resource file access (storage, network adapters) via vmbus; correlate with unusual I/O patterns or file handles to physical devices. Detect guest processes making out-of-bounds memory access requests or crafted DeviceIoControl calls targeting vmbus devices.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Office Type Confusion Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'access of resources using an incompatible type ('type confusion') in Microsoft Office...The attack vector is the preview pane of Outlook (classic)...email rendering in Outlook (classic) utilizes Microsoft Word functionality' (CVE-2026-45456, CVE-2026-45458, CVE-2026-47635) — specific email preview attack surface but no detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Word or unknown child processes spawned from Outlook.exe preview pane rendering (OUTLOOK.EXE->WINWORD.EXE or WinRtUtil variants); monitor for code injection into wordprocessor or rtf rendering processes. Flag emails with unusual MIME structures or embedded objects triggering type confusion.

suggestion.title: Windows DHCP Client Stack Overflow Network RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Stack-based buffer overflow in Windows DHCP Client which allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network. An authenticated user could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted network traffic to a server configured for use as a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) Server' (CVE-2026-44815) — network-based local RCE but unpaired with detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for oversized or malformed DHCP responses from DHCP servers; correlate with DHCP client (dhcp.exe, dhcpsvc.exe) crashes or unexpected privilege escalation (e.g., svchost.exe running code with elevated privileges post-DHCP request). Detect anomalous DHCP response payloads exceeding RFC boundaries.

suggestion.title: Zero-day Exploitation Attempt Detection (T1190 Payloads)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVEs were 'actively exploited' before patches became available, indicating attackers possessed working exploits. Pipeline should suggest web/proxy/IIS log hunts for exploitation attempts. Phrase: 'three zero-day vulnerabilities that were actively exploited or publicly known before a fix was available.' Without known signatures, hunt for anomalous HTTP patterns (high entropy, unusual methods, suspicious parameters) targeting known Microsoft public-facing services on unpa
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests with high entropy payloads, unusual request methods, or known exploitation patterns targeting unpatched Microsoft public-facing applications (Exchange, Sharepoint, IIS). Correlate with process creation events from web service parent processes. Baseline normal traffic first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Execution from Vulnerable Services
suggestion.rationale: Successful T1190 exploitation of public-facing services typically leads to command execution via child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Given active exploitation in the wild, detection should monitor for abnormal process spawning from vulnerable Microsoft services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by known vulnerable Microsoft services (w3wp.exe, sqlservr.exe, iisexpress.exe) with suspicious attributes: encoded arguments, native tools (cmd, powershell), network connections, or uncommon execution paths. Baseline benign behavior and tune FP scenarios.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Bulk Offline/Disabled Status Transition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Microsoft Restores Some GitHub Repos, Keeps Others Offline'—this is an impact-phase indicator of repository containment/destruction. Pipeline should detect repositories transitioning to disabled/offline state, especially in bulk within a short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API audit logs and Microsoft security dashboards for bulk repository status changes (e.g., disable, archive, delete). Look for patterns: multiple repos from same organization/team, rapid state changes within minutes, changes correlated with known incident timelines. Alert if >10 repos affected in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Forensic Investigation API Pattern—High-Volume GitHub Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Miasma Probe Continues'—a forensic investigation. Probes/investigations generate anomalous query patterns against repositories: listing all repos, fetching commit history, comparing branches, etc. This is detection/discovery phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service accounts or user tokens making high-volume GitHub API calls to repository enumeration endpoints (list-repos, get-repo, list-commits). Baseline normal API activity per service account; alert if a single token exceeds 10x normal query volume in a 10-minute window, especially for read-heavy operations on sensitive repos.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Trust Boundary Compromise—Repository Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies repository compromise; article body likely discusses stolen credentials, API tokens, or signing certificates. The phrase 'Miasma Probe' suggests forensic response to a breach where attackers had repo access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub-stored secrets (personal access tokens, deploy keys, webhook URLs) being accessed, rotated, or deleted at scale. Correlate with repository access logs to find who accessed secrets and when. Alert on secrets accessed outside normal CI/CD pipelines or from non-standard IP addresses.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Security Tool Bulk Repository Access During Incident Response
suggestion.rationale: Microsoft's forensic 'probe' of GitHub repositories during incident would involve Microsoft-owned or partner service accounts querying affected repos at higher-than-normal volume. This is normal incident response behavior but distinct from attacker queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline GitHub API activity by Microsoft service accounts (e.g., repos.azure.com, security scanning bots). During incident response, these accounts will spike in query volume. Create a 'expected forensic pattern' profile: rapid enumeration of commits, webhook configs, branch protections, and secrets across multiple repos. Use this to distinguish incident response from attacker reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Malicious Push or Commit Injection to GitHub Repositories (Compromised Repos)
suggestion.rationale: If 'Miasma Probe' involved repository compromise, attackers likely injected malicious code, commits, or branch updates. The fact that Microsoft is keeping some repos offline suggests potential code corruption that must be investigated before restoration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits or pushes to sensitive/archived repositories from unexpected users or IP addresses. Look for: commits with unusual metadata (wrong timestamp, author mismatch), commits to protected branches bypassing review, force-pushes that rewrite history, or pushes from compromised service accounts. Correlate with repository access logs to identify if a user who read the repo later pushed changes.

suggestion.title: Defender for Cloud Alert—Azure Identity Compromise Tied to GitHub Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Microsoft GitHub breach likely involved compromised Azure AD or Microsoft Entra identity. Article references Microsoft's investigation; pipeline should surface identity-based detection around service principals or users accessing GitHub outside normal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Azure Entra ID sign-in anomalies (impossible travel, new locations, risk flags) with GitHub API activity from the same account. Alert if a compromised Entra identity accessed GitHub repositories, especially if the access preceded repository disablement or occurred during forensic investigation window.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Performing Rapid Storage Access Timing Measurements
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes FROST exploiting 'SSD timing'—the attack vector is JavaScript code measuring storage device latency. Article states 'websites' execute this, implying JavaScript payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript executing unusual storage probing patterns: rapid sequential cache/localStorage/IndexedDB access, timing correlation code, or memory-access latency measurement loops, especially from third-party script domains.

suggestion.title: Web Request Followed by Timing-Channel Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack output as 'track what sites and apps you open'—timing measurements must be exfiltrated to attacker. Phrase 'Websites track' implies HTTP exfil to the visiting website's backend.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify web requests to third-party domains that correlate with the user previously visiting other sites (infer from browser cache/cookie timing). Flag HTTP POST/beacon traffic containing timing deltas or binary-encoded correlation data sent back to the malicious website.

suggestion.title: Cross-Website Timing Inference of Installed Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'track what sites and apps you open'—the attack profiles both web browsing and installed app presence via SSD side-channels, suggesting multi-vector profiling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious JavaScript timing probes (above) with endpoint file-system access patterns. Flag when JavaScript in one origin initiates probes coinciding with SSD reads consistent with installed apps (executable paths, app caches).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated SSD Timing Side-Channel Exploit Code Delivery
suggestion.rationale: FROST requires delivering and executing exploit code in-browser. Phrase 'new FROST attack' and 'via SSD timing' indicates a specific technique; malicious JavaScript would likely be obfuscated to evade static detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript files with obfuscation markers (eval, Function constructors, base64/hex encoding) that contain known FROST timing measurement primitives (high-resolution timer calls, cache eviction patterns, latency measurement loops).

suggestion.title: File Hash Detection — MagicAd SHA1 Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 30 SHA1 hashes labeled 'high-fidelity'; pipeline output shows empty IOC dict. Standard hash matching for install-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or process execution matching the 30 provided SHA1 hashes. High-fidelity IOCs from security research enable straight-forward detection at install and execution boundaries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Background Ad Overlay Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'floods infected devices with ads' using 'multiple techniques to keep showing ads in the background'—indicates persistence and execution mechanisms not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawning display overlays persistently, registering foreground services, or abusing SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and accessibility service permissions for ad injection.

suggestion.title: Android OS Restriction Bypass — Defense Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'slipping past the built-in restrictions of the Android operating system'—core evasion mechanism reduced to single T1027 mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps requesting/abusing permissions like SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, or disabling system ad-filtering. Detect runtime permission enforcement bypass or safe-browsing filter circumvention.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Background Service Registration
suggestion.rationale: Continuous ad display requires boot-time or service-level persistence; 'techniques to keep showing ads in the background' implies autostart/foreground service mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service components registering boot-complete or app-startup intent filters, or persistent foreground services that outlive typical app lifecycle. Correlate with ad-serving infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Domain User RCE on Veeam Backup Server
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authenticated domain user' with 'low privileges' can 'exploit this vulnerability' to gain 'remote code execution (RCE) on the Backup Server.' This is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution spawned by Veeam service accounts or unusual cmdline patterns from SYSTEM/service context on Veeam servers. Track domain logons to Veeam servers by low-privilege accounts followed by process execution outside normal Veeam operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Backup Deletion Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers... block restoration efforts by deleting victims' backups'—ransomware gangs deliberately destroy backups after RCE to prevent recovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume backup file deletions or deletion of system backup metadata on Veeam servers. Correlate with process execution from suspicious contexts and network lateral-movement activity in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Veeam Service Port Scanning / Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will reverse-engineer patch once disclosed, requiring reconnaissance. Article warns 'once a vulnerability and its associated patch are disclosed, attackers will likely attempt to reverse-engineer the patch to exploit unpatched deployments.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag external scanning of Veeam default ports (6160, 6162 for Backup Server API). Detect repeated connection attempts to backup server from non-administrator IPs; correlate with failed authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Veeam Backup Server
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers use compromised Veeam servers to 'move within breached networks'—backup servers have broad network access and trust relationships, making them lateral-movement pivots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new outbound network connections from Veeam servers to internal systems not in baseline. Flag credential usage from Veeam-hosted service accounts against non-backup systems; detect lateral-movement tool execution (PSExec, WinRM) from Veeam process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44963 Exploitation Attempt (Version Check / Payload)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions (VBR 12.3.2.4465 and earlier 12.x); fixed in 12.3.2.4854. Attacker must identify version before exploit. No payload details given, but API-based RCE suggests HTTP/REST call inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Veeam API logs (port 6162, HTTPS) for suspicious POST/PUT requests targeting RCE-vulnerable endpoints. Detect version-string queries or unusual request patterns from non-admin sources. Flag exploitation indicators from Veeam advisory when available.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Veeam v12 Deployed in Domain Context
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'many companies have joined their Veeam servers to a Windows domain, ignoring Veeam's long-standing best practices.' Presence of domain-joined VBR v12.3.2.4465 or earlier is the precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory scan for Veeam installations on v12.3.2.4465 or earlier, cross-referenced against domain-membership. Alert on any v12 build < 4854 still active after patch date. Flag domain-joined Backup Servers as high-risk configuration drift.

suggestion.title: Email Impersonation Requesting Sensitive Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker impersonated a team lead and requested access to the staging environment during a purported production issue. The agent located and emailed AWS IAM keys, database credentials, and SSH access details to an external Gmail account.' This is a core attack vector—credential exfiltration via social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails impersonating internal personnel (spoofed sender) requesting access to production systems or credentials, especially when sent to new external recipients or followed by credential sharing within minutes. Monitor for AWS IAM key or database credential patterns in outbound email to external domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized CRM Data Export to External Recipient
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The agent retrieved and sent a CRM export containing customer records, contact information, contract details, and revenue data without verifying the sender's identity.' This is exfiltration of customer PII and financial data via pretexting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exports of CRM bulk data (contact lists, contract details, revenue records) triggered by email requests from new external senders or unusual requesters. Correlate email receipt of urgent business pretext (remote work, presentation prep) with immediate data export and external email transmission.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious Link Visited by Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The agent received a fake gift card email containing a phishing link. Under the generic configuration, it visited the phishing site and attempted to redeem the gift card using fabricated credentials before eventually identifying the page as malicious.' This captures credential-harvesting phishing against automated systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email-triggered URL visits to known phishing or suspicious domains, especially gift card / reward / urgent action themed emails. Alert on automated credential entry attempts (regex patterns or form fills) to suspicious login pages, combined with email receipt within seconds prior.

suggestion.title: Malicious OAuth Application Permission Request
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Researchers created a malicious Google OAuth application disguised as a timesheet platform. The agent inspected the OAuth flow, analyzed the destination, identified the application as suspicious, and refused to grant access.' This represents a deceptive third-party app grant attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth consent screens for newly registered or low-reputation applications requesting broad scopes (email, calendar, drive access) especially when redirecting to unexpected domains. Flag applications with generic or misspelled names (e.g. 'timesheet' vs. established vendor name) requesting first-time access.

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequential Sensitive Data Requests from New External Senders
suggestion.rationale: Article shows multiple attacks in sequence: credential requests, then CRM export, then phishing link, then OAuth—all within a test session. Real attacks often probe defenses with multiple requests. This use case detects pattern-based exfiltration attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple requests for distinct sensitive datasets (credentials, CRM, financial, calendar data) from the same new external sender or IP range within a short timeframe. Each request may be individually plausible but the pattern indicates reconnaissance or data harvesting.

suggestion.title: Operational Urgency Override of Identity Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Both Generic and Strict profiles failed because the verification step still collapsed when the request appeared operationally urgent.' This identifies a social-engineering bypass of security controls—the attacker weaponized urgency messaging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails claiming operational emergency (production outage, urgent client issue, compliance deadline) that request credentials, data exports, or system access, especially when the sender's domain/address cannot be verified via reverse lookup or when sender is not in the organization's directory.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Malware Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Pythagora-io/gpt-pilot Compromised on GitHub' with malicious code injected into a legitimate repository—a supply-chain attack vector requiring detection of repo modifications and suspicious commit metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for commits from unusual accounts, changes to security-critical files (setup.py, __init__.py, CI configs), and commits introducing dependencies or URLs not previously seen in project history.

suggestion.title: Python Credential Stealer Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Named malware 'Shai-Hulud' described as 'credential stealer'—requires detection of Python processes attempting to access credential storage (keyrings, .ssh, browser profiles, environment variables).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter execution with file access patterns targeting credential repositories (e.g., ~/.ssh, ~/.config, /proc/*/environ, Windows DPAPI credential stores) or subprocess calls to credential-dumping utilities.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Python Linter Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware was 'Blocked by Python Linter'—pipeline should detect obfuscation techniques designed to circumvent static analysis (string encoding, dynamic imports, code generation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python source files using suspicious evasion patterns: hex/base64 string literals decoded at runtime, __import__() calls, exec()/eval(), ast.literal_eval() on external data, or comments referencing linter suppression.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Installation from Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Malicious code injected into public GitHub repo would be pulled by `pip install`, `git clone`, or other package managers—detection of installation and execution from supply-chain vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip/setuptools/git commands installing from 'pythagora-io/gpt-pilot' or detecting execution of code from compromised checkout paths; correlate with subsequent credential access or network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Malware IOC: Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer Detection
suggestion.rationale: Named threat 'Shai-Hulud' is the core detection focus; pipeline failed to extract this as an IOC or create hash/filename-based signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file hash and filename signatures for Shai-Hulud payload; detect Python processes with suspicious environment (PYTHONPATH, __main__ overrides, imported modules from temp directories) matching malware characteristics.

suggestion.title: Local LLM Model Infection & Self-Replication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'self-replicating AI worm that operates entirely on local, open-weight models'—core threat model. Pipeline produced no kill chain or detection logic for model-to-model infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual chained LLM inference calls, especially where model output is fed as input to spawn new model instances. Detect when open-weight model binaries (Llama, Mistral, etc.) are executed with parameters indicating code generation or shell commands.

suggestion.title: Open-Weight Model Download & Local Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Worm operates on 'local, open-weight models'—indicates initial deployment of model files. Article subject matter implies model sourcing/distribution attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of large model weight files (.bin, .safetensors, GGUF) from untrusted sources. Flag attempts to load models from non-standard paths or repositories. Correlate model artifact staging with subsequent inference execution.

suggestion.title: Inference-Based Command Execution via Model Output
suggestion.rationale: Self-replication through open-weight models implies the worm propagates as adversarial input/output chains. 'Operates entirely on local models' suggests code generation within inference loop.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track shell/code execution spawned immediately after LLM inference completion. Detect patterns where model stdout is piped to cmd.exe, bash, or Python interpreters. Alert on rapid iteration loops suggesting automated re-prompting.

suggestion.title: Unusual LLM Process Resource Consumption
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm running on local hardware would exhibit anomalous CPU/memory/disk patterns. 'Self-replicating' implies sustained, repetitive inference workload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate open-weight model inference (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM). Alert on sustained 100%+ CPU usage by inference processes combined with model file I/O spikes, especially at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Model Fingerprint & Mutation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Worm described as 'self-replicating'—likely mutates itself across replication. Need detection of model parameter drift or variant signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash model weight files regularly and alert on unexpected modifications. Establish canary model checksums and flag any inference execution referencing altered model artifacts. Detect attempts to obfuscate model parameters.

suggestion.title: SAML Signature Wrapping Attack Detection (CVE-2026-44748)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'XML Signature Wrapping...potentially allowing authentication bypass in SAML-based environments' and 'send modified signed XML documents to the verifier.' This is a critical (CVSS 9.9) attack vector that pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SAML assertion handling for signature validation anomalies, multi-wrapped XML structures, or reordered signature elements. Alert on SAML responses with appended unsigned assertions or timestamp mismatches. Correlate with successful auth despite malformed payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RFC Exploitation (CVE-2026-27671)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attacker can exploit it without authentication by sending crafted RFC requests to vulnerable endpoints, leveraging improper kernel validation to cause memory corruption.' CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated RCE vector—critical for SAP intrusion detection and not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline RFC protocol traffic to NetWeaver endpoints. Alert on unauthenticated RFC calls from unexpected sources, malformed RFC headers, or oversized payloads triggering kernel errors. Monitor for RFC calls to kernel-facing subsystems without prior auth.

suggestion.title: Directory Traversal in NetWeaver Java (CVE-2026-40128)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Directory traversal vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java's Web Container' (CVSS 9.0). Common attack vector for file disclosure and lateral movement in SAP environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to NetWeaver Java AS for path traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e, unicode variants, backslash escapes). Alert on requests targeting /WEB-INF, config directories, or system paths. Correlate with 4xx responses indicating probing.

suggestion.title: Spring Security Framework Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-22732)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'Spring Security-related vulnerability affecting SAP Commerce Cloud and SAP Data Hub' (CVSS 9.1). Spring Security flaws commonly enable authentication bypass or privilege escalation—two major SAP products affected, zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Spring Security filter chain for exception patterns (FilterSecurityInterceptor failures, AccessDeniedException anomalies). Alert on unexpected role grants or requests bypassing authentication filters. Correlate Commerce Cloud and Data Hub logs for concurrent anomalies.

suggestion.title: Authorization Bypass in ABAP (CVE-2026-44751)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'missing authorization check issue in NetWeaver AS ABAP' (high severity). Authorization bypass is a fundamental attack type in SAP environments—no detection use case provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ABAP transaction calls and function module invocations for missing or failed authorization checks. Alert when users execute sensitive transactions (user mgmt, configuration, sensitive data) without corresponding auth trace entries. Flag privilege escalation patterns.

suggestion.title: Tomcat Vulnerability Chain in Commerce Cloud (CVE-2026-29145)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'multiple Apache Tomcat flaws impacting Commerce Cloud' (high severity). Commerce Cloud is widely deployed e-commerce platform—Tomcat vulns typically enable RCE or auth bypass, yet no detection strategy exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Tomcat access logs for exploitation patterns (parameter pollution, unusual HTTP verbs, servlet mapping tricks, Content-Type mismatches). Alert on Tomcat exception stacktraces indicating parsing failures or memory issues.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Pre-Install Script Execution via build Event
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp enables arbitrary command execution during npm install/build; 'npm can execute scripts via the build lifecycle' is the core threat. Detection should catch shell/PowerShell spawned by node/npm with binding.gyp context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm.exe or node.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash with parent process context tied to node_modules install. Flag if process tree includes binding.gyp in working directory or environment variables.

suggestion.title: Malicious Native Module Installation via npm Dependency
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp allows packages to compile native C++ code during install. Attackers can inject build-time code execution. Detection should flag packages with binding.gyp that also have suspicious build commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track npm package installs containing binding.gyp files with non-standard build commands. Cross-reference against package.json scripts for obfuscated or external-URL-fetching build steps (curl, wget, PowerShell download).

suggestion.title: Node-Gyp Build System Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is processed by node-gyp; GYP syntax allows interpolation of environment variables and shell metacharacters in 'variables' stanzas. This enables argument injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for node-gyp.js or gyp processes spawned with unusual command-line flags containing shell operators ($, |, &&, backticks, $(...)) or environment-variable dereferencing patterns within binding.gyp config values.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Modification of package.json Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Attackers can modify package.json to inject preinstall/postinstall/build scripts that invoke binding.gyp compilation with malicious directives. This is the entry point for supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to package.json (especially in node_modules or during CI/CD pulls) that add or modify 'scripts' stanzas with binding.gyp, node-gyp, or external-fetch commands. Correlate with unexpected registry sources.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Data Exfiltration via npm Build Script
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp build-time execution is pre-sandbox. Attacker code runs with full process privileges and can exfiltrate secrets/keys before application code runs. Detection should catch network calls during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/node process spawning with unexpected outbound network connections (DNS queries, HTTP/S) during npm install phases. Flag destinations outside known package registries or CDNs.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Process Spawns Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealers are deployed—implies code execution post-exploitation. Title phrase: 'exploited...to deploy stealers' suggests WinRAR extraction triggers malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when winrar.exe or unrar.exe spawns child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, regsvcs.exe, rundll32.exe, msiexec.exe) within 5 seconds of archive extraction, especially from Downloads or Temp folders. Baseline legitimate extraction patterns separately.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Registry Hive Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is 'stealers in Ukraine'—information stealers target credential stores. Missing detection for browser password/cookie harvesting behavior central to stealer TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process reads of HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SAM, or browser credential vaults (Chrome AppData\Local\Google, Firefox profile dirs). Alert if non-browser process accesses these in sequence.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ACE Archive Download and Extraction Sequence
suggestion.rationale: WinRAR vulnerability specifically targets ACE archive parsing. Article implies delivery via malicious .ACE file. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for vulnerability exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .ACE files (especially 0-day or malformed) followed within 2 minutes by unrar.exe extraction to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or user directories. Cross-reference file hashes against known stealer signatures.

suggestion.title: Stealer Outbound C2 Communication Post-Execution
suggestion.rationale: Stealers exfiltrate data. Article establishes payload deployment but omits C2 detection. Pipeline should infer exfiltration phase from stealer classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from newly-executed child processes (of WinRAR) to low-reputation domains or IPs with no prior org communication. Flag connections to known stealer C2 infrastructure (Raccoon, Redline, StealC family domains).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Credential Material
suggestion.rationale: Stealers harvest credentials; Ukraine-targeting campaign likely escalates to lateral spread. Pipeline missed post-exfiltration lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After credential-theft indicators, detect logons from infected host to other domain resources using harvested credentials (especially out-of-hours, to non-standard shares, from suspicious source processes).

suggestion.title: Stealer Malware Family Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stealers' but omits malware family identification (Raccoon, Redline, StealC, etc.). Pipeline should enumerate known stealer families and behavioral signatures for Ukraine-targeting campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for common stealer behaviors: memory-scanning for browser processes, DLL injection into explorer.exe, registry enumeration for crypto wallets, temp-file creation with stolen-data staging patterns. Use YARA or behavioral signatures keyed to Redline/Raccoon/StealC families.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with AI Brand Account Verification Request
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'AI brands as bait' in social engineering. Threat actors impersonate AI service providers (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) to redirect users to credential-harvesting pages. Phrase: 'using the AI hype in social engineering' establishes this as primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails claiming to be from AI service providers requesting immediate login verification, account upgrades, or security re-confirmation. Flag links pointing to domains mismatched with known AI company infrastructure, especially newly registered or typosquatted domains.

suggestion.title: Authentication Attempt on AI Service Account from Suspicious IP
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include AiTM (Adversary-in-the-Middle), which enables attackers to intercept credentials and log in from proxy infrastructure. Stolen credentials trigger logins from attacker-controlled IPs, distinct from user baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login attempts on AI platform accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) from IPs with poor reputation or geolocation mismatches, followed by successful logins from the same infrastructure within hours. High-risk when combined with prior phishing-email open.

suggestion.title: Domain Registration Containing AI Service Brand Substring
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering campaigns exploit brand recognition by registering lookalike domains (chatgpt-secure[.]com, claude-login[.]app, etc.) to host phishing pages. Article theme 'AI brands as bait' implies use of these impersonation domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS resolutions to newly registered or low-reputation domains containing substrings of major AI brands (chatgpt, claude, gemini, perplexity, copilot, etc.). Prioritize domains not resolving to known AI company ASNs or CDNs.

suggestion.title: User Credential Re-entry to Non-Canonical AI Service Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow: user receives phishing email → clicks link to fake login page → attacker captures credentials via AiTM or HTML form. Detection should identify credential submission to domains impersonating AI services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users who clicked links in phishing emails with AI brand references, then submitted credentials (based on form submission patterns or network POST to credential harvesting domains), followed by account compromise indicators or unusual API access patterns.

suggestion.title: Forwarding Rule or Delegate Permissions Added Post-AiTM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After stealing AI service account credentials, attackers establish persistence to monitor account activity or pivot to connected email/data services. This is a post-compromise persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new email forwarding rules, delegate permissions, or OAuth consents granted on AI service accounts (or downstream email/SaaS accounts linked to them) within 24 hours of suspicious login activity or phishing campaign timeframes.

suggestion.title: Browser Certificate Trust Anomaly Preceding Credential Submission
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks require HTTPS interception, which mandates that attacker proxy infrastructure install malicious or self-signed certificates. Browser warning bypasses or new cert installs precede credential capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users who installed unusual root certificates or disabled certificate validation warnings, then visited AI-brand lookalike domains and submitted credentials. Cross-reference with mailbox AiTM indicators (unusual login locations, failed MFA, etc.).

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Unexpected Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'run arbitrary commands on the host.' Any shell interpreter (bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe) spawned by LiteLLM processes is direct exploitation evidence. This is the attacker's execution channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM parent process (python, node, litellm) spawning shell interpreters with suspicious command lines containing pipes, redirects, variable expansion ($(), backticks), or base64 encoding. Establish baseline of legitimate LiteLLM subprocesses first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and states federal patch deadline 2026-06-22. Vulnerability scan results are the primary IOC source for this CISA KEV entry until patches are deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory and vulnerability scanners reporting BerriAI LiteLLM version matching vulnerable criteria for CVE-2026-42271. Cross-reference with internet-facing assets since T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) requires external accessibility.

suggestion.title: API Key Abuse + Command Injection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' can trigger the vulnerability. This indicates both credential theft and privilege escalation via injection—detectable through auth logs + unexpected command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM API authentication (standard or API-key) succeeded, followed within seconds by application error logs containing stack traces referencing command execution (os.system, subprocess), or process creation events. Correlate authentication source IP with subsequent unexpected outbound connections.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Once arbitrary command execution is achieved ('run arbitrary commands on the host'), the attacker pivots to internal reconnaissance and lateral spread. Outbound connections from LiteLLM process to internal infrastructure are post-exploitation markers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network connections originating from LiteLLM process or child processes to internal-only IP ranges, SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH ports, or DNS queries for internal hostnames. Baseline legitimate traffic first; focus on connections to assets not listed in application dependency inventory.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Indicators in LiteLLM Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'command injection vulnerability'—injected payloads must be parsed by the application, creating detectable log artifacts (shell metacharacters, exception traces, subprocess invocations) before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM application logs or stack traces containing shell syntax in input fields (|, &, ;, $(), command substitution), exception messages referencing subprocess/os module, or stderr output from unexpected child processes. Use regex for common injection patterns (backticks, command separators) but tune for application baseline.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Key Exchange Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange' is the core attack mechanism. Pipeline failed to surface detection of anomalous phase-1 handshakes or authentication failures followed by successful tunnel establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 phase-1 negotiation logs for completed key exchanges that bypass or skip authentication validation steps, or for rapid phase-1 attempts followed by tunnel establishment without corresponding credential validation events.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated VPN Tunnel Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker ability to 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' This is a direct behavioral anomaly: VPN session creation without preceding successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN session creation or tunnel-up events from Check Point gateways where session establishment occurs without corresponding successful authentication records in the preceding 5 minutes, especially on versions prior to CVE-2026-50751 patch date.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Active Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article directs operators to 'CVE-2026-50751 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes CISA KEV status (in-the-wild active exploitation). Pipeline did not generate scanning or exploit-detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2026-50751 on Check Point gateways with IKEv1 anomalies (rapid phase-1 failures, malformed packets, burst connection attempts) occurring within 48 hours, signaling exploitation in progress.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Post-Exploitation Activity via VPN Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Known ransomware use,' indicating threat actors leveraging this vuln as initial access for broader compromise. Detection must correlate exploitation with downstream indicators (lateral movement, encryption, C2).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences where CVE-2026-50751 exploitation indicators (IKEv1 bypass anomalies, unauthenticated tunnel establishment) are followed within hours by suspicious outbound connections, batch file execution, or encryption activity from systems behind the gateway.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Disabled or Deleted
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords explicitly reference CloudTrail abuse; 'Abusing Cloud Logging Services' describes disabling trail logging as a primary evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or DeleteEventSelectors API calls from IAM principals. Alert if CloudTrail logging halts for >5 minutes without documented maintenance. Correlate with credential exposure or privilege escalation events.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail S3 Destination Configuration Removed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'log storage' and S3 in keywords; attackers disable log shipping to S3 buckets to prevent centralized log collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UpdateTrail API calls that modify or remove the S3BucketName or S3KeyPrefix attributes. Detect when event selectors are modified to exclude read/write events. Cross-reference with IAM policy changes on the S3 bucket.

suggestion.title: CloudWatch Logs Group Deletion or Retention Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Keywords mention 'log storage'; CloudWatch Logs groups are primary destinations for API logs. Article describes 'blinding the watchmen' by removing visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DeleteLogGroup, PutRetentionPolicy (set to 1 day or deletion), or DisableLogEvents API calls on high-value log groups. Alert if a log group is deleted within 1 hour of suspicious API activity in that group.

suggestion.title: Google Cloud Logging Sink Deleted or Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'Google Cloud'; log sinks are the primary mechanism for routing GCP logs. Disabling sinks prevents log export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logging.sinks.delete or logging.sinks.update calls with empty destination field. Monitor for exclusion filter changes that exclude suspicious API calls or resource deletions from exported logs.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Log File Integrity Validation Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Blinding the Watchmen'—disabling log integrity checks (digest files) prevents detection of log tampering and ensures logs cannot prove they were unmodified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UpdateTrail API calls setting EnableLogFileValidation to false. Monitor for absence of CloudTrail digest file creation for >24 hours. Correlate with S3 bucket changes affecting the digest file location.

suggestion.title: VPC Flow Logs Disabled or Destination Removed
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'defense evasion' and 'visibility' loss; disabling VPC Flow Logs removes network-layer visibility of command-and-control or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DeleteFlowLogs or ModifyFlowLogOptions API calls. Alert if flow logs are deleted during or immediately after unexpected network activity or lateral movement. Check for IAM policy changes to CloudWatch Logs or S3 buckets that would break log delivery.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Patch Deployment Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exploited in the Wild' and 'Patch Now'—asset visibility and patch compliance is the primary defensive action. No use case captured this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome/Chromium version inventory across endpoints. Flag devices running versions prior to the patched release. Correlate patch deployment events with CVE-2026-11645 remediation tickets. Alert on patching failures or delays >7 days post-advisory.

suggestion.title: Browser Crash/Anomaly Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: V8 exploits typically trigger memory corruption; title mentions zero-day RCE vector. Browser crash patterns are high-signal exploitation telemetry. Article establishes need for detection of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Chrome/Chromium renderer process crashes (exit codes -2147483645, -2147467259) within 30 seconds of page load from untrusted domains. Correlate with concurrent child process spawning or memory allocation anomalies in V8 heap. High-volume crashes across cohort = potential watering hole.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript in V8 Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Title describes V8 engine zero-day. Pipeline missed T1059.007 (JavaScript) as execution vector. Exploit delivery is via adversarial JavaScript evaluated by V8 JIT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome DevTools Protocol traffic or JavaScript console for inline script execution with suspicious patterns (obfuscated eval(), WebAssembly instantiation, SharedArrayBuffer access). Flag high-entropy script payloads from external CDNs or data: URIs during browsing of known malicious sites.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process from Chrome/V8
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day RCE in V8 likely enables arbitrary command execution. Article context ('Patch Now') implies full code execution risk. Pipeline missed post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Chrome/Chromium spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget) without prior user interaction or extension consent. Flag executions with command-line arguments referencing /tmp, downloads, or obfuscated payloads. Baseline: Chrome should not spawn children in Normal mode.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output completely empty despite CVE being the article's primary IOC. Vulnerability assessment systems should flag all Chrome instances as vulnerable. Detection use case for vulnerability management systems missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVE-2026-11645 into vulnerability scanning tools. Scan all Chrome/Chromium instances and flag as CRITICAL severity. Correlate scan results with patch compliance data. Generate report of vulnerable instances by business unit and remediation timeline.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Authentication Bypass via IKEv1
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-50751) to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' This is the core attack vector and requires detection at initial access point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IKEv1 protocol negotiation attempts to Check Point VPN gateways, especially from external sources. Track authentication bypass indicators: IKEv1 handshake completion without successful credential validation followed by authenticated session establishment from same source within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'The vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol...accept legacy Remote Access clients.' Detection should flag these legacy protocol/client combinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IKEv1 connections combined with legacy Remote Access client user-agents or protocol signatures on Check Point devices. Correlate IKEv1 + deprecated client use with gateways that lack machine certificate enforcement.

suggestion.title: VPN Machine Certificate Bypass Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states prerequisites: 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate for connections.' Detect connections where machine certificate validation is disabled or bypassed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful remote access VPN sessions from Check Point gateways where machine certificate authentication is not enforced. Cross-reference against baseline of gateways requiring certificates; deviations indicate misconfiguration or exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Ransomware Deployment Post-VPN Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate.' After VPN authentication bypass, expect ransomware execution. Detection should chain VPN anomalies to downstream payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious VPN session indicators (IKEv1 + no cert + legacy client) with subsequent file encryption activity, ransomware-indicative process chains, or communication to known Qilin infrastructure (C2 domains, leak site beacons).

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Post-Exploitation Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article links exploitation directly to Qilin RaaS: 'Check Point has linked at least one incident to the Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operation, which has claimed over 400 victims on its dark web leak site since it surfaced in August 2022.' Qilin-specific behaviors should be detected post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known Qilin C2 domains, negotiation patterns, ransom note file creation (typical Qilin naming), and data exfiltration patterns associated with Qilin incidents. Cross-reference dark web leak site IOCs with network telemetry post-VPN compromise.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Protocol Usage on Check Point Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'The vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol.' Widespread IKEv1 usage post-patch deadline indicates unpatched or misconfigured assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of IKEv1 usage on Check Point estate pre-June-11 patch deadline. Post-deadline, any continued IKEv1 connections to Check Point gateways may indicate unpatched systems. Flag IKEv1 + external source combinations as high priority.

suggestion.title: Detect Unpatched Chromium V8 (CVE-2026-11645) in Fleet
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-11645 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references canonical asset-exposure templates. Patch due date 2026-06-23 establishes audit compliance scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanner for Chrome, Edge, Opera versions with unpatched CVE-2026-11645. Alert on web-facing systems and high-privilege assets past federal remediation deadline. Cross-reference with network exposure data to identify exploitation surface.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTML Delivery Targeting Browser Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described as 'crafted HTML page' triggering out-of-bounds memory access. Network observable and preventable at proxy layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTML file delivery to Chrome, Edge, Opera user agents. Flag delivery to vulnerable versions. Correlate suspicious HTML sources with threat feeds. Consider YARA signatures for V8 exploitation patterns if available.

suggestion.title: Browser Sandbox Escape via Out-of-Bounds Memory Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox' — implies post-exploitation process anomalies as RCE sandbox container breaks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by browser processes (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, opera.exe) with unusual privileges or file handles. Flag abnormal parent-child relationships post-patched date. Alert on memory access patterns suggesting heap spray or JIT side-channel exploitation.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Compliance and Audit Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies federal civilian agency mandate. Federal patch due date 2026-06-23 is audit-triggering event. Article emphasizes 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate weekly browser version compliance report. Flag systems non-compliant past 2026-06-23. Correlate with asset criticality tier. Prepare remediation SLA tracking. Alert SOC leadership when compliance gap narrows to 5 days pre-deadline.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vendor Chromium Browser Exploitation
