suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'Unauthorized Access to Customer Instances' indicates post-exploitation account activity; pipeline produced no use cases for anomalous login patterns, session hijacking, or mass data access following initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logins to ServiceNow instances from unexpected IPs, rapid sequential API calls querying user/incident/CMDB tables post-initial-access timestamp, or service account usage outside maintenance windows. Cross-reference with exploitation indicators from initial-access phase.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Mass Data Export or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Unauthorized Access'—implies data theft; pipeline generated no detection logic for bulk export patterns, large result-set queries, or authenticated data download anomalies typical of post-compromise reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API queries returning >10k records, list view exports, or scheduled report generation by compromised/stolen accounts. Correlate with unusual outbound connections to non-approved endpoints or compression/archiving tools on ServiceNow application servers.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Vulnerable Systems — CVE-2026-50507 and CVE-2026-45585 Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' hunt with confidence 'High' and phase 'recon'. Pipeline failed to instantiate this template. Detects systems vulnerable to disclosed BitLocker bypass affecting encryption bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Windows systems running OS versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-50507 or CVE-2026-45585. Prioritize systems with BitLocker enabled. Cross-correlate with patch-management inventory to flag unpatched assets in sensitive environments.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Disablement or Recovery Key Access — Unauthorized Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthorized attacker with physical access to bypass BitLocker Device Encryption.' Detection should monitor for BitLocker state changes and recovery key access indicative of exploitation or post-compromise forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Event Log 4656 (BitLocker Preparation Tool) and 5061 (Encryption state change). Flag unexpected BitLocker disablement, recovery-key extraction, or decryption initiation outside maintenance windows. Correlate with physical-access logs and after-hours activity.

suggestion.title: Mass File Access on Previously Encrypted Storage — Post-Bypass Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article culminates in impact: 'access sensitive data on the system's storage device.' After BitLocker bypass, attackers enumerate and exfiltrate. Detection closes post-exploitation gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-BitLocker-disablement, monitor for rapid file listing, copy operations on system or user data folders (AppData, Documents, System32), and unusual external device connections. Correlate with BitLocker state changes and time-of-day anomalies.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Logging Disabled or StopLogging API Called
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly references 'abusing cloud logging services'; disabling CloudTrail is the primary AWS logging evasion vector described in this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or PutEventSelectors API calls in CloudTrail logs targeting production accounts. Monitor for successful trail disable within 5 minutes of privilege escalation or credential compromise. Correlate with failed log access attempts by same principal.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Log Files Deleted from S3
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'log storage' and deletion of log entries; S3 bucket tampering is a direct attack vector when CloudTrail logs are stored in S3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk DeleteObject or DeleteVersion calls against S3 buckets designated as CloudTrail log destinations. Alert on deletion patterns that remove logs spanning suspicious activity windows. Cross-reference with IAM policy changes granting s3:DeleteObject to compromised principals.

suggestion.title: Cloud Logging Configuration Modified to Reduce Log Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'log router' and 'log sink' abuse in Google Cloud context; configuration modification narrows logging scope without full disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UpdateSink calls with modified filter expressions that suppress log types, DeleteSink calls removing sinks to SIEM, or UpdateLoggingBucket calls disabling retention. Alert on configuration changes affecting data-access or activity logs post-compromise.

suggestion.title: IAM Policy or Role Modified to Grant Logging Impairment Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article implies privilege escalation step before logging attacks; attacker must escalate to role/principal with logging-modification permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inline or managed policy attachments granting logging-modification actions (logs:*, s3:DeleteObject on log buckets, logging.logEntries.delete). Alert on creation of custom roles with overly permissive logging-related actions. Correlate policy changes with subsequent logging API calls.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Cloud Logging Configuration and Storage Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker enumeration of logging infrastructure as prerequisite; DescribeTrails, ListTrails, and similar discovery calls precede disablement.
log_sources: GCP Audit Logs (List, Get on logging resources)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of logging-discovery API calls (DescribeTrails, GetTrailStatus, ListTrails, ListSinks, GetBucket) in rapid succession from single principal. Alert on enumeration from newly-compromised credentials or atypical source IP. Baseline expected discovery from compliance/audit tools.

suggestion.title: GCP Log Sink Disabled or Forwarding Target Removed
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'log router' and 'log sink' as abuse targets in Google Cloud; sinks forward logs to storage or external SIEM—removal is evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UpdateSink calls that set includeChildren=false, disable sinks, or modify filter to exclude critical log types. Alert on DeleteSink operations removing sinks that forward to external storage (GCS, BigQuery, Pub/Sub). Correlate with later activity in same GCP project.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Exploitation Attempt - Memory Corruption Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Chrome V8 Zero-Day'—indicating memory corruption vulnerability exploitation. Article states 'Exploited in the Wild' but pipeline generated no corresponding detection for memory-based exploitation or browser crash/hang patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome/Chromium renderer processes terminating abnormally with memory access violations or executing unusual child processes post-crash recovery. V8 exploits typically trigger segfaults or heap corruption errors in V8.dll/libv8.so.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Title includes specific CVE identifier (CVE-2026-11645) but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should flag attempts to exploit this public CVE once patches become available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match Chrome version against known vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-11645. Alert on unpatched versions accessing untrusted content or responding to targeted phishing campaigns linking to exploit pages.

suggestion.title: Malicious Browser Content Delivery to Unpatched Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates wild exploitation but no detection for delivery mechanism. Browser zero-days typically require social engineering or drive-by download to reach victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails linking to attacker-controlled domains serving exploit kits targeting Chrome. Correlate with browser crash telemetry or suspicious process execution following web browsing sessions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Behavior After Browser RCE
suggestion.rationale: Chrome V8 exploits enable code execution in renderer context. Pipeline missed detections for lateral privilege escalation or payload staging following successful browser compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts (token impersonation, UAC bypass) launched from Chrome child processes or following abnormal Chrome termination and restart. Detect suspicious signed-binary abuse (LOLBins) spawned by browser context.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-50751) to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' This is the core initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN gateways for IKEv1 Key Exchange traffic from external sources that establishes VPN sessions without valid credential submission. Alert on authentication bypasses or successful session establishment without corresponding RADIUS/TACACS+ authentication events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous VPN Session Establishment to Check Point Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploitation began on May 7 and surged over the weekend' targeting 'few dozen targeted organizations globally.' New or suspicious VPN source IPs should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN connections from novel source geographies, previously unseen ASNs, or off-hours access patterns to Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access appliances. Correlate timing with known exploitation window (post-May 7, 2026).

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Post-Compromise Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate.' VPN compromise should precede ransomware execution (file encryption, exfiltration, ransom note).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 48 hours of VPN compromise, alert on mass file encryption activity (bulk file modifications), process execution from SYSTEM context with suspicious parents (psexec, WMI, RDP), or large data exfiltration to novel external IPs known or suspected as Qilin infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Enabled on Check Point Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' and 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate.' Configuration audit should flag this weakness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Check Point gateway configurations for IKEv1 enablement on Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN instances. Packet inspection should detect and alert on IKEv1 Key Exchange messages on systems that should be IKEv2-only.

suggestion.title: Machine Certificate Authentication Disabled on Check Point VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate for connections and accept legacy Remote Access clients' are vulnerable. Machine cert auth enforces device identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Check Point Remote Access VPN configurations for mandatory Machine Certificate Authentication. Alert if disabled or optional. Cross-reference successful VPN sessions against client certificate logs to identify device-unauthenticated connections.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Version Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera' — asset inventory and patch verification against federal remediation deadline (2026-06-23) is foundational for this CISA KEV threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query installed software inventory for Chrome, Edge, Opera versions and compare against CVE-2026-11645 patch release dates. Alert on vulnerable versions persisting past federal due date 2026-06-23. CISA KEV status confirms active in-the-wild exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Execution from Browser Engine
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation outcome as 'arbitrary code inside a sandbox' — detection must flag unexpected child processes spawned from browser engines with anomalous execution patterns or resource access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation where parent = chrome.exe, msedge.exe, or opera.exe and child is not a known legitimate subprocess. Flag processes with suspicious cmdline arguments, memory access anomalies, or correlation with V8 engine exceptions.

suggestion.title: V8 Engine Crash Correlated with Suspicious Post-Crash Activity
suggestion.rationale: Out-of-bounds read/write vulnerability ('CVE-2026-11645 — Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Read and Write') consistently triggers application crashes during exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on chrome.exe, msedge.exe, or opera.exe crashes with access violation (0xC0000005) or heap corruption exception codes, especially if followed within seconds by unexpected child process spawning, outbound network connections, or file I/O to sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: Browser Sandbox Escape Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Real-world exploitation of client-side RCE vulnerabilities frequently escalates from browser sandbox context to system privileges — monitor for privilege boundary violations even though sandbox escape is not explicitly stated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes or their child processes attempting HKLM registry writes, System32 directory modifications, device driver loading, or direct kernel API access. Flag process injection attempts originating from browser sandboxes.

suggestion.title: Web Request to Suspicious Content Followed by Browser Crash
suggestion.rationale: Attack delivery mechanism: 'via a crafted HTML page' — correlation between web requests and subsequent browser crashes may indicate exploitation of CVE-2026-11645.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP/HTTPS requests or DNS queries from browser processes to low-reputation or suspicious content sources, followed within seconds by browser process crashes with memory violation exceptions. High fidelity if correlated with V8-specific crash signatures.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Suspicious Crafted File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'supplying a crafted file to the affected system' as the exploitation mechanism. Detection should monitor file uploads to SD-WAN Manager endpoints for suspicious patterns or unusual payload characteristics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for unusual file uploads or POST requests with file parameters. Correlate with subsequent process execution. Alert on files with suspicious entropy, encoding oddities, or unexpected MIME types directed at vManage endpoints.

suggestion.title: Elevated Privilege Code Execution from SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... execute arbitrary commands as root'. This privilege escalation pattern is detectable via process execution monitoring on systems running SD-WAN Manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Cisco SD-WAN Manager processes (vManage child processes, wrapper scripts) spawn root-level command shells or execute system binaries with UID=0. Establish baseline of legitimate root execution and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Authentication Anomaly Preceding Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'authenticated, local attacker' access. Detect authentication patterns that precede file uploads or process anomalies, including failed login attempts, lateral movement to management interfaces, or credential reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager (vManage) authentication logs for: (1) successful logins from unexpected source IPs, (2) login spike preceding file upload, (3) service account abuse, (4) failed login patterns suggesting credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Output Encoding Failure in SD-WAN Manager Request/Response Cycle
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'improper encoding or escaping of output'. Detection should identify HTTP responses or logs from SD-WAN Manager showing unescaped/unencoded payloads, command injection signatures, or encoding bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP responses from SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing unencoded command syntax (bash operators, shell metacharacters) in error messages, parameter echoing, or debug output. Correlate with requests containing special characters (;, |, &&, etc.).

suggestion.title: Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerability Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and references asset-exposure template in _TEMPLATES.md; no use case generated. Federal patch due 2026-06-23 makes this time-critical for compliance hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and CMDB for Arista EOS instances with version matching CVE-2026-7473 eligibility. Correlate against network-exposed assets via port scans or NetFlow. Alert on unpatched devices remaining 5 days before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Arista Decapsulation Error Rate Spike
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically involves incorrect decapsulation of tunneled packets ('incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet'); error logs should surface exploitation attempts before successful packet forwarding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS syslog and CLI logs for decapsulation failures, malformed packet drops, or tunnel validation errors. Establish per-device baseline; alert on 4σ spike or sustained 2-3x elevation, particularly if correlated with external source traffic.

suggestion.title: Arista Tunneled Packet Misdirection via Decapsulation IP Collision
suggestion.rationale: Technical root cause: device forwards packets where destination IP matches configured decapsulation IP but originate from unexpected sources. This mismatch behavior should be detectable via netflow and packet content analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline valid tunnel encapsulation patterns per Arista device (legitimate source/dest pairs, protocols). Flag netflow tuples where inner packet destination IP equals the device's configured decapsulation IP but source deviates from baseline, or where encapsulation headers fail signature validation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Unauthorized File Access Without Token Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token.' Attack succeeded because files were accessible via media IDs scraped from messages, bypassing authentication controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests for media resources using ID patterns extracted from message contents, without corresponding token validation events. Alert on single account/IP downloading files across multiple conversations or users within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Message and Account Enumeration Across Shards
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor scraped 'nearly 650,000 messages and information on over 73,000 accounts' and stated 'Everything below is what that one account could reach, other shards will have more.' Indicates systematic enumeration across organizational boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single compromised account accessing conversation metadata, message history, or account rosters from domains/shards outside its organizational unit (e.g., education shard account accessing tax authority or health ministry shard metadata).

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor stated: 'I social engineered a valid account on the education shard.' Account was used as entry point for reconnaissance and data exfiltration across the platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in events followed by unusual account behavior: first-time access to administrative APIs, bulk message queries, cross-shard roster enumeration, or file downloads from conversations not previously accessed by that account.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Exposure in PowerShell Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor claims: 'hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director.' Script exposure enabled subsequent lateral movement and authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts containing LDAP connection strings with embedded credentials (pattern: LDAP://host with password in credentials object). Alert on scripts shared via messaging platforms or stored in common collaboration directories.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Matrix Protocol Shards
suggestion.rationale: Attacker statement 'Everything below is what that one account could reach, other shards will have more' combined with 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token' indicates cross-shard access without re-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single Matrix account issuing requests to multiple shard domains (matrix.agent.*.tchap.gouv.fr) within same session or with same bearer token. Detect file/room queries targeting organizational units (shards) outside user's assigned domain.

suggestion.title: Web server process spawning shell interpreter from POST handler
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'any authenticated user to execute arbitrary OS commands' and 'complete RCE with web server privileges.' The terminal handler spawning sh/bash/dash is the core exploit behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP-FPM, Apache, or Nginx processes spawning shell interpreters (sh, bash) in web server user context (www-data, apache, nginx, nobody). Filter for parent_process in {php, php-fpm, apache2, httpd, nginx} and child_process in {sh, bash, dash}. High confidence when combined with pheditor.php in call stack.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to pheditor.php with shell metacharacters in request body
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'shell metacharacters into the dir POST parameter' as exploitation vector. Detection at network/WAF layer before PHP execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to *pheditor.php with action=terminal parameter and request body containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, >, <, $(, backticks). Medium confidence due to FP risk from legitimate parameter escaping; escalate if combined with subsequent process execution from web server user.

suggestion.title: PHP-FPM/Apache writing executable PHP to common webroot during RCE window
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'achieving full Remote Code Execution' and typical post-exploit persistence involves webshell drop. Detectable via file creation events to webroot with executable permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of .php files by PHP processes (php-fpm, apache2, httpd, nginx) in webroot paths (/var/www/*, /srv/www/*, /usr/share/nginx/html/). Flag especially if filename is generic (shell.php, upload.php, tmp.php) or if parent process matches suspicious pattern (concurrent with T1059.004 spawn).

suggestion.title: Direct CVE-2026-48030 asset inventory hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article is titled with explicit CVE. Patch management and asset exposure are foundational. 'CVE present' mentioned in severity justification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify web servers hosting pheditor application. Cross-reference version manifests, web directory indices, or application fingerprinting logs against CVE-2026-48030 affected versions. High priority: any externally-facing pheditor instance.

suggestion.title: Playground endpoint reconnaissance and WebSocket upgrade requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'phoenix_storybook playground accepts user-controlled attribute values over WebSocket'. No detection exists for the initial-access vector—probing or successfully connecting to the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to /playground, /storybook, or similar paths on Phoenix applications; flag WebSocket upgrade attempts from unauthenticated clients or from unexpected source IPs. Establish baseline for legitimate playground traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: HEEx template-injection attempts in WebSocket payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'interpolates them unsanitized into a HEEx template that is subsequently compiled and evaluated'. No hunt detects the injection mechanism itself—payloads containing HEEx syntax, Elixir module references, or code-execution attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect WebSocket frames to playground endpoints for HEEx template syntax ('<%= %>', 'Kernel.', 'System.' references) or Elixir module-access patterns. Alert on payloads that deviate significantly from expected component-attribute structure.

suggestion.title: Elixir runtime code-evaluation and dynamic compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'HEEx template that is subsequently compiled and evaluated with full Elixir Kernel access'. If Elixir runtime or application logs capture code-eval events, these would signal active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for unexpected Elixir code-eval events, dynamic module loading, Kernel-function invocations in unusual contexts, or template-compilation warnings/errors that include user-supplied input in the compiled bytecode.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable phoenix_storybook in application dependency manifest
suggestion.rationale: Complements UC_12_4 (filesystem scan). Article identifies vulnerable versions 0.5–1.0. Hunt should also flag vulnerable versions in mix.lock or dependency-management files before deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan mix.lock, Gemfile, package.json for phoenix_storybook entries in versions <1.1. Alert on newly committed or deployed dependencies introducing vulnerable versions; correlate with CI/CD pipeline events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious temporary-file creation by BEAM process during playground activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes live HEEx compilation and Kernel.eval. Template compilation often generates temporary artifacts in /tmp or application-temp directories. File creation by BEAM correlated with WebSocket playground traffic signals active code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-creation events by BEAM/Erlang processes in /tmp, /var/tmp, or app-specific temp directories. Correlate spike in file creation with WebSocket requests to playground endpoint; flag if timing suggests active template compilation.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 RCE via Crafted HTML Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation mechanism: 'remote attackers can exploit via crafted HTML pages to execute arbitrary code inside the web browser's sandbox.' No UC exists to detect delivery or post-exploitation process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious HTML file downloads followed by Chrome process spawning child processes with elevated privileges or unusual network connections. Monitor for V8 compiler errors or crashes combined with process injection indicators.

suggestion.title: Chrome Patch Deployment & Version Drift
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions (149.0.7827.102/103) rolling out to users. Unpatched versions remain attack surface. Pipeline missed detection hypothesis for version monitoring during active exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome processes running versions <149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or <149.0.7827.103 (Mac) after patch release date. Correlate with web traffic to known exploit distribution sites.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass & Out-of-Bounds Memory Read
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'could also be exploited to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR, making it easier to achieve code execution via another weakness.' This is a distinct defense-evasion technique not captured in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome processes for memory disclosure behaviors (reading process/library addresses) or multiple failed memory access attempts prior to RCE-like behavior. Cross-reference with V8 engine error logs if available.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption & Sandbox Escape Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'heap corruption' and potential sandbox escape via 'access data beyond the memory buffer.' No UC maps out-of-bounds access as a sandbox-breakout precursor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome processes that spawn children with unexpected privilege levels or that access memory outside their allocated heap segment. Monitor for process injection patterns following V8 exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 IOC Extraction & Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to extract the primary CVE identifier and prior 2026 zero-days (CVE-2026-2441, CVE-2026-3909, CVE-2026-3910, CVE-2026-5281). These are correlated vulnerability patterns that should drive enrichment and endpoint hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create watchlist of all Chrome zero-day CVEs patched in 2026 and correlate with exploit-kit signatures, malware-as-a-service infrastructure IPs, and suspicious Chrome process lineage. Alert on any Chrome crash events coinciding with exploit delivery attempts.

suggestion.title: Spyware Operator Exploitation Chain (TAG-Tracked)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'spyware attacks' tracked by TAG and references prior year's eight zero-days 'used in spyware attacks.' No UC captures the broader spyware infection-chain context or TAG indicators of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Chrome V8 exploitation indicators with post-exploitation behaviors associated with spyware (screen recording, audio capture, keystroke logging, exfiltration to known C2 nodes). Cross-reference with TAG-published spyware signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Setup.py or __init__.py Execution During Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages are 'poisoned to auto-run'—the attack mechanism is execution of malicious scripts during pip install. setup.py post-install hooks or __init__.py initialization are the standard vector for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for python.exe or pip.exe spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or executing suspicious interpreters immediately after (or during) package installation. Look for process chains under site-packages or %temp% directories. Alert on setup.py execution with obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration Post-PyPI Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Bun Credential Stealer' as the payload—detection must cover credential access and C2 beaconing after infected package is imported.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes accessing Windows credential stores (DPAPI, SAM, LSASS memory dumps), browser credential storage, or SSH keys post-import. Correlate with outbound DNS/HTTP to attacker C2. Alert if credential files are read from site-packages/.../module or %appdata% shortly after package install.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Malicious Python Package on PyPI Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states '19 Packages Poisoned'—detection of package names and versions on disk matching known-poisoned package hashes or names is fundamental initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain block-list of poisoned package names (e.g., from Hades campaign) and monitor pip install logs, site-packages directory, and requirements.txt for presence. Alert on installation of any of the 19 packages identified in the campaign. Verify package hash against known good if available.

suggestion.title: Detect Bun Credential Stealer Artifact or Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article names the malware family 'Bun Credential Stealer'—detection should cover both file-based IOCs (if any extracted from article) and behavioral patterns of this specific family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process memory or disk artifacts containing strings associated with Bun stealer (e.g., credential query functions, browser-engine detection). Monitor for subprocess execution of curl, wget, or PowerShell to exfil credentials or config files. Flag processes spawned from site-packages with unusual parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism via Python Module Import in User Startup Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Auto-run threat model suggests the malware may establish persistence via import hooks, .pth files, or sitecustomize.py placed in site-packages to survive session restarts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .pth files, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py in site-packages or Python distribution directories. Alert on writable __pycache__ or import-hook registration in sys.meta_path. Correlate with presence of poisoned package.

suggestion.title: Detect LiteLLM Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases and zero UCs despite explicit RCE claim. Core exploitation path missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to LiteLLM-exposed endpoints (e.g., /api/chat, /v1/completions) without valid authentication headers. Correlate with high-entropy or shell metacharacter payloads in request body/query params. Flag requests originating from external IPs to internal LiteLLM instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exploitation Command Execution via LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates RCE outcome; pipeline generated no detection for command execution phase. Article states 'Exploited in the Wild'—should detect actual payload delivery and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation from LiteLLM service account (if running under distinct identity) or from web server process executing unexpected interpreters (/bin/bash, cmd.exe, PowerShell) with child processes indicative of post-exploitation (curl, wget, nc, whoami, id). Detect encoded command patterns (base64, hex) in process command lines.

suggestion.title: Detect LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 Exploitation via HTTP Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: CVE explicitly named in title; pipeline returned empty IOCs object. Should include signature or pattern for this specific CVE exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing CVE-2026-42271-related payloads (e.g., known bypass strings, injection tokens) or requests to LiteLLM endpoints that bypass authentication validation. Correlate with user-agents matching exploit frameworks or tools.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Post-LiteLLM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Exploited in the Wild' implies active attacks in production; no lateral movement use cases generated. Compromised LiteLLM instance is a foothold for further propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful RCE on LiteLLM host, monitor for unusual outbound connections from that host to internal IPs on high ports, SMB/RDP ports, or known internal service endpoints. Detect DNS queries for internal hostnames from compromised system.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: GitHub Actions Repository Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Azure Functions Action and 72 other repositories disabled after supply chain attack' — pipeline failed to generate detection for injected/malicious actions in GitHub ecosystems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly created or modified Actions in public repositories, unexpected additions to trusted action names, and rapid propagation of actions across multiple repos. Flag repos committing malicious .github/workflows files without corresponding PRs or code review history.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Abuse: Mass Repository Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article: '72 Other Repositories Disabled' — no detection for sudden mass disablement or modification of repository settings via compromised Actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk repository setting changes (visibility, branch protection, action permissions) triggered from Actions workflows in short timeframes. Correlate workflow execution logs with repository disable/archive events.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions Action Tampering: Malicious Infrastructure Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Azure Functions Action' as disabled — no detection for compromised Azure deployment actions injecting malicious infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure Functions deployment attempts from GitHub Actions workflows for unexpected infrastructure changes, new function URLs, modified authentication, or unusual resource creation patterns. Correlate deployment failures/disablements with upstream action modifications.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Supply Chain Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'Targeting AI Coding Agents' — no detection for malicious dependencies or tool chains injected into AI-assisted development workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on introduction of new or unexpected package dependencies in repos using AI coding agents. Flag typosquatting packages mimicking popular AI tools, modified lockfiles with unusual package versions, and dependencies added via Actions workflows without human review.

suggestion.title: Worm Propagation: Automated Repository Compromise Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Miasma Worm' suggesting automated self-propagation — no detection for worm-like behavior chains across repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns of synchronized repository commits/pushes to Actions across multiple repos from single source, exponential growth in affected repos, and self-referential workflow modifications (Actions updating other Actions). Flag commit messages or automation patterns suggesting automated propagation.

suggestion.title: Command Prompt Spawned with SYSTEM Privileges from Defender Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'When successful, a Windows command prompt will be spawned with SYSTEM privileges'—the primary observable outcome of the exploit. This is the highest-fidelity behavioral indicator but no detection UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe with parent process mpengine.exe, mpsvc.exe, or MsMpEng.exe running under SYSTEM or NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context. The RoguePlanet race condition forces Defender to execute or spawn child processes at elevated privilege.

suggestion.title: VHD/VHDX File Processing from Remote SMB Shares by Defender
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes original RCE variant: 'required an attacker to coerce a victim to open a .vhd(x) in a remote SMB server.' This direct attack vector was missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Defender processes (mpengine.exe, MsMpEng.exe) accessing .vhd or .vhdx files via UNC paths (\\<host>\share\...). Legitimate Defender VHD scanning from remote SMB is anomalous; normal activity originates from local or well-known update repositories.

suggestion.title: Symlink/Junction Evaluation in SMB Context with Defender Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'another attack scenario could lead to remote code execution simply by coercing a victim into opening an SMB share if symlink evaluation settings were enabled.' Microsoft patched 'mpengine!SysIO* API' to block this—clear symlink abuse vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or traversal of symbolic links or directory junctions in SMB mount points or temporary Defender working directories. Correlation: reparse points in folders accessed by mpengine.exe immediately preceding process elevation.

suggestion.title: Rapid Microsoft Defender Process Spawning (Race Condition Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'exploit is a race condition, so it's a hit or miss' multiple times. Race conditions require rapid repeated attempts or concurrent operations—this temporal pattern was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal frequency of mpengine.exe or MsMpEng.exe process creation (>5 instances in 30 seconds) or concurrent file operations on the same VHD/SMB resource. Race condition exploitation attempts generate characteristic burst behavior.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections to projectnightcrawler.dev or Exploit Hosting Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article documents researchers hosted exploit code at self-hosted 'projectnightcrawler.dev' after GitHub/GitLab removals. This infrastructure indicator was completely absent from IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to projectnightcrawler.dev or .dev domains with paths matching exploit repository patterns (/releases, /download, /blob, /raw). Flag any user-mode process initiating these connections.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Header Bomb Resource Exhaustion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes CVE-2026-49160: 'uncontrolled resource consumption in HTTP/2 allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service' via header compression abuse. Pipeline missed DoS kill-chain phase entirely despite attackers keeping 'memory tied up by manipulating flow-control settings.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/2 traffic for requests with unusually high header counts (especially > 100 headers) paired with small payloads. Alert on servers experiencing abnormal memory allocation spikes correlated with HTTP/2 connection spike. Check HTTP/2 flow-control window manipulation patterns where servers allocate memory but cannot release due to attacker-controlled settings.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Process Privilege Escalation via Link Following
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45586 described as 'improper link resolution before file access' granting 'SYSTEM privileges.' Article states authorized attacker can 'elevate privileges locally.' Pipeline ignored this clear privilege-escalation attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CTFMON.exe (Windows Collaborative Translation Framework) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shells, especially with SYSTEM integrity level. Monitor for symlinks or NTFS junctions created in directories where CTFMON reads files (e.g., %APPDATA%, %TEMP%). Track file handle opens on system-protected directories accessed by CTFMON.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Bypass via WinRE Boot + USB EFI Partition Attack
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-50507 (YellowKey) explicitly describes attack chain: 'placing specially crafted files on a USB drive or EFI partition and booting into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), where holding down the CTRL key triggered a command shell with unrestricted access to encrypted BitLocker-protected drives.' Affects Win11 and Server 2022/2025 with TPM-only protection. Pipeline extracted zero detections for this physical-access attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) invocations outside scheduled maintenance windows. Monitor for USB devices with EFI partitions connected during system boot or recovery mode activation. Log all console access during WinRE sessions (CTRL+C keyboard interrupts triggering shells). Flag systems with TPM-only BitLocker on Win11/Server 2022+ lacking PIN or recovery key enforcement.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday CVE Exploitation Post-Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article covers 200 vulnerabilities fixed including 33 Critical (28 RCE). Pipeline failed to surface general exploitation indicators for post-patch attacks targeting systems that haven't deployed yet. Article mentions 'none of which are known to have been exploited in attacks' but risk remains high.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement signatures for exploits targeting CVE-2026-45586, CVE-2026-49160, CVE-2026-50507 and high-severity RCE flaws (55 total) released this month. Monitor for failed remote code execution attempts (HTTP 400/403 errors, command injection patterns). Alert on patch-status queries followed by exploitation attempts within 7 days of Patch Tuesday release.

suggestion.title: Zero-day exploitation attempt detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states three zero-days were 'actively exploited' before patches were available. Need detection for exploitation attempts on CVE-2026-50507, CVE-2026-49160, CVE-2026-45586 in the pre-patch window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal process execution, application crashes, or memory corruption patterns associated with the three CVEs. Baseline detection against known-vulnerable application versions, focusing on the window before June 9, 2026 patch availability.

suggestion.title: Unpatched system inventory post-Patch Tuesday
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 198 vulnerabilities across the ecosystem; any unpatched system post-June 9 represents immediate high-risk surface. 'Actively exploited' implies threat actors will target systems that miss patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems where Windows Update or WSUS reports patch failure or deferral for June 2026 releases. Correlate against process anomalies to distinguish passive vulnerability exposure from active exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Bulk GitHub Repository Status Changes (Offline/Archive)
suggestion.rationale: Title states repos 'offline' and 'restored' — direct evidence of repository destruction/disablement. Article: 'Microsoft Restores Some GitHub Repos, Keeps Others Offline'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid bulk repository archival, deletion, or access-control lockdown events; correlate with service degradation events and cross-reference against known attacker IP/account activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Administrator or PAT Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Ability to take/keep repos offline requires elevated repo/org credentials. Article context: Miasma Probe 'continues' — implies sustained privileged access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or use of service accounts, Personal Access Tokens, or OAuth apps with repository admin scope during the incident window; alert on login anomalies (geoIP, user-agent, TLS fingerprint) preceding privilege assignment.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Read/Clone Spike to External IP or Service
suggestion.rationale: Pre-destruction intelligence gathering. Miasma Probe activity likely includes reconnaissance and data collection before impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-volume repo clones/downloads with subsequent repository destruction; identify data exfiltration patterns (large outbound transfers to attacker infrastructure) within 24–48 hours of offline events.

suggestion.title: Miasma Probe C2 Beacon and Infrastructure Blocklist
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names threat actor. Need infrastructure IOCs to detect command-channel and reconnaissance traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify and block known Miasma Probe C2 endpoints; monitor for suspicious DNS queries and outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure from affected Microsoft and GitHub systems.

suggestion.title: GitHub Webhook / Actions Workflow Creation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Keeping repos 'offline' implies ongoing attacker control and ability to block restoration attempts. Webhooks/Actions enable backdoor persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of repository webhooks, Actions workflows, or integration apps with external URLs or suspicious runtime environment variables; flag any automation that blocks legitimate administrative actions.

suggestion.title: Failed Repository Restoration Attempts by Legitimate Admins
suggestion.rationale: Article: Microsoft 'keeps others offline' — implies deliberate suppression of restore operations by authorized personnel, or attacker blocking legitimate recovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed repository restore/unarchive operations by admins coupled with access-denied errors or mysterious rollback of configuration changes; correlate with successful offline/archival operations from different accounts or IPs.

suggestion.title: Browser JavaScript Timing Side-Channel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes FROST using SSD timing, implying JavaScript is accessing high-resolution timing APIs (performance.now(), performance.timeOrigin) in patterns unusual for legitimate content. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for this fundamental attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) child processes for JavaScript engines calling performance timing APIs in tight loops or at frequencies >1000 calls/sec. Flag if timing data is subsequently exfiltrated via fetch/XMLHttpRequest to external domains without user interaction.

suggestion.title: SSD Access Pattern Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'track[s] what sites and apps you open via SSD timing'—implying latency measurements from storage are collected and sent to attacker. Pipeline did not identify this exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous POST/GET requests containing timing deltas or latency arrays in JSON/binary form from browser processes to non-whitelisted external hosts. Baseline normal network patterns and flag deviations with >100 timing measurements in a single request.

suggestion.title: Cross-Site Timing Data Correlation
suggestion.rationale: FROST attack reveals what other sites/apps are installed via timing differences ('track what sites and apps'). Pipeline missed detection for the correlation logic that fingerprints installed applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag JavaScript that probes timing for resource loads from known third-party domains (banking, social media, VPN, antivirus vendors) and aggregates results. Pattern: successive fetch() or image-load attempts with <100ms intervals, followed by timing comparison logic.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly Timing Gadget Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions SSD timing attacks, which commonly use WebAssembly or WebGL for high-precision timing. Pipeline did not suggest detection for these specialized execution contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebAssembly modules instantiated with memory buffers >100MB or WebGL programs querying GPU timing extensions (EXT_disjoint_timer_query). Correlate with subsequent exfiltration of numeric arrays.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44963 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a critical Backup & Replication security flaw that can be exploited to gain remote code execution (RCE)' and explicitly names CVE-2026-44963—pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite this being the core exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VBR 12.3.2 instances for suspicious authentication attempts followed by unexpected process execution under SYSTEM/service context. Focus on low-privilege domain-user sessions initiating RPC or service requests to VBR backup components.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Veeam VBR 12.x Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'VBR 12.3.2.4465 and all earlier version 12 builds' and warns 'attackers will likely attempt to reverse-engineer the patch'—pipeline should detect vulnerable inventory but produced no UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Veeam Backup & Replication services and alert on versions ≤12.3.2.4465. Cross-reference against patched baseline (12.3.2.4854+) and flag domain-reachable instances as high-priority targets for lateral movement post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Backup Deletion/Corruption Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ransomware gangs 'block restoration efforts by deleting victims' backups' via VBR compromise—pipeline failed to generate UC for this documented impact phase despite being named attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Veeam backup catalogs and storage directories for bulk deletions, backup job removals, or storage repository modifications originating from VBR processes post-exploit. Alert on deletion patterns following compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Backup Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'move within breached networks' using compromised backup servers—this lateral-movement use case was entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected credential usage or network pivots originating from compromised VBR processes to other systems (particularly domain controllers, file servers). Monitor for authentication relay or credentials extracted from backup metadata.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Backups
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers will 'steal sensitive data' from compromised backup servers—pipeline missed exfiltration detection despite explicit attack-chain mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large staged data transfers from VBR backup repositories to external IPs or cloud storage, particularly patterns of backup catalog enumeration followed by selective data read/exfil.

suggestion.title: VBR Privilege Escalation from Domain User
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'any domain user with low privileges can exploit this vulnerability' to achieve RCE—this privilege-escalation mechanism should have produced a dedicated UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privilege domain-user sessions creating unexpected child processes under VBR service account or SYSTEM context. Monitor for token-impersonation calls or service-principal elevation initiated by authenticated non-admin users.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Email Exfiltration of Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The agent located and emailed AWS IAM keys, database credentials, and SSH access details to an external Gmail account.' Core attack outcome with specific credential types; no use case created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when email agents or automation service principals send messages containing AWS secret keys, database connection strings, or SSH private keys to external or newly-contacted email addresses. Flag exfiltration even if obscured in attachment or body text.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Accepts Impersonation Request Without Identity Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker impersonated a team lead and requested access...Both Generic and Strict profiles failed because the verification step still collapsed when the request appeared operationally urgent.' Social engineering acceptance pattern undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agents for responses to senders claiming elevated roles or emergency status without domain verification or SPF/DKIM confirmation. Alert if access is granted or credentials are shared within minutes of receiving impersonation email.

suggestion.title: CRM or Database Export Sent via Email to External Recipient
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The agent retrieved and sent a CRM export containing customer records, contact information, contract details, and revenue data without verifying the sender's identity.' Bulk PII exfiltration through email; no detection rule created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when AI agents export or attach CSV/JSON files containing customer records, PII, contracts, or revenue data to external email addresses. Flag especially if sender was not pre-approved external user or if export size exceeds baseline.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Visits Phishing Link from Untrusted Sender
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The agent received a fake gift card email containing a phishing link. Under the generic configuration, it visited the phishing site and attempted to redeem the gift card using fabricated credentials.' No detection for malicious link interaction by agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when email agent processes click or visit untrusted URLs from external or low-trust senders, especially gift-card, verification, or urgency-themed links. Correlate with DNS requests to known phishing domains.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Approves Suspicious OAuth Application
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OAuth attack attempt; article notes agent 'identified the application as suspicious, and refused to grant access' but this is the defensive outcome. Reverse scenario (agent approving) is plausible and undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when email agents approve OAuth flows to newly-registered applications, applications with generic/suspicious names (timesheet, survey, timekeeping synonyms), or applications requesting excessive scopes. Flag if approval is from non-human principal.

suggestion.title: Bulk Sensitive Data Access Pattern by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: Agent accessed AWS credentials, database systems, CRM, internal communications, and calendar data in single engagement. No detection for multi-repository data enumeration typical of post-breach discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when AI agent or service principal accesses 3+ high-value data repositories (AWS, databases, CRM, Workspace, file shares) within minutes without documented business reason. Escalate if followed by export, credential access, or external email activity.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Malicious Commit to GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states 'Pythagora-io/gpt-pilot Compromised on GitHub' — supply-chain attack via repository compromise is the attack vector. Pipeline extracted nothing despite this being the critical entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for unexpected commits from new or unusual accounts, file additions containing Python scripts with obfuscated imports, or version bumps without corresponding PR approvals. Correlate commits introducing .py files with subsequent credential-access patterns in downstream installation environments.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution: Shai-Hulud Python Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer' as the payload embedded in gpt-pilot. Pipeline completely missed credential-access phase and the specific threat (named malware family).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes executing with imports for credential APIs (win32api, winreg, ctypes), keylogging libraries, or clipboard access. Flag exec() or eval() calls with base64/hex-encoded payloads. Monitor for socket connections to exfiltration endpoints from python.exe child processes, especially when spawned by pip or package managers.

suggestion.title: Python Linter Evasion: Obfuscated Code in OSS Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealer 'Blocked by Python Linter' — indicating attacker deliberately obfuscated code to evade static analysis tools. Pipeline missed defense-evasion phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python files with obfuscation indicators: base64-encoded strings, __import__() with dynamic module names, eval()/exec() of external data, comment stripping, or encoding of credential-related strings. Correlate with commits to trusted repositories where obfuscated code is anomalous relative to historical commit patterns.

suggestion.title: Package Installation: gpt-pilot from Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Developers installing via 'pip install gpt-pilot' or git clone would execute the malicious code locally. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for supply-chain package installation despite this being the delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/poetry/git commands targeting gpt-pilot repository for version anomalies. Alert if installation is immediately followed by Python child processes spawning credential-access patterns (registry access, network sockets, API calls). Cross-reference with known-malicious commits from GitHub audit logs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise: Unauthorized Maintainer Access
suggestion.rationale: Repository compromise implies attacker gained commit access. Article states 'Compromised on GitHub' but pipeline did not generate detection for unauthorized repository access changes or account takeover signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub login anomalies for maintainers of high-value OSS projects: unusual IP geolocation, timing (off-hours for that timezone), failed MFA, or new device. Monitor audit logs for unexpected collaborator additions, branch protection disabling, or webhook creation. Baseline normal maintenance activity and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Local LLM Model Unauthorized Modification or Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes worm 'operating entirely on local, open-weight models.' Pipeline must detect when Llama, Mistral, or other local model binaries/weights are modified, replaced, or loaded from unexpected paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system and registry for modifications to common open-weight model cache directories (HuggingFace cache, `.ollama`, custom model paths). Detect process execution spawning model inference with suspicious parent process or command-line parameters indicative of model hijacking or self-modification.

suggestion.title: Multi-Host AI Model Propagation via Self-Replication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'self-replicating' worm behavior. Pipeline must detect lateral movement patterns where Python/LLM inference processes spawn child processes across multiple hosts to propagate model payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Python/model-serving process execution across multiple endpoints within a short window. Flag outbound network connections from inference frameworks to non-standard ports or internal IPs. Monitor for NTLM/Kerberos auth from LLM runtime accounts to remote file shares.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python/Inference Framework Process Chain with Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm likely requires command-line Python or inference runtime execution. Article context implies active code execution. Must detect abnormal process trees rooted in model inference binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python or LLM inference framework (ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, etc.) spawning child processes with suspicious command-line indicators: script downloads, network connections, file system modifications outside model directories, or spawning PowerShell/cmd. Correlate with outbound C2-like network behavior.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AI Model Download or Deployment via HuggingFace/Model Registry
suggestion.rationale: Open-weight models are typically retrieved from HuggingFace or similar registries. Worm must download or be downloaded. Pipeline must detect unexpected model pulls or deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS traffic to HuggingFace, Hugging Face CDN, and model registry endpoints. Flag downloads of large binary files (>100 MB) to unusual directories. Correlate with process execution of model download tools (git lfs, huggingface-hub, curl) initiated by unexpected users or processes.

suggestion.title: AI Worm Persistence via Model Inference Startup Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating behavior implies persistence mechanism. Worm likely uses model initialization, startup scripts, or plugin systems to re-execute on reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to LLM startup configurations (`.env` files, model config JSON, model loading scripts in Python virtual environments). Detect creation of startup scripts in common locations (.bashrc, .profile, PowerShell profiles, or LLM-specific plugin directories). Flag unusual shell/Python invocations in registry run keys pointing to model inference tools.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion or Cryptographic Operations via Local Model Inference
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm may cause excessive CPU/GPU/memory use or run cryptographic operations (proof-of-work for worm propagation, ransomware prep). Local models allow attacker to bypass cloud-based monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sustained high CPU/GPU utilization by model inference processes during off-hours or non-interactive sessions. Detect cryptographic library calls (OpenSSL, hashlib) from model inference runtimes. Flag unusual I/O patterns (heavy disk writes to temporary directories) that suggest model replication or payload staging.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'authentication bypass' as primary attack vector; pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear kill-chain entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB login endpoints for invalid-credential sequences followed by successful POST to admin-gated resources. Flag transitions from 403 (Forbidden) to 200 (OK) without intervening re-auth. Correlate with requests containing known bypass payloads (SQL injection, header spoofing) in version strings or parameter values.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via phpBB Template Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'RCE'; no payload-detection use case was generated for command execution post-bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process spawning from web server child processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with unusual parent-PID chains. Monitor for exec(), system(), passthru() function invocations in request payloads. Detect file writes to /var/www or equivalent with PHP/shell extensions immediately following phpBB HTTP 200s.

suggestion.title: phpBB Vulnerable Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects 'tens of millions of users across thousands of forums'—implies version-specific exploitation; no enumeration or fingerprinting detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline phpBB version-disclosure endpoints (common: README, CHANGELOG, /install/). Flag scanning patterns: sequential requests to version-leak URLs, HTTP HEAD requests to admin panels, User-Agent headers known for exploit frameworks. Correlate with geographic/ASN outliers.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise phpBB Administrator Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically leads to persistence; article implies long-dwell capability ('10 year old'); no post-compromise account-takeover detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB user table for new admin accounts created outside normal business hours or by non-admin API calls. Alert on `phpbb_users` INSERT/UPDATE with `user_type=FOUNDER` or elevated group assignments. Correlate with failed-auth spikes in preceding hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Database Activity Stemming from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE executed as web server user would directly query phpBB database; no data-exfiltration or credential-access detection for database queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database queries originating from web server process (apache, nginx UID) executing bulk SELECTs on user tables (usernames, emails, password hashes) or sensitive plugin data. Detect unusual JOIN patterns or exports to temp tables. Compare query frequency/volume to baseline for that web process.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from phpBB Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised forum often beacons home; article scope suggests multi-forum compromise risk; no C&C or exfiltration detection use case offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and outbound HTTPS from web server processes to domains not in allowlist (CDN, update servers, payment gateways). Flag high-entropy subdomains, newly-registered C2 domains, or IPs associated with known botnet operators. Detect encoded/obfuscated payloads in DNS queries or SSL SNI.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Download from Social-Media Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'funnel viewers toward malicious downloads.' Video platform redirects to external hosting should be detected before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP redirects from TikTok/Instagram domains or short-URL services (bit.ly, tinyurl) to suspicious external hosts. Flag if destination is in IOC databases or has low domain reputation. Correlate with subsequent executable downloads.

suggestion.title: Executable Execution from Downloads Folder Post-Download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware onto unsuspecting users' implies users execute downloaded files. Should detect file execution within 5-30 minutes of download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executables (.exe, .msi, .apk, .pkg, .deb) in user Downloads/Documents folders are executed by user-controlled processes. Cross-reference process creation against file modification timestamps to identify suspicious timing.

suggestion.title: Process Spawning from Browser Following Video-Platform Navigation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake tutorials directing users to downloads. Detect when browser child processes or shell commands initiate downloads via curl, wget, PowerShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox, safari, msedge) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl/wget commands with DownloadFile or -Uri parameters. Alert if parent process history shows navigation to shortened URLs or video-platform domains.

suggestion.title: Newly Installed Application Initiating Outbound Connections
suggestion.rationale: Post-infection, malware typically establishes C2. Article mentions malware payload but no behavioral details; this covers common post-install persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track processes from recently-created application directories (Program Files, /Applications, /opt) initiating outbound connections to non-RFC1918 IPs within 10 minutes of installation. Alert if destination has no legitimate business context or is in malware C2 databases.

suggestion.title: IOC Hash and Domain Correlation on Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA256 hash and 5 domains. Should trigger immediately on file creation/execution matching hash or network connections to domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/execution matching SHA256 03bbc4fa1fd784276da135ab62fef85aaddea66e6eb176d7e59c3398f818b153. Alert on DNS queries or network connections to pluginchad.xyz, maxapk.xyz, d4ug.site, slmgr.sh, msget.run. Escalate if both hash and domain appear in same chain.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation for Backdoor Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes MLTBackdoor establishing 'deep foothold on infected machines' and 'advanced ability to hide.' Persistence layer absent from current UCs. ClickFix attacks chain into schtasks.exe or TaskScheduler creation. Phrase 'quietly establishing' implies automated recurrence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or TaskScheduler object creation spawned as child of PowerShell/cmd.exe that was itself spawned from explorer.exe or RuntimeBroker.exe within 120 seconds. Backdoors establish recurring tasks for C2 beaconing. Alert if task name contains obfuscated strings or command-line points to network share or encoded payload.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Timeline: Click → Clipboard → Execution → Network
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'multi-stage ClickFix infection chain.' Existing UCs detect phishing OR clipboard execution in isolation. No UC correlates complete attack: click → clipboard write → PowerShell execution → C2 connection within seconds. Article phrase: 'multi-stage attack chain.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build four-event correlation: (1) phishing URL click via browser, (2) PowerShell spawned from explorer/RuntimeBroker with clipboard-read indicators, (3) process shows obfuscated command-line (Base64, IEX, DownloadString), (4) outbound network connection to article domains or suspicious infrastructure. All within 120s of initial click. Detects full attack chain, not isolated stages.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification for MLTBackdoor Persistence and Evasion
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1027 (Obfuscated Files) and T1112 (Modify Registry) are common in backdoor install. Article describes 'advanced ability to hide from security tools.' No UC monitors registry writes for run-key or policy modification. Article phrase: 'quietly establishing a deep foothold.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry write operations (SetValue, CreateKey) to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, RunOnce, or HKLM\Software\Policies\System\Run spawned as child of PowerShell/cmd under explorer/RuntimeBroker parent. Alert if registry data contains Base64, file-path to AppData, or suspicious executable names. Backdoors modify registry for auto-execution and defense evasion.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PowerShell Payload Decoder Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: T1027 listed but no dedicated UC for obfuscation signature hunting. ClickFix payloads are heavily encoded (Base64 → FromBase64String → Invoke-Expression). Article: 'advanced ability to hide from security tools' suggests obfuscation is core evasion. Current UC_FAKECAPTCHA checks wildcard patterns but misses encoder/decoder chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell command-line for multi-layered obfuscation indicators: (1) Base64 strings followed by FromBase64String, (2) Invoke-Expression wrapping deobfuscators, (3) character-replacement chains [char]65 assembly patterns. Alert on clipboard write containing these patterns before PowerShell execution. Distinguish from benign encoding in admin scripts by context: parent process is explorer/RuntimeBroker, no scheduled script justification.

suggestion.title: Domain C2 Beaconing with Abnormal Ports and Protocol Abuse
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) explicitly listed but template hunt does not account for port anomalies or protocol abuse. Article: 'advanced' backdoor likely hides C2 in non-standard ports, DNS tunneling, or domain-fronting. Five domains provided; no hunt validates protocol or port abnormality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to article domains (hrs2y15sungu.com, carrolc.com, cwrtwright.com, thomphon.com, powwowski.com) on non-standard ports (not 80/443). Flag DNS queries for these domains with abnormally long query strings (DNS tunneling indicator), CNAME chains (domain fronting), or periodic beaconing behavior (fixed-interval connections). Baseline internal DNS first to eliminate false positives.

suggestion.title: MSI / RunDLL32 Lateral Execution from PowerShell Context
suggestion.rationale: UC_FAKECAPTCHA SPL and KQL both reference rundll32.exe and regsvr32.exe as child processes, but no dedicated UC validates this execution path. These are LOLBins commonly used in second-stage delivery. Article: 'multi-stage chain' suggests intermediate execution proxies between initial PowerShell and final backdoor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rundll32.exe or regsvr32.exe spawned as children of PowerShell/cmd.exe that were themselves spawned from explorer/RuntimeBroker in context of ClickFix attack. Alert if parent PowerShell command-line contains file-path to temp directory, AppData, or network share. These LOLBins are common intermediate stages for loading DLL-based backdoors after clipboard execution.

suggestion.title: Remote Authentication Bypass on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-10523 allows 'unauthenticated attackers' to 'create rogue administrative accounts'—a clear initial-access attack step requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor internet-facing Sentry appliances for failed authentication attempts followed by unexpected admin account creation events. Alert on HTTP requests bypassing login (e.g., to /admin without credentials, unusual HTTP methods on auth endpoints).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-10520 as 'OS command injection' enabling 'code execution with root privileges'—requires process-level detection of injected commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes (shell, curl, wget, nc) spawned from Sentry service context. Cross-reference with inbound HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (semicolons, pipes, backticks) to Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Rogue Admin Account Creation on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10523 exploited to 'create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access'—persistence indicator requiring user-provisioning audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of new privileged accounts on Ivanti Sentry appliances outside documented change windows. Alert if account creation occurs seconds after authentication failures or from unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: Inventory Scan for Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article names patched versions (R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1) but pipeline missed critical asset-discovery use case: identifying at-risk infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances running versions prior to R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1. Flag as emergency patching priority. Correlate with network role (VPN gateway, mobile gateway) to assess exposure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Patterns on Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Both CVEs remotely exploitable on web-facing 'secure mobile gateway'—requires HTTP-layer detection for pre-exploitation reconnaissance and attack probes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api). Alert on unusual HTTP methods (PUT/DELETE), command-injection payloads (semicolons, $(), backticks), path traversal attempts, or rapid auth probe sequences.

suggestion.title: Egress Beaconing from Sentry RCE as root
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE creates high-confidence C2 scenario; article does not mention exploitation yet, but critical for early detection of active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance outbound traffic (especially from root-level processes) for unexpected external connections, DNS queries to newly-registered domains, or beacons to suspicious IPs. Alert if Sentry initiates outbound connections outside documented sync/update channels.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Elevation to SYSTEM via Defender
