suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states vulnerability 'Grants SYSTEM Access'—core attack outcome that must be detectable. Pipeline missed privilege escalation from Defender context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with SYSTEM context sourced from Defender processes (DefenderService.exe, MpCmdRun.exe, MsSecurityScanner.exe). Alert on unexpected parent-child relationships or unusual elevation chains. Correlate with process tokens to detect impersonation or token theft.

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Service Abuse for Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is embedded in Defender itself; title indicates exploitation path through Defender service. Detection for service-abuse execution is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious command execution via Defender service processes (MpCmdRun.exe with unexpected arguments, NisSvc.exe spawning child processes). Monitor for Defender service imagepath modification or suspicious registry values under Defender service HKLM paths. Flag environment variable manipulation in service execution context.

suggestion.title: Defense Mechanism Impairment—Defender Service Disruption
suggestion.rationale: Defender zero-day may manifest as service crash, restart loop, or failure—direct defense-evasion indicator that pipeline did not capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Microsoft Defender service processes (DefenderService, NisSvc, MpCmdRun) for unexpected termination, exit codes indicating crash, or rapid restart loops. Detect gaps in Defender telemetry collection following process termination. Alert on service binary replacement or imagepath modification.

suggestion.title: RoguePlanet Vulnerability Exploitation Signature
suggestion.rationale: Title names the vulnerability 'RoguePlanet'—a specific exploit identifier that should appear in artifact detection. Pipeline extracted no signatures or payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create detection for RoguePlanet-specific exploitation patterns: file artifacts with RoguePlanet references in name/metadata, process arguments containing version-detection patterns or exploit techniques, or known gadget chains invoking Defender vulnerability. Baseline against CVE identifier once disclosed.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Defender Version Inventory and Patching Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Updated Windows' with Defender vulnerability—implies version-specific exposure. Pipeline should identify and track vulnerable installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for Microsoft Defender versions affected by RoguePlanet (specific version range to be confirmed from CVE disclosure). Flag endpoints not applying patches within remediation SLA. Correlate inventory gaps with observed exploitation telemetry.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Microsoft RCE Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'critical RCE bugs'—this is a direct attack vector that should trigger execution-phase detection rules. Pipeline missed primary threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on exploitation patterns: unusual child processes from vulnerable services (w3wp.exe, Exchange worker processes), suspicious DLL injection into LSASS, or code execution from network shares. Look for parent-child process chains: vulnerable service → cmd.exe/powershell.exe.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Vulnerable Microsoft Software Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on 'Microsoft Patches Record 206 Flaws'—inventory detection for unpatched versions is foundational. No software version detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag machines running unpatched Microsoft products (Windows, Exchange, Office, SQL Server) by comparing software version inventory against published CVEs and KB articles. High-confidence vulnerability signal.

suggestion.title: Web Service Process Anomalous Behavior
suggestion.rationale: RCE bugs in IIS/Exchange imply code execution in service context. Pipeline extracted no detection logic for vulnerable service exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe, MSExchangeUMWorkerProcess.exe for spawned cmd/PowerShell, file writes to system directories, network connections from service account context. These should have minimal interactive process behavior under normal operations.

suggestion.title: Mass Scanning for Microsoft Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Three zero-days indicate high-profile targeting and likely scanning precursors. Pipeline should flag reconnaissance activity preceding exploitation of these surfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid connection attempts to Microsoft service ports (Exchange 443, IIS 80/443, RDP 3389) from single source, especially when followed by exploitation indicators or matching known CVE scanner signatures.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Post-RCE Activity
suggestion.rationale: RCE bugs lead to shell/PowerShell execution; article implies code execution capability but pipeline generated no post-exploitation monitoring rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encoded PowerShell, registry access patterns (credential enumeration), process discovery cmdlets, or network outbound from cmd/PowerShell spawned by vulnerable service processes. Focus on unusual working directories, temp execution, suspicious parent-child chains.

suggestion.title: AWS CloudTrail Disablement or Event Selector Narrowing
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords explicitly reference 'AWS CloudTrail' and 'defense evasion.' Attackers call StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or PutEventSelectors to blind audit trails. Pipeline missed core attack vector despite clear keyword signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on StopLogging, DeleteTrail, UpdateTrail, or PutEventSelectors API calls from non-administrative IAM principals or outside maintenance windows. Flag multiple logging-service API modifications within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: GCP Log Sink Deletion or Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'Google Cloud' and 'log router.' Attackers delete or redirect logging sinks (google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteLogSink, UpdateLogSink) to prevent exfiltration detection. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DeleteLogSink and UpdateLogSink operations. Alert if sinks exporting to external SIEM or buckets are deleted within 24 hours of suspicious activity (exfiltration, privilege escalation).

suggestion.title: S3 Access Logging Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly list 'S3' and 'log storage.' Attackers disable S3 access logging (PutBucketLogging with LoggingEnabled=false) to hide data exfiltration. Pipeline failed to surface this defense-evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PutBucketLogging operations that disable logging on S3 buckets. Correlate with prior s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject activity or data exfiltration indicators from the same principal.

suggestion.title: Logging Service Enumeration Followed by Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'abusing cloud logging services' as multi-step attack. Attackers enumerate available logging (DescribeTrails, ListLogSinks, GetBucketLogging) then disable. Pipeline missed this two-phase pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of logging discovery calls (DescribeTrails, ListLogSinks, GetLoggingStatus) followed within 15 minutes by disablement calls (StopLogging, DeleteLogSink, PutBucketLogging with logging disabled).

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Organization Trail Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article on cloud logging defense evasion should detect attacks on organization-wide trails. Attackers target organization trails (organization:StopOrganizationTrail, organization:DeleteOrganizationTrail) to hide multi-account activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on organization-level CloudTrail modifications (StopOrganizationTrail, DeleteOrganizationTrail, PutOrganizationEventSelectors) from non-management-account principals. These indicate lateral movement to hide org-wide compromise.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 V8 Exploit Detection – Process & Memory Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Chrome V8 Zero-Day CVE-2026-11645 Exploited in the Wild' explicitly identifies the vulnerability and active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting exploitation attempts or post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome/Chromium processes with abnormal command-line arguments, unexpected child processes, or V8-related crashes. Detect rapid memory allocation/deallocation patterns or JIT compilation anomalies. Correlate with unpatched Chrome inventory and follow-on sandbox-escape indicators.

suggestion.title: Browser Sandbox Escape Post-V8 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploited in the wild' — active exploitation of render-engine zero-days typically chains to privilege escalation/sandbox bypass. Pipeline missed privilege-escalation phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes spawning system binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, reg.exe) or accessing protected OS resources without expected parent-child relationships. Monitor for explorer.exe or svchost.exe launched from chrome.exe context.

suggestion.title: Malicious Drive-by or Watering-Hole Delivery Vector
suggestion.rationale: Browser zero-days 'in the wild' are deployed via drive-by or site compromise. Article implies active campaigns but pipeline reconstructed no initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network requests to infrastructure hosting V8 exploits (if identified post-analysis). Detect suspicious HTML/JavaScript downloads, malformed iframes, or malvertising campaigns. Correlate web traffic with exploit-timing indicators (crashes, sandbox anomalies) within seconds of page load.

suggestion.title: Chrome Version Rollback or Disabled Auto-Updates
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls for patching ('Patch Now'). Attackers and defenders race to patch/bypass; no detection recommended for update-evasion or persistence-via-downgrade.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome version downgrades post-CVE announcement, disabled auto-update services, or Group Policy overrides preventing patching. Flag organizations with unpatched Chrome inventory >7 days post-announcement.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape enables lateral movement; 'exploited in the wild' implies campaigns beyond single-host impact. Pipeline generated no lateral-movement or impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser-spawned processes creating network connections to internal resources, SMB shares, or lateral-movement tools (PsExec, WinRM). Detect browser context accessing credential-storage paths (LSASS, SAM, credential manager).

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-50751 Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw...to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' Direct initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful VPN session establishment on Check Point Remote Access/Mobile Access gateways where preceding authentication events show failure or absence of credential validation. Alert on any IKEv1 connections lacking valid machine certificate validation, especially from legacy remote access clients. Correlate session IP/timestamp with known attack windows (May 7 onwards).

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Deprecated Protocol Usage on Check Point Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'The vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' and recommends 'configure...Remote Access VPN Authentication to IKEv2 only.' IKEv1 is the vulnerability prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Check Point Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN deployments; flag any still using IKEv1. Alert on any legacy remote access client IKEv1 connections to vulnerable gateways. Correlate with failed/missing authentication steps to detect exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Qilin Post-VPN Lateral Movement & Ransomware Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms: 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' and Qilin has '400+ victims on its dark web leak site since August 2022.' Post-access behavior is critical for breach containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting anomalous VPN access or CVE-2026-50751 indicators, monitor for rapid credential enumeration, network share enumeration, backup system discovery, and mass file access patterns consistent with Qilin pre-encryption reconnaissance (file servers, NAS, backup appliances).

suggestion.title: Absence of Mandatory Machine Certificate on Check Point VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate for connections' as a vulnerability precondition. This configuration gap enables the bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Check Point gateway configurations for any that do not enforce machine certificate authentication. Alert on configuration changes that disable or weaken certificate requirements, particularly on IKEv1-enabled gateways. Escalate if disabled after May 7, 2026.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Connections to Check Point VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'accept legacy Remote Access clients' as vulnerability condition and mitigation is to 'remove support for the legacy remote access client.' Legacy clients are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any legacy remote access client versions connecting to Check Point VPN gateways, especially on IKEv1-enabled endpoints. Flag connections lacking proper authentication context. Correlate legacy client usage with CVE-2026-50751 exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Data Staging & Exfiltration Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Qilin RaaS operation maintains dark web leak site; post-compromise activity includes data exfiltration before encryption. Article indicates 'few dozen targeted organizations globally' have been compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound data transfers immediately after VPN compromise detection. Alert on file compression/staging operations on accessible shares (ZIP, RAR, 7z creation in bulk). Detect DNS queries and connections to known Qilin C2 or data-staging infrastructure (correlate with public Qilin IOC lists).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Chromium V8 Browser Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal agencies must remediate CVE-2026-11645 by 2026-06-23 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline failed to generate asset-exposure UC for unpatched Chrome, Edge, Opera instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for browser processes (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, opera.exe) running versions below the patched threshold for CVE-2026-11645. Correlate with endpoint management scans to identify unpatched instances across the fleet. Alert on execution of vulnerable versions 48+ hours post-patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTML Delivery and Browser Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation vector: 'via a crafted HTML page.' Pipeline should detect delivery of malicious HTML payloads to vulnerable browsers, the primary exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses containing suspicious HTML payloads served to vulnerable browser versions, particularly with unusual script tags, memory manipulation code, or obfuscated JavaScript. Correlate with browser crashes, sandbox violations, or abnormal child process creation.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Bounds Memory Access in Browser Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability.' Pipeline should detect memory corruption indicators characteristic of this CVE's exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag browser renderer processes with access violations (0xc0000374 or similar), out-of-bounds memory patterns, or abnormal memory allocation behavior. Correlate Windows Event Logs and crash dumps with vulnerable browser execution following HTML page rendering.

suggestion.title: Cisco vManage Asset Exposure and Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager' — basic asset exposure hunt missing entirely. Recommended hunts section explicitly references 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' for asset-exposure pattern, yet pipeline produced zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (vManage) instances via port discovery (443, 8443), banner grabbing, TLS certificate inspection, or vulnerability scanner output. Establish complete inventory of vManage appliances in network scope to prioritize patching.

suggestion.title: Cisco vManage Patch Compliance and Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies vulnerable versions exist but does not enumerate them — version-based detection missing entirely. Federal patch deadline 2026-06-23 emphasizes inventory urgency; article states 'patch lag is the silent killer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20245 detections on Cisco vManage appliances. Cross-reference inventory against vendor patch status. Alert on any vManage systems not patched by 2026-06-23 federal deadline. Monitor patch management system for compliance.

suggestion.title: Authentication Followed by Privilege Escalation on vManage
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, local attacker' and 'execute arbitrary commands as root' — authentication + privilege escalation is the core attack pathway but completely missing from kill chain and detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage authentication logs for successful logins followed by unexpected privilege escalation to root. Alert on root elevation without corresponding legitimate administrative action. Detect session privilege-escalation patterns inconsistent with normal administrative workflows.

suggestion.title: Crafted File Upload and Command Injection Detection on vManage
suggestion.rationale: Article attack vector is explicitly 'supplying a crafted file to the affected system' — this is the attack primitive but completely absent from generated use cases. Vulnerability class is 'improper encoding or escaping' indicating payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage file upload endpoints (configuration imports, device templates, policy uploads) for suspicious submissions. Detect filenames or file content containing special characters, escape sequences, or encoding tricks suggesting injection. Correlate file uploads with subsequent unexpected process execution.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Post-Authentication on vManage
suggestion.rationale: Article's explicit impact statement is 'execute arbitrary commands as root' — this is the culmination and highest-confidence detection signal but completely missing from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell execution (bash, sh, python) running under root context on vManage appliances. Detect unexpected process spawning post-authentication from non-system accounts. Flag root command execution without corresponding legitimate administrative activity or scheduled tasks.

suggestion.title: Detect Arista EOS Devices Vulnerable to CVE-2026-7473
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE-2026-7473 as substitution parameter; CISA KEV status means active exploitation in the wild with 2026-06-23 federal patch deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Arista EOS devices running vulnerable versions of the OS. Cross-reference with network exposure data to identify externally-facing instances; compare patch status against federal due date.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Tunneled Packet Processing on Arista Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific attack mechanism: 'incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet'; requires network-level detection of decapsulation failures or packet handling anomalies on compromised devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS syslog and packet capture for decapsulation errors, tunnel processing failures, or unexpected packet forwarding to non-whitelisted tunnel endpoints. Alert on rapid increases in tunneled traffic volume or traffic to anomalous destinations.

suggestion.title: Alert on Arista EOS Decapsulation Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation depends on tunnel decapsulation configuration; unauthorized modifications to tunnel IP addresses or forwarding policies represent attack preparation or configuration tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any changes to Arista EOS tunnel decapsulation IP addresses, tunnel endpoint whitelists, or forwarding policies. Correlate configuration changes with subsequent network anomalies or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Bulk Message Scraping from Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages' from one compromised education shard account, far exceeding normal user message access volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single account generates sustained message enumeration/read requests at 10x+ baseline rate for user's role. Baseline typical message access per user; flag sustained high-volume room enumeration, message exports, or archive bulk-reads from non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credentials in PowerShell—Credential Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director' as mechanism for obtaining platform access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan PowerShell execution logs and shared scripts for patterns indicating LDAP/service-account credential strings (uid=, password=, -Credential patterns). Cross-reference any discovered credentials against recent authentication events to identity compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Download via Media ID Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker noted 'every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token' and obtained files by extracting media IDs from messages, indicating broken access control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor direct media/file endpoint requests to Tchap CDN lacking valid session tokens or authorization headers. Alert on sequential bulk media ID requests (especially numeric patterns) or file downloads spanning multiple organizational shards from single source IP or account.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Targeted Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes entry: attacker 'social engineered a valid account on the education shard (matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr)' indicating targeted spearphishing of government personnel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account compromise through anomalous signin patterns: first-time login from new country/IP, off-hours access, logins from new device immediately before bulk data access, or historical atypical behavior. Correlate with subsequent mass message/file access from same account within hours.

suggestion.title: Systematic Account and Organizational Metadata Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'scraped...information on over 73,000 accounts, including email addresses, organization information, meeting links, and account and device metadata'—large-scale user enumeration and intelligence gathering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on accounts performing abnormally high-volume directory queries, org-structure enumeration, or metadata extraction. Establish baseline queries per user role; flag sustained rates >10x normal, especially when combined with device/meeting metadata access or cross-shard visibility.

suggestion.title: Cross-Shard Lateral Enumeration from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Attacker stated 'other shards will have more' when describing scope from education shard, indicating pivot capability across normally-isolated organizational partitions (Matrix federation shards).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single accounts accessing data/messaging from multiple organizational shards when architectural design segregates them. Flag rapid traversal across shards or access patterns inconsistent with user's assigned organizational unit.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to pheditor.php with shell metacharacters in 'dir' parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability as 'unsanitized dir parameter' accepting 'shell metacharacters' to 'completely bypass TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist'. This is the direct exploitation vector but generated zero detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP POST to pheditor.php where 'dir' parameter contains shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $(), newlines, >>, <<). Legitimate terminal operations use clean directory paths. Web proxy/WAF logs are most reliable source; application logs may not capture POST body.

suggestion.title: PHP-FPM/Apache process spawning unexpected children post-pheditor exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE achieved 'with web server privileges'. Successful exploitation flows POST request → command injection → process spawning under www-data/nginx/apache user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST timing to pheditor.php with immediate child process creation (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, python, perl) spawned by PHP process. Alert on process lineage: apache2/nginx/php-fpm → shell or network utility.

suggestion.title: Web shell persistence post-pheditor RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article shows attacker achieves 'full RCE' and 'web server privileges'—logical follow-on is persistence via .php file drop. Article body references UC_12_3 on PHP file creation in webroot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .php file creation/modification in /var/www/*, /srv/www/*, /usr/share/nginx/* by php/apache/nginx processes. Establish temporal correlation with prior pheditor POST requests.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: Asset exposure to pheditor instances running vulnerable code
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-48030 requires specific Pheditor version. Article mentions pheditor.php application but pipeline extracted no version info or patched-status hunting logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset hunt for web servers hosting pheditor.php endpoint (HTTP fingerprint, version headers, directory traversal to /pheditor.php). Cross-reference CVE-2026-48030 patch status against deployed versions.

suggestion.title: Known-Malicious PyPI Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states '19 Packages Poisoned.' Pipeline should surface all 19 package names as IOCs and detect their installation via pip logs or process creation. Article phrase: '19 Packages Poisoned to Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is 'pip.exe' or 'python.exe -m pip' installing any of the 19 identified poisoned packages by name. Trigger on pip install command with package name matching threat intel feed or article IOC list.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes packages that 'auto-run' code—indicating setup.py or import-time payload execution. Article phrase: 'Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer' indicates code executes without explicit invocation at install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation spawning immediately after 'pip install' or during Python package import phase. Flag process ancestry chains from python.exe → subprocess with unusual parent-child relationships, high entropy command lines, or network activity during setup scripts.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from Bun Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Attack specifically targets 'Bun Credential Stealer'—indicating the payload accesses Bun credential stores or authentication tokens. Article phrase: 'Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer' implies direct targeting of Bun's local credential storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file I/O operations targeting Bun credential storage directories (e.g., ~/.bun, ~/.bunfig.toml, or Bun cache paths) from processes spawned post-pip-install. Alert on process attempting to read Bun authentication tokens or configuration files containing credentials.

suggestion.title: Setup.py or Egg Metadata Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: PyPI packages execute code at install time via setup.py hooks. Article indicates packages 'auto-run'—typical mechanism is setup.py install scripts or entry_points that execute on import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor setup.py or egg_info script execution during pip install phases. Detect anomalous commands: network calls, file exfiltration, credential access, or spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) during the install-time hook execution window.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Post-Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies C2 communication to exfiltrate stolen Bun tokens. Attack likely culminates in outbound data movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file access to Bun credentials with subsequent outbound network connections from Python processes or their children. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with base64-encoded payloads, or unusual DNS queries from processes spawned during/after pip install.

suggestion.title: Bun-Specific Credential Store Access from Non-Bun Process
suggestion.rationale: Bun credentials should only be accessed by legitimate Bun processes. Any non-Bun process (Python, child procs) accessing Bun auth data is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of which processes legitimately access Bun credential stores. Flag any non-Bun, non-authorized process attempting to open/read Bun credential files or environment variables containing Bun tokens.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to LiteLLM Vulnerable Endpoint with CVE-2026-42271 Payload Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploited in the Wild, Chains to Unauthenticated RCE.' Indicates active wild exploitation; should detect HTTP requests targeting the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to LiteLLM services for requests matching known CVE-2026-42271 exploit signatures (malformed parameters, payload injection patterns). Baseline legitimate LiteLLM API calls and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from LiteLLM Service or Python Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'chains to Unauthenticated RCE.' RCE success results in command execution; detect unexpected subprocess creation (cmd.exe, powershell, bash) under LiteLLM process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/bash spawned by litellm service account or Python interpreter running LiteLLM. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes and flag first-time spawns.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from Compromised LiteLLM Host to Suspicious Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Title implies post-exploitation impact ('chains to RCE'); detect C2 beacons or data exfiltration from affected system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile normal egress from LiteLLM hosts. Alert on new connections to non-whitelisted IPs, high-entropy domains, or known malware C2 infrastructure. Monitor for data volume anomalies.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass or Missing Credential Checks in LiteLLM API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE'—vulnerability bypasses authentication. Detect requests that access protected endpoints without valid API keys or auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls to LiteLLM for missing authorization headers, invalid/expired tokens, or requests to authenticated endpoints from unauthenticated sources. Flag requests with common bypass patterns (header injection, path traversal).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Changes to LiteLLM Configuration or API Key Storage
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE followed by RCE execution may allow attacker to persist via config tampering or API key exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file modifications to LiteLLM config files, environment variable stores, and API key directories. Alert on writes by unexpected processes or service accounts. Track deletion/weakening of authentication controls.

suggestion.title: Unusual outbound data uploads to Meta domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'off-site business data' being sent to Meta for 'Feed and AI Personalization'—describes exfiltration of internal business data to external platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data transfers from internal business systems to Meta IP ranges or graph.instagram.com, instagram.com, facebook.com API endpoints. Baseline business-to-Meta traffic, alert on unusual payload sizes or frequency outside known sync windows.

suggestion.title: Configuration changes enabling third-party data collection
suggestion.rationale: Policy explicitly enables off-site data to be used for feed personalization—implies configuration or policy changes to data-sharing settings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on changes to data-sharing policies, API integrations, or business rules that grant external platforms access to customer/business data. Monitor for new integrations to Meta Business API or conversion tracking pixels being deployed.

suggestion.title: Meta Business Partner API authentication abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article references using 'off-site business data'—implies API authentication or integration credentials being used to pull data from business platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service account logins or API key usage tied to Meta integrations. Alert on unusual frequency of credential reuse, failed auth attempts before successful API calls, or credentials being used from unexpected geographies.

suggestion.title: Detection of data broker enrichment activities
suggestion.rationale: Article states Meta will use 'business data' from off-site sources—suggests data enrichment or third-party data aggregation from business intelligence brokers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound traffic to known data broker APIs (Databox, Segment, Mixpanel, etc.) that feed Meta. Baseline expected integrations, alert on new data broker connections or unusual volume.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions with Unexpected Permissions or Scope Elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'supply chain attack targeting AI Coding Agents' via 'Azure Functions Action'—compromised GitHub actions would require elevated permissions to disable 72 repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions execution with unexpected cloud provider integrations (Azure, AWS) or permission scope changes. Flag actions that modify repository state (disable, fork, transfer) outside of known CI/CD patterns. Correlate action execution timing with bulk repository changes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Disablement or State Modification in Single Session
suggestion.rationale: '72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack'—mass, coordinated repository operations are anomalous and warrant detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥10 repository state changes (archive, disable, delete, transfer) within 1 hour from single user/service account. Include disabled actions, branch protections removed, and collaborator removals. Correlate with supply chain monitoring tools.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution via Compromised AI Coding Agent Tools
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'targeting AI Coding Agents'—these agents execute code autonomously; detect injection of malicious payloads into their execution context or tool dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI coding agent execution (e.g., Copilot, Codex integrations in IDEs) for unexpected code generation output containing known malware signatures, C2 domains, or credential-theft patterns. Flag agent tool invocations with elevated privilege requests or shell escapes.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious Package/Action Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: 'Supply Chain Attack'—implying compromised dependencies; 'Azure Functions Action' is a GitHub Marketplace action, suggesting the attack vector was a malicious or hijacked action package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package resolution and GitHub action pulls for version mismatches, unexpected source changes, or pulls from fork/alternative registries. Alert on action re-pins or silent version downgrades. Correlate action publish events with subsequent repository disablement.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Azure Functions or Cloud Execution Contexts
suggestion.rationale: 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled'—suggests attacker gained control of Azure Functions execution, likely via compromised credentials or token exfiltration from the CI/CD pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure Functions authentication for unexpected service principals, bearer token usage, or cross-tenant access. Alert on function deployments from non-standard CI/CD runners or unrecognized GitHub Actions service identity. Correlate function execution timing with repository disablement events.

suggestion.title: Repository Access from Unusual Geographic or Network Locations
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often involve attacker reconnaissance; 72 repositories disablement suggests access from a single pivoted context, detectable via login geolocation or network anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repository access (push, admin actions, disable events) from IPs or geolocations inconsistent with known development teams. Monitor for rapid sequential repository enumeration followed by state modifications. Correlate GitHub login location with Azure authentication location.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM-Privileged Command Prompt Spawning from Microsoft Defender
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'When successful, a Windows command prompt will be spawned with SYSTEM privileges' via Defender race condition. This is the primary attack output and directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe (or powershell.exe) process creation with parent=mpengine.exe OR w3wp.exe AND token elevation to SYSTEM from non-SYSTEM parent. Add context: process name, parent image, user account, timestamp. Baseline Defender process children in your environment first to identify anomalies.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Operations on Microsoft Defender mpengine Temporary Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes race condition exploiting 'mpengine!SysIO*' API and 'Defender overwriting its own files'. This indicates detectable high-frequency file activity targeting Defender engine processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency file creation/deletion/modification in %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender, %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows Defender, and temp directories within 1-second windows. Correlate with mpengine.exe process handle events. Race conditions manifest as temporal clustering of conflicting file ops.

suggestion.title: VHD/VHDX Remote File Access Correlated with Defender Defensive Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article details original RCE vector: 'attacker to coerce a victim to open a .vhd(x) in a remote SMB server' which triggered Defender file operations leading to code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .vhd or .vhdx file opens from remote SMB paths (\\<host>\<share>\*.vhd*) immediately followed by elevated Defender process activity (mpengine spawning child processes, file system churn). Include SMB share source, file path, and downstream Defender behavior in alert context.

suggestion.title: Symlink/Junction Creation Followed by Microsoft Defender File System Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states Microsoft 'patching "mpengine!SysIO*" API, which blocked junction attacks' and mentions 'symlink evaluation settings were enabled' as attack precondition. This is a two-stage pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink or junction creation in user-writable paths (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%, user Desktop) immediately preceding mpengine.exe file operations on the same target directory. Flag if user context creating symlink differs from Defender service account. Include symlink target, link location, and Defender process tokens in alert.

suggestion.title: Application Allowlisting Policy Exceptions for Microsoft Defender Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Organizations using application allowlisting can prevent the exploit from executing.' Implies Defender process names or executables must be explicitly allowed—monitor for policy modifications or bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new application allowlist exceptions added for mpengine.exe, MsMpEng.exe, or Defender directories. Correlate with prior failed execution attempts or unusual Defender spawning. Check registry HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender for policy modifications by non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Defender Process Token Elevation via Impersonation or Capability Inheritance
suggestion.rationale: The exploit 'requires an attacker to coerce a victim' but results in SYSTEM-level cmd.exe, implying token impersonation or inherited capabilities from Defender service context during race condition window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with Impersonation Level = Delegation or System when parent is mpengine.exe or a user-context child of Defender. Include token changes (before/after elevation), parent process image path, and command line. Cross-check if process was launched from writable temp/user paths.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Bomb Memory Spike on HTTP.sys
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Uncontrolled resource consumption in HTTP/2 allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network…send very small amounts of data that force servers to allocate disproportionately large amounts of memory.' Directly correlatable to memory metrics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP.sys process memory consumption spikes (>50% increase in <5min) concurrent with small HTTP/2 payload volume. Flag if MaxHeadersCount registry not present or set below 100. Correlate memory spike timeline with HTTP/2 SYN_HEADERS flood patterns.

suggestion.title: Excessive HTTP/2 Request Headers Detection
suggestion.rationale: Patch note: 'MaxHeadersCount registry setting allows you to limit the number of headers included in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests.' Implies header count is the attack vector; absence of registry enforcement is a detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 requests with header count >200. Flag requests with small total payload (<10KB) but >150 headers. Baseline per environment; alert on 3-sigma deviation. Correlate multiple requests from single IP within 60s window.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Symlink Following Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Improper link resolution before file access (link following) in Windows Collaborative Translation Framework allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.' CVE-2026-45586 requires symlink creation + CTFMON execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symbolic link creation in System32\ctfmon paths or temporary directories, followed within 30s by CTFMON.exe spawning elevated child process (token elevation). Alert on symlinks targeting %SYSTEM32% followed by process with SYSTEM integrity level.

suggestion.title: WinRE Boot Detection + Command Shell Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article on YellowKey: 'specially crafted files on a USB drive or EFI partition and booting into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), where holding down the CTRL key triggered a command shell with unrestricted access to encrypted BitLocker-protected drives.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unscheduled WinRE boots (compare System event log startup sequence). Flag command shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawning within WinRE context. Correlate BitLocker unlock events without PIN/password prompts. Monitor USB/EFI partition access timing relative to WinRE boot.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Process Execution from Non-Standard Path
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45586 affects CTFMON.exe implementations lacking June 2026 patch. All CTFMON execution is post-compromise persistence risk if symlink vulnerability used.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal CTFMON.exe execution path (%System32%\ctfmon.exe). Alert on CTFMON spawned from user temp, %AppData%, or UNC paths. Flag CTFMON parent process as anything other than Explorer.exe, winlogon.exe, or services.exe. Monitor for CTFMON loading unusual DLLs.

suggestion.title: June 2026 Microsoft Patch Non-Compliance for RCE Flaws
suggestion.rationale: Article lists '55 Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities' in June 2026 Patch Tuesday. 28 of 33 Critical flaws are RCE. Inventory-based gap detection for unpatched systems (KB5094126, KB5094127, KB5093998) is baseline hygiene.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Windows 11/10/Server assets for missing June 2026 patches. Priority: systems with missing KB5094126 (Win11) or KB5094127 (Win10) exposed to 55 RCE, 28 of Critical severity. Escalate unpatched RCE-vulnerable systems in DMZ or external-facing segments within SLA.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Protocol Heap Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'heap-based buffer overflow in Remote Desktop Client' in CVE-2026-42985, CVE-2026-42992, CVE-2026-44799, CVE-2026-44801, CVE-2026-47289, CVE-2026-48563 allowing 'unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Six RDP RCE variants warrant coordinated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mstsc.exe process crashes, abnormal termination, or memory faults correlating with inbound RDP traffic. Monitor for RDP client spawning unusual child processes or attempting privilege escalation immediately post-connection.

suggestion.title: HTTP.sys Integer Overflow via Malformed Requests
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-47291 described as 'integer overflow or wraparound in Windows HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys)' exploitable by 'sending a specially crafted packet.' Requires detection of anomalous HTTP traffic structure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect http.sys process crashes or kernel faults correlating with HTTP requests containing oversized/negative Content-Length, malformed Range headers, or invalid TCP structures.

suggestion.title: Office Type Confusion via Email Preview Rendering
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45456, CVE-2026-45458, CVE-2026-47635 described as 'access of resources using an incompatible type in Office' exploitable 'via Outlook (classic) preview pane' when 'rendering emails' using 'Microsoft Word functionality.' Email delivery + Office rendering = distinct attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Outlook.exe and Word.exe for unexpected child process spawning, suspicious DLL loads, or code execution immediately following email preview operations. Detect crashes in Office rendering engines post-email ingestion.

suggestion.title: Windows Kernel Use-After-Free via TCP/IP Packets
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45657 is 'use after free vulnerability in Windows Kernel' where 'malicious network packets could trigger a flaw in how the Windows kernel processes certain TCP/IP data, potentially allowing the attacker to run code with system-level privileges.' Network-exploitable kernel flaw warrants low-level monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect kernel BugCheck/crash events correlating with inbound TCP/IP traffic containing malformed headers, invalid flags, or unusual fragmentation patterns preceding system-level code execution or SYSTEM privilege processes.

suggestion.title: Hyper-V Guest-to-Host Escape via File Operations
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45607, CVE-2026-45641, CVE-2026-47652 described as 'out-of-bounds reads' from 'authenticated attacker on guest VM sends specially crafted file operation requests to hardware resources within the VM which could result in remote code execution on the host server.' Guest escape vector requires guest-host interaction detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor guest VMs for file I/O operations targeting hardware resource paths. Correlate host SYSTEM privilege processes or kernel anomalies with preceding guest file operation anomalies or guest process crashes.

suggestion.title: DHCP Client Stack Buffer Overflow from Malformed Response
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-44815 is 'stack-based buffer overflow in Windows DHCP Client' allowing 'unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network' via 'specially crafted network traffic' from 'DHCP Server.' DHCP protocol-level exploitation requires payload structure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DHCP responses with oversized option fields, invalid structure, or payloads exceeding RFC limits. Monitor dhcp.exe for crashes, unexpected child processes, or system privilege escalation following address renewal cycles.

suggestion.title: Zero-day exploitation on unpatched Microsoft targets
suggestion.rationale: Article states zero-days were 'actively exploited or publicly known before a fix was available.' This indicates live exploitation in the wild. Detection should hunt for post-exploitation artifacts on systems running unpatched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution patterns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, svchost.exe anomalies) on systems with vulnerabilities CVE-2026-50507, CVE-2026-49160, or CVE-2026-45586. Cross-reference asset inventory to filter for unpatched targets in the 48-72 hours post-advisory window.

suggestion.title: Patch Tuesday non-compliance — critical Microsoft CVEs unpatched
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 3 zero-days actively exploited; presence of unpatched systems post-Patch Tuesday is a major risk indicator that should trigger compliance hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Windows endpoints with CVE-2026-50507, CVE-2026-49160, or CVE-2026-45586 present 5+ days post-June 9, 2026. Correlate with patch failure logs (WinEventLog System events showing update failures). Flag for remediation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance targeting vulnerable Microsoft products
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors discovering or probing for systems vulnerable to the 3 zero-days would exhibit scanning or enumeration behavior before exploitation. Article does not detail this but it is a pre-exploitation phase gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for abnormal network scanning or connection attempts from external IPs to ports/services associated with affected Microsoft products (e.g., Exchange, RDP, SMB) on systems known to have these vulnerabilities. Baseline against clean traffic.

suggestion.title: GitHub Bulk Repository State Change Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Microsoft 'Keeps Others Offline' — selective mass repository disablement indicating large-scale tampering that should trigger alerts on repo disable/delete bulk operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API audit logs for >5 repository disable/delete events within 1 hour by single service principal or user; correlate with unexpected privilege grants or new OAuth app approvals.

suggestion.title: GitHub PAT Creation and Malicious Scoping
suggestion.rationale: Repository breach suggests initial compromise via stolen or malicious PAT; need detection for overly-permissive token creation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new Personal Access Token creation with admin:repo_hook, delete_repo, or admin:org scope; flag tokens created by service accounts outside CI/CD pipelines; correlate creation with unusual geographic origin or time-of-day anomaly.

suggestion.title: GitHub Branch Protection Bypass / Disablement
suggestion.rationale: To selectively take repos offline or corrupt them, attacker must disable branch protection rules; article implies targeted repo compromise, not wholesale deletion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for branch protection rule modifications (dismiss reviews, allow force push, remove required status checks) on critical repos; flag if performed by non-standard CI/CD accounts.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Clone / Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Breach context suggests potential data exfiltration alongside availability impact; large-scale git operations should be baselined and anomalies surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk git clone/fetch operations by service accounts or over anomalous bandwidth; correlate source IPs against organizational whitelist; track repository size and frequency of operations.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth App Approval for Overly Broad Scopes
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of GitHub itself or insider access may involve OAuth app installation; monitor for suspicious app permissions requested by attacker.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag OAuth app installations requesting admin, delete_repo, or write:repo_hook scopes; correlate approver against user risk profile and review app publisher reputation against threat intel.

suggestion.title: Miasma Campaign IOC Enrichment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Miasma Probe' investigation but pipeline surfaced zero threat actor intelligence; should correlate with public ATT&CK, CISA, and vendor threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Miasma campaign against MITRE ATT&CK, CISA advisories, and vendor reports; surface associated C2 infrastructure, malware hashes, phishing domains, and GitHub attacker accounts; update incident response taxonomy.

suggestion.title: Storage Timing Side-Channel Measurement from JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: FROST 'exploit[s] SSD Timing' to infer application state. Detection must catch JavaScript profiling storage subsystem response times via high-resolution timers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser processes for sustained performance API calls (performance.now(), Date.now() in tight loops) bracketing local storage queries or file access. Establish baseline for legitimate JS I/O; alert on cyclical timing-measurement patterns consistent with side-channel reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin Application Presence Discovery via Timing Inference
suggestion.rationale: Attack goal stated: 'track what sites and apps you open.' Attacker enumerates user applications by timing resource/API availability from hostile origin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript from low-reputation or attacker-controlled origins probing for application presence by measuring response delays to requests for known app manifests, service-worker endpoints, or OAuth providers. Flag origins that test >5 distinct application targets in <1 minute.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Enumerated Application and Browsing Inventory
suggestion.rationale: After FROST reconnaissance phase infers open applications, attacker exfiltrates collected app/site list via network request. Phrase: 'track what sites and apps you open via SSD Timing.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from JavaScript origins to attacker infrastructure containing structured payloads encoding application names, URLs, or process identifiers (JSON arrays, base64-encoded lists, or custom binary formats). Correlate with prior enumeration activity from the same origin within session.

suggestion.title: Information Query from System via Local Storage Side-Channel
suggestion.rationale: FROST reads system state (presence of applications, recent user navigation) through indirect timing channels. This is T1005 applied to a side-channel context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated, rapid accesses to IndexedDB, LocalStorage, or browser cache from a single JavaScript origin, especially when access patterns show statistical correlation with application/site detection routines. Baseline normal application access and alert on suspicious query diversity.

suggestion.title: Android App Process Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'keep[s] showing ads in the background using multiple techniques'—background persistence is core to the attack. No use case generated for this behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or heavily obfuscated Android processes maintaining persistence across reboots, executing from non-standard directories, or registering for high-frequency broadcasts (SCREEN_ON, PACKAGE_REBOOT) to maintain background ad execution.

suggestion.title: Android System Setting Restriction Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'slip[s] past the built-in restrictions of the Android operating system.' Detection should focus on modification of Android security settings, but none was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for modifications to Android Settings database (settings.db, global, secure, system namespaces) that disable ad restrictions, notification shade restrictions, or overlay permissions; correlate with installation of suspicious APKs.

suggestion.title: Unusual Ad-Serving Network Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Core behavioral indicator: 'flooding infected devices with ads' requires outbound connections for ad delivery/C2. No network-based detection suggested despite clear command-and-control inference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP/HTTPS connections to ad-serving domains with high frequency, unusual user-agent strings, or encrypted payloads; correlate spike in ad-network traffic with known MagicAd SHA1 execution.

suggestion.title: Overlay Window Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Flooding with ads inherently requires drawing overlay windows on top of user UI. Article describes the attack method but no detection for overlay abuse was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW or SYSTEM_OVERLAY_WINDOW permission abuse; monitor for apps requesting TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY or similar; correlate with pop-up/ad rendering from background processes.

suggestion.title: Package Installation and Privilege Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Malware must discover installed packages and available APIs to inject ad content effectively. Article provides no detail, but this is a standard Android malware reconnaissance step that should be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of PackageManager or getInstalledPackages() calls; correlate with suspicious APK execution and subsequent overlay permission requests.

suggestion.title: VBR RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection (CVE-2026-44963)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'remote code execution (RCE) on domain-joined backup servers' and 'any domain user with low privileges can exploit this vulnerability.' No detection for exploitation attempts or suspicious RCE patterns on VBR processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Veeam Backup Service process (VeeamBroker.exe, VeeamAgent.exe) for spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or cscript.exe with suspicious command-line arguments. Alert on execution chains initiated by low-privilege domain user accounts accessing VBR admin endpoints. Baseline normal child process behaviors and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Domain User VBR Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authenticated domain user with low privileges can exploit this vulnerability' and vulnerability is specific to 'domain-joined backup servers.' Pipeline missed detection for privilege boundary violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication events showing low-privilege domain users accessing VBR administrative interfaces, API endpoints, or service accounts. Correlate with failed privilege escalation patterns. Track cross-forest or unexpected source IPs authenticating to VBR servers.

suggestion.title: Backup Store Deletion or Mass Modification Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states ransomware gangs 'target Veeam backup servers because this allows them to...block restoration efforts by deleting victims' backups.' No detection for backup data destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Veeam backup storage paths for bulk delete operations, truncations, or encryption events. Alert on Veeam service account or spawned processes (PowerShell, cmd) deleting .vbk, .vrb, or .vib files. Establish baseline backup maintenance patterns and flag anomalous deletion velocities.

suggestion.title: VBR Backup Configuration Tampering by Domain User
suggestion.rationale: Article describes domain users exploiting VBR for 'move within breached networks'—suggests lateral movement via backup configuration changes. No detection for suspicious config modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Veeam configuration files (Backup.cfg, agent registry hives) for unauthorized writes by non-admin domain accounts. Alert on VBR job creation, credential updates, or repository path changes initiated by low-privilege users. Log all VBR API calls and filter for config-modify operations by unexpected actors.

suggestion.title: Veeam Service Restart or Agent Injection Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability implies attacker gains code execution in Veeam context. Article warns 'attackers will likely attempt to reverse-engineer the patch to exploit unpatched deployments'—suggests post-exploitation persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected restarts of VeeamBroker.exe, VeeamAgent.exe, or Veeam Backup Service. Alert on DLL load anomalies in Veeam processes (unusual DLL search paths, unsigned DLLs). Establish and monitor white-list of expected service dependencies and plugin locations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44963 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'version 12.3.2.4465 and all earlier version 12 builds, fixed in version 12.3.2.4854.' Pipeline failed to extract version indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Veeam Backup & Replication version ≤ 12.3.2.4465. Correlate with network logs showing these systems receiving inbound traffic from untrusted networks. Flag any domain-joined VBR servers running vulnerable versions and initiate patch/isolation workflows.

suggestion.title: Email Agent Emitting Credentials to Unverified External Recipient
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'agent located and emailed AWS IAM keys, database credentials, and SSH access details to an external Gmail account.' This is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection. Pipeline generated zero use cases for credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email agents for outbound messages containing credential strings (AWS key patterns, database passwords, SSH keys, API tokens) sent to external or newly-added email recipients. Alert if sender of inbound credential request uses internal-looking display name but originates from external domain. Correlate with claims of operational urgency.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Export Exfiltrated via Email Without Sender Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'agent retrieved and sent a CRM export containing customer records, contact information, contract details, and revenue data without verifying the sender's identity.' No detection for data theft via false pretext.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large or sensitive data exports (CRM, customer lists, financial records) triggered by email requests from unverified senders. Alert if export is immediately followed by outbound email to external domain. Enforce multi-factor approval for customer data or financial exports regardless of sender claimed authority.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Following Phishing Link or Visiting Suspicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Under the generic configuration, it visited the phishing site and attempted to redeem the gift card using fabricated credentials.' Pipeline missed detection opportunity for agent URL visitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network activity from AI agent execution contexts for HTTP requests to newly-registered domains, domains flagged for phishing, or URLs with suspicious patterns (shortened links, homoglyph domains, credential-entry pages). Alert if agent account or host attempts credential submission on external domains, particularly from email attachments or links.

suggestion.title: Email Agent Granting Permissions to Unvetted OAuth Application
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OAuth scenario where agent 'inspected the OAuth flow, analyzed the destination, identified the application as suspicious, and refused to grant access.' This is detectable agent behavior that pipeline should flag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth authorization flows initiated from or approved by AI agent service accounts. Alert on grants of high-privilege scopes (Gmail full access, Drive broad permissions) to recently-registered applications or applications with typosquatting names. Block agent approval of OAuth flows without explicit human authorization.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Sending Email to New External Recipient Without Approval
suggestion.rationale: Article shows agent mailing credentials and sensitive exports to external Gmail accounts. Varonis recommendation: 'be prevented from emailing new external recipients without approval.' Pipeline generated no detection for this behavioral anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email agents for first-time communication to external domains or free email providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo). Require approval workflow before agent sends outbound email to previously-unknown external recipients. Alert if agent adds external domain to CC/BCC or forwards incoming email externally.

suggestion.title: Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer Payload Detection in Python
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes injection of named malware 'Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer' into public repository; no use cases generated for credential-stealer detection in Python source code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect imports of credential-stealing libraries (keyloggers, OAuth token harvesters, clipboard monitors) in Python commits. Alert on functions exfiltrating secrets to external domains within injected code payloads.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via GitHub Repository Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title and setup establish compromise of public gpt-pilot repository; no detection use case for unexpected or malicious commits to trusted repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits from unusual committers, commits merged without review, commits with obfuscated strings or suspicious imports (os.system, requests to external C2). Flag commits that introduce credential-theft patterns or evasion of linters.

suggestion.title: Python Linter Evasion Techniques in Malicious Code
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes payload was 'blocked by Python linter,' implying obfuscation or syntactic evasion attempts; no detection for linter-bypassing constructs in code analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect string encoding/decoding (base64, rot13, hex), dynamic code generation via eval/exec with obfuscated parameters, or inline hex/octal literals in Python that bypass static analysis. Flag constructs that bypass linter rules.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Injected Dependencies in gpt-pilot
suggestion.rationale: Shai-Hulud is explicitly a credential stealer; no detection use case for exfiltration channels (DNS, HTTP, HTTPS) used by injected malware to transmit stolen secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from gpt-pilot-dependent builds/deployments for connections to non-standard ports, unrecognized domains, or high-entropy POST payloads consistent with base64-encoded credential dumps.

suggestion.title: GitHub Commit Metadata Anomalies in Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes GitHub compromise; no detection for unusual commit signatures, timestamps, or author metadata that deviate from repository norms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits with forged or unexpected signatures, commits authored outside working hours, or commits that skip required branch protection rules (reviews, CI checks). Baseline repository commit patterns for deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Local Model Execution Burst
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes model operates 'entirely on local, open-weight models' and is 'self-replicating.' Detecting resource-intensive, repetitive model inferences spawned without user interaction is the primary behavioral signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid successive spawning of Python/LLM inference processes on local machines, especially those loading open-weight model weights (Llama, Mistral, etc.) without preceding user shell commands. Correlate with filesystem access to .safetensors, .bin, or .gguf model files and memory spikes consistent with inference workload.

suggestion.title: Model File Replication and Mutation
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm explicitly requires duplicating malicious payloads. Pipeline should detect filesystem activity: copying/modifying model weight files, creating new subdirectories to stage variants, or checksum mismatches in verified models.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mass filesystem writes to model directories (.cache/huggingface, .ollama, local model repos) that do not correspond to legitimate package manager downloads. Flag creation of shadow copies of model files with minor name mutations, or rapid in-place modifications to .safetensors/weight files outside of expected update windows.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Prompt Injection Targeting Local Models
suggestion.rationale: Worm operates via 'local, open-weight models'—likely via prompt injection or indirect command execution. Article describes self-replication implying automated prompt chains; detection should flag unusual prompt patterns requesting model self-modification or code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inference API calls and Python REPL logs for prompts requesting model weight exports, serialization, or code generation with executable intent. Flag iterative self-referential prompts (e.g., 'output your system prompt', 'generate a script that calls this model again') and prompts explicitly requesting replication or spreading logic.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Model Sandbox Escape
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating implies lateral movement from model context to OS. Pipeline should flag attempts to invoke system commands, network calls, or file I/O from within model inference or containerized model environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when model inference processes (Python, ollama, vLLM, etc.) spawn child processes outside their expected sandbox, make unexpected network connections, or request filesystem access beyond model directories. Flag subprocess calls to curl, wget, ssh, or PowerShell initiated from model execution context.

suggestion.title: Self-Replicating Process Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: 'Self-replicating' worm should exhibit process tree anomalies: a model inference process launching identical children, or recursive spawning patterns absent from legitimate model serving.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent-child process relationships where model inference binaries (python, node, etc.) spawn near-identical copies of themselves or invoke model loading commands recursively. Use entropy-based hashing to detect minor code mutations across generations. Flag scheduled task or cron creation by model processes attempting persistent re-execution.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'auth bypass' as core attack vector; no UC for detecting bypass attempts. Article phrase: 'Critical phpBB Vulnerability: Auth Bypass + RCE'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB login endpoints (/ucp.php, /login) for repeated authentication failures followed by success without credential re-entry, or successful authentication from IPs with no prior login history. Correlate with known phpBB authentication-bypass payload signatures in HTTP User-Agent, POST body, or URL parameters.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via phpBB Context
suggestion.rationale: Article claims RCE as second attack stage; no UC for detecting code execution post-bypass. Article phrase: 'RCE Since 2014'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process execution (php.exe, php-cgi) spawned from web server context (w3wp.exe, apache2, nginx worker) with unusual child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash). Flag successful HTTP requests to phpBB directories followed immediately by process creation or file writes outside normal application paths.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in phpBB Directory
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities typically lead to web shell deployment; no UC for post-exploitation persistence detection. Attack pattern implicit in 'critical vulnerability affecting tens of millions of users'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB installation directories (/forum, /phpbb, /includes, /cache) for new .php files created/modified outside normal update windows, especially with suspicious content patterns (eval, system, exec, passthru, assert). Correlate file writes with no corresponding HTTP upload traffic or unattended administrative access.

suggestion.title: Mass Scanning for Vulnerable phpBB Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'tens of millions across thousands of forums'—implies threat actors are likely fingerprinting and scanning for vulnerable installations. No UC for detecting reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to known phpBB version-detection endpoints (/common.php, /includes/version.php) or phpBB admin control panels from external IPs with no prior session history. Detect rapid probing of phpBB-related paths (10+ unique paths in <5 min from single source) indicative of automated scanning.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution from Web Root
suggestion.rationale: RCE+web-shell implies attacker will execute system commands; no UC for detecting command activity. Phrase: 'RCE' implies arbitrary code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web-server child processes (nginx, apache, w3wp) spawning interactive shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or executing common post-exploitation tools (curl, wget, nc, whoami, id, ifconfig). Flag process chains: httpd → bash → curl/wget (data exfil signature) or httpd → cmd.exe → net/whoami (recon).

suggestion.title: Unusual Database Access from phpBB Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass may grant attacker direct database manipulation; no UC for detecting lateral movement to database layer. Implicit in scope of 'critical vulnerability' affecting user data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs (MySQL, PostgreSQL) for connections originating from phpBB web-root context with abnormal query patterns: bulk SELECT from users table, ALTER TABLE statements, or queries from IPs/accounts not in baseline. Detect SQL injection signatures in application logs preceding database anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Download and Execution via Browser
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'funnel viewers toward malicious downloads' via fake tutorials. Pipeline missed T1204 family and execution detection. Article phrase: 'create polished, convincing videos that promise free access to popular premium software, then quietly funnel viewers toward malicious downloads.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser process initiating file downloads with execution-suspicious naming (free*, crack*, serial*, keygen*), followed by child process creation from Downloads/Temp directories. Flag if file lacks valid code signature or has suspicious publisher metadata.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Software Domain Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Domains like 'slmgr.sh' (mimics Windows licensing tool), 'msget.run' (mimics Microsoft), 'pluginchad.xyz' (masquerades as plugin provider) indicate T1036 masquerading technique entirely missed by pipeline. Article: 'create polished, convincing videos' establishing impersonation as core tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate domain resolutions matching software/vendor naming patterns (Microsoft, Windows, plugin, serial) with suspicious TLDs (.site, .run, .sh) against user browsing sessions from social media referrers.

suggestion.title: Social Media Phishing URL Redirect to Malware Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article's entire attack vector is 'TikTok and Instagram Reels' distribution. No T1566.003 phishing technique captured. Expected detection: URL shorteners from social platforms redirecting to malware domains. Article phrase: 'using fake software tutorials on TikTok and Instagram Reels to push malware.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP redirect chains originating from TikTok, Instagram, or their shortened-URL services (tiktok.com/@ video descriptions, Instagram story link previews) to any of the identified malware domains or suspicious .exe download hosts.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communications to Malware Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Domains tagged as C2 phase in article (d4ug.site, msget.run, etc.) require operational detection use case. T1071 identified but no detection guidance generated. Article phrase: implicit in infrastructure list 'funnel viewers toward malicious downloads.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound DNS queries and network connections from downloaded executables (especially from user-writable directories) to the identified domains, particularly from processes with no known legitimate software attribution.

suggestion.title: Downloaded Malware File Execution from User-Accessible Directories
suggestion.rationale: Attack relies on user downloading and executing files. No specific UC for suspicious file age + execution pattern. Article: 'malware onto unsuspecting users' + 'funnel viewers toward malicious downloads' establishes user as delivery mechanism.
