suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration during build phase requires detection of data leaving build environment. Article establishes exfiltration as primary payload; pipeline did not surface detection of bulk data transfer from CI/build systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-volume data transfers initiated from build systems or developer machines to external IPs during or immediately after dependency resolution. Baseline normal source-code size + dependencies; alert on multiples of baseline egress in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation Detection (Rust Registry)
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise requires detection at dependency ingestion point. Pipeline did not surface use case for identifying malicious or modified packages from crates.io or other Rust registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo manifest changes and crates.io package queries; alert on installation of packages on threat-intel blocklists or with unusual metadata (newly-created author, recent version bumps, abnormal dependency chains). Cross-reference against supply-chain threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Code Injection via Build-time Dependency Execution
suggestion.rationale: Rust crate execution happens at build/compile time; pipeline missed detection for code execution during dependency compilation. Phrase: 'performs code exfiltration' implies runtime behavior during build.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for proc_macro or build.rs script execution from Cargo dependencies outside expected system paths. Alert on rustc child processes invoking network utilities (curl, wget, PowerShell) or opening unexpected files during compilation phase.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45447 Exploitation via Malformed PKCS7/S/MIME Messages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'triggered when applications process specially crafted PKCS7 or S/MIME signed messages.' Initial-access detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal PKCS7 or S/MIME message processing: malformed ASN.1 structures, unusual message sizes, repeated failed signature verification attempts, or messages targeting mail servers and TLS libraries. Flag unexpected network traffic patterns to systems known to process S/MIME content.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption and Process Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'heap use-after-free bug' causing 'memory corruption'—execution-phase detection required to catch in-flight exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process crashes, memory access violations, or unhandled exceptions in OpenSSL-linked processes immediately following PKCS7_verify function invocation. Flag unexpected child processes spawned from crashed or recovering OpenSSL contexts.

suggestion.title: OpenSSL Version Inventory for CVE-2026-45447 Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE affecting OpenSSL—asset discovery hunt absent despite this being foundational recon phase work.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all processes executing OpenSSL libraries and extract version information. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-45447 patch timeline to identify unpatched endpoints. Prioritize mail servers, TLS termination points, and S/MIME-capable applications.

suggestion.title: RCE Code Execution Detection Post-Heap-Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Article's RCE impact requires execution-phase detection. Pipeline missed T1059/T1203 implications of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected command execution or script spawning from OpenSSL or S/MIME processing contexts. Monitor for process parent-child anomalies where shell interpreters are launched from library contexts normally incapable of process spawning.

suggestion.title: JWT Cryptographic Validation Against Known Hardcoded Secret
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery.' Direct cryptographic validation—tokens that verify against the string 'random' as the HMAC-SHA256 key—would catch active exploitation.
log_sources: Web access logs with Authorization headers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement JWT signature validation in HTTP access logs. Flag tokens that cryptographically validate against the hardcoded secret 'random'. Correlate against legitimate authentication paths; forged tokens will bypass login/MFA flows.

suggestion.title: go-base Repository Access and Source Code Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the hardcoded secret is 'shipped to all users' in dev.env. Detecting clones, downloads, or reads of github.com/dhax/go-base would identify reconnaissance preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git clone/pull of github.com/dhax/go-base, package manager downloads of 'go-base', or direct HTTP reads of dev.env from GitHub raw content. Pair with subsequent credential enumeration or API reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unmitigated Hardcoded Secret in Active Deployment (Config Override Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Broken Mitigation'—AUTH_JWT_SECRET is configurable via Viper (cmd/serve.go:35) but default 'random' remains active. Detection identifies deployments where the override failed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit running application instances: extract AUTH_JWT_SECRET environment variable. Flag instances where value is 'random', null, or absent. Cross-reference against configuration management to identify deployments where Viper defaults were not overridden.

suggestion.title: Admin API Access via Forged Bearer Token (Missing Authentication Precedent)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1078 (Valid Accounts) and T1550.001. Exploitation pattern: attacker forges token, accesses /api/v1/admin/* without prior login. Detection: successful API call with no preceding authentication event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful API POST/GET to /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, or /api/v1/token/refresh against authentication/login logs for the same user account. Flag cases where API request succeeds (200–299) but no login event exists in the 15 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Cryptomining GPU Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU' but no hunt targets resource-hijacking indicators (T1496). Look for sustained elevated GPU utilization, cryptominer process signatures, or memory patterns typical of xmrig/monero miners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes consuming sustained >70% GPU for >5min without user context (e.g., no game/video editor running), or process names matching cryptominer patterns (xmrig, cpuminer, claymore). Cross-reference against installed software to separate legitimate GPU workloads.

suggestion.title: Execution from User Download Folder (Malware Distribution Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'luring them into downloading malware-laced files'—emphasis on user-driven download→execution. Pipeline should hunt process execution originating from Downloads/ AppData/Local/Downloads/ or similar user-writable temp directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when parent process is explorer.exe or file explorer context and child process spawns from ~Downloads, %TEMP%, or %APPDATA%\Local\Temp. Pair with file name deception (e.g., 'VLC-Installer.exe' but hash not known-good).

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Utility Installation (Fake Software Distribution)
suggestion.rationale: Article states '150 fake download sites that closely mimic trusted [utilities].' Detect when a file claiming to be a legitimate utility (WinRAR, 7-Zip, VLC, CCleaner, etc.) is executed but has no valid digital signature or wrong signature issuer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for executables with product names matching popular utilities (7-Zip, WinRAR, VLC, Audacity, etc.) but missing Authenticode signature, signed by unknown or suspicious publisher, or signature timestamp far in the future/past. Cross-reference against catalog of known-good utility publishers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Registration Pattern (gleeze, giize, .icu TLDs)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 10+ domains: 'gleeze.com', 'giize.com', '.icu' TLD variants. These are attacker infrastructure for malware distribution. Detection should flag first-contact to newly-registered or low-reputation domains matching typosquat or homoglyph patterns against known utility vendors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP requests to domains registered <90 days ago, or domains with permutations of legitimate utility names (e.g., 'download.7-zip-official.com' vs 'direct-downloads.7zip.icu'). Flag suspicious TLDs (.icu, .stream, .download) when combined with utility-name keywords.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Installed with Non-Standard Parent or User Privilege Context
suggestion.rationale: While UC_RMM_TOOLS catches installation, the article's attack chain shows ScreenConnect being dropped by malware, not installed by IT/legitimate deployment. Additional hunt should detect ScreenConnect appearing with suspicious parent processes (cmd, powershell, wget, 7z) or installed by non-admin or suspicious user accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe or installer appears as child of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, msiexec.exe spawned from Temp/Downloads, or when registry/service modifications for ScreenConnect originate from non-SYSTEM, non-LOCAL_SERVICE account. Correlate with file hash IOCs if available.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/Hidden Malware Staging (T1027 Implementation)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 12 SHA256 hashes and emphasizes obfuscation; pipeline caught T1027 at the technique level but generated no detection. Hunt should look for packed/encrypted files (low entropy, signatures matching UPX/Themida/VMProtect), files with abnormal section names, or DLLs with no export table.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executable or DLL is loaded with anomalous headers (entropy >7.8, UPX/packed signatures, corrupted or missing standard sections), or when file is written to disk and immediately accessed by multiple processes before any user interaction. Cross-reference with detonation/sandbox signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation—Threat-Intel-Flagged Package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware-laden npm package 'dbmux' installed on developer systems: 'capable of giving attackers complete control over any developer's system that had it installed or running.' This is the primary Initial Access vector; pipeline generated zero detection for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install/update operations where package name or version matches threat-intel feeds (e.g., dbmux). Correlate package installation with child process spawning from node_modules. Monitor for postinstall script execution during suspicious package initialization.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution from npm Postinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes malware capability yielding 'complete control'—this implies code execution during or immediately after package installation via postinstall hooks or module init. Pipeline missed Execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or system utilities from npm/node_modules context during package installation. Alert on privilege-escalation attempts or system-level operations (registry modification, service creation) from npm postinstall execution.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanisms Installed by Malicious npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article's claim of 'complete control' implies persistent backdoor, not ephemeral malware. Pipeline failed to hypothesize persistence techniques (startup items, cron jobs, registry runkeys, shell profile injection) typical of full-system compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions to startup locations (registry HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce, user startup folder, .bashrc/.bash_profile, cron, launchd) coinciding with npm package installation. Alert on scheduled task or service creation by node.js or npm processes.

suggestion.title: Credential and Source-Code Exfiltration from Compromised Developer Workstation
suggestion.rationale: With 'complete control' of developer systems, attackers logically target high-value assets: SSH keys, API credentials, Git tokens, and source repositories. Pipeline missed Impact-phase detection despite this being critical for developer-targeted compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTPS/DNS activity from developer systems post-npm-infection, especially to non-whitelisted IPs or cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, GitHub gists). Alert on unusual data transfers, credential-store access (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain), or .ssh directory enumeration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Developer System Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Developer workstations with full system compromise are staging points for internal infrastructure attacks: Git repositories, CI/CD platforms, artifact registries, and shared development servers. Pipeline ignored this logical attack continuation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections from compromised developer systems to internal Git/CI/CD infrastructure (GitLab, Jenkins, GitHub Enterprise) or shared development servers outside baseline access patterns. Alert on service-account credential usage originating from developer workstations.

suggestion.title: In-memory PowerShell/CLR assembly loading without disk artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'runs entirely in memory, leaving almost no trace behind'—core evasion tactic. Pipeline generated no detection for unsigned .NET assembly loading, memory-resident shellcode, or WMI event sink persistence. This is the defining characteristic of the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or rundll32 loading unsigned .NET assemblies into memory (via Assembly.Load or reflection), or WMI event sinks created without corresponding .ps1 file on disk. In-memory malware avoids file enumeration but leaves traces in ETW event logs and memory introspection tools.

suggestion.title: Process injection / memory manipulation from script engines
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage malware execution with in-memory payload typically involves process injection (T1055) or hollowing. Pipeline maps T1218 but no UC detects injection patterns (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext calls or suspicious remote handle opens).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell or VBScript spawning svchost.exe, dllhost.exe, or other system processes with no command-line arguments and no corresponding task/scheduled job registry entry. Or detect unsigned code execution in legitimate service processes (signatureless child or remote thread creation).

suggestion.title: Multi-stage malware dropper-to-payload execution chain
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage malware' but pipeline generated no UC for detecting the dropper→payload sequence. Typical chain: initial executable launches PowerShell or VBS, which decodes/downloads second stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid (<5 second) parent-child process chains where initial process (powershell, cmd, wscript) spawns a second script engine or LOLBin with suspiciously short lifetime. Correlate with network events (DNS/HTTP) at same time to confirm payload fetch.

suggestion.title: C2 communication from application-layer protocols (post-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1071 'Application Layer Protocol' is listed, implying HTTP/HTTPS or DNS C2 callbacks, but no UC detects beaconing patterns. In-memory malware needs command channel to adversary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual DNS or HTTP traffic from PowerShell (or other script engine child processes) to the extracted IOC domains (guhxmg.com, naiqja.icu, zh-welcome-1xbet.com, etc.) with periodic/regular timing (C2 beacon pattern). Include failed connection attempts to staging domains.

suggestion.title: Credential entry / form submission to tax-themed phishing domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impersonation of 'official Indian government tax authorities'—credential harvesting is the typical end-goal. No UC covers detecting users entering credentials into non-legitimate tax websites or forms.
log_sources: browser process memory or HTTP body inspection (DLP-adjacent)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) navigation to extracted IOC domains (e.g., taxations.indiagov.it.com, taxations.cn-web-okooo.com) followed by form POST requests or password managers being triggered. Cross-reference with known Indian tax domain patterns (indiagov.nic.in) to confirm the impersonation.

suggestion.title: Registry persistence / scheduled task creation without file artifact
suggestion.rationale: In-memory malware often persists via registry run keys, WMI event sinks, or scheduled tasks rather than .exe files on disk. No UC detects this evasion variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entries or scheduled tasks pointing to PowerShell/WMI commands (especially obfuscated or base64-encoded) without corresponding .exe file on disk. Combine with process execution logs to confirm task execution.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection — Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'critical vulnerabilities' from three major vendors; exploitation is the primary attack vector implied by vulnerability disclosure patterns. No use case generated despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests containing known exploit signatures or payloads targeting Ivanti Connect Secure, Fortinet FortiGate, and SAP NetWeaver management interfaces. Flag POST requests with suspicious parameter encoding or known CVE payload patterns to these devices.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Inventory — Patch Applicability
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vendors 'releasing patches'; detection should identify systems still running pre-patch versions vulnerable to disclosed CVEs. No inventory use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify installed Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP software versions against published vulnerability timelines. Flag systems running versions released before the patching date or versions explicitly listed as vulnerable in CVE databases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Patch Behavior Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: If a system running these products exhibits anomalous behavior after the vulnerability window, it may indicate successful pre-patch exploitation. Article implies potential for undetected compromise during vulnerability window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For systems hosting Ivanti, Fortinet, or SAP services, correlate unusual outbound connections, process spawning, or DNS queries in the 24-48 hours post-patch deployment with known C2 patterns or data exfiltration signatures.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Authentication Bypass via CVE-2026-10523
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10523 is 'a critical authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts.' This is a distinct attack phase preceding RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for unauthenticated requests that successfully create or modify administrative user accounts. Correlate failed authentication attempts followed by new privileged account creation within the same session.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection via Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-10520 as 'an OS command injection weakness' that 'enables remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' This is the execution/privilege escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell metacharacters and command substitution patterns in HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints. Look for pipe, semicolon, backtick, or $() sequences in parameter values followed by unexpected process spawning on the appliance.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'enables remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' Post-exploitation detection must key on root UID processes initiated from the gateway appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events on Ivanti Sentry infrastructure where PPID or user context indicates root execution initiated from network-facing processes or authentication paths. Baseline legitimate system services and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Administrative Account Creation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10523 allows attackers to 'create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' Account creation is a persistence and privilege escalation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track user/account creation events on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially admin-level accounts. Correlate account creation with authentication bypass signatures, unusual timestamps (off-hours), or non-standard credential materials.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Ivanti Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Sentry as 'a security gateway appliance that secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices.' A compromised gateway is a lateral movement pivot to internal networks and endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from Ivanti Sentry appliances for connections to internal subnets or corporate systems that deviate from baseline gateway-to-backend patterns. Flag connections to ports typically associated with internal access (RDP, SSH, LDAP, database ports).

suggestion.title: Defender Process Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states zero-day 'grants SYSTEM access'—privilege escalation is the attack's core. Pipeline missed all privilege-elevation detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Defender engine processes (MpEngineProcess, MsSense, NisSrv) for token elevation from non-SYSTEM to SYSTEM context or spawning children with unexpected privilege levels. Baseline normal Defender privilege contexts and alert on anomalous jumps.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from Defender Engine Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of Defender vulnerability typically results in attacker code executing within the elevated Defender process. Pipeline missed post-exploitation process execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned from MpEngineProcess or MsSense that are not known Defender components. Include detection of DLL injection or process hollowing attempts targeting Defender PIDs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL Load into MpEngineProcess
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation via in-process vulnerability requires loading malicious code into the elevated Defender service. Pipeline failed to identify DLL-load anomalies as detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or non-Microsoft-signed DLLs loaded into MpEngineProcess. Flag loads from %Temp%, %AppData%, or other non-standard locations. Cross-reference against baseline Defender DLL manifests.

suggestion.title: Defender Service Crash Correlation with Process Elevation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of in-process engine vulnerability typically crashes the service during attack execution. Pipeline failed to correlate Defender process failures with suspicious activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate MpEngineProcess crashes or abnormal terminations with privilege-escalation events or unexpected process creation in the same 30-second window. Track MpEngine restart cycles and suspicious parent-child chains.

suggestion.title: Registry Tamper Targeting Defender Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Defender exploits may involve disabling features or modifying behavior to avoid detection. Article mentions 'updated Windows,' implying vulnerability persists across patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender for exclusion list tampering, signature rollback, or real-time protection disablement from non-administrative processes. Alert on registry changes from Defender PIDs during suspicious activity.

suggestion.title: Detect XSS Payloads in OWA-Targeted Email
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sending a specially crafted email to a user' + 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed'—pipeline must detect inline scripts, event handlers, and obfuscated JavaScript in email bodies reaching vulnerable Exchange versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing script tags, event handlers (onclick, onload, onerror), or JavaScript payloads delivered to Exchange servers. Correlate with known vulnerable versions (2016, 2019, SE) and flag obfuscated encoding (base64, unicode, hex escapes) combined with script patterns.

suggestion.title: Monitor Unexpected JavaScript Execution from OWA/Outlook Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' when user opens email in OWA; detection must capture abnormal script execution from Outlook/Edge triggered by email interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript/JScript execution (wscript, cscript, Edge DOM events) spawned by or within Outlook.exe/Edge.exe process. Baseline normal OWA interactions and alert on deviations, especially those reaching external hosts or modifying DOM/credentials.

suggestion.title: Flag Emails Matching CVE-2026-42897 Exploit Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability is 'actively exploited in attacks'—detection should match known XSS payloads and structural patterns specific to this CVE (Exchange 2016, 2019, SE vulnerable code path).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create gateway rules and endpoint detection to identify malformed MIME, HTML injection in specific Exchange fields, or attribute-based XSS payloads known to trigger CVE-2026-42897 in vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous OWA Session Activity Post-Email Open
suggestion.rationale: XSS in OWA can lead to session hijacking or credential theft; article's execution context suggests post-exploitation activity (mailbox access, forwarding rules, credential exfiltration) should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email delivery events (flagged as XSS-suspicious) with account anomalies within 5-30 minutes: new forwarding rules, unusual sign-in locations, mailbox rule modifications, delegate additions, or multiple authentication failures.

suggestion.title: Alert on EEMS Mitigation Trigger Spikes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'automatic temporary mitigation through the Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service (EEMS)' deployed mid-May—high-volume EEMS blocks indicate active exploitation attempts and should be surfaced to analysts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Exchange event logs and EEMS telemetry for elevated mitigation trigger counts (XSS payloads, script injection blocks). Alert on sustained spike from single sender domain or targeting multiple org recipients—signals active campaign.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day RCE Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Critical RCE Bugs' and 'Three Zero-Days' — pipeline missed detection for active exploitation code execution chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) spawned from known vulnerable Microsoft applications (Office, Windows services). RCE flaws typically result in immediate code execution; correlate with unusual parent process behaviors or network indicators post-spawn.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day RCE bugs typically enable privilege escalation; article implies full attack chain but pipeline captured no PE phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes spawning SYSTEM/Administrator children, unusual service creation, or registry modifications enabling persistence post-RCE. Privilege escalation typically follows initial RCE execution in unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise System Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: After RCE exploitation, threat actors perform discovery (whoami, systeminfo, net commands). Pipeline missed entire discovery phase despite critical RCE attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequential execution of reconnaissance commands (systeminfo, ipconfig, net view, tasklist) from unusual parents or in rapid succession immediately post-RCE. Establish baseline for normal administrative activity to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Probe Detection for Known Zero-Days
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions specific zero-days but pipeline extracted no CVE identifiers. Detection must key on exploit signatures or vulnerable application versions under active attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic and web logs for exploit signatures matching the three zero-days mentioned (payload patterns, crafted HTTP requests, unusual URI parameters targeting Microsoft applications). Alert on probes against unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: Missing Security Updates on Critical Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article is about 206 patches including critical RCE flaws; detection must track patch compliance and flag non-compliant systems within SLA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on systems failing to apply Microsoft security patches within organizational SLA (especially critical/RCE patches). Monitor for deferred, failed, or rolled-back updates on systems running vulnerable Microsoft versions post-patch-Tuesday.

suggestion.title: SSH Brute Force Against PeopleSoft Admin Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'script attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm.' This is credential spray/brute force activity that should trigger detection on failed SSH auth followed by success, or high failure counts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed SSH authentication attempts followed by successful authentication to PeopleSoft systems using hardcoded admin accounts (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) from external IPs. Correlate failed auth in auth.log with subsequent key-based auth success, or rapid sequential failed logins from the same source.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Deployment to PeopleSoft Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'shell script designed to create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT on an internal PeopleSoft server after it is breached.' File creation artifact with specific name pattern is immediately detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of files matching pattern 'README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.*' or similar ransom note naming conventions in PeopleSoft installation directories (/opt/psoft, /u01/app/pt, etc.). Alert on any file write events to known PeopleSoft web/app server directories from unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Agent Discovery and Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exposed online directories containing tooling related to this attack. Also visible were staging materials, including MeshCentral agents.' This indicates post-exploitation deployment of remote access tools for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of MeshCentral agent binaries from known attacker infrastructure (142.11.200.x subnet) or suspicious process execution patterns consistent with MeshCentral agent (meshcentral-agent, meshagent processes with callback command-line arguments).

suggestion.title: /etc/hosts Parsing for Internal Network Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack script: 'script parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems and attempts to connect to them over SSH.' This discovery activity is a clear tactical indicator of internal reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious read/access of /etc/hosts file from unexpected processes (especially non-root or processes not typically requiring hosts file access). Correlate with subsequent SSH connection attempts to internal systems listed in hosts file, particularly to systems matching PeopleSoft patterns.

suggestion.title: External IP Connections to PeopleSoft SSH Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article provides concrete IOCs: '142.11.200.186, 142.11.200.187, 142.11.200.188, 142.11.200.189, 142.11.200.190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24' as IPs used in attacks. SSH connection attempts from these subnets represent direct malicious activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound SSH connections (port 22, or non-standard SSH ports) from known attacker IP addresses (142.11.200.0/24 subnet, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) to any PeopleSoft application servers. Low threshold for alerting given concrete IOC attribution to ShinyHunters infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'ShinyHunters says they are using a gadget chain of old and zero-day vulnerabilities to conduct the attacks.' Detecting exploitation attempts against known PeopleSoft CVEs or anomalous web application behavior is critical for initial access prevention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft web interfaces for exploitation indicators: abnormal HTTP requests containing Java deserialization payloads, SQL injection patterns, or directory traversal attempts. Look for requests to known vulnerable PeopleSoft endpoints with suspicious parameter values or embedded serialized objects.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Query Execution Against ServiceNow Instance Tables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'improper access controls that may enable attackers to execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication'—core attack vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow query logs for table access without valid authentication context, particularly to sensitive tables (sys_user, cmdb_ci, incident). Detect sequential table enumeration or bulk row extraction from unauthorized principals.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow API Access Without Valid Authentication Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly bypasses authentication controls ('without proper authentication'). Detect HTTP requests missing Bearer tokens or session cookies succeeding when they should fail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to /api/now/* endpoints lacking Authorization headers or valid session tokens that return data (200 responses with table rows) instead of 401/403 errors.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Bulk ServiceNow Table Queries
suggestion.rationale: High severity and 'unauthorized access to customer instance tables' indicate data exposure; detect large result sets and exports suggesting staging for exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries returning >10k rows, concurrent multi-table queries, export operations, or API requests with unusually large response payloads following authentication bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Against ServiceNow Metadata and Table Schema
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must enumerate available tables and columns before querying sensitive data. Phrase 'query customer instance tables' implies schema discovery activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to ServiceNow sys_db_object, sys_dictionary, or metadata endpoints from unauthenticated contexts, or DESCRIBE-like queries probing table structure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Langflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027 Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE.' Zero detections for web-based exploit payloads or malformed requests targeting this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Langflow endpoints for payloads consistent with CVE-2026-5027 exploitation: serialization gadgets, code injection patterns, or known malicious query strings. Correlate with successful HTTP responses (200/302) followed by unexpected child process creation from Langflow worker process.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution via Langflow RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes remote code execution as attack vector. No UC for detecting process spawning or shell invocation from vulnerable Langflow service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Langflow services (python, java, node depending on deployment variant) with anomalous characteristics: command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash), obfuscated or base64-encoded arguments, execution from temp/cache directories, or network connection attempts within first 5 seconds of spawn.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Discovery and Enumeration from Langflow
suggestion.rationale: Successful unauthenticated RCE grants shell access; article does not describe but standard attack chain includes reconnaissance. No UC for discovery activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After code execution, attackers enumerate running processes, user accounts, network config, and installed software. Alert on discovery commands (ps, whoami, id, ifconfig, systeminfo, uname) executed as children of Langflow or spawned from Langflow-spawned shells in temporal clusters.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command & Control from Compromised Langflow Instance
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE enables reverse shell and persistent C2 channel; no detection for exfiltration or callback traffic initiated from Langflow process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor persistent or repeated outbound connections from Langflow processes to non-whitelisted external IP addresses, particularly on non-standard ports (8080, 4444, 9999, etc.). Alert on suspicious DNS queries for known C2 domains or fast-flux patterns originating from Langflow service accounts.

suggestion.title: Langflow Service Availability Anomaly or Crash Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts and RCE can destabilize service or cause resource exhaustion. No UC for service health degradation or process restarts correlating with attack activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 5xx errors or high request latency on Langflow endpoints with spike in CPU/memory consumption, process crashes, or restart of Langflow service. Baseline response time and error rates, alert on sudden degradation overlapping with suspicious web requests or process spawning.

suggestion.title: Low-privilege process spawning SYSTEM child via CTFMON
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows a local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM'—core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege boundary crossing where low-privilege parent spawns SYSTEM-level child, especially involving CTFMON.exe in call chain. Flag elevation via token duplication or inherited handles.

suggestion.title: CTFMON.exe abnormal process spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CTFMON (Collaborative Translation Framework Monitor) as vulnerable component—abnormal execution is exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CTFMON.exe is background IME service and should not spawn children. Detect any child process creation, especially with elevated privileges or suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Token elevation or handle duplication via CVE-2026-45586
suggestion.rationale: Described as 'post-exploitation primitive'—mechanisms typically involve token theft, handle duplication, or elevation via kernel object manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cross-privilege thread creation, suspicious handle requests to SYSTEM processes, or DuplicateHandle calls from low-privilege context targeting elevated tokens.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation registry/file persistence via elevated context
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'valuable post-exploitation primitive'—implies follow-on persistence or lateral movement using escalated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HKLM/Services registry writes or system directory file modifications originating from CTFMON child process or low-privilege parent that spawned elevated child.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Logging Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly focuses on "Abusing Cloud Logging Services" — disabling CloudTrail is the canonical attack. Title phrase: 'Blinding the Watchmen' directly references disabling observability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for StopLogging, DeleteTrail, UpdateTrail with logging disabled, or DisableLogging API calls. Alert on successful trail disablement especially within minutes of suspicious API activity. Cross-check for deletion of CloudTrail digest files.

suggestion.title: S3 Bucket Logging Disabled or Redirected
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'S3' and 'log storage'. Article discusses abusing cloud logging services; S3 bucket access logging is primary target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PutBucketLogging calls that disable logging (empty target bucket), or PutBucketPolicy/PutBucketAcl that revoke cross-account logging permissions. Detect gaps in S3 access log ingestion for previously-logging buckets.

suggestion.title: CloudWatch Logs Deletion or Stream Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article covers 'defense evasion' in Google Cloud and AWS logging services. CloudWatch Logs deletion is a direct logging evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DeleteLogGroup, DeleteLogStream, PutRetentionPolicy (set to 1 day), or DisableLogAggregation calls. Flag rapid deletion of log groups following suspicious activity. Correlate with IAM credential usage.

suggestion.title: GCP Log Router Sink Deletion or Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords mention 'Google Cloud' and 'log router'. Article discusses multi-cloud logging evasion; GCP's log routing is primary defense mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DeleteSink calls in GCP Cloud Logging audit logs, or UpdateSink calls that redirect logs to untrusted/external destinations. Detect loss of log flow to SIEM post-sink modification.

suggestion.title: IAM Privilege Escalation Preceding Log Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Defense evasion via logging tampering requires privileged credentials. Article title implies attackers must gain privilege before 'blinding' logging. Kill-chain reconstruction missing this prerequisite phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account enumeration calls (ListRoles, ListUsers, GetUser) with subsequent logging-modification IAM actions. Flag privilege escalation (AttachUserPolicy, CreateAccessKey) immediately followed by logging API calls within same session.

suggestion.title: Log Deletion via Cloud Storage Bucket Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'log storage' abuse and 'log poisoning'. Direct deletion or overwrite of logs in cloud object storage (S3, GCS, AzureBlob) is core evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DeleteObject or PutObject operations targeting known log storage buckets/containers. Alert on batch delete operations (DeleteObjects) on audit log prefixes. Correlate with logging service configuration changes.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Exploitation Execution via Malicious Content
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'V8 Zero-Day...Exploited in the Wild', establishing active code-execution attacks. Pipeline missed the execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child-process spawns from Chrome (e.g., rundll32, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with no user interaction or suspicious memory allocation patterns within V8 heap space (Kernel32.VirtualAlloc with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE from chrome.exe).

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chrome Instance Remains in Production
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Patch Now', indicating vulnerable versions persist. No detection for outdated browser versions was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome processes with version strings matching pre-patch builds after CVE-2026-11645 patch release date. Correlate against auto-update logs to identify systems with disabled updates or broken update mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Drive-by Download of V8 Exploit Payload
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation requires delivery mechanism; 'exploited in the wild' implies network-based attacks. Pipeline overlooked initial-access indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests from Chrome to suspicious or newly-registered domains followed by inline script execution or conditional binary downloads. Flag User-Agent sniffing requests that serve payloads conditionally based on Chrome version.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping Post-V8 Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful V8 RCE grants code-execution context; article implies real-world post-exploitation. No detection for credential access from browser context was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lsass.exe access or LSASS dump attempts (*.dmp files) originating from Chrome child processes. Flag DPAPI key access or VAULT credential queries triggered by browser-spawned executables.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via V8 Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Browser contexts typically run with user privileges; article does not specify post-compromise objectives. Detection for UAC bypass or kernel-exploitation attempts following V8 RCE was omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UAC bypass techniques (fodhelper, eventvwr, registry-based COM hijacking) or kernel-driver loading initiated from Chrome child processes. Monitor for SYSTEM-context process creation chains originating from browser execution.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chromium Browser Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.' Pipeline must inventory browser versions and flag pre-patch versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query installed software inventory for Chrome, Edge, Opera versions released before 2026-06-23. Cross-correlate with vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-11645 hits. Flag any pre-patch version running on internet-facing systems.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Vulnerability Scanner Hit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'CVE-2026-11645 — match against your vulnerability scanner' in Indicators of Compromise section. Pipeline must surface scanner findings as structured detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner logs for any positive CVE-2026-11645 findings. Correlate with asset inventory and apply criticality scoring based on asset exposure (internet-facing, user-facing, public-cloud). Alert on any vulnerable asset without documented remediation plan.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Crafted HTML Delivery Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'a crafted HTML page' sent to remote users. Pipeline must detect delivery of malicious HTML payloads targeting browsers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email and web traffic for HTML attachments or links with obfuscation patterns, suspicious script tags, or known exploit delivery domains (post-IOC publication). Correlate with browser process anomalies to identify suspected delivery attempts.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Unexpected Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution inside a sandbox' which, if breaking out, would spawn child processes from browser parent. Pipeline must monitor for execution anomalies post-V8 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by Chrome, Edge, Opera. Flag unexpected children (cmd.exe, powershell, net.exe, whoami, etc.) spawned from browser parent in unpatched versions running on/after 2026-06-09. Correlate with failed patch compliance.

suggestion.title: Browser Crash Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Out-of-bounds read/write vulnerabilities frequently cause memory faults and process crashes. Article specifies this as an out-of-bounds vulnerability type that may manifest as instability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden spikes in browser process crashes (Chrome/Edge/Opera) on systems without CVE-2026-11645 patches. Correlate crash timestamps with unusual network activity or HTML delivery events to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-23' and article header emphasizes that CISA KEV adds 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Pipeline must track compliance against deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate compliance report for CVE-2026-11645 patches across all government/regulated assets. Track patch deployment progress weekly. Alert if any compliance deadline risk detected. Verify patches actually applied (not just released by vendor) by validating software inventory against known-good versions.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references template at `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Pipeline produced no use cases despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for externally-accessible Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances via SSL certificate fingerprinting, HTTP response headers, or DNS records. Correlate against internal asset inventory to identify unaccounted or unpatched deployments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes patch lag risk. Pipeline generated no scanner-based detection case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner reports identifying CVE-2026-20245 in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager assets. Escalate for patch prioritization against federal due date of 2026-06-23.

suggestion.title: Crafted File Upload to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack requires 'supplying a crafted file to the affected system.' No execution-phase detection suggested despite this being the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager file upload endpoints for unusual file types, sizes, encoding anomalies, or malformed submissions. Correlate with application error logs indicating parsing failures or encoding/escaping exceptions.

suggestion.title: Root Command Execution from SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Article's core impact is 'arbitrary commands as root'—endpoint visibility into privilege escalation and command execution by the SD-WAN Manager service is essential for post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned with root privilege by the Catalyst SD-WAN Manager service account (vManage daemon). Flag shell invocations (bash, sh, cmd.exe), script interpreters, or suspicious binaries executed with elevated context.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated, local attacker'—malicious actors must first gain or abuse valid credentials. Pipeline missed credential-access and valid-account-abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for failed login attempts followed by success, unusual geographic logins, credential spraying, or authentication from non-whitelisted IP ranges targeting Catalyst SD-WAN Manager administrative interfaces.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Vulnerability Scanner Match — CVE-2026-7473
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner'—the most direct detection method for a CISA KEV entry. Identifies systems running affected Arista EOS versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Arista EOS devices with version <patched_version> in vulnerability scanner output or asset inventory. Alert on any system matching CVE-2026-7473 signature. Cross-reference with network exposure logs to prioritize public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Public-Facing Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes 'exploit public-facing application'—T1190 requires internet-reachable targets. Identifies which Arista EOS devices are exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Arista EOS devices with outbound internet routing or inbound SSH/HTTPS exposure. Flag any with SSH port 22, HTTP port 80, or HTTPS port 443 reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate with vulnerability scan results to identify exploitable targets.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Tunnel Decapsulation and Packet Forwarding Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP'—indicates packet forwarding misbehavior when tunnel config is present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS syslog for tunnel decapsulation errors or unexpected packet forwarding events. In NetFlow/sFlow, detect packets arriving on tunnel interfaces and being forwarded to mismatched destination IPs. Flag packets with destination IP matching the device's decapsulation IP but arriving from unusual source VLANs or ingress interfaces.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Configuration Drift — Tunnel Decapsulation Settings
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability manifests when 'switch incorrectly decapsulate'—implies configuration-driven behavior. Detection should track tunnel decapsulation configuration changes and drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Arista EOS device configuration changes to tunnel decapsulation settings (IP, VXLAN, MPLS, or custom tunnel types). Alert on addition or modification of decapsulation rules. Cross-reference with asset inventory to flag devices where tunnel decapsulation is unexpectedly enabled or misconfigured.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-7473 Patch Compliance for Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and Federal due date is 2026-06-23. Detection must verify patch application across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Arista EOS devices are running patched version ≥ [patched_version]. Alert on devices with EOS version < patched_version or last patch date > 2026-06-23. Escalate any unpatched systems to incident response by the Federal due date.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Installation Triggers Postinstall Credential Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Article states '19 Packages Poisoned' with 'Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer' — primary attack vector with zero detection proposed. setup.py auto-execution is the critical entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install / poetry add spawning setup.py or setup.cfg from untrusted PyPI packages, especially when setup.py creates child processes (Bun, Node, Python subshell). Correlate with network callbacks or credential file access within 120s of install completion.

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Credential Stealer Execution from Package Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Bun Credential Stealer' but zero detection for Bun process spawned from package management context was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Bun process spawned with parent process being Python, pip, setup.py, or node. Flag if Bun invoked with suspicious arguments (env var dump, file listing, network binaries). Cross-correlate with package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Credential Storage Access During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware targets browser cookies, SSH keys, and cloud credentials post-install. Article describes credential theft but zero filesystem/browser access detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned from pip/setup.py context accessing ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh, .kube/config, .git/config, or browser credential DBs (Chrome/Firefox Default/Profile). Flag if access pattern indicates enumeration or exfiltration (read-only sequential scans of credential paths).

suggestion.title: Package Setup Egress to Non-Repository Command-and-Control
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain stealer requires C2 callback to exfiltrate credentials. No detection for setup.py or postinstall spawning network callbacks to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate pip install / poetry add activity with outbound connections to non-PyPI/non-trusted-registry destinations within 60s. Alert on HTTPS POST with credential-sized payloads (300B–50KB) to unregistered domains contacted only during/post-package-install.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE' — implies exploitation of CVE-2026-42271 via LiteLLM service. Should detect anomalous request patterns, error responses, or payload indicators targeting LiteLLM endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to LiteLLM API endpoints with unusual content-length, chunked encoding, or polyglot payloads. Flag requests with error codes 5xx following suspicious parameter patterns indicative of code injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Execution from LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE' — means successful exploitation results in command execution without authentication. Should detect process spawning from LiteLLM process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is LiteLLM (litellm.exe, python litellm runner, or container process) with suspicious command-line arguments, especially shell invocations (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, /bin/bash) from unexpected user context or with network I/O patterns.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Anomalous Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploited 'in the wild' implies attacker gains network access; should detect exfiltration, C2 callbacks, or lateral movement from compromised LiteLLM process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from LiteLLM process to non-allowlisted destinations, especially to IPs with low reputation, suspicious TLDs, or dynamic DNS. Monitor DNS requests from LiteLLM for known C2 domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Payload Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies specific CVE — need signature-based detection for known exploitation patterns or payloads documented in public PoCs or breach data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for known CVE-2026-42271 payload patterns in request bodies, headers, or URL parameters. Flag requests containing documented gadget chains or serialization payloads known to trigger the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious Commits to CI/CD Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled' — direct evidence of repository modification. Pipeline failed to surface detection for unauthorized commits to build automation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor high-trust GitHub repositories (esp. Actions, CI/CD templates, widely-forked projects) for commits outside normal maintainer/branch patterns. Flag unsigned commits, new branch protections disablement, or workflow file modifications in Actions repos.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Compromised GitHub Actions Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Azure Functions Action' as compromised — Miasma Worm distributed through published Actions artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of scripts or binaries pulled from GitHub Actions during workflow runs, especially from newly-released or recently-modified Actions. Correlate artifact hashes against malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Repository Disablement or Access Revocation
suggestion.rationale: Title: '72 Other Repositories Disabled' — bulk repository disabling is an impact indicator requiring detection of unauthorized admin API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk GitHub repository disablement or visibility changes, especially via API tokens or SSH keys. Alert on repositories disabled outside maintenance windows or by unexpected accounts.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Command Injection via Malicious Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'AI Coding Agents' as attack target — supply chain attack likely delivers malware through code dependencies processed by agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent sandboxes/containers for unexpected child process spawning, outbound network connections, or file I/O when processing code from untrusted repositories. Flag execution of shell commands within agent workflows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Credentials: Anomalous API/SSH Key Activity
suggestion.rationale: Repository compromise implies credential abuse — attacker credentials used to commit malware and disable repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub API calls or SSH commits from new geographic locations, non-business-hours, or IPs not in baseline for repository maintainers. Flag PAT/SSH key usage anomalies per repository or developer.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: Enumeration of CI/CD Workflows and Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack on AI agents implies attacker reconnaissance of GitHub Actions workflows to identify injection points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual read access to workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml), secrets, and action.yml metadata, especially from new IPs or non-standard authentication methods.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Race Condition SYSTEM Command Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'When successful, a Windows command prompt will be spawned with SYSTEM privileges via a Microsoft Defender race condition vulnerability.' This is the core exploit mechanism with zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as SYSTEM from Microsoft Defender processes (mpengine.exe, MsSecurityEngine.exe, MpCmdRun.exe). Alert on race-condition indicators: rapid successive file I/O in Defender directories (%ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender) coinciding with unexpected child process creation. Flag any non-service SYSTEM-context spawn from Defender—this is abnormal.

suggestion.title: SMB-Hosted VHD File Handling by Microsoft Defender
suggestion.rationale: Article details original RCE variant: 'required an attacker to coerce a victim to open a .vhd(x) in a remote SMB server, succesful exploitation resulted in defender overwriting its own files.' Attack vector explicitly described with zero detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .vhd/.vhdx file opens from remote SMB shares (\\\\server\\share pattern) followed by Defender process file writes to system directories. Monitor for SMB mount attempts combined with Defender binary/DLL access. Flag symlink/junction creation in SMB-sourced directories.

suggestion.title: Defender Self-File Modification During Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation outcome: 'defender overwriting its own files.' This is a distinctive LPE indicator absent from pipeline detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Defender processes for write/modify operations to their own binaries, DLLs, or config files in %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender\*. This should never occur in normal operation. Alert on version mismatches, file hash anomalies, or unexpected load of modified Defender modules.

suggestion.title: Junction/Symlink Attack on Microsoft Defender Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Microsoft silently hardened Defender in mid-May by patching mpengine!SysIO* API, which blocked junction attacks.' Detection needed for attempted (now-blocked but historical) junction exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mklink /J or fsutil usn createjournal commands targeting Defender directories. Flag junction creation in attacker-writable locations pointing to %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender paths. Monitor for file access failures on Defender binaries that may indicate symlink interception attempts.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Creation/Deletion in Defender Cache During Process Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Race condition exploitation typically manifests as timing-dependent file operations. Article: 'The exploit is a race condition, so it's a hit or miss.' Correlating rapid I/O with unexpected process elevation detects this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect temporal clusters of file creates/deletes in Defender's engine/cache directories (typically C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\) within <100ms windows coinciding with child process creation with elevated privilege. This race-condition signature is specific to timing-sensitive exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Defender Process Elevation on Non-June-2026-Patched Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability affects fully patched Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices' and 'tested against Windows 11... with KB5094126 installed.' Exploitation persists even after June 2026 patches, requiring version-aware detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Windows 10/11 systems pre-June-2026 or missing KB5094126: alert on mpengine.exe spawning SYSTEM cmd/powershell. Post-patch systems: baseline normal Defender behavior and alert only on anomalies. Cross-reference OS build and Defender version to contextualize risk.

suggestion.title: Detect phpBB Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass' as the entry vector (URL: phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce). Pipeline produced no detections for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB login endpoints for malformed authentication requests, missing or invalid credential headers, and unusual parameter combinations targeting known bypass patterns. Detect requests with craft payloads in POST auth parameters or URI path traversal attempts to circumvent login checks.

suggestion.title: Detect Code Execution Post-phpBB Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle explicitly states '+RCE'—the critical execution phase. Pipeline provided zero execution detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe) from web server runtime (apache, httpd, nginx, php-fpm) with high confidence after a successful phpBB auth bypass. Flag unexpected PHP system calls or exec() functions with attacker-controlled arguments in PHP error logs or process monitoring.

suggestion.title: Detect Backdoor Admin Account Creation in phpBB
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE compromise typically establishes persistence via admin accounts. Article establishes full RCE capability but pipeline missed persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB application and database audit logs for creation of new administrator-level user accounts immediately following suspected auth bypass exploitation. Correlate rapid account elevation (user → moderator → admin) with RCE activity and atypical account names or registration patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Modified phpBB Core Files Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically results in webshell implants or core file modifications for persistence. Article establishes execution capability; pipeline missed post-exploitation file integrity detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected write operations to phpBB core directories (config.php, includes/, ext/) outside of installation/update maintenance windows. Flag creation of new PHP files in web-accessible directories (phptmp/, temp/, cache/) with timestamps correlating to auth bypass exploitation or RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk User Data Exfiltration from Compromised phpBB
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums'—massive data exposure surface. Pipeline generated zero exfiltration detections despite explicit user impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound network flows from compromised phpBB servers post-RCE, especially targeting cloud storage or attacker-controlled IP space. Flag unusual database query patterns querying user tables (passwords, emails, user PMs) in high volume or bulk database dumps triggered via RCE execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Mass Account Compromise Signals in phpBB Forum Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'tens of millions of users affected'—pipeline should detect post-compromise user-level compromise signals. Phrase: 'affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate forum activity from compromised instances to detect bulk account takeover: simultaneous password changes across hundreds of accounts, login surges from unexpected geographies, synchronized mass posting of spam/malicious links from dormant accounts, or bulk account state/permission changes within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing - Periodic Outbound Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 1,500+ devices in active botnet—requires C2 communication mechanism. Phrase 'botnet expands' implies ongoing command infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic outbound connections from multiple hosts (100+) to rare external IPs/domains with consistent timing intervals, low data volume, and user-mode process origination. Exclude legitimate SaaS and Windows Update traffic.

suggestion.title: Mass Reconnaissance Commands - Network Discovery Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states objective is 'cyber reconnaissance'—botnet performs systematic discovery. Phrase 'reconnaissance' directly indicates T1087/T1018 behaviors across compromised fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate discovery command patterns (net user, net group, net view, dsquery, ipconfig /all, arp -a, systeminfo) executed across 10+ hosts within 1-hour window from non-admin user context. Flag execution from temporary directories or LOLBin chains.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement - Credential Enumeration Across Subnet
suggestion.rationale: Botnet targeting 1,500 devices requires propagation mechanism. 'Reconnaissance' phase precedes lateral movement; typical botnet attack involves credential harvesting and reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed SMB/RDP login attempts (>5 per host) from single source to multiple internal targets within 30-min window, followed by successful logon. Cross-reference with uncommon source processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe spawned from svchost, explorer, etc.).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution - Botnet Malware Staging
suggestion.rationale: 1,500 devices implies malware execution on compromised hosts. Title 'JDY Botnet expands' denotes active malware deployment and persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of JDY variants (file hash/name if available from extended article) or generic botnet markers: unusual parent-child process chains (explorer.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe → curl/wget), process execution from %TEMP%, AppData\Local\Temp, or other writable locations, unsigned executable spawning cmd/powershell, or scheduled task creation with random naming patterns.

suggestion.title: Network Enumeration Spike - ARP Flooding & NBSTAT Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance objective requires active scanning. Botnet malware typically performs ARP/NBSTAT enumeration to map local network before credential attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal ARP request volume from single host (>100 requests/min to unique IPs), nbtstat -a or -A scans against Class C subnet, or NetBIOS enumeration commands executed by non-admin processes. Flag if source process is unsigned or running from temp directory.

suggestion.title: Code Execution Across Dev Environments
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Code is being written everywhere'—implies multi-environment code execution and deployment risk. No kill-chain reconstruction and no UC generated despite HIGH severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected code execution and interpreter invocation (shell, Python, Node.js, Go) across developer workstations and CI/CD systems. Correlate with unusual source-code repositories or build triggers that deviate from established patterns.

suggestion.title: Device as Persistent Attack Vector
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'device is the only constant'—suggests devices are central to threat model. No threat-actor motivations or persistence mechanisms identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious auto-start mechanisms (Registry boot folders, scheduled tasks, cron jobs) added to developer devices. Correlate with code-commit timestamps and unusual system-level privilege escalations on machines with git or IDE access.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Code Injection via Developer Devices
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses attacks via compromised dev endpoints, no UC addresses the hand-off between device compromise and supply-chain impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authenticated commits or pushes from non-standard git clients, unusual clone/fetch frequency, or API calls to package registries from developer devices at off-hours or from atypical locations.

suggestion.title: Detection of onering Malicious Rust Crate Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly names 'onering' as the compromised crate. Pipeline failed to generate initial-access detection for this known-bad dependency — explicit IOC present but not acted upon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cargo or rustc processes downloading/installing 'onering' package from crates.io or resolving it in Cargo.lock files. Monitor for dependency manifest modifications adding onering. Flag installations in development, CI/CD, or build systems.

suggestion.title: Code Exfiltration via Compromised Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'performs code exfiltration' as the attack outcome. Pipeline generated zero detections for the exfiltration phase despite being the primary attack indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rustc/cargo processes spawning child processes (curl, wget, Python, PowerShell) with outbound connections to non-standard infrastructure. Alert on source repository contents being archived or staged prior to transmission. Correlate code I/O operations during build with exfiltration-pattern network activity.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via Rust Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Rust crates execute via build.rs hooks during installation. Article implies execution but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process spawning from cargo/rustc context (shells, network utilities, system commands). Alert on build.rs files from ~/.cargo/registry or vendor/ invoking suspicious executables or network calls. Detect child process creation with abnormal parent relationships.

suggestion.title: Rust Build Manifest Tampering and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Compromised crates alter Cargo.toml or build.rs. Article title indicates crate-level compromise but pipeline generated zero persistence-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to build.rs files within ~/.cargo/registry/src. Alert on Cargo.toml entries with inline build dependencies, base64-encoded payloads, or obfuscated code. Track integrity hashes and timestamps of cached crate metadata.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Dependency Resolution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise requires resolution to a malicious version. Pipeline failed to generate detection for package registry resolution bypasses or version-pinning circumvention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor crates.io API queries and package registry resolution. Alert on Cargo.lock entries pinning unexpected onering versions or pre-release tags. Detect version constraint modifications or git-based dependencies masquerading as registry packages.

suggestion.title: Source Code Staging for Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration requires collection and staging. Pipeline generated zero collection-phase detections despite exfiltration being the stated attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build processes for archiving operations (tar, zip, rar, 7z) targeting source code directories. Alert on temporary files in /tmp, %AppData%, or build directories containing repository snapshots. Correlate archive creation timing with child process spawning and exfiltration network signatures.

suggestion.title: S/MIME Message Processing Crash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes heap use-after-free triggered by 'specially crafted PKCS7 or S/MIME signed messages.' Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite clear exploitation vector in mail processing pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal termination (non-zero exit codes, segmentation faults, or memory exceptions) in OpenSSL, postfix, sendmail, or mail client processes during S/MIME signature verification. Correlate with unusual child process spawning or memory access violations immediately following message processing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45447 Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Public CVE with disclosed technical attack surface; pipeline should generate proactive hunt for external reconnaissance. Article provides sufficient detail for attackers to identify and scan for vulnerable systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS handshakes with explicit PKCS7 cipher suite requests targeting mail servers (port 25, 465, 587). Look for repeated failed TLS handshakes or certificate validation errors from single source to multiple mail gateways in short window.

suggestion.title: RCE Post-Exploitation Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states heap corruption can 'allow attackers to run arbitrary code.' Pipeline completely missed the execution phase following successful heap corruption—the highest-impact detection opportunity.
