suggestion.title: JWT claims anomaly: issuance time mismatch or non-standard expiration patterns
suggestion.rationale: UC_21_1 title references 'extreme far-future JWT' — article describes attackers forging claims on tokens. No detections target JWT iat/exp/iss/aud mismatch, which would distinguish forged tokens from legitimately issued ones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode JWTs and flag: (1) exp > 1 year in future (vs. typical 1-24 hour lifetime), (2) iat (issued-at) timestamp in future relative to request time, (3) iss claim not matching expected go-base application identity, (4) multiple tokens with identical claims from different sources within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Baileys protocolMessage payload anomalies (spoofing detection)
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'maliciously crafted protocolMessage payload' sent to trigger fake 'messages.upsert' event with 'fake message key and payload.' Need direct detection of protocolMessage deserialization failures or key mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys session processes for deserialization exceptions or error codes related to protocolMessage validation. Flag when messages.upsert events originate from non-standard encryption contexts or contain message keys that don't match the payload signature state.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp/Baileys app state sync corruption indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key s...' (truncated). This is impact-level behavior—detection of app state divergence from canonical server state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag app state sync operations that fail consistency checks, trigger rollbacks, or result in mismatched local/remote key-value pairs. Monitor for repeated attempts to resync the same state blocks within short time windows (indicates attacker retries).

suggestion.title: Baileys npm package exploit attempt via Node.js process
suggestion.rationale: T1059.007 (JavaScript execution) is the actual weaponization. Detection should monitor Node.js processes loading baileys for suspicious behavior post-patch absence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js processes with baileys module loaded and versions < 7.0.0-rc12 / < 6.7.22 that issue network connections to WhatsApp infrastructure (143.110.0.0/16 or similar disclosed ranges). Correlate with unexpected file writes to node_modules or package-lock.json modifications.

suggestion.title: Fake utility executable downloaded and executed from browser
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'users who search for popular PC utilities online…downloading malware-laced files.' T1204.001 user execution and T1566/T1195 initial access missing from technique list despite being the infection trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .exe files with names spoofing legitimate utilities (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, WinRAR, etc.) from domains with high edit distance from legitimate vendors, followed by immediate execution from Downloads or Temp folder within same process chain.

suggestion.title: GPU/CPU resource hijacking from non-system process
suggestion.rationale: Article's explicit payload: 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU.' T1496 Resource Hijacking is the attack's primary impact but entirely absent from MITRE technique mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user-writable-location processes sustaining >75% GPU/CPU utilization for >10 minutes with network connections to known cryptocurrency mining pools or C2 infrastructure (gleeze.com, giize.com subdomain outbound attempts).

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect service installed from non-standard path
suggestion.rationale: Attack deploys ScreenConnect for remote hands-on-keyboard access. Legitimate ScreenConnect typically installs to Program Files; malware variant would use Temp, Downloads, or %APPDATA%. T1543.003 persistence technique not listed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe or ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe being created in or executed from user-writable directories (Temp, Desktop, Downloads, %APPDATA%), or service installation initiated by non-admin user account.

suggestion.title: Browser child process spawning service installer or RMM setup binary
suggestion.rationale: Execution chain absent from narrative reconstruction: browser downloads payload → payload spawns service setup (msiexec, sc.exe) or RMM installer. Detects T1204→T1543 handoff.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) spawning msiexec.exe, sc.exe, net.exe, or known RMM setup tools (ScreenConnect*, AnyDesk.exe, TeamViewer*.exe) as direct child without user UAC prompt recorded.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Dependency Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious package targeting software developers has been discovered on npm' — supply chain compromise is the initial access vector and must be detected at installation/import time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/add commands targeting the dbmux package or unusual package manager activity from development workstations. Correlate with subsequent file writes to node_modules and package-lock.json modifications. Flag installations of packages from unfamiliar registries or with newly-registered author accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Code Execution from npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hidden malware capable of giving attackers complete control' — the infection must execute after installation, likely through package lifecycle hooks (postinstall scripts) or require-time execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or anomalous process execution originating from node_modules directories, npm lifecycle scripts (postinstall/preinstall), or Node.js runtimes spawning unexpected child processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe, curl, wget). Monitor for file creation/modification in system directories triggered from npm context.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installed by Compromised Package
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malware grants 'complete control' over developer systems — this requires persistence beyond the current session, typically via scheduled tasks, registry modifications, or startup folder entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation, WMI event consumer installation, or registry modifications (Run keys, startup folders) originating from npm-related processes. Correlate with installation of the dbmux package within 5-60 minutes prior to persistence artifacts. Look for modifications to Windows Defender exclusions or firewall rules.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance or Credential Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gain 'complete control over any developer's system' — subsequent phases likely include credential harvesting (SSH keys, .git credentials, environment variables) and reconnaissance typical of developer-targeted malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes reading .ssh directories, .git configs, .npmrc, environment variable exfiltration, or credential manager access from npm/Node.js child processes. Monitor for unusual SSH or git operations shortly after package installation.

suggestion.title: DNS query to tax-phishing C2 domain
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 9 C2/payload-staging domains (guhxmg.com, naiqja.icu, etc.) but no hunt for their resolution. T1071 listed but undetected. Article states 'multi-stage malware' implying post-compromise callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query DNS logs for resolution of IOC domains (naiqja.icu, guhxmg.com, zh-welcome-1xbet.com, etc.) from non-browser processes or from system-level resolvers. Correlation to Processes.parent_process_name IN (powershell.exe, wscript.exe, rundll32.exe) increases confidence for post-compromise callback.

suggestion.title: In-memory code execution: suspicious rundll32/regsvr32 with no parent file
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'runs entirely in memory, leaving almost no trace behind' — classic process hollowing or direct memory injection. Article lists T1027 (obfuscation) and T1218 (LOLBin execution) but no hunt for orphan/unusual parent chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe, or mshta.exe spawned from non-standard parents (explorer.exe, svchost.exe, lsass.exe) with unusual command-line patterns (no visible DLL path, base64-encoded args, or ReflectiveInjection signatures). In-memory payloads often proxy through process hollowing.

suggestion.title: VBS script execution from Office context
suggestion.rationale: T1059.005 (Visual Basic) listed but no hunt. Article implies multi-stage delivery; VBS is common Office macro alternative for staging. 'Office app spawning script' hunt covers child process but not direct VBS file execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for wscript.exe or cscript.exe spawning from explorer.exe (user interaction with downloaded .vbs) or from Office parents (macro-sourced) with encoded or obfuscated command-line args. Correlate to Endpoint.File events for .vbs creation/modification in temp directories.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to staging domains with suspicious user-agent
suggestion.rationale: T1071.001 (HTTP/HTTPS) implied by C2 infrastructure but no hunt. Multi-stage malware requires callback for payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to IOC domains (taxations.cn-web-okooo.com, taxations.indiagov.it.com, ws4962.com) from non-browser processes (powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, wmic.exe) or with User-Agent headers mimicking Windows Update or generic patterns.

suggestion.title: Masquerade-domain phishing: sender domain spoofing Indian tax authority
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'impersonating official Indian government tax authorities' — classic T1036.001 spoof. No hunt for lookalike sender domains or display-name spoofing. Email header analysis needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails with SenderFromDomain NOT matching organizational whitelist AND (DisplayName contains 'tax', 'indian', 'gov', 'income', 'revenue' OR Subject matches regex like 'tax.*notification|refund|penalty'). Elevated risk if From-Domain resembles legitimate domain (taxations.indiagov.it.com vs indiagov.com).

suggestion.title: Potential IOC validation: IP 43.128.54.184 egress traffic to malware infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Single IPv4 listed (43.128.54.184) but no corroboration of its role. Is this the attacker infrastructure, compromised host, or relay? Missing UC to hunt for outbound traffic from internal IPs to this C2 IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from internal hosts to 43.128.54.184 on ports 80, 443, 8080, or dynamic ports. Correlate to process parents (powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, legitimate browser) and timestamps post-phishing click to validate IP as C2 vs. false positive.

suggestion.title: Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly flags 'critical vulnerabilities' from three major vendors—minimum expected detection UC monitors for attack signatures, HTTP POST patterns, or command injection attempts targeting known CVE endpoints. No such UC generated despite 'multiple critical vulnerabilities' language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to vendor product endpoints with suspicious payloads (SQL injection, command injection, path traversal patterns). Correlate with product version enumeration or exploitation POC activity. Flag process execution chains spawned by web services unexpected to that product.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Vulnerability Assessment by Vendor Product
suggestion.rationale: Article is patch-release notification—UC should detect systems running unpatched versions before remediation window closes. Pipeline extracted no version indicators, no asset-enumeration use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest software inventory for Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP product versions. Cross-reference against published CVE version ranges. Alert on systems running deprecated/EOL versions or those below patch cutoff dates announced in the advisory.

suggestion.title: Opportunistic Exploitation Post-Patch Release
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities trigger threat-actor pivot to exploit-in-the-wild within hours of patch release. Article title conveys urgency ('multiple critical') but pipeline produced no UCs for post-exploitation activity (lateral movement, persistence, exfiltration) expected to follow successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral-movement patterns (SMB/RDP to secondary hosts, scheduled task creation, credential dumping tools) originating from systems identified as compromised via Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP exploitation. Baseline expected asset-to-asset communication and flag anomalies within 24–72 hours post-patch release.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Ivanti Sentry Request Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-10520 'stems from an OS command injection weakness' enabling RCE as root. This is the primary exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP request logs for command injection metacharacters in parameters: pipes (|), semicolons (;), backticks (`), command substitution ($(), $(cmd)). Correlate requests to endpoints processing external input with unusual subprocess creation or system command execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to Ivanti Sentry Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10523 is 'critical authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers.' Alert on admin endpoint access without valid session/token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative endpoints lacking valid authentication headers or session cookies. Flag 401/403 status codes followed by successful requests from the same source without credential re-submission.

suggestion.title: Rogue Administrative Account Creation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers via CVE-2026-10523 can 'create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' Monitor user creation with admin role assignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry audit logs showing creation of new users with administrative privileges, especially when preceded by unauthenticated HTTP requests to admin endpoints or within sessions originating from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Code Execution from Ivanti Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10520 enables attackers to 'execute code with root privileges.' Detect privilege escalation beyond the Sentry service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by the Ivanti Sentry service account that escalate to root/SYSTEM privileges. Flag sudoers invocations, setuid binary executions, or kernel-level privilege escalation originating from web application handlers.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions: R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1. Identify systems running unpatched releases of CVE-2026-10520 / CVE-2026-10523.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scan results for Ivanti Sentry instances with versions prior to R10.5.2 (R10.5.x branch), R10.6.2 (R10.6.x branch), or R10.7.1 (R10.7.x branch). Escalate external-facing or mobile-gateway-role instances.

suggestion.title: Defender Service Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability grants SYSTEM access via Defender—core attack chain is Defender abuse for privilege elevation. Must detect local privesc originating from MsMpEng.exe or landing in SYSTEM context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by MsMpEng.exe or MsSense.exe running as SYSTEM with suspicious parent-child relationships or command lines. Flag unexpected elevation of child processes via Defender service context. Correlate with registry writes to Defender config paths from unprivileged source contexts preceding SYSTEM-level activity.

suggestion.title: Defender Signed Binary Abuse Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once SYSTEM is granted, attacker controls privileged Defender executables (MsMpEng.exe, MpCmdRun.exe) for lateral movement, credential access, or code execution masquerading as legitimate antimalware activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Defender binaries spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or net.exe outside of standard remediation workflows. Monitor for unsigned DLL loads by Defender processes or DLL injection into Defender from external sources. Alert on Defender binaries accessing credential storage or network shares with non-standard access patterns.

suggestion.title: RoguePlanet Zero-Day Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability named RoguePlanet must be tracked by name and CVE (not provided in truncated article). Detection requires identifying malicious inputs/payloads targeting Defender parsing or policy handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for crafted file submissions to Defender scan, suspicious scheduled task creation targeting Defender, or malformed configuration changes to Windows Defender settings. Alert on Defender version/build correlation with disclosed vulnerability versions. Detect exploitation via file paths, registry keys, or network requests matching published RoguePlanet PoC indicators.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM-Context Registry and File Modifications via Defender
suggestion.rationale: SYSTEM-level access enables persistence and privilege hardening—attacker will write to HKLM for boot persistence, RDP backdoors, or scheduled tasks. Defender-sourced writes to sensitive registry paths indicate post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag writes to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run*, HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services, or terminal services registry paths originating from Defender processes or SYSTEM-context children. Alert on unexpected modifications to Defender exclusion lists or disabled tamper protection changes.

suggestion.title: Defender Process Anomalies Indicating Active Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Defender service will show behavioral anomalies: unusual CPU/memory spikes, unexpected child processes, network activity, or file access patterns inconsistent with antimalware scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline MsMpEng.exe resource consumption and network behavior. Alert on sustained anomalies: high CPU without corresponding scan activity, outbound connections to non-Microsoft IPs, large data exfiltration via Defender processes, or WMI event subscriptions created by Defender-elevated contexts. Detect Defender proxy abuse for C2 communication.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42897 XSS Payload in Email to OWA Users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user. If the user opens the email in Outlook Web Access and certain interaction conditions are met, arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context.' Core attack vector with no detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails to Exchange users for embedded JavaScript payloads, script tags, event handlers (onclick, onload, onerror), or suspicious encoded content targeting OWA. Baseline: high false-positive rate; refine on known CVE-2026-42897 PoC patterns. Flag emails that reach OWA parsing layer after June 2026 if unpatched Exchange is detected.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary JavaScript Execution in Outlook Web Access Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' during OWA. This is post-delivery execution that detection should capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA sessions (typically HTTPS to /owa/ or /ecp/) for injection of unexpected JavaScript execution, unusual DOM modifications, or frame manipulation. Detect parent process OWA.exe or w3wp.exe (IIS) spawning script interpreters or making unexpected network calls. Look for session tokens being read or exfiltrated after JavaScript execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Administrative Action Post-OWA XSS Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies follow-on abuse: 'If the user opens the email in Outlook Web Access' leading to code execution, which typically precedes account takeover or mailbox rule creation. XSS in OWA can steal session tokens for privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate OWA session with suspicious administrative actions (mailbox rule creation, forwarding rules, delegate access grant, AzureAD app authorization) within 5 minutes of unusual JavaScript execution or XSS payload delivery. Especially flag actions from unexpected source IPs or non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Exchange Server Running Unpatched Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'affects Exchange Server 2016, Exchange Server 2019, and Exchange Server Subscription Edition.' CISA mandate to patch within two weeks by May 29. Unpatched systems post-deadline are indicators of compromise or negligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Exchange servers and flag any running Exchange Server 2016/2019/SE without June 2026 patch or EEMS mitigation applied post-May 15. Cross-reference with security logs for any exploitation attempts (XSS payloads, unusual OWA traffic) on unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: EEMS Mitigation Bypass or Disable Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft rolled out automatic temporary mitigation through the Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service (EEMS).' Attackers would attempt to disable or bypass EEMS to exploit the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell commands or Exchange Management Shell commands attempting to disable EEMS mitigations, modify Exchange service binaries, or revert security settings. Flag Set-IRMConfiguration, Remove-IRMConfiguration, or direct XML config modifications on vulnerable Exchange versions.

suggestion.title: Historical Exchange Vulnerability Exploitation by Ransomware
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Over the past five years, CISA has added 20 Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerabilities to its list of exploited security flaws, with ransomware gangs having exploited 14 of them.' Establishes ransomware interest in Exchange attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain historical detections for prior ransomware-exploited Exchange CVEs (e.g., ProxyLogon chain, ProxyShell) and correlate with CVE-2026-42897 exploitation attempts. If legacy techniques observed alongside new XSS payloads, escalate to ransomware campaign detection.

suggestion.title: Microsoft RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Critical RCE Bugs' but pipeline generated zero detection hypotheses. RCE vulnerabilities in widely-used Microsoft products are high-priority exploitation targets requiring behavioral and signature-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution, unusual child processes spawned from patched Microsoft services (e.g., SYSTEM-privileged children from Exchange, Windows Print Spooler, or RDP Service), and anomalous network connections to ports typically associated with RCE exploitation. Correlate with failed patching inventory.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Microsoft Software Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'record 206 flaws' requiring urgent patching. Pipeline should flag detection of unpatched versions as critical baseline before exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify endpoints running Microsoft product versions matching vulnerable baselines described in patch advisory. Query software inventory for presence of affected versions and lack of corresponding KB/patch application within 48 hours of advisory.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Zero-Day Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'three Zero-Days' without specifying if any enable privilege escalation, but zero-days in Microsoft products frequently chain to privesc. This gap in kill-chain reconstruction is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation chains initiated from unprivileged or service account contexts correlating with known RCE or vulnerability exploitation patterns. Monitor for impersonation tokens, process elevation anomalies, and access to high-privilege resources immediately following suspicious RCE-phase activity.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Lateral Movement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Patch advisories for critical RCE assume compromise risk; pipeline generated no post-exploitation detection use cases despite 'critical' severity designation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After RCE exploitation window, look for lateral movement from affected host: SMB C$ access, WinRM connections, credential material extraction (LSASS dumping), and propagation to other endpoints. Baseline against normal inter-system traffic from that host type.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Patch Deployment Monitoring for Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'record 206 flaws' requiring rapid patching. Pipeline should generate detection use case validating patch application to reduce re-exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Update logs, WSUS reports, and installer process execution to confirm KB patches are applied. Flag hosts that block updates, fail patch application, or remain unpatched >7 days post-advisory for prioritized remediation.

suggestion.title: Inbound SSH from Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'The researcher shared the following IP addresses as IOCs related to these attacks: 142.11.200[.]186-190, 108.174.202[.]99, 176.120.22[.]24'. Attack narrative: 'script...attempts to connect to them over SSH'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any inbound SSH connections (port 22 or variants) originating from 142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, or 176.120.22.24. Escalate if destination is a PeopleSoft server or known database host.

suggestion.title: SSH Brute Force with PeopleSoft Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack payload: 'attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm. If password authentication fails, the script attempts to use SSH key-based authentication as a fallback.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed SSH authentication attempts against accounts psoft, oracle, linuxadm from external sources. Alert if >3 failures within 60s from same source, or if authentication method switches from password to key-based on same account.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note File Creation in PeopleSoft Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article documents payload: 'shell script designed to create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT on an internal PeopleSoft server after it is breached' and 'drops the ransom note into directories associated with PeopleSoft web and application servers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft installation and web server directories for creation of files matching 'README-*.txt', 'HACKED*.txt', or ransom notice patterns. Alert on writes by non-privileged or service accounts.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Agent Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cybersecurity researcher...found several exposed online directories containing tooling related to this attack...visible were staging materials, including MeshCentral agents, and a defacement and credential spray script.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshCentral agent binary execution (meshagent, meshagentservice processes) or network connections to *.meshcentral.com or known MeshCentral C2 IPs. Flag agent deployment to non-standard directories.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'ShinyHunters says they are using a gadget chain of old and zero-day vulnerabilities to conduct the attacks.' Targeting 'cloud and on-premises Oracle PeopleSoft customer instances.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft HTTPS interfaces for exploitation signatures: serialized Java objects (ysoserial gadget chains in base64), unusual HTTP request sequences targeting well-known PeopleSoft endpoints, or process spawning (bash, sh) under web service account immediately after failed HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from PeopleSoft Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms data theft: 'claiming to have stolen data from 300 instances across more than 100 organizations...Nottingham University...data has already been published on the ShinyHunters data leak site.' Implies large-scale extraction and transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound data transfers from PeopleSoft systems. Monitor for connections from PeopleSoft servers to attacker infrastructure (142.11.200.0/24, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24, azurenetfiles[.]net). Flag archive creation (tar, zip, 7z) in data directories before transfer.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Queries to ServiceNow Backend Instance Tables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication.' This is the core attack mechanism and was not surfaced by the pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT/query operations against system tables (cmdb_ci, sys_user, incident, change_request, sc_request) from unauthenticated or non-admin service accounts. Monitor for bulk queries without corresponding UI session activity.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of ServiceNow Access Control Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is described as 'improper access controls'—a direct exploitation of authentication/authorization. Missing T1190 mapping indicates pipeline did not infer exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests bypassing role-based access control (RBAC) checks—e.g., non-admin users accessing /api/now/* endpoints, requests with null/bypass ACL parameters, or API calls succeeding after failed authentication.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Traffic to Article IOC 51.159.98.241
suggestion.rationale: Article lists IOC and explicitly recommends network hunt template, yet pipeline generated zero UCs and empty IOC dict. Standard hunter template should have fired.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from ServiceNow application servers/clients to 51.159.98.241 on any port. Monitor for sustained beaconing, data exfiltration patterns, or secondary payloads.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Export from ServiceNow CMDB and User Tables
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'data exposure across enterprise environments'—implies large-scale collection/exfiltration. Pipeline kill-chain is blank; missing exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume table exports, bulk API GETs returning >10k rows, exports to external cloud storage, or staged data (compression, S3 upload, email delivery) of customer configuration/user records.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of ServiceNow Instance Tables and Schema
suggestion.rationale: Attack involves querying 'customer instance tables'—attacker must first enumerate available tables. T1526 (enumerate cloud resources) should be core technique; pipeline missed this step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated table/API endpoint enumeration: requests to /api/now/table/*, /api/now/ui/*, or schema queries; 404s followed by 200s on different table names; or requests listing available tables without corresponding business context.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Revocation Triggers Destructive Filesystem Wipe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'a "dead-man switch" that is installed when the malware uses a victim's stolen GitHub token as an exfiltration channel. The component monitors the token's validity every minute and, if it's revoked, executes a destructive command (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents), recursively deleting files and directories in the user's home and Documents folders.' Unique, high-fidelity pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on recursive directory deletion commands (rm -rf ~/ or ~/Documents) executed within 2 minutes of GitHub token revocation or API auth failure events. Correlate Process Events (rm with -rf flag) with WebActivity or API logs showing credential invalidation. Establish baseline for legitimate home-directory cleanup; flag aggressive multi-directory recursion outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Credential Store Harvesting from CI/CD, Cloud Providers, and Password Managers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The framework harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores, and abuses them to compromise npm, PyPI, and RubyGems packages.' Describes T1555/T1040 pattern not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process file-system access to credential vaults: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/config, password manager databases (1Password, Bitwarden, Keepass vaults). Alert on suspicious process parents (npm, node, Python interpreters) reading these paths. Baseline legitimate credential access during CI/CD; flag out-of-band reads correlating with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH and AWS Systems Manager with Harvested Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM).' Explicit lateral movement attack vector not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SSH outbound connections from developer machines to internal/AWS resources with credential access logs (aws-cli calls, ssh-key usage). Alert on AWS SSM StartSession API calls using credentials sourced from compromised dev machines. Flag: sessions to unusual targets, sessions outside business hours, sessions using previously-unseen SSH keys, rapid session activity from single source.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Writes to AI Coding Tools (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Cline, Gemini, Kiro)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline.' Supply-chain poisoning + defense evasion specific to developer toolchains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to AI tool config directories: ~/.config/{cursor,copilot,claude,cline}/*, ~/.cline/, ~/.cursor/. Alert on unauthorized modifications to API keys, model settings, or plugin/extension configurations. Flag writes outside user-interactive tool installers or update processes. Correlate with other IoCs: obfuscated parent processes, unsigned executables, or exfiltration network activity.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Poisoning: Anomalous npm/PyPI/RubyGems Publishing from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'uses those to compromise legitimate repositories and packages, publishing trojanized versions to infect downstream developers and repeat the cycle.' Affects npm, PyPI, RubyGems, JFrog Artifactory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish, PyPI upload, gem push, and JFrog Artifactory PUT operations. Alert on publishing from unusual IP geographies, out-of-business-hours timing, or new publisher accounts on established packages. Flag: packages with obfuscated/randomized names per build, embedded binary assets, executable payloads. Cross-check with git credential compromise indicators and build-system anomalies.

suggestion.title: Polymorphic Multi-Layer Build-Time Encryption and Obfuscation Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'five-stage build pipeline that generates unique payloads for each build... per-file AES-256-GCM encryption... JavaScript obfuscation... three layers of encryption. Random keys and a randomized outer encoding layer ensure that each generated sample differs from previous builds, making signature-based detection and static analysis harder.' Process-level defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual cryptographic operations in build contexts: OpenSSL/GnuPG with AES-256-GCM parameters spawned by build tools (npm, cargo, pip, gradle). Alert on build processes generating high-entropy unique binaries per commit (hash entropy analysis). Flag JavaScript obfuscation tools (terser, uglify-js, webpack with obfuscation plugins) running outside normal package build steps. Baseline legitimate build-time encryption; escalate on frequency/parameter anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-5027 Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero use cases. This is the primary vulnerability indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Langflow services (product name present in title) on default or common ports followed by suspicious response codes or patterns. CVE-2026-5027 exploitation typically involves unauthenticated POST/GET requests to vulnerable endpoints. Baseline all Langflow installations and flag any public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Langflow RCE Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unauthenticated RCE' explicitly. Post-exploitation detection for process execution following successful exploitation is critical but absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or child processes from Langflow application processes or the application user context. RCE payloads typically result in shell process creation. Correlate with web server logs showing prior unauthenticated request patterns.

suggestion.title: Langflow Installation Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'Langflow' as the vulnerable product. No inventory/discovery use case generated despite this being essential for triage of unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Langflow-specific HTTP headers, response signatures, or UI fingerprints in web logs/proxies. Search for DNS queries to 'langflow' domains or subdomains. Map instances against patch status queries (check /version or /health endpoints) to identify unpatched instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-5027.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Unexpected Child Process Execution with Privilege Elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability as a 'post-exploitation primitive,' implying code execution within low-privilege context escalating to SYSTEM. Exploiting CVE-2026-45586 would spawn elevated child processes from CTFMON. Direct phrase: 'allows a local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ctfmon.exe spawning child processes with elevated privileges (SYSTEM, LocalService). Flag unexpected executables (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, svchost.exe). Create baseline of legitimate CTFMON children; alert on deviations or unsigned binaries in sequence.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL Injection or Module Load to CTFMON
suggestion.rationale: CTFMON privilege escalation exploits typically leverage DLL injection or unauthorized module loading as the escalation vector. Article implies code execution capability within low-privilege context; DLL injection is a standard privilege escalation attack for Windows services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or system-folder DLLs loaded by ctfmon.exe. Flag DLL loads from user-writable paths (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%). Monitor for CreateRemoteThread or WriteProcessMemory targeting CTFMON from low-privilege processes; correlate with CVE-2026-45586 indicators.

suggestion.title: Windows Service Registry Modification Related to CTFMON
suggestion.rationale: CTFMON runs as a Windows service; CVE-2026-45586 exploitation involves service/registry hijacking for escalation. Article: 'escalate to SYSTEM' suggests leveraging Windows service machinery or system object manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services from low-privilege processes. Flag service creation, SetServiceObjectSecurity calls, or SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG operations from CTFMON context. Correlate with suspicious process spawning or DLL injection events.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Behavioral Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Create a composite behavioral signature for CVE-2026-45586 exploitation. Article describes privilege escalation from 'low privileges to SYSTEM'; detecting the sequence of exploitation indicators (child spawning, DLL injection, service modification) within a time window is a strong post-exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create correlation rule: CTFMON or low-privilege parent process → unexpected DLL load + elevated child process spawn + registry modification under HKLM\Services, all within 5-minute window. Alert on sequence match as strong indicator of active CVE-2026-45586 exploitation.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Disablement or Trail Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article title frames 'Blinding the Watchmen' as abusing cloud logging for defense evasion. Disabling CloudTrail is the primary blinding technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on StopLogging, DeleteTrail, PutEventSelectors (with logging disabled), or UpdateTrail API calls. Correlate disablement with preceding privilege escalation or credential access activity to detect post-compromise cover-up.

suggestion.title: S3 Logging Bucket Policy Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'S3' and 'log storage'. Attackers modify bucket policies to prevent log delivery or delete logs after intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PutBucketPolicy, DeleteBucketPolicy, and PutBucketAcl on S3 buckets designated as CloudTrail destinations. Alert on removal of logging service principals or public-read removal.

suggestion.title: Log Sink or Aggregation Route Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'log router' abuse; GCP Cloud Logging sinks and log forwarding rules are primary targets for defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CreateSink, UpdateSink, DeleteSink (GCP) or equivalent log aggregation API modifications. Flag deletion of sinks or modification that removes BigQuery/Pub-Sub destinations for forensic logs.

suggestion.title: Batch Log Deletion from Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article scope includes 'log storage' tampering; post-compromise attackers execute DeleteObject/DeleteBucket on logging destinations to destroy evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid or bulk DeleteObject calls against S3 buckets or Cloud Storage buckets configured for CloudTrail/audit log receipt. Correlate with antecedent data exfiltration or privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Logging Disabled Before Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates coordinated attacks on logging infrastructure; adversaries disable logging, pivot laterally, then re-enable logging to hide activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CloudTrail disablement with subsequent unusual cross-account access, credential creation, or VPC/security-group modifications. Detect re-enablement of logging after a suspicious activity window.

suggestion.title: KMS Key Rotation or Deletion for Encrypted Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses log storage tampering; if logs are encrypted with customer-managed KMS, attackers may rotate or delete keys to render logs unreadable without destroying them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ScheduleKeyDeletion, DisableKey, and CreateGrant calls on KMS keys used for CloudTrail log encryption. Alert if key state changes occur outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawned from Chrome/Chromium Renderer
suggestion.rationale: V8 sandbox escapes typically spawn system processes post-code-execution; article states exploitation is 'in the wild' but provides no details. Attack must include execution-to-impact bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on chrome.exe, msedge.exe, or brave.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or regsvcs.exe with obfuscated command lines or unusual parent-child patterns. Correlate with network communication or file writes to %temp%.

suggestion.title: Chrome Process Crash Followed by Rapid Restart and Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Memory-corruption bugs in V8 may cause process termination before or after exploitation. Attacker may trigger crash, exploit, succeed on retry, or establish persistence. No article body to clarify exploitation flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome/Chromium crashes (exit code -1073740791, 0xc0000374, memory violations) followed within seconds by process restart and unexpected DNS queries, HTTP POST to suspicious IPs, or TLS handshakes.

suggestion.title: User Navigation to Newly Registered or Low-Reputation Domain Followed by Browser Crash
suggestion.rationale: Typical V8 exploitation vectors: watering hole, phishing, drive-by download. Article title alone provides no attack-vector context. Detection should assume web-based delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag users clicking links to domains registered <30 days prior, or domains with low domain reputation scores (VirusTotal, Cisco Talos), immediately followed by Chrome crash or unexpected child-process spawning.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Heap Spray or Unusual Memory Allocation Pattern in Chrome Process
suggestion.rationale: V8 type-confusion and memory-corruption exploits rely on heap shaping; article provides no technical details of vulnerability class, so detection must assume common V8 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome processes with abnormal memory growth (>500MB delta in <5s), repeated allocation/deallocation cycles, or suspicious page-allocation patterns correlating with JavaScript execution and subsequent code-execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Modification of Chrome User Profile or Preferences Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article does not clarify persistence or post-exploitation objectives. V8 code execution may lead to browser hijacking, extension injection, or preference tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Local AppData\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default (Preferences, Secure Preferences, Extensions) or equivalent Chromium paths for file modifications outside of normal Chrome update cycles, especially targeting extension manifests or search-engine settings.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-11645 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite direct template guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management tools for unpatched Google Chrome, Chromium, Microsoft Edge, or Opera browsers. Focus on assets where patch date is before 2026-06-23 (federal due date). Alert on any detected instance of V8 versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-11645.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution inside a sandbox' but pipeline provided no execution-phase detection. Successful exploitation should manifest as unusual child processes or privilege escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for elevated process spawning from browser processes (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, opera.exe) or unexpected privilege escalation following browser activity. Correlate with browser crashes or exceptions in V8 logs as potential exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTML Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is explicitly 'crafted HTML page' but pipeline generated no detection for HTML-based delivery or execution. This is the initial infection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of untrusted HTML files via email or web download followed by browser execution. Flag HTML attachments from external domains, HTML files downloaded from non-standard sources, or HTML rendering immediately after receipt.

suggestion.title: V8 Out-of-Bounds Exception Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: CVE describes 'Out-of-Bounds Read and Write'; failed exploitation attempts will generate detectable exceptions or memory access violations in browser crash logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor system and browser event logs for out-of-bounds memory access exceptions, segmentation faults, or access violations originating from V8 / browser processes. Cluster by source HTML origin and alert on multiple failures from single domain.

suggestion.title: Post-Sandbox Escape Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: If exploitation succeeds, attacker gains code execution and may establish C2. Article implies potential for lateral movement via remote code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from Chrome, Edge, or Opera processes, especially to non-whitelisted IPs, uncommon ports, or known malware C2 ranges. Baseline normal browser traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references template `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure` with explicit instruction to substitute CVE-2026-20245. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventories for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager or vManage instances. Flag any report of CVE-2026-20245 or absence of patched version 20.9.x+ (assumed fix). Identify externally exposed instances via DNS CNAME, firewall rules, or IP geolocation.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Crafted File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary commands as root by supplying a crafted file'. No use case for file-based exploitation vector detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints for unusual file uploads (especially .sh, .py, binary, or config files) to web interface or filesystem paths. Correlate uploads with subsequent root-level process execution within 60 seconds. Flag uploads by non-admin service accounts.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Command Execution from vManage Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary commands as root'—explicit privilege escalation. Pipeline missed privilege-escalation kill-chain phase and detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vmanage, confd, or related daemons) with UID=0. Especially flag shell command execution (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, /bin/python) under root context initiated from web interface or file-upload paths.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Patch Compliance by Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-23' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Pipeline generated zero use cases for deadline-driven compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instance not patched to version 20.9.x (or advised fix) by 2026-06-23. Audit patch-delay timeline: days unpatched post-deadline. Prioritize systems exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: Authentication Abuse Against Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, local attacker'. Requires pre-compromise access. No use case for auth-chain detection preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager login attempts for brute-force, credential-spraying, or default-credential use. Look for rapid auth failures followed by successful login. Correlate suspicious logins with crafted-file uploads or root command execution.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Exposed Assets Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'Extensible Operating System' with CISA KEV status and federal patch due 2026-06-23; any exposed EOS instance is a direct exploitation target for this known-wild CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Arista EOS devices via port scanning, SNMP, device management interface probing, or asset inventory. Immediately flag any device accessible from untrusted/external networks. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-7473 positive results.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerability Detected on Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'CVE-2026-7473'; vulnerability scanners must flag any Arista EOS system as vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-7473 on Arista EOS. Alert immediately if exposed; escalate if unpatched >30 days before federal due date 2026-06-23.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Packet Decapsulation Activity on Arista Switch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vulnerability: 'incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP'—the exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS for tunneled packets (GRE, VXLAN, Geneve) being unexpectedly decapsulated and retransmitted to unintended destinations. Baseline normal tunnel behavior; alert on sudden increases in decapsulation events with malformed headers or unexpected egress next-hops.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Packet Forwarding from Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'forwards other unexpected tunneled packet'—the observable impact phase when exploitation causes traffic misrouting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect egress anomalies from Arista EOS: spikes in packet volume, tunneled traffic decapsulated to management subnets, packets retransmitted to atypical next-hops, or tunnel protocols on non-standard interfaces. Correlate against device forwarding table baseline.

suggestion.title: Malformed Tunnel Packet Sent to Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability involves 'incomplete comparison with missing factors'—implies attacker constructs crafted tunneled packets to trigger the comparison logic flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IDS/IPS detects malformed/incomplete tunnel packets (GRE, VXLAN) delivered to known Arista EOS IPs. High confidence if packet triggers error responses or observable behavior changes on vulnerable device. Establish baseline of valid tunnel packet structures from logs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt: POST to pheditor.php action=terminal with command-injection payload in dir parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unsanitized dir POST parameter' and 'shell metacharacters' are injection vector. Current UC_33_4 is too generic (all POSTs). Need specific hunt for POST body containing known injection patterns ($(, backticks, semicolons, pipes) in dir or cmd parameters.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with body inspection
HTTP request logs from Apache/Nginx with mod_security enabled
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to /pheditor.php where action=terminal and dir or cmd parameters contain shell metacharacters ($, `, ;, |, &, >, <). Correlate successful requests (HTTP 200/302) to subsequent process spawning or file creation by web server user within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Authenticated session to admin panel followed by terminal RCE exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any authenticated user' can exploit. Current detections miss the authentication context. Need to hunt for suspicious exploitation chains: valid session + POST to pheditor.php + process spawning.
log_sources: Apache/Nginx access logs with session tokens
Endpoint process telemetry with parent HTTP session tracking
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authenticated HTTP sessions to pheditor.php with subsequent shell process spawning from web server user. Flag if shell spawning occurs within 10 seconds of suspicious POST; indicates validated session was leveraged for exploitation.

suggestion.title: Directory listing/traversal via 'dir' parameter prior to command injection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'dir' parameter as injection point. Pattern suggests potential directory discovery/enumeration phase before exploitation. Article states vulnerability 'completely bypassing the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist', implying attacker must probe available commands first.
log_sources: Web logs with POST body inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for repeated POST requests to pheditor.php action=terminal with varying dir parameter values (e.g., /, /bin, /usr/bin, /var) before a successful command execution. Cluster these discovery requests by source IP + session token.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell or C2 connection from PHP web server process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE with web server privileges. Attacker would likely establish persistence or callback. No UC addresses outbound network connections from PHP processes to external IP/port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network connections from php-fpm, apache2, nginx processes to non-RFC1918 IP addresses or known C2 domains. Combine with process lineage from pheditor.php POST request within prior 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Installation Executes Credential Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 19 poisoned packages that 'auto-run Bun credential stealer' on installation. Pipeline missed the core execution pattern: package post-install scripts trigger malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python/pip processes spawning unexpected child processes (especially Bun-related binaries) during or immediately after package installation. Look for setup.py or install-time hooks executing system commands or accessing credential stores.

suggestion.title: Credential Store Access Following PyPI Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Stealer explicitly targets 'Bun credentials'; article indicates automated credential harvesting. Pipeline failed to generate detection for credential access patterns post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Python/pip process execution with subsequent file access to ~/.bun, ~/.bunrc, ~/.npmrc, or similar credential storage directories. Detect reads from credential managers or env var dumps that follow package install windows.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'PyPI Attack'; attack vector is poisoned packages on the official repository. Pipeline did not surface supply-chain compromise as kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install requests to PyPI for packages matching known or suspected compromised versions. Baseline normal package install sources per organization; flag installs from unexpected mirrors or with typo-squatting patterns.

suggestion.title: Bun Credential Stealer Post-Installation Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Stealer harvests credentials then must exfiltrate; article mentions 'auto-run' but pipeline generated no detection for C2 communication or credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network egress for beaconing patterns or unusual DNS lookups originating from processes spawned during pip install. Detect encrypted/obfuscated outbound traffic correlated with credential stealer execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Package Setup.py or Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'auto-run' payload; PyPI packages deliver malicious code via setup.py or install-time hooks. Pipeline should have flagged this mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect setup.py and pyproject.toml for entry points, console scripts, or install-time commands that invoke non-Python binaries (e.g., shell commands, binary downloads). Trigger on setup() calls with `scripts=` or `entry_points=` that reference external executables.

suggestion.title: Package Typo-Squatting or Repository Mirror Fallback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often rely on package name similarity or mirror injection. Article does not explicitly confirm this, but pipeline should have suggested typo-squatting detection as a supply-chain use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a baseline of legitimate package names per environment. Alert on pip install or import attempts for package names within edit-distance 1-2 of known libraries (typo-squatting). Correlate with install source to detect non-official PyPI repos.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 LiteLLM Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild'. This is the attack's entry point and should trigger detection of HTTP requests to LiteLLM endpoints with known exploit payloads or suspicious parameter injection patterns. Title establishes the vulnerability name and in-the-wild exploitation, yet pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill chain context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to LiteLLM API endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /completion/*) containing payloads consistent with unauthenticated parameter injection or code template injection. Flag requests that bypass expected authentication headers or originate from untrusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE', indicating successful exploitation enables remote code execution without credentials. Pipeline failed to identify the execution phase or expected command-shell activity post-compromise. This is a critical attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful CVE-2026-42271 exploitation, monitor for unexpected process spawning from LiteLLM service accounts (e.g., python.exe, bash, cmd.exe, /bin/sh). Look for parent-child process chains where the parent is the vulnerable application. Flag execution of reconnaissance commands (whoami, ifconfig, systeminfo) or reverse-shell payloads.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Compromise Behavioral Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE implies attacker gains arbitrary code execution within LiteLLM process context. Pipeline should have identified behavioral monitoring signals: unexpected network connections, file writes outside expected directories, or privilege escalation attempts initiated by the service. Title indicates impact severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LiteLLM process making unexpected outbound network connections (especially to non-cloud infrastructure), writing binaries to temp directories, modifying system files, or clearing event logs. Correlate with exploitation timeline to establish causal link.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Payload Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: "Exploited in the wild" signals active, weaponized POC or exploit kit. Pipeline should have surfaced expected payload signatures, file hashes, or command patterns observed in wild exploitation samples. Zero IOCs extracted suggests no payload analysis was performed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures for known LiteLLM RCE payloads (if disclosed in public exploits). Monitor for suspicious request bodies containing template injection syntax, escape sequences, or code execution primitives. Flag file uploads containing base64-encoded or obfuscated scripts.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Accessibility Post-Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: If service is accessible unauthenticated, pipeline should propose detection of anomalous access patterns: brute-force attempts to exploit the flaw, repeated requests from same source, or volumetric exploitation campaigns. Title's 'in the wild' status implies attack is widespread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request volume and distribution to LiteLLM endpoints by source IP. Detect anomalies in request patterns, user-agents, or geolocation of origin IPs. Baseline normal LiteLLM API access and flag deviations (e.g., mass requests from VPS providers, Tor exit nodes, or previously unseen geographic regions).

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title and URL explicitly reference 'authentication-bypass'. Pipeline missed the primary attack vector. Web logs showing auth endpoint abuse, forced session creation, or admin escalation without valid credentials are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /ucp.php?mode=login or /app.php/user/login endpoints with anomalous parameter sequences, token reuse across sessions, or auth tokens created without corresponding login events. Monitor for admin account creation immediately following failed auth attempts from the same source.

suggestion.title: phpBB Remote Code Execution via Vulnerability Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'RCE' in title. Post-auth-bypass, execution indicators must be detectable: unusual command spawning from PHP processes, write-then-execute patterns in web-accessible directories, or template injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned by PHP-FPM or Apache worker processes. Alert on execution of file-write operations (touch, echo, wget) followed immediately by PHP script execution in the same session. Detect encoded or obfuscated command strings in PHP process arguments.

suggestion.title: Rogue Admin Account Creation in phpBB Database
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE compromise typically persists by creating administrative users. Article describes 10-year-old vulnerability with industrial-scale adoption, implying mature attacker playbooks centered on persistence through user creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database process logs for INSERT queries against phpbb_users and phpbb_user_group tables. Alert when new accounts are granted GROUP_ID 4 (administrators) without corresponding phpbb_users_admin audit records. Detect bulk user creation patterns or accounts with randomized/obfuscated names created within minutes of exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Creation or Modification in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: RCE allows file write; attackers drop shells or backdoors. Article scope (tens of millions affected) indicates high operator sophistication and likely multi-stage payloads requiring file persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file creation outside scheduled maintenance windows in phpBB root, styles/, ext/, or includes/ directories. Monitor modification timestamps of config.php, functions_admin.php, or template files when no code deployment occurred. Flag files written from web service process contexts.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Encoded Payload Execution in phpBB Context
suggestion.rationale: Mature phpBB exploits use eval(), base64_decode(), gzuncompress(), or assert() to load payloads. Article's 10-year-old timeline suggests attackers have perfected obfuscation techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP eval() calls with base64-encoded or gzipped arguments in request parameters. Monitor for proc_open(), passthru(), or system() calls receiving data from HTTP request objects ($_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST) without sanitization. Flag include() statements with remote URLs or php:// stream wrappers.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from Compromised phpBB Host
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers establish C2 to stage secondary payloads. Article mentions 'tens of thousands of forums' affected, strongly implying a coordinated campaign with infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from web server processes to non-ASN infrastructure (especially bulletproof hosting, dynamic DNS, recently-registered domains). Monitor for DNS queries from PHP processes to suspicious domains. Flag data exfiltration patterns (POST requests with large payloads to external IPs).

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beacon Detection (JDY)
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 1,500+ compromised devices performing 'cyber reconnaissance'—implies active command-and-control channel. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no C&C kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous outbound connections from multiple internal hosts to the same external IP or domain with consistent timing/volume patterns. Filter for suspicious DNS queries to known botnet C&C infrastructure or DGA domains characteristic of JDY variants.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Activity Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle explicitly states purpose is 'cyber reconnaissance'—pipeline failed to map this to discovery/reconnaissance kill-chain phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution (net view, arp, ipconfig, tasklist, wmic, systeminfo) on compromised hosts. Correlate with outbound SMB/SNMP scanning or ARP broadcasts indicating internal network enumeration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Botnet Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: 1,500+ device footprint implies lateral propagation mechanism. Article mentions botnet expansion but pipeline produced no lateral-movement TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement attempts using SMB, RDP, or PSExec-like utilities originating from known botnet-infected hosts. Alert on suspicious file transfers paired with execution on secondary targets.

suggestion.title: Initial Access Vector for JDY (China-Linked)
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies initial compromise mechanism but pipeline produced no initial-access or execution phase. Missing exploitation or delivery method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email delivery (phishing), web browsing to malicious sites, or drive-by download activity with subsequent JDY botnet payload execution signatures. Alert on executable downloads followed by process spawning known botnet variants.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Botnet C2
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance activity inherently leads to data collection and exfiltration; pipeline extracted no exfiltration techniques despite 'cyber reconnaissance' mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume outbound data transfer to C&C endpoints, compressed archives being staged for transfer, or suspicious file access patterns consistent with credential/configuration harvesting.

suggestion.title: Compromised Rust Crate Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Compromised Rust crate onering' — no detection for package manager installation of flagged crate versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cargo install, cargo add, and Cargo.toml updates for known-malicious crate names and versions. Alert on package downloads from non-canonical repositories or version constraints that pull flagged builds. Correlate with build environment metadata.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from Build System
suggestion.rationale: Article states crate 'performs code exfiltration' — no UC for detecting when rustc/cargo child processes initiate external connections during compilation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl, wget, or native HTTP calls spawned from cargo build environments sending data to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains. Alert on encrypted channels from build processes, unusual DNS queries from rustc contexts, or traffic on atypical ports.

suggestion.title: Source Code Enumeration and Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'code exfiltration' — missing detection for malicious crate code accessing and reading project source files and secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Rust build/runtime processes recursively reading .rs files, .git directories, .env, or SSH keys at scale. Alert on file read patterns suggesting inventory of source code, configuration, or credentials by untrusted module code.

suggestion.title: Build Script Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised crates execute arbitrary code during build via build.rs — no detection for shell invocation or unusual child processes spawned from Rust compilation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rustc or cargo spawning shell interpreters (bash, cmd.exe, powershell), encoders (base64, certutil), or network tools (curl, nc) during builds. Alert when build.rs executes scripts from dependencies with file I/O or network access patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Package Repository Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Compromised 'onering' performs exfiltration — data could be tunneled through test output, build logs, or registry uploads; no detection for this covert channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for source code, hashes, or base64-encoded secrets appearing in test output, cargo publish artifacts, or git commit messages during builds. Alert on unusual file uploads or registry API calls immediately after suspicious build activity.

suggestion.title: Rust Toolchain Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Compromised crate could persist via rustup, sysroot, or cargo config modifications — no detection for toolchain tampering or bootstrap code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rustup directories, cargo-config.toml, and sysroot for unexpected modifications. Alert on custom cargo hooks or build.rs scripts persisting across project boundaries. Detect rustc wrapper overrides or build cache poisoning.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Validation with Hardcoded Secret 'random'
suggestion.rationale: Article states `AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random` is shipped as template default in `dev.env` line 10 and `cmd/serve.go` line 35. Pipeline missed detection for tokens signed with this known secret value.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag JWT tokens where the signature validates against the hardcoded secret 'random' or tokens with claim issuer/subject patterns matching dhax/go-base boilerplate defaults. Secondary: detect tokens with extreme expiration times (15+ years) indicating manual forgery rather than legitimate issuance.

suggestion.title: Exposed dev.env File with JWT Secret in Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies `dev.env` line 10 as containing hardcoded secret shipped to users. This is reconnaissance-phase detection for attackers discovering the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub/GitLab API queries or git clone/pull operations against `dhax/go-base` repository. Detect extraction or inspection of `.env` or `dev.env` files from public or compromised repos. Flag on automation tools (requests from non-browser user agents) or rapid sequential clones.

suggestion.title: Repeated Admin Endpoint Access with JWT Bearer Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article documents exploitation phase with requests to `/api/v1/admin/users`, `/api/v1/me`, `/api/v1/token/refresh`. Pipeline's UC_21_1 covered this partially, but pipeline itself generated nothing. This is the direct exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful (HTTP 200) requests to `/api/v1/admin/*`, `/api/v1/me`, or `/api/v1/token/refresh` endpoints when Authorization header contains JWT token and caller is external (non-internal ASN, non-dev IP range). Correlate with short time window (token refresh loops, enum patterns) and abnormal user-agent.

suggestion.title: Legitimate go-base Application Deployment Without Secret Rotation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 1,685 stars on GitHub — significant deployed installed base. Organizations running unpatched dhax/go-base with default `AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random` are high-risk assets even before exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory applications using github.com/dhax/go-base package. Flag installations where JWT auth is enabled but secret configuration matches default 'random' value. Cross-reference with exposed repository history or source commits in build artifacts.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Signature Verification Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded secret enables signature replication. Attackers will craft tokens with manipulated claims (admin=true, iss=admin, exp=2050) — these may appear as validation errors or anomalous claim values in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JWT parsing/validation failures that recover gracefully (status 200 despite invalid signature, or silent downgrade to unauthenticated). Flag tokens with claims that contradict user context (user_id=1 from external IP, admin claim from non-admin source IP).

suggestion.title: Baileys Vulnerable Version Detection via package.json/package-lock.json
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions: '< 7.0.0-rc12, and < 6.7.22'. Current UC_3_2 detects presence only. Need version-aware detection to identify actual vulnerability. Parse dependency lock files to isolate vulnerable versions and reduce false negatives from unaffected newer installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for baileys or @whiskeysockets/baileys entries in lock files and extract version strings. Flag versions matching <7.0.0-rc12 or <6.7.22. Correlates with UC_3_2 to identify only truly vulnerable installations.

suggestion.title: Node.js Process Spawned from Baileys Package Directory with Unusual Parent
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript' (T1059.007). Exploitation occurs when attacker's maliciously crafted protocolMessage triggers code execution. Detect suspicious Node.js process spawning from baileys package paths with unexpected parent processes (not typical npm, npm ci, or app startup).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe, nodejs, or npm processes with CommandLine containing baileys package paths or spawned from *\node_modules\baileys\ or equivalent Unix paths. Exclude legitimate parents: npm.exe, the host application process, package managers. Flag any spawning from user-initiated script or unexpected service account.

suggestion.title: npm Package Install/Upgrade of Vulnerable Baileys Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article details version bounds where vulnerability exists. Detect installation or update of Baileys to versions < 7.0.0-rc12 or < 6.7.22. Supply chain compromise (T1195.001) often manifests as package installation to dev machines before lateral spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for npm install, npm update, or yarn add commands targeting 'baileys' or '@whiskeysockets/baileys' where version specifier in command line OR resulting package.json entry matches <7.0.0-rc12 or <6.7.22. Correlate with UC_3_2 file events to establish install-to-execution timeline.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Baileys Session Message Spoofing (Application-Level Logging)
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'trigger a fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload'.
