suggestion.title: Source Code Repository Exposure - github.com/dhax/go-base Cloning
suggestion.rationale: Article references 1,685 GitHub stars; boilerplate is widely deployed. Attackers clone or fork the repository to obtain the source code, including hardcoded secret and API structure. Unusual clone volumes or access from non-development IPs signals reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository clone events and API access for unusual client IPs, user agents (bots), or high-volume clones—patterns typical of attacker reconnaissance and boilerplate code acquisition.

suggestion.title: Far-Future JWT Expiry Claims in Authorization Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article UC specifies 'extreme far-future JWT'—forged tokens with exp claims decades in the future bypass normal token-rotation defenses. Legitimate tokens expire within hours or days. Presence of exp claims beyond 1 year or year 2999 is a strong indicator of forged credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode Bearer token JWT claims from Authorization headers (proxies/WAF) and alert on exp timestamps beyond 365 days in the future or set to year >2100—pattern unique to forged tokens designed to evade session management.

suggestion.title: Message upsert event spoofing via protocolMessage payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'trigger[s] a fake `messages.upsert` event with a **fake message key and payload**' but pipeline generated no behavioral detection. This is post-exploitation impact and should trigger on anomalous message events in Baileys session logs or app instrumentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baileys session receiving and processing protocolMessage with mismatched sender/key properties, or app event logs showing messages attributed to wrong accounts. Look for messages.upsert events where message.key.fromMe=false but message.participant=self, or fake keys not in message history.

suggestion.title: App state sync corruption via fake key injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker ability to 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key s…' (truncated) but no detection for app state integrity was suggested. This is a distinct impact vector requiring app-level or file-level monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baileys session state files (typically .json in ~/.baileys or app-specific paths) containing message keys or metadata that don't match actual message receipts, or state files with timestamps/key formats inconsistent with legitimate protocol flow.

suggestion.title: Baileys module code instrumentation to detect malicious payload handling
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'sent a malicious payload via the placeholderResendMessage'. No detection for malformed or oversized placeholder messages was generated. Runtime behavior could be instrumented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: JavaScript/Node.js instrumentation of Baileys message handlers logging protocolMessage payloads with unusual size, encoding, or structure (e.g., nested protobuf or crafted fields targeting placeholderResendMessage parsing). Flag messages with key mismatch against session state.

suggestion.title: Package.json / npm audit detection for vulnerable Baileys versions
suggestion.rationale: Article requires versions <7.0.0-rc12 AND <6.7.22. Pipeline generated TVM queries but missed direct dependency scanning of project manifests, which is often earlier signal than installed package detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Presence of package.json or package-lock.json containing baileys or @whiskeysockets/baileys with semver matching <6.7.22 or <7.0.0-rc12. Detect writes to these files indicating new dependency introduction, not just filesystem package presence.

suggestion.title: Download from typosquatting or fake-mirror domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'network of more than 150 fake download sites that closely mimic trusted' utilities. Domains direct-download.gleeze.com, free-download.giize.com explicitly listed. Initial-access phase entirely undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file downloads (exe, zip, msi, dll) from domains matching typosquatting patterns (gleeze, giize, directdownload.icu subdomains like 'direct-download.*', 'free-download.*'). Correlate against threat-intel feed of 150+ fake mirrors. High confidence if downloaded to Downloads folder by non-admin user, not signed by legitimate publisher.

suggestion.title: User execution of unsigned/mismatched utility executable
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'users who search for popular PC utilities online, luring them into downloading malware-laced files' and then run them. Execution pivot (T1204.002) completely missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Explorer, browser, or Downloads folder and executable name mimics legitimate software (VLC.exe, 7zFM.exe, Audacity.exe, etc.) but file hash does not match known-good signed binary from vendor. Baseline legitimate tool hashes monthly.

suggestion.title: GPU/CPU-intensive mining process spawned unexpectedly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU.' Impact phase absent; T1496.001 (Resource Hijacking) not detected despite being core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of known mining software patterns (xmrig, teamredminer, phoenixminer, cgminer child processes). Correlate with sustained GPU/CPU > 80% utilization baseline anomaly on non-rendering/non-scientific-compute hosts. Alert if spawned from ScreenConnect parent or obfuscated parent process.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 communication to article-listed infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) and T1027 (Obfuscation) techniques but no hunt correlates C2 commands to the 4 article-listed IPs (193.42.11.108, 93.115.10.35, 198.23.185.238, 2.59.132.106). Command-and-control phase missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/TLS from ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe or parent processes to article-listed IPv4s or to gleeze.com/giize.com/directdownload.icu domains on ports 443, 8040, 8041, 6000-6100. Flag persistent beaconing (> 5 outbound sessions in 1h) as hands-on-keyboard C2.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Blocked or Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'dbmux' as a malicious npm package. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should flag any installation or require() of known-malicious package names from threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install / npm require operations invoke a package matching a blocklist of known-malicious npm package names (dbmux, typosquats, variants). Cross-reference against threat intelligence feeds for supply chain compromise IOCs.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawned During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hidden malware capable of giving attackers complete control.' Execution occurs during package installation via post-install scripts or require() hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned from npm.exe or node.exe during installation. Alert on obfuscated commands, base64 encoding, or network tool invocations (curl, certutil, reg.exe) in post-install context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Network from npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'complete control over developer systems' implies C2 or exfiltration. Malware must communicate to attacker infrastructure post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated by node.exe / npm.exe. Flag connections to newly-registered domains, reputation blacklists, or geographically anomalous destinations during or immediately after package install.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installed via npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'fully compromise developer systems,' requiring persistent access beyond single execution. Malware establishes foothold on disk or registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows registry run keys (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services) and filesystem startup folders for changes initiated from npm/node contexts. Alert on scheduled tasks or WMI event bindings created post-install.

suggestion.title: npm Package Supply Chain Threat Intel Integration
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should ingest known-malicious npm packages from security feeds and alert on installation. dbmux requires continuous registry monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a synchronized blocklist of known-malicious npm packages from official registries and threat feeds. Cross-reference against organization's CI/CD pipelines, package-lock.json files, and node_modules directories for installed matches.

suggestion.title: In-Memory Process Injection / Code-Cave Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'runs entirely in memory, leaving almost no trace behind.' File-based IOC hunts are useless. Must detect process injection via remote-thread creation, memory writes, or direct syscalls characteristic of in-memory payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CreateRemoteThread or ProcessAccess events where source process is PowerShell, cmd, mshta, rundll32, or regsvr32 writing to non-child process memory. In-memory malware must inject into a process to execute; this is the primary execution trace left after disk-write obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Outbound Traffic to TaxShadow Malicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 9 command-and-control domains (guhxmg.com, naiqja.icu, zh-welcome-1xbet.com, zhengfu666.com, asdqxcdsa.icu, appradarr.cc, ws4962.com, d.pc-weide.com, taxations.*.com variants). Pipeline produced zero IOC hunts; this is critical for in-memory malware exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/443, TCP/80, or DNS queries to the 9 confirmed malicious domains. In-memory malware must exfiltrate data over the network; this is the only externally-visible trace. Correlate with process execution to identify compromised endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PowerShell Cradle Execution (Download + Decode + Execute)
suggestion.rationale: T1059.001 (PowerShell) is listed as a technique. Multi-stage delivery pattern requires initial payload downloaded and decoded in-memory. Detect one-liner PowerShell with DownloadString, IEX, FromBase64String patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell.exe process with command line containing (case-insensitive): 'DownloadString', 'IEX', 'Invoke-Expression', 'FromBase64', '-enc', '-e', '|iex', '|%{' (piped aliases). In-memory malware commonly delivered via one-liner. Exclude administrative/IT contexts via allowlist.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence for In-Memory Loader Relaunch
suggestion.rationale: In-memory execution implies persistence mechanism. Malware must survive reboot via RunKey, startup folder, or scheduled task. Detect non-administrative process writing to HKLM/HKCU Run keys with URLs, encoded payloads, or LOLBin proxies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-admin process (PowerShell, cmd, Office) writing to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* or HKCU equivalent with REG_SZ values containing http(s)://, cmd.exe /c, or rundll32/regsvr32 proxies.

suggestion.title: Tax-Authority Spoofed Domain DNS/HTTP Access
suggestion.rationale: Campaign theme is impersonating Indian government tax authority. Domains include 'taxations.indiagov.it.com', 'zhengfu666.com', 'cn-web-okooo.com'—clear spoofing patterns. Detect DNS queries and HTTP requests to these lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS lookups or HTTP traffic to FQDN matching regex '(taxations|indiagov|zhengfu|pc-weide)' or using deceptive TLD patterns (.cn-web-*.com, .icu). Verify resolved IP is NOT within Indian government ASNs (AS55836, AS55960). Alert if resolved to non-government infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Ivanti Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions Ivanti critical patch release; Ivanti endpoint/identity products frequently target authentication mechanisms. Article body unavailable, but standard Ivanti CVE pattern involves auth bypass or RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual authentication patterns or failed/anomalous login sequences to Ivanti-managed endpoints or identity services, particularly from untrusted networks or with anomalous user-agent/geolocation combinations. Track HTTP POST requests to Ivanti web interfaces with abnormal parameter payloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Fortinet FortiGate RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Fortinet (FortiGate/FortiOS) frequently ships with remote code execution vulnerabilities. Article title indicates critical patches; standard exploitation involves HTTP POST to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known vulnerable Fortinet endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /cgi-bin/*, /system/api/rest) with suspicious payloads, command injection patterns, or oversized requests. Flag successful (200/302) responses to suspected exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect SAP ERP Privilege Escalation or RCE via Patch-Targeted Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: SAP enterprise applications frequently suffer from privilege escalation and RCE bugs in kernel modules and web interfaces. Article states 'multiple critical vulnerabilities'; detection should cover both pre-auth and post-auth exploitation paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SAP NetWeaver, HANA, and gateway logs for abnormal HTTP method combinations (OPTIONS/TRACE on production endpoints), unusual /sap/* URI patterns, and proof-of-concept injection attempts (e.g., XML external entities, LDAP injection). Correlate with process spawning unusual child processes from SAP daemons.

suggestion.title: Monitor Failed Patch Deployment and Vulnerable Instance Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article is about patches being released; detection must capture organizations that fail to deploy or whose systems remain unpatched. Title indicates 'multiple critical' severity, raising the stakes for post-release monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management systems (SCCM, Jamf, Saltstack, Ansible) for failed patch rollouts or exclusions targeting Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP products. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify systems still reporting vulnerable product versions 30+ days post-patch release.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Patch Exploitation Forensics and Lateral Movement from Compromised Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Fortinet and Ivanti are network perimeter/gateway appliances; successful exploitation often precedes lateral movement. Article context suggests these are high-value targets for initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After confirmed or suspected exploitation of a gateway device (Fortinet/Ivanti), detect lateral movement via suspicious outbound SSH/RDP/WinRM sessions from the gateway to internal subnets, process spawning indicative of post-exploitation (bash, perl, python child processes on a FortiGate, or unusual service restarts).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection - CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection weakness' enabling 'remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' This is a direct command execution attack requiring detection of injection payloads in network traffic to the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters or command substitution syntax (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons) in parameters. Alert on anomalous system process execution at root privilege level on the Sentry appliance following such requests.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthorized Administrative Account Creation - CVE-2026-10523
suggestion.rationale: Article states auth bypass 'can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' Requires detection of account creation operations without corresponding authenticated sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative account creation on Ivanti Sentry outside normal change windows, or where account creation succeeds despite no authenticated session. Cross-reference account creation timestamps against authentication logs to identify out-of-band account provisioning.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Privileged Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies auth bypass allows exploitation 'remotely by unauthenticated attackers.' Baseline normal auth flows and detect privileged operations (admin endpoint access, config changes) lacking valid authentication credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative endpoints or configuration interfaces that complete successfully without valid session tokens, authentication headers, or prior successful login. Flag especially account creation endpoints accessed without credentials.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes RCE executes 'with root privileges.' Root-level command execution from network-facing Sentry gateway processes is anomalous and should trigger investigation given the privilege escalation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry processes spawn child commands executing at root/SYSTEM privilege, especially when initiated from network-facing handlers or web service accounts. Root execution on security appliances should be rare and require audit trail validation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies fixed versions as R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1. Verify patched deployment and alert on systems running pre-patch versions that remain exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and device inventory for any Ivanti Sentry appliances running version numbers older than R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1. Flag unpatched instances and correlate with network exposure to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Privilege Escalation via Microsoft Defender Zero-Day
suggestion.rationale: Article title states zero-day grants SYSTEM access. This is the primary attack vector and must be detected by monitoring for unexpected SYSTEM-level privilege grants originating from Defender service components or processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by mpengine.exe, MpService.exe, or related Defender services running with SYSTEM privileges where parent process was user-mode. Detect elevation of privilege from medium integrity (user) to SYSTEM (high integrity) via Defender components. Baseline normal Defender service behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Defender Service/Binary Tampering or Injection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of Defender vulnerability likely requires either code injection into Defender processes or direct binary/service manipulation. The article references a zero-day, suggesting active exploitation code path that should leave forensic traces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection into MpService.exe or other Defender executables. Detect suspicious Defender registry modifications (service image path, parameters, or policy settings). Flag file write/modification events to Defender binary paths (%ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender, %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows Defender\). Alert on unauthorized service restart or state changes.

suggestion.title: Defender Disable/Bypass via Policy or Registry Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day granting SYSTEM access enables subsequent defense evasion. Pipeline should detect attempts to disable or downgrade Defender protections via registry or Group Policy, a natural post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to Defender policy keys (e.g., HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender). Detect modifications to DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableBehaviorMonitoring, or DisableOnAccessProtection. Alert on tampering with exclusion lists that could whitelist exploit code or payload directories.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SYSTEM-Context Process Execution from Defender Components
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies SYSTEM-level access grant. Normal Defender operations run within constrained service contexts; any SYSTEM-spawned child processes from Defender are suspicious and should trigger escalation workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events where ParentImage is Defender-related (mpengine.exe, MpService.exe, mpcmdrun.exe) and ProcessIntegrityLevel is 'System' and the child process is NOT a known Defender internal module. Correlate with command-line arguments that deviate from legitimate Defender operations (e.g., spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or remote access tools).

suggestion.title: Defender Service Unplanned Restart or Unexpected Shutdown
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may cause service instability or require attackers to restart the service to trigger the vulnerability or hide tracks. Unexpected service lifecycle events are behavioral indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor System event logs for MpService and related Defender service stops/starts outside normal patch cycles or IT-initiated actions. Correlate timing with process anomalies or privilege escalation events. Alert on rapid restart cycles that may indicate exploitation attempts or crash-driven exploitation.

suggestion.title: Detector Version Mismatch or Downgrade Attack
suggestion.rationale: A zero-day in 'updated Windows' Defender suggests version-specific vulnerability. Pipeline should detect downgrades or mismatched versions as indicators of preparation for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected Defender engine and definition versions per patch cycle. Alert on unexpected downgrades or version rollbacks. Monitor for modification of version registry keys or replacement of mpengine.dll with older versions. Cross-correlate with exploit preparation indicators (debugging tools, privilege escalation payloads staged locally).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Delivery Targeting OWA Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user.' Initial-access vector must be detected at mail gateway. No use case was generated for email content analysis despite clear threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email content for JavaScript tags, obfuscated script payloads, and anomalous sender behavior targeting Exchange users. Flag MIME structures with embedded script elements or base64-encoded JavaScript, particularly in HTML-based email bodies targeting OWA endpoints.

suggestion.title: XSS Code Execution in Outlook Web Access Session
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation: 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' following user email interaction. This execution phase has no corresponding detection use case despite being the critical moment of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected JavaScript execution within w3wp.exe (Exchange IIS worker) or browser processes during OWA sessions. Alert on XMLHttpRequest calls to untrusted origins, DOM manipulation during mail-read operations, or console API abuse from non-developer contexts.

suggestion.title: Post-OWA Exploitation Mailbox Enumeration and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Implied by article's context: XSS execution leads to data access. Article notes threat is 'actively exploited' but provides no detection for attacker post-exploitation activity—mailbox exports, forwarding rules, credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual OfficeActivity events post-OWA compromise: mail forwarding rule creation, bulk mailbox export operations, unusual search volume, or out-of-hours mailbox access from the same session that exhibited XSS execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Exchange Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Pattern (CVE-2026-42897)
suggestion.rationale: CISA added to exploited-in-the-wild list 15 May 2026, yet pipeline generated no signature-based or behavior-based detection. Article explicitly identifies the vulnerability CVE-2026-42897 with transport/payload characteristics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create pattern-match signatures for known CVE-2026-42897 exploitation: malformed email MIME boundaries, script injection attempts in email headers/body, and obfuscated payload delivery mechanisms. Cross-reference against known exploitation tool signatures.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Staging Post-OWA Access
suggestion.rationale: Historical context: 'ransomware gangs having exploited 14 of [20 Exchange vulnerabilities].' Pipeline missed opportunity to alert on post-exploitation behaviors (shadow copy enumeration, bulk file operations) that follow successful OWA compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful OWA XSS exploitation with downstream ransomware indicators: vssadmin.exe deletion, encrypted-file extension proliferation, credential-dumping tool execution, or lateral movement scanning originating from the compromised user's context.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Exchange Server Exposure Scan Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article implies active attacks and recommends immediate patching. Pipeline should generate detection for reconnaissance/vulnerability scanning traffic targeting Exchange ports/endpoints that may precede exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for external reconnaissance scanning of Exchange OWA endpoints, HTTP OPTIONS requests to /owa/ paths, or fingerprinting attempts targeting Exchange version/build identifiers before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Critical RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'critical RCE bugs' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections despite this being immediate post-compromise threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal process spawning or command execution originating from Microsoft service contexts or exposed application processes. Flag code execution with network callbacks post-RCE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Microsoft Product Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: With 206 flaws patched simultaneously, pipeline should establish inventory detection for systems not yet applying patches—'record' patch release demands immediate visibility into remediation gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Windows/Office hosts running build versions prior to post-announcement patch KB numbers. Prioritize internet-facing systems and cloud workloads.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out 'three zero-days' explicitly, highest-confidence attack surface, but pipeline ignored. Should establish canary/pattern-based detections for early exploitation signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious HTTP request patterns, malformed protocol frames, or binary payloads targeting known Microsoft zero-day vulnerability surface (e.g., Exchange, Outlook, Windows kernel services).

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Privilege Escalation Chain
suggestion.rationale: RCE implies initial foothold often in unprivileged context. Article does not clarify if flaws grant direct SYSTEM access, requiring detection of escalation attempts following execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate RCE-phase process creation with token impersonation attempts, UAC bypass techniques, or suspicious registry modifications to security policies post-exploit.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Microsoft Service Modification
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE in Microsoft services creates immediate persistence vector through service binary/DLL hijacking. Pipeline missed continuation attack after initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to Microsoft service ImagePath, DependOnService, or DLL load order hijacking. Correlate with RCE exploitation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Patch Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Attackers who exploit before patching may pivot to unpatched systems in same network. Pipeline should model threat persistence across heterogeneous patch levels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag lateral movement attempts (RDP, SMB, WinRM) from compromised but unpatched host to other internal systems. Correlate with RCE exploitation chain timing.

suggestion.title: SSH Credential Spray Against PeopleSoft Admin Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker script 'attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm.' This is the primary post-exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of failed SSH authentication attempts to accounts psoft, oracle, linuxadm, and root from a single source within a narrow time window, especially followed by successful key-based auth to the same account. High-fidelity indicator of orchestrated compromise.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Creation in PeopleSoft Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'script designed to create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT on an internal PeopleSoft server after it is breached.' File creation confirms successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation for README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT or similar ransom note naming patterns in PeopleSoft web/app server root directories. Treat as immediate breach confirmation.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral C2 Agent Staging and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Researcher discovered 'staging materials, including MeshCentral agents, and a defacement and credential spray script' in exposed attacker directories. MeshCentral is a persistent remote access platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshCentral binary creation or execution in suspicious contexts (temp, staging directories, post-exploitation scripts). Correlate with PeopleSoft application directories and outbound connections to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Network Connections from ShinyHunters Staging Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Researcher identified multiple IP addresses from exposed directories, corroborated by TLS certificate CN 'azurenetfiles.net' linked to ShinyHunters. Addresses: 142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on inbound or outbound connections to listed IPs, especially on PeopleSoft application ports (typically 8000-9000) or SSH (22). Treat as high-risk indicators of active reconnaissance or exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Host File Enumeration for PeopleSoft Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The script parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems and attempts to connect to them over SSH.' This is lateral movement reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of tools like cat/grep parsing /etc/hosts or /etc/passwd post-compromise, especially followed by SSH connection attempts. Look for process trees showing shell script execution from unexpected parent processes on PeopleSoft servers.

suggestion.title: Gadget Chain Exploitation of PeopleSoft Application Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers use 'a gadget chain of old and zero-day vulnerabilities' and that 'exploitation success may depend on how an instance is configured.' This is the root compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application logs for serialized Java object deserialization patterns, unusual POST/PUT requests with binary payloads, exception stack traces from gadget chain classes (Commons Collections, Spring, etc.), and correlate with outbound connections from the app server to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect path traversal sequences in Langflow /api/v2/files multipart filenames
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences (\"../\").' Core exploit vector requires direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST requests to /api/v2/files endpoints for multipart form data containing 'filename' parameters with path traversal payloads ('../', '..\\', encoded variants). Correlate with file creation events in system or unexpected directories from Langflow process ID.

suggestion.title: Detect arbitrary file writes following CVE-2026-5027 exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances.' Active exploitation with observable file I/O side effects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or write operations executed by Langflow processes (langflow, python, node) in system-protected directories (/etc, /var, C:\\Windows, C:\\System32) or directories outside application install paths, especially within seconds of /api/v2/files POST requests.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated initial API access to Langflow instances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Because Langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token before proceeding with exploitation.' Initial-access foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST/GET requests to /api/v2* or /api/v1* endpoints from external/untrusted networks that generate valid session tokens without prior authentication events (missing bearer tokens, API keys in request headers).

suggestion.title: Inventory Langflow versions and flag unpatched instances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'vulnerable instances', versions <1.9.0 and langflow-base <0.8.3. Censys identified ~7,000 exposed instances. Vulnerability management requires version visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform application fingerprinting on accessible Langflow instances (banner grab, /api/version endpoint, response headers). Alert when Langflow version is <1.9.0 or langflow-base <0.8.3. Cross-reference with external exposure scans (Shodan, Censys).

suggestion.title: Correlate attacks across related Langflow CVEs within targeting window
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Exploitation of CVE-2026-5027 comes shortly after similar activity targeting other Langflow vulnerabilities earlier this year, including CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, and CVE-2026-33017.' Temporal clustering signals coordinated campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate exploitation attempts across CVE-2026-5027, CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017 endpoints. Alert when the same source IP or ASN targets multiple distinct Langflow CVE vectors against the same instance within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Malicious Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt with high confidence and phase c2. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections from ServiceNow instances or user sessions to 51.159.98.241. Flag sustained or repeated connection attempts on HTTPS or alternate ports suggestive of C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of ServiceNow Access Control Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper access controls that may enable attackers to execute queries... without proper authentication'—this is the exploitation vector. Pipeline kill chain is empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls to protected ServiceNow endpoints (e.g., query parameters, table API) with missing or invalid authentication tokens. Alert on unauthenticated POST requests that succeed to sys_* or cmdb_* table endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Backend Instance Table Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication'—core attack is unauthorized data enumeration and access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume or sequential queries targeting sys_user, cmdb_ci_*, or other backend instance tables from unauthenticated or low-privilege sessions. Flag aggregation queries or data dumps of sensitive columns (password, api_token, etc.).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Customer Data from Instance Tables
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'data exposure across enterprise environments' and access to 'customer instance tables'—collection and exfiltration is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful unauthorized table queries with large data transfers or unusual API export requests. Alert on bulk data access followed by external data transfers (FTP, S3, email) or compression of customer records.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ServiceNow Instance API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'queries against backend instance tables'—pipeline should flag query-based exploitation patterns in API logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-standard or malformed API calls to query endpoints (e.g., sysparm_query parameters with unusual filters, high LIMIT values, or multiple table joins). Flag rapid-fire queries or iterative table enumeration.

suggestion.title: Bulk malicious repository creation with 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' naming pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'In each of those accounts, the threat actors leaked the source code in a repo named "Miasma-Open-Source-Release."' This is a direct, reproducible indicator for detecting compromised developer accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API and audit logs for rapid repository creation (≥3 repos within 1 hour) matching 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' or similar open-source framework release naming patterns. Correlate with account activity anomalies (new geographic login, failed 2FA). Trigger immediate credential revocation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized credential harvesting from password managers and Kubernetes secret stores
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores.' No detection for these credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-CI processes spawning subprocess access to local credential storage (.1password, .gnupg, .aws/credentials, .kube/config files, or HashiCorp Vault/Kubernetes API calls). Look for child process execution from build tools or development environment variables accessing these stores outside expected deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Dead-man switch persistence: destructive systemd/LaunchAgent creation triggered by token revocation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific persistence mechanism: 'a "dead-man switch" that is installed when the malware uses a victim's stolen GitHub token...executes a destructive command (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents)...The monitor runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS, and remains active for up to 72 hours.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of systemd user services in ~/.config/systemd/user/ or ~/.local/share/systemd/user/ with destructive payloads (rm -rf patterns). On macOS, monitor ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ for similar. Correlate timing with GitHub credential access logs and token revocation events. Check systemd timer jobs monitoring for periodic validation loops.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with harvested credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'It can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM)' using stolen credentials from developer machines. No detection specified for anomalous SSM session initiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail for StartSession calls with IAM credentials harvested from developer workstations (detected via credential access use cases). Trigger on sessions initiated from unusual geographic regions, non-production accounts accessing production infrastructure, or sessions to EC2 instances not in baseline CMDB for that developer.

suggestion.title: AI coding tool configuration poisoning: injection of malicious hooks into Claude, Cursor, Copilot configs
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline.' No detection for unauthorized modification of AI tool settings to inject credential-harvesting or pivoting hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to AI tool config directories (.vscode/settings.json for Cursor/Copilot, .cline, .cursor, local LLM proxy configs) to inject custom API endpoints, authentication overrides, or system prompts that exfiltrate context/credentials. Flag config changes from processes spawned by build tools or CI runners outside scheduled deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Trojanized package publication with multi-layer AES-256 encrypted embedded payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack: 'uses those [stolen credentials] to compromise legitimate repositories and packages, publishing trojanized versions' and details the evasion: 'five-stage build pipeline...combines per-file AES-256-GCM encryption of embedded assets, randomized string obfuscation...ensuring that each generated sample differs from previous builds, making signature-based detection and static analysis harder.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package uploads to npm, PyPI, and RubyGems by recently-compromised developer credentials. Flag: uploads within 72 hours of credential theft, version inconsistencies, binaries with embedded AES-256-GCM streams, or self-extracting loader patterns. Cross-reference upload timing with GitHub Actions job executions and build environment secrets access.

suggestion.title: Langflow Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027 Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE' — this is the core attack vector and should be the primary detection hypothesis. Pipeline missed generating any use case for exploitation pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Langflow instances with CVE-2026-5027 vulnerability indicators (specific endpoint paths, payload markers if disclosed, or unauthenticated access patterns). Flag requests targeting known vulnerable Langflow versions without valid authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: RCE Command Execution from Langflow Process
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Unauthenticated RCE' — the execution phase after successful exploitation. Pipeline did not generate detection for suspicious process spawning or command execution initiated by Langflow runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Langflow Java/Python runtime with suspicious command-line patterns (reverse shells, curl/wget downloads, base64-encoded payloads, /bin/bash -c execution). Correlate with failed auth logs or suspicious API calls to Langflow endpoints.

suggestion.title: Langflow Version Enumeration or Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attackers typically enumerate service versions before exploitation. Article mentions 'unpatched' vulnerability affecting specific Langflow versions — detection should cover reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to common Langflow endpoints that leak version info (/api/version, /health, /status, package.json, requirements.txt) or HTTP requests with suspicious User-Agents targeting Langflow. Baseline against known security scanner patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Access to Protected Langflow Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: The core flaw is 'unauthenticated' access to what should be protected. Pipeline should flag attempts to invoke protected endpoints without valid auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow API logs and web server logs for HTTP 200/201 responses to sensitive endpoints (/api/*, /chat/*, /flow/* paths) when request lacks Authorization header or contains invalid/empty auth tokens. Threshold on failed→success sequences from same source.

suggestion.title: Langflow Dependency/Plugin Download from Suspicious Sources
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers often persist via malicious dependencies or plugins. RCE allows injecting or downloading external code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP(S) requests from Langflow process to non-whitelisted package repositories (PyPI, npm, Maven mirrors beyond org allowlist), especially to newly-registered domains or IPs. Flag requests with high entropy or obfuscated paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45586 CTFMON Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM' via 'Windows Collaborative Translation Framework'. No use case generated despite being the core attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation attempts via ctfmon.exe exploitation. Monitor for process token elevation events where a low-privilege user context transitions to SYSTEM or HIGH integrity following ctfmon execution. Alert on unusual ctfmon parent processes or token impersonation patterns.

suggestion.title: Abnormal CTFMON Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable process but pipeline generated no execution-layer detections. CTFMON baseline abuse patterns are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: ctfmon.exe normally launched by explorer.exe, no command-line args, runs from System32. Alert on ctfmon spawning child processes, accepting unexpected arguments, or executing from non-standard paths (Downloads, Temp, user home dirs).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable CTFMON Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references June 9, 2026 patches. Pre-patch systems exploitable. File hash and version correlation required but not generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ctfmon.exe execution against vulnerable file hashes/versions (pre-2026-06-09). Alert if vulnerable binary executes, especially from non-standard contexts (downloads, USB, network shares, temp directories).

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Privilege Escalation via CTFMON
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'valuable post-exploitation primitive'. Attack assumes prior low-privilege access; escalation phase should trigger secondary alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate low-privilege process anomalies (suspicious parent, command injection, DLL injection) with subsequent ctfmon execution and token elevation. Flag sequences where unprivileged process → ctfmon interaction → SYSTEM context achieved.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Execution from Untrusted Package
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly flags npm install scripts as the attack vector for supply-chain compromise. Scripts execute during dependency installation with ambient process context—detection should monitor for unexpected spawned child processes, network egress, or file modifications during 'npm install'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell, cmd.exe, bash, or node.exe spawned as children of npm.exe or node.exe during package installation. Flag child processes with network egress (curl, wget, Invoke-WebRequest) or file writes outside project directory. Correlate with package manifest (.npmrc) for unusual registry configurations or auth tokens.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion or Typosquatting Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via npm commonly use name-squatting (e.g., 'lodash' vs 'lodash-v2') or private/internal package replacement. Detection should identify installation of similarly-named or unexpected packages, especially from public registry when internal/private was expected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install/npm ci operations pulling packages with names that closely match organizational conventions, internal prefixes, or known typos. Cross-reference against lockfile expectations (package-lock.json) and flag upgrades/downgrades of core transitive dependencies. Monitor npm registry requests for anomalous auth or unusual repository URIs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Authentication or Publish Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks can involve package hijacking or malicious republish. GitHub's remediation suggests focus on install-time execution, but detection should include unusual npm publish, registry authentication, or token usage patterns indicating attempted package compromise or artificial propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm login/logout activity, .npmrc token creation/modification, and 'npm publish' invocations from non-CI/non-authorized accounts. Alert on multiple failed package publish attempts or successful publishes of versions differing only in build metadata. Correlate with source-control pushes to identify timing gaps suggesting registry compromise independent of code commit.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Transitive Dependency
suggestion.rationale: npm supply-chain attacks often target widely-used transitive dependencies (ones pulled in indirectly) to maximize blast radius. Detection should identify installation of deep dependencies with suspicious install scripts or those previously flagged in threat intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package list (from npm ls or node_modules introspection) against threat-intel feeds of known-malicious packages. Flag installs of packages with elevated download anomalies (sudden spike in version-specific downloads) or packages recently transferred to new maintainers. Monitor for execution of scripts under node_modules/.bin/ with unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: npm pre/post-install Script Disabling Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: GitHub's mitigation disables install scripts by default. Detection should identify attempts to re-enable scripts via --ignore-scripts=false, .npmrc configuration, or environment variable overrides, signaling adversary awareness of the defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm invocations with --ignore-scripts=false or --scripts flags set to true. Alert on .npmrc modifications enabling scripts or NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS environment variable set to false. Flag npm ci/install calls with verbose/debug logging that suggest deliberate script-execution testing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-6973 / CVE-2026-10727 Asset Inventory Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists two CVEs affecting Ivanti EPMM 12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1, etc. The briefing mentions this hunt but pipeline produced zero use cases. This is the canonical vulnerability-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-asset inventory against Ivanti EPMM versions known vulnerable to CVE-2026-6973 or CVE-2026-10727. Flag systems running 12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1, or other confirmed-vulnerable builds. Correlate with network exposure (internet-facing, VPN access, untrusted subnets) to prioritize patch urgency.

suggestion.title: Ivanti EPMM Apache Configuration Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'inject malicious Apache configuration directives' for RCE—a specific technical pivot. Pipeline missed the execution-phase IOC. Detection should key off httpd.conf or Apache config modifications from EPMM service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti EPMM (ivanti*, epmm*) processes for Apache config file writes (httpd.conf, conf.d/*, .htaccess). Detect spawned child processes from EPMM service account, particularly shell interpreters or Apache directives being executed. Alert on httpd/Apache restart events following suspicious config modifications.

suggestion.title: Ivanti EPMM Authenticated RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated attackers' injecting config directives to gain RCE—indicates post-auth privilege escalation or code execution. Pipeline's empty kill-chain missed execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti EPMM authentication logs with subsequent Apache config modifications or unexpected process spawning from EPMM context. Alert on authenticated sessions followed by command execution, shell spawning, or file writes to config directories. Flag successful authentications to EPMM instances on vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'stems from an OS command injection weakness' and reports public PoC with active exploitation ('large amount of...exploitation attempts'). Pipeline extracted zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API requests (e.g., /api/admin, servlet endpoints) for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, backticks, $(), command substitution) in parameters. Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to known vulnerable endpoints combined with command-injection payloads. Correlate with 5xx error responses or admin activity anomalies.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Code Execution on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables 'execute code with root privileges on Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways.' Pipeline did not identify privilege escalation detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process execution with UID 0 (root) on Sentry appliances, especially child processes spawned by gateway/web server service accounts. Correlate with recent HTTP requests matching CVE-2026-10520 exploitation patterns or unexpected command strings (curl, wget, bash, nc).

suggestion.title: Sentry Gateway Backdoor Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' with 'at least 2 backdoored' confirmed. Pipeline missed persistence detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized SSH public key additions to root or service accounts on Sentry appliances. Monitor for suspicious cron jobs, new systemd services, or modifications to existing init scripts. Cross-reference timeline with confirmed CVE-2026-10520 exploitation attempts and alert on any persistence mechanism installed post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Gateway Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Shadowserver scanning detected exposed instances and warned 'if you have not patched now you are most likely compromised.' Asset inventory is prerequisite for exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build and maintain inventory of all Ivanti Sentry instances with external Internet connectivity (ports 443, 8443, admin interfaces). Correlate inventory with internal CMDB and alert on any gap. Flag instances with public DNS records or routable IPs as immediate patching priority.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1 released June 10, 2026. Inventory of unpatched versions is critical baseline for vulnerability assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Sentry instances for product version via admin interfaces or SNMP. Flag any version prior to R10.5.2 (R10.5.x), R10.6.2 (R10.6.x), or R10.7.1 (R10.7.x) as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Correlate with exploitation attempt logs to identify systems likely compromised before patching.

suggestion.title: Sentry Gateway to Internal Network Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Sentry's role as 'secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices'—a compromised gateway is network pivot point. Pipeline missed post-exploitation lateral movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected SSH, SMB, or database connections initiated from Sentry appliances to internal backend systems. Alert on data exfiltration attempts from compromised gateway toward internal corporate networks. Cross-reference with known CVE-2026-10520 exploitation timeline to identify lateral movement windows.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ShinyHunters used 'a gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities' to breach PeopleSoft—a specific, detectable exploitation pattern targeting serialized Java object deserialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious HTTP POST requests to PeopleSoft endpoints (/pls/, /psigw/) containing serialized Java objects or gadget chain payloads. Alert on exploitation attempts combining known CVEs with uncommon deserialization patterns. Correlate with failed authentication attempts followed by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Export of Student Records and Financial Data
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration of 40GB+ containing 454,600 student records with names, addresses, phone numbers, passport numbers, academic enrollment, and fee payment details—observable as anomalous database queries or multi-gigabyte file transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk SELECT queries from student record tables (EMPLID, PSBIRTHDATE, PSBIRTHCOUNTRY, PSPERSDATA) returning >10,000 rows outside business hours. Correlate with large outbound data transfers (GB-scale) to external IPs or Tor exit nodes. Flag queries by service accounts with unusual privilege levels.

suggestion.title: Cross-Campus PeopleSoft Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates breach affected 'University of Nottingham and its Malaysia and China campuses'—suggesting lateral movement or replication of exploit across federated instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication and replication traffic between geographically-distant PeopleSoft instances outside maintenance windows. Alert on service account lateral movement across campus boundaries, particularly access from non-campus network segments.

suggestion.title: Configuration-Conditional Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'not working on all systems, likely because successful exploitation depends on each instance's configuration'—indicating attackers enumerate and target based on environment-specific factors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track PeopleSoft patch levels and configuration differences via CMDB. Detect exploitation attempts targeting specific CVE + configuration combinations. Flag when different exploit payloads are sent to the same target in sequence, indicating reconnaissance-and-exploit pattern.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Archiving for Dark Web Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ShinyHunters 'shared an archive of allegedly stolen documents' on dark web leak site—indicating compression, staging, and archiving of exfiltrated data for external publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for zip, tar, or 7z compression of student_records, financial_data, portal_exports directories. Flag execution of archiving tools on database servers or with elevated privileges outside scheduled maintenance. Correlate compression events with file access spikes and subsequent exfiltration.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass' as core vulnerability; 'Critical phpBB Vulnerability: Auth Bypass + RCE Since 2014' in title explicitly establishes this as exploitable attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB login endpoints (admin/index.php, ucp.php) for anomalous authentication patterns: repeated 401s followed by successful auth, unusual User-Agent distribution, or requests from suspicious geographic origins. Alert if attacker bypasses password validation by exploiting improper session/token validation.

suggestion.title: phpBB Post-Authentication Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RCE as the second exploit stage: 'Auth Bypass + RCE' and URL slug 'phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce' confirms code execution capability after auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP command execution post-phpBB auth: monitor for shell_exec(), system(), exec(), passthru() calls in phpBB request/response chains. Flag unexpected child processes spawned from web server (php.exe, bash, cmd.exe). Correlate with successful prior auth to same phpBB instance within session window.

suggestion.title: phpBB Vulnerable Endpoint Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: 10-year-old vulnerability since 2014 implies specific vulnerable code paths; detection should target known phpBB admin/installation endpoints exploited in public PoCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to known-vulnerable phpBB URIs (install/, admin/index.php with unusual parameters, ucp.php with session-bypass payloads). Monitor POST requests with suspicious phpBB-specific parameters (username, password, login, session handling). Flag requests if they arrive on unpatched phpBB versions (identify version via headers or 404 patterns).

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning from PHP Execution
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability allows attacker to execute arbitrary commands; article scope ('Remote Code Execution') implies spawning of reverse shells or system utilities post-auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation under IIS (w3wp.exe) or Apache (httpd.exe/apache2): cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget, nc.exe. Correlate timing to HTTP request spike or phpBB-specific traffic. Flag particularly if parent is web-server and child is network-aware tool (curl, wget, ncat).

suggestion.title: Mass phpBB Forum Compromise Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes scale: 'affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums' — implies detection should flag organizational/network-level patterns of simultaneous phpBB exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect coordinated exploitation of phpBB instances: multiple internal forums or managed hosting providers all logging auth bypasses or post-auth RCE within short window. Monitor for synchronized admin account creation, defacement file uploads, or C2 beacons across phpBB instances. Flag if single source IP exploits multiple distinct phpBB domains in < 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beacon Detection – JDY
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet 'Expands to 1,500+ Devices' requiring active command-and-control. Reconnaissance mission implies ongoing C2 heartbeats and telemetry collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound connections from multiple hosts to rare external IPs (beaconing pattern). Monitor DNS queries for JDY-associated domains or DGA patterns. Flag connections to known botnet sinkhole/C2 infrastructure IPs.

suggestion.title: Botnet Payload Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: 1,500-device 'expansion' phase indicates active infection campaign requiring malware execution on victim systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious script execution (PowerShell, cmd, bash) with rare parent-child process relationships. Alert on binary execution from temporary/staging directories (/tmp, %temp%) followed immediately by network egress. Flag process command lines containing obfuscation indicators or environment variable references.

suggestion.title: Host Reconnaissance Activity Cluster
suggestion.rationale: Article states explicit mission: 'cyber reconnaissance.' Reconnaissance phase requires enumeration of processes, services, systems, and network configuration on infected and adjacent hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency execution of discovery commands (tasklist, Get-Process, wmic, sc, systemctl, ipconfig, route, netstat) from single host in short time window. Alert on ping sweeps, port scans (nmap, Nessus activity), or ICMP requests originating from newly-compromised systems.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Reconnaissance from Botnet Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Botnet scale (1,500 devices) and reconnaissance mission suggest capability to enumerate adjacent systems and move laterally within networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SMB (445), RDP (3389), SSH (22), or WinRM (5985) connection attempts from single source to multiple destinations. Alert on failed authentication attempts followed by success (credential spray). Monitor for unusual lateral movement patterns from hosts without prior lateral history.

suggestion.title: Botnet Data Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance mission implies collection and exfiltration of discovered system/network data back to attacker C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high data-transfer volume (GB scale) to rare external IP or suspicious domain. Alert on clustering of 10+ hosts all communicating with single non-CDN external IP. Monitor for DNS queries to newly-registered or fast-flux domains associated with botnet C2.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence Establishment Detection
suggestion.rationale: 1,500-device botnet requires persistence mechanisms to survive reboots and maintain long-term foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks (schtasks, at commands) with rare names or unusual trigger times. Alert on registry modifications in HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or startup folder additions. Monitor for service installation with binaries in non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Code Deployment from Unauthorized Development Device
suggestion.rationale: 'Code is being written everywhere' implies distributed development; detection should flag code commits/pushes from devices outside expected CI/CD infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code repository commits, pushes, or deployments originating from development devices outside expected CI/CD pipelines. Baseline which user devices are authorized to commit to which repositories. Alert on direct pushes to protected branches from user workstations, bypassing code-review gates.

suggestion.title: Persistent Development Tool Compromise via Autostart
suggestion.rationale: 'Device is the only constant' emphasizes the device as persistent attack surface; threat actors compromise development tools (IDE, git, build systems) for sustained code-supply-chain access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to development environment files outside package managers (git hooks, IDE configs, build scripts). Flag suspicious autostart entries launching development tools. Monitor for unsigned/unexpected executables in development application directories.

suggestion.title: Code Exfiltration to Unauthorized Repository or Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Title implies code is written and synchronized across many device contexts; threat is unauthorized push to external git servers, attacker-controlled repos, or personal cloud accounts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for git and cloud-sync patterns on development devices. Alert on high-volume or unusual git activity, pushes to non-standard remotes, or code directories synced to non-enterprise cloud accounts. Flag use of personal GitHub/GitLab accounts from corporate devices.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Exfiltration from Rust Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'code exfiltration'—the core attack behavior. No use case generated to detect unauthorized data leaving the build pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections initiated by Rust compiler, cargo, or processes spawned during crate inclusion. Correlate with DNS queries to exfiltration domains and alert on non-standard HTTP/DNS traffic encoding code or configuration data.

suggestion.title: Malicious Rust Crate Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is about a 'compromised Rust crate onering'—supply chain attack vector. Pipeline should detect suspicious package downloads and integrity failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cargo or rustc processes downloading from unexpected registries, crate versions with hash mismatches, or execution of unsigned/suspicious post-install scripts within crate dependencies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code/Secrets Collection by Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern is code exfiltration via compromised dependency—need detection for when dependencies enumerate, read, or transmit source files or credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Rust build process or spawned threads reading .git directories, .env files, source code, or credential stores—especially when parent process is a known malicious crate or third-party library with suspicious privileges.

suggestion.title: Anomalous DNS/Network from Package Manager Operations
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration mechanism requires C2 or data sink. No detection generated for abnormal network behavior during crate installation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate cargo/rustc process initiation with DNS queries to newly-registered or reputation-flagged domains; alert on non-standard ports, encrypted tunnels, or protocol anomalies during build phase.

suggestion.title: Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints with far-future JWT expiration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details this attack: 'Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints with extreme far-future JWT'. Pipeline failed to extract the existing UC_24_1 hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify bearer tokens claiming far-future expiration (years ahead of current date) used against /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh endpoints. Correlate successful responses (HTTP 200) with absent OAuth initiation or legitimate session context.

suggestion.title: Token forgery via hardcoded JWT secret exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'dev.env line 10: AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random — template default shipped to all users'. Tokens signed with the literal string 'random' must trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JWT tokens whose signatures validate against hardcoded secret 'random'. Monitor go-base application logs for token creation/validation against dev.env configuration. Flag any environment config exposure.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of public-facing go-base endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' as initial technique. Boilerplate has 1,685 GitHub stars indicating broad deployment; direct attacks on exposed endpoints are expected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to /api/v1/admin/*, /api/v1/token/refresh, /api/v1/me with successful responses from IPs lacking legitimate user context. Baseline against go-base deployment signatures.

suggestion.title: Account takeover via forged valid-account credentials
suggestion.rationale: T1078 'Valid Accounts' paired with T1606 'Forge Web Credentials' indicates attackers create valid-looking tokens to assume privilege. Monitor for high-privilege access without corresponding login events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with bearer tokens decoding to admin/privilege-escalated roles appearing without successful authentication events. Cross-reference token issue timestamps against application startup times.

suggestion.title: Malicious protocolMessage payload processing anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'sent a malicious payload via the placeholderResendMessage'—core attack vector with zero detection coverage. No hunt targets unusual protocolMessage structure, failed proto parsing, or validation errors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes running Baileys for exceptions during protobuf message deserialization, unusual memory patterns during message.upsert event processing, or protocolMessage validation failures. Detect if messages lack expected cryptographic signature or sender-key fields.

suggestion.title: Fake message.upsert event and message spoofing indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger a fake `messages.upsert` event with a fake message key and payload'—defines the exploitation outcome. Zero hunts target spoofed message detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for messages appearing from unexpected senders, messages with malformed or reused message-keys, or messages that violate timestamp/sequence constraints. Detect message.upsert events triggered outside normal client->server flow.

suggestion.title: Application state synchronization failure and corruption patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'corrupt the app state sync system'—describes persistence/corruption phase with no detection. Sync system is attack target but not monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated app-state-sync failures, inconsistency detection in Baileys state store, rollback of state to prior versions, or corruption recovery mechanisms being invoked. Alert on state key mismatches between client and server.

suggestion.title: Baileys version downgrade or patch evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article lists vulnerable versions <7.0.0-rc12 and <6.7.22. No hunt monitors version pinning, downgrades, or prevention of patches—common post-compromise persistence tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for package.json modifications that pin Baileys to vulnerable versions, npm install commands with --save-exact or --no-save for old versions, or git commits reverting Baileys upgrades. Detect installation of Baileys from non-standard registries.

suggestion.title: Node.js process spawning chat/messaging libraries with suspicious behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1059.007 (JavaScript execution). Baileys is loaded in Node.js context; exploit payload may execute within that runtime. No hunt targets unusual child processes, file access, or network behavior from Baileys-hosting processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes that load Baileys for spawning unexpected child processes, writing to disk outside normal app directories, or establishing network connections to C2 infrastructure. Detect eval/exec/require calls on data sourced from remote messages.

suggestion.title: Unusual WhatsApp/Baileys client authentication or session anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Baileys authenticates as WhatsApp client; malicious payloads arrive post-auth. No hunt monitors for session hijacking, re-authentication under suspicious conditions, or device-binding anomalies that might indicate account takeover prep.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Baileys sessions that re-authenticate after brief uptime, sessions from multiple IP ranges in short timeframe, or device-binding requests that fail then succeed (typical of account recovery abuse). Monitor for QR-code scans or session-restoration outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: Fake utility download site access and executable fetch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'network of more than 150 fake download sites that closely mimic trusted' utilities as the initial vector—no UC addresses first contact with lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS downloads of executable files from recently-registered domains with typosquatted names (e.g., 7z-download, winrar-official) or from IPs in bulletproof-hoster ASNs. Correlate domain reputation with download binary hash.

suggestion.title: GPU resource hijacking by unknown process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU'—no detection for sustained GPU utilization from non-whitelisted processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger when GPU utilization >70% sustained >30min from process NOT in approved-list (rendering software, development tools, games). Cross-check process hash/path against malware IOC list; low FP if whitelist is current.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded executable—filename mimics utility, signature mismatched
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malware-laced files'—files named '7-Zip.exe' or 'WinRAR.exe' but signed by attacker or unsigned. RMM hunt misses execution of the initial-stage dropper.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag executables where ProductName/OriginalFilename matches common utility (WinRAR, 7-Zip, VLC) but SignerName != legitimate vendor, or where embedded signatures are invalid/absent. VirusTotal query on hash validates maliciousness.

suggestion.title: Executable downloaded from suspicious domain, executed <2min later
suggestion.rationale: Kill-chain link (download → execution) is the critical hand-off; RMM hunt only detects downstream ScreenConnect process, not the malware bootstrap itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate proxy log (executable MIME-type from non-whitelisted domain) → file write to user Downloads/Temp → process execution of that file within <120s window. High-risk if hash is not in known-good catalog.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 from ScreenConnect on non-IT workstation
suggestion.rationale: RMM hunt detects installation only; does not detect command-and-control beaconing. ScreenConnect must establish outbound sessions to attacker C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/SSL from ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe originating on non-IT-owned device, destined to IPs not in public ScreenConnect relay-server range. Escalate unknown C2 IPs; known-attacker IPs (from article IOCs) trigger incident.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or packed payload executed by legitimate-looking parent
suggestion.rationale: Article notes obfuscation (T1027); typical cryptominer dropper is legitimate utility or downloader that unpacks/injects hidden miner. Detects defense-evasion layer between download and mining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag parent process (utility or ScreenConnect installer) spawning child with command-line >500 chars, base64 encoding, PowerShell -enc flags, or suspicious image loads (unusual DLLs, in-memory injection markers). Hash child process against malware IOCs.

suggestion.title: npm Package Supply Chain Compromise - dbmux Installation Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malicious package targeting software developers has been discovered on npm' and 'dbmux' contains 'hidden malware.' Package name is a canonical IOC; no installation detection UC was generated despite being the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install/require operations for package 'dbmux' or on rapid installations of newly-published low-reputation npm packages.
