Monitor package-lock.json and package.json for package name matches. Correlate timestamp of install with subsequent unexpected process spawning or network egress.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Execution - Child Process Anomaly from node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'capable of giving attackers complete control over developer's system.' Execution phase is mandatory but absent. Process spawning from node_modules or npm lifecycle hooks must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child process execution spawned by node.exe, npm.exe, or from node_modules/.bin paths, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, or curl/wget. Alert on processes with Base64-encoded arguments or obfuscated command lines. Correlate timing to npm install events.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Compromised Developer Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'complete control over developer's system' implies persistent adversary access. No C2 or exfiltration detection UC was suggested despite explicit threat of post-exploitation control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from dev systems shortly after dbmux installation. Alert on non-standard ports, DGA-like domains, or IP ranges with no prior whitelisting. Correlate DNS queries and TLS handshakes with known C2 signatures or anomalous certificate names.

suggestion.title: Persistence via npm Lifecycle Scripts (postinstall / prepare hooks)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'complete control' requires persistence. npm postinstall/prepare scripts are a known persistence vector for package malware; no UC captured this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json and package-lock.json for unusual lifecycle script entries (preinstall, postinstall, prepare). Alert on scripts that spawn system processes, write to startup directories (/etc/profile, HKLM\Run), or establish reverse shells.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Metadata Anomaly - Rapid Package Republish / Publisher Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks exploit registry trust. Article does not detail version history or account compromise, but a detection UC should hunt for suspicious publisher activity or version anomalies (huge jumps, rapid iteration after silence).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry metadata (dbmux) for unexpected version increments, sudden republishes without matching commits, or account changes. Alert on packages newly published/modified by low-reputation accounts or after acquisition by high-value packages.

suggestion.title: dbmux Malware Hash / Signature - Known Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'dbmux' as the compromised package. Zero IOC output despite a canonical identifier. Block/alert on any file hash or package version matching known malicious dbmux releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain watchlist of dbmux package name and any published versions with known malicious payloads (hash signatures). Alert on installations or existing instances in node_modules directories. Trigger automated remediation: package removal, dependency audit, and system scan.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt against Ivanti critical vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly signals 'critical vulnerabilities' in Ivanti requiring patches; no use case generated despite Ivanti (IT management/Connect/Endpoint Manager) being frequent RCE target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti management endpoints (ports 443, 8080) for HTTP POST requests with suspicious payloads; inspect service account process creation for anomalous child processes; correlate inbound connections from untrusted sources with patched-application error logs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt against Fortinet critical vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms critical Fortinet patches; FortiGate/FortiProxy are primary attack surface for perimeter bypass. Pipeline extracted no Fortinet-specific detection scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiGate HTTP/HTTPS access logs to known-vulnerable endpoints (e.g., FortiOS REST API, Web UI); monitor for unexpected admin account creation/login post-vulnerability date; track policy/rule changes made via vulnerable interfaces.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt against SAP critical vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies SAP patches; SAP vulnerabilities (Gateway, Web Dispatcher, Portal) provide deep organizational penetration. No SAP-specific use case present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SAP application logs for SQL/ABAP injection patterns in Gateway or Dispatcher traffic; track authentication anomalies followed by privilege-escalation attempts; detect new RFC/system user creation in vulnerable SAP systems post-patch announcement.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP asset detection
suggestion.rationale: Patch-window risk is critical for vulnerability disclosures; pipeline generated zero inventory/patch-management use case despite this being the primary defensive action post-patch release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/SCCM for Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP product versions predating patched builds; cross-reference patch-deployment logs against vulnerable-product registry; escalate unpatched assets on critical networks post-patch-availability window (7+ days).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'maximum-severity flaw that enables remote attackers to execute code with root privileges' via 'OS command injection weakness.' No detection use case was generated despite clear attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs and network traffic for malicious command patterns, shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks), or encoded commands targeting the vulnerable endpoint. Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service with root privilege tokens.

suggestion.title: Rogue Admin Account Creation via Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10523)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables attackers to 'create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access' via authentication bypass. Critical persistence mechanism absent from use case list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any administrative account creation without corresponding authorization workflow or ticket trail. Monitor for account creation following failed authentication attempts against Sentry appliance. Track admin account login from unexpected sources or at unusual hours post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Exploitation Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes both flaws are exploitable 'remotely by unauthenticated attackers' with 'no evidence of exploitation in the wild.' Early detection rules needed for reconnaissance and exploitation attempts before patches deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Sentry traffic patterns. Alert on anomalous HTTP requests to known vulnerable endpoints, unusual User-Agent strings, rapid request sequences, or authentication-bypass payloads targeting Sentry API endpoints before version verification gates.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Privilege Escalation to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies execution occurs 'with root privileges' — this is not standard privilege level for secure gateway appliance processes. Elevation anomaly should trigger investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry process privilege levels. Alert on child processes spawned by Sentry service running with unexpected UID 0 (root) or escalation events. Correlate with suspicious command execution in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Sentry is 'a security gateway appliance that secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices'—compromise grants attacker position to pivot internal. No detection for post-exploitation movement captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Sentry appliance IP to internal corporate systems outside baseline. Alert on atypical protocols, large data transfers, or connections to multiple internal hosts from single compromised appliance. Correlate timing with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Version Validation & Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions are R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1. Organizations running pre-patch versions require continuous compliance monitoring. Version-tracking detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and device configuration repositories for Ivanti Sentry appliances. Alert on inventory records showing versions earlier than patched thresholds (< R10.5.2, < R10.6.2, < R10.7.1). Flag for remediation and escalate based on network exposure.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'RoguePlanet' as a Microsoft Defender zero-day. Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts: malicious arguments to Defender CLI tools, suspicious spawning from Defender processes, or instrumentation of MsMpEng.exe with high privileges. Article phrase: '[CRIT] Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual spawning of mpCmdRun.exe or MsMpEng.exe with command-line arguments containing suspicious paths, legitimate privilege escalation triggers, or execution from unexpected parent processes. Alert on any process with SYSTEM token creation traced back to Defender binaries in non-standard execution paths.

suggestion.title: Defender Engine Process (MsMpEng.exe) Abuse
suggestion.rationale: RoguePlanet targets Defender internals to reach SYSTEM. Detection must capture abnormal MsMpEng.exe behavior: unexpected child processes, network connections, file writes to sensitive locations, or timing inconsistencies. Title establishes Defender engine as attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline MsMpEng.exe process behavior (parent, children, network peers, file I/O patterns). Alert on spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other non-expected child processes; outbound network connections from the Defender engine; or writes to registry/system paths not consistent with legitimate scanning/update.

suggestion.title: Defender Update or Scan Weaponization
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day in Defender suggests exploitation may occur during scan initiation, update deployment, or task scheduling. Article states 'Updated Windows'—implying recent patch versions are exploitable. Detection needed for Defender task abuse or scan parameter injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor scheduled tasks invoking Defender components, esp. with arguments injected from user-writable paths. Track Defender configuration changes and scan task spawning with non-standard parent processes or elevated privilege requests outside of Windows Update context.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Privilege Token Creation via Security Product
suggestion.rationale: Impact is explicit: 'Grants SYSTEM Access.' Must detect when privilege escalation succeeds—new SYSTEM tokens created or impersonated after Defender interaction. Article title directly establishes SYSTEM as the goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on token impersonation or elevated process creation (SYSTEM level) originating from or correlated with Defender process execution, mpCmdRun.exe invocation, or Defender service manipulation within seconds. Cross-correlate process creation with privilege level transition events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Defender CLI Invocation (mpCmdRun.exe)
suggestion.rationale: Defender has command-line interfaces (mpCmdRun.exe) that could be weaponized if vulnerable. Article indicates interaction method unknown, but CLI abuse is a common vector for Defender-based privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mpCmdRun.exe execution with arguments containing path traversal sequences, quoted or obfuscated parameters, invocation from non-System processes, or execution with unusual parent processes. Alert if mpCmdRun.exe spawns elevated child processes or accesses sensitive system files.

suggestion.title: Defender Service Elevation or Restart Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Windows Defender service (WinDefend) runs as SYSTEM. Exploitation could pivot through service restart, configuration reload, or handler registration. Article states SYSTEM access is granted, suggesting service manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinDefend service start/stop/restart events, esp. initiated by non-SYSTEM processes. Alert on service binary path modification, handler or dependency injection, or rapid service state transitions preceding SYSTEM token creation. Track service restart triggered by user-mode code.

suggestion.title: Exchange OWA Email-Based XSS Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'sends a specially crafted email' and 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' when opened in OWA. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for malicious email payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails for embedded JavaScript, script tags, event handler attributes, or obfuscated code patterns. Alert on payloads intended for DOM manipulation or browser execution, especially those targeting OWA DOM elements or form handlers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Execution in OWA Application Pool
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' when user opens email in OWA. Detection must trigger on unexpected code execution within Outlook Web Access worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal child process creation from w3wp.exe (OWA pool), unexpected shell spawning from OWA context, or suspicious DLL injection into OWA processes during or shortly after user email interaction.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42897 Exchange XSS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-42897 is the specific zero-day disclosed as actively exploited across Exchange 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. Pipeline must map this vulnerability to exploitation pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests and email content for CVE-2026-42897-specific XSS patterns (unusual header encodings, DOM-clobbering payloads, or script injection targeting OWA client-side handlers). Correlate with unpatched Exchange versions.

suggestion.title: Correlated Email Receipt-to-OWA Session Behavior Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack trigger: 'user opens the email in Outlook Web Access' → JavaScript executes. Detection must correlate inbound email delivery with anomalous OWA session activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound emails with suspicious OWA behavior within 5–10 minutes of user opening message: mailbox rule creation, rapid folder enumeration, credential access attempts, unexpected mailbox delegation, or process spawning from OWA session.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Encoded JavaScript in Inbound Emails
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'arbitrary JavaScript' payloads—likely obfuscated or encoded to bypass content filters. Detection must identify encoding/obfuscation tactics in XSS payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with base64-encoded JavaScript, hex-encoded strings, Unicode escapes, eval() calls, atob() functions, String.fromCharCode chains, or dynamic script generation. Prioritize payloads that decode to OWA-targeting code.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Microsoft Zero-Day RCE via Network Boundary
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Critical RCE Bugs' but pipeline extracted zero detections for RCE exploitation. Title alone demands initial-access detection for vulnerability abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound network traffic to known vulnerable Microsoft service ports (Exchange MAPI, IIS, SQL Server) from external sources on unpatched systems. Correlate with immediate process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) in SYSTEM context without corresponding user logon or legitimate application trigger.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Launch from Vulnerable Microsoft Service Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE execution phase missing entirely. Title guarantees RCE payloads lead to process execution; pipeline surfaced zero execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes (especially interpreters: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wmic.exe, cscript.exe) spawned from vulnerable service processes (w3wp.exe, sqlservr.exe, msexchangeserverd.exe) running as SYSTEM. Alert if parent process has no recent user logon or legitimate business reason to spawn children.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Exploitation Attempts on Unpatched Systems
suggestion.rationale: 206-flaws article likely includes elevation-of-privilege CVEs (common in Microsoft patches). Pipeline missed all privilege-escalation detection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes attempting to access token-impersonation APIs, opening LSASS handles for token theft, or modifying registry/file permissions to escalate. Correlate with vulnerability scanners reporting unpatched privilege-escalation CVEs on the same asset.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Registry Modification from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: RCE often leads to persistence mechanisms (Run keys, scheduled tasks, services). Article implies post-compromise activity but pipeline generated zero persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, or scheduled task creation originating from vulnerable service process contexts. Alert if modifications occur during off-hours or outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Exchange or SQL Service Account
suggestion.rationale: High-severity RCE in Exchange/SQL Server (common Microsoft attack surface) typically leads to lateral movement. Article title guarantees compromised systems exist; pipeline missed post-compromise movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service account authentication (Exchange service, SQL Agent, IIS AppPool identity) authenticating to systems outside normal trusted VLAN or performing SMB/RDP to sensitive servers. Flag failed logons followed by successful authentication immediately after RCE indicators on the source service host.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised Vulnerable Service
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'record 206 flaws'; RCE leads to confidentiality loss. Pipeline missed collection and exfiltration-phase detections despite high-impact vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers (>100MB) initiated from vulnerable service processes to external IPs, cloud storage, or staging servers. Correlate with file access to sensitive locations (mailbox stores, database files, share roots) by service account outside normal backup/maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: SSH Lateral Movement to Internal PeopleSoft Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes script that 'parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems and attempts to connect to them over SSH' — clear lateral movement attack after initial breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH connections originating from external IP ranges to internal PeopleSoft servers (port 22). Alert when connection attempts use known service accounts (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) and target multiple internal hosts within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Spray Against PeopleSoft Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Script 'attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm' — indicates automated credential testing against known account names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated SSH authentication failures using known PeopleSoft account names (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) from single source IP across multiple destination hosts within minutes — pattern consistent with credential spray.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Creation in PeopleSoft Application Directories
suggestion.rationale: Script found in bash_history designed to 'create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT' and 'drops the ransom note into directories associated with PeopleSoft web and application servers' — impact phase marker.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation events with filenames matching 'README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT' or similar ransom note patterns in PeopleSoft web/app directories (typically /apps/peoplesoft/webserver, /peoplesoft/appserver paths).

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Agent Deployment in PeopleSoft Environments
suggestion.rationale: Researcher discovered 'staging materials, including MeshCentral agents' in exposed directories — indicates remote access tool staging for persistence or post-exploitation command & control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of MeshCentral agent binaries or child processes spawned from PeopleSoft application directories. Monitor for network connections to known MeshCentral C2 addresses from PeopleSoft servers.

suggestion.title: TLS Certificate Reuse Across Multiple Malicious IPs
suggestion.rationale: Five IPs 'used a TLS certificate that has a common name of azurenetfiles[.]net' which is 'previously linked to the ShinyHunters extortion gang' — infrastructure fingerprint enabling actor tracking and attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS certificates with common name 'azurenetfiles[.]net' (or variants) in traffic from/to PeopleSoft infrastructure. Cross-reference certificate-issuing IPs against blocklist. Historic link to ShinyHunters provides high-confidence attribution.

suggestion.title: Exposed Web Directories Containing Attack Staging Materials
suggestion.rationale: Researcher found 'exposed online directories containing tooling related to this attack' and 'staging materials' visible publicly — indicates misconfigured web server exposure of attacker infrastructure or post-compromise staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for 404/200 responses on common staging directories (staging, temp, admin, tools). Alert on directory listings returning script files (.sh, .py, .ps1) or tool binaries in unexplained locations.

suggestion.title: POST /api/v2/files Request with Path Traversal Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences (\'../\').' This is the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/v2/files for filename parameters containing ../, ..\ or null-byte injection. Alert on multipart form data where filename parameter includes directory traversal patterns or path separators not matching expected filename format.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Session Token Issuance on Langflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token.' Detection should capture unexpected token generation without authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect session token generation or issuance events in Langflow logs without preceding credential validation or login request. Flag unexpected token creation from external network sources or from unexpected client applications.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Probes for Exposed Langflow Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Censys scans identified roughly 7,000 publicly exposed Langflow instances.' Detection should identify external scanning for Langflow endpoints or fingerprinting of Langflow deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential HTTP requests from single external source targeting Langflow-specific paths (/api/v2/files, /login, characteristic error pages). Alert on rapid probing patterns consistent with automated reconnaissance of Langflow instances.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Writes via Web Application Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances.' This describes the impact—arbitrary filesystem writes—separate from the upload request itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow application process for file creation outside designated upload directories. Correlate file writes with timestamps of suspicious POST /api/v2/files requests. Alert on writes to system directories, config paths, or non-standard locations coinciding with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Langflow Version Pinning Below Patch Level
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'issue was fixed in langflow-base package version 0.8.3, while the Langflow application itself received a patch in version 1.9.0' and recommends upgrade to 1.10.0. Detection should identify infrastructure running unpatched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow application version across inventory and runtime environments. Alert on instances running versions < 1.9.0 (Langflow) or < 0.8.3 (langflow-base). Track for version downgrades or stalled patch timelines post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to ServiceNow Vulnerability Actor IP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 51.159.98.241 as IOC and recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt with High confidence in phase c2; pipeline extracted zero IOCs and generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound/outbound network connections to 51.159.98.241 from ServiceNow instances or cloud infrastructure. Prioritize correlation with authentication anomalies and instance table access logs to confirm exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Unauthorized Table Query Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector not surfaced: 'execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication'—collection phase entirely absent from pipeline kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or inadequately-privileged API/query requests targeting sys_* tables, user rosters, or configuration tables. Flag rapid table enumeration, bulk metadata queries, or queries from IPs/sessions lacking RBAC grants to accessed table.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Authentication Bypass & Access Control Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper access controls...enable attackers to execute queries'—privilege escalation/auth bypass mechanism not represented. No T1078 or T1548 captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication failures preceding successful backend access, requests with missing/malformed auth headers, JWT/token tampering, or unexpected elevation of table-level permissions outside normal admin workflow.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing ServiceNow Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: T1190 absent: vulnerability resides in public-facing SaaS application requiring initial exploitation to trigger unauthorized access. Attack chain begins with vulnerability abuse, not direct C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation indicators: malformed query parameters, direct access to backend table endpoints, JWT/session token abuse, or API requests with known ServiceNow CVE signature patterns.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance & Tenant Metadata Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: ServiceNow is cloud-hosted SaaS; attack enables querying 'customer instance tables'—T1526 not captured despite cloud discovery being core to multi-tenant environment reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API enumeration of customer instances, tenant metadata queries, or requests to discovery endpoints iterating instance identifiers, particularly when correlated with subsequent table-access attempts.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Revocation Followed by Recursive Destructive File Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes dead-man switch: 'monitors the token's validity every minute and, if it's revoked, executes a destructive command (rm -rf ~/ ; rm -rf ~/Documents), recursively deleting files and directories.' This is a signature behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub token revocation events (via integration logs or credential manager logs) with subsequent shell commands executing rm -rf on user home directory. Monitor for systemd user services or LaunchAgent plist files with 'token' or 'validity' in their logic that trigger on credential invalidation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Credential Harvesting from Diverse Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores.' This pattern of scraping multiple credential sources in rapid succession is distinctive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing multiple credential storage locations in sequence (e.g., ~/.ssh, ~/.kube/config, ~/.aws, ~/.docker/config.json, browser password stores, 1Password/LastPass vaults) within a short time window on a single host, especially from build or CI/CD execution contexts.

suggestion.title: AI Tool Configuration File Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific targets: 'poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline.' Modifications to editor/IDE config files for these tools are abnormal and trackable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to .cursor/config, .vscode/settings.json, or IDE plugin directories that modify AI assistant endpoints, authentication tokens, or model selections. Correlate with suspicious process parents or after credential harvesting activity.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Compromise via Stolen GitHub Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Core TTPs: 'uses those [stolen credentials] to compromise legitimate repositories and packages, publishing trojanized versions.' Detection should focus on abnormal package publishing from compromised tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package pushes to npm, PyPI, or RubyGems that originate from GitHub tokens used previously for reconnaissance (e.g., same token, different org). Alert on unusual commit patterns (bulk file changes, build artifact modifications) or package version bumps without corresponding release notes in the repository.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH with Recently-Harvested Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM).' Credential harvesting followed by SSH lateral movement is the kill-chain signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful credential harvesting on Host A with subsequent SSH connections from Host A to developer machines or CI/CD systems using credentials obtained in that same session. Look for SSH to unusual hosts (non-standard dev infrastructure) shortly after password manager or secret store access.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Obfuscated Payload with AES-256-GCM Encryption Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'five-stage build pipeline that generates unique payloads: per-file AES-256-GCM encryption of embedded assets, randomized string obfuscation, source transformations, JavaScript obfuscation, and a self-extracting loader with three layers of encryption.' Detection must focus on behavioral indicators since signatures fail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multi-layer decryption/deobfuscation sequences: look for processes that decode/decompress multiple times in memory before executing (e.g., base64 → gzip → AES decrypt → script execution). Monitor for self-extracting archives spawning shell interpreters or Node.js with in-memory script arguments.

suggestion.title: Langflow CVE-2026-5027 Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE'—the primary exploitation vector—but no detection rule was generated. This is the core attack scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to known Langflow endpoints (/api/*, /run, /execute, /build) lacking authentication tokens or with suspicious command-injection payloads. Flag successful (200/201) responses from unauthenticated clients, especially from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from Langflow Python Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article references RCE exploitation but no detection covers post-compromise command execution phase spawned from the vulnerable application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by python.exe or langflow process with suspicious command lines: reverse shells, encoded payloads, curl/wget for staged downloads, or unexpected network connections from Langflow service account.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Langflow Installation Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Unpatched Langflow'—no inventory/asset discovery rule to identify vulnerable instances was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Langflow process detection with version parsing. Alert if version is below patched threshold. Cross-reference asset database to flag unpatched instances for remediation.

suggestion.title: Missing Authentication on Langflow API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access is the vulnerability class ('Unauthenticated RCE')—no detection for missing auth controls was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints (200/201 response) that lack Authorization header, Bearer token, or valid session cookie. Correlate with request body containing code fragments, templates, or shell metacharacters.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Unexpected Child Process with System Privilege
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows a local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM.' A core detection should hunt for CTFMON (running as user) spawning child processes running as SYSTEM or elevation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CTFMON.EXE creating child processes where the child's integrity level or privilege elevation exceeds the parent. Baseline legitimate CTFMON spawns; flag anomalous children or SYSTEM-level execution.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Token Impersonation or Access Token Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation primitives for privilege escalation often involve token theft or manipulation. Article describes this as a 'valuable post-exploitation primitive,' suggesting token-level attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where CTFMON or child processes request SeDebugPrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege, or other elevation tokens. Look for unusual token parent-child relationships or impersonation handles.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Registry or File System Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation often involves modifying HKLM registry keys or system files. Article implies CTFMON can be abused to modify protected resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CTFMON writing to HKLM registry hives, Windows\System32 directories, or other protected paths. Baseline normal CTFMON file/registry activity; flag writes that deviate.

suggestion.title: UAC Bypass via CTFMON or COM Elevation Moniker
suggestion.rationale: Framework name 'Collaborative Translation Framework' and 'CTF' acronym suggests possible COM object or script host abuse. Local privilege escalation often leverages UAC bypass via elevated COM interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for child processes spawned by CTFMON or services interacting with CTFMON where the child inherits elevated integrity level despite the parent being medium. Detect COM object elevation patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-35616 Public Exploit Activity on SOHO Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'rapid vulnerability exploitation' of CVE-2026-35616. Recommended hunt provided in article ('Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)') was not generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound exploit traffic to CVE-2026-35616 on SOHO/IoT default management ports (80, 443, 8080). Correlate with device type enumeration and firmware extraction attempts. Flag if same source scans multiple /24 residential blocks within 12 hours.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to JDY Botnet C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides five explicit C2 IPs with recommended hunt marked 'phase: c2, confidence: High'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/UDP to 149.248.3.38, 23.27.120.240, 109.104.154.116, 216.173.65.250, 194.14.217.88 from residential/SOHO IP blocks. Prioritize sustained connections or regular callback patterns characteristic of botnet C2.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware File Hash Detection and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article lists eight SHA256 hashes with recommended hunt ('File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match', phase: install). Pipeline ignored this structured hunt entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or execution of eight provided hashes on SOHO devices (routers, NAS, IoT). Prioritize persistence locations (/etc/cron.d, /usr/local/bin, firmware partitions). Alert on any match.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Malware Payload Execution on IoT Firmware
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as observed technique. Pipeline failed to create corresponding detection for encoded/packed malware characteristic of botnet propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64 or hex-encoded command execution on SOHO devices. Look for entropy anomalies in process memory, shell invocations with obfuscated arguments, or compressed payloads extracted at runtime matching hash IOCs.

suggestion.title: npm Script Execution During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks'—the attack vector is script execution during npm install. No use case generated despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by npm or node with command lines containing postinstall, preinstall, or install script directives. Flag execution of unexpected shell commands (bash, powershell, cmd.exe) as children of npm install operations, especially with outbound network or file write activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses npm package compromise as the delivery mechanism. Needs detection for unexpected or unauthorized package downloads and installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry calls for installation of packages not in org whitelist, or packages installed outside of CI/CD pipelines. Flag connections to non-standard npm registries or package sources with mismatched hash signatures.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via npm install
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain scripts often run with developer or elevated privileges. Article emphasizes disabling by default—implying the danger is privilege abuse during installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install or npm scripts executed with admin/sudo privileges. Alert on UAC bypasses or token elevation attempts triggered by npm processes. Monitor for process elevation immediately following package.json modification.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Dependency Addition
suggestion.rationale: The mitigation disables install scripts—attack requires first injecting malicious script into package.json or a package. Detection should cover unauthorized dependency changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to package.json or package-lock.json files outside of standard developer workflows (time-of-day anomalies, unusual accounts, non-CI commits). Correlate with subsequent npm install operations.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from npm Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Malicious install scripts would exfiltrate data or download payloads. Article threat model implies C2 or data-theft payloads executed post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections originating from node.exe or npm child processes during or immediately after install. Alert on non-repo, non-CDN destinations (new domains, high-risk geoIP, known C2 infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Ivanti EPMM Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-6973 and CVE-2026-10727 in indicators section; pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the entry point for asset-driven detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti EPMM instances running versions 12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1 or other vulnerable versions. Cross-correlate with vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-6973 and CVE-2026-10727. Alert on unpatched systems in production and track remediation closure time.

suggestion.title: Apache Configuration Directive Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack mechanism: 'injecting malicious Apache configuration directives'—critical execution phase requiring dedicated detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti EPMM admin and config endpoints for payloads containing Apache directive syntax (LoadModule, Include, ProxyPass, AddHandler, SetHandler). Flag POST/PUT requests with special characters or bracket syntax to configuration paths. Correlate with subsequent service restarts or unexpected process spawning.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Ivanti EPMM Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated attackers'; pipeline missed detection for baseline authentication patterns and anomalous post-login behavior despite article emphasis on authentication requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Ivanti EPMM administrator and service account authentication patterns. Alert on: (1) successful login immediately followed by requests to sensitive endpoints (/config, /admin, /upload); (2) failed authentication attempts within 5 minutes preceding successful access; (3) user account creation or privilege escalation post-login.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Signal — Unexpected Process from Ivanti Service
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is remote code execution; pipeline proposed no detection for post-exploitation process spawning despite RCE being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent is Apache httpd or Ivanti EPMM service spawning unexpected children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc, curl, wget, python, perl). Alert on web-service-context process execution. Whitelist known legitimate child processes to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Service Restart or Crash Anomaly Correlated with Exploitation Window
suggestion.rationale: Malicious Apache directives may cause service instability or restart; pipeline did not propose detection for unexpected Ivanti service state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected service restarts or crashes of Ivanti EPMM or Apache httpd. Correlate timing with preceding HTTP error bursts (500, 502, 503) and requests containing injection payloads. Track service uptime anomalies in time window post-exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection from Compromised Ivanti EPMM Host
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE may enable command-and-control channel establishment; pipeline did not propose network-based detection for C2 signaling post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Ivanti EPMM server following suspected exploitation window. Alert on connections to suspicious IPs/domains, DNS queries to known C2 domains, encrypted traffic to non-standard ports, and beaconing patterns (periodic outbound connections at fixed intervals).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'We are observing a large amount of Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 exploitation attempts based on the public PoC today.' Pipeline generated zero detection for active exploitation despite explicit confirmation by security researchers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to Ivanti Sentry admin interfaces containing command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax). Correlate requests with source IP geolocation, velocity (scanning patterns), and User-Agent anomalies. Baseline legitimate Sentry admin access and flag deviations from known administrator IP ranges or time-of-day patterns.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Sentry Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'maximum-severity flaw in Ivanti Sentry, enabling them to execute code with root privileges.' The vulnerability is explicitly 'an OS command injection weakness.' Pipeline missed execution-layer detection despite this being the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service principal (typically running as root/system). Alert on process creation with command-line arguments containing shell metacharacters (;|&$()\`), network utilities (curl, wget, nc), or reverse-shell patterns. Flag process ancestry anomalies where web service spawns system shells.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence on Compromised Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online.' Shadowserver confirmed at least 2 confirmed backdoors, warned 'all remaining likely compromised too.' Zero persistence detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification in Sentry installation directories, particularly unexpected binaries, scripts, or libraries. Monitor for scheduled task/cron job creation on gateway systems post-patch date. Track unauthorized user account creation within Sentry admin interfaces or underlying OS. Correlate with network telemetry showing outbound C2 callbacks from gateway.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article shows: 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online (Shadowserver).' Pipeline generated zero detection for exposed attack surface despite explicit documentation of Internet-facing admin interfaces being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry gateways exposed on the public Internet by scanning for characteristic TLS certificates, HTTP response headers (Server: MobileIron, Set-Cookie patterns), or admin portal paths (typically /sentry/admin, port 8443). Alert on any Sentry instance responding to external IP ranges without VPN/corporate network geofencing. Correlate external access attempts with vulnerability disclosure dates.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'entry point into targets' enterprise networks' for 'theft of sensitive customer and corporate data.' Pipeline missed post-exploitation detection despite explicit narrative of gateways being used for network pivoting and data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for atypical egress traffic from Ivanti Sentry gateway subnets, including network reconnaissance activity (port scans to internal ranges, DNS queries to previously uncontacted internal hosts), large data transfers to external IPs, or reverse-shell callbacks. Establish baseline of normal gateway traffic and alert on deviations post-compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists patched versions (R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1) but pipeline generated zero inventory detection. Vulnerable gateways running pre-patch versions are critical assets requiring immediate remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry version information via admin portal banner grabbing or SNMP. Alert on gateways running versions prior to R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unpatched instances. Correlate version detection with external exposure (public DNS records, shodan/censys data) and timeline against CVE disclosure (2026-06-11) for post-disclosure exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure – CVE-2026-42897 on-premises Exchange Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'zero-day spoofing flaw in on-premises Exchange Server, tracked as CVE-2026-42897' — must identify vulnerable Exchange instances via patch management and vulnerability inventory before attackers do.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify on-premises Exchange Server instances via asset inventory or vulnerability scans. Cross-reference against Microsoft patch/advisory KB articles for CVE-2026-42897. Flag systems running unpatched versions and prioritize for remediation.

suggestion.title: Weaponized Email Delivery – CVE-2026-42897 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'weaponized email that a victim opens in a browser' as the attack vector. Must detect emails crafted to exploit CVE-2026-42897 before users open them in OWA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateways for messages targeting OWA users with JavaScript payloads, suspicious attachment types, or content matching known CVE-2026-42897 exploitation patterns. Correlate sender reputation, recipient role (Exchange admin), and delivery to OWA users.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Execution in OWA Session Context
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in Outlook Web Access' — must detect unexpected script execution within OWA worker processes or browser context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA sessions for unusual script injection, DOM manipulation, or console execution. Alert on HTTP requests to OWA endpoints containing JavaScript payloads, inline script execution from OWA-originated processes, or anomalous function calls from OWA security context.

suggestion.title: OWA Access Pattern Spike Correlation with Email Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires email delivery → user opens in OWA → exploitation. Detect correlated spikes in OWA login/access from users who received weaponized email.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate weaponized email distribution events (by sender, subject, attachment hash) with subsequent OWA access from recipient accounts within 5–30 minutes. Alert on bulk email campaigns followed by anomalous OWA login patterns, especially from unusual geographies or endpoints.

suggestion.title: Exchange Server HTTP Request Anomalies – CVE-2026-42897 Exploitation Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: JavaScript execution in OWA implies HTTP requests carrying malicious payload. Exchange/IIS logs should contain evidence of exploitation attempts before JavaScript execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Exchange Server and IIS HTTP logs for POST/GET requests to OWA endpoints containing encoded JavaScript, script tags, or known payload signatures. Alert on requests triggering 500-level errors or unusual status codes before user interaction completes.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities in attacks' against PeopleSoft 'cloud and on-premises instances.' Detection must identify exploitation attempts leveraging Java deserialization or unpatched RCE flaws.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft web endpoints (/psc/*/iscript/ paths) for POST requests with Java serialized object payloads (ysoserial, CommonsCollections signatures), unusual Content-Encoding, or Content-Length anomalies. Correlate with cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from web server process (tomcat.exe, java.exe).

suggestion.title: Bulk Exfiltration of Student Records Database
suggestion.rationale: Article describes theft of 'over 40GB of documents' from 'student record system' containing names, addresses, phone numbers, ethnicities, passport numbers, academic enrollments, payment data. Single-stage exfiltration of this magnitude is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries returning >100MB of student PII (multi-column SELECT on names, addresses, phone, passport, ethnicity fields). Detect network transfers of >500MB to non-approved external IPs from database server. Flag Service Account reading >1M student records in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Multi-Organization PeopleSoft Campaign Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'widespread data theft campaign in which ShinyHunters gang has stolen data from over 100 organizations worldwide' targeting PeopleSoft. Cross-org pattern recognition is critical for early warning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate source IPs performing reconnaissance against multiple PeopleSoft tenant instances (via /psc/*/iscript/ enumeration, /PHANPRD/ directory scanning). Alert on auth failures → successful login cycles across multiple .ac.uk or corporate domains. Monitor for Shodan/zoomeye queries for 'PeopleSoft' or 'HCM' in Education sector.

suggestion.title: Extortion Threat / Dark Web Leak Site Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ShinyHunters claimed responsibility on Tuesday and shared an archive of allegedly stolen documents' posted to 'their dark web leak site.' Implies pre-extortion communication or threat posting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor threat feeds and dark web archives for references to 'Nottingham University,' '454,600 students,' or '40GB' data dump. Correlate with known ShinyHunters infrastructure IOCs if available. Flag C2 beacons to Tor exit nodes or known extortion site hosts within 72 hours of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Inconsistent PeopleSoft Exploitation Success Rates Across Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'attack is not working on all systems, likely because successful exploitation depends on each instance's configuration.' This indicates configuration-dependent RCE (likely improper patching or hardening variance).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed RCE exploitation attempts (HTTP 500/502 errors, timeout patterns, incomplete code execution) correlated with successful ones. Alert when same source IP/domain probes PeopleSoft with identical gadget chain payload but succeeds only against subset of instances (suggests version/patch fingerprinting).

suggestion.title: Third-Party PeopleSoft Hosting Compromise Affecting Multiple Institutions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'working with the third party that maintains the platform' and breach affected Nottingham UK, Malaysia, and China campuses via shared cloud infrastructure. Suggests supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cross-tenant lateral movement within PeopleSoft cloud hosting (e.g., Nottingham Malaysia/China campus data accessed from non-Malaysia/non-China IP). Monitor third-party service account privilege escalation or unusual administrative logins to PeopleSoft SaaS tenants. Flag concurrent access to multiple customer records from single compromised provider account.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'authentication bypass' is the primary attack vector. Pipeline extracted no logic to detect login success without credential validation or session fixation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB login endpoints for successful authentication followed immediately by privilege escalation actions without intermediate password reset events. Detect repeated failed logins from same IP within <5min followed by success without account lockout reset. Alert on access to /admin/ or /adm/ paths post-login without proper group membership.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Attempt via phpBB
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'RCE' as primary impact from vulnerability. No detection logic for unauthenticated code execution attempts on phpBB endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to phpBB pages (e.g., posting, profile, search endpoints) containing shell metacharacters, encoded payloads (base64, URL-encoded), or script directives when originating from non-admin IPs. Correlate with spawned child processes (php-cgi, bash) from web server parent.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Placement in phpBB Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability implies post-exploitation persistence. Article does not detail but is standard; pipeline missed file-write detection use case entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB web root and subdirectories (/styles/, /images/, /files/) for unexpected .php, .phtml, .php5 files created outside of legitimate installation/update timeframes. Alert on files with suspicious naming (test.php, shell.php, admin.php in non-standard locations) or atypical content entropy.

suggestion.title: Admin Panel Enrollment via Authenticated phpBB Session
suggestion.rationale: Post-auth-bypass, attacker would create persistent admin account. Article states 'tens of millions affected'; detection for admin account creation is critical and missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag admin account creation or privilege escalation events in phpBB database/logs when initiated by accounts outside administrative groups or during RCE indicators. Correlate new user/group assignments with unusual source IPs or password reset events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from phpBB Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE enables command execution and potential data exfiltration or C2 callback. Article implies scale ('tens of millions'); detection for web-server-initiated C2 is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by web server process (apache2, httpd, nginx, php-fpm) to non-whitelisted external IPs on non-standard ports. Alert on DNS queries to malware/botnet domains from web context. Establish baseline of legitimate external calls (updates, APIs) and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Log Injection / Log Tampering in phpBB
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with RCE would disable audit trails. Article mentions 'critical' and historical reach; defense-evasion via log deletion is standard post-exploitation tactic not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag deletion or truncation of phpBB log files (error logs, access logs, admin action logs) outside of maintenance windows. Detect gaps in log sequence numbers or timestamps. Monitor for direct filesystem writes to log locations bypassing application API.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'JDY Botnet expands to 1,500+ devices'—indicates active command-and-control infrastructure and sustained C2 communication. No C&C detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound beacons from infected hosts to botnet C2 servers. Monitor for DNS queries to C2 domains, repeated connections to static IPs on non-standard ports, and encrypted payloads to command infrastructure. Correlate multiple internal IPs connecting to same external endpoint.

suggestion.title: Cyber Reconnaissance - Network & Host Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'cyber reconnaissance' as the botnet objective. No detection rules provided for reconnaissance-phase activity (network scanning, port probing, service enumeration, system discovery).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance commands executed from compromised hosts: nping/nmap scanning, ipconfig/arp enumeration, route table queries, netstat/netsh execution. Alert on systematic IP enumeration, ICMP sweep patterns, and rapid port scanning attempts across internal subnets.

suggestion.title: Botnet Execution & Persistence Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 1,500+ infected devices but supplies no detection logic for botnet sample execution, DLL injection, registry persistence, or malware installation artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect botnet sample execution via unsigned binaries, DLL sideloading, or process hollowing. Monitor registry for Run/RunOnce modifications, startup directory writes, and scheduled task creation. Correlate process execution against known botnet sample hashes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement & Network Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Botnet 'expands to 1,500+ devices' indicates propagation and lateral movement across networks. No detection cases for SMB exploitation, RDP abuse, or worm-like spreading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB/RDP lateral movement and WMI exploitation. Detect suspicious process spawning (cmd/powershell from svchost), failed authentication bursts across multiple hosts, and remote process execution patterns. Alert on unusual share enumeration and network propagation artifacts.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Data Exfiltration to C2
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance-focused botnet must exfiltrate collected enumeration data. No use case for detecting data exfiltration of network topology and host discovery results to command servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag abnormally large outbound data transfers from infected hosts to C2 servers following reconnaissance activity. Correlate reconnaissance command execution with subsequent outbound connections. Detect compression or encoding of enumeration data being transmitted externally.

suggestion.title: Development Environment Code Injection via Cross-Platform Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'code is being written everywhere'—indicates threats targeting development environments and IDEs where code originates and flows across platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected code execution, compilation, or interpreter invocation (python, node, java, dotnet) from dev directories. Alert on IDE or git processes spawning uncommon shell commands or accessing credential stores.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Development Platform Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Subtitle 'device is the only constant' suggests threat actors leverage shared dev tools/credentials across heterogeneous endpoints to pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect development tool usage (git, npm, ssh keys, docker) from non-development systems. Flag developer account credentials being used across non-dev network segments or unusual login times.

suggestion.title: Rust Crate Installation from Suspicious Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes supply-chain attack via compromised Rust package ('onering'); no use case for detecting installation or import of malicious crate versions from public registry or local cache.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cargo or rustc processes installing crate 'onering' with version signatures tied to malicious releases. Monitor .cargo directory for unexpected manifest changes or crate downloads from non-standard sources. Alert on build pipelines that pull unvetted dependency versions.

suggestion.title: Code Exfiltration via Rust Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'code exfiltration' as attack payload; no use case for detecting suspicious data staging or network beaconing during compilation or post-build artifact delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rustc, cargo, or spawned child processes initiating outbound connections to external C2 or exfiltration endpoints during build. Monitor for creation of staging files in /tmp or similar during compilation that could indicate source-code collection. Watch for base64-encoded or compressed payloads in network traffic matching Rust source patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Build Artifact in Compiled Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration; no detection for injected code or suspicious symbols embedded in compiled binaries produced from 'onering' dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan compiled binaries (ELF/dylib) for embedded URLs, hardcoded IPs, or suspicious function names injected by 'onering' dependency. Monitor for unsigned or anomalously-signed binaries built with malicious crate. Check DWARF debug info for exfiltration logic markers.

suggestion.title: Crate.io or Alternative Registry Compromise Signaling
suggestion.rationale: Article implies successful supply-chain compromise; no use case for detecting account takeover, typosquatting, or version poisoning on Rust package registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual Crates.io publisher activity: version uploads from new geolocations, rapid version releases, yanked+repushed versions, or commits to crate source repo from unfamiliar actors. Monitor for similar crate names (typosquatting). Correlate with dependent-project build logs for surprise crate downloads.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion or Lockfile Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack likely requires victims to pull malicious version; no use case for detecting modified Cargo.lock, .git/config, or registry downgrades that force old/malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Cargo.lock downgrades or version specifications that relax constraints, pulling lower/older 'onering' versions post-compromise. Detect git config modifications redirecting crates.io to alternative registry. Monitor build containers for environment variable overrides of CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN or similar.

suggestion.title: Post-Execution Code Callback from Onering Payload
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration implies active callback; no use case for detecting callback traffic from binaries linked to malicious 'onering' at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and outbound TCP/UDP from processes spawned by code compiled with 'onering' dependency, targeting known C2 domains or IP ranges. Watch for encoded/chunked exfiltration traffic masquerading as normal HTTP/S. Alert on child processes of build tools making network calls.

suggestion.title: Baileys protocolMessage deserialization — synthetic message.upsert detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger a fake `messages.upsert` event with a **fake message key and payload**' and 'allows anyone to spoof messages.' No application-level detection for message integrity or spoofing indicators provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys message logs for upsert events with message keys failing integrity validation or sender mismatches against session history. Flag protocolMessage deserialization that generates synthetic upsert records without corresponding user message actions.

suggestion.title: App state sync — malformed keyData mutations and truncation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key s...' describes integrity violations in state sync. Existing hunts detect package presence only; missing is behavioral detection for state corruption signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys app state directory for rollback, malformed keyData structures, or truncated sync operations that don't correlate with user message activity. Alert on unexpected state mutations or key deletions outside normal sync patterns.

suggestion.title: Baileys version compliance — post-deployment patch threshold enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerable versions explicitly '< 7.0.0-rc12, and < 6.7.22' are enumerated. TVM and filesystem hunts detect presence; missing is continuous version compliance and downgrade detection post-deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Weekly parsing of package.json and package-lock.json in monitored Node.js project roots to verify Baileys is at or above patch threshold. Alert on version downgrades below cutoff or dependency-pin evasion.

suggestion.title: GPU resource hijacking — cryptominer process anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU' but no detection for miner behavior. Expect xmrig, claymore, or similar crypto-process execution or unusual high GPU utilization from non-graphics applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process creation of known cryptomining tools (xmrig, claymore, kryptex, etc.) or children of ScreenConnect/suspicious installers. Complement with GPU utilization spike >80% sustained for >10min from processes lacking graphics legitimacy (non-game, non-rendering software).

suggestion.title: Suspicious file execution from Downloads folder
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'users downloading malware-laced files' from fake sites. No UC for user-executed binaries from Download/Temp directories post-download. This is core T1204.002 execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process is explorer.exe or file manager, child process is .exe/.msi/.scr from user's Downloads, AppData\Local\Temp, or %TEMP% folder. High risk if parent is browser and file was downloaded <5min before execution.

suggestion.title: Typosquat / fake utility download domain access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '150 fake download sites' mimicking legitimate utilities. No hunt for domain reputation or known typosquats (gleeze, giize subdomains). Users visiting malicious download sites should trigger alerts before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network connections to suspicious download domains with low reputation scores. Flag subdomains of gleeze.com, giize.com, directdownload.icu and any domain registrations <30 days old with 'download', 'direct', 'free' in the name accessed by non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Packed/obfuscated executable detection via file entropy
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1027 'Obfuscated Files or Information' is listed but no specific detection. The 12 SHA256 hashes are likely packed or obfuscated payloads. Detect via entropy, section names (UPX, .packed), or signature of packing tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File created in user-writable directory (Downloads, Desktop, Temp) with high entropy (>7.5 bits) or PE header signatures of common packers. Or process creation where image file was modified <1min before execution from suspicious source.

suggestion.title: C2 communication to mining pools
suggestion.rationale: Installed miner must communicate with mining pool for work distribution and result submission. T1071 Application Layer Protocol is listed, suggesting C2 communication. Detect egress to known mining pool IPs/domains and unusual outbound connection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Egress network connections from non-browser processes (ScreenConnect children, or processes created after suspicious executable) to minemine.gleeze.com, known mining pool IPs (nicehash, supportxmr, etc.), or unusual port usage (ports 6667, 3333, 7777 for stratum mining protocol).

suggestion.title: Ingress of secondary payloads via ScreenConnect
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect is foothold for attacker to deploy miner. Article doesn't detail staging, but likely ScreenConnect command execution downloads miner executable. Detect file write/download by ScreenConnect process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process is ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe or child of its svchost wrapper, executing suspicious commands or creating/writing executable files to System32, AppData, or Temp. Look for powershell.exe, cmd.exe, certutil.exe, or file write activity from ScreenConnect context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation (Supply Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'dbmux' as malicious npm package; 'any developer's system that had it installed' establishes execution on install. Pipeline missed basic package-name IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update operations for known-malicious package names. Trigger on package.json or package-lock.json modifications adding 'dbmux' or similar indicators. Cross-reference against curated supply-chain IOC feeds updated during initial-access phase.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Node Modules Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'capable of giving attackers complete control' after install—implying post-install execution. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for node_modules-spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from node_modules directory (especially .bin executables) with unusual command-lines, parent processes, or target privileges. Flag shell interpreters (PowerShell, bash) invoked from npm package context during install/startup phases.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall Hook Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware execution on npm package install typically occurs via postinstall scripts or preinstall hooks. Article's 'installed or running' suggests hook-based execution not surface-level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of scripts defined in package.json's postinstall, preinstall, or install hooks. Flag obfuscated script content, non-standard interpreters, or network callbacks initiated during these phases. Correlate with parent npm process to baseline expected behavior.

suggestion.title: Package Registry Upload by Unauthorized Actors
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hackers infect' dbmux, implying unauthorized package version push. Pipeline missed threat-actor IOC or registry-integrity monitoring for this initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious package versions uploaded to npm registry: version bumps without corresponding repository commits, uploads by new/compromised accounts, or rapid version iteration in short timeframe. Cross-reference maintainer account activity with known compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: System Compromise Indicators Post-npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article claims 'complete control over any developer's system'—impact phase includes persistent access, C2, and lateral-movement preparation. Pipeline generated zero impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-npm install, monitor for unusual network connections from Node.js/npm context, unauthorized scheduled tasks, persistence mechanisms (registry modifications, cron jobs), or privilege escalation attempts. Establish timeline: npm install → first anomalous activity as indicator of successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Against Patched Vulnerability (Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or attack signatures. Cannot cite specific CVE without readable article body, but patch-release articles inherently describe exploitation patterns that should yield at least 1–3 detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP systems with patterns consistent with known CVE exploitation (malformed headers, SQL injection attempts, path traversal, authentication bypass attempts). Correlate with recent patch-release dates to identify pre-patch attack windows.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution via Patched Vendor Software
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities in network-facing appliances (Ivanti Connect Secure, FortiGate) and business systems (SAP) historically lead to RCE. Article mentions 'patches' but pipeline surfaced no execution-phase detection. Should detect shell/command activity spawned by compromised vendor processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of system shells (cmd.exe, bash, powershell.exe) or suspicious scripts spawned by Ivanti, Fortinet, or SAP application processes. Flag unusual parent-child process relationships or network I/O from these processes to external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation via Compromised Vendor Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti Connect Secure and FortiGate are network gateways; successful exploitation enables internal reconnaissance and lateral movement. Pipeline supplied no kill-chain phases indicating this progression. Article should reference scenarios where gateway compromise leads to internal network compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual inter-VLAN traffic originating from Ivanti/FortiGate appliance IPs, unexpected user logons from gateway process context, or SMB/RDP connections to internal systems initiated immediately after exploitation timeframes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Admin Account Creation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-10523 is 'a critical authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' This is the primary initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry administrative account creation events in audit logs for accounts created without a corresponding authenticated user session in the preceding 5 minutes. Flag admin account creation from IPs with no successful prior authentication.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection to Root Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10520 stems from 'an OS command injection weakness' enabling 'remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' Direct privilege escalation path via exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell processes (bash, sh, cmd) spawned directly or transitively from Ivanti Sentry daemon processes running as root. Flag unexpected child processes with environment variables or arguments containing encoding markers, redirects, or command separators.

suggestion.title: HTTP Payloads with Shell Metacharacters to Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Command injection vulnerabilities are exploited via HTTP parameters containing shell operators (semicolons, pipes, backticks, $(), redirects). Article describes attack as 'remotely' accessible without credentials, implying HTTP endpoint vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode and inspect HTTP request bodies to Ivanti Sentry endpoints. Flag URIs or POST parameters containing shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, ampersand, backtick, dollar-parenthesis, angle-brackets, newline encodings %0a %0d) especially from external networks.

suggestion.title: Version Detection: Ivanti Sentry Pre-Patch Inventory
