suggestion.rationale: Article names patched versions R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1 released June 10, 2026. Any earlier versions are vulnerable to both CVEs and should trigger urgency for patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Ivanti Sentry appliances via SNMP, HTTP version headers, or console access. Flag instances reporting version < R10.5.2, < R10.6.2, < R10.7.1 across respective release trains. Correlate with last patch timestamp.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Without Credential Elevation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: The kill chain chains auth bypass (CVE-2026-10523) → RCE as root (CVE-2026-10520). Sequential exploitation should show non-root process elevation to root without sudoers or setuid invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track privilege transitions on Ivanti Sentry appliance. Alert if a network-facing web service process spawns a child running as root without an intervening sudo/su call or setuid-bit transition visible in process audit logs.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Microsoft Defender Process Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access on Updated Windows'—a direct privilege escalation attack. Pipeline produced no detection UC for elevation to SYSTEM from Defender context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of child processes with SYSTEM privileges spawned from Microsoft Defender binaries (MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe) or elevation of these processes themselves via token manipulation or elevation control bypass. Flag any attempt to grant SYSTEM or TrustedInstaller tokens to non-Microsoft-signed processes.

suggestion.title: Unusual Microsoft Defender Memory or Handle Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Defender zero-day typically exploits Defender internals. Article hints at attack against the defender itself ('Defender RoguePlanet'), but pipeline generated no detection for process injection, memory access, or handle operations targeting Defender.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag remote memory reads/writes, DuplicateHandle, or memory mapping operations targeting MsMpEng.exe from unexpected parent processes. Monitor for loading of suspicious DLLs into Defender process address space or abnormal handle acquisition.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM-Level Process Spawning from Non-Standard Parent or Location
suggestion.rationale: Title states impact is 'SYSTEM Access'; this typically manifests as child process creation with SYSTEM privileges. No UC exists to detect the post-exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes running as SYSTEM spawned from user-mode contexts, interactive parent processes, or non-standard system directories. Baseline Defender-spawned processes; flag unexpected children outside normal Windows service operations.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification Targeting Microsoft Defender Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Exploits of system services often target registry keys controlling behavior or permissions. No UC for Defender-specific registry tampering (e.g., HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender, Service registry).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to Windows Defender registry paths, specifically Service configurations, security settings, or exclusion lists. Flag writes from non-SYSTEM, non-admin contexts or attempts to disable real-time protection via registry.

suggestion.title: Malicious Email Detection for CVE-2026-42897 XSS Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user.' No detection rule was generated for email content inspection or sender reputation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails with JavaScript/script tag payloads, HTML event handlers (onload, onerror), or encoded XSS patterns targeting Outlook Web Access. Correlate with sender reputation and recipient role (Exchange admin targets higher priority).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary JavaScript Execution via OWA User Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' when email opened in OWA 'and certain interaction conditions are met.' No detection for unexpected script execution from OWA sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual JavaScript execution, network requests, or DOM manipulation originating from OWA sessions. Alert on script execution with high entropy/obfuscation or attempts to exfiltrate session tokens or form credentials.

suggestion.title: EEMS Mitigation Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Microsoft deployed 'automatic temporary mitigation through the Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service (EEMS)' in mid-May, then later patch in June. No detection for attempts to bypass or detect circumvention of these mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to EEMS rules, disabling of mitigation scripts, or attempts to deliver payloads using encoded/obfuscated techniques not caught by standard XSS filters. Monitor for POST requests to Autodiscover or EWS APIs that attempt alternate delivery paths.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft or Session Hijacking Post-XSS Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article notes threat is 'high-severity spoofing vulnerability' that executes in 'browser context'—strong implication of credential or session token theft. No detection for post-execution credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual signin activity or API calls immediately following XSS exploitation windows (within minutes of user opening malicious email in OWA). Detect abnormal mail forwarding rules, delegate mailbox access changes, or uncharacteristic calendar/contact exports.

suggestion.title: Exchange Server Version/Build Enumeration Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'affects Exchange Server 2016, Exchange Server 2019, and Exchange Server Subscription Edition (SE).' No detection for reconnaissance probing to identify target version before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for probing requests to Exchange version-disclosure endpoints (e.g., Autodiscover, OWA version headers, 404 patterns). Flag repeated requests from single source attempting to fingerprint Exchange build.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Delivery Post-CVE-2026-42897 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Over the past five years, CISA has added 20 Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerabilities to its list of exploited security flaws, with ransomware gangs having exploited 14 of them.' Historical context suggests post-exploitation payload delivery is primary impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect living-off-the-land tools (PowerShell, wmic, certutil) or lateral movement activity originating from OWA/Exchange processes following successful XSS. Monitor for encryption/ransom note activities on file shares accessible from Exchange service account context.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Against Unpatched Microsoft RCE Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Critical RCE Bugs' and 'three Zero-Days.' Pipeline must detect exploitation vectors targeting these flaws, e.g., malformed network payloads to vulnerable services or suspicious spawned child processes from known Microsoft service executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal process spawning or command execution chains originating from vulnerable Microsoft service processes (e.g., SYSTEM-context child processes from svchost.exe, WMI processes, or RPC services). Flag memory access violations or crash dumps within vulnerable service address spaces.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Following RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE exploits are immediately leveraged for privilege escalation. Article describes RCE without privilege context; detection must cover elevation from initial compromise to SYSTEM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect token elevation attempts, scheduled task creation with SYSTEM privileges, or UAC bypass patterns immediately following anomalous execution from RCE attack surface (e.g., network service ports, WMI). Monitor for getsystem-style privilege token leakage.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploits chain to persistence via WMI subscriptions, scheduled tasks, or registry hives. Pipeline missed post-exploitation persistence detection for zero-day chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WMI event subscription creation, scheduled task registration with SYSTEM context, or HKLM registry modifications (Run keys, Services) occurring within seconds of suspicious RCE-origin process execution. Alert on unsigned binaries in System32 drop patterns.

suggestion.title: Delayed or Failed Deployment of Critical Microsoft Patches
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'record 206 flaws' requiring urgent patching. Detection must track deployment failure windows—every unpatched hour extends exploit window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WSUS/Windows Update logs for failed or stalled installations of KB articles targeting the 206 flaws. Alert on compliance drift—systems where patches succeeded on June 12 but failed on June 13, indicating potential rollback or tamper attempts.

suggestion.title: Active Reconnaissance for Unpatched Microsoft Services
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors scan for unpatched systems post-disclosure. Pipeline should detect enumeration of vulnerable service ports and version fingerprinting attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic for port scans targeting known vulnerable Microsoft service endpoints (e.g., RPC, DCOM, WMI ports). Flag repeated connection attempts to the same vulnerable port across multiple internal IPs, and unusual reverse-shell callback patterns to external C2.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exploited Credential or Service Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE with SYSTEM context enables lateral movement. Pipeline lacks detection for service-context lateral movement (network logons, psexec-style lateral spread).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network logons from SYSTEM or compromised service account context to adjacent systems. Alert on administrative share access (\\HOST\IPC$, \\HOST\ADMIN$) originating from initially-exploited host immediately following RCE timestamp.

suggestion.title: SSH Brute Force Against PeopleSoft Administrative Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'script attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm'. Pipeline missed detection for rapid SSH auth failures followed by key-based auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed SSH authentication attempts against known PeopleSoft admin accounts (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) from single source within short window, especially if followed by SSH key-based auth attempt. Baseline typical authentication patterns for these accounts and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Creation in PeopleSoft Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article cites: 'shell script designed to create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT on an internal PeopleSoft server'. Pipeline generated no detection for this post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of files matching ransom note pattern (README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS*, README-*-HACKED*) in PeopleSoft application directories (/opt/oracle/psft, /apps/peoplesoft). Flag even single occurrence as high-confidence compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Host File Enumeration for PeopleSoft Infrastructure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'script parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems'. Pipeline missed detection for host-file access patterns during lateral reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on subprocess spawning cat/grep against /etc/hosts after initial shell access. Especially suspicious if followed by SSH connection attempts to hostnames extracted from /etc/hosts. Correlate with failed auth logs to identify spraying behavior.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Remote Access Agent Installation
suggestion.rationale: Researcher found 'staging materials, including MeshCentral agents' in exposed directories. Pipeline failed to create detection for C2 agent drops.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MeshCentral binary installation/execution or unusual privileged service registration related to remote management. Monitor for MeshCentral config files in /opt, /etc, or user home directories. Flag network connections to known MeshCentral infrastructure ports.

suggestion.title: Credential Spray Script Execution Against Web Services
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'defacement and credential spray script' exposed in staging directories. Pipeline missed detection for spray attack patterns against PeopleSoft portals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on burst of HTTP POST requests to PeopleSoft portal login endpoints from single IP with varying credentials across short timeframe. Baseline normal authentication failure rates per source and flag anomalous spray patterns. Correlate with exposed IP addresses from IOC list.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Gadget Chain Exploitation of PeopleSoft
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'ShinyHunters says they are using a gadget chain of old and zero-day vulnerabilities'. Pipeline did not map exploit chain or initial access technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual HTTP requests to PeopleSoft endpoints from staging infrastructure IPs (142.11.200.0/24, 108.174.202.99). Alert on requests containing serialized Java objects or uncommon gadget-chain patterns. Track PeopleSoft patch levels and flag unpatched instances exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Sequences in Langflow File Upload (CVE-2026-5027)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences (\'../\')'. This is the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/v2/files where the 'filename' form field contains ../ or ..\\ sequences, or attempts to reference parent directories. Correlate with suspicious HTTP 200-201 responses that indicate file write success. Alert on repeated attempts with incrementing path depth (../../, ../../../, etc).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Langflow API Access via Auto-Login
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Because Langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token before proceeding with exploitation.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/v2/files from external IPs without prior authentication headers. Flag session token generation in HTTP responses following an unauthenticated request. Alert when /api/v2/* access occurs within <1 second of initial connection (indication of single-request exploit chain).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write via Web Application Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'write arbitrary files on exposed servers' and 'honeypots have now detected attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances'. This indicates post-exploitation file placement on disk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation events by Langflow/web-server process (java, python, node) in non-standard locations outside /uploads, /tmp, or application base directory. Flag executable (.sh, .bat, .exe) or script (.py, .rb, .js) file creation by web processes. Correlate with preceding HTTP POST to /api/v2/files within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Pattern: Multiple File Upload Probes to Langflow
suggestion.rationale: Attackers test exploitation via repeated requests; article mentions 'honeypots' detecting activity, implying iterative probing. Bulk scanning occurs before committed exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of 5+ POST requests to /api/v2/files from single source IP within 60 seconds. Flag requests with varying filename payloads (../etc/passwd, ../../windows/system32, etc). Alert on mixed success/failure HTTP status codes (200, 400, 413) indicating fuzzing or path-depth enumeration.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Langflow Version Detection (< v1.9.0 or langflow-base < 0.8.3)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions: fixed in 'langflow-base package version 0.8.3, while the Langflow application itself received a patch in version 1.9.0'. Outdated instances are exploitation targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses or User-Agent strings revealing Langflow version strings <1.9.0. Flag requests to /api/v2/files against known-vulnerable version fingerprints. Alert when version-specific CVEs (CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017) are exploited against matching version discovery.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Unauthenticated API Query Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication' — core exploit mechanism. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow /api/now/ endpoint requests for missing/invalid Authorization headers followed by successful table queries. Flag responses >1MB from unauthenticated or low-privilege sessions.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Instance Table Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'query customer instance tables' — attackers must discover tables first. 'Improper access controls' implies enumeration is possible before authentication enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential probing of /api/now/table/ or wildcard endpoints. Flag 403-then-200 response patterns (enumeration bypass) or systematic table-list requests from non-browser agents.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Extraction via Unauthenticated ServiceNow API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'potential data exposure across enterprise environments' — indicates large-scale exfiltration. Pipeline missed collection/exfiltration phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated /api/now/*/list API calls with incrementing OFFSET, large LIMIT parameters, or wildcard selectors from unauthenticated sessions. Flag total extracted bytes per session and sensitive table names (cmdb_ci, incident, sys_user, sys_user_grmember).

suggestion.title: Network Traffic to ServiceNow Exploitation Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends: 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' phase 'c2' confidence 'High' listing 51.159.98.241. Pipeline output IOCs field is empty — extraction failed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound/outbound connections to 51.159.98.241. Correlate with ServiceNow API calls and non-standard ports. Verify against passive DNS for historical resolution patterns.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Access Control Bypass via Missing/Spoofed Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access controls' is the root cause. Pipeline missed T1556 (Modify Authentication Process) and focus on auth-header manipulation/removal as bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests missing Authorization headers, or with null/empty Bearer tokens, or with X-Forwarded-For spoofing bypassing internal IP checks. Correlate with successful subsequent queries.

suggestion.title: Data Exposure Impact: ServiceNow Credential/CMDB Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability enables 'unauthorized access to customer instance tables' — likely includes sys_user, credentials, and CMDB. Pipeline generated no impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful API queries returning sensitive fields (password_hash, oauth_token, api_key, ssn, email in bulk). Monitor for queries to sys_user and sys_user_grmember tables without proper role/group filtering.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Multiple Storage Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores.' Pipeline extracted zero use cases for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal access to credential storage locations: ~/.ssh, ~/.kube/config, ~/.aws/credentials, Kubernetes API lookups, HashiCorp Vault queries, and password manager CLI invocations. Flag when non-privileged user or unusual process contexts query multiple credential stores in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH and AWS Systems Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM).' Pipeline generated no lateral-movement use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH port forwarding or remote command execution initiated from compromised developer machines. Monitor for ssm:StartSession API calls using developer credentials from unusual locations or times. Alert on SSH key material being copied or used outside normal development workflows.

suggestion.title: Dead-Man Switch Destructive File Deletion Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'dead-man switch' that executes 'rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents' if GitHub token revoked. Pipeline missed this impact/persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on recursive rm -rf commands targeting home directory (~/) or Documents folders. Monitor for child processes spawned by systemd user services (Linux) or LaunchAgents (macOS) that issue mass file deletions. Correlate token revocation events (GitHub API) with subsequent high-volume file deletion on same host within 60s.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Poisoning via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'abuses them to compromise npm, PyPI, and RubyGems packages, as well as GitHub repositories.' Pipeline failed to detect supply-chain attack indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publish, PyPI upload, or RubyGems push operations using developer credentials from compromised machines. Flag when package versions are published outside normal CI/CD pipelines or from unusual IP/geographies. Detect changes to package.json, setup.py, or gemspec shortly after credential compromise.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Abuse for Autonomous C2 and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'requires no command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to operate, as it uses GitHub for that purpose' via 'stolen GitHub token.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or C2-related detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency GitHub API calls using personal access tokens from non-standard IP ranges or at unusual times. Detect API calls that enumerate repositories, create/modify workflows, or push commits without user interaction. Alert on GitHub API requests from processes spawned by package-manager or CI/CD tasks.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Systemd User Service and macOS LaunchAgent Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS.' Pipeline identified zero persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.config/systemd/user/ for new service files and ~/.launchagents/ for new plist files created by user processes. Flag service/agent definitions that execute unusual binaries, especially those that reference GitHub tokens or credential paths. Alert when these persistence mechanisms remain active for > 72 hours post-compromise detection.

suggestion.title: Langflow CVE-2026-5027 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027 Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE'—direct application-level exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Langflow instances for requests to vulnerable endpoints with exploitation payloads. Look for unauthenticated access to Langflow API endpoints that should require authentication, particularly flow execution or configuration modification requests.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Langflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states outcome: 'Unauthenticated RCE'—detect execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell or interpreter spawning from Langflow service context (parent: python, node, java, or containerized process). Alert on command execution with suspicious arguments, env-var exfiltration patterns, or outbound network connections from RCE child process.

suggestion.title: Langflow Authentication Bypass or API Key Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated' RCE—suggests auth bypass or missing auth enforcement in vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow application logs for authentication failures followed by successful unauthenticated requests, or requests lacking expected auth tokens. Track calls to sensitive Langflow APIs (flow execution, node execution, file upload) without valid session or API key.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Process Execution with Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM'—detection must monitor for ctfmon.exe elevating tokens from low-privilege contexts to SYSTEM level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ctfmon.exe process creation with elevated integrity level (SYSTEM) when spawned from low-privilege parent. Track token impersonation or UAC bypass patterns. Correlate with exploit activity targeting CVE-2026-45586.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Binary Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CTFMON as the vulnerable binary in CVE-2026-45586. Need detection for suspicious execution patterns, unusual arguments, or in-memory modifications to ctfmon.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ctfmon.exe execution from non-standard parents (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe), unusual command-line arguments, or loading suspicious DLLs. Cross-reference with known CVE-2026-45586 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: CTFMON File/Registry Modifications at SYSTEM Level
suggestion.rationale: Once escalated to SYSTEM via CTFMON, attackers gain ability to modify protected files/registry. Detection needed for ctfmon.exe or child processes making system-level changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ctfmon.exe or processes spawned by ctfmon.exe accessing/modifying Run keys, services, scheduled tasks, or system binaries. Focus on HKLM writes and System32 file modifications post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Escalation Lateral Movement from CTFMON Access Token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation to SYSTEM, enabling post-exploitation. Detection needed for token theft or lateral movement leveraging elevated CTFMON context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections initiated from ctfmon.exe or child processes spawning remote execution tools (psexec, wmic, winrm) after SYSTEM privilege escalation. Monitor for unusual service creation or remote share access.

suggestion.title: Unusual CTFMON Parent Process or Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: CTFMON normally runs as a system service in user session context. Article implies exploitation from low-privilege attacker context—detection must identify abnormal execution conditions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ctfmon.exe spawned from user-mode executables (explorer.exe, user applications), scheduled task creation launching ctfmon, or ctfmon spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe). Baseline against normal CTFMON behavior.

suggestion.title: npm Install Script Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that npm install scripts enable arbitrary code execution during package installation—the core supply-chain attack vector GitHub is addressing: 'npm install scripts...stop supply chain attacks.' Detection of script execution is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by npm/node with postinstall, preinstall, or prepare script invocations. Baseline legitimate package installations and alert on scripts executing external binaries, establishing network connections, or writing to unexpected directories. Correlate process ancestry to identify if scripts are launched during dependency installation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article context indicates compromise occurs at the package distribution layer. Detection should identify unusual package registry queries or downloads that precede malicious install script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple rapid npm registry API calls (registry.npmjs.org) for package metadata or version enumeration from single host. Flag downloads of packages not in historical baseline or from untrusted registries. Correlate registry access with subsequent install script execution to validate attack chain.

suggestion.title: package.json Install Hook Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies install scripts in package.json as the attack surface. Detection should catch dynamic insertion of postinstall, preinstall, or install directives—the mechanism by which malicious packages execute code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json files for additions or modifications of lifecycle script hooks (postinstall, preinstall, install, prepare) not present in committed baselines. Alert on scripts invoking external executables, curl/wget, or spawning shell sessions. Cross-reference with git blame or package-lock.json to distinguish legitimate updates from compromise.

suggestion.title: npm Audit Suppression or Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article's mitigation (disabling scripts by default) implies organizations require compensating controls. Detection should catch security-check suppression that would hide malicious package indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install commands with --audit=false, --force, --legacy-peer-deps flags, or .npmrc modifications that disable audit policies. Flag suppression of npm-audit warnings via .npmrc (audit=false). Correlate audit bypass with subsequent install script execution—combination is high-confidence evasion indicator.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Transitive Dependency Introduction
suggestion.rationale: Article's supply-chain focus implies attackers compromise packages to inject malicious dependencies. Detection should identify new or unexpected transitive dependencies that bypass direct-dependency vetting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the complete dependency tree (direct + transitive) for each project via package-lock.json. Alert when npm-install resolves new transitive dependencies not in baseline, or when dependency versions jump beyond declared semver ranges. Flag dependencies introduced by packages with recent version bumps or from new maintainers.

suggestion.title: npm Cache Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses attack surface during install phase. Detection should identify cache corruption or injection that would cause repeated install of compromised packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm cache directory (~/.npm) for unexpected modifications or deletions, and alert on npm install --force/--cache-min 9999 commands (cache refresh indicators). Detect if package tarball hashes in cache diverge from npm registry checksums. Alert on repeated npm cache clean followed by install of same packages.

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Offline Scan Triggering Followed by BitLocker Status Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers with physical access...by leveraging an obscure but common side effect of Windows Defender Offline Scan.' Exploit explicitly involves invoking WD Offline, then using its side effect to bypass encryption. Detection must capture this sequencing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Defender Offline Scan invocation (wcesvc, WDOffline boot processes) followed within 5 minutes by BitLocker status queries (manage-bde.exe /status) or encryption state changes (cipher /c queries, WMI Win32_EncryptableVolume access). Correlate with physical access indicators if available.

suggestion.title: Physical Access Paired with Firmware/Boot Environment Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'requires physical access' and 'no login required' indicates offline boot exploitation. Must detect BIOS/bootloader access or recovery environment invocation on BitLocker-encrypted systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag BIOS/UEFI entry attempts, WinRE (Windows Recovery Environment) launches, or boot sequence alterations on systems with active BitLocker encryption. Alert if bcdedit is used to disable secure boot or modify boot parameters on physical-access-vulnerable systems.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of GreatXML Zero-Day via WD Offline Cache Side Effect
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'GreatXML' as the CVE name and describes specific exploitation vector: 'Windows Defender Offline Scan...side effect.' Detection should trigger when the documented exploit conditions are present (WD Offline + specific cache/memory access patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Defender Offline processes with unusual child process spawning, kernel driver access, or memory region reads targeting BitLocker metadata. Alert on processes accessing WD Offline scan cache or temporary files outside normal system directories.

suggestion.title: Enumeration and Extraction of Encrypted Volume Data Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fully bypass BitLocker drive encryption.' After bypass is achieved, attacker must access encrypted volume contents. Detect file enumeration and bulk reads from previously-inaccessible encrypted volumes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large sequential reads from NTFS volumes that were encrypted pre-compromise, recursive directory enumeration in System Volume Information or $RECYCLE.BIN post-WD-Offline-invocation, or data copy operations (robocopy, xcopy) from encrypted partitions to staging areas or external media.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to git.projectnightcrawler.dev Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists git.projectnightcrawler.dev as explicit IOC in 'Indicators of Compromise' section. Post-exploit, attacker likely exfiltrates data or receives further commands from this domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS resolution or outbound TCP/443 connections to git.projectnightcrawler.dev or subdomains from systems exhibiting BitLocker bypass indicators (WD Offline invocation + encryption status change). Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests with non-standard User-Agents, excessive data transfer, or git/API-like endpoints.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading via Legitimate VMware Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Threat actors have been abusing a legitimate, digitally signed VMware binary to slip a custom malicious loader called NIGHTFORGE onto victim systems. This technique, known as DLL sideloading' — this is the core attack vector and explicitly named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DLL loading where parent is signed VMware binary (vmrun.exe, vmtoolsd.exe, vmware-vmx.exe) but DLL is loaded from non-standard paths or matches the 5 provided NIGHTFORGE hashes. Secondary: unexpected child process spawning from VMware binaries in combination with suspicious network connections.

suggestion.title: NIGHTFORGE Malicious Loader File Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'custom malicious loader called NIGHTFORGE' with 5 file hashes provided. Each hash should trigger alerts on execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of files matching any of the 5 SHA256 hashes: 90bba96afe1b5b8410c4f1649adeb8ca1f04c816c64f46912d5bca890f8b2c0a, b34b34310b963fd2901b6e00b0e9a01be6c19d40e68101f0cc1d34ae7f22a4af, 3a33a10901e9ef89eace7834f9c7ce14f590e58bb1b50ec5bd44b4ef1ca5555a, 1852120a84a328edd1995e633dfd2009867898a8e3f0b385e2490cf21c77a994, b3e853eee14fb7948c6907888ee07139085ba9af4231c30e97ff6236b86ca024 — particularly with parent process chain including VMware binaries.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to NIGHTFORGE Infrastructure IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'espionage operation' with infrastructure IPs 193.150.240.37 and 104.192.244.99 provided as high-fidelity indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from any host to 193.150.240.37:* or 104.192.244.99:* regardless of port. Elevate confidence if source process chain includes NIGHTFORGE hash execution or VMware binary abuse. Geographic context: Cambodia government targeting suggests destination IPs should be checked for ASN/hosting attribution.

suggestion.title: Living-Off-the-Land Execution with VMware Utilities
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'legitimate, digitally signed VMware binary' abuse — this is explicitly a LOLBin pattern where legitimate signed tools are used for malicious execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VMware binary execution (vmrun.exe, vmtoolsd.exe, vmware-vmx.exe, vmtools.exe) with suspicious parent processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, explorer.exe) or command-line arguments containing DLL paths, inline library loading, or non-standard working directories. Flag combination of legitimate binary execution + unusual child processes.

suggestion.title: Cambodian Government Entity Targeting via Initial Access Vector
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'targeting government institutions in Cambodia' — detection should focus on identifying initial compromise vectors (phishing, watering hole, supply chain) targeting .gov.kh or Cambodian government-affiliated entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag spear-phishing emails targeting Cambodian government email addresses containing suspicious attachments (VMware-themed decoys, Office documents with DLL stagers). Monitor web proxy logs for watering-hole or supply-chain compromise indicators (trojanized software delivery, known malicious download sites). Correlate with downstream NIGHTFORGE execution for confirmation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Discovery - CVE-2026-6973 / CVE-2026-10727 (Ivanti EPMM RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies: 'Specifically, impacted versions include 12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1'. Asset vulnerability scanning is foundational for any exploitation threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile installations with version in {12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1} or other unpatched versions. Correlate with vulnerability scanner reporting CVE-2026-6973 or CVE-2026-10727 present on the host.

suggestion.title: Apache Configuration File Tampering - EPMM Servers
suggestion.rationale: Stated attack method: 'injecting malicious Apache configuration directives'. File modifications to *.conf files on EPMM systems must be detected to catch exploitation in-flight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of Apache configuration files (httpd.conf, *.conf) on Ivanti EPMM servers, especially additions containing SetHandler, ProxyPassMatch, LoadModule, or other directives capable of executing commands. Whitelist legitimate administrative changes.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution - Unexpected Child Processes from Apache/httpd
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'achieve remote code execution by injecting malicious Apache configuration directives'. RCE manifests as process creation from the Apache process; detection of shell spawning from httpd is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell interpreter or command-execution process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned from httpd/Apache process context on EPMM servers. Baseline benign child processes (CGI scripts, legitimate hooks) and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Authentication + Malicious HTTP Payload Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability description: 'authenticated attackers'. Correlating successful EPMM authentication with suspicious Apache directive payloads in subsequent HTTP requests enables high-fidelity exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful login to Ivanti EPMM with HTTP requests to the same instance containing Apache keywords (ProxyPass, SetHandler, LoadModule) within 60 seconds, from the same source IP. Alert if payloads are URL-encoded or obfuscated.

suggestion.title: HTTP Payload Analysis - Apache Configuration Injection Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is HTTP; payloads must traverse the wire. Inspection for Apache directive patterns in HTTP request bodies/parameters enables in-network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti EPMM endpoints containing Apache configuration keywords (SetHandler, ProxyPassMatch, LoadModule, <Directory>, <Location>) especially with double-encoding, Unicode escapes, or variable substitution. Cross-reference against known CVE-2026-6973 POC signatures.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers are now targeting a recently patched maximum-severity flaw in Ivanti Sentry' with 'OS command injection weakness' — no detection logic for exploitation payloads surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry gateway access logs for command injection payloads in request parameters (shell metacharacters: $(), backticks, pipes, semicolons in HTTP POST/GET to admin endpoints). Correlate with HTTP 200 responses and process spawn events on gateway. Baseline common legitimate parameter values.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'execute code with root privileges on Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways' and Shadowserver reports 'backdoored' instances — no detection for child process spawning or shell execution from Sentry daemon context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell or scripting interpreter processes (bash, sh, python, perl) spawned as children of Ivanti Sentry gateway processes (java, tomcat, or custom gateway daemons). Elevate alerts if spawned processes open network connections or write to system directories. Establish baseline of normal Sentry-spawned processes per environment.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online' with visual screenshot and Shadowserver reports 'backdoored' gateways — implies attacker access to admin interface, no detection for anomalous portal access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor successful logins to Ivanti Sentry admin UI (/admin, /mobilegateway, /secure) for anomalies: first-time source IPs, logins outside business hours, failed login storms followed by success, or logins from IPs not in corporate network whitelist. Flag any admin account creation or privilege escalation post-successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Implant Communication from Ivanti Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' — implies persistent implants but no detection for C2 or exfiltration traffic originating from compromised gateway appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Ivanti Sentry gateway IP address for anomalies: connections to non-approved infrastructure, C2-pattern DNS queries (DGA-like domains, high subdomain entropy), suspicious port combinations (ephemeral client ports to uncommon server ports), or traffic to non-corporate IP ranges. Establish baseline of legitimate gateway-to-backend flows.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions 'prior to R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1' and Shadowserver found 19 vulnerable instances — no detection for version enumeration or vulnerability scanning against unpatched assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect version string exposure in HTTP response headers (Server, User-Agent, X-Powered-By) from Ivanti Sentry instances. Flag any version matching vulnerable ranges (R10.5.0-10.5.1, R10.6.0-10.6.1, R10.7.0). Correlate with vulnerability scanner reports indicating CVE-2026-10520 detection. Combine with asset inventory to identify patching gaps.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Compromise: Sentry Gateway as Pivot Point
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Ivanti Sentry as 'entry point into targets' enterprise networks, enabling the theft of sensitive customer and corporate data' — no detection for lateral movement or internal reconnaissance initiated from compromised gateway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network flows FROM Ivanti Sentry gateway to internal backend systems for anomalies: connections to systems not in pre-approved whitelist, port scans (sequential port connection attempts), database probing (3306, 5432, 1433), or credential-related protocols (LDAP, Kerberos). Establish baseline of legitimate gateway-to-backend communications per environment.

suggestion.title: Weaponized Email Delivery to OWA Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'sending a weaponized email that a victim opens in a browser' — phishing delivery is the primary initial access vector but no phishing-specific detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails triggering OWA preview rendering from untrusted senders, especially those with JavaScript payloads, obfuscated HTML, or known exploit kit indicators. Monitor for user clicks on malicious links within weaponized emails that redirect to OWA endpoints.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary JavaScript Execution in OWA Context
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in Outlook Web Access (OWA)' — yet no execution-phase detection was proposed for JavaScript in OWA rendering contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA request/response logs for JavaScript injection payloads, particularly in email preview or reading pane contexts. Flag obfuscated or minified JavaScript passed through OWA parameters; correlate with CVE-2026-42897 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42897 Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'active exploitation' of the vulnerability but pipeline generated no hunt for actual exploitation artifacts or post-compromise indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Exchange and OWA logs for request patterns, timing signatures, and parameter mutations consistent with CVE-2026-42897 exploitation. Flag anomalous OWA sessions immediately following email delivery and rendering of suspicious content.

suggestion.title: Post-OWA Compromise Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms active exploitation suggesting attacker foothold, but no detection for post-compromise behavior (privilege escalation, lateral movement, data access) was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful OWA compromise with unusual mailbox access patterns, forwarding rule creation, or outbound data transfer. Track anomalous service-to-service activity initiated from compromised OWA session contexts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt (CVSS 9.8)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-20253 'carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and affects Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.2.4'. This is the primary vulnerability driver; requires version-based asset detection and exploitation indicator hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Splunk Enterprise instances running versions below 10.2.4 via asset inventory or version-detection scans. Monitor patch management logs for failure-to-patch on critical CVE-2026-20253. Alert when unpatched Splunk instance receives exploitation attempts (HTTP fuzzing, suspicious web UI requests).

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Execution from Splunk Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'execute malicious scripts' as the primary post-exploitation attack vector. Pipeline lists only T1190 but omits execution-phase techniques required to detect this critical step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child process spawning from Splunk daemons (splunkd.exe, python.exe processes running under Splunk context) for unexpected interpreters: powershell.exe, cmd.exe, bash, /bin/sh. Flag processes with suspicious arguments (Base64 encoding, obfuscation, script blocks). Correlate timing with web UI authentication anomalies or privilege escalation indicators.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Post-Splunk Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'exfiltrate sensitive data' as a consequence of successful exploitation. This is a distinct exfiltration-phase attack with separate detection requirements from initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound bulk data transfers from Splunk indexers/search heads to external IPs outside known backup/replication patterns. Track large transfers of sensitive data indices (authentication logs, PII-tagged fields). Alert on HTTP/HTTPS uploads to cloud storage or SMB exfiltration from Splunk processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Filesystem Operations from Splunk Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthorized file operations' as an attack outcome. Requires filesystem-level auditing to detect file access, modification, or deletion outside normal Splunk operating scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access and modification events from Splunk process context targeting sensitive paths (/etc, /var/log, SYSTEM32, HKLM registry, user home directories). Alert on bulk file deletions, encryption activities, or access to high-value datastores (databases, credential stores) initiated from Splunk daemons post-vulnerability detection.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Splunk Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Multiple 'critical' CVEs strongly imply privilege escalation pathways enabling system-level compromise. Article does not detail escalation mechanics, but this kill-chain phase must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Splunk processes spawning higher-privileged child processes (SYSTEM, root). Track service creation or modification initiated by Splunk runtime. Alert on Splunk processes accessing privileged resources (registry handles, process tokens, SAM/shadow file reads).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Splunk Admin Account Creation or Privilege Grant
suggestion.rationale: With script execution and privilege escalation, attackers would establish persistence through admin account creation. Article does not detail persistence methods, but this is standard post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for new admin-level user creation or privilege grants outside scheduled change windows. Track role and capability assignments to existing accounts. Alert on unexpected privilege escalation within Splunk's internal user database or system-level account creation from Splunk process context.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers used 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities in the attacks' against PeopleSoft. This describes Java deserialization/gadget chain payload execution, a known attack pattern against Java-based enterprise software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application servers for suspicious HTTP POST requests to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /psft-services, /ps/signon.html) followed by unexpected process spawning (java.exe child processes, cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Alert on deserialization gadget chain indicators in request payloads or process command lines.

suggestion.title: Bulk Student Records Access from PeopleSoft
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'accessed...student records system' and stolen data 'containing student finance data, billing and payment information, credit card and payment details.' This indicates targeted collection of structured sensitive data from repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume queries against PeopleSoft student record tables (STDNT_CAR_TERM, PS_STDNT_ADDR, PS_PERSONAL_DATA) from non-standard service accounts or during off-hours. Flag data exports involving >1000 rows of personally identifiable information (PII), financial records, or payment details from a single session.

suggestion.title: Large Data Exfiltration from PeopleSoft Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'stolen over 40GB of documents' representing coordinated bulk exfiltration. This 40GB size is far beyond typical backup or legitimate operational data transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained high-volume outbound data transfers (>1GB/hour) from PeopleSoft application servers to external IP addresses, particularly to anonymized/VPN endpoints. Correlate with unusual process execution (curl, wget, python) or archive tool usage (7zip, rar, zip) on application servers within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft Zero-Day / Unpatched Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities' and notes 'attack is not working on all systems, likely because successful exploitation depends on each instance's configuration.' Indicates dependency on outdated patch levels or specific misconfigurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of PeopleSoft patch versions and vulnerability scores across enterprise. Flag any instances running unpatched versions known to contain gadget chain-exploitable deserialization flaws. Monitor for exploitation signatures: unusual JVM heap dumps, exception handling in PeopleSoft logs referencing serialization, or RCE error patterns in Web Access logs.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from PeopleSoft Cloud and On-Premises Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'breaching their cloud and on-premises Oracle PeopleSoft instances,' implying successful authentication or credential compromise to maintain access across hybrid infrastructure. Likely T1110 (Brute Force) or T1557 (Man-in-the-Middle) against both environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed PeopleSoft application login attempts (check application logs, not just ADFS) from unusual geolocations or IPs. Flag successful logins to PeopleSoft immediately following high-frequency authentication failures. For cloud instances, alert on unusual service principal or managed identity access patterns to PeopleSoft databases.

suggestion.title: Extortion Threat Communication & Dark Web Leak Site Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states ShinyHunters 'claimed responsibility on Tuesday and shared an archive of allegedly stolen documents' on their 'dark web leak site.' Extortion threat communication is a critical indicator of breach confirmation and imminent data publication demands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor underground forums and dark web leak aggregator sites for posts referencing organization name, PeopleSoft breaches, or student records. Detect inbound emails to trust/security/executive mailboxes containing extortion demands, data leak proof-of-concept samples, or ransom negotiation language. Correlate timing with suspicious access patterns on PeopleSoft instances from 1-2 weeks prior.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Malware Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names SPECTRALVIPER as malware deployed in FireAnt campaign; no execution detection generated despite this being a core IOC. Process execution follows initial email delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution patterns from temporary directories or unusual parent-child relationships following email delivery to investment sector targets; correlate process names and command-lines with SPECTRALVIPER staging patterns.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Spear-Phishing Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus is documented spear-phishing APT (explicitly named in title); no initial access detection generated despite it being the primary attack vector for delivering SPECTRALVIPER to Vietnam investors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails to Vietnam-based investment organization domains with malicious links or attachments; correlate sender infrastructure, link destinations, and attachment hashes against OceanLotus phishing infrastructure patterns.

suggestion.title: Registry Run Keys Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus campaigns consistently establish registry-based persistence; no persistence UC generated. SPECTRALVIPER would require registry modifications to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run[Once] or HKCU equivalents occurring within 2 hours of suspicious process execution from temporary or user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Command & Control Communications
suggestion.rationale: FireAnt campaign implies coordinated attack; no C2 detection generated. SPECTRALVIPER payloads require beaconing to attacker infrastructure for task delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS connections with suspicious characteristics (self-signed certs, JA3 fingerprints, atypical TLS) from compromised investment hosts to non-VietTel/Vietcombank ASNs; correlate against OceanLotus C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Financial Credential Harvesting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets Vietnam investors indicating financial credential objectives; no credential-access detection generated. SPECTRALVIPER malware likely includes infostealer functionality for credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration of credential manager, browser password stores, or LSASS memory access followed by suspicious network exfiltration; correlate with web browser or office application child processes spawning from SPECTRALVIPER loader.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via phpBB Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass'—core attack vector. No detection proposed despite direct mention in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous authentication patterns to phpBB: successful login immediately following failed auth attempts from same IP, impossible travel between login events, or requests to known phpBB auth bypass endpoints. Monitor for session creation without corresponding credential validation logs.

suggestion.title: RCE via phpBB Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions RCE—the critical impact phase. No execution detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter (php-cgi, php-fpm) spawning unexpected child processes (sh, bash, wget, curl, nc) or accessing OS binaries from web root context. Flag execution of system commands from within phpBB's web directory or via PHP eval/exec functions.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Web Context
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass + RCE typically chains to privilege escalation; pipeline reconstructed no such progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation attempts from low-privilege web application account (www-data, apache, nginx user): sudo calls, capability additions, SELinux context changes, or attempts to access files owned by root/privileged users.

suggestion.title: Unusual Database Access from Web Tier
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 10-year unpatched vulnerability affecting 'tens of millions'—likely database compromise is secondary impact. No data-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database access from web application user account for unusual query patterns: bulk SELECT statements, access to sensitive tables (users, credentials, admin), DDL/DML operations, or connections from IPs/sessions not in baseline.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised phpBB Instance
suggestion.rationale: 'Tens of millions of users across thousands of forums'—once one instance is compromised, attacker can pivot to forum users' credentials or host infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from compromised phpBB host to unusual destinations (C2, internal network scans), credential theft attempts (auth cookies, password hashes in memory), or SSH/RDP brute-force attempts against internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Persistence via PHP Webshell Installation
suggestion.rationale: RCE capability enables webshell placement for durable access; no persistence detection despite obvious attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file creation/modification in phpBB directories (.php files with low entropy, Base64-encoded content, eval() calls) and web server logs showing requests to unexpected .php endpoints. Cross-check file timestamps against known install/update times.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states '1,500+ devices' infected and 'cyber reconnaissance' purpose—implies active C2 channels. Zero use cases generated for detecting command-and-control communication patterns despite this being the core mechanism of a botnet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound connections to low-frequency domains/IPs from compromised hosts, manifesting as short-lived connection bursts at regular intervals. Flag user-agents and connection patterns inconsistent with legitimate browser/service behavior.

suggestion.title: Network and Host Reconnaissance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes purpose as 'cyber reconnaissance.' No use cases for reconnaissance behavior (scanning, enumeration, system discovery) despite being the stated threat objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scanning/enumeration patterns: rapid failed connections to consecutive network ranges, LDAP/RPC queries from unexpected processes, command-line net/whoami/systeminfo execution in bulk, or ARP sweeping from single source.

suggestion.title: Botnet Lateral Movement and Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Expansion to 1,500+ devices requires lateral movement mechanism (worm propagation or credential reuse). Pipeline generated zero use cases for lateral movement despite growth trajectory implying this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious remote execution (SMB, WMI, RDP, SSH) originating from known-infected hosts to new targets. Detect daisy-chain connection patterns, mass file copy operations, or scheduled task creation across multiple hosts.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence via Service/Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Maintaining infection across 1,500+ devices requires persistent mechanisms (service installation, startup folders, scheduled tasks). No persistence detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag service creation with random/obfuscated names, unsigned DLL injection into system processes, suspicious registry modifications under RunOnce/Run keys, or scheduled tasks with randomized names executing external payloads.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Tampering - Dependency Artifact Modified
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'code is written everywhere' suggesting artifacts are being injected/modified across multiple distribution points (package repos, build systems, registries). No detection UC was generated despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned, newly-published, or hash-mismatched package versions in language package managers. Flag artifacts with suspicious metadata changes (author, repository URL, signature). Alert on install of versions immediately after account compromise or zero-day.

suggestion.title: Code Injection in CI/CD Pipeline - Unauthorized Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'code is written everywhere' implies attackers can inject into build pipelines and CI systems. No UC captured CI/CD compromise patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CI/CD pipeline modifications by non-code-owners, unsigned commits merged to protected branches, new IAM roles added with deployment permissions, and unexpected build artifact outputs uploaded to external storage.

suggestion.title: Cross-Layer Code Execution - Multiple Cloud Regions Simultaneous Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'device is the only constant' implying code executes across different environments (cloud, IDEs, local) but converges on endpoints. No detection for distributed execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate code execution events (script invocation, compiler runs) triggered from geographically dispersed IPs within minutes. Alert on DevTools or IDE launching code from untrusted registries. Detect parent-child process chains where grandparent is network-resident (downloaded script).

suggestion.title: Persistent Device Compromise via Injected Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article suggests attackers can inject code that persists on developer devices via toolchain compromise. No UC for persistence via development environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to .bashrc, .zshrc, IDE config files, package manager configs, or ~/.ssh/config. Alert on unsigned packages installed into /usr/local/bin or Python site-packages. Flag unexpected auto-execute hooks in version control hooks (.git/hooks).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared Code Repositories and Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Code written 'everywhere' implies shared dependencies become lateral movement vector across multiple projects/teams/orgs. No UC for supply-chain-based lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on identical malicious dependency versions installed across multiple cloud accounts, VPCs, or teams within short timeframe. Detect internal package forks/mirrors being used instead of canonical upstream. Flag reuse of stolen credentials across multiple shared dependency repositories.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Injected Code Callbacks to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain injected code would beacon out; 'device is only constant' suggests C2 convergence point. No exfiltration UC for code-injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS/HTTP from development tools, package managers, or build processes to newly-registered or suspicious domains. Flag exfiltration of source code, credentials, or environment variables through indirect channels (error reports, metrics, logs). Alert on encrypted tunnels initiated by package installation scripts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious onering Crate Import Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'onering' as a compromised Rust crate. Any import or dependency resolution involving this crate name warrants detection, especially post-disclosure versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Cargo.toml modifications that add 'onering' dependency, or Cargo.lock entries referencing onering. Correlate with build process logs to identify which projects were affected.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Traffic from Rust Runtime Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states crate 'performs code exfiltration' — when the compromised library is loaded, it will initiate outbound C2 or data exfil connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from rustc.exe / cargo.exe / compiled Rust binaries. Flag unusual C2 patterns: DNS queries to newly registered domains, HTTPS to non-standard ports, or traffic to IP geolocation inconsistent with development environment.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Execution via Rust Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised crate code executes during compilation or runtime. Article describes 'code exfiltration' implying active execution, not passive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by rustc, cargo, or Rust binary execution that are unusual: curl/wget, powershell, cmd.exe, or network tools. Flag process execution with suspicious working directories or command-line arguments referencing sensitive data.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Integrity: Crate Version Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Cargo manifest or lock files show onering at unexpected versions or with timestamps that don't match official releases. Article implies malicious version was injected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare crate hash/checksum against crates.io official registry. Flag mismatches, yanked versions still in use, or versions not found in official repository records.

suggestion.title: Source Code or Build Artifact Exfiltration Post-Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article says crate 'performs code exfiltration' — likely targets source files or compiled artifacts from projects using onering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file I/O on .rs source files, Cargo.toml, .git directories, or build artifacts (target/ folder) concurrent with unexpected network I/O. Look for multi-megabyte uploads to unexpected domains.

suggestion.title: Detection of tokens signed with hardcoded 'random' HMAC secret
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' is shipped as template default in dev.env—attackers will forge tokens offline using this predictable secret. Core credential-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate JWT claims inspection with known weak-secret signatures. Flag tokens with exp claims >30 days in future, iat in past without corresponding log evidence of creation, or HMAC-SHA256 signatures matching 'random' secret hashes. Prioritize tokens used for admin endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Public GitHub repo (dhax/go-base) exploitation surface scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '1,685 stars on GitHub'—reachable public attack surface. Developers clone vulnerable boilerplate; attackers enumerate clones by scanning for endpoint paths mentioned in repo or default config. Phase: Recon/Initial Access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external HTTP requests attempting enumeration of /api/v1/admin, /api/v1/users, or /api/v1/token/* endpoints without prior authentication context. Correlate source IPs performing mass endpoint scanning against multiple targets with known vulnerability scanner UA strings or exploit-kit HTTP signatures.

suggestion.title: Token refresh abuse via forged JWT credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists '/api/v1/token/refresh' as exploitable endpoint. Token refresh requests using forged credentials (signed with 'random' secret) indicate active privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid token refresh sequences (>5 refreshes/minute from same source) or refresh requests where token claims are logically impossible (exp before iat, exp year >2038). Correlate refresh success with prior failed admin endpoint requests—pattern indicates attacker testing then escalating.

suggestion.title: Message spoofing via malicious protocolMessage in placeholderResendMessage
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can be sent a malicious payload via the placeholderResendMessage and trigger a fake `messages.upsert` event with a **fake message key and payload**.' Pipeline generated no detection for this core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys-running processes (Node.js contexts with Baileys in require/import chain) for message.upsert event emissions with invalid or spoofed message keys. Correlate with inbound protocolMessage structures that lack valid sender attribution or contain unexpected placeholderResendMessage references.

suggestion.title: App state sync corruption via fake key injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key s[...]' but pipeline did not suggest detection for state-level corruption indicators or sync anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys-spawned processes for exceptions or errors related to app state synchronization, key validation failures, or state-object inconsistencies. Track divergence between expected and actual app state structure post-message arrival.

suggestion.title: Baileys package runtime exploitation detection
suggestion.rationale: Article exploits are triggered at runtime by 'maliciously crafted protocolMessage payload' but pipeline missed detection for unusual Message.proto handling or deserialization anomalies in Baileys contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes with Baileys loaded for abnormal protocolMessage parsing, exception handling on message deserialization, or runtime errors in message-handling code paths triggered by malformed protocolMessage structures.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency mining process execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU' as campaign objective, yet pipeline generated zero detection for mining process signatures (xmrig, monero, claymore). This is a core impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cryptocurrency mining executables by name (xmrig, minerd, claymore, cryptonight) or behavioral indicators (high GPU utilization, outbound to mining pool ports 3333/3334/9999, wallet addresses in process args). Correlate GPU spike with process execution time.

suggestion.title: Access to fake download domain infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'network of more than 150 fake download sites' using specific domains (gleeze.com, giize.com, directdownload.icu), but only generic IOC-template hunts provided. Needs domain-specific detection for initial compromise chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS resolution and HTTP traffic to gleeze.com, giize.com, directdownload.icu subdomains. Correlate with file download events or process execution within 5 minutes to identify successful infection chain. Alert on subdomain variations (direct-download*, start-download*, free-download*).

suggestion.title: Malware execution from user download directory
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative 'luring them into downloading malware-laced files' establishes initial access via file download, but no UC for detecting execution from typical download paths (Downloads, Desktop, temp folders).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent is browser or file manager (explorer.exe, chrome.exe, firefox.exe, iexplore.exe) and child is launched from C:\Users\*\Downloads, C:\Users\*\Desktop, C:\Windows\Temp, or AppData\Local\Temp. Flag if executable name matches obfuscated patterns or has no company name metadata.

suggestion.title: GPU resource utilization anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly targets 'GPU' for mining (stated in title and body), but no detection for the sustained GPU overutilization that would necessarily follow persistent cryptomining activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Performance Monitor counter 'GPU Engine Utilization %' for sustained elevation >75% over 1+ hour. Exclude known legitimate high-GPU processes (3D rendering, video encoding). Correlate with unknown process names or execution from suspicious paths. Alert on per-user baseline deviation.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect lateral movement and command execution
suggestion.rationale: While UC_RMM_TOOLS covers initial installation, article's 'sophisticated' campaign and RMM use warrants lateral movement detection. Standard pattern for RMM-based post-exploitation is horizontal spread to other machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe (parent or child) initiating remote process execution to non-localhost IPs via WMI (Win32_Process), PsExec, RDP, or SSH. Flag if source account is non-admin or service account. Correlate outbound network connections to internal subnet from ScreenConnect process.

suggestion.title: UC_MULTISTAGE_EXECUTION · Second-stage malware download from initial execution context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'multi-stage malware' but no UC detects stage-1→stage-2 handoff. Critical gap for catching lateral-move or C2 callback that fetches true payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate initial parent process (Office, Explorer, PowerShell from email execution) with outbound network connections to known IOC domains or suspicious IP:port pairs, followed within 10 seconds by child process creation (rundll32, regsvr32, mshta) or file creation in temp directories. Stage 2 fingerprint is \x4d\x5a (MZ header) or PE signature detection.

suggestion.title: UC_INMEMORY_EVASION · Process memory injection or reflective DLL injection detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim is 'runs entirely in memory, leaving almost no trace.' Pipeline mapped T1027 (obfuscation) but missed T1055 (Process Injection) and T1140 (deobfuscation) which are the mechanisms. No UC to detect process hollowing, code caves, or reflective loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Suspicious parent→child process pair where child has abnormally low disk footprint or zero file creation but high private memory growth. Look for rundll32/regsvr32 spawning without corresponding *.dll file in typical paths, or process creation with command line containing hex/base64 patterns. Correlate with unsigned image loads or load of mscoree.dll (CLR injection) from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: UC_VB_MACRO_EXECUTION · Visual Basic macro deobfuscation and execution chain
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline mapped T1059.005 (Visual Basic) but generated no UC. Article implies VB scripts are delivery vector (common in Office attachments). UC_OFFICE_CHILD catches execution but not the deobfuscation of obfuscated VB code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Office process (winword.exe, excel.exe) creating temporary script files with .vbs/.js extensions in %temp%, %appdata%, or C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Temp. Follow with detection of VBScript.Encode or suspicious VB string patterns (Chr(XX) concatenation, Replace() calls, Eval equivalents). Correlate to subsequent cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawn.

suggestion.title: UC_TAXIMPERSONATION_PHISHING · Fake tax authority domain access from email phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically targets 'impersonating official Indian government tax authorities' but no domain-pattern or sender-pattern UC to detect these fakes. Domains like 'taxations.indiagov.it.com' and 'zhengfu666.com' are obvious fake-authority indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Email received from external domain with subject containing tax-authority keywords ('income tax', 'ITR', 'GST', 'revenue', 'assessment', 'refund', 'tax notice', 'compliance').
