Recipient clicks URL or downloads attachment pointing to domain containing keywords ('tax', 'taxation', 'indiagov', 'zhengfu') with suspicious TLD (.icu, .xyz, .cn) or subdomain pattern (taxations.* or similar spoofing). Correlated sender domain should not match legitimate Indian tax authority (income-tax.gov.in, etc.).

suggestion.title: UC_POWERSHELL_DOWNLOADER · Inline base64-encoded PowerShell downloader execution
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PowerShell-based 2nd-stage download (T1059.001 mapped but no UC). 'Multi-stage' malware pattern requires first-stage to fetch second-stage; PowerShell is common vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PowerShell process spawned from email-execution context (parent: Outlook, Explorer, Word, or browser) with command line containing base64-encoded payload (-EncodedCommand, -enc) or file I/O redirection (< or >). Correlate to outbound HTTP/S connection to external IP or suspicious domain (IOC-matched). Payload deobfuscation reveals DownloadString, IEX, or curl invocation.

suggestion.title: UC_REGISTRY_PERSISTENCE_CHECK · Registry modification for persistence setup or evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'leaves almost no trace'—implies cleanup or anti-forensics. No UC for registry persistence checks (DisableRealTimeMonitoring, etc.) or evidence removal (clearing Event Logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PowerShell or cmd.exe process modifying HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run (persistence) or clearing Event Log providers (reg delete HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\eventlog). Correlate to initial-access parent process.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts Against Announced Critical CVEs (Pre-Patch)
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities' and 'Patch Release'—the gap between announcement and deployment is the highest-risk exploitation window. Pipeline should flag detections for known-CVE exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP service processes for anomalous child spawns, unexpected network callbacks, or crash behavior patterns consistent with exploitation of publicly-disclosed critical vulnerabilities during pre-patch window.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Version Inventory and Alerting
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities'—implies vulnerable versions exist in the wild. Pipeline should generate use cases to inventory vulnerable product versions and flag systems at risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for running instances of Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP products; extract version strings; compare against announced vulnerable-version ranges; alert on pre-patch instances in real-time with remediation urgency.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti and Fortinet typically operate as perimeter/network appliances; critical vulnerabilities grant initial foothold for lateral movement into trust zones. Pipeline missed detection use case for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor internal traffic egress from known Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP appliance IPs; flag unusual service-to-service authentication and uncommon internal port scanning or lateral pivot attempts post-compromise.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Ivanti Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10520 'stems from an OS command injection weakness' enabling 'execute code with root privileges'. No detection use case was generated for this execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry gateway logs and system calls for command injection payloads (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipe operators) in input parameters. Alert on any shell command execution initiated from the Sentry gateway process, especially execution with root privileges.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Admin Account Creation via Sentry Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10523 described as 'authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts'. No detection use case captured this specific post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative account creation events in Ivanti Sentry where the source IP or initiating session shows no prior successful authentication. Flag any account creation from unauthenticated or guest contexts.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Sentry 'secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices', implying a network pivot point. With root code execution (CVE-2026-10520), lateral movement is expected but no detection use case was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Ivanti Sentry gateway for suspicious internal connections to corporate back-end systems, database servers, or administrative systems following execution patterns. Baseline normal Sentry-to-backend traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Detection: Ivanti Sentry Version Below R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides fixed versions: 'Sentry versions R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1'. No inventory or vulnerability management detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and software inventory for Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron Sentry instances running versions older than R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1. Cross-reference against network asset inventory and alert on unpatched appliances on public-facing network segments.

suggestion.title: Network Access Attempts to Unpatched Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Both CVE-2026-10520 and CVE-2026-10523 are remotely exploitable without authentication. Article states Sentry is 'secure mobile gateway', implying external-facing. No external attack surface monitoring use case suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances for reconnaissance or exploitation attempts. Alert on unusual HTTP/HTTPS patterns, command-injection-like payloads in HTTP parameters, or multiple rapid authentication attempts from external IPs prior to CVE patching.

suggestion.title: Defender MsMpEng Process Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access'—a clear privilege escalation vector. Detection should monitor for non-SYSTEM processes spawning or elevating MsMpEng or WinDefend to SYSTEM context, or parent-child anomalies involving Defender binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with low privilege creating child processes running as SYSTEM, or for MsMpEng.exe parent process events where parent is not NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. Flag any process image loading from unusual paths into MsMpEng memory space.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Binary or Service Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day in Defender itself implies exploitation of Defender code or service boundaries. Article phrase 'on Updated Windows' suggests the flaw persists across patched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modifications to Defender binaries in C:\Program Files\Windows Defender or C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender. Monitor for writes to Defender service registry keys (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinDefend or variants).

suggestion.title: Rapid or Unexpected Defender Process Restart Cycles
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of a Defender vulnerability likely involves triggering crashes or restarts of the engine process to transition privilege or load malicious code during restart.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences of MsMpEng.exe process creation/termination within short time windows (3+ restarts in <5 minutes). Correlate with unexpected AvgIdleTask or other Defender scheduled tasks spawning outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Unverified Code Execution via Defender Service
suggestion.rationale: If the vulnerability allows arbitrary code injection into the Defender service context, look for indicator of unsigned DLL loads or code execution branches from Defender service processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for image load events involving DLLs with invalid or missing digital signatures loaded into MsMpEng or WinDefend processes. Flag child processes spawned from Defender services without expected code signing.

suggestion.title: Defender Configuration or Exclusion Bypass Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After achieving SYSTEM via Defender, attacker would modify Defender settings to enable persistence and evasion. Look for post-exploitation configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to Defender exclusion registry keys or policy files, particularly additions of file paths, process names, or cloud submission settings after anomalous Defender process activity.

suggestion.title: Outlook Web Access XSS Payload Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute arbitrary JavaScript code in cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks targeting Outlook Web Access users.' This is the core execution vector and must be detected at the network and application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA HTTP traffic for inline JavaScript, script tags, event handlers (onerror=, onclick=), and encoded XSS patterns. Alert on POST/GET requests to /owa/ endpoints containing script injection markers. Correlate with unpatched Exchange versions.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Email with XSS Exploitation Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user.' Emails targeting this vulnerability will contain distinctive XSS patterns and script injection code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound email for XSS payloads, embedded JavaScript, script tags with event handlers, and HTML/MIME crafting typical of CVE-2026-42897 exploitation. Alert on mail destined for OWA-enabled users from untrusted senders.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Exploitation of CVE-2026-42897
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attackers with no privileges' can trigger exploitation. Unauthenticated exploitation attempts should be detected at the perimeter targeting vulnerable Exchange endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Exchange-facing endpoints (/owa/, /api/) for unauthenticated requests bearing XSS and script injection signatures (percent-encoding, Unicode escapes, inline scripts). Flag requests from external sources to vulnerable server versions (2016, 2019, SE).

suggestion.title: Post-XSS Execution - Lateral Movement or Data Exfiltration Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Once JavaScript executes 'in the browser context,' attacker can steal session cookies, harvest credentials, or pivot to other systems. Detection must capture follow-on malicious behavior post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTPS connections to non-Microsoft domains originating from OWA browser processes. Alert on DNS queries for suspicious domains, exfiltration of session material to external IPs, or unusual API calls post-XSS.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Exchange Server - CVE-2026-42897 Compliance Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'deploy them as soon as possible' (June 2026 patches) and CISA ordered patching by May 29. Unpatched instances remain critical risk and must be identified and flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Exchange Server 2016, 2019, and SE instances for June 2026 security update installation. Flag any unpatched systems with outbound connectivity as critical exposure. Escalate based on internet-facing OWA availability and dwell time since patch release.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Microsoft Product Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Record 206 Flaws...Critical RCE Bugs' being patched; detection should identify systems not applying the patch release. 'Critical RCE' indicates immediate risk if patch is not deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed Windows/Office build versions and KB articles against CVE advisory patch baseline. Flag systems with OS/application dates prior to patch-release date. Monitor Windows Update logs for failed or deferred patch deployment.

suggestion.title: RCE Exploitation via Microsoft Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: 'Critical RCE Bugs' indicates remote code execution vectors in Microsoft services (kernel, Exchange, Teams, Office). Execution attempts should be detected before patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child processes spawned from Microsoft service executables (svchost.exe, w3wp.exe, iexplore.exe). Flag cmd.exe or powershell.exe execution with parent = system service. Detect anomalous network calls from service contexts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: '206 Flaws' implies multiple CVE categories; privilege-escalation flaws typically accompany RCE. Detection should capture priv-esc attempts following RCE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UAC bypass patterns, token impersonation, or service ACL modifications following suspicious process execution from Microsoft services. Flag HKLM Registry writes in same process chain as RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Persistence Establishment via Service/Scheduler Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: '206 Flaws' provides multiple attack surface; persistence via scheduled tasks or services is common post-RCE. Detect creation of persistence mechanisms in patch-window timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new scheduled task or Windows service creation with suspicious parameters post-vulnerability-window. Flag Registry modifications to Run/RunOnce or WMI event subscriptions occurring after suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Gap Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes bulk patch release ('Record 206'). Detection should identify the cumulative patch-deployment gap across infrastructure to quantify attack-surface reduction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all systems' installed KB articles and build versions. Aggregate count of systems missing all-206-patch bundle. Flag departments/asset groups with <SLA% patch coverage within 30 days of release. Track time-to-patch metric per product line.

suggestion.title: SSH Brute Force with PeopleSoft Administrative Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The script attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm.' Non-standard account enumeration is high-fidelity—standard brute-force detection would miss this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed SSH authentication attempts using specific PeopleSoft account names (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) against any PeopleSoft system within 10 minutes. Correlate source IPs with known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note File Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the script drops the ransom note into directories associated with PeopleSoft web and application servers' with filename 'README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT'. Atomic post-compromise indicator with negligible false positive rate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation matching README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT in PeopleSoft directories (/opt/peoplesoft, /data/psoft, /home/psoft, application server root). Alert immediately on any match.

suggestion.title: Inbound Connections from Attacker-Controlled IP Space
suggestion.rationale: Article: researcher exposed 7 attacker IPs (142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) and states 'If these IOCs are found, organizations should immediately begin incident response.' Corroborated by TLS cert CN linking to ShinyHunters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any inbound connection from 142.11.200.186, .187, .188, .189, .190, 108.174.202.99, or 176.120.22.24 to PeopleSoft systems. Cross-reference against TLS cert collection for CN=azurenetfiles.net.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Remote Access Tool Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed online directories containing tooling related to this attack. Also visible were staging materials, including MeshCentral agents.' Indicates persistence/lateral movement tool deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MeshCentral binary execution, installation, service creation, or registry artifacts on non-sanctioned systems. Alert on outbound HTTPS/WebSocket traffic from PeopleSoft hosts to known MeshCentral relay servers.

suggestion.title: TLS Certificate Anomaly - Attacker Infrastructure Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'TLS certificate that has a common name of azurenetfiles[.]net, which is a domain previously linked to the ShinyHunters extortion gang.' Direct C2/staging infrastructure indicator with prior threat-actor attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshakes with certificate CN or SAN containing azurenetfiles.net from internal PeopleSoft systems. Alert on any issuance or validation of certs from this issuer on breach-sensitive networks.

suggestion.title: Publicly Exposed Bash History Containing Attacker Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Five of the servers exposed a .bash_history file that gave some insight into the attacks.' Indicates insufficient access controls and reveals reconnaissance/staging commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to /.bash_history, /shell_history, or similar shell configuration files accessible from web roots. Correlate with URI patterns containing attack keywords (ssh, spray, hydra, credential, password).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Session Token Generation + Rapid API File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token.' Pipeline missed detection of auto-login abuse preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP requests to Langflow that result in successful session token issuance (HTTP 200/302 with session cookie), followed within seconds by POSTs to /api/v2/files from the same source IP. Langflow's default auto-login design reduces friction for attackers; token-to-exploitation time <5 seconds is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal in Multipart Filename Parameter (POST /api/v2/files)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing...path traversal sequences (\'../\').' Pipeline extracted no detection for this core technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any POST to /api/v2/files with filename parameter containing consecutive dots and slashes (../) or URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e%2f). Cross-reference against Langflow version <1.9.0 to reduce false positives from patched systems.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write to Out-of-Application Directory from Web Context
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers are 'actively exploiting CVE-2026-5027 to write arbitrary files on exposed servers.' Pipeline did not suggest detection for file writes to unexpected filesystem paths from the Langflow process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow process (java or node-based, depending on deployment) for file writes outside /app, /opt/langflow, and temp directories. Alert if writes land in /etc, /home, /root, /var/www, or other application-unrelated paths. Correlate with recent POST /api/v2/files requests.

suggestion.title: Test File Droppage on Vulnerable Langflow Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'VulnCheck honeypots have now detected attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances.' Pipeline missed indicator of post-exploitation reconnaissance (test files suggest staging before destructive actions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of files with names matching test/probe patterns (test.txt, probe.bin, /tmp/chk*, .../check) in unexpected directories on Langflow-running hosts, especially if filenames or contents include timestamps or version fingerprinting data.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Related Langflow CVEs in Cluster (CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'similar activity targeting other Langflow vulnerabilities earlier this year,' but pipeline assigned zero CVEs and did not suggest multi-CVE exploitation pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests targeting endpoints associated with CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, and CVE-2026-33017 within 1-hour windows on the same Langflow instance. Multiple distinct CVE exploitation attempts on one target in short duration suggests coordinated scanning or targeted campaigns.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater Reconnaissance of Langflow Instances (CVE-2025-3248 Precedent)
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses: 'activity linked to the Iranian threat group MuddyWater' in context of CVE-2025-3248 and notes 'VulnCheck continues to observe activity.' Pipeline failed to extract threat-actor attribution and link to Langflow infrastructure targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track IP/User-Agent signatures associated with MuddyWater scanning (identified in CVE-2025-3248 activity). Cross-reference against logs of Langflow instances for /api/v2/files or related CVE-2026 endpoint probes. Langflow instances with >3 unique attacker IPs in 7 days warrant escalation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from CI/CD, Cloud, and Password Managers
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores' — direct credential_access attack requiring detection of suspicious file access and API calls to sensitive stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process attempts to enumerate or read files in .aws/, .kube/, .ssh/, ~/.config/*manager directories, or unexpected API calls from git/build contexts to credential services (1Password, Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault). Correlate with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Poisoning via Trojanized Package Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'publishing trojanized versions' to npm, PyPI, and RubyGems 'to infect downstream developers.' Detectable via anomalous package release patterns from compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious package repository uploads: unexpected version publishes from dormant maintainers, rapid multi-package releases within minutes, version bumps without corresponding git commits, API token usage from non-expected locations or timezones.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistence via Systemd/LaunchAgent
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'dead-man switch is installed as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS' — direct persistence mechanism creating detectable file artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation in ~/.config/systemd/user/ or ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ by non-root processes; unexpected systemd service/timer registration from developer contexts; LaunchAgent plist modification with suspicious payloads (rm, curl, network calls).

suggestion.title: AI Coding Tool Configuration Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies novel vector: malware 'poison[s] configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline' — requires detection of unauthorized writes to IDE config directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious writes to .cursor/config, .vscode/settings.json, ~/.config/copilot, ~/.config/claude, ~/.config/cline from non-IDE parent processes. Flag modifications that add execution hooks, credential exfiltration endpoints, or disable security features.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise and Bulk Repo Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'leaked the source code in a repo named Miasma-Open-Source-Release' via 'numerous compromised developer accounts' — mass repository creation with pattern names and credential exfiltration are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid creation of repositories with pattern names from single account; GitHub API token usage from unexpected geolocation; mass SSH key registration; Actions workflow creation without human interaction; token usage immediately after access to ~/.ssh or credential files.

suggestion.title: Destructive Dead-Man Switch File Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'monitors token validity every minute and, if revoked, executes rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents' — mass home directory deletion is distinctive impact signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on recursive deletion (rm -rf) targeting home directories or Documents folders, especially when preceded by credential access attempts, spawned by systemd user service or LaunchAgent, or correlated with GitHub token revocation events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Langflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE' and names the CVE, but pipeline generated zero detection use cases for exploitation attempts against Langflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Langflow API endpoints (common paths: /api/, /run/, /upload/) for payloads matching known CVE-2026-5027 exploitation signatures. Detect unauthenticated requests with script injection, command substitution, or remote payload delivery patterns.

suggestion.title: Langflow Process Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim is 'Unauthenticated RCE' but no use case for post-exploitation process execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawn (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python subprocess calls) originating from Langflow application parent processes. Flag execution of shell interpreters or suspicious binaries with atypical working directories or command-line patterns.

suggestion.title: Pre-Exploitation Langflow Service Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Typical attack chain includes reconnaissance; no detection for port scans or service enumeration targeting Langflow default ports (8501, 7860, 3000).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed connection attempts to known Langflow ports followed by successful access. Alert on HTTP requests probing for Langflow version strings, health endpoints, or common vulnerability scanners targeting Python/LLM-based applications.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Credential and Configuration Access
suggestion.rationale: RCE context implies attackers will access Langflow configs, API keys, and database credentials; no detection for unauthorized file reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access to Langflow config directories, .env files, or database connection strings from non-service processes. Alert on reads of environment variables or config files containing API keys, OpenAI tokens, or database credentials from Langflow's runtime context.

suggestion.title: SOHO/IoT Device Inventory & Patch Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes '1,500+ SOHO and IoT devices' as the attack surface but pipeline generated no device-discovery hunt. Gaps in device inventory and missing patches for CVE-2026-35616 are the root cause of compromise.
log_sources: Audit logs from device management solutions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SOHO/IoT devices (routers, NAS, smart home hubs, printers) missing patches for CVE-2026-35616. Cross-reference vulnerability scan results against device inventory. Flag any unpatched instances within 48 hours of advisory publication.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beacon Patterns — Low-Entropy Protocol Use
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active botnet operation ('now controls more than 1,500') and T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) is listed. Pipeline mapped technique but generated no specific hunt for botnet command channels, beacon timing, or protocol anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for periodic outbound connections from SOHO/IoT devices to the five C2 IPs on HTTP/HTTPS with low request entropy (GET requests to fixed paths, predictable interval, identical User-Agent across devices). Flag devices making frequent small HTTP requests (< 1 KB) to these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Executable Delivery — Script Dropper Pattern
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files) is identified but pipeline generated no detection for how the obfuscated payload (8 SHA256 hashes) reaches SOHO/IoT devices. Typical botnet infection chains use script interpreters or firmware update mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SOHO/IoT device process creation logs showing script interpreters (shell, Python) downloading and executing files matching the eight SHA256 hashes. Look for parent-child relationships between HTTP clients (curl, wget) and script execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_0_3: 'Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039 exploitation)' marked as delivery phase. Pipeline produced empty UC array, failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Public-sourced HTTP POST to /*.mcp* on port 8080 with HTTP 200 success response, excluding internal CIDR ranges (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12), indicates exploitation attempt against unauthenticated MCP interface.

suggestion.title: Meta Graph API token exfiltration in URL query string
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_0_4: 'Meta Graph API outbound request carrying access_token in URL query string' marked as c2 phase (credential-access/exfiltration). Pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTPS outbound to graph.facebook.com with 'access_token=' present in URL parameters signals post-compromise token exfiltration. Extract token preview and correlate temporally with prior /mcp endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp process/inventory detection
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_0_5 defines inventory hunt: 'Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp installation inventory (CVE-2026-48039) on managed hosts' marked as recon phase. Pipeline extracted zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process execution or software inventory entries for meta-ads-mcp or meta_ads_mcp running under Python/uvicorn/gunicorn/Docker process trees, prioritized on versions ≤ 1.0.101 (commit 496c988–7d14226).

suggestion.title: OAuth2 suspicious consent grant (post-token-theft)
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_OAUTH_ABUSE: 'OAuth consent / suspicious app grant' marked as actions phase, directly correlates MITRE T1098.001 (Account Manipulation) and T1556 (Modify Authentication Process). Pipeline generated no UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unusual OAuth2PermissionGrant, delegated-permission-grant, or consent-to-application events on accounts previously tied to token-theft or /mcp endpoint access indicate persistence or privilege escalation post-compromise.

suggestion.title: POC exploitation tool execution (http_auth_integration.py, api.py, poc.py)
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_0_2: 'Article-specific behavioural hunt... http_auth_integration.py, api.py, poc.py' marked as exploit phase. Pipeline empty; missed explicit file-name IOCs baked into article's own detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File creation or process execution of http_auth_integration.py, api.py, or poc.py on managed hosts; correlate parent process and creation context to distinguish dev activities from live exploitation.

suggestion.title: npm install Script Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes npm install scripts as arbitrary code execution vector: 'npm install scripts...executing during dependency installation' and GitHub's decision to disable them by default confirms the threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm or yarn processes spawning unexpected child processes (shells, interpreters, network utilities) with parent process npm/yarn and command line containing 'install' or 'postinstall'. Filter for unsigned/unsigned-by-publisher scripts.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Substitution or Typosquatting Install
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'npm install scripts...supply chain attacks' implies unauthorized packages installing. Monitor installations of packages with suspicious naming patterns or unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installs where package name differs from source repository origin (typosquatting), or where install occurs from non-standard registry, or where installed package version does not match requested version.

suggestion.title: node_modules Directory Suspicious Modification or Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes install script execution as supply chain payload delivery mechanism. node_modules directory modifications outside of package manager control indicate post-install compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect direct file writes into node_modules/ directories outside of npm/yarn processes, or execution of scripts from node_modules with unexpected parent processes, especially with network or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via npm postinstall Hook
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies install scripts as code execution pivot; scripts routinely targeted for stealing .env, SSH keys, API tokens. 'execute...during dependency installation' describes the attack window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install child processes for file access patterns targeting .env, .aws/, .ssh/, git config, or credential manager stores, followed by network egress (HTTP POST, DNS exfiltration, WebSocket).

suggestion.title: npm Hook Override or Lifecycle Script Injection
suggestion.rationale: GitHub's policy change to disable install scripts by default confirms malicious package authors abuse package.json lifecycle hooks. Article establishes: 'npm install scripts by default'—these are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to package.json 'scripts' or '.npmrc' that introduce new postinstall, preinstall, or prepare hooks, especially in dependencies or via supply chain poisoning (package replacement).

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Offline Scan Execution with Non-Standard Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'leverages an obscure but common side effect of Windows Defender Offline Scan.' Pipeline detected no execution-phase activity. Offline scan initiation outside scheduled maintenance patterns should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Defender Offline Scan process execution triggered outside normal update schedules or system maintenance windows. Flag scans initiated from non-standard locations, with unusual parameters, or preceded by physical media insertion within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Decryption Events Without User Login Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'no login required, under certain conditions.' This directly indicates BitLocker unlock/decryption occurring before or outside normal user authentication—a distinctive defense evasion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BitLocker unlock events (Event ID 1 in Event Viewer) occurring without an active user session or during pre-boot/WinPE phases. Flag decryption completion during Windows Defender Offline environment execution window.

suggestion.title: Registry Enumeration of BitLocker Configuration During Offline Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'discovered accidentally during a roughly four-hour research session' implies systematic exploration of BitLocker state. Query Registry for BitLocker keys is a clear discovery technique exploited here.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry reads to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\BDESVC or BitLocker recovery key locations (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker) during Windows Defender Offline Scan execution window. Flag from WinDefend or offline scan processes.

suggestion.title: USB Device Insertion Immediately Preceding Offline Scan Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers with physical access…' and exploit requires manual triggering. Temporal correlation of removable media arrival and Offline Scan initiation is suspicious and specific to this attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for USB or external device PnP insertion followed by Windows Defender Offline Scan scheduling within 2-minute window. Flag patterns on encrypted volumes, especially repeated or failed scan attempts.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Volume Mount Following Offline Scan Completion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fully bypass BitLocker drive encryption.' Post-exploit impact is unauthorized access to encrypted drive. Volume mount events post-scan without BitLocker unlock are suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag volume mount operations on BitLocker-encrypted drives occurring within 10 minutes of Windows Defender Offline Scan completion. Alert if mount succeeds without BitLocker unlock prompt or without valid unlock credentials logged.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Offline Scan Process Parameters or Timing Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploit…enables attackers…to fully bypass BitLocker.' Exploit likely requires specific scan parameters or conditions. Non-standard Offline Scan invocation should be detectable via process telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Offline Scan initiation via PowerShell or WMI with parameters deviating from Microsoft-documented normal usage. Flag scheduled tasks creating Offline Scan jobs outside standard boot-time scan scheduling.

suggestion.title: VMware Signed Binary Loading Unsigned DLL
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'legitimate, digitally signed VMware binary' used for 'DLL sideloading'—the attack's defining mechanism. No detection hunt exists for this evasion pattern despite it being the operational core.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VMware-signed binaries (process name contains vmware, vmrest, vdiskmanager, or similar) performing suspicious DLL loads from non-standard locations (%TEMP%, user APPDATA, working directory, or network UNC paths). Establish baseline of expected VMware DLL behavior per your environment; flag deviations, especially unsigned or unknown-hash DLLs loaded post-execution.

suggestion.title: NIGHTFORGE Loader Execution (Behavioral Sig)
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'NIGHTFORGE' as custom loader by name but provides only file hashes for detection. Behavioral signatures beyond hash matching would persist across recompiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect the 5 provided NIGHTFORGE SHA256 hashes as baseline. Extend with loader-behavior heuristics: monitor for unsigned executables creating/writing DLLs to disk followed immediately by process injection or reflective DLL load; flag parent processes matching VMware binaries in the same session.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections to Article C2 IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies C2 IPs (193.150.240.37, 104.192.244.99) and categorizes as 'high confidence' phase:c2, but this detection is listed in manual recommendations only—not in programmatically generated use cases array.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP connections from any process to 193.150.240.37 or 104.192.244.99 on any port. High fidelity if initiating process is unsigned, loaded via VMware binary, or originates from %TEMP%. Lower false-positive risk with correlation to file-write events for NIGHTFORGE hashes in the same timeline.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Legitimate VMware Binaries (Living off Land)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that attackers exploit 'legitimate' software as cover—core T1036.005 pattern. No detection specifically alerts on VMware binaries being invoked from unexpected contexts or with suspicious arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for VMware binary execution (expected parent processes, user contexts, command-line patterns, invocation frequency). Alert on deviations: VMware exe launched from non-standard paths, by non-admin users, with arguments referencing unusual directories/DLLs/scripts, or spawning unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure — Ivanti EPMM vulnerable versions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt in 'Recommended hunts' section and specifies 'Recon' phase. Pipeline failed to generate it. Requires asset inventory queries for affected EPMM versions (12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query internal asset management systems and vulnerability scanners to identify deployed Ivanti EPMM instances across versions 12.9.0, 12.8.0.2, 12.7.0.1 and earlier. Priority on internet-exposed instances. Correlate with network segmentation data.

suggestion.title: EPMM exploitation — malicious Apache config directives
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'inject malicious Apache configuration directives' to trigger RCE. This is the exploitation vector but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections. Requires HTTP request inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti EPMM endpoints for unusual Apache configuration directives in POST bodies or parameters (httpd.conf patterns, LoadModule directives, script execution directives). Alert on successful 2xx responses following such requests.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE process execution from EPMM
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability achieves 'remote code execution' per article title, but pipeline generated no detection for the RCE payload execution phase. Requires process telemetry correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) spawned by or under the EPMM application context (Ivanti service accounts or web server processes) following HTTP requests to EPMM endpoints.

suggestion.title: EPMM file system anomalies — Apache config tampering
suggestion.rationale: Injection of 'malicious Apache configuration directives' (article) implies direct or indirect writes to httpd.conf or loaded config files. Pipeline did not flag file system correlation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation, modification, or deletion of Apache configuration files (httpd.conf, .conf files in conf.d/, modules, etc.) on systems running Ivanti EPMM. Correlate with EPMM process activity and HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Attackers are now targeting a recently patched maximum-severity flaw in Ivanti Sentry' and Shadowserver confirmed 'exploitation attempts based on the public PoC.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Internet-facing Ivanti Sentry admin interfaces for HTTP requests with OS command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters, command chaining). Correlate failed exploit attempts with subsequent successful access or process execution on same appliance.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Privilege Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'execute code with root privileges' via 'OS command injection weakness.' Pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation command execution as privileged user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell process spawning (sh, bash, dash) from Ivanti Sentry gateway processes running under root/SYSTEM context. Establish baseline of expected privileged processes and flag anomalous invocations originating from appliance management or network-facing services.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Persistent Backdoor Installation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online.' Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection for indicators of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file writes to Sentry startup/initialization directories post-exploitation. Flag cron job modifications, rc script changes, or systemd service additions occurring within hours of detected exploitation attempts or Shadowserver advisory timestamps.

suggestion.title: Admin Portal Exposure and Access to Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways' and shows 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online.' Pipeline failed to generate access monitoring for exposed administrative interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/S access to Ivanti Sentry admin portals from external or non-corporate IP ranges. Establish geographic and ASN baselines for expected admin access. Alert on access attempts to unpatched versions (< R10.5.2, < R10.6.2, < R10.7.1) from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with Exchange RCE payload delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers send 'weaponized email that a victim opens in a browser'—T1566 (Phishing) is core to initial access but pipeline emitted zero phishing techniques. Missing from both MITRE list and kill-chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with embedded OWA-targeted payloads or CVE-2026-42897 exploitation code (JavaScript, HTML, etc.). Look for attachments or links that resolve to OWA endpoints with malformed or obfuscated script injection. Flag emails from external senders with suspicious macro/script/MIME structures.

suggestion.title: JavaScript execution in OWA application context
suggestion.rationale: Article's core attack vector: 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in Outlook Web Access (OWA) simply by sending a weaponized email.' No use case detects browser-side script execution or DOM injection into OWA; T1190 maps only to server-side application exploitation, not client-side execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on JavaScript execution within OWA (w3wp.exe parent, iisexpress.exe, or browser process with OWA origin). Monitor for eval(), Function(), setTimeout/setInterval with suspicious payloads. Detect script tags injected into OWA HTTP responses. Correlate with prior email delivery within user session window.

suggestion.title: Exchange Server patch compliance for CVE-2026-42897
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-42897 vulnerability but pipeline produces no inventory or patch-status hunt. Prerequisite detection: which on-premises Exchange servers remain unpatched?
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for on-premises Exchange Server instances. Cross-reference with patched/unpatched status (build number, KB article, WSUS reports). Flag any server running vulnerable version (pre-2026-patch date). Baseline: 0% unpatched servers; escalate any detection to immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Anomalous mailbox access and enumeration post-OWA exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After JavaScript execution, attacker likely achieves post-compromise objectives. Article does not detail payload behavior, but typical OWA compromises enable mailbox collection (T1114) or lateral movement. No use case captures this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation detection: flag unusual mailbox access patterns (forwarding rules, delegate additions, rapid folder enumeration) in windows 5–60 minutes after detected OWA JavaScript execution. Alert on cross-mailbox searches from single OWA session. Baseline per-user access and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE affecting versions below 10.2.4 — no asset-exposure detection was output despite the template being matched. This is table-stakes for a vulnerability briefing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Splunk process version strings, registry Software hives, or package manager queries against CVE-2026-20251–20260 baseline. Flag instances reporting Splunk Enterprise < 10.2.4.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Execution via Splunk Interpreter Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body explicitly state 'execute malicious scripts' — no execution-phase detection was generated despite this being the primary attack outcome described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or perl spawned as children of Splunk processes (splunkd.exe, splunk.exe) with suspicious encoding, unusual working directories, or obfuscated arguments.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration Post-Splunk Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'exfiltrate sensitive data' as an attacker capability — no exfiltration-phase detection was generated despite clear intent stated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Splunk process outbound connections to non-infrastructure IPs on non-standard ports. Correlate with file read activity from sensitive paths (/etc, /var, Windows AD, password managers) to establish data staging.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Operations from Splunk Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'perform unauthorized file operations' — this destructive capability was not mapped to a detection hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file create/delete/modify events from Splunk service accounts on executable directories, system binaries, or restricted paths. Flag batch operations or encryption activity originating from splunkd.exe context.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft Exploitation via Gadget Chain Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers used 'a gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities' against PeopleSoft systems. This is the attack entry point and should trigger detection for exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft listener ports (8000, 9000, 8444) for serialized Java payload patterns, JNDI injection attempts, and known gadget library exploitation signatures. Alert on HTTP requests with suspicious servlet access patterns or classpath resource access combined with exceptions in PeopleSoft application logs.

suggestion.title: Bulk Database Export from Student Records System
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stolen over 40GB of documents containing student finance data, billing and payment information, credit card and payment details'. This represents collection/exfiltration of massive structured data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multi-gigabyte archive creation (zip, 7z, tar) containing database exports on PeopleSoft servers. Alert on bulk SELECT statements from non-application service accounts, unusual data exports from PS_PERSONAL_DATA, PS_PAYMENT_INFO, and PS_STUDENT_FINANCE tables, or suspicious use of database export tools (sqlplus, pg_dump) outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PeopleSoft Administrative Access and Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hacking group gained access to its student records system', implying attacker moved from initial foothold to administrative access capable of exporting bulk student data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft user audit logs for administrative credential use from non-standard IPs/locations immediately following exploitation signatures. Alert on creation of new administrative users in PeopleSoft, role assignment changes enabling data export, or su/sudo elevation to database service accounts on the PeopleSoft application server.

suggestion.title: Multi-Campus Coordinated Data Extraction Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'campus portal exports from the University of Nottingham and its Malaysia and China campuses'—indicating coordinated attacks across geographically distributed instances of the same system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unusual portal/API export activity across multiple campus instances occurring within tight time windows. Flag bulk API requests to student data endpoints from different geographic regions with shared authentication tokens or patterns. Alert on concurrent bulk downloads from Malaysia and China portals targeting overlapping student populations.

suggestion.title: Widespread PeopleSoft Instance Reconnaissance Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article notes ShinyHunters 'stolen data from over 100 organizations worldwide after breaching their cloud and on-premises Oracle PeopleSoft instances'—indicating scanning/recon phase targeting PeopleSoft deployments at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning activity targeting PeopleSoft default ports and paths (/psc/, /student-portal, /manage) from external IPs. Alert on systematic probes of PeopleSoft version disclosure endpoints, license server endpoints, and listener service detection. Flag HTTP User-Agent patterns consistent with automated vulnerability scanning tools against PeopleSoft infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Attacker-Controlled Dark Web Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'shared an archive of allegedly stolen documents as proof' on their 'dark web leak site', indicating bulk data staging and exfiltration to external infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large archive file creation on PeopleSoft servers followed by large outbound HTTPS/SSH transfers to anonymization infrastructure (Tor proxies, residential proxies). Alert on staging directories containing student_data, backup exports, or portal_exports with concurrent network activity to known attacker infrastructure or anonymization services.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing to Vietnam Finance Sector
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors with SPECTRALVIPER'—initial access is almost certainly phishing or watering hole; no detection suggested despite actor specializing in targeted spear-phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails to Vietnam-based investment/finance entities containing links or attachments, with sender reputation anomalies or spoofing of known financial institutions. Correlate with downstream execution signals.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title names SPECTRALVIPER as the payload but zero IOCs or execution detections. Malware name alone should trigger child-process, module-load, and file-write patterns associated with the family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious child processes spawned from browsers/document readers, file creation in AppData/Temp with executable properties, and module loads from untrusted or obfuscated DLLs.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: No command-and-control detection suggested. OceanLotus campaigns historically use HTTP/HTTPS C2; article context (malware post-execution) implies C2 callbacks must occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS traffic from SPECTRALVIPER process to known or suspected C2 domains; monitor for beaconing patterns (regular connections at fixed intervals), abnormal TLS certs, or DNS queries to DGA-pattern domains.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Finance Systems
suggestion.rationale: Target is 'Vietnam Investors'—implies multi-stage attack against financial infrastructure. No lateral-movement detection for reconnaissance of investor data or lateral access to internal systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attacker enumerating file shares, spawning remote shells (PsExec, WMI), or lateral RDP/SMB connections from initially compromised investor endpoints to internal banking/trading systems.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to SPECTRALVIPER C2
suggestion.rationale: Attack against investors implies theft of investment data, portfolios, or credentials. No exfiltration detection despite clear motive and presence of C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track large data transfers from SPECTRALVIPER process or child processes to external C2; monitor for unusual volume egress during off-hours; correlate with document access logs for portfolio/research files.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry/Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: FireAnt campaign name and high severity suggest sustained presence; no persistence mechanisms detected despite OceanLotus historically using registry run keys, scheduled tasks, or service installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous registry writes to CurrentVersion\Run or Scheduled Task creation from malware process; monitor for legitimate-looking service installations referencing suspicious binary paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-35273 PeopleSoft RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote code execution vulnerability' in 'Updates Environment Management component of PeopleSoft PeopleTools.' T1190 confirms exploitation is the attack vector. Detection must identify HTTP requests to vulnerable PeopleSoft endpoints with exploitation signatures or known CVE-2026-35273 payload patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to PeopleSoft PeopleTools paths (typically /psp/*, /pscript/*, or /psftapi/*) for exploitation indicators: suspicious query parameters, encoded payloads, unusual POST bodies, or known CVE-2026-35273 POC patterns. Alert on requests returning HTTP 200 followed by outbound connections from the PeopleSoft application server process.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from PeopleSoft Services
suggestion.rationale: Article defines the vulnerability as 'remote code execution,' which necessarily results in command execution after exploitation. No detection exists for abnormal child process spawning from PeopleSoft application server processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process creation from PeopleSoft service accounts (e.g., PSADMIN.EXE, PSPWEB.EXE, or w3wp.exe running PeopleTools AppPools). Flag spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network utilities (net, ipconfig, nslookup) without prior vulnerability patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable PeopleSoft PeopleTools Inventory and Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes urgency in 'enterprise environments' requiring remediation. Pipeline must establish asset inventory of systems running the vulnerable 'Updates Environment Management component' before detections can be effectively targeted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for PeopleSoft process execution and enumerate PeopleTools version from Registry (HKLM\Software\PeopleSoft*) and application startup logs. Flag systems running vulnerable versions (exact version bounds depend on Oracle patch release, but typically affects 8.x and early 9.x). Correlate with patch deployment status.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'authentication bypass' as primary attack vector; zero detection rules generated for this phase despite it being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated access to phpBB admin-only endpoints, requests bypassing session validation, or auth-related parameters being modified or omitted in requests to protected resources. Look for rapid session escalation from user to administrator privilege level.

suggestion.title: phpBB Remote Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifies 'RCE' as critical impact; no execution-phase monitoring rules provided despite this being the most dangerous attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious child process spawning from web server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe). Detect shell metacharacters and command separators in HTTP request parameters passed to vulnerable phpBB endpoints.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment in phpBB Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities typically lead to web shell persistence; no file-system monitoring for post-exploitation artifacts despite critical compromise described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB upload and cache directories for unexpected executable files (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php5, .phar, .phps). Alert on file write events in core phpBB directories outside known patch/update windows. Check for double-extension files or null-byte bypasses.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized phpBB Administrative User Creation
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE compromise typically establishes persistence via rogue admin accounts; no detection for privilege escalation or account manipulation despite full system compromise described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB user and administrator creation events for accounts created outside normal deployment windows or by non-administrative API calls. Track rapid privilege escalation events and suspicious modifications to user role/permission tables in phpBB database.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 1,500 active compromised devices—implies persistent C2 communication infrastructure and command execution. Title: 'Cyber Reconnaissance' indicates ongoing C&C signaling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on regular outbound connections from multiple hosts to uncommon external IP/port pairs at fixed intervals. Monitor for DNS queries to uncommon domains and unusual DNS response patterns. Detect long-lived TCP/UDP sessions with botnet-typical traffic patterns (small request/response pairs, periodic activity).

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Activity from Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article states explicit purpose: 'Cyber Reconnaissance'—yet no use case captures the discovery phase. Should detect internal enumeration by botnet agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of network enumeration tools (ipconfig, nslookup, net user, arp -a, systeminfo). Alert on process chains launching discovery commands followed by C2 beacon. Monitor for Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) queries gathering system/network details.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution & Code Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: 1,500 active devices indicates malware payload execution across fleet; no detection rule for execution or process hollowing typical of botnets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned from system utilities (cmd, powershell) or network-delivery mechanisms. Detect process creation with mismatched parent/child pairs. Monitor for unusual DLL loading patterns or code injection into benign processes.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: 1,500 devices require persistence across reboots; article provides no detection for registry, scheduled task, or service persistence vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys and services with obfuscated/unusual names. Detect scheduled task creation with suspicious executable paths or system utilities as launchers. Alert on modification of startup folders or logon scripts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement within Botnet Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Expansion to 1,500+ devices from initial compromise requires lateral movement; reconnaissance activity (stated in article) typically precedes internal network spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential spraying attempts (multiple failed logons followed by success). Monitor for SMB/RPC connections to multiple internal hosts followed by process execution or file copy. Alert on exploitation of network protocols (PSEXEC, WMI, SSH) for lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Initial Access Vector for JDY Botnet Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes botnet expansion mechanism but provides no use case for initial compromise detection. How did 1,500 devices get infected?—critical gap for early warning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious email attachments (zip/exe) or phishing links leading to malware downloads. Detect exploitation of known CVEs on exposed services (RDP, HTTP servers). Alert on credential compromise or insider downloads of botnet samples.

suggestion.title: Code Execution Across Multiple Device/Environment Boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'code is written everywhere' with 'device [as] the only constant'—implies execution patterns that traverse development, staging, and production environments. This is a lateral-movement or supply-chain execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code execution initiated from build pipelines (CI/CD) that spawns child processes or scripts on multiple distinct devices within short time windows. Flag when same binary/hash executes across dev→staging→prod boundaries with shared parent process or command context.

suggestion.title: Device Fingerprinting for Build Identity Tracking
suggestion.rationale: 'Device is the only constant' suggests attackers may use device fingerprints or hardware identifiers as persistence or identification markers in a supply-chain attack context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for processes querying hardware identifiers (HWID, MAC address, SerialNumber) during build or deployment phases. Flag unusual collection of device properties by build agents or code-distribution tooling.

suggestion.title: Build System / CI-CD Compromise Leading to Widespread Code Injection
suggestion.rationale: If 'code is written everywhere,' a single compromise of a centralized build system could serve as an initial-access vector for supply-chain injection affecting all downstream artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous modifications to build scripts, package managers, or artifact repositories. Alert on build-system service accounts executing code outside normal CI/CD workflows or downloading/executing unsigned binaries from external sources.

suggestion.title: Installation of Malicious Rust Crate 'onering'
suggestion.rationale: Article title and context explicitly identify 'onering' as the compromised package vector. Must extract crate name, affected versions, and distribution timeline for dependency vulnerability detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock file modifications and package manager logs for installation of 'onering' crate. Alert on artifact registry pulls of onering before compromise disclosure date. Correlate with build process initiation.

suggestion.title: Code Exfiltration from Build Environment to External C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states payload is 'code exfiltration'—must detect bulk source code reads from project directories followed by network transmission to attacker infrastructure during build/compilation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from cargo/rustc processes to non-standard external hosts; correlate bulk .rs/.toml file access with HTTP POST/PUT/exfil protocols. Establish baseline for legitimate build egress first.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawning from Compromised Crate Import
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware executes code at import time—execution chain should reveal child processes (curl, wget, cmd, powershell, bash, nc) spawned by rustc/cargo without corresponding build config.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawns from rustc.exe or cargo.exe, especially network-capable tools. Cross-reference against Cargo manifest and build scripts. Alert on abnormal command lines and C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Source Code Collection Prior to Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration requires enumeration and staging—detect bulk file access patterns targeting .rs sources, Cargo.lock, config files, and credential stores before data leaves the host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mass file enumerate/read operations on project directory (especially source files) by processes spawned from crate import context or build toolchain. Baseline normal build patterns first.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration implies command-and-control infrastructure—Rust build processes should have whitelist-only egress (crates.io, mirrors, package registries). Any deviation is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Rust toolchain egress (crates.io, github.com, official mirrors). Alert on any outbound connections from cargo/rustc to non-whitelisted domains/IPs. Investigate ASN, geolocation, and passive DNS history.

suggestion.title: JWT Signature Validation Failure Against Hardcoded Secret
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery'—any JWT signed with 'random' should fail validation in properly configured systems, but attackers will send such tokens. Missing detection for auth errors or signature mismatches when forged tokens are submitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs for HTTP 401/403 responses following Bearer token authentication attempts to `/api/v1/*` endpoints. Alert on repeated failed JWT validations from same source IP within 5-minute window (indicates token forgery attempts). Correlate with successful 200 responses on subsequent requests from same IP (exploitation success).

suggestion.title: JWT Claims Inspection: Far-Future Expiration (exp) in Bearer Tokens
suggestion.rationale: UC_34_1 title explicitly references 'extreme far-future JWT' but provided detection queries never inspect the exp (expiration) claim. Article describes vulnerability enables token forgery—attacker-crafted JWTs will have suspicious lifetime values inconsistent with legitimate token rotation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract exp claim from JWT Bearer tokens in Authorization headers. Alert if exp-issued_at > 86400 seconds (24-hour lifetime is suspicious; legitimate JWTs typically 15-60 minutes). Enrich with known hardcoded secret signatures; flag if token validates against 'random' string hash.

suggestion.title: Admin Endpoint Access Without Prior Authentication Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article lists `/api/v1/admin/users` and `/api/v1/token/refresh` as sensitive endpoints. Legitimate access should follow login flow (POST /login → 200 + Bearer token → subsequent requests). Attacker with hardcoded secret can skip login entirely and directly forge tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to `/api/v1/admin/*` endpoints. Alert if source IP accessed the endpoint without a preceding successful /login or /oauth/token response in the same session. Baseline on user-agent + source IP combinations; flag new anomalies.

suggestion.title: go-base Repository Access Pattern: Hardcoded Secret in Local Testing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability article states 'dev.env' and 'cmd/serve.go' contain template defaults shipped to all users. Article references 1,685 GitHub stars. Detect if environment variables or process command-lines contain the literal strings 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' or 'jwt.*secret.*random'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation or environment variable audit logs containing 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET' set to 'random' or similar hardcoded default. Cross-reference with vulnerable go-base clones in repositories or vendor directories (github.com/dhax/go-base). Escalate if found in production or long-running services.

suggestion.title: Baileys Exploitation — Message Spoofing Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can be sent a malicious payload via placeholderResendMessage and trigger a fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload.' Pipeline missed detection for the IMPACT phase — actual spoofed messages in chat logs with metadata inconsistencies (sender mismatch, timestamp anomalies, key validation failures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys application logs for message.upsert events where sender identity fails validation against message key signature, or where timestamps are logically impossible (future-dated, gaps in conversation). Look for placeholderResendMessage events followed by unverified message creates.

suggestion.title: App State Corruption — Sync Failure and State Inconsistency
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key' but no detection exists for the corruption OUTCOME. Pipeline ignored the impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys app state sync logs for rollback events, state version conflicts, or failed sync reconciliation. Flag rapid state mutations following unusual protocolMessage processing errors or exceptions in message validation routines.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Execution — Suspicious Node.js Baileys Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1059.007 (Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript) but pipeline generated zero detections for JavaScript/Node.js execution anomalies. Missing visibility into process behavior, module loading, and resource consumption of Baileys under exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js process hosting Baileys for unusual child process spawning, unexpected module loading (crypto, network modules), abnormal CPU/memory spikes during message processing, or exceptions in protocolMessage parsing.

suggestion.title: Version Enforcement — Outdated Baileys Running in Production
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects versions < 7.0.0-rc12 AND < 6.7.22 (compound boundary). Pipeline extracted no version indicators. UC_24_2 detects presence but not outdated instances actively running.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor running Node.js processes for Baileys package.json version field or require() module version reporting. Correlate against known vulnerable ranges. Flag if process is still running after known patch release dates without update attempt.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain — Baileys Update Lag Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes supply chain angle (T1195.001) but pipeline ignored the temporal signal: patched versions exist (7.0.0-rc12+, 6.7.22+) and unpatched instances are lagging. No detection for failure to apply available patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Baileys versions deployed across fleet. Alert when a host has a known-vulnerable version AND no update attempt has occurred within 30 days of patch availability. Distinguish active use from archived code.

suggestion.title: Vendor Security Patch Release Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article announces patches from Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP for critical vulnerabilities; pipeline should create use case to monitor vendor advisory feeds and track CVE publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads and references to Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP patch advisory pages. Flag HTTP requests to vendor security bulletin URLs and patch-distribution servers.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection - Patch-Disclosed Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities in Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP are now public; detection use case needed to flag exploitation attempts against these products via T1190 techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous process execution and network behavior from Ivanti clients, Fortinet appliance management ports, and SAP application servers. Alert on unexpected child processes or suspicious outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Unpatched System Inventory - Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Patch announcement creates urgent need to identify unpatched instances; use case should track version compliance against disclosed vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate patch release dates against system inventory. Flag systems running vulnerable versions. Alert on absence of patching activity within X days post-release.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Admin Account Creation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10523 'can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts.' Direct entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag admin account creation events in Ivanti Sentry logs where no successful authentication precedes them from the source IP. Correlate account-creation events with external/untrusted IP ranges. Alert on admin account provisioning outside scheduled change windows.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Ivanti Sentry HTTP Parameters
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10520 described as 'OS command injection weakness' enabling code execution. Detection must catch shell metacharacters in request payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $(, command substitution syntax) in HTTP request parameters to known Ivanti Sentry endpoints. Combine with successful response codes (2xx). Flag payloads containing command keywords (id, whoami, cat, curl, nc, bash).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Privilege Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'execute code with root privileges' as the impact of CVE-2026-10520. Detection must capture root-level child process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by the Ivanti Sentry service with effective user = root/SYSTEM. Baseline known legitimate spawning and alert on deviations. Cross-check parent command line for injection patterns or suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Sequential Unauthenticated Access → Admin Account → Root RCE on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Kill chain combines three phases: (1) unauthenticated auth bypass, (2) rogue admin account creation, (3) command injection with root execution. Correlated detection increases fidelity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alert when the same source IP exhibits: unauthenticated access attempt to Sentry admin interface, followed within 10 minutes by admin account creation event, followed within 30 minutes by unexpected root-privilege process spawning. Treat this 3-event sequence as exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Pre-Patch Version Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions: any < R10.5.2, < R10.6.2, < R10.7.1. Version discovery is critical for prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory and asset management databases for Ivanti Sentry running versions prior to R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1 (track by release track). Cross-reference with network scans to identify internet-facing Sentry instances. Flag for immediate patch priority.

suggestion.title: Unexpected SYSTEM Process Spawn from Microsoft Defender
