suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states vulnerability 'grants SYSTEM access.' Detection must catch when Defender processes (mpengine.exe, MsSense.exe, MdCorpusImpressionService) spawn child processes with SYSTEM privilege—the core exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with SYSTEM privilege spawned by Microsoft Defender engine or service processes. Privilege escalation via Defender zero-day produces anomalous parent-child relationships that violate expected Defender process behavior patterns.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Engine Abnormal Execution or Memory Access
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day in Defender itself requires exploitation of mpengine.exe or related engine logic. Title 'RoguePlanet' suggests targeted Defender component. Detection should identify anomalous engine behavior preceding SYSTEM escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Defender engine for unusual DLL loads, memory allocations, or internal API invocations preceding privilege escalation. Correlation: anomalous Defender behavior + SYSTEM child process spawning within 10 seconds = exploitation.

suggestion.title: Defender Service Crash or Restart Preceding Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation of security products often triggers crashes or restarts. Title indicates vulnerability present on 'Updated Windows,' suggesting recent patches may not fully mitigate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MsMpEngine.exe or Defender service crashes/restarts immediately preceding SYSTEM escalation events. Correlation rule: Defender service termination → SYSTEM process spawn within 5 seconds = exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Scan Triggering Defender Vulnerability Chain
suggestion.rationale: Common attack vector for Defender zero-days is weaponized file scanning. Article body missing, but if vulnerability triggered by file type/pattern, detection must correlate: file creation → Defender scan → privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation followed by Defender scan activity, then immediate SYSTEM process spawning. Payload files triggering Defender zero-days often have distinctive characteristics (archive entropy, size, embedded metadata).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement Following SYSTEM Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Once SYSTEM is obtained via Defender vulnerability, attacker typically pivots laterally or establishes persistence. Detection must flag anomalous network and process activity post-escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SYSTEM-level process spawning (from Defender exploit) with immediate network connections to internal systems, remote admin tool execution (PsExec, WMI), or service creation on remote hosts within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Outlook Web Access JavaScript Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user. If the user opens the email in Outlook Web Access and certain interaction conditions are met, arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context.' This directly describes the execution phase requiring OWA-specific script detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA session events and browser process execution for unexpected JavaScript execution following email message interaction. Alert on script execution within Outlook Web Access context tied to email message processing, especially with API calls to mailbox enumeration or credential access functions.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with XSS Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector: 'An attacker could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user.' Email gateways must detect crafted payloads targeting CVE-2026-42897.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing XSS injection patterns (script tags, event handlers, encoded payloads) in body and HTML parts. Correlate with threat intel on CVE-2026-42897 exploit signatures and baseline suspicious email patterns against user OWA mailbox opens.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Public-Facing Exchange OWA Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote attackers with no privileges' can exploit the vulnerability, indicating OWA is the public-facing attack surface. Attacks require no prior access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to OWA for requests containing XSS-like payloads in query parameters, POST bodies, headers, or MIME parts. Flag requests from non-corporate IP ranges with encoding/obfuscation patterns targeting message composition or rendering endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Email Collection After Successful XSS
suggestion.rationale: Successful arbitrary JavaScript execution in the user's browser context enables attackers to access mailbox data, message enumeration, and credential harvesting beyond initial code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After XSS payload execution in OWA, detect unusual mailbox access patterns: bulk message reads, export requests, contact list enumeration, message search operations with unusual query volume, or folder tree traversal from a single OWA session.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Exchange Server Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Microsoft recommends installing the June 2026 Security Updates for your version of Exchange Server as soon as possible.' Must inventory and flag unpatched vulnerable versions (2016, 2019, Subscription Edition) exposed to OWA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously scan for Exchange Server installations running 2016, 2019, or Subscription Edition versions without June 2026 security patches. Prioritize systems with external-facing OWA endpoints. Alert on any unpatched instances matching the vulnerable version matrix.

suggestion.title: RCE Execution from Vulnerable Microsoft Software
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Critical RCE Bugs' but pipeline generated zero detection hypothesis for exploitation. RCE is the attack's entry point and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Microsoft RCE vulnerabilities (Office, Edge, IE) typically manifest as unexpected child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, csc.exe) or suspicious network callbacks from vulnerable parent processes. Correlate vulnerable app version with child process creation and outbound network events within 10 seconds of receipt of malicious content (email, web, SMB).

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Exploitation via Behavioral Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'Three Zero-Days' but pipeline offered no behavioral detection strategy for unknown/unpatched vulnerability patterns. Zero-days lack CVE context and require anomaly-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Zero-day RCE often executes shellcode in out-of-process memory or via unusual execution contexts (native client, binary planting in temp directories). Flag process execution with unusual image load order, unsigned child processes, or syscalls to kernel APIs not typical for the parent process.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Critical RCE Bugs' that typically chain to privilege escalation; no detection use case for post-execution privilege gain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: RCE exploitation often precedes UAC bypass or token theft. Detect sudden elevation requests (Event ID 4624 with RunLevel=High), unusual rundll32.exe or eventvwr.exe invocations, write attempts to protected kernel structures, or LSASS memory read access from non-system processes.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment and Vulnerable Endpoint Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article references 206 patches released; pipeline did not propose tracking patch application or identifying unpatched hosts vulnerable to the announced CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Update logs (Event ID 19, 20) for successful installs of known RCE-patch KB numbers. Cross-reference with process telemetry to identify endpoints still running vulnerable component versions >72 hours post-patch release. Tier by criticality: unpatched RCE vulnerabilities = high-risk.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection from Compromised Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE vulnerabilities enable lateral propagation within networks; title establishes RCE risk but pipeline generated no detection for intra-network spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE lateral movement manifests as new NTLM/Kerberos auth from unexpected sources, lateral SMB/WinRM connections to internal IPs, or tool execution (PsExec, RemCom, wmic) from child processes spawned by vulnerable software. Baseline normal lateral movement and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Detect POST /api/v2/files with path-traversal payload in filename
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to /api/v2/files for filename parameters containing '../', '..\\', or encoded variants. Alert on any attempt regardless of source, as endpoint is unauthenticated by default. Deploy at reverse-proxy or WAF layer for broad coverage.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated session token issuance from Langflow API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Because Langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track session/JWT token generation from Langflow API. Flag any token issuance without prior credential exchange. Establish baseline of legitimate anonymous tokens; alert on spikes or tokens issued to suspicious IP space.

suggestion.title: Hunt for Langflow instances < version 1.9.0 or langflow-base < 0.8.3
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the issue was fixed in the langflow-base package version 0.8.3, while the Langflow application itself received a patch in version 1.9.0'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory, package managers, and application banners for Langflow versions prior to 1.9.0. Cross-reference with network exposure scans (article: ~7,000 exposed instances detected by Censys). Prioritize internet-facing instances for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Detect arbitrary file writes originating from Langflow process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-5027...to write arbitrary files on exposed servers' and 'drop test files on vulnerable instances'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow process (langflow, python, java) for file-write syscalls to system/sensitive directories (/etc, /var, /tmp, C:\Windows\System32). Correlate with preceding POST /api/v2/files requests containing path traversal to establish exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Track MuddyWater exploitation of Langflow CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Caitlin Condon says VulnCheck continues to observe activity, including activity linked to the Iranian threat group MuddyWater' (CVE-2025-3248 and related Langflow flaws)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploitation attempts against Langflow CVEs (CVE-2026-5027, CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017, CVE-2025-3248) with MuddyWater infrastructure/TTPs. Monitor for IP/ASN patterns, user-agent strings, and payload timing consistent with prior campaigns.

suggestion.title: Honeypot-based detection of Langflow path-traversal attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'According to VulnCheck security researcher Caitlin Condon, their honeypots have now detected attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy non-production Langflow honeypot instances on isolated network segments. Log all POST /api/v2/files requests and track file-write attempts. Any exploitation triggers alert and feeds threat intelligence (attacker IP, payload, timing). Correlate with production instances for validation.

suggestion.title: Langflow RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027 Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE'—no detection rule was generated for identifying exploitation attempts against this vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/flows, /upload, vulnerable parameter injection points) without valid authentication tokens. Look for POST/GET requests with serialized payloads, code injection patterns, or unusual parameter encoding typical of RCE exploits. Baseline legitimate Langflow traffic first; flag requests with command-like syntax or binary payloads in request body.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution from Langflow Service
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Unauthenticated RCE' but no detection was created for the actual code execution artifacts—child processes spawned from Langflow after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Langflow process (or child of Langflow parent) spawns suspicious child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget, nc, or processes with obfuscated names. Flag execution of system utilities (whoami, systeminfo, dir, ls) or reverse-shell indicators. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes first (e.g., legitimate API integrations); flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from Langflow to Non-Whitelisted C&C Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploits typically lead to outbound C&C or data exfiltration (article mentions 'exploited' but context for attacker post-compromise actions missing from pipeline analysis). No network-based detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Langflow service/process (by PID or process name) to external IPs/domains not in a pre-established whitelist. Flag DNS requests from Langflow for suspicious domains (newly registered, low reputation, known C&C infrastructure). Alert on unexpected protocols or ports used by Langflow (e.g., non-standard HTTP, HTTPS to unusual ports). Correlate with exploitation detection above.

suggestion.title: Langflow Service Restart or Crash Following Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: No defensive evasion or persistence detection created. Attacker may restart Langflow to disable application-layer logging or maintain access; article doesn't detail but standard RCE post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Langflow service stop/start/restart events (especially if unscheduled or outside change windows). Correlate with prior exploitation attempts. Monitor for log deletion or rotation anomalies on Langflow application/access logs immediately following suspected RCE activity.

suggestion.title: Authorized BAS Tool Reconnaissance Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article frame assumes CISOs deploy BAS to simulate real attacks. Pipeline should surface detection strategies that distinguish BAS-authorized reconnaissance (network scanning, enumeration, exploitation) from genuine adversary activity. Reference: 'CISOs are moving budget to BAS'—implies widespread deployment of attack simulation requiring detection tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: BAS platforms (e.g., AttackIQ, SafeBreach, Rapid7 InsightVM) execute reconnaissance modules that generate process trees, network traffic, and file access consistent with live attacks. Detect by process lineage (managed process → nmap/masscan/proprietary scanner), network source-IP tagging (known BAS infrastructure), and correlated timing with authorized security testing windows.

suggestion.title: Simulated Credential Theft Activity
suggestion.rationale: BAS value proposition includes testing credential compromise and post-exploit paths. If article emphasizes why organizations prefer BAS over static vulnerability scanning, it likely references testing realistic attack chains including credential access. Detection should whitelist authorized simulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag credential access attempts (failed or successful) that originate from known BAS platforms or test accounts, persist for abnormally short duration (<5 minutes), or occur from known test-infrastructure IP ranges. Correlate with approved testing schedules to suppress.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Authorized Exploitation Testing
suggestion.rationale: BAS tools execute real or real-like exploit code to assess detection gaps. Article's premise (AI broke VM, CISOs shifting to BAS) implies organizations need to detect whether defenders catch simulated attacks—which requires monitoring for execution of potentially destructive or evasive techniques in controlled contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attempts to disable/bypass security tools (Windows Defender, EDR, logging) when launched from BAS tool infrastructure or tagged test accounts. Create alert rules that fire but tag as 'authorized testing' rather than incident when source is confirmed BAS platform.

suggestion.title: SOHO/IoT Device Compromise via CVE-2026-35616 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'rapid vulnerability exploitation' and '1,500+ SOHO and IoT devices'—implies active exploitation campaign. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection. Article provides CVE but no payload delivery chain; need behavioral hunt for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests matching CVE-2026-35616 exploitation patterns (SQL injection, path traversal, RCE payload delivery) to SOHO device management interfaces (common ports: 80, 443, 8080, 8443). Baseline expected traffic to known-good firmware update servers and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence on Compromised SOHO/IoT Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '1,500+ devices' under botnet control—implies post-exploitation persistence. No hunt provided for how malware maintains foothold on these devices. Expected: autostart mechanisms, firmware modification, or scheduled tasks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SOHO/IoT device firmware modification attempts, unauthorized cron/scheduled task creation, and modifications to system startup sequences. Flag unsigned firmware updates or out-of-band binary execution from non-vendor paths.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Scanning Activity from Compromised Bot Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names JDY as 'one of the most capable reconnaissance tools'—implies active internal network scanning. No hunt provided for lateral reconnaissance. Expect port scanning, host enumeration, and service discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile network behavior from SOHO/IoT devices at 149.248.3.38, 23.27.120.240, etc. to detect anomalous scanning (many failed connections, port sweep patterns). Alert on internal network discovery—ARP scanning, DNS reverse lookups, ICMP sweeps—from devices normally exhibiting stable traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication Patterns for JDY Botnet Agents
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) but provides no detail on protocol/port/timing. Five C2 IPs identified but no behavioral signature for command channel. Need hunt for periodic C2 beacons and command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile outbound connections from SOHO/IoT devices to the five identified IPs for protocol, payload pattern, and interval. Expect HTTP/HTTPS POST with beacon data. Flag consistent communication windows (e.g., every 5-10 minutes), encrypted payloads, and fallback channels to alternative IPs if primary IP is blocked.

suggestion.title: Malware Staging and Secondary Payload Download
suggestion.rationale: Article provides eight SHA256 hashes but no context on relationships or deployment order. Likely represents dropper → payload chain. Hunt needed for inter-stage file delivery and process injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation and execution of the eight provided SHA256 artifacts; correlate timing to identify staging order (dropper executes first, fetches final payload from C2). Flag parent-child process chains indicating injection or process hollowing. Check for file write to temp/cache directories followed by rapid execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-35616 Vulnerability Scan and Exploitation Footprints
suggestion.rationale: CVE mentioned but no details on affected product, version, or exploitation method. Recommend proactive hunt for scanning activity and successful exploitation indicators before devices are compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with known CVE-2026-35616 exploit patterns (payload signatures, error response chains). Correlate with failed authentication attempts, privilege escalation logs, or file uploads to detected vulnerable product versions. Flag any device that shows both scanning activity AND successful exploitation within 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: npm Install Script Execution with Elevated Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly names npm install scripts as supply-chain attack vector: 'GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks.' Pipeline missed the execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell/powershell/cmd.exe processes spawned by npm or node executables, particularly with parent-child relationships suggesting postinstall/preinstall/prepare script execution. Alert on npm child processes accessing the filesystem outside node_modules or spawning network connections. Baseline legitimate preinstall behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Registry or Package Source
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise hinges on installation of malicious or substituted packages. Article context ('stop supply chain attacks') implies detection should monitor the initial fetch phase before scripts execute.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install requests to non-canonical registries (not registry.npmjs.org or approved internal mirrors). Alert on package installations where reported hash/signature mismatches occur, or on fallback behavior when primary registry is unavailable. Monitor for typosquatting patterns in dependency names.

suggestion.title: package.json Script Field Modification Before Install
suggestion.rationale: Attack prerequisite: malicious script must be injected into package.json or transitive dependency. Article establishes threat model; pipeline missed pre-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthorized changes to package.json scripts (prepend, postinstall, prepare) with npm install execution within short time windows. Alert on script values containing encoded payloads (base64, hex), curl/wget invocations, or shell metacharacters. Compare against known-good baseline scripts per project.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Override of npm Script Restrictions
suggestion.rationale: GitHub's mitigation targets developer and pipeline security. Article implies defenders need to detect scenarios where security controls are bypassed in automation contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install commands with --scripts-prepend-node-path, --ignore-scripts=false, or other flags that override default script-disabling policies in CI/CD contexts. Alert on npm executed with elevated privileges (sudo, RunAs) in pipeline jobs not explicitly authorized. Monitor for npm environment variable overrides (NODE_SKIP_PLATFORM_CHECK, NPM_CONFIG_*).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Activity During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Malicious install scripts may exfiltrate data or establish persistence by reaching external C2. Article threat model presupposes post-execution detection is necessary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by child processes of npm/node during install phase. Alert on connections to unusual ASNs, domains flagged for malware/phishing, or internal network scanning from build systems. Correlate timing of install completion with external DNS queries or HTTP beacons.

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Offline Scan Triggering BitLocker Key Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'leveraging an obscure but common side effect of Windows Defender Offline Scan' to bypass encryption. No detection for Windows Defender Offline Scan invoked outside maintenance windows, preceding BitLocker mount attempts without credential prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Defender Offline Scan initiation (WinRE or boot-sequence triggers) immediately followed by BitLocker volume access without corresponding unlock events in the security event log or Defender activity logs. Flag sequences where scan completes and encrypted volume is mounted without credential validation artifacts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Windows Recovery Environment Access for Encryption Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires boot-time access under 'certain conditions' and 'no login required', indicating WinRE abuse. Article describes physical access triggering pre-OS modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected Windows Recovery Environment boots outside scheduled maintenance windows, particularly those involving BitLocker volume initialization or recovery-key operations. Correlate with physical access indicators (unexpected system restarts, recovery partition modifications, or boot device changes).

suggestion.title: BitLocker Volume Mount Without Authentication After Offline Scan
suggestion.rationale: Core attack effect: 'fully bypass BitLocker drive encryption on Windows systems...no login required'. Describes complete circumvention of encryption protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for BitLocker-protected volumes being accessed with read/write permissions when no corresponding BitLocker unlock event, recovery-key input, or PIN entry is logged. Particularly sensitive if preceded by WinRE activity or Defender Offline Scan within the same boot session.

suggestion.title: GreatXML Campaign – Exploit Kit or Tooling Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names exploit 'GreatXML'—this should be extracted as campaign identifier for hunt correlation, tooling discovery, and actor tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference 'GreatXML' against file names, process command lines, registry modifications, and network traffic metadata. Hunt for post-exploitation persistence mechanisms if the exploit leaves boot-time artifacts, modified recovery partitions, or BitLocker configuration changes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous BitLocker Recovery Key Access or Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Bypass mechanism likely involves key material recovery or circumvention. Article hints at decryption without credential submission, suggesting key extraction or derivation from Windows Defender Offline Scan artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for recovery key read operations, WMI queries to BitLocker objects, or access to BIOS/firmware settings that correlate with Offline Scan events. Flag processes accessing encrypted volume metadata without user-initiated unlock prompts.

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Offline Scan Abuse for Pre-OS Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly hinges on 'obscure but common side effect' of Offline Scan—this is the defense evasion mechanism itself. No detection suggested for this technique variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows Defender Offline Scan initiated with non-standard parameters, unusual scheduling, or triggered by non-administrator accounts. Correlate with subsequent BitLocker modifications, recovery environment changes, or encryption key operations to establish abuse pattern.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading via Legitimate VMware Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers have been abusing a legitimate, digitally signed VMware binary to slip a custom malicious loader called NIGHTFORGE onto victim systems. This technique, known as DLL sideloading'. No detection generated for this core attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when legitimate VMware-signed executables (vmware.exe, vmx.exe, etc.) load non-VMware or unsigned DLLs from directories outside standard VMware installation paths. Key signals: process parent=VMware binary, image load from temp/user directories, or DLL lacking VMware signature.

suggestion.title: NIGHTFORGE Loader File Hash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 5 SHA256 hashes with 'high-fidelity' designation. Pipeline extracted zero file hashes. These should be immediately translated into hash-based detections across endpoint and file repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any file writes or process execution matching provided SHA256 hashes: {90bba96afe1b5b8410c4f1649adeb8ca1f04c816c64f46912d5bca890f8b2c0a, b34b34310b963fd2901b6e00b0e9a01be6c19d40e68101f0cc1d34ae7f22a4af, 3a33a10901e9ef89eace7834f9c7ce14f590e58bb1b50ec5bd44b4ef1ca5555a, 1852120a84a328edd1995e633dfd2009867898a8e3f0b385e2490cf21c77a994, b3e853eee14fb7948c6907888ee07139085ba9af4231c30e97ff6236b86ca024}.

suggestion.title: Network Communications to Article-Provided C2 IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Indicators of Compromise' lists IPv4 addresses 193.150.240.37 and 104.192.244.99 as high-fidelity C2 indicators. Pipeline extracted zero network IOCs. 'Recommended hunts' section explicitly suggests network-IOC hunts against these addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound network connections (TCP/UDP any port) from endpoints to C2 IPs 193.150.240.37 or 104.192.244.99, especially when source process is a child of or related to DLL sideloading activity or NIGHTFORGE hash.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write Near VMware Installation Directory
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern: 'DLL sideloading' typically involves writing malicious DLL to same directory as legitimate VMware binary. Article describes targeting 'government institutions' suggesting precision staged delivery; no behavioral detection for this staging pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes to VMware installation paths (e.g., C:\Program Files\VMware\* or C:\Program Files (x86)\VMware\*) from processes not tied to VMware installer/updater, especially .dll writes in same directory as VMware executables.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from DLL Sideloading Context
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires that legitimate VMware binary execute and load malicious NIGHTFORGE DLL. Article states loader 'slips onto victim systems' implying execution. No detection for processes spawned immediately after unusual DLL load from VMware context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process chains where: (1) legitimate VMware-signed executable is parent, (2) image load of non-VMware or unsigned DLL observed in same timeframe, (3) child process spawned with network connectivity or unusual command-line. Cross-reference loaded DLL against NIGHTFORGE hashes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempts on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers are now targeting a recently patched maximum-severity flaw in Ivanti Sentry' and Shadowserver observed 'a large amount of Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 exploitation attempts based on the public PoC'. This is the confirmed initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance access logs and gateway web server logs for HTTP POST requests containing shell metacharacters, backticks, or OS command delimiters (|, &, ;, $()) targeting the Sentry admin interface. Correlate with IDS signatures for CVE-2026-10520 exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Root Privilege Code Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'enabling them to execute code with root privileges on Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways'. Detection should focus on unexpected SYSTEM/root-level process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution spawned from Ivanti Sentry gateway service accounts with privilege level SYSTEM or root, especially for shell interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or system utilities. Monitor parent-child process relationships where parent is gateway web service.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Gateway Backdoor Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver reported 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' with at least 2 confirmed backdoors among 19 vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry system for creation of executable files or scripts in startup/init directories, unexpected scheduled tasks, cron jobs, or unauthorized modifications to gateway configuration files. Flag changes to web root directories and service binaries.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication to Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online' as attack vector. Combined with active exploitation reports, this indicates attackers targeting exposed admin interfaces directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts to Sentry admin portals from non-corporate IP ranges, Tor exit nodes, or known proxy services. Alert on successful logins followed immediately by anomalous gateway activity (config changes, user creation, file uploads). Establish baseline of normal admin patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Ivanti Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states gateway provides 'entry point into targets' enterprise networks' and describes attackers stealing 'sensitive customer and corporate data', indicating post-compromise lateral movement to internal systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from compromised Ivanti Sentry appliances to corporate systems behind the gateway. Flag connections from gateway's SYSTEM/root processes to internal networks on SMB (445), RDP (3389), SSH (22), and RPC ports. Alert on DNS queries from gateway to internal domain names not in baseline.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker objectives explicitly: 'theft of sensitive customer and corporate data' and 'Hackers often target Ivanti security flaws because they provide an entry point into targets' enterprise networks, enabling the theft of sensitive customer and corporate data'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor large data transfers outbound from compromised Ivanti Sentry appliances to external IP addresses not in allow list. Alert on creation of large archives (.zip, .tar.gz) or database dumps. Flag unusual egress patterns in volume, destination, or protocol (DNS tunneling, HTTPS to non-standard ports).

suggestion.title: Splunk Remote Code Execution via Malicious Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute malicious scripts' as primary attack vector. No detection use case addresses in-instance script execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk internals for unexpected code execution within search/Python/Perl processes. Flag: system() calls in custom search commands, inline Python/Perl in scheduled searches outside approved repository, REST API calls with code injection patterns, splunkd spawning shell interpreters.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Compromised Splunk Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'exfiltrate sensitive data' as explicit attack outcome; no detection addresses data theft from Splunk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk data exports and outbound transmission from Splunk: large result set exports via REST, unusual cloud storage uploads (S3/Azure), data sent to non-approved destinations, service account performing atypical searches at scale.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File System Operations from Splunk Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'unauthorized file operations' but no detection covers file system activity initiated by compromised Splunk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file create/modify/delete events where parent process is splunkd or search process. Flag: writes outside Splunk directories, system directory modifications, executable creation in temp paths, deletion of audit/log files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Public-Facing Vulnerability Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: T1190 exploitation traffic should have dedicated detection beyond asset inventory. Article does not detail signatures but WAF/proxy would log exploitation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS inbound traffic to Splunk management ports (8089, 8000) for exploitation payloads: null-byte injection, path traversal, unusual parameter encoding, authentication bypass attempts, requests matching known CVE-2026-202xx patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Version and Vulnerability Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance precedes exploitation. Article does not detail scanning but version-disclosure endpoints are reconnaissance precursor to CVE matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external requests to version-disclosure endpoints (/api/server/info, /services/server/info) and repeated probing of Splunk services from untrusted IPs, especially followed by exploitation attempts or from known scanner ranges.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers used 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities in the attacks' against PeopleSoft; no detection rule generated despite explicit exploit chain identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application servers for Java deserialization of untrusted data, ClassPathXmlApplicationContext or CommonsCollections gadget chain patterns, and unusual servlet instantiation. Flag process creation from PeopleSoft JVM with suspicious command lines (java.lang.ProcessBuilder, Runtime.exec), especially when originating from HTTP request processing threads.

suggestion.title: Bulk Student Records Extraction from Campus System
suggestion.rationale: Article reports '40GB of documents containing student finance data, billing and payment information...campus portal exports'—massive structured data theft from known system; no exfiltration detection rule created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk exports of student records by monitoring database query patterns for SELECT * or COUNT(*) operations against student_records, billing, or payment tables followed by large data egress. Alert on export-function invocations (campus portal batch export APIs) outside maintenance windows, especially with subsequent file uploads to external IP space or Tor exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PeopleSoft System Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Breach confirmed via 'student records system has been accessed by a well-known cybercriminal group'—successful compromise of PeopleSoft system should trigger detection of anomalous system access; pipeline missed this collection phase indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application logs for unusual user/service account access to sensitive student record tables, API calls to student_records or financial_data endpoints, and data export operations by non-administrative accounts. Flag sequential access patterns suggesting enumeration or bulk extraction.

suggestion.title: Multiple University Targets by ShinyHunters Gadget Chain Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies pattern: 'widespread data theft campaign in which the ShinyHunters gang has stolen data from over 100 organizations worldwide after breaching their...Oracle PeopleSoft instances'—campaign-level detection opportunity missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag organizations running PeopleSoft for network traffic or application-level signatures of known gadget chain probes. Monitor failed authentication attempts to PeopleSoft portals from external IPs, unusual HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE) against PeopleSoft endpoints, and exploitation-attempt patterns (stack overflow markers, serialized Java objects in requests).

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Dark Web Leak Site Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states ShinyHunters 'shared an archive of allegedly stolen documents...posted on their dark web leak site'—data staging and dark web exfiltration phase has no detection rule despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect staging and uploading of bulk archives: monitor for large .zip, .tar.gz, or .rar file creation on internal systems followed by outbound transfer to Tor exit nodes, known dark web marketplace IPs, or through anonymization proxies. Alert on archive creation containing student/financial PII keywords.

suggestion.title: Configuration-Dependent Exploitation Success Rate Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article notes ShinyHunters stated 'the attack is not working on all systems, likely because successful exploitation depends on each instance's configuration'—vulnerability maturity and exploit reliability variation; opportunity for config-based risk scoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Score PeopleSoft instances by exploitation likelihood based on configuration: flag instances with known vulnerable versions, outdated patches, disabled security filters, or exposed endpoints. Correlate exploitation attempts against config baseline—successful compromises should trigger re-audit of all similarly-configured instances.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Postinstall Script Execution During Install
suggestion.rationale: Article URL explicitly references 'block-postinstall', confirming postinstall scripts are the attack vector. Threat actors abuse postinstall execution hooks to run arbitrary code during 'npm install'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install / npm ci spawns unexpected child processes (bash, powershell, cmd) with network connections, file writes to system paths, or credential-access attempts. Baseline legitimate postinstall in environment and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Introduction via package.json Modification
suggestion.rationale: npm security article discussing supply-chain improvements implies threat actors are exploiting package.json/lock-file modification to inject malicious dependencies, a known T1195.001 pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file integrity on package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, especially in CI/CD. Alert on unexpected edits introducing new packages from unknown publishers, or dependency version changes outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Anomaly or Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article topic (npm v12 security) strongly suggests threat actors target npm registry/metadata as attack surface. Expected discussion of how malicious packages evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to registry.npmjs.org for unusual patterns: rapid package pulls, mismatched versions between manifest and actual download, pulls from non-standard registries, or requests with credential-stuffing patterns.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Untrusted or Typosquatted Source
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via npm commonly leverage typosquatting or private registries. Article's high severity and 'biggest security improvements' framing suggests this is an active, widespread threat pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package installations from unknown/unapproved registries or packages with names that closely resemble legitimate popular packages (edit distance, homoglyph variants). Cross-check declared publisher against expected maintainer metadata.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER malware execution and registration
suggestion.rationale: Article title names SPECTRALVIPER as the primary malware payload in OceanLotus attack; pipeline extracted no malware-related use cases or IOCs despite clear presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SPECTRALVIPER process launches, DLL injection patterns, or command-line activity consistent with known OceanLotus deployment techniques. Track network connections from infected hosts to known C2 infrastructure associated with FireAnt campaign.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus spear-phishing and initial access to investor organizations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting of Vietnam investors; typical OceanLotus initial vector is spear-phishing with malicious documents. No initial-access or credential-access use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails targeting investment sector with attachments matching OceanLotus decoys (government/regulatory-themed documents in Vietnamese). Monitor for suspicious Office macro execution or embedded scripts from external emails.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement within investor networks post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: FireAnt campaign name and investor targeting implies multi-stage intrusion. No lateral-movement or discovery phase use cases generated despite these being core OceanLotus TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pass-the-hash, SMB scanning, or RDP lateral movement from initially compromised investor workstations. Track network reconnaissance activity (net view, ipconfig, arp commands) consistent with OceanLotus post-compromise enumeration.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration from investment firm networks
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus targeting investors suggests financial/intelligence collection objective. No exfiltration-phase use cases generated despite being the likely campaign goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data transfers to non-business IP ranges, compression of investment data files (.zip, .rar), or direct exfiltration via HTTPS tunneling to infrastructure associated with OceanLotus C2 nodes.

suggestion.title: HTTP exploitation attempts against PeopleSoft Updates Environment Management endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'critical remote code execution vulnerability' in 'Updates Environment Management component'—must detect HTTP/HTTPS requests with exploitation payloads targeting those endpoints, which are the attack surface for T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to PeopleSoft instances for HTTP requests to vulnerable component paths (updates, environment-config, admin console URIs) with anomalous payload sizes, command-injection/SQL-injection signatures, or rapid error-response patterns. Correlate with host-side process and file-system events immediately following failed vs. successful requests.

suggestion.title: Unexpected process spawning from PeopleSoft application processes post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE by definition enables arbitrary command execution on the target. Detection must cover shell processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) spawned from PeopleSoft runtime processes (PSADMIN, PSJVM, psae) following or concurrent with exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where ParentImage contains PeopleSoft-specific strings (jvm, PSADMIN, psae) and spawns command-shell or scripting interpreters. Baseline known administrative maintenance tasks and trigger on unknown child processes, encoded commands, or network-access child processes.

suggestion.title: Application error-rate spikes and exceptions in PeopleSoft Updates Environment Management logs
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts against the vulnerable component (article specifies 'Updates Environment Management') generate application exceptions and HTTP error responses. These are the signals of attack progression before successful code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application logs and web-server access logs for error-rate spikes (500/502 responses, stack traces, null-pointer or buffer-overflow exceptions) from the Updates Environment Management component, especially when preceded by inbound requests with suspicious parameters, oversized payloads, or encoding anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized file modifications in PeopleSoft application and configuration directories
suggestion.rationale: Following successful RCE, attackers stage payloads, inject backdoors, or modify startup/configuration files for persistence. Article describes 'critical RCE'—file-integrity monitoring on /PS_HOME is essential for detection of post-exploitation footprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized writes to /PS_HOME/appserv, /PS_HOME/webserv, PeopleSoft configuration directories, and startup-script paths. Flag modifications to .jar, .class, .properties, startup scripts, or web.xml files outside of scheduled patch windows or not sourced from configuration-management systems.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement and reconnaissance activity from exploited PeopleSoft server
suggestion.rationale: The article's 'critical' and 'urgent remediation' language indicates the vulnerability poses broad enterprise risk—attackers gaining RCE on PeopleSoft (which often manages HR, finance, or supply-chain data) will conduct network discovery and lateral movement to databases or other assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from the PeopleSoft application server for port-scanning, enumeration of database ports (1433, 3306, 5432, 27017), or lateral-movement protocols (RDP, SSH, SMB) not in baseline traffic. Correlate with unexpected process spawning (net.exe, nmap, credential-dumping tools) on the compromised host.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'authentication bypass + RCE' — pipeline missed execution phase detection. Post-auth code execution is the core attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uncommon PHP interpreters spawning child processes post-authentication, or web-server processes executing system commands. Look for php-cgi, php-fpm executing /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or command-injection patterns within httpd/apache/nginx context.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload to phpBB Directory
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability implies file upload or code injection — no use case covers artifact staging. Pipeline missed persistence/execution pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php, .phtml, .phar file creation in phpBB root, cache, upload directories, or temp paths post-exploitation window. Correlate with auth logs showing activity from unexpected accounts or IPs.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Database Access from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass requires credential harvesting or direct DB manipulation — pipeline omitted credential access / data exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web-server process (apache, nginx) initiating direct SQL connections outside expected application flow, or querying admin/user tables with unusual WHERE clauses (e.g., blanking password_algorithm, elevating user role).

suggestion.title: Mass Account Creation or Privilege Escalation Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'authentication bypass' — typical next step is creating backdoor admin accounts. Pipeline did not surface post-compromise privilege escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB user/admin tables for rapid INSERT/UPDATE of new high-privilege users, especially with timestamps clustering post-breach. Alert on admin-panel access from non-standard geographies or user-agents immediately after auth-bypass window.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Vulnerable phpBB Installation Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass typically exploits specific endpoint or parameter. Article establishes 'critical vulnerability' but pipeline missed initial-access HTTP-level indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to known vulnerable phpBB endpoints (e.g., auth-related paths, session-handling routes) with suspicious parameter patterns, encoding attempts, or multi-stage payload patterns. Baseline on phpBB version detection via Server header or config.php disclosure.

suggestion.title: Detect JDY Botnet C2 Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes multi-thousand-device botnet coordination requirement—'Expands to 1,500+ Devices'—mandating C2 infrastructure, yet pipeline extracted zero callback signatures or C2 indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic outbound connections from hosts to JDY C2 infrastructure; botnets typically beacon at 5-min to hourly intervals. Flag connections to China-geolocated ASNs or historically compromised Chinese infrastructure. Correlate DNS resolution of malware domains with follow-on process execution and data exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Reconnaissance Tool Execution from Botnet Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'Cyber Reconnaissance' as botnet objective: 'for Cyber Reconnaissance' clearly establishes discovery/enumeration as kill-chain phase, but pipeline generated zero detection rules for recon tool deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequential execution of discovery utilities (systeminfo, ipconfig, net.exe, whoami, nslookup, tasklist) from hosts with established JDY C2 callbacks. High-confidence pattern: recon command execution → immediate callback to C2 with encoded output → repeat cycle. Deduplicate on per-host basis to avoid alert fatigue.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Device Enrollment and Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Scale indicator 'Expands to 1,500+ Devices' implies active propagation vector; pipeline failed to generate initial-access or propagation detections: article phrase establishes ongoing recruitment of new botnet members.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For newly enrolled hosts: detect initial compromise vector (phishing attachment execution, drive-by download, malicious update). Signature: suspicious process launch from unexpected source → anomalous outbound connection → C2 callback establishment within 30 minutes. Flag hosts transitioning from clean baseline to active C2 state within 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: Detect Persistence Mechanisms on Botnet-Infected Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Maintaining 1,500+ device botnet across time requires persistence installation; article specifies scale/expansion implying long-term control, but pipeline generated zero detection for startup modification, scheduled tasks, or service abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of HKCU/HKLM Run registry keys with suspicious executables, new Windows services spawning from svchost.exe with uncommon parent-child relationships, and scheduled tasks named to masquerade as system utilities. High-fidelity when modifications appear post-C2 callback and target temp/appdata folders.

suggestion.title: Compromised Rust Crate Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'onering' crate is compromised; pipeline extracted no IOC for the package name or version range. Should alert on installation of affected 'onering' versions from crates.io or transitive dependency pulls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for `cargo add onering` or `cargo build` dependency resolution pulling the compromised crate versions. Correlate with project manifest changes. Alert on installations of onering prior to patch release date.

suggestion.title: Code Exfiltration via Rust Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code exfiltration; no use case generated for detecting outbound exfiltration from build pipeline. The malicious crate likely triggers data collection and C2 callbacks during compilation or runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous outbound connections initiated by cargo, rustc, or processes spawned during Rust builds. Look for connections to non-standard ports, unrecognized domains, or data exfiltration patterns (large POST requests, DNS tunneling).

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates crate registry compromise; pipeline missed registry-level IOCs. Should detect version injection, checksum mismatches, or timing anomalies in crate.io releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on crate 'onering' version releases with short time deltas to previous versions, missing provenance metadata, or Cargo.lock hash mismatches between crates.io and local cache.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency in Build Graph
suggestion.rationale: No use case for transitive dependency tracking. Projects importing libraries that depend on 'onering' are also exposed; pipeline missed this lateral impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan dependency trees (via `cargo tree --all` or `Cargo.lock`) for presence of compromised 'onering' package either directly or transitively. Flag all projects with any path to the malicious crate.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution in Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Rust crates can execute arbitrary code in build.rs; article references 'code exfiltration' suggesting custom build scripts. Pipeline did not surface T1027 (obfuscation) or build-script inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect build.rs, build dependencies, and proc-macro crates for encoded/obfuscated strings, network calls, or file I/O operations. Alert on build scripts invoking curl, wget, or shell commands with base64/hex encoding.

suggestion.title: Registry Poisoning Recovery Verification
suggestion.rationale: After patching, pipeline should verify removal/quarantine of malicious versions. No use case for post-incident validation or attestation checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify that affected 'onering' versions are yanked from crates.io, pulled projects have upgraded to patched versions, and no lingering references exist in lock files or build caches.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery via Hardcoded Secret 'random'
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery' and specifies 'template default shipped to all users' in dev.env line 10; detection of JWTs validated against the known hardcoded secret or bearing anomalous far-future expiration claims (>365 days) is the core exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for JWT tokens in Authorization headers that either validate against the hardcoded secret 'random' or contain exp claims extending >365 days into the future. Correlate successful token usage with subsequent access to `/api/v1/*` endpoints from untrusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Admin Endpoint Access with Far-Future JWT Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies explicit hunt: 'Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints with extreme far-future JWT' and lists protected endpoints `/api/v1/admin/users`, `/api/v1/me`, `/api/v1/token/refresh`; HTTP 200 responses to these endpoints from non-admin sources with anomalous token lifetimes indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful (HTTP 200) access to `/api/v1/admin/users`, `/api/v1/me`, or `/api/v1/token/refresh` endpoints from IP ranges outside whitelisted admin subnets or unexpected user-agent strings. Decode JWT claims and flag tokens with exp >365 days or iss values matching go-base boilerplate patterns.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Exposure in Configuration File Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability root: '`dev.env` | 10 | `AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random` — template default shipped to all users'; detection of .env or config files containing `AUTH_JWT_SECRET=` committed to version control or exfiltrated blocks the credential-discovery phase upstream of token forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits of .env, dev.env, config.yml, or similar configuration files to public or private version control systems; alert on process creation where git, npm, or rsync read files matching `.*\.env.*` patterns. Flag file uploads to unauthenticated sharing services containing `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` or `SECRET_KEY` assignment patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious protocolMessage processing in Baileys
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'sent a malicious payload via the placeholderResendMessage' — detection should target exception handling, parsing failures, or unusual message envelope attributes that trigger the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Node.js processes (npm-installed Baileys apps) exhibiting exception patterns when processing WhatsApp protocol messages. Monitor for protocolMessage deserialization failures, unexpected exception rates in Baileys stack frames, or abnormal message envelope sizes. Correlate with network ingress from unexpected WhatsApp protocol sources.

suggestion.title: Message spoofing authenticity failures in Baileys consumer
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'trigger a fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload. This allows anyone to spoof messages.' — apps using Baileys should fail message signature/MAC verification or exhibit impossible message origin chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys-dependent applications (WhatsApp bots, bridges, automation scripts) for sudden message influx from unexpected sources or message timestamps incompatible with session history. Detect rapid upsert event generation without corresponding network inbound flow. Flag message events where sender identity diverges from historical roster.

suggestion.title: Baileys app-state sync corruption or rollback
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key...' — attackers can poison Baileys' state synchronization, causing chat/contact state divergence or data loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Baileys state file mutations (typically in .wwebjs_cache/ or similar directories). Detect state rollback patterns, state file rewrites outside normal sync intervals, or state corruption indicators (missing conversation threads, contact list resets). Correlate with app-state sync process restarts or exceptions.

suggestion.title: Node.js process execution with vulnerable Baileys version in memory
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Any baileys session under the latest version (< 7.0.0-rc12, and < 6.7.22)' — runtime detection of vulnerable code paths executing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js process spawns with --require or module-load patterns that load Baileys directly from vulnerable package directories. Cross-reference package-lock.json or node_modules metadata against known vulnerable version ranges. Flag processes running from vulnerable dependency trees.

suggestion.title: Unexpected network traffic from Baileys protocol handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes WhatsApp protocol message processing; unusual network flows from Baileys apps may indicate payload exfiltration or C2 channeling via spoofed messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes hosting Baileys for network connections to non-WhatsApp infrastructure. Flag high-frequency or large-volume outbound traffic that correlates with message upsert spikes. Detect connection attempts to known C2 domains or IP ranges where message spoofing could tunnel commands.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Vulnerable Version Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Ivanti...Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities'—organizations require baseline detection of vulnerable Ivanti product versions before patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Ivanti product versions (Connect Secure, Policy Secure, etc.) across inventory. Alert on version numbers matching known vulnerable ranges. Cross-reference with patch management systems to identify unpatched assets at exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Vulnerable Firmware Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Fortinet...Release Patches'—FortiGate and related appliances are perimeter-facing, high-value targets. Version detection is critical for vulnerability tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet product firmware versions via SNMP, management interface interrogation, or inventory tools. Alert on vulnerable firmware versions. Correlate with exploit-in-the-wild indicators and suspicious management access logs.

suggestion.title: SAP Vulnerable Version Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article includes 'SAP Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities'—SAP systems process sensitive business/financial data and require proactive vulnerability posture assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SAP kernel and component versions via system inventory or change logs. Alert on versions matching published CVE vulnerability ranges. Flag systems in production without corresponding patch deployment records.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt - Critical Vendor Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities' in network/application infrastructure vendors. Exploitation attempts on these products would generate high-fidelity indicators before patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP management/application interfaces for exploitation signatures: unusual parameter encoding, directory traversal patterns, SQL injection attempts, XXE payloads, or known CVE-specific proof-of-concept request patterns.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Process Spawning Interactive Shell with SYSTEM Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'grants SYSTEM access.' Core detection gap: child process spawning from Defender services with IntegrityLevel escalation or parent-child privilege boundary violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or svchost.exe spawned from MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe, or WdFilter.sys-linked processes with IntegrityLevel=System or TokenElevationType indicating impersonation of privileged tokens.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Service Crash Preceding Privilege Escalation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Zero-days exploiting Defender typically trigger crashes or abnormal terminations as part of the exploitation sequence. Article describes active exploit scenario; detect crash + escalation correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate MsMpEng.exe termination (exit code != 0) or restarts with subsequent SYSTEM-level process creation or network outbound connections within 3-minute window; flag especially if elevated process lacks legitimate parent.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Registry or File Access by Defender Components
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation from Defender's execution context often involves persistence attempts or configuration tampering. Article indicates post-exploitation SYSTEM access; detect registry writes to boot/service hives from Defender.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services, HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, or HKLM\Software\Policies originating from Defender-linked PIDs or SYSTEM-context child processes with Defender as ancestor.

suggestion.title: Defender Real-Time Protection Engine Disabled or Bypassed via Exploit Path
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of Defender typically results in defense evasion: disabling real-time scanning, quarantine bypass, or signature tampering. Article describes an active exploit; detect defensive controls being compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection and quarantine directory (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine) for unexpected modifications or deletions; correlate with Defender process execution.

suggestion.title: Defender Update/Download Service Fetching Unexpected Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'updated Windows'—suggests Defender update mechanism is attack surface. Detect anomalous network behavior from Defender update processes or unexpected file downloads in Defender cache.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual outbound connections from MsMpEng.exe, WinDefend.exe, or update-related processes to non-Microsoft CDNs or IPs; detect file writes to %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender or %Temp% with suspicious entropy or signatures.

suggestion.title: Token Impersonation or Delegation from Defender Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation mechanics in modern Defender exploits often involve token-stealing or impersonation. Article outcome (SYSTEM access) implies token manipulation; detect impersonation of high-integrity tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ImpersonateLoggedOnUser or token duplication calls originating from Defender-linked PIDs; alert on SYSTEM token impersonation attempts or duplicate handle requests targeting System account.

suggestion.title: OWA XSS Payload in Email Content
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers send 'specially crafted email' with 'arbitrary JavaScript' executed in 'browser context.' Pipeline missed obvious email gateway detection rule for malicious script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Exchange transport logs and email gateway logs for MIME parts or message bodies containing <script>, javascript:, onerror=, onload=, or other XSS payloads in emails destined for OWA users. Focus on messages triggering Exchange anti-XSS filtering or arriving from external senders.

suggestion.title: Exchange Server CVE-2026-42897 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacks are happening in the wild via OWA. Monitor OWA access logs and HTTP request logs for exploitation patterns targeting the specific code path affected by this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search OWA IIS logs (W3SVC) for suspicious GET/POST requests to OWA endpoints with base64-encoded or URL-encoded payloads in query strings or POST bodies. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses followed by unusual script execution or session hijacking indicators.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Exchange Server Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-42897 affects Exchange 2016, 2019, and SE. Detection infrastructure should track deployed versions and alert when vulnerable versions are discovered post-patch deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Exchange Server versions via WMI (Get-ExchangeServer cmdlet output), SCCM, or Sentinel asset inventory. Alert if any instance running 2016, 2019, or SE remains unpatched after June 2026 patch Tuesday deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Execution in OWA Session Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states JavaScript executes 'in the browser context' of OWA users. Behavioral detection should catch script execution anomalies within OWA iframe or session sandbox.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual PowerShell or WScript.exe execution spawned from rundll32.exe (common XSS to RCE vector) or detect script debugging API calls from browser processes (mshtml.dll, jscript.dll) combined with suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service (EEMS) Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Microsoft deployed temporary mitigations via EEMS in mid-May. Detection should identify exploit attempts that specifically bypass or trigger EEMS WAF rules, indicating targeted/advanced threat behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Exchange FrontEnd and HttpProxy logs for requests triggering EEMS mitigation actions (HTTP 403 responses, blocked by 'EMSRules' header) followed within seconds by retry attempts using modified parameters, URL encoding obfuscation, or alternate payload encodings.

suggestion.title: Critical Microsoft RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'critical RCE bugs' and 'three zero-days' without mapping any behavioral detections. RCE vulnerabilities in widely-used Microsoft products demand immediate post-patch exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal child process spawning from Microsoft application contexts (Office, Exchange, Edge, Outlook) in the 48–72 hours post-patch release. Prioritize system utility spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, regsvcs.exe) from document-handling or network-facing processes. Correlate with patch status to identify exploitation of unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Unpatched System Vulnerability Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article states 206 flaws patched, implying large-scale inventory reconciliation required. Pipeline missed detection for systems remaining unpatched post-release, a critical defense gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Windows Update/WSUS logs 14+ days post-patch release for systems with failed patch installations or OS versions prior to the patched build. Cross-reference with network scan data to identify exposed, unpatched systems still accepting connections on vulnerable services.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Active Exploitation Behavioral Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'three zero-days' but pipeline failed to model zero-day-specific detection patterns. Zero-days are exploited in the wild before patch availability; behavioral heuristics must apply even without CVE identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual process spawning, code injection, or privilege escalation chains originating from Microsoft Office, Exchange, or Edge processes within 72 hours of patch release. Flag exploitation patterns in sandboxes or EDR that predate public CVE disclosure. Correlate email/web delivery with downstream suspicious execution.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Cascade Risk from Mixed-Severity Flaws
suggestion.rationale: 206 flaws in one patch cycle suggests chaining opportunities: low-severity flaws paired with RCE bugs to bypass mitigations. Pipeline did not model multi-stage exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attack sequences combining non-RCE flaws (e.g., info disclosure, DLL hijacking) with RCE flaws within the same incident timeline. Example: Office code execution → Windows kernel flaw escalation. Flag unusual process token elevation or UAC bypass patterns from Microsoft application contexts.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Lag Window Exploitation Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'record 206 flaws' indicating deployment complexity and lag risk. Pipeline missed detection for systems exploited during patch delay period.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Calculate time-to-patch for high-risk systems post-release. Correlate systems unpatched 30+ days after critical RCE CVE release with incident alerts in the same timeframe. Flag patch failures, deferred updates, or manual patch blocklisting as defense evasion indicators.

suggestion.title: Patch Metadata Harvesting and Targeted Exploit Development
suggestion.rationale: 206 flaws released simultaneously increases threat actor focus on patch reverse-engineering and zero-day variant creation. Pipeline did not map threat-actor repositioning intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor underground forums, paste sites, and VirusTotal submissions for early proof-of-concept uploads targeting the 206 flaws or derivative techniques. Track exploit-kit vendor activity, kit builders, and packers post-patch release. Flag infrastructure pivots or malware recompilation tied to the vulnerability cohort.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters IP - PeopleSoft SSH Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes SSH-based lateral movement from attacker IPs to PeopleSoft systems using service accounts: 'the script attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH authentication from ShinyHunters IP range (142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) to PeopleSoft systems targeting accounts psoft, oracle, linuxadm. Correlate failed password auth followed by successful key-based auth as fallback exploitation pattern.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft Service Account Credential Spray
suggestion.rationale: Article describes enumeration of known service accounts: 'script attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid SSH login attempts targeting psoft, oracle, linuxadm accounts from single source IP within short window. Surface pattern of multiple failed password attempts followed by successful key-based auth as compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note File Creation - PeopleSoft Directories
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise activity: 'Once connected, the script drops the ransom note into directories associated with PeopleSoft web and application servers' named 'README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation matching README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS*.TXT pattern in PeopleSoft application/web directories. Correlate with unauthorized bash/shell script execution and successful prior SSH authentication from attacker IP.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Agent Deployment - PeopleSoft Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article documents attacker infrastructure: 'exposed several directories revealing ongoing targeting of PeopleSoft environments. Also visible were staging materials, including MeshCentral agents'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshCentral binary execution, msiexec deployment, or powershell invocations matching agent install patterns. Monitor for C2 domains/IPs associated with MeshCentral infrastructure during PeopleSoft maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Host Discovery via /etc/hosts Parsing
suggestion.rationale: Attack methodology explicitly documented: 'The script parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems and attempts to connect to them over SSH'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes (cat, grep, awk, sed) accessing /etc/hosts immediately followed by SSH connection attempts to non-standard ports or high-volume parallel connections. Pattern: read hosts file → network enumeration.

suggestion.title: Exploit Chain - Gadget Vulnerability on PeopleSoft
suggestion.rationale: Initial access vector: 'ShinyHunters says they are using a "gadget chain" of old and zero-day vulnerabilities to conduct the attacks'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft instance logs for serialized object deserialization attempts, ClassPathXmlApplicationContext instantiation, or unusual Java method invocations. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to same targets within hours.

suggestion.title: Langflow Path Traversal in File Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences (../).'
