This is an explicit, exploitable attack pattern with clear detection signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/v2/files for filename parameters containing path traversal sequences (../, .., \..\) or attempts to write outside expected upload directories. Log the full multipart request body including filename, source IP, and User-Agent to correlate with honeypot findings of 'test file' drops.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Session Token Creation in Langflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token.' This is a precondition for exploitation that should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect session or authentication tokens issued from requests to /api/v2/files or related endpoints that lack authentication headers or pre-existing session tokens. Flag when tokens are minted for previously-unseen source IPs or from automated/scripted User-Agents within short time windows (batch token generation).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write via Langflow Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances' and describes capability to 'write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.' This should be detected via file integrity monitoring or endpoint logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/write events on Langflow servers for files created outside standard upload directories (e.g., outside /uploads or /data). Correlate with POST /api/v2/files requests. Flag writes to system directories, web-accessible directories, or files with executable extensions (.sh, .exe, .jsp, .php) dropped via the upload API.

suggestion.title: Mass Exploitation of Publicly-Exposed Langflow Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Censys scans identified roughly 7,000 publicly exposed Langflow instances' and VulnCheck honeypots detected active exploitation. Organizations should detect reconnaissance and exploitation of their own Langflow deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple requests from single source IP to /api/v2/files endpoint across multiple Langflow instances or within a short time window (< 5 min). Monitor for requests with identical or similar path traversal payloads to multiple servers. Alert on successful HTTP 200/201 responses to file upload attempts with suspicious filenames.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Cloud & CI/CD Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores'—no detection use case generated for this attack vector despite being central to the worm's propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious access to credential stores (.aws/credentials, .kube/config, ~/.ssh, password manager sockets). Detect unusual file reads in home directories targeting known credential locations, particularly when followed by environment variable enumeration or network access to package registries (npm, PyPI, RubyGems).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Repository Activity from Compromised Developer Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'leaked the source code...via numerous compromised developer accounts' in repos named 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release'—no use case for detecting bulk malicious repository activity or mass source-code dumps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub account activity anomalies: multiple repository creations or bulk modifications within short windows, commits containing source-code dumps or malware artifacts, or repository initialization patterns matching 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' naming convention. Correlate with geographically impossible logins or API token generation.

suggestion.title: Dead-Man Switch Persistence & Destructive Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'dead-man switch' installed via systemd user service or LaunchAgent that 'monitors the token's validity every minute' and 'executes a destructive command (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents)'—both persistence and impact mechanisms with no corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of systemd user services or LaunchAgent plist files in user home directories with names or logic referencing token validation or credential monitoring. Correlate with execution of recursive rm -rf commands targeting home and Documents directories by systemd or LaunchAgent processes running in user context.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Package Upload to Public Registries
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'compromises legitimate repositories and packages, publishing trojanized versions' to npm, PyPI, RubyGems—yet no use case for detecting unauthorized package uploads or modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous package uploads to npm, PyPI, RubyGems from known compromised developer accounts: uploads from unusual geographies, off-hours activity, modified package.json/setup.py, or packages containing obfuscated JavaScript or encrypted payloads consistent with multi-stage build pipeline characteristics.

suggestion.title: AI Development Tool Configuration Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions malware 'poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline'—a clear detection gap for unauthorized config file modifications in .claude/, .gemini/, .cursor/ directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor developer machines for suspicious file modifications in .claude, .gemini, .cursor, .copilot, .kiro, or .cline configuration directories. Alert on creation or modification of config files that redirect API endpoints, inject authentication credentials, or alter tool behavior, especially when correlated with prior credential access or package repository write events.

suggestion.title: SSH Key Theft & Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM)' using stolen credentials, but no detection use case for SSH key abuse or SSM session hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections from compromised developer accounts to infrastructure targets, particularly when SSH keys are accessed from .ssh/ directories or private key materials are read by unexpected processes. Correlate with AWS Systems Manager Session Manager abuse (StartSession API calls) without corresponding MFA challenges or cross-account role assumption.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Langflow API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE' in title, indicating authentication bypass or public-facing API exploitation. This is the initial-access vector that must be detectable before code execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated or anomalous HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints (/api/, /flow/, /execute) from external sources without valid authentication tokens. Flag 401-to-200 transitions (auth bypass attempts followed by success) or direct code-execution endpoint hits without prior session establishment.

suggestion.title: Langflow Process Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Unauthenticated RCE'—implies arbitrary code execution within Langflow's application context. Article phrase 'Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE' establishes execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Langflow service (langflow.py, langflow_server, or equivalent), especially with command-line arguments containing code interpretation (python -c, bash -c, cmd /c). High signal if spawned process is network-aware (curl, wget, nc, powershell).

suggestion.title: Langflow Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities typically lead to command-and-control callbacks. Article title 'Exploited' suggests attackers gain shell access and would exfiltrate or maintain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Langflow service initiating outbound connections to non-whitelisted IPs/domains, especially over uncommon ports (4444, 5555, 8888, high-numbered ephemeral ranges). Correlate with process execution events showing shell or interpreter activity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Langflow Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw'—inventory and version checking are prerequisite detections. Cite: 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of Langflow deployments and their versions via asset scans or application server metadata. Alert on presence of Langflow < [patched version] (when disclosed). Correlate with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Langflow Endpoint Error/Exception Spike
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts against a vulnerability often generate error logs, HTTP 500s, or exception stack traces before successful RCE. Pipeline did not capture precursor detection signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of HTTP 500, 502, 503 responses or Python/Java stack trace errors from Langflow endpoints. Alert on spike in errors correlating with HTTP requests to specific vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /api/flows/execute, /api/chat). Combine with authentication logs to separate legitimate issues from exploitation.

suggestion.title: Python HTTP framework process spawning child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated HTTP MCP Tool Execution' implying HTTP framework (uvicorn/gunicorn) spawning MCP tool subprocesses. No detection hunts for abnormal process lineage: python.exe/uvicorn/gunicorn → child process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for python.exe, uvicorn.exe, or gunicorn spawning children with short lifetimes or uncommon names immediately after HTTP listen events. MCP tool execution implies process invocation triggered by remote HTTP request, not normal long-running daemon behavior.

suggestion.title: meta-ads-mcp package installation and startup
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names vulnerable package (pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp ≤1.0.101). Need to detect when this specific package is installed (pip/npm install, git clone) and started, independent of CVE scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git clone operations against pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp repository, pip/npm install commands for meta-ads-mcp, or startup of uvicorn/gunicorn with this package in PYTHONPATH. Establishes baseline for vulnerable deployment even before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated requests to Python web framework internal endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CWE-287 (improper authentication) and unauthenticated HTTP POST to /mcp. Need detection for requests lacking Authorization headers to endpoints that *should* require them (inferred from response 200 on unauth POST).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP POST requests to /mcp endpoint without Authorization/X-API-Key headers receiving successful (2xx) responses. Compare against baseline of normal authenticated requests; missing auth headers to sensitive endpoints indicates bypassable auth.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration: access_token parameter in outbound URLs (refined)
suggestion.rationale: UC_14_4 covers Meta Graph API tokens, but article implies *any* MCP tool could exfil credentials via query string. Broaden detection to detect auth tokens in URL parameters to *any* external domain, not just graph.facebook.com.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound HTTP/HTTPS with access_token=, api_key=, token=, or credential= in URL query string to non-internal destinations. Flag if RemoteUrl contains common token parameter names and RemoteIP resolves to cloud/SaaS provider.

suggestion.title: Abnormal requests to meta-ads-mcp HTTP listen port from untrusted networks
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates MCP tool listens on HTTP (TCP 8080). Detect when this port receives traffic from IPs outside expected developer/staging networks, indicating external reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connections to TCP 8080 from public IP ranges where meta-ads-mcp is running, especially if traffic patterns include HTTP POST to /mcp path. Correlate with absence of VPN/proxy headers.

suggestion.title: Meta API token format in process memory or command-line arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates token exfil via query strings; prior step is token residing in process memory. Detect Meta API tokens (bearer token formats) in Processes.command_line, environmental variables, or file contents post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Regex-match Meta API token patterns (bearer tokens with specific prefix/length) in process command lines, file contents written by uvicorn/python processes, or log files generated by the MCP tool. High-confidence indicator of active token theft.

suggestion.title: Webserver process writes executable to upload directory with mismatched declared vs. detected extension
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'uploaded file named `shell.php` containing GIF-like content could pass validation' because MIME-type checking bypassed extension validation. No hunt in pipeline output captures detection of polyglot files where filename extension diverges from MIME-detected extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation events from webserver processes (php-fpm, httpd, nginx, w3wp, caddy) in upload-style directories where the declared filename has executable extensions (.php, .phar, etc.) but content analysis or MIME detection suggests image types. Correlate file creation timestamp with subsequent HTTP access to that path.

suggestion.title: CodeIgniter4 ext_in rule validation: HTTP multipart upload with image MIME but executable extension
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names the vulnerable rule 'ext_in[avatar,gif]' — request-level detection should look for multipart uploads declaring image Content-Type while uploading files with PHP/shell extensions, the exact bypass condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/multipart requests to upload endpoints with Content-Type: image/* (or similar) but filename extension matching PHP/PHAR variants. Particularly suspicious if followed by access to that uploaded file via HTTP GET within minutes.

suggestion.title: Reverse engineering / re-verification of validation rule state post-upload
suggestion.rationale: Defenders should audit CodeIgniter4 configurations for `ext_in` rules that reference MIME-guessed extensions rather than declared filenames. Article narrative makes clear the root cause: 'checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Code-level audit of upload validation rules: scan CodeIgniter4 applications for `ext_in` validation rules and verify they operate on the declared filename extension, not MIME-type-guessed extension. Compare application code against CVE-2026-48062 patch to confirm fix is applied.

suggestion.title: Suspicious postinstall script execution during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states npm's attack vector: 'automatic execution of installation scripts by default.' Pipeline missed the core npm-specific threat: malicious actors embed code in 'postinstall' or 'preinstall' hooks in package.json that execute during `npm install`. The article narrative centers on this mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install spawning unexpected child processes (non-node, non-gyp) or writing to sensitive directories. Monitor for postinstall/preinstall hook execution outside node_modules context. Alert on npm processes with suspicious environment variables (_INSIDE_HOOK) or network outbound from npm child processes.

suggestion.title: Package.json manifest with unusual script directives
suggestion.rationale: The article's vulnerability is that npm scripts (preinstall, postinstall, preuninstall, prepare) execute arbitrary shell code. This UC should detect package manifests with suspicious script content before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package.json files with postinstall/preinstall scripts containing: encoded payloads (base64, hex), outbound network commands (curl, wget, powershell, bash -c), archive extraction (tar, unzip), or spawning shell interpreters. Look for obfuscation (hex escapes, variable expansion, command substitution).

suggestion.title: Npm registry pull of multiple package versions within short window
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often involve typosquatting or version confusion. Article mentions npm as supply chain vector; detections should cover pre-exploitation package acquisition phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single host pulling multiple versions of the same package (potential version pinning test), pulling deprecated/old versions, or pulling packages with names similar to popular libraries within same session.

suggestion.title: npm Install Script Execution (Post/Pre-Install Hook)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'npm install scripts' as supply-chain attack mechanism. Pipeline missed T1059.001 and T1195.001 execution detection despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/sh during install phase. Establish baseline of known-good post-install scripts by package; flag unsigned or unknown scripts executing with user/dev privileges. Monitor for scripts that shell-out immediately vs. legitimate build/compile operations.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Integrity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article frames npm supply-chain as attack surface; pipeline did not generate detection for package modifications, version substitution, or checksum mismatches. T1195.001 not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare downloaded package hashes/signatures against npm registry canonical values. Alert on new install-script fields in recent package versions or scripts added in patch/minor releases. Flag packages with version-downgrade requests or new maintainer takeovers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Child Process (Post-Install Reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: Malicious install scripts perform recon (whoami, systeminfo, env, uname). Pipeline did not detect this subprocess anomaly. Article context implies code-execution threat; reconnaissance follows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag node/npm child processes executing reconnaissance binaries: whoami, systeminfo, ipconfig, ifconfig, net user, uname, env, curl, wget. Alert on command-line captures of environment variables or credential-related API calls from npm context.

suggestion.title: npm Package Registry Access (Typosquatting / Alternative Registry)
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often rely on registry substitution or typosquatting. Article emphasizes npm ecosystem risk; pipeline should detect unusual registry access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/proxy logs for requests to alternative npm registries or lookalike domains (npmjs.io, npm-packages.com, etc.). Alert on bulk package-list queries or rapid downloads of packages not in corporate approved-list. Flag requests to non-standard registry endpoints.

suggestion.title: npm Install Script Writing to Startup/Persistence Paths
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain code execution can enable persistence. Pipeline missed T1543.003, T1547.014 as follow-on threat from malicious scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node process writing to Windows startup folder, run registry keys, or Unix rc files (.bashrc, .profile, cron, launchd). Flag any file-writes outside the package install directory that persist across session restarts or modify shell initialization.

suggestion.title: Non-browser process accessing browser credential stores
suggestion.rationale: Core attack pattern: article explicitly states Lumma, Vidar, StealC steal credentials from browsers. Should be foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-browser processes access Chrome/Edge Login Data, Firefox logins.json, or cookie stores. High signal when parent is Go executable or process resides in %TEMP%.

suggestion.title: Go executable with abnormally large PE overlay
suggestion.rationale: Article's defining evasion characteristic: 'Uses Massive PE Overlay.' Detecting Go binaries with overlay exceeding normal ratios is primary loader detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PE files with Go compilation markers where overlay size exceeds 50% of file size. Correlate with child process spawning or DLL loads from %TEMP%.

suggestion.title: Child process spawned by Go loader accessing credential databases
suggestion.rationale: Loader 'decodes and drops dangerous information-stealing programs.' Parent-child execution chain from GoFlateLoader to Lumma/Vidar/StealC is critical kill-chain node.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by Go-compiled executables that immediately access browser credential files. Parent-child relationship and target DB are key signals.

suggestion.title: Execution of known infostealer families (Lumma, Vidar, StealC)
suggestion.rationale: Three specific payload families named in article but no hash-based or behavioral detection provided. Should include IOC hunts and family-specific signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on hash matches for known Lumma/Vidar/StealC samples and behavioral signatures: Lumma API hooks, Vidar module enumeration, StealC browser DB scraping patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential exfiltration via HTTPS to suspicious infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Infostealers inevitably exfiltrate stolen credentials. Credential theft is described but no C2 or network-based detection provided; missing exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor infostealer processes for outbound HTTPS to rare/newly-registered domains with high-entropy URIs or POST requests containing encoded credential material.

suggestion.title: C2 traffic to SniperDz/PhaaS IOCs (Application Layer Protocol)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists domain IOCs (win.feezossl.xyz, sniperdz.com, etc.) but no use case detects T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) communication to them. Phase should focus on C2 beaconing post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS queries or HTTP(S) connections to branded PhaaS C2 domains. Filter for non-browser processes initiating connections to identified IOCs. Look for high-volume or periodic beacon patterns typical of PhaaS callback infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Social media phishing redirect chain (Facebook/Instagram landing)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'targeting victims across the Middle East and North Africa through social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram,' but all provided hunts assume email delivery. Need detection for social-media-initiated phishing flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users clicking social-media URLs (facebook.com, instagram.com referrers) that redirect through phishing infrastructure domains (aff.bnaoswhye.shop, raviral.com). Correlate to subsequent browser child-process execution. High false-positive risk requires URL category filtering and domain reputation scoring.

suggestion.title: Browser extension or homepage hijacking install
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Browser Hijacking' but no detection for browser modification. Article suggests PhaaS platform modifies browser settings for credential intercept. Should detect registry/config changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Main [Start Page], Chrome extension directories (LocalAppData\Google\Chrome\User Data), or Firefox profile changes. Correlate to prior phishing/Office execution chain. Watch for unsigned registry modifications from browser parent processes.

suggestion.title: DMG mount execution from user home directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'weaponized DMG files' and 'fake software installers' as delivery mechanism. Pipeline mapped zero Initial Access techniques despite article explicitly describing user deception into opening DMG mounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes executing from /Volumes/* (DMG mount points) without corresponding .dmg parent process or launched via OpenProcess from Finder. Focus on executable binaries masquerading as legitimate installers (names like 'Install.app', 'Setup.app', 'UpdateMacOS.app'). Correlate process launch time with recent user download and Finder file opens.

suggestion.title: Fake application masquerading by bundle identifier mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'disguised as legitimate apps' and 'fake software installers.' No UC addresses T1036 (Masquerading) despite this being core to social engineering attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for app bundle identifiers that don't match their executable names or code-signing certificates. Example: process claiming to be 'CleanMyMac' but with unsigned or third-party certificate. Correlate against macOS App Store bundle IDs. Alert on mismatches between process display name and actual binary path.

suggestion.title: macOS Keychain access from suspicious process tree (DMG-origin)
suggestion.rationale: Article targets macOS specifically, but current browser-stealer UC is Windows-only. macOS uses Keychain for credential storage, not %APPDATA% directories. Need Mac-native detection for 'Infostealer malware' accessing Keychain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-Safari, non-Chrome processes calling `security find-generic-password`, `security find-internet-password`, or accessing ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db directly. Correlate parent process chain back to /Volumes/* mount to link back to DMG execution. High fidelity if process is unsigned or signed by untrusted certificate.

suggestion.title: Network connections to high-volume generated-looking domains (infostealer C2)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 30+ domains with algorithmic/gibberish names (e.g., 'enslavculprit.digital', 'resilientlimb.icu', 'paralegalmustang.icu'). These indicate C2 beaconing but no UC maps T1071 or network IOC hunts to this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections from processes spawned from /Volumes/* to domains with high entropy names, unusual TLDs (.digital, .icu, .cfd, .cyou), or matching the 30 domains listed in IOCs. Flag DNS queries for these domains even if connection is blocked. Correlate with Keychain/browser-database process access to confirm data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: File hash match — malware executables embedded in DMG or dropped post-execution
suggestion.rationale: Four SHA256 hashes provided in article IOCs (9d2da07aa6e7..., 7ca42f1f23d..., etc.). No UC generated to hunt for these hashes at file creation, execution, or download time. Pipeline output shows empty IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, copy, or execution matching provided SHA256 hashes. Prioritize detection on files created in /Volumes/*, ~/Downloads, /tmp, or launched with parent=Finder. Include hash lookups at EDR ingest time to catch execution immediately.

suggestion.title: Python/shell script execution from DMG-mount context (post-exploitation scripting)
suggestion.rationale: Infostealer campaigns often use shell or Python scripts post-execution to enumerate and steal credentials. Article mentions 'Infostealer malware' but doesn't describe the post-execution mechanism—common pattern is shell script that enumerates browser caches and exfiltrates. No UC covers this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect /bin/bash, /bin/zsh, /usr/bin/python3, or script interpreters spawned by processes with parent in /Volumes/* or spawned shortly after DMG execution. Flag scripts that call keychain utilities, SQLite for browser databases, or curl/wget to exfiltration domains.

suggestion.title: Miasma/Hades Executable Detection by Hash or Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspicious Files'—implies specific file indicators and signatures exist for these malware families, but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or file-based detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or presence of files matching known Miasma or Hades signatures (MD5/SHA1/SHA256 hashes, file names, paths). Look for execution from unusual directories (Downloads, Temp, AppData, developer tool folders). Monitor for failed hash lookups followed by rapid execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Download in Developer Tool Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article scope is developer machines with file-based detection; typical attack chain for Miasma/Hades involves luring developers to download malicious installers or project files. 'Detect them on developer machines' implies download phase precedes execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables or archives downloaded to developer tool directories (node_modules, .git, vs projects, Python venvs, Maven cache). Flag executable downloads from non-CDN sources to developer home directories. Cross-reference with email metadata if available.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Dev Tool or Startup Folder Modification
suggestion.rationale: Malware on developer machines typically establishes persistence to maintain access across reboots. Article's 'spreading' language and developer-machine focus implies lateral persistence mechanisms, likely leveraging dev-tool startup hooks or Windows autorun locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Registry Run/RunOnce keys, Startup folder, and shell extension/handler modifications for dev tools (Visual Studio, VS Code, Git, npm, Python). Alert on unexpected .lnk (shortcut) creation or modification in startup paths. Track DLL injection into dev tool processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Attempt from Compromised Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: High-severity malware on a developer machine poses supply-chain risk—attackers pivot from dev environment to internal network or repositories. No kill-chain phase covers lateral movement, critical omission for dev-machine compromise scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH, RDP, or Git push/pull activity from compromised dev machine to non-standard targets. Alert on credential enumeration (whoami, net user, Get-LocalUser) followed by outbound connection attempts. Track code repository access anomalies (push to protected branches, new SSH keys added).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting on Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines store credentials (git tokens, API keys, SSH keys, source code repository access). Miasma/Hades on dev machines likely target credential harvesting for supply-chain attacks. No collection-phase use case present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on keylogging processes, clipboard access utilities, or file-access patterns targeting .ssh, .git, .aws, .azure folders or credential manager DBs. Monitor for grep/findstr commands searching for 'password', 'token', 'key' in source files or config directories.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Hidden Executable in Developer Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspicious Files' and 'Spreading Now' implies malware actively evading detection through obfuscation or hiding. Zero detection use cases address file-level evasion patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on double-extension files (.txt.exe, .pdf.scr), files in Hidden or System attributes within developer directories, renamed executables matching dev-tool names, or packed/signed-but-suspicious binaries. Monitor for deobfuscation or decoding activity preceding execution.

suggestion.title: Compromised installer spawning shell interpreters or living-off-land tools
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijacking a popular investment software platform' via supply chain. Backdoor delivered through compromised FireAnt installer requires execution of payload-launching utilities during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FireAnt-related installer processes (setup.exe, update.exe) for spawning PowerShell, cmd, rundll32, or regsvr32. Baseline legitimate update chains first; any deviation is high-confidence given supply chain compromise vector.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 callbacks to article-provided domains and IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deliver a powerful backdoor' with 8 C2 IP addresses and 6 command-and-control domains explicitly listed. No detection suggested for actual communications to these IOCs despite them being primary delivery artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any outbound connections from stock-investor machines to the 8 listed IPs or 6 domains. High-fidelity indicator; these are not common legitimate destinations for financial software.

suggestion.title: Process or file execution matching provided SHA1 IOC hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 20 SHA1 file hashes but pipeline generates no hash-based detection. Hashes represent the actual backdoor binaries delivered by the compromised installer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file hashes (SHA1) against the 20 provided indicators at process execution and file-write events. High specificity; any match is confirmed malware from this campaign.

suggestion.title: Registry or service persistence following backdoor installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes persistent 'powerful backdoor' but no persistence mechanism or post-installation artifacts are mentioned or hunted. Backdoors require startup hooks (registry, services, scheduled tasks, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In systems with prior execution of the SHA1-hashed files, look for subsequent writes to HKLM\..\Run registry keys, service installation, or scheduled task creation. Time-series: backdoor execution → persistence setup within minutes.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names SPECTRALVIPER malware as the attack payload; no execution-phase detection suggested despite this being the core technical IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with SPECTRALVIPER signatures, command-line patterns, or parent-child relationships consistent with loader→malware chains. Look for suspicious script interpretation (PowerShell, cmd.exe) with file-write or registry-modification actions targeting investor/finance verticals.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Phishing to Vietnam Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: Target profile (Vietnam investors) and threat actor (OceanLotus, known for spear-phishing via email) strongly imply initial-access vector never surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for emails with financial/investment-themed subjects, Vietnam-language content, or spoofed legitimate investment firm headers targeting known investor domains. Track attachment types and URLs typical of OceanLotus delivery (Office macros, LNK, ISO).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from SPECTRALVIPER
suggestion.rationale: APT campaign implies persistent C2 infrastructure; no command-and-control detection use case proposed despite being standard for attribution-level attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTP/HTTPS and DNS queries from infected endpoints (investor terminals) to known OceanLotus C2 domains or newly registered sinkhole/look-alike domains. Prioritize long-lived persistent connections with regular interval timing (beaconing).

suggestion.title: Financial Data Exfiltration to OceanLotus C2
suggestion.rationale: Investor targeting implies intent to steal financial data; exfiltration phase entirely absent from pipeline reconstruction despite being fundamental to APT32 operational pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk reads of investment/banking application memory or files (e.g. Excel, Access, Lotus Notes), followed by large data transfers to OceanLotus infrastructure. Monitor for tools used by APT32 for data staging (WinRAR, 7-Zip, tar) or direct exfil via HTTPS POST.

suggestion.title: Defender Evasion: Antivirus Disablement
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus historically employs defense evasion; no detection for endpoint protection tampering despite this being expected pre-ransomware or in long-dwell scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry key modifications disabling Windows Defender, termination of antivirus processes, or PowerShell commands with disable-realtime-monitoring flags. Correlate with SPECTRALVIPER process hash or parent to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes Gentlemen as a ransomware variant; encryption is core impact behavior but pipeline generated zero detections for file modification patterns, high-entropy writes, or encryption-consistent access sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, sequential file modifications with extension changes or high-entropy content writes. Monitor for processes writing to bulk file targets (e.g., >100 files in <60 seconds) and correlate with potential ransom-note file creation in same directory tree.

suggestion.title: SMB/Network Share Lateral Propagation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ransomware 'can spread like a worm'; lateral movement via share enumeration and remote execution is core to worm-class propagation but no detection rule was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious SMB connection chains: process-initiated SMB to non-standard hosts, enumeration of administrative shares (admin$, c$, ipc$), or spawned child processes originating from UNC paths. Correlate new host encryption events post-connection.

suggestion.title: Script-Based Payload Execution for Ransomware Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware distribution typically leverages PowerShell or command-line execution; no use case covers script-based infection chain despite being standard attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell or cmd.exe spawned by unusual parents (Office applications, SYSTEM context, network paths), Base64-encoded/obfuscated command lines, or commands disabling security controls. Cross-correlate command execution timeline with downstream encryption events.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note File Deployment Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware variants typically leave ransom notes post-encryption (likely README.txt or variant-named files); no detection rule exists for this post-impact artifact creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of text/HTML files named DECRYPT*, README*, RESTORE*, or matching '<variant>_*' patterns across multiple directories in short timespan. Flag simultaneous encryption and ransom-note creation in same parent folder structure.

suggestion.title: Service or Scheduled Task Persistence Mechanism Creation
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware often establishes persistence for re-infection or command-execution capability; no detection for service/task creation by suspicious processes post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service creation from non-standard sources (PowerShell, cmd, network paths, SYSTEM privilege escalation). Alert on scheduled task registration by unprivileged accounts or child processes of known ransomware infection vectors. Correlate with encryption timeline.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Security Product Termination or Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify anti-analysis techniques, but worm-class ransomware typically disables AV/EDR; no detection rule covers this evasion phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process termination of security product executables (MsMpEng, CylanceSvc, SentinelOne, etc.), registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services (disabling/deleting security services), or command-line invocations of sc.exe, taskkill.exe targeting AV/EDR. Alert pre-encryption.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'authentication bypass'—describes the primary exploitation vector. Defenders need to detect attempts to exploit this flaw, evidenced by non-standard login paths, session token manipulation, or privilege escalation without credential entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB /login.php and authentication handlers for requests with malformed parameters, token reuse, or direct session ID manipulation. Flag successful authentication that lacks corresponding credential submission events or privilege escalation without password verification.

suggestion.title: phpBB RCE Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'RCE Since 2014'—Remote Code Execution is the outcome. Detect suspicious process spawning, shell invocation, or script execution from the web server context that would follow successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process creation from apache2/nginx/php-fpm parent processes: bash, cmd.exe, powershell, sh execution with command-line arguments. Monitor for base64 decode + exec patterns, reverse shell indicators, or web server spawning system admin utilities.

suggestion.title: phpBB User Data Exfiltration Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'affecting tens of millions of users'—attacker motivation after RCE is credential harvesting, private message theft, or account takeover. Requires detection of abnormal database access patterns from compromised web context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk SELECT queries on users, user_group, privmsgs tables executed from web service account. Flag large result sets returned to non-standard code paths, unusual database connection frequency, or exfiltration via HTTP responses.

suggestion.title: phpBB Vulnerability Probe and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: '10 year old critical vulnerability'—attackers probe for vulnerable phpBB instances before exploitation. No detection for version enumeration, file path scanning, or known PoC request signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential requests to phpBB reconnaissance endpoints: /install/, /config.php, /includes/functions.php in error responses revealing version. Follow with known CVE-specific payload patterns or template injection attempts.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet C2 Beaconing and Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active botnet infrastructure controlling 1,500+ devices but pipeline extracted no command-and-control detection logic. Botnet C2 communication is foundational kill-chain activity and must be detected via network or process telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound network beaconing from endpoints to known or suspected JDY C2 infrastructure. Monitor for periodic connection attempts (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS), suspicious process spawning associated with malware tasking, and command execution patterns consistent with botnet behavior.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Command Execution from Infected Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware purpose is 'cyber reconnaissance' but no detection use case provided for reconnaissance activity. This is a critical gap—reconnaissance commands (process enumeration, network scanning, credential harvesting) are detectable and should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of host and network reconnaissance commands (e.g., net view, tasklist, ipconfig, systeminfo, arp -a, route print) from compromised endpoints. Monitor for scanning traffic patterns, rapid port probing, or LDAP queries consistent with active reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: JDY Malware Process Execution and Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero malware execution signatures or behavioral patterns despite 1,500+ devices infected. No detection for suspicious process spawning, command-line indicators, or parent-child relationships typical of botnet malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of JDY botnet payloads via process command-line patterns, parent-child process anomalies (e.g., browser spawning cmd.exe), or known malware signatures. Flag suspicious interpreter invocations (powershell.exe, cmd.exe) with obfuscation or encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet Persistence Mechanisms (Registry, Scheduled Tasks, Services)
suggestion.rationale: No persistence detection provided. Botnet must establish persistence across reboots on 1,500+ devices via registry modification, scheduled tasks, or service installation—all detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of auto-start persistence mechanisms: registry Run/RunOnce keys, scheduled tasks with suspicious binaries or scripts, or new Windows services with unusual descriptions or binary paths.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement and Credential Access by JDY Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article implies reconnaissance for lateral movement ('cyber reconnaissance' purpose suggests network mapping for next-stage attacks), but pipeline generated no detection for credential harvesting or lateral movement exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement attempts from botnet-infected hosts: suspicious file transfers to internal systems, authentication attempts using compromised credentials, or RDP/SMB exploitation activity targeting other hosts on the network.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Traffic from Botnet-Infected Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline provided zero network-based detection. No IOCs (C2 IPs/domains) listed, no network behavior rules suggested despite article describing active botnet infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous outbound traffic from infected hosts: connections to non-standard ports, unusual DNS queries (domain generation algorithm patterns), encrypted tunneling protocols, or large data transfers to external IP ranges consistent with exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Commit from Non-Standard Development Location
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly positions 'the device as the only constant' across code-writing environments. Need detection for commits/PRs originating from unusual geolocation, time-of-day, or IP reputation not matching baseline developer patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits and push events for source IP geolocation, timestamp anomalies, or user-agent mismatches. Baseline per-developer by location and time-of-day; alert on >2σ deviation. Correlate with zero-day supply chain indicators.

suggestion.title: Development Tool Compromise via Unusual Installation Source
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses code being written everywhere, attackers may compromise development toolchains (npm, pip, cargo, Maven) installed on non-corporate machines. Detect package installs from suspicious mirrors or with altered checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager activity for installs from non-canonical registries, mismatched checksums, or versions not in official release notes. Alert on package.json/requirements.txt changes pulling from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared Code Repository Access Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Device-centric threat model suggests attackers may steal repo tokens from .git/config or environment variables on compromised machines. Detect token exfiltration attempts to external storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes reading .git directories, bash_history, env var exports, or credential stores on developer machines. Alert on subsequent outbound HTTPS to non-GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket CIDRs with auth-like payloads.

suggestion.title: Detection of Compromised Rust Package Installation or Version Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Compromised Rust crate onering'—package name and compromise status are explicit. Pipeline missed initial_access vector entirely. Must detect cargo install/update of 'onering' or hash/version verification failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cargo invocations for 'onering' crate, flag unpinned versions or registry source changes. Cross-correlate with Cargo.lock hash mismatches and first-time execution of pulled binaries in build/dev environments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Access and Exfiltration from Package Import Context
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'performs code exfiltration'—malicious code in crate reads source files and ships them out. Pipeline did not surface exfiltration detection. Must catch file-read chains + C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawned from 'onering' or Rust toolchain imports open handles to .rs source files, then establish outbound HTTPS/DNS to rare/unallowed domains. Establish baseline of legitimate crate file-read patterns in sandbox.

suggestion.title: Compile-Time or Import-Time Hook Execution from Untrusted Crate
suggestion.rationale: Malicious Rust crates inject build scripts or procedural macros. 'Code exfiltration' implies systematic execution, not passive storage. Pipeline did not capture execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rustc or cargo build-script-build processes with 'onering' in parent or working directory. Flag child processes (curl, wget, tar, python, bash) spawned during compilation. Correlate with unexpected environment variable reads or credential access.

suggestion.title: Lateral Exfiltration via Supply Chain Artifact in CI/CD Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Compromised crate affects all downstream projects. Pipeline did not suggest detection for propagation through build chains—critical for blast-radius reduction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD jobs for 'onering' crate or Cargo.toml changes. Correlate with first-ever outbound network from runners or artifact repositories. Isolate affected build hosts and downstream projects before deploying.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret Detection in Source Code
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" in dev.env (line 10) and cmd/serve.go (line 35)' — pipeline missed code-scanning detection vector. Detection should monitor repositories for AUTH_JWT_SECRET patterns and weak default values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor source code repositories and SAST tools for commits containing AUTH_JWT_SECRET, jwt.*secret, or hardcoded token defaults matching /^random$/ or similar weak patterns in config files (.env, serve.go, config.yaml). Alert on any public repository fork of github.com/dhax/go-base with unmodified hardcoded secret; correlate against internal deployments via software inventory.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery via Weak Secret Cryptanalysis
suggestion.rationale: Article attack vector: 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery' and T1606 (Forge Web Credentials) — detection should identify JWT tokens cryptographically verifiable against known weak secret.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect JWT Bearer tokens from /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh requests. Offline cryptographic analysis: attempt signature verification using known weak secret 'random' (HMAC-SHA256). Alert on successful verification, indicating attacker-forged token. Tuning: baseline legitimate tokens from known-good service accounts first to avoid noise.

suggestion.title: JWT Tokens with Extreme Far-Future Expiration Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt explicitly references 'extreme far-future JWT' but lacks dedicated detection rule. Attackers with secret can craft tokens with exp claims years ahead for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode JWT Bearer tokens in admin endpoint requests. Extract exp (expiration timestamp) claim and calculate token lifetime (exp - iat). Alert when lifetime > 30 days, or exp date > 5 years in future. Establish baseline per environment: production tokens typically < 1 hour, service accounts < 30 days. Combine with issuer (iss) claim analysis to identify forged tokens from mismatched issuers.

suggestion.title: Admin Endpoint Enumeration via Forged Token Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three admin endpoints as attack surface (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh). Kill-chain gap: detection of suspicious access *patterns* — multiple admin endpoints hit in short window from non-admin source or with token claim anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to /api/v1/admin/*, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/* endpoints when: (a) source IP not in admin CIDR allowlist, OR (b) ≥3 distinct admin endpoints accessed within 5-min window, OR (c) timestamps outside business hours + source IP not whitelisted, OR (d) user-agent is non-browser (curl, Python, requests, missing user-agent). Requires baselining legitimate admin access patterns (IPs, timings, endpoints per user).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable dhax/go-base Boilerplate Detection in Internal Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies affected software: 'github.com/dhax/go-base with 1,685 GitHub stars' — commonly cloned/forked boilerplate. Asset exposure vector: internal forks with hardcoded dev.env still in use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal GitHub/GitLab/self-hosted Git for clones/forks of dhax/go-base. For each repository found, programmatically check dev.env and serve.go for AUTH_JWT_SECRET config. Alert with risk level (high if hardcoded 'random' present and repo is linked to production deployment, medium if dev/staging only). Cross-reference with application inventory to identify live attack surface.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin API Access Success via Anomalous JWT Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article kill-chain implies impact: 'Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints' (HTTP 200 success). Gap: correlation of successful admin requests with JWT claim anomalies (forged issuer, altered sub, far-future exp, weak secret signature).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For HTTP 200 responses on admin endpoints, decode JWT Bearer token and extract claims (sub, iat, exp, iss). Alert when: (a) multiple successful requests from same source with different sub claims (token swapping), OR (b) exp claim > 10 years ahead of iat, OR (c) iss (issuer) claim missing or mismatched against known issuers, OR (d) request rate from same source/token > 10 req/sec (indicates automated exploitation). Requires JWT schema baseline per application.

suggestion.title: protocolMessage Payload Anomaly Detection in Baileys Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'maliciously crafted protocolMessage payload' as attack vector. Need detection for malformed, oversized, or structurally anomalous protocol message handling in Baileys/Node.js event streams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js processes running Baileys that emit unusual or high-frequency protocolMessage parsing errors, or message event objects with key/payload mismatches indicating spoofed messages.

suggestion.title: Baileys Message Upsert Event Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack triggering 'fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload.' Need detection for message events with fabricated sender identity or timestamp incongruence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys application logs or in-process event streams for messages.upsert events where the message key does not cryptographically validate against session state, or where sender JID contradicts prior conversation metadata.

suggestion.title: Application State Sync Corruption Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attacker to 'corrupt the app state sync system.' Need detection for Baileys/Node.js apps experiencing unexpected state divergence, failed sync operations, or integrity check failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Baileys processes logging state sync errors, version mismatches in app state snapshots, or repeated failed reconciliation attempts following placeholderResendMessage handling.

suggestion.title: npm Baileys Package Dependency Supply Chain Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in Baileys library (versions < 7.0.0-rc12, < 6.7.22). Beyond UC_22_2 file presence, need hunt for package.json / package-lock.json containing vulnerable version pinning across development and production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for package.json or package-lock.json files referencing baileys or @whiskeysockets/baileys with version constraints that include vulnerable ranges (< 7.0.0-rc12, < 6.7.22), then cross-correlate with npm install/ci operations.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempts against disclosed Ivanti vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article title: '[CRIT] Ivanti...Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities'—attackers will target unpatched instances before organizations patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/GET requests to Ivanti Connect Secure or Ivanti Policy Secure endpoints with suspicious payloads (SQL injection, path traversal, RCE patterns). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from Ivanti service accounts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempts against disclosed Fortinet vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article title names Fortinet as one of three vendors with critical patches—FortiGate appliances are high-value targets if unpatched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet logs for authentication bypass patterns, admin console access from unusual source IPs, or API calls to administrative functions without proper authorization.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempts against disclosed SAP vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article title names SAP—SAP systems handle critical business processes; unpatched instances are prime targets for data exfiltration and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SAP application logs for SQL injection attempts in ABAP reports, unusual data exports via RFC calls, unauthorized SM59 (RFC destination) modifications, or mass data access from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable software inventory detection—Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP
suggestion.rationale: Article states patches were released for critical flaws; detection must identify unpatched versions in the environment to prioritize patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate endpoint/network software inventory against CVE databases. Alert on presence of Ivanti, Fortinet, or SAP products with versions known to be vulnerable to disclosed CVEs and not yet patched.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender SYSTEM Privilege Escalation via RoguePlanet Vector
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Grants SYSTEM Access'—privilege escalation is the direct impact. Pipeline missed core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Microsoft Defender processes (MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe) create child processes with elevated privilege token (NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM), or when process elevation occurs from non-system context to SYSTEM without UAC prompts logged.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies a specific zero-day in Defender. Pipeline should detect exploitation patterns—file access to Defender binaries, unusual DLL loads, or version-mismatch indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution involving known-vulnerable Defender binary versions (hash-based or metadata version checks), or unusual DLL loads into MsMpEng.exe from non-standard paths (outside %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender).

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Microsoft Defender Service Manipulation Post-RoguePlanet Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article context ('Updated Windows') implies successful exploitation enables further evasion. Pipeline missed defense-evasion detection for stopping, disabling, or replacing Defender.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation (sc.exe, powershell.exe, taskkill.exe) targeting MsMpEng.exe or WinDefend service stop/disable, or registry modifications to HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender that disable real-time protection or reporting.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly features 'critical RCE bugs' in title. Zero execution-phase detections generated despite RCE being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation from vulnerable Microsoft service processes (LSASS, Services.exe, lsm.exe) or inline script execution patterns (PowerShell, VBScript) spawned by service host processes.

suggestion.title: Unpatched System Scanning and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Patch release announces vulnerabilities; threat actors scan for systems not yet patched. No discovery-phase detections despite this being explicit attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scanning or service enumeration targeting vulnerable Microsoft RPC/SMB endpoints within 48-72 hours post-patch announcement, correlate with subsequent exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Persistence via Service/Scheduled Task
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploits require persistence mechanisms. Zero persistence-phase detections despite zero-days typically being chained with T1547 or T1543 techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sc.exe or schtasks.exe invocation from service-context child processes with suspicious binary paths or encoded commands; flag registry Run/RunOnce modifications by processes spawned from vulnerable services.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaws often chain with privesc. Article title implies 'critical' impact suggesting kernel or system-level vulnerabilities. No T1134 or token manipulation detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token duplication/impersonation requests from non-admin processes, handle requests to LSASS or winlogon from low-privilege contexts, elevation of privilege API calls preceding service creation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Host
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE leads to internal propagation. Zero lateral-movement use cases despite multi-system compromise being natural progression from successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SMB/RPC outbound connections from newly-RCE-compromised system to internal hosts, PSEXEC or WMI command execution patterns originating from vulnerable service compromise, credential access on remote systems.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Payload Detection - Network Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Title signals three zero-days and RCE vectors but no network-based exploitation indicators extracted. Should detect protocol abuse or payload signatures targeting vulnerable Microsoft services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound HTTP POST/PATCH requests with unusual content-length, binary/encoded payloads, or abnormal User-Agent to Microsoft service endpoints (Exchange, SharePoint, IIS); correlate spike with vulnerability announcement date.

suggestion.title: Langflow Unauthenticated Endpoint Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027 Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE'—establishes attack vector as unauthenticated API endpoint access enabling arbitrary code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to Langflow API endpoints (/api/*, /v1/* patterns typical of Python frameworks) from unauthenticated sources. Flag requests containing command/code payload markers (eval, exec, __import__, etc.). Correlate with subsequent process creation from Langflow service to detect successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Langflow Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states RCE outcome; unauthenticated endpoint access would result in arbitrary command execution under Langflow service privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Langflow parent (langflow.exe, python.exe with Langflow arguments) with suspicious execution patterns: shell interpreter creation (cmd.exe, /bin/bash), encoded command-line arguments, credential access utilities, network utilities for data exfiltration, or reverse shell indicators.

suggestion.title: Langflow Service Fingerprinting for CVE-2026-5027 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes active exploitation; attackers must first enumerate Langflow service versions to identify vulnerable targets before payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for enumeration requests to version disclosure endpoints (/version, /health, /api/version, /docs, /static/swagger) that would leak Langflow version. Alert on version-detection probes followed within minutes by exploitation payloads or process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Rapid BTC Deposit-to-Withdrawal Layering Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes AudiA6 operation: 'accept cybercrime proceeds, move the money around through complex transaction routes that obscured its origin, and return it cleaned to the holders in about an hour, minus a 3-10% service commission.' This temporal and layering signature is directly detectable on blockchain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large BTC deposits to known mixing-service wallets followed by outbound transfers with multi-hop layering (intermediate wallet chains) completed within 60-120 minute windows. Flag wallets exhibiting statistical deviation from legitimate trading: high frequency of same deposit-withdrawal cycle, consistent commission decay (~3-10%), and temporal clustering.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payment Proceeds to Mixing Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'approximately 393.39 BTC...were received directly from known darknet markets, ransomware organizations, cybercrime services.' Direct link between ransomware payment infrastructure and AudiA6 wallets is a high-fidelity detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate known ransomware payment addresses (from leak site monitors, ransom notes, OSINT) against blockchain transaction ledger. Alert on outbound transfers from ransomware operators' wallets to AudiA6-attributed addresses or other known mixing-service infrastructure. Enrich with timeline correlation to victim incident reports.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Multi-Domain KYC Account Creation at Scale
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals: 'thousands of fraudulent exchange accounts opened using stolen or purchased identities' and 'the massive network of money mules used multiple domains to register accounts on cryptocurrency exchanges.' This domain-hopping evasion pattern against exchange KYC controls is systematically detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build graph database of KYC submissions across exchanges. Flag cohorts of new accounts where identity attributes (photo hash, document ID, phone, email domain) recur across multiple exchanges but registration domain referrals differ. Detect VPN/proxy infrastructure used to bypass geo-restrictions during account creation bursts from single operator identity pool.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Forum Money Mule Recruitment Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Dark2Web underground forum...which cybercriminals used to advertise illicit services' and 'Russian-speaking intermediaries that recruited [mules] specifically for this purpose.' Forum posts offering money-mule work are directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dark2Web and peer dark-web forums for recruitment posts using keywords: 'money mule,' 'payment processor,' 'crypto account opener,' 'fast cash.' Flag Russian-language intermediary accounts with post history spanning multiple months and recruitment success metrics. Correlate recruitment timelines with surges in fraudulent KYC submissions on exchanges.

suggestion.title: Telegram Channel Crypto Mixing Operational Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Blocked Telegram accounts used by the network.' Telegram was operational infrastructure for money-mule payments and mixing-service administration. Messaging app monitoring captures operational tempo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Telegram for channel activity discussing crypto 'cleaning,' money mule payment confirmations, or exchange account status. Flag channels with rapid message velocity around payment forwarding, KYC document sharing, or wallet address distribution. Correlate message timestamps with blockchain deposit/withdrawal cycles and exchange account creation bursts.

suggestion.title: Identity Theft at Scale for Exchange Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals extraction of '6,000 KYC records linked to money mule accounts' created with 'stolen or purchased identities.' The 6,000-account KYC corpus is an IOC of identity-fraud scale and source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspected stolen-identity databases (dark web leak feeds, breaches) against KYC submissions on exchanges using fuzzy-matching on identity document fields and biometric vectors. Flag cohorts of 100+ submissions sharing document metadata or photo characteristics. Cross-reference with OSINT on identity-theft marketplaces to establish source supply.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—exposure is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances on public-facing IPs or reachable from untrusted networks. Look for characteristic signatures: HTTPS on port 8020, certificate CNs containing 'Sentry'/'MobileIron', or Ivanti-specific HTTP headers in proxy/firewall logs. Flag unmanaged instances (no mTLS/EPMM enrollment indicators).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—requires HTTP requests crafted with injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management endpoints for OS command-injection metacharacters: semicolons, pipes, backticks, $(), &&, ||, or base64-encoded payloads. Prioritize unauthenticated requests (no valid session token) from external sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation spawns processes with UID=0 on the appliance, observable in syslog/audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry systems, alert on process creation with UID=0 where parent is web service (nginx, java, vendor process). Red flags: bash, sh, nc, curl, wget spawned from non-service accounts or at unusual times. Establish baseline of normal root processes on Sentry to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Egress from Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Root RCE enables C2 callback, reverse shell, or lateral movement—observable as anomalous outbound connections from appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound connections from Sentry appliances. Alert on unexpected egress to non-corporate IPs, especially ports 443, 4444, 5555, or UDP DNS tunneling patterns. Correlate with exploitation-attempt detections to establish attack timeline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due date 2026-06-14; CISA KEV items are active threats—unpatched instances must be identified and prioritized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances and flag those running vulnerable versions pre-dating the patch release. Cross-reference with external-exposure scans to prioritize exposed-and-unpatched instances. Track remediation progress against the 2026-06-14 deadline.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway exploitation attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass user authentication' via CVE-2026-50751/50752, mapping to T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). No UC provided for detecting exploitation at gateway layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication sequences or protocol violations in Check Point Security Gateway logs. Monitor for HTTP requests with indicators of CVE-2026-50751 exploitation (e.g., malformed auth tokens, bypass patterns). Correlate with successful VPN tunnel establishment immediately following failed auth attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN session establishment from external IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article's core threat is 'establish unauthorized VPN connections' via auth bypass. No UC maps to detection of anomalous VPN logins or out-of-band session creation despite this being the immediate exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN session creation from external IPs matching article's attacker infrastructure (45.77.149.152, 209.182.225.136, etc.). Detect successful logins without prior failed-auth attempts. Identify VPN sessions from accounts not in identity provider or with missing device posture/MFA records.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 communications to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 16 attacker-controlled IPv4 addresses and includes T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) in technique mapping, but no UC detects egress traffic to these C2 nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/UDP connections from internal endpoints to any of the 16 IOC IPs. Monitor for DNS queries resolving to these IPs. Correlate command-line arguments with process trees to identify which processes (malware, post-exploit tools) initiated C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /mcp Endpoint (CVE-2026-48039 Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents 'Unauthenticated HTTP MCP Tool Execution' as the attack vector, with UC_19_3 providing detection logic. Initial access phase exploitation of the vulnerable endpoint was entirely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to */mcp* endpoints on TCP 8080 with 200 status responses from non-RFC1918 sources. Include process context filters (python, uvicorn, gunicorn, node, docker) to isolate vulnerable service exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: Meta Graph API Token Exfiltration via Query String
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'Leaks Operator Meta Access Token' and UC_19_4 documents the exfiltration signature: requests to graph.facebook.com with access_token in URL query parameters. Token theft phase completely undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound requests to graph.facebook.com with 'access_token=' in the URL query string. Extract token prefixes for preview and correlation. Cross-reference with meta-ads-mcp process execution context to confirm post-exploitation abuse.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Tool Execution: Named Python Exploit Files
suggestion.rationale: UC_19_2 explicitly names three exploit-associated files: http_auth_integration.py, api.py, poc.py. These are concrete behavioral indicators of active CVE-2026-48039 exploitation attempts. Completely absent from pipeline use case output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process creation or file modification events for http_auth_integration.py, api.py, or poc.py. Correlate with Python interpreters and WSGI servers. Capture full command line and parent process context to distinguish exploit execution from legitimate development activity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp Package Inventory (Versions ≤1.0.101)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions ≤1.0.101 across commits 496c988–7d14226 in repository pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp. UC_19_5 provides software and process inventory queries for discovery of vulnerable installations. Completely undetected in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for meta-ads-mcp package name and version. Hunt for process command lines containing 'meta_ads_mcp' or 'meta-ads-mcp' combined with Python/uvicorn/gunicorn/docker contexts. Flag any installations ≤1.0.101 as vulnerable and flag versions 1.0.102–1.0.105 as unconfirmed patch status.

suggestion.title: OAuth Consent Grants and App Permission Assignment (Account Hijacking)
suggestion.rationale: Article includes T1098.001 (Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials) and UC_OAUTH_ABUSE detects suspicious OAuth consent grants and delegated permission grants. This persistence mechanism following token theft was entirely undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful OAuth2 permission grants, delegated permission assignments, and app role assignments from compromised or suspicious accounts. Alert on grants of broad Meta/Facebook API scopes (ads_read, pages_read_engagement, business_management_api) following suspicious token access patterns.

suggestion.title: Polyglot file artifact detection—GIF magic bytes with embedded PHP signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article core technique: 'uploaded file named `shell.php` containing GIF-like content'. Current UCs detect post-facto (UC_4_1 file creation, UC_4_3 access) but not the polymorphic artifact itself. Forensic scanning of upload directories can identify files with GIF magic (47 49 46 38) paired with PHP signatures (`<?php`, `<?`), exposing the evasion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan files in upload directories for GIF magic bytes (4749 4638) immediately followed by PHP opening tags or common webshell patterns. Aggregate by directory and filename to isolate polyglot uploads from legitimate images. High specificity; minimal false positives expected.

suggestion.title: Upload request with Content-Type/filename extension mismatch targeting upload endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the root cause: 'The `ext_in` upload validation rule checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.' Detection requires observing the upload request itself where `Content-Type: image/gif` pairs with filename containing `.php`. Catches the exploit attempt at ingress, not post-landing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In HTTP POST requests to CodeIgniter4 upload endpoints, flag instances where the Content-Type header indicates an image MIME type (image/gif, image/png, image/jpeg) but the filename parameter contains executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar, .phps). Requires application-level HTTP logging or WAF rule set.
