suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' — exploitation attempts manifest as malformed HTTP payloads with shell metacharacters or encoded commands targeting vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry for command injection indicators: pipes (|), semicolons (;), backticks (``), dollar-parentheses ($(...)), ampersands (&), or Base64/URL-encoded equivalents in query parameters or request bodies. Alert on suspicious input to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation yields arbitrary commands as root. Host-based detection of unexpected root process spawning from Sentry application context is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for unexpected process creation with UID=0 (root), especially child processes from Sentry daemons or web server worker processes. Baseline legitimate Sentry operations and alert on deviations (e.g., reverse shells, credential dumping tools).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Assessment: CVE-2026-10520 Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active in-the-wild exploitation. Standard vulnerability management requires immediate scanning and remediation; article sets federal due date of 2026-06-14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute vulnerability scans against all Ivanti Sentry assets for CVE-2026-10520 presence. Cross-reference unpatched instances against patch management records; flag systems overdue for remediation by the federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Configuration Audit: Sentry Managed State and Network Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' enables exploitation. Mitigation: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' — configuration verification prevents exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for managed state configuration and network access controls. Verify mTLS with EPMM is enabled; verify HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM is restricted. Flag any unmanaged instances or those with open external network accessibility.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes exploitation precondition: 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Baseline UC must detect external access attempts to unmanaged Sentry appliances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS connections from external networks to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces (typical ports 443, 8443, 4430) without valid TLS client certificates (mTLS). Exclude traffic from known management subnets and those behind Neurons for MDM or EPMM.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload in Ivanti Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability mechanism: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline must detect injection payloads in request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect backtick, $(), pipe, semicolon, or &&/|| injection patterns in HTTP request parameters/bodies sent to Ivanti Sentry endpoints. Focus on unauthenticated endpoints and common injection vectors (API paths, upload handlers, configuration parameters).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline must detect when Sentry service process (typically unprivileged) spawns child processes with SYSTEM/root privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell process creation (bash, sh, zsh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with SYSTEM or UID 0 parentage where parent is Ivanti Sentry, MobileIron, or related service processes. Establish baseline for legitimate privilege escalation paths; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Following successful RCE, attacker executes reconnaissance/lateral-movement commands. Article confirms 'root-level' capability, enabling unrestricted command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious commands spawned from Sentry child processes: reconnaissance utilities (id, whoami, uname), network tools (curl, wget, nc), credential dumping (cat /etc/shadow), or reverse shell patterns. Prioritize any commands executed with root privileges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with vulnerability scanner. Pipeline must flag vulnerable Ivanti Sentry instances by CVE identifier and version ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match Ivanti Sentry version information against vulnerable ranges for CVE-2026-10520. Prioritize instances that are externally routable and NOT behind mTLS, EPMM, or Neurons for MDM. Flag patch lag relative to 2026-06-14 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Service Network Anomalies Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes compromised appliance 'could allow' command execution; post-compromise, appliance may be used as pivot or C2 relay. Detect abnormal egress from Sentry service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Ivanti Sentry outbound network behavior. Alert on outbound connections to non-whitelisted destinations, unusual port combinations (e.g., 443 to non-HTTPS ranges), or data exfiltration patterns inconsistent with appliance function.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'actively exploited.' Pipeline generated zero detections for exploitation traffic or attack signatures against Serv-U listeners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Serv-U service ports with payloads matching publicly disclosed DoS exploit patterns. Flag anomalous request volume from single sources, malformed requests targeting known vulnerable parameters, or rapid repeated connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Traffic Volume to Serv-U Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: DoS vulnerability by definition requires detection of volumetric or application-layer attacks. Article confirms active exploitation; pipeline missed network-layer detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline inbound traffic volume to known Serv-U service ports. Alert on sustained traffic spikes, connection floods from single sources, or high-volume malformed/incomplete requests consistent with DoS attacks.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Unavailability / Unexpected Downtime
suggestion.rationale: DoS impact directly targets availability. 'Critical' severity denotes business-impacting flaw. Pipeline generated no detection for service disruption, process crashes, or availability loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process health, port responsiveness, and response latency. Alert on unexpected process termination, port unreachability, spike in connection-refused errors, or service restart loops correlated with unusual traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Version Fingerprinting / Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is version-specific. Attackers enumerate versions before exploitation. Article silence on reconnaissance activity; pipeline missed discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for banner-grabbing attempts, version-disclosure HTTP requests, or User-Agent strings associated with vulnerability scanners. Flag repeated probing of Serv-U endpoints from external sources, particularly from infrastructure hosting known vulnerability scanners.

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder account gains global builder flag
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'the SDK grants `builder.global=true`' — this is the exploit's outcome and must be directly detected via account state inspection before/after the vulnerable endpoint call.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate builder accounts with builder.global unset or false + builder.apps set (workspace-scoped) at T-1, then presence of builder.global=true at T+0, within 5-minute window of POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign. Alert on any account state flip from workspace-only to global privilege.

suggestion.title: Non-admin source account POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'builderOrAdmin middleware, which passes any user who is a builder for the app' — exploit originates from builder accounts, not admins. Detection must filter by source privilege level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POSTs to /api/public/v1/roles/assign. Flag requests where SourceAccountPrivilegeLevel is 'builder' (not 'admin', not 'global_builder'). Filter to requests with HTTP 200/201 response and role-escalation parameters in request body (global=true, role=admin, etc.).

suggestion.title: Role assignment request with builder.global or admin role grant in request body
suggestion.rationale: Article states the controller 'spreads the request body into the SDK call' — payload inspection is critical to distinguish exploit attempts from legitimate role assignments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST body payloads to /api/public/v1/roles/assign. Alert on presence of: builder.global=true, role=admin, privilege escalation keywords. Correlate with source account being non-admin. High confidence if request from workspace-scoped builder includes global privilege grant.

suggestion.title: Rapid or bulk role assignments from single source account
suggestion.rationale: Exploit pattern suggests concentrated privilege-escalation attempt; normal workflow involves single or sporadic role assignments. Spike detection needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Count successful POSTs to /api/public/v1/roles/assign per (SourceIP, SourceAccount) in 5-minute sliding window. Alert if count > 3 in window, or if single request grants multiple roles (global builder, admin, etc.) in one payload.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Modifications to PAM/SSH Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes backdoored 'Linux Login Software'—likely PAM, SSH, su, or sudo. Article states attackers 'hide for nearly a decade,' implying undetected binary modifications and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to authentication binaries (/usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /bin/su, /usr/sbin/sudo) via FIM or package-manager integrity checks. Track mismatches between installed package hash and filesystem hash. Detect kernel module insertion (insmod, modprobe) or LD_PRELOAD manipulation of libc.

suggestion.title: Backdoor C2 Communication from Authentication Subsystem
suggestion.rationale: Article implies persistent command-and-control: attackers maintained access for '~10 years,' requiring hidden C2 channels. Backdoored login binary would need out-of-band signaling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS or HTTP queries originating from authentication binaries (sshd, PAM libraries) or with unusual timing/frequency. Look for anomalous outbound connections from root-context processes during login phases. Correlate failed login attempts with subsequent DNS/network activity.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft or Interception via Compromised Login Binary
suggestion.rationale: A backdoored login mechanism (SSH, su, sudo) enables plaintext credential capture on every login attempt for a decade. Article does not mention detection method, suggesting captures went unnoticed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for duplicate or anomalous copies of authentication binaries in alternate locations (e.g., /lib, /tmp, LD_PRELOAD paths). Detect keylogging or credential-logging via environment variable checks and library injection. Flag logins from same source IP with multiple rapid failures followed by success.

suggestion.title: Kernel or Rootkit Installation for Hiding Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'hide for nearly a decade,' implying evasion of auditing and logging. Backdoor persistence likely supported by kernel-level hiding (rootkit, syscall hooking, or LKM).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or anomalous kernel modules via 'lsmod' and 'modinfo' signatures. Detect syscall table modifications or eBPF bytecode injection. Flag missing auditd rules or syslog corruption. Correlate audit gaps with authentication activity.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain or Package Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes backdoor affecting Linux login software broadly. Distribution model likely supply-chain (compromised tarball, repo mirror, or build system) rather than per-host. Signature mismatch across multiple systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-site package-hash verification: compare downloaded package checksums against official GPG-signed manifest. Detect unsigned package installations or downgrades. Monitor repository mirrors for TLS downgrade or man-in-the-middle indicators. Flag installations from non-standard repositories.

suggestion.title: Long-Lived Dormant Backdoor Reactivation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '~10-year' persistence, implying dormancy or long gaps between activity. Detection may spike when backdoor is leveraged post-discovery. Reactivation logic or update mechanism.
log_sources: Scheduled task logs (cron, at, systemd timers)
Process anomaly (sleeping parent processes, unexpected wake)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cron jobs or systemd timers running with unusual permissions (root) or scheduled for maintenance windows. Detect process resurrection (child spawned after long parent idle time). Monitor for file-touch/modification on binaries after months of inactivity.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'VerdantBamboo Deploys BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances'—execution is the central attack action. No process-level detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Linux/BSD appliances for process execution matching BRICKSTORM process names, suspicious parent-child chains (e.g., shell spawning unknown binary), or command-line patterns known to trigger the malware. Cross-reference process hash against threat-feed samples.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Persistence via Cron and Init Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Infrastructure malware targeting appliances must persist across reboots. Title implies active deployment but no persistence-layer detection UC was generated for Linux/BSD-appropriate mechanisms (cron, systemd, init.d).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to cron jobs, systemd units, or init.d scripts with suspicious timing or process references. Flag unexpected additions to /etc/cron.d, /etc/rc.local, or /etc/systemd/system on appliances.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM C2 Beacon and Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Deployed malware must communicate with command-and-control. Article provides no C2 indicators but network-level detection is primary for infrastructure compromise. Pipeline generated zero C2 UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor appliances for outbound traffic to known BRICKSTORM C2 infrastructure. Alert on anomalous DNS queries, repeated connection attempts on non-standard ports, large data transfers, or encrypted tunnels from appliance networks.

suggestion.title: BSD Variant Detection and Cross-Platform Malware Adaptation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM'—port to non-native OS is significant. Detect execution of Linux-family malware on BSD and vice versa; flag compilation artifacts suggesting active customization by the actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify BRICKSTORM samples compiled for BSD when typically distributed for Linux, or vice versa. Alert on unusual ELF/Mach-O headers, mismatched binary vs. OS, or compilation timestamps/build paths suggesting recent actor modification.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Between Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'appliances' (plural, implied). Infrastructure devices are typically adjacent; pipeline should detect lateral spread via SSH, management interfaces, or protocol-specific attacks. Zero lateral-movement UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH brute-force or key-based access from compromised appliances to adjacent devices. Alert on enumeration of management interfaces (HTTP/HTTPS ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443) or reachability scanning across appliance networks.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo Initial Access and Campaign Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Named actor 'VerdantBamboo' should have registered TTPs and initial-access vectors. No actor-specific detection or IOC patterns generated despite clear attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on known VerdantBamboo initial-access patterns: exploitation of specific CVEs in appliance firmware, credential stuffing against management interfaces, or exposure of appliance admin panels. Cross-reference against threat-feed IOCs for the actor.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Internet Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — direct asset-exposure hunt requirement for unpatched internet-facing instances
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry appliances (legacy product name) accessible from external networks on default or known service ports. Alert if instance is unmanaged, lacks mTLS/restricted HTTPS protection, or is unpatched for CVE-2026-10520. Correlate with patch-management inventory.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt on Sentry Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is defined as 'OS command injection' permitting 'root-level remote code execution' — exploitable via HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints with injected shell commands
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Sentry endpoints (and legacy MobileIron Sentry endpoints) for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $()), command substitution, base64-encoded commands. Alert on unauthenticated requests matching injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Host
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation behavior detectable via anomalous process spawning from Sentry service context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes (shells, curl, wget, python, perl) spawned from Sentry service accounts or system daemons running as root. Flag reverse-shell patterns or outbound network connections initiated by Sentry-associated processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status with federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 mandates inventory tracking; article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — failure to patch known-exploited vulnerability creates immediate risk
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scans against all Ivanti Sentry instances to confirm patched status for CVE-2026-10520. Alert on unpatched instances. Cross-reference with network-exposure inventory to identify unpatched + internet-accessible appliances as critical-risk assets requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Request to Sentry Endpoint Preceding RCE
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'unauthenticated' — detection signature is absence of authentication context before successful exploitation; HTTP 200/command-execution responses to unauthenticated requests
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST/GET requests to Sentry endpoints with no prior authentication session that trigger successful responses or error messages containing command execution artifacts. Flag requests with command-like payloads (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc) that return command output or shell error messages.

suggestion.title: MobileIron Sentry Legacy Product Name Detection in Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes product is 'formerly known as MobileIron Sentry' — legacy naming appears in older CMDB records and patch-tracking systems; dual-name detection required to cover all deployment instances
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search asset inventory, service-discovery logs, and CMDB for 'MobileIron Sentry' in addition to 'Ivanti Sentry' product identifiers. Flag any instances still tagged with legacy name as potential patch-tracking gaps or audit misses. Correlate with vulnerability-scan results to ensure coverage under both naming conventions.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—exposure is the enabling condition. Foundational hunt before RCE detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from untrusted network segments. Flag instances without mTLS enrollment or EPMM registration, as these lose the protection layer described in the article.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability'—direct attack vector. Exploitation occurs via crafted requests containing shell metacharacters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry admin or API endpoints for command substitution patterns ($(), backticks, semicolons, pipes, command separators) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Alert on requests from untrusted sources to vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawning from Sentry Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article guarantees 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation results in OS-level privilege escalation from web service to uid=0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation on Ivanti Sentry systems where parent process is a web service (Java, httpd) or application daemon and child process executes with uid=0. Correlate timing with HTTP access logs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability requires 'unmanaged state'—appliances not enrolled in EPMM or lacking mTLS protection are exposed. mTLS/EPMM enrollment status determines exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset query: Ivanti Sentry appliances where (epmm_enrolled = false OR mtls_enabled = false). Cross-reference against external IP ranges. Prioritize by internet-facing exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'match against your vulnerability scanner'—explicit requirement for CVE-2026-10520 detection via CVSS/NVD integration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Ivanti Sentry asset flagged by scanner as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Escalate if asset is both vulnerable and externally reachable without mTLS/HTTPS restrictions.

suggestion.title: Restricted HTTPS / mTLS Enforcement Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'—detection of configuration gaps where mTLS/HTTPS restrictions are absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configuration: verify mTLS certificate pinning, HTTPS enforcement, and EPMM/Neurons for MDM connectivity. Flag appliances with permissive TLS or unencrypted admin access paths.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Exposure detection is first-line hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (SSL certificate CN/SAN matching 'Sentry' or 'MobileIron', HTTP response headers, reverse DNS patterns) visible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against asset inventory to flag unmanaged instances responding to external scans or exposed on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection of injection payloads in HTTP requests is critical before RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing OS command injection patterns (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, command substitution in URL parameters or POST bodies). Alert on successful exploitation indicators: 200/302 responses followed by unexpected child processes, or IPS/WAF command-injection signatures.

suggestion.title: Privileged Process Spawning from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack achieves 'root-level remote code execution' via unauthenticated access. Post-exploitation detection must identify unexpected elevated-privilege process execution initiated from Sentry service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry service process spawns child processes with root/elevated privileges, especially uncommon binaries (bash, wget, curl, nc, sh, python). Baseline expected child processes; flag anything outside normal operations. Focus on process ancestry: sentry service → unexpected root process.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution and Lateral Movement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants 'root-level' access enabling privilege escalation and lateral movement. Detection of suspicious root-level commands from compromised appliance is essential for post-compromise hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate root-level process execution from Sentry service context with lateral movement: SSH to other hosts, cron/SSH key installation, persistence mechanisms, or data exfiltration. Flag reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, arp, netstat, route) and privilege escalation commands (sudo, su) originating from compromised appliance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan and Patch Status Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with federal 3-day remediation deadline (2026-06-14). Vulnerability scanning and patch status are baseline detective controls. Article explicitly mandates: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Ivanti Sentry instances against CVE-2026-10520 in vulnerability scanner. Verify patch status; flag any running vulnerable versions immediately. For unpatched instances, verify mitigating controls active (mTLS with EPMM, restricted HTTPS via Neurons for MDM). Track exceptions with remediation timeline.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV entries require immediate remediation; scanner hits are the primary control signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry appliances. Correlate with patch due date (2026-06-14) to identify overdue remediation and flag as critical-priority incidents.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Externally Exposed
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the attack prerequisite; mTLS and HTTPS restrictions prevent exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry appliances and validate they are NOT externally accessible or have mTLS + restricted HTTPS enforced. Flag any with open HTTP ports (8080, 443 without mTLS) or unmanaged configuration state as high-risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation leverages command metacharacters in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (backtick, $(), |, ;, &&, ||) and OS command keywords (bash, sh, cmd, powershell, nc). Correlate with authentication failures or unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome. Unexpected spawning of system commands at root privilege from Sentry process is post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process creation from Ivanti Sentry service account/daemon with root or SYSTEM privilege, especially shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or system utilities (wget, curl, nc).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline generated zero detection for exploitation attempts against this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (commonly ports 8443/8080) containing OS command injection metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &, ;) or known CVE-2026-10520 payload signatures. Baseline typical Sentry traffic, alert on deviations or obvious shell metacharacters in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable only 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline missed the asset-exposure hunt entirely despite the article naming this as the precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally routable Ivanti Sentry instances on standard ports (8443, 8080, 443). Cross-reference against internal asset inventory; flag any unmanaged instances or those in uncontrolled network zones. Correlate with exposure platforms (Shodan, Censys) to identify internet-facing Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'root-level remote code execution' but pipeline generated no post-exploitation detection. This is the final, critical attack step requiring urgent detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent is Ivanti Sentry service/daemon running as root/SYSTEM, or unusual process lineage (web server → shell). Monitor for shell process spawning (bash, sh, dash, cmd.exe) with root UID=0 context originating from Sentry network context or bound ports.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS mitigations prevent external access, implying escalation path from authenticated/compromised context. Pipeline did not detect escalation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Ivanti Sentry processes requesting elevated privileges (sudo, UAC, setuid), credential theft attempts targeting Sentry service accounts, or lateral movement from Sentry to adjacent endpoints with root execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline generated no detection for vulnerability presence/absence despite this direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output, Tenable, Qualys, or similar, for Ivanti Sentry product detections. Flag any instance reporting Sentry version < patched version (per vendor advisory). Correlate patch status against patch deadline 2026-06-14 for compliance tracking.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Prerequisite attack condition must be huntable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances with public-facing IP bindings or externally routable connectivity. Correlate vulnerability scanner results against network boundary segmentation rules. Alert when appliances lack expected mTLS, EPMM integration, or Neurons for MDM enrollment—the three mitigations explicitly cited in the article.

suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Active exploitation vector currently observed in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: semicolons, pipes, backticks, $(), command substitution syntax). Correlate request anomalies (malformed parameters, unusual User-Agents, unauthenticated endpoint access) with subsequent child process spawning from Sentry daemon.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation behavioral signature for successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry daemon and child executes with UID 0 / root. Flag unexpected shells, system utilities, network tools, or reverse-shell indicators spawned from Sentry context. Alert on long-lived child processes or suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' CISA KEV status requires tracking of vulnerable versions and remediation deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry appliances below patched version. Cross-reference with asset exposure hunting results. Generate compliance alerts for instances not remediated by federal due date. Correlate patch status with network exposure metrics.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unmanaged state' is explicit prerequisite: 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Loss of mitigating controls enables attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry configuration for removal or disablement of mTLS with EPMM, restricted HTTPS access, or Neurons for MDM enrollment. Alert on loss of management heartbeat or unexpected configuration drift. Track management enrollment status and flag transitions to unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: HTTP Tunneling Command Payloads in Sentry Access Logs

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP access logs for requests with base64/hex-encoded bodies, chunked transfer encoding, multipart form data with binary blobs, or unusual Content-Encoding headers in admin endpoints. Correlate with command execution events.

suggestion.title: Detect Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and identifies 'remote unauthenticated user' access as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero asset-detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances by version, product banner, or CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability scanner hits on external IPs or public-facing networks. Correlate with absence of mTLS/EPMM enrollment or restricted HTTPS protection.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability...root-level remote code execution' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase use cases for detecting exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry API and web endpoints for command-injection payloads (backticks, semicolons, pipes, shell metacharacters). Alert on unauthenticated requests with injection patterns against vulnerable Sentry versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Privileged Process Execution from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' but pipeline generated zero post-exploitation process monitoring use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned with UID 0 (root) or SYSTEM privilege from Ivanti Sentry daemon processes or service account. Flag unexpected shell interpreters or system utilities executed from Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Detect Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is a prerequisite for exploitability; absence of mTLS/EPMM enrollment enables attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry appliances and verify enrollment in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Alert on appliances in unmanaged state with external reachability. Audit for absence of mTLS certificates or restricted HTTPS policies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — exposure is the attack surface prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (default ports 8443, 9443) with external network reachability or accessible from non-trusted networks. Flag unmanaged state indicators in device telemetry. Baseline internal-only access patterns.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Pattern — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user' — detect exploitation attempts before RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for shell metacharacters, command separators, or encoded payloads in user-supplied parameters. Detect patterns like backticks, $(...), pipes, semicolons in single requests to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation process activity is the decisive signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned with root/SYSTEM privileges that originate from or are triggered by Ivanti Sentry daemon processes (sentry, mobileiron, or related parent processes). Establish baseline for legitimate Sentry-spawned activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' — urgent patching deadline requires tracking and alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for any Ivanti Sentry instances lacking CVE-2026-10520 patch. Alert on unpatched instances and track days-to-deadline. Cross-reference with network exposure data to prioritize externally-reachable instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Authentication Bypass or Suspicious Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'remote unauthenticated' access — monitor for authentication-bypass indicators or access without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate authentication patterns to Sentry management interfaces. Alert on repeated failed-then-successful sequences, access from new geolocations, or requests that bypass normal authentication endpoints (e.g., direct API calls without login sessions).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — device configuration is a critical control indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for management enrollment status (EPMM/Neurons for MDM). Alert on instances that are unenrolled, have disabled mTLS, or have changed from managed to unmanaged state. Cross-correlate with external reachability.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear exploitation vector and CISA KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing OS command metacharacters (pipes, backticks, command substitution) in parameters. Track for known CVE-2026-10520 payload signatures and exploitation attempts from untrusted networks to externally exposed Sentry instances.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry with External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Article template references standard asset-exposure hunt; pipeline generated zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query infrastructure for Ivanti Sentry instances marked unmanaged or without trusted management state. Identify instances with external IP exposure, internet-facing DNS records, or public cloud accessibility. Alert on unmanaged appliances lacking mTLS/EPMM or Neurons for MDM protections.

suggestion.title: Root-Level RCE on Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact. No privilege-escalation detection UC generated despite clear vertical escalation from unauthenticated network user to root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for unexpected command execution with root/system privileges, particularly from network ingress or unauthenticated sources. Flag shell spawning (sh, bash, cmd) or privilege escalation events on Sentry hosts not paired with legitimate administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and stresses 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No remediation-tracking or deadline-compliance UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry instances running vulnerable versions of CVE-2026-10520. Flag unpatched systems. Prioritize federal civilian agencies and track compliance against 2026-06-14 due date; escalate non-compliant assets.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Network Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation works because 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Detection gap for unprotected, unauthenticated Sentry network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accepting connections without mTLS or EPMM/Neurons authentication from untrusted networks. Alert on any cleartext or weakly-authenticated sessions to command-injection attack surface.

suggestion.title: macOS Tahoe 26 Menu-Selection Artifact Baseline and Access Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact that tracks user menu selections across the operating system.' The artifact's presence and normal access patterns are legitimate detection targets; pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear forensic-defense implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for the macOS Tahoe 26 menu-selection artifact location, ownership, and access frequency on clean systems. Detect anomalous access from unexpected processes, unsigned binaries, or elevation attempts targeting the artifact.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Forensic Artifact Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: If attacker gains macOS access, they would enumerate forensic artifacts to reconstruct user intent and admin activity. Article establishes the artifact's value for behavior reconstruction—threat actors would exploit the same capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential file-system enumeration targeting known macOS forensic artifact locations (menu logs, plist databases, system state files) by single process or user. Flag invocation of forensic parsing tools or shell scripts against these paths post-compromise.

suggestion.title: File Hash Mismatch on Core Login Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'backdoored Linux login software' — requires detection of XZ utils, sudo, su, sshd, or glibc with unexpected hashes vs. official packages and threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file hashes for XZ utils, glibc, openssh, and sudo binaries on Linux hosts. Alert when local binary SHA256 diverges from upstream repository or known-bad hashes from threat intel. Compare against official vendor published hashes at package import.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process from Login Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hid for nearly a decade' — backdoor in login software implies active post-authentication execution. Detect unexpected process spawning from sshd, su, sudo, or PAM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell spawns, network tools, or system utilities launched from sshd, su, sudo parent processes outside known privilege-escalation patterns. Flag compilation tools, curl/wget, or nc from login context. Establish baseline of normal children and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: LD_PRELOAD or Init Hook Modification in Login Path
suggestion.rationale: Article: persistence 'for nearly a decade' — supply-chain backdoor likely uses LD_PRELOAD, PAM modules, or shell initialization (.bashrc/.profile) to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of /etc/pam.d/*, ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, /etc/ld.so.preload, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variables set during login. Alert on unsigned shared objects in preload paths. Flag unexpected library loads in login process memory.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from Login Daemon to Non-Standard Port
suggestion.rationale: Article: active backdoor 'hid for nearly a decade' — C&C beaconing from login software implies outbound connections from sshd or PAM spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/UDP connections from sshd, su, sudo, or login-spawned processes. Flag non-standard ports (not 22, 25, 53, 80, 443) or connections to known C&C infrastructure. Baseline normal login-context DNS/IP and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Strings or Entropy Anomalies in Login Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hid for nearly a decade' in widely-distributed software — YARA and binary analysis should detect XOR-encoded payloads, packer signatures, or unusual code sections in login binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run entropy-based YARA rules and deobfuscation checks on XZ utils, glibc, and login binaries. Flag sections with anomalously high entropy or known obfuscation patterns. Compare binary structure against clean upstream binaries; alert on unexpected code sections.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Modification Timestamp or Package Version Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'supply-chain' compromised — detect discrepancies between file modification time, package manager record, and binary version string in login software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package manager (dpkg, rpm) for installed vs. on-disk version/checksum of XZ, glibc, openssh. Alert on modification times older than expected for patched versions or checksums diverging from official repositories. Flag packages with future timestamps.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Cordova Callback Dispatch from InAppBrowser
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'passes the `id` field from a WKScriptMessage body to commandDelegate sendPluginResult:callbackId: with no format validation' (CDVWKInAppBrowser.m:560–574). This is the exploitation vector—unvalidated callback ID dispatch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript within InAppBrowser WebView posting WKScriptMessage objects with `id` fields matching Cordova callback ID patterns (numeric or known plugin callback constants). Flag rapid/sequential callback invocations or IDs unregistered by the host app.

suggestion.title: Plugin Method Invocation via Untrusted WebView Origin
suggestion.rationale: Article describes arbitrary callbacks triggering plugin methods. Cordova callbacks invoke native APIs (token, account, permission APIs). Detection must correlate plugin invocation with untrusted web content origin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cordova plugin method invocations (account, OAuth, token, credential APIs) originating from JavaScript within InAppBrowser. Correlate with non-standard callback sequences or rapid invocation patterns inconsistent with legitimate UX flows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Web Content Injection into InAppBrowser
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires attacker-controlled web content loaded in InAppBrowser. Article describes 'any web content loaded inside the InAppBrowser can fire any pending Cordova callback.' Detection should identify suspicious URLs or redirect chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect URLs opened in InAppBrowser (Cordova plugin context) from phishing, typosquatting, or attacker infrastructure. Cross-reference against app's bundled/whitelisted domains—external URLs in InAppBrowser increase exploitation surface.

suggestion.title: Token/Credential Theft via Cordova Callback Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article threat includes T1528 and T1098.001 via triggering credential-access callbacks. Detection must flag credential APIs preceded by suspicious WKScriptMessage patterns or abnormal callback dispatch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect calls to token refresh, account metadata retrieval, or permission-grant APIs preceded by rapid/unusual WKScriptMessage dispatch or callback invocations originating from InAppBrowser JavaScript context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-47430 affects specific Cordova InAppBrowser plugin versions on iOS. Asset inventory must identify affected apps for patch/upgrade prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for installed iOS apps with cordova-plugin-inappbrowser version < [PATCHED_VERSION]. Correlate against MDM inventory, app manifests, and store metadata to identify affected users and internal/external apps.

suggestion.title: WebView Origin/Format Validation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Root vulnerability: 'no format validation' of WKScriptMessage `id` field. Detection should flag message-passing patterns with missing origin checks or permissive CORS policies in WebView contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebView message dispatch for missing/permissive origin validation. Flag WKScriptMessage or postMessage calls from non-whitelisted origins that trigger plugin callbacks or native code execution paths.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable when appliance is 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Article references standard asset-exposure hunt templates as canonical detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-10520 against network exposure data. Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from internet or untrusted networks. Verify absence of mTLS/EPMM or restricted HTTPS access controls that would render the appliance inaccessible.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs for request patterns containing shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or known command injection payloads in unauthenticated endpoints. Alert on command execution logged to system context without prior authentication.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'root-level remote code execution.' Any legitimate RCE would originate from authenticated requests; unauthenticated root execution is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service (or injection point) that execute with uid=0 or root context, especially without corresponding sudolog entries or privilege escalation workflows.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Deployed Without mTLS or Restricted HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these controls is a direct exploitability enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances without mTLS enabled and without restricted HTTPS controls. Cross-reference against network exposure scans to identify internet-exposed unprotected instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability only exploitable when 'appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — asset discovery is mandatory first control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances on public internet via DNS, netflow, and scanner data. Cross-reference inventory to locate appliances NOT protected by mTLS client certificates or restricted HTTPS proxy per vendor guidance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' — exploit attempts inject shell metacharacters and command substitution into HTTP request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection signatures: backticks, $(…), command chaining operators (&&, |, ;, >), process substitution, or URL-encoded variants in query strings and POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution Post-Sentry Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation spawns elevated shell or system commands from Sentry process context, anomalous to baseline operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected spawning of bash, sh, cmd, powershell with root/SYSTEM privileges from Sentry service account or daemons. Establish baseline of normal Sentry process tree first; flag deviations as likely post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS and Restricted HTTPS Control Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — audit vendor-recommended mitigations are enforced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all exposed Ivanti Sentry appliances enforce client-certificate mTLS or sit behind IP-restricted HTTPS proxies per vendor guidance. Flag appliances accessible without these controls as vulnerable.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — unmanaged assets lack baseline security posture and monitoring integration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all Ivanti Sentry appliances against MDM enrollment (EPMM, Neurons for MDM). Flag appliances NOT enrolled in expected management framework as unmanaged and higher-risk exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires immediate inventory of unprotected external-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product banners on HTTPS/443 or `/admin/` paths) responding to external queries without mTLS enforcement or HTTPS restrictions. Flag instances where firewall rules permit inbound access from untrusted networks to management interfaces.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Requires monitoring for injection metacharacters in HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns: `;`, `|`, `&`, `$(...)`, backticks, or newlines in query parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Prioritize requests missing valid session authentication.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' as impact. Requires detection of privilege escalation indicators and unexpected root process spawning from web service parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, alert on process creation with uid=0/root spawned by web service processes (httpd, nginx, java) or suspicious parent-child chains. Flag shell process creation (bash, sh) without corresponding user authentication events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Hunting
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch deadline 2026-06-14. Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—requires scanner queries to confirm unpatched instances across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances with unresolved CVE-2026-10520. Correlate with asset inventory to identify federal/critical systems. Flag instances running vulnerable Sentry versions as high-priority remediation targets with compliance deadline context.

suggestion.title: mTLS Enforcement Bypass or HTTPS Restriction Circumvention
suggestion.rationale: Article states protections include 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM'—attack surface depends on misconfiguration or bypass of these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TLS handshake failures, certificate validation errors, or plain-HTTP requests to Sentry ports where mTLS/HTTPS is enforced. Detect attempts to reach management interfaces via non-standard ports, proxies, or forwarding that might circumvent encryption/authentication requirements.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally-Reachable Appliance Inventory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external IP ranges for Ivanti Sentry appliances via product fingerprinting (SSL cert, HTTP headers, API enumeration). Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched versions. Alert on any externally-reachable Sentry not behind mTLS/Neurons gateway as described in mitigation section.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'remote unauthenticated' access to achieve 'root-level remote code execution' — no detection for injection attempts or successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API/web endpoints for payloads indicative of command injection: backticks, shell metacharacters ($(), |, &, ;), or encoded command sequences in HTTP parameters. Correlate with Sentry application error logs showing shell command output or unexpected process spawning. Success indicator: shell output echoed in HTTP response or spawning of sh/bash/cmd.exe process.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Creation from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation yields 'root-level remote code execution' but no hunt for post-RCE privilege escalation or unexpected system-level activity from Sentry process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry service (or child processes spawned by Sentry) executing with UID=0 or SYSTEM privileges. Flag spawning of system utilities (iptables, useradd, apt, curl) from Sentry context. Behavioral baseline: normal Sentry process tree does not spawn shells or privilege-escalation tools.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control Traffic from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE from network-adjacent appliance position but provides no hunt for post-exploitation outbound activity, C2 beaconing, or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Sentry egress (Ivanti servers, MDM backends). Flag unexpected outbound connections on non-standard ports, DNS queries to newly-registered domains, or SSL traffic with suspicious certificate attributes. Prioritize unpatched/unmanaged Sentry instances identified in asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE from infrastructure node positioned adjacent to MDM/management systems but no hunt for post-exploitation reconnaissance, credential theft, or internal scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After RCE detection on Sentry, hunt for outbound port scans (SYN floods), enumeration of adjacent subnets, or credential attacks against MDM backends and management systems. Flag unexpected SSH/RDP sessions initiated from Sentry IP. Sentry compromise is a potential pivot point into high-value infrastructure.

suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Primary indicator for enterprise hunts. Pipeline produced no IOCs despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Ivanti Sentry appliance detected with version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (pre-patch). Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to prioritize unmanaged instances with external network exposure.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance External Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Sentry appliances (identify by SSL cert, HTTP headers, or port 443 + characteristic banner) accessible from external networks without mTLS or HTTPS restrictions. Flag for immediate patch or network segmentation.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry interfaces for command injection metacharacters (backticks, $(…), |, &, ;, pipes, shell redirects) in URL paths, query parameters, or POST bodies. Baseline against known legitimate API patterns.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 200 or 201 responses to Sentry API endpoints that return sensitive data (admin endpoints, configuration, device lists) without prior successful authentication handshake or valid session token. Flag as reconnaissance or exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure Detection

Flag any asset with management interface (port 8443) reachable from external IPs. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances without mTLS/EPMM.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation from Sentry Process

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawned with root or SYSTEM privilege from Ivanti Sentry service context. Flag unexpected child processes (shells, interpreters, network tools) executing under root from service account lineage.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'—unmanaged status is a risk classifier and detection pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and Ivanti management console to identify Sentry instances lacking mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM. Flag unmanaged + externally exposed combinations as critical risk.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Discovery

Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner to flag instances with CVE-2026-10520. Prioritize unmanaged appliances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Without mTLS or HTTPS Restrictions

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — CVE-2026-10520 (Ivanti Sentry)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE-2026-10520 as the substitution variable. Pipeline generated no use cases despite this clear template directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances in vulnerability scanner data matching CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with network scanning to confirm external reachability. Prioritize instances in 'unmanaged state' (not using mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS per article).

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Validation — mTLS and HTTPS Restriction
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' This mitigation-validation use case was missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance configurations for disabled or misconfigured mTLS and HTTPS restriction settings. Flag appliances not enforcing these controls as vulnerable to unauthenticated remote access.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline mapped T1190 but missed the T1059.001 execution vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry for payloads containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $()), command substitution syntax, or Unix command keywords. Correlate with authentication failures or anomalous Sentry service behavior.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieve 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline did not suggest post-exploitation process behavior detection despite this critical indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance system logs and process execution for unexpected child processes spawned under root privileges from Sentry service contexts. Flag interactive shells, reverse shells, or suspicious utility execution (curl, wget, nc, bash, sh).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability can be 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the mandatory attack prerequisite; article itself recommends asset-exposure hunt template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances listening on public-routable IPs/domains. Identify instances lacking mTLS or HTTPS hardening by cross-referencing certificate inspection, EPMM enrollment status, and Neurons for MDM enrollment. Prioritize flagging unmanaged appliances before June 14 due date.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Hit Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and directs readers to validate scanner findings. CVE-2026-10520 signatures from Qualys, Tenable, or MDE should trigger alerting on unpatched Sentry instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-10520 affecting Ivanti Sentry product versions. Alert on any unpatched instances. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm patch status and flag non-compliant hosts for remediation prior to federal due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation attempts inject shell metacharacters into Sentry API/web parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests targeting Ivanti Sentry administrative interfaces (typically port 443) for payloads containing OS command injection metacharacters: |, semicolon, backtick, $(), &, &&, ||. High-fidelity indicators: environment variable syntax, /bin/sh invocations, curl/wget, or redirection operators in request body.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Unexpected process creation or system-level commands executed under Sentry service context indicate successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances: alert on unexpected process creation under root UID, unexpected outbound network connections from Sentry process context, unauthorized file modifications in /etc or /root, or cron/systemd persistence mechanisms added by Sentry service account.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged instances lack mTLS/HTTPS restrictions that block external exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query device inventory and MDM enrollment status to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Cross-reference with network reachability scans to surface unmanaged instances exposed externally. Flag immediately for remediation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Appliance - CVE-2026-10520 Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry) appliances unpatched for CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with external exposure scans and network segmentation logs. Alert on any exposed instances without mTLS EPMM protection.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation - Ivanti Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance processes for unexpected shell execution, command-line arguments suggestive of injection payloads, or child process spawning from the Sentry service with suspicious identifiers.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Privilege Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on uid=0 or root-level processes created by or descended from Ivanti Sentry daemon processes. Monitor /var/log/auth for sudoers violations or privilege escalation attempts tied to the Sentry appliance.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Network Activity from Compromised Ivanti Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Ivanti Sentry appliance network egress (mDM communication, updates). Alert on unexpected outbound connections, DNS queries to non-Ivanti domains, or data exfiltration patterns from the appliance IP.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry service ports (443, 8443) reachable from untrusted networks without mTLS validation or HTTPS access controls. Correlate network telemetry with asset inventory to surface unmanaged appliances. Alert on external inbound HTTPS to Sentry ports.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads in Sentry HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'. Detect exploitation attempts via malicious request payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP request logs for command injection syntax (backticks, $(), command separators, pipes) in parameters and headers. Baseline legitimate Sentry API traffic. Flag requests lacking authentication with suspicious command-like payloads.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawning from Sentry Service Context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Sentry service (java, tomcat, or named Sentry process) spawns child processes running as root/SYSTEM. Monitor for shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) created from Sentry context. Correlate with network intrusion indicators.

suggestion.title: Sentry mTLS/HTTPS Control Disablement

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry config for disabled mTLS enforcement or missing HTTPS restrictions. Monitor config change events disabling security controls. Alert on Sentry instances with unencrypted HTTP traffic to service ports or transition from managed to unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Unmanaged State Configuration Check

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Remote Code Execution Success Indicator

suggestion.title: Sentry mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Protective Control Validation

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection

Flag instances missing mTLS or HTTPS-only access controls and cross-reference against internal asset register for unmanaged deployments.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Payload Detection

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Admin Endpoints

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry sessions (valid session cookies, expected User-Agent strings, geographic patterns). suggestion.title: mTLS / Restricted HTTPS Enforcement Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'protection via mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access.' Verify deployed instances enforce these controls; flag instances accepting HTTP or lacking client-certificate validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Ivanti Sentry deployments for mTLS enforcement (client certificate validation) and HTTPS-only access policies. Alert on instances accepting unencrypted HTTP, responding with invalid/self-signed certificates, or lacking TLS 1.2+ enforcement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Matching

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Application Access Logs

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Sentry Service Context

Flag shell invocations (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell) running as root/SYSTEM from non-root service contexts. Alert on post-exploitation commands (curl, wget, nc, base64) spawned from Sentry processes.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Privilege Escalation to Root

Flag access control policy changes that grant Sentry elevated capabilities (sudoers modifications, capability grants, etc.).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Outbound Communications from Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Once root RCE is achieved, compromised Sentry appliance can serve as beachhead for lateral movement, persistence, or attacker C2 callback. External reachability makes this likely.

Monitor for unexpected connections to external/untrusted destinations, unusual DNS queries, reverse shells, or high-volume data transfers. Alert on connections to known C2 infrastructure or anomalous ports/protocols from Sentry IP space.

suggestion.title: Publicly-reachable Ivanti Sentry detection

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE from Sentry service
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Execution without preceding authentication is the signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry parent processes for child process spawning (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) in absence of user authentication event. Root-level UID execution from Sentry service account is high-confidence indicator of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Command injection payloads in Sentry requests

Correlate with process creation logs to confirm payload execution. High-confidence if followed by root-level child process.

suggestion.title: Root-level code execution from unauthenticated context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution'—process UID 0 spawned by unauthenticated request is exploitation proof.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry + external network exposure correlation
