Flag when compromised credentials are used to access sensitive systems within 24-48 hours of vishing reports.

suggestion.title: Physical Access Paired with Data Copy Operations
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed detection linking physical intrusions to exfiltration. Article states physical intrusions occurred in same campaign as data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate physical access alerts (badge swipe, security camera alerts, door unlock) with bulk file copy/archive operations (robocopy, 7z, zip commands, USB mount followed by file copies) on the same system within ±2 hour window. Alert on unusual user performing admin-level data collection post-physical event.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Staging to Exfiltration Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Data theft campaign requires staging phase before exfil; pipeline generated no detections for bulk staging activity described implicitly in 'data theft' attack goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid copy of large volumes of files to a single staging directory or external share, followed by archive/compression operations, especially when performed by compromised credentials or unfamiliar user accounts. Alert on data concentration patterns (many files in short time from multiple source folders → one destination).

suggestion.title: Extortion Demand Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed detection for extortion communication phase. Article title explicitly mentions 'extortion campaign' but no UC for detecting extortion threats or ransom communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with extortion language, threats to publish exfiltrated data, or demands for payment from external threat actor email addresses. Correlate with prior data exfiltration events on the recipient's domain. Flag threats mentioning stolen data sets or specific company names.

suggestion.title: Vishing-to-VPN-Access Chain
suggestion.rationale: Vishing success typically leads to credential use for VPN or remote access; pipeline missed this chaining detection. Title describes vishing but no detection for post-vishing network access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After vishing report or credential compromise alert, detect new or unusual VPN/RDP connections from the compromised account. Flag logins from IPs geographically inconsistent with the vishing source, or access from consumer ISPs/VPN services during normal business hours when account historically used corporate networks.

suggestion.title: Insider Facilitation of Physical Intrusion
suggestion.rationale: Physical intrusions in corporate settings often require insider assistance or access coordination. Pipeline generated no UC for insider collaboration signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious badge access patterns: valid credentials used to unlock areas outside normal work geography/hours, or badge events preceded by tailgating alerts. Correlate with communication patterns (emails to facilities, IT, security) from vished employees, or unusual after-hours building access by employees with data access roles.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Sentry appliance...with its endpoints externally reachable' is the exploitation prerequisite; asset inventory and network exposure assessment is standard first-response for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product: Sentry) reachable from external networks via port scanning or asset inventory cross-reference. Flag any exposed instances as immediate remediation priority against federal due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Ivanti Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly identified as 'OS command injection' — requires monitoring for metacharacter sequences in HTTP request logs to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry for command injection metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||) in query parameters and POST bodies. Correlate with Sentry process execution logs to identify successful injection.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can trigger RCE — requires monitoring for successful access without valid credentials to normally-protected management APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs for API/endpoint access without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Flag any calls to administrative or management interfaces from IP addresses without prior authentication events.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Privilege Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — post-compromise detection must identify suspicious processes with elevated privileges spawned from web service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service accounts running with root/system privileges. Alert on any privilege escalation from normally unprivileged web server process.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable' in 'unmanaged state'. No external asset inventory hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query DNS records, public IP databases, and passive DNS for Ivanti Sentry product signatures (appliance hostnames, default ports, HTTP banners). Correlate with internal asset inventory to flag externally-facing instances that should be behind firewall/VPN.

suggestion.title: Sentry OS Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' but pipeline provided no execution-phase detection. This is the core attack—spawning arbitrary commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry service processes for spawning shell interpreters (/bin/sh, cmd.exe) or unexpected child processes. Flag HTTP POST/PUT requests to Sentry endpoints immediately followed by process creation under the Sentry service account.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' but no privilege-escalation detection was suggested. Root context is the impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry service (typically non-root) spawning processes with uid=0 or running as SYSTEM. Cross-reference process execution timestamps with web server access logs to narrow suspicious windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should surface scanner hits for this CISA KEV entry as a key hunt. None were included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner or penetration test result flagging CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry. Correlate scanner timestamps with process anomalies on matching assets to detect post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401/403 Bypass Attempts to Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated' access, implying bypassing normal auth. Detection for unusual HTTP patterns to Sentry API endpoints was absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Sentry API traffic patterns. Alert on HTTP requests to known Sentry admin/API paths (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*) without authentication tokens or with atypical payloads (special characters, command separators), especially from external IPs.

suggestion.title: External Exposure Hunt — Ivanti Sentry Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Foundational network exposure detection for pre-compromise hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances reachable from untrusted networks via port scanning, certificate chain analysis, or HTTP banner inspection. Flag instances WITHOUT mTLS or IP-restricted HTTPS gating as unmanaged/exposed. Cross-reference against asset inventory to surface instances not marked as internet-facing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Match — Asset Inventory + Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-06-14. Straightforward IOC-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Ivanti Sentry assets with CVE-2026-10520 findings in scanner results. Stratify by asset classification (externally reachable vs. internal). Enforce remediation tracking against 2026-06-14 federal due date; escalate unpatched internet-exposed instances to critical.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry HTTP Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Need application-layer detection for injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP request logs for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $(), backticks) or common OS command injection patterns in unauthenticated endpoints. High confidence if originating from external IP + successful HTTP 200 response + absence of mTLS certificate chain validation.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawned by Sentry Service (EDR Post-Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' EDR detection for unexpected privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running Ivanti Sentry, alert on root (uid=0) or SYSTEM processes spawned by or under the Sentry service parent (e.g., sentry → /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell). Filter out expected administrative activity; correlate with known external exposure and unpatched CVE-2026-10520 status.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure + unmanaged state = exploitation condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry instances. Cross-correlate with network reachability scans to identify externally accessible instances. Flag instances lacking mTLS EPMM or restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM as unmitigated. Establish SLA for remediation by federal due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Injection attack is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application and WAF logs for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $()), command substitution, or argument injection patterns. Focus on unauthenticated access attempts. Alert on any successful injection indicators (e.g., error messages from command injection, unexpected stdout in responses).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Coverage - CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit hunt instruction: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the canonical recommended detection method from CISA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Activate/verify CVE-2026-10520 detection plugin in all vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.). Ensure Ivanti Sentry instances in asset inventory are scanned. Correlate scan results with patch dates to identify remediation delays. Flag any 'not vulnerable' results on instances with update lag.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'could allow remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-injection execution on Sentry host is the impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events on Ivanti Sentry appliances for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service accounts or root. Alert on command shells, scripting interpreters, or system utilities executed with root privileges from Sentry processes. Baseline legitimate Sentry-spawned processes to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: macOS Plist-based Artifact Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'tracks user menu selections' and is a 'new macOS Tahoe 26 artifact' — strongly suggests plist manipulation for persistence or state-tracking; no use case generated despite this being a classic macOS C2 or persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/Preferences/ and ~/Library/Application Support/ directories for plist file modifications, especially those related to macOS UI/menu state. Look for unexpected plist creation or modification timestamps that predate legitimate user activity, or plist files loaded at boot-time with suspicious origin.

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder privilege escalation pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'workspace-scoped builders (`builder.apps` set but `builder.global` unset)' can escalate via the `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` endpoint. Pipeline did not generate any use case correlating role-scope detection with subsequent global privilege grant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful POST to `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` from a user with workspace-scoped builder role (verified via prior profile queries or user enumeration) with subsequent audit logs showing `builder.global=true` or `admin.global=true` set on that user. Alert if workspace-scoped builder transitions to global scope within 10 minutes of API call.

suggestion.title: Request body field injection via roles/assign API
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'controller then spreads the request body into the SDK call' — this is a body-field-smuggling attack. No detection of unexpected or dangerous fields in the POST body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` containing request body fields outside a whitelist (e.g., `builder`, `admin` objects with nested `global` or `apps` fields that bypass normal role assignment workflows). High-fidelity if paired with successful 200/201 response and evidence of privilege change in audit logs.

suggestion.title: Backdoored Login Binary Execution with Suspicious Network Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article describes backdoor embedded in 'Linux login software'—sshd, PAM, login daemon are prime targets. Phrase: 'backdoored login software' establishes malicious code execution during authentication phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sshd, login, or PAM processes initiating unexpected network connections to non-standard destinations, or login-related binaries executing child processes not in baseline. Flag modifications to /etc/pam.d/* or /etc/ssh/sshd_config_d/* outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Long-Duration Persistence: Unchanged Backdoor Across Software Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'hidden for nearly a decade' indicates the backdoor persisted through multiple software releases without re-infection. This is characteristic of supply-chain compromise, not runtime injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare binary hashes of login-related binaries against official upstream repositories across version deltas. Flag when identical malicious hash persists across multiple product versions or when binary modification timestamps predate vendor release dates.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Compromised Login Path
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored login software can intercept credentials before or after authentication. Article phrase: 'backdoored Linux login software' implies direct access to authentication flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual processes attached to sshd or login parent processes (strace, gdb), or sshd processes reading from unexpected memory regions. Correlate with outbound HTTPS/DNS exfiltration to newly-registered or bulletproof-hosting IPs.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PAM Module Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Linux login software may be backdoored via malicious PAM modules rather than binary replacement. Article refers to 'backdoored software'—could be dynamic injection at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate PAM modules in /lib/security/ and /lib64/security/ monthly; flag unsigned or newly-appeared .so files. Monitor pam-config or pam.conf modifications for entries pointing to non-standard paths or symlinks.

suggestion.title: Login Software Supply Chain: Binary Hash Deviation from Distro Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain backdoor (implied by 'nearly a decade' of secrecy) suggests either upstream compromise or repackaged binaries in update mirrors. Phrase: 'backdoored...software' targets production installs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash all login binaries (sshd, login, su, sudo) against official distro repos and NVD signatures. Alert on mismatches; cross-reference package install logs with OS image builds to detect out-of-band modifications.

suggestion.title: Undetected Backdoor Persistence: Zero-Day or Signature Gap in Auth Stack
suggestion.rationale: Successful hiding 'for nearly a decade' implies bypass of known EDR/integrity-check mechanisms. Article establishes long evasion window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy behavioral baselining on sshd and login: flag unusual syscall sequences, exception handling patterns, or resource allocation (memory, file descriptors) that deviate from clean vendor binaries. Use entropy analysis on executable sections.

suggestion.title: Cordova-plugin-inappbrowser vulnerable versions (3.1.0–6.0.0) on iOS devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies affected version range and patch version (6.0.1). This is the foundational asset-exposure hunt. Article body provides concrete Splunk/KQL (UC_100_2) that pipeline should have detected or generated independently.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for cordova-plugin-inappbrowser versions 3.1.0–6.0.0 on iOS devices. Join with device vulnerability records to confirm CVE-2026-47430 exposure. Prioritize devices in untrusted network zones or with history of loading external web content.

suggestion.title: WKScriptMessage callback ID injection in InAppBrowser context
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'passes the id field from a WKScriptMessage body to commandDelegate sendPluginResult:callbackId: with no format validation' (CDVWKInAppBrowser.m:560–574). This is the actual attack vector, yet pipeline generated zero detections for malformed, non-numeric, or enumerated callback IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WKScriptMessage dispatch logs for 'id' field values that are non-numeric, contain unexpected characters, or do not match the host app's pending-callback registry. Detect rapid successive IDs suggesting callback enumeration or brute-forcing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth/credential grant following InAppBrowser activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1528 (Steal Application Access Token) and T1098.001 (Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials) as post-exploitation impacts. Article provides generic OAuth hunt (UC_OAUTH_ABUSE) but pipeline generated no use cases and no CVE-specific correlation tying InAppBrowser to credential events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate InAppBrowser or cordova-plugin-inappbrowser exploitation indicators with subsequent OAuth consent grants, permission-grant events, or new application credentials within 15 minutes on the same device/user. Escalate detections where InAppBrowser loaded remote/untrusted content immediately before credential event.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Cordova callback execution from untrusted web context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary Cordova callback IDs can be dispatched without validation from InAppBrowser WebViews'—core privilege-boundary bypass. No detection suggested for unexpected callback origins or privilege-escalation implications despite T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism) being listed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument Cordova callback dispatch to log callback ID, origin context (in-app vs. InAppBrowser), and privilege level. Alert when callbacks triggering privileged operations (account modification, token access, permission elevation) are invoked from InAppBrowser WebView context with unregistered callback IDs or from untrusted content origins.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the primary exposure condition; any Sentry appliance accessible from untrusted networks is at immediate risk of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 443, product identification in HTTP headers or TLS certs) originating from external/untrusted ASNs. Cross-reference against known internal Sentry IPs. Alert on any unauthenticated successful connection. The article notes mTLS/restricted HTTPS is protective, so absence of these controls is a gap.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Sentry Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling RCE. Detection must target injection payloads in Sentry request logs, command metacharacters in API parameters, or shell-like syntax in input fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API endpoints and request handlers for shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||) in parameters. Flag requests from unauthenticated sessions. Correlate with process execution events showing unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry daemon.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection must identify unexpected process spawns with elevated privilege context on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process creation (parent: Sentry service, user context: root) that deviates from normal Sentry operations. Flag any command-line execution containing suspicious binaries (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, wget, curl, nc) spawned by Sentry.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Configuration Gap (Unmanaged State)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Appliances lacking mTLS, EPMM integration, or restricted HTTPS are vulnerable; this is a configuration risk hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances; flag any missing mTLS configuration, lacking EPMM integration, or not enforcing restricted HTTPS access. Cross-reference against external-reachability scan data. These appliances are immediate remediation targets.

suggestion.title: Failed/Unusual Authentication Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user,' implying brute-force or bypass attempts preceding injection. Sentry logs should show authentication anomalies from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry login endpoints for high-volume failed auth attempts from external IPs, repeated auth bypass attempts, or unusual HTTP status codes (401, 403 clusters). Flag any successful auth from unauthenticated or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Match (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Appliances reported patched by scanners may be lagging; manual verification needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily hunt: cross-reference Ivanti Sentry instances in your environment against CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability data. Flag all instances running vulnerable versions (< patched release). Do NOT rely solely on scanner status; verify patch dates manually. Federal due date is 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Network Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Unmanaged + external = vulnerable to T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances responding on public IP ranges or DNS-resolvable to external FQDNs. Flag those lacking mTLS or HTTPS enforcement. Search for HTTP responses bearing Ivanti/MobileIron signatures or characteristic admin panel paths (/mifs, /api, /security).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection vulnerability.' This is T1190 + T1059 execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (especially /api/*, /mifs/*, /security/*) for command injection payloads. Watch for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks) in parameters, especially unauthenticated requests. Correlate with absence of authentication headers.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' RCE indicator is unusual root spawning and command execution from network-reachable daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry daemon (typically running under service account) executing as root or using setuid. Alert on shell invocations (bash, sh) or reverse shells originating from network interfaces.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Enforcement Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Detection opportunity is verifying hardening in place.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Sentry endpoints enforce mutual TLS (check certificate requirements, cipher suites) and restrict HTTP access. Alert if mTLS is disabled, HTTPS enforcement is removed, or endpoints downgrade to plaintext communication. Cross-reference with asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14,' establishing critical patching deadline. Detect systems still running vulnerable versions after deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Ivanti Sentry instances in asset database with patch status from scanner. Flag any system not reporting Sentry version ≥ [patched version] after 2026-06-14. Correlate scanner silence with network-exposed instances to identify drift.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states appliance vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the precondition for all exploitation; pipeline missed foundational asset-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry appliances with listening sockets on public or untrusted networks. Query asset inventory for externally-exposed instances; cross-reference against firewall inbound rules. Alert on any new external exposure or removal of mTLS/EPMM restricting access (mentioned in article as protective controls).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2026-10520 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as a required hunt. Pipeline did not generate vulnerability scanner use case or correlate with patch-due-date (2026-06-14).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-10520 on all Ivanti Sentry instances. Prioritize findings on externally-reachable appliances. Flag instances remaining vulnerable >7 days post patch-release date (2026-06-14). Coordinate with patch-management team for immediate remediation of critical-severity RCE on externally-exposed assets.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' — implies attacker sends shell metacharacters or command delimiters in HTTP request parameters. Pipeline generated no injection-detection hypothesis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry appliance for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, ||, $(), backticks, etc.) in query parameters and POST bodies. Alert on requests containing both benign parameter names and suspicious command injection patterns. Correlate with HTTP 200/500 responses indicating potential command execution or error-based exploitation.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution: Root-Level Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline did not suggest detection of RCE artifacts (child process spawning, privilege escalation to UID 0).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by Sentry application process (sh, bash, powershell, cmd.exe). Alert on process execution with UID 0 / SYSTEM privilege originating from Sentry application context. Correlate process-creation events with HTTP request logs to the appliance to establish exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Sentry as an appliance managing endpoints; successful RCE grants pivot point for lateral movement. Pipeline did not suggest detection of outbound reconnaissance or credential abuse from compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound network connections from Sentry appliance to internal subnets, managed endpoints, or attacker infrastructure post-compromise. Alert on DNS queries from appliance to internal hosts, credential-spraying attempts, or port-scanning activity originating from compromised appliance. Track lateral movement patterns typical of post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Tracking: CVE-2026-10520 Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline did not suggest compliance tracking or post-remediation verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post patch-release (2026-06-14), verify all Ivanti Sentry appliances have been patched across the fleet. Query patch-management logs for deployment status; flag instances still running vulnerable versions >14 days after due-date. Alert on rollback attempts or patching failures on externally-exposed Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`.' Baseline detection for any CISA KEV entry; directly cited in source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances (product identification, version, exposure: external vs. internal). Flag instances lacking patches as of federal due date 2026-06-14. Prioritize appliances in 'unmanaged state' (no mTLS, no EPMM integration) as imminent compromise risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation to Sentry Management Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline failed to surface the execution phase—inbound requests with shell metacharacters targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry management interface logs and HTTP proxies for requests containing OS command metacharacters (pipe, ampersand, semicolon, backtick, $(), etc.) in URI and request body. Correlate with successful HTTP responses (2xx, 3xx) to assess exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Process Spawning from Sentry Services
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation will spawn processes at UID 0 from Sentry daemon contexts; pipeline omitted impact-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts (mobileironsentryserver, sentry daemon, etc.) executing with UID 0 or EUID 0. Scope to unexpected binaries (shells, curl, wget, nc, dd, iptables).

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Regression: mTLS Disable, Unmanaged Transition
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible.' State transitions that remove protections are high-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration changes disabling mTLS enforcement, removing EPMM enrollment, setting appliances to unmanaged mode, or opening HTTPS access beyond restricted subnets. These transitions create exploit preconditions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Identifier Match: CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'CVE-2026-10520' as the vulnerability central to this advisory; any asset scanner or vulnerability manager hit must be correlated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances (any version) flagged with CVE-2026-10520 or unpatched Sentry appliances. Correlate against the federal remediation due date (2026-06-14). High-fidelity indicator of affected systems.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'; this is the exposure condition enabling T1190
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances with routable external IPs or DNS resolution from untrusted networks. Cross-check against mTLS/EPMM enrollment and Neurons for MDM status—unmanaged/unprotected instances are vulnerable. Network exposure hunt baseline.

suggestion.title: Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'; detect payloads with shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, backticks, $()) targeting Sentry endpoints

suggestion.title: Sentry Root Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' is achievable. Post-exploitation detection must identify unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry daemon with UID 0 privilege, indicating command injection success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service/parent process (common parents: java, sentry, tomcat) running as UID 0 (root). Baseline legitimate children (system services, agents). Flag anomalies: shell processes (bash, sh, zsh), network tools (curl, wget, nc), or interpreter processes (python, perl, ruby) spawned with root. Include command-line inspection for suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Sentry Post-Exploitation Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE enables file system modification for backdoor/persistence. Article does not detail post-exploitation but root privilege implies capability for cron, systemd, or root-level service persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance filesystem for unauthorized modifications: new files in /root, /opt/sentry, /etc with unexpected ownership; cron job additions; systemd service unit registration; SSH authorized_keys modifications. Baseline expected patch cycles; escalate on unexplained changes especially if occurring outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Sentry Management State Loss
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires 'unmanaged state' precondition. Continuous validation that appliances maintain proper management enrollment (mTLS EPMM or Neurons MDM) prevents exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Ivanti Sentry management state telemetry (enrollment status, last-sync timestamp, mTLS session validity, policy version). Alert on state transitions to 'unmanaged', management heartbeat loss >4 hours, or mTLS/HTTPS enforcement bypass. Correlate with external connectivity scanning; flag unmanaged+externally-routable as immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability only exploitable when 'endpoints externally reachable' — this is the gating condition. Scanning/enumerating which Sentry appliances are internet-facing is the mandatory first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results, CMDB, and SSL certificate data for Ivanti Sentry product instances with public-IP exposure or resolvable hostnames. Cross-reference with firewall/WAF rules permitting inbound access. Flag appliances not behind mTLS or HTTPS restrictions.

suggestion.title: Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' requiring 'unauthenticated' access. Detection should focus on malformed/suspicious HTTP payloads to Sentry endpoints attempting to inject shell metacharacters (command separators, redirects, subshells).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for requests containing OS command injection patterns (;, |, &, $(), backticks, newlines, etc.) in query parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Correlate with 4xx responses (failed injection) and subsequent 2xx (successful exploitation). Alert on unauthenticated requests reaching vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Sentry Process Spawning Child Commands as Root
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'achieve[s] root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Post-exploitation detection should identify unusual child processes spawned from Sentry parent processes running under root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where Parent Process = Ivanti Sentry service/daemon, Parent User = root/SYSTEM, and Child Process contains command-line patterns inconsistent with legitimate Sentry operation (bash, sh, cmd, powershell, curl, wget, ncat). Baseline expected child processes for your Sentry deployment and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Network Connection Abnormality Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After achieving RCE, attacker likely pivots or exfiltrates data. Article implies Sentry controls endpoint management, making compromised Sentry a springboard for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for network connections initiated by Sentry service processes (normal = queries to Ivanti cloud, LDAP, internal PKI). Alert on outbound connections to external IPs, unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8888, common reverse-shell ports), or repeated connection attempts post-exploitation timeframe.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration/Log Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE implies ability to modify logs, disable auditing, or alter Sentry configuration. Detection should capture suspicious writes to Sentry directories or log rotation/clearing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system writes to Sentry installation directory, /var/log/sentry*, or configuration files (/etc/sentry*). Alert on deletion or truncation of log files, especially within minutes of exploitation-attempt timeframe. Track calls to log-rotation tools (logrotate, clear logs) initiated from non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Core hunt is identifying exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances listening on public IPs or accessible via external DNS. Cross-reference with asset inventory to surface unmanaged instances. Filter for those NOT behind mTLS/HTTPS restrictions per vendor guidance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Command injection is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry processes for unusual child process spawning (shell interpreters, script engines) or encoded command patterns typical of injection payloads. Alert on command execution spawned by unauthenticated network requests.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Root-Level Privilege Escalation on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution' from unauthenticated access, representing privilege escalation from no-auth context to root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry processes executing with root/SYSTEM privileges when spawned from network-facing daemons. Detect sudo or privilege-escalation calls lacking legitimate operational context.

suggestion.title: Sentry External Connectivity Configuration Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability only exploitable when 'endpoints externally reachable.' Configuration changes enabling external access or disabling mitigations (mTLS, HTTPS restrictions) are precursors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance network policies and firewall rules for changes increasing external accessibility. Alert if mTLS or HTTPS access controls are disabled or if appliance transitions from internal-only to externally-routable.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Confirmation Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalogs only 'vulnerabilities that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Confirm patch status and exposure across fleet, accounting for patch-lag risk windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched. Investigate patched instances for exposure overlap—when they were externally reachable before patch application.

suggestion.title: Detect vishing campaign reconnaissance patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states UNC3753 'Used Vishing' as primary attack vector. Article phrases: 'vishing and physical intrusions.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for phone-based social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for statistically unusual inbound call volumes to specific departments or employee lists, followed within 24 hours by failed login attempts, credential submissions to fake portals, or authentication events from new geographic sources.

suggestion.title: Detect data collection following physical facility access anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Physical Intrusions' as attack method paired with 'Data Theft' objective. Phrase: 'Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft.' Pipeline missed correlation between physical access and cyber exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk file collection from sensitive shares and unusual USB/removable media activity following unauthorized badge access, after-hours facility presence, or guest network connections in security-sensitive areas.

suggestion.title: Detect data exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign'—central to extortion capability is confirmed exfiltration. Article states threat stole data for extortion leverage. Pipeline missed exfiltration detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-volume data transfers to non-whitelisted external cloud services, file-sharing platforms, or residential IP ranges, especially during off-hours or from compromised internal accounts with recent credential reuse indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect extortion threat communication and ransom messaging
suggestion.rationale: Campaign objective is 'Extortion'—article explicitly states threat demanded payment. Pipeline generated zero use cases for ransom-demand communication detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails containing keywords associated with data extortion (exfiltrated, leaked, ransom, encrypted, deadline, payment, proof-of-breach) paired with organization name references or specific data-set descriptions, or URLs to known extortion/leak-site infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—canonical first hunt per referenced template is asset inventory of vulnerable Sentry versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 matches against Ivanti Sentry appliances. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify deployed instances, confirm version, verify patch status, and prioritize appliances marked unmanaged or with unknown management state.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation via Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection'—detect injection payloads and spawned processes from Sentry context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry access logs for URL/parameter patterns indicative of command injection (shell metacharacters: backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, command separators). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service processes, particularly shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or with privilege level elevated to root/SYSTEM.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation requires 'Sentry appliance in an unmanaged state'—identify Sentry instances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliance configuration database (or via API) to enumerate all instances and verify enrollment status in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Flag any with management_status = unmanaged, null, or unknown. Verify mTLS is enabled and HTTPS restrictions are active per mitigation controls.

suggestion.title: External Network Exposure of Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'endpoints externally reachable' as prerequisite—audit and alert on Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct regular network reachability scans of Sentry appliances from external/WAN segments. Alert if Sentry default ports (443, 8443, admin interfaces) respond to external connection attempts. Verify firewall rules restrict inbound access to Sentry to trusted networks only.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation results in 'root-level remote code execution'—detect commands executing with root privileges following injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned with UID=0/SYSTEM integrity level that originate from Sentry processes or are triggered by Sentry request handlers. Correlate command injection detection signals with subsequent privilege-elevated process creation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'CVE-2026-10520' as the canonical vulnerability indicator. Pipeline produced no IOCs or use cases despite this being a CISA KEV entry with active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platforms for any assets running Ivanti Sentry versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with exposed instances detected via network scanning.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation requires 'Sentry appliance in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the prerequisite for the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify via HTTP headers, certificate CN, or known ports) accessible from untrusted networks without protective mTLS. Appliances not communicating with MDM/EPMM for >7 days likely in unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'; exploitation requires sending injection payloads to the appliance. Article phrase: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs for unauthenticated requests containing command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), backticks, &&), executable names (bash, sh, cmd.exe), or common injection frameworks in URI parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Following Sentry Web Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'root-level remote code execution'; successful exploitation results in arbitrary commands executing as UID 0. This is the post-exploitation detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints with subsequent high-privilege process creation (UID 0) on the appliance. Flag process lineage: web server → shell → root-level command execution within 60 seconds of request.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is an enabled condition for attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Sentry appliances with no MDM (Neurons for MDM) or EPMM registration, no mTLS handshakes, or absent management heartbeats for ≥7 days. These systems lack the mitigating controls referenced in the article.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—implying attackers will attempt to circumvent these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake failures, certificate validation errors, or repeated HTTP (non-HTTPS) requests to Sentry endpoints. Flag protocol downgrade attempts, invalid client certificates, or bypass techniques targeting mTLS enforcement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag scanner findings reporting CVE-2026-10520 or Ivanti Sentry versions identified as vulnerable. Cross-reference with network segment data to confirm external reachability. Prioritize unmanaged appliances (those without mTLS/Neurons for MDM enrollment).

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only 'where Sentry appliance is in unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the requisite initial-access condition; no UC generated for this discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (port 443/8443) with inbound routes from untrusted networks or public internet. Query asset management systems for Sentry appliances not restricted to internal-only access. Correlate with mTLS enrollment status—managed instances have restricted interfaces; flag unmanaged + exposed.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability allowing remote unauthenticated user' to execute code. Exploitation phase (T1059) entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP request logs for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks) in URL parameters or POST bodies, particularly targeting known Sentry endpoints. Unauthenticated requests with injection signatures followed by process creation on the appliance are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Root-level RCE from Sentry Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation phase (T1548) missing. Root RCE is the post-exploitation artifact; detection must look for service-to-root process elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where Ivanti Sentry web service (non-root parent) spawns UID=0 child processes (shells, utilities). Monitor for unexpected commands (curl, wget, bash, python, nc) launched with root privileges from Sentry process context. Correlate temporal proximity with unauthenticated HTTP access.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Restriction Configuration Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS 'make interfaces inaccessible' to attackers—conversely, absence of these controls is a vulnerability condition. No defensive posture assessment UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configurations for mTLS enablement and HTTPS-only enforcement. Verify Sentry appliances are enrolled in Neurons for MDM. Flag any instances with deprecated HTTP endpoints, missing client certificate requirements, or permissive CORS policies. Correlate with external reachability data.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states only 'unmanaged' appliances are exploitable; mTLS/Neurons enrollment protects. Identifying unmanaged instances is the foundational discovery hunt; pipeline output is blank.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EMM platforms (Neurons for MDM) for Ivanti Sentry enrollment status. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Prioritize unmanaged + externally routable appliances. Confirm patch status against CVE-2026-10520 remediation timeline (federal due date 2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed to Unauthenticated External Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'unmanaged state' as the vulnerability exposure surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry default ports (443, 8443) from external networks. Flag Sentry instances not behind mTLS EPMM or Neurons for MDM gateway. Monitor for scanning/probing patterns from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload in Sentry Request
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters in parameters: ;, |, backticks, $(), newlines. High-fidelity: external source sends injection pattern and receives 200/302 response from vulnerable endpoint.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation manifests as unexpected privileged child processes from web service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service running as root (especially shell, file utilities, or network tools). Baseline: Sentry service typically runs unprivileged; root child processes = post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Lateral Movement via Outbound Connection
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation behavior; attacker uses root RCE from appliance for internal reconnaissance, C2, or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry service to non-whitelisted destinations. Flag internal IP connections, high-entropy domains, or suspicious ASNs. Correlate with confirmed unpatched CVE-2026-10520 status.

suggestion.title: Missing mTLS Certificate in Direct Sentry Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS...makes interfaces inaccessible' — legitimate traffic includes these protections; absence indicates bypass or unprotected exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Sentry instances expected behind mTLS/EPMM gateway: alert on requests missing mutual TLS certificates, requests arriving directly at Sentry port (bypass), or requests from IPs outside approved MDM infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Version Detection via Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article provides CVE-2026-10520 as the vulnerability identifier and is CISA KEV (federal agencies required to patch by 2026-06-14); baseline is vulnerability scanner coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry appliances and confirm patching status. Alert on exposed version banners, vulnerable version detection in unauthenticated API responses, or missing patches. Flag any externally reachable unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Repository Unauthorized Commit/Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 400+ packages hijacked; implies attacker injected malicious code into package sources. No UC for detecting unauthorized commits, version anomalies, or account takeover on AUR maintainer accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AUR repository for unusual commits outside maintainer's typical workflow (new committer, unusual hours, large diffs to build scripts or PKGBUILD files). Alert on package version bumps without corresponding source hash changes. Detect compromised credentials via velocity (multiple packages modified in short window by single account).

suggestion.title: Package Installation with Malicious Execution
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages execute attacker code during install. No UC captures suspicious process spawning, file writes, or network activity during package decompression/build phase (T1059).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash/sh processes spawned from /tmp/.pacman-* or similar AUR build directories executing unexpected binaries, writing to system paths, or making network calls. Baseline normal makepkg behavior and flag deviations (curl to C&C, iptables modifications, cron injections).

suggestion.title: Package Signature/Hash Integrity Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often require compromising package checksums or signatures. No UC for verifying package integrity against known-good hashes or detecting signature validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs (pacman) for GPG signature verification failures, hash mismatches, or fallback to unsigned downloads. Flag packages downloaded from non-standard mirrors. Compare installed package checksums to upstream AUR repository values post-install.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 400+ packages implies either credential theft or account compromise at scale. No UC for detecting abnormal AUR login patterns, unusual geographic access, or MFA bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AUR account logins from new/unusual IP ranges, velocity spikes in package uploads, logins at unusual hours compared to maintainer baseline, or MFA disable events. Cross-reference multiple maintainer accounts compromised within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Persistence Mechanisms in Packages
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages likely establish persistence (cron, systemd, shell hooks). Article context implies packages affect user systems. No UC for detecting persistence installation during/after package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron jobs, systemd timers, or bashrc/profile modifications written by package installation. Flag packages that create scheduled tasks for non-standard intervals or modify user shell initialization after install. Alert on file writes to ~/.config or /etc during makepkg execution.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Mirror/Repository Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may have compromised AUR infrastructure or mirrors. No UC for detecting repository serving mismatched packages, unusual metadata, or serves different content to different clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package hashes downloaded from different mirrors/times. Alert on CDN/mirror serving different package content for same version string. Monitor DNS for AUR domain hijacking or unusual NS/A record changes. Flag HTTP redirects to non-standard package mirrors.

suggestion.title: Forensic Artifact Creation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered'—implies the artifact exists at a specific file path. Pipeline should detect writes to or creation of this artifact file (path not available due to missing article body).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of the macOS Tahoe 26 artifact file. Alert on processes accessing the artifact outside expected forensic tools. Detect bulk reads of artifact data that could indicate exfiltration of user activity records.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Menu Interaction Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the artifact as 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—sensitive activity log. Detect non-privileged or non-expected process reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes attempting to read the artifact file that are not system utilities, forensic tools, or the OS kernel. Monitor for repeated sequential reads that suggest data scraping for espionage.

suggestion.title: Artifact Exfiltration via Network I/O
suggestion.rationale: If threat actor learns of this artifact's forensic value (via article or research), they may attempt to steal accumulated user menu data. Pipeline should correlate artifact access with suspicious network outbound.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-frequency reads of the artifact file with unusual outbound network connections. Alert on compression or encoding of data read from artifact path followed by exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder requests roles/assign endpoint before privilege grant
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'builderOrAdmin middleware passes any user who is a builder' but 'workspace-scoped builders (builder.apps set but builder.global unset)' should never be calling this endpoint. The middleware bypass is the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign from a user whose audit log shows builder.global=false. The middleware bypass means workspace-scoped builders reach an endpoint they should not. Even non-200 responses are suspicious and warrant investigation.

suggestion.title: POST to roles/assign contains both app-level and global role fields
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'controller spreads request body into SDK call' — the SDK grants builder.global=true or admin privileges without re-validating scope. A workspace-scoped builder submitting global role fields is exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST bodies to /api/public/v1/roles/assign for presence of global-scope role assignments (builder.global, admin.global, admin role) from users without global privileges. Any POST body containing both app-scoped and global-scoped role fields is exploitation in progress.

suggestion.title: Admin or builder role grant to service account or newly-created user
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker escalating 'workspace-scoped builder' to global admin—a privilege transition. Monitor for rapid admin grants to users with no prior admin API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin or global builder role assignments to users with no prior API calls, no prior audit log presence, or accounts matching service-account naming patterns. Excludes planned onboarding (use context from ServiceNow/ITSM if available).

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder queries self endpoint after successful roles/assign
suggestion.rationale: Article describes escalation to global admin. Post-exploitation, attacker would verify the privilege grant by calling /api/global/self or similar to confirm builder.global=true.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chain detection: POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign (200/201) immediately followed by GET to /api/global/self* or similar self-verification endpoint within 5 seconds, from the same user/IP. Attacker verifying successful privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Lateral escalation: admin grants admin to other users in same workspace
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on individual escalation but doesn't address lateral spread. Once attacker gains admin, they can use the same vulnerable endpoint to grant admin to other compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where a newly-promoted admin (from roles/assign) immediately calls roles/assign themselves to promote other accounts. Multiple roles/assign POSTs from different users targeting the same workspace within 2 minutes suggests attacker spreading privileges laterally.

suggestion.title: IP or API key pivots after successful admin grant via roles/assign
suggestion.rationale: Article describes workspace-scoped builder exploit. After successful escalation, attacker may pivot to new IP or API key to obfuscate the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a successful POST to roles/assign (200/201) followed by audit/API log entries from a different source IP or API key, attributed to the same user or workspace, within 10 minutes. Suggests attacker using privilege escalation as a pivot point.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Hash-Mismatched Authentication Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'backdoored Linux Login Software' — core attack vector is injection into /bin/login, sshd, or PAM libraries. 'Hide for nearly a decade' implies binaries evaded hash-based integrity checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modification events to /bin/login, /usr/bin/sshd, /lib/pam*, /etc/pam.d/* and hash mismatches against baseline or vendor manifests. Correlate mtime changes with missing audit logs or log deletion events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Egress from sshd or login Process
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persisting 'nearly a decade' requires command-and-control or systematic data exfiltration; authentication binaries should have zero expected outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline sshd and login processes for zero network egress. Alert on outbound connections initiated by these PIDs to any external IP or non-standard ports, especially over multi-year persistence windows.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Compromised Authentication Subsystem
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'backdoored Linux Login Software' directly handles UID/GID assignment during authentication; enables unauthorized privilege escalation without sudo/setuid.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation with unexpected privilege levels spawned from sshd or login parent. Detect spawning of root shells (uid=0) from unprivileged source sessions or unusual child processes from authentication daemons.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious Package in OS Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Linux Login Software' backdoor with system-wide impact and decade-long evasion; implies infection at package distribution or source code level pre-deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track binary hashes of login/sshd packages against upstream vendor GPG signatures and SBOM metadata. Alert on unsigned packages, hash mismatches in installed vs. repository versions, or packages from unexpected mirrors.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Intercepted Authentication Calls
suggestion.rationale: Compromised /bin/login or PAM library enables credential interception at kernel boundary; article's multi-year persistence implies active credential collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous read/write syscalls from sshd/login to sensitive memory regions or files (/etc/shadow, /proc/*/mem). Detect function hooking or LD_PRELOAD patterns targeting libc credential functions.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module or eBPF Hook Enabling Multi-Year Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hide for nearly a decade' — userland-only backdoor would be detected by package manager re-verification or OS updates. Implies kernel-level persistence or bootkit-style mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned kernel modules loaded post-boot, eBPF programs attached to security-sensitive hooks, or processes that map kernel memory. Detect hidden processes via discrepancies between /proc enumeration and netstat/ps output.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection — Ivanti Sentry Scanning Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 as CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild) with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14. Pipeline must trigger on scanner matches and patch compliance gaps. Cite: 'CVE-2026-10520...Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scans detect Ivanti Sentry product instances or CVE-2026-10520 matches in environment. Cross-reference against federal patch deadline (2026-06-14) and escalate any overdue assets as high-priority due to known active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability only exploitable when appliance is 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints with command-injection payloads: shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `), command substitution ($(), backticks), OS-specific binary paths (/bin/sh, cmd.exe), or multi-stage encoding typical of injection exploits.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Instance Inventory Gaps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly conditions exploit on 'unmanaged state'—mTLS and restricted HTTPS prevent attacks. No detection for discovery of unmanaged appliances or inventory drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry appliances missing management-plane heartbeats (EPMM/Neurons MDM), deployed outside restricted network zones, or failing to report for >7 days. Flag unpatched instances in this category for CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution'—implicit privilege escalation. No post-exploitation RCE detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry service (UID<1000 or known sentry account) spawning SYSTEM/root processes, interactive shells, or commands outside maintenance windows. Correlate with failed/successful authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user'—the attack requires no credentials. No authentication-bypass or unauthorized-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 200 responses from Ivanti Sentry admin/API endpoints (/api/*, /admin, /system) from external IPs without prior session establishment or valid auth tokens. Alert on unauthenticated requests to endpoints that should require authentication.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external asset exposure is the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (product identifiers, version strings, API signatures) responding to external network queries. Cross-reference vulnerability scan results flagging CVE-2026-10520 against network baselines to identify externally reachable instances. Prioritize unmanaged appliances not protected by mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Scanner-Sourced Vulnerability Alert
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV deadline of 2026-06-14 requires urgent remediation tracking. Pipeline must surface CVE presence in scanner output to operationalize remediation workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert whenever Qualys, Nessus, or other vulnerability scanners flag CVE-2026-10520 in asset discovery. Include affected asset inventory, vulnerable versions, federal remediation deadline, and correlation with externally reachable instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection Against Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector leading to root RCE. Direct payload detection on exposed Sentry endpoints captures exploitation in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP traffic to Ivanti Sentry API/web endpoints for command injection signatures: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), command substitution), Unix command separators (|, ;, &, &&, ||), base64-encoded payloads, and common payload prefixes (/bin/sh, exec, system). Flag POST/GET parameters destined for backend command execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation detection captures actual command execution activity on compromised Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process execution logs for unexpected root-privilege spawns, especially shell interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, /bin/ksh), system utilities (curl, wget, nc, socat), scripting languages (python, perl, ruby), and reverse shell indicators. Baseline expected Sentry daemon processes and alert on anomalous deviations.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitability depends on 'unmanaged state' appliances; mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS mitigates. Identify configuration gaps in management frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry asset inventory against MDM enrollment records and EPMM management console. Flag instances absent from EPMM, lacking valid mTLS certificates, or not protected by restricted HTTPS firewall rules. Correlate with CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability scanner findings.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset-exposure hunt is canonical for any CISA KEV. Pipeline produced zero UCs despite article recommending this hunt by name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for external HTTP/HTTPS connections to Ivanti Sentry appliances (detect via fingerprint or certificate CN='Sentry'). Correlate with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Leverage SHODAN/Censys queries for external surface mapping.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Core exploitation pattern entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, $()) in Sentry API/web requests from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with root process spawning or command execution logs on Sentry appliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Code Execution Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow...achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection for privilege escalation outcome missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected processes spawned by Sentry service account running with UID 0 or in SYSTEM context. Detect execution of shell, compiler, or lateral-movement tools (ssh, nc, wget) post-command-injection indicators.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Detection should include inventory/configuration assessment, not just network traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and EPMM/MDM enrollment logs for Ivanti Sentry instances. Flag appliances NOT listed as managed via mTLS+EPMM or with restricted HTTPS access per article's mitigation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article's IOC section explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; this is the minimum extractable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry inventory. Flag any host showing vulnerable version. Cross-reference with external-reachability and management-state indicators.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Asset Inventory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry instances exposed on public internet via port scanning, certificate transparency logs, or asset management systems. Cross-reference hostnames against known vulnerable versions prior to patch deadline (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
