suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters in query parameters or POST bodies. Baseline normal traffic pre-patch; alert on injection-like patterns originating from external IPs to vulnerable appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user'—the exploit requires zero credentials. Flag unauthenticated HTTP requests reaching sensitive Sentry endpoints (config, API, command execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authenticated vs. unauthenticated Sentry requests. Alert on HTTP requests lacking expected authentication tokens/headers (Authorization, X-Auth, etc.) targeting administrative endpoints or command execution paths.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Remote Code Execution Success Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome—successful exploitation produces observable post-execution artifacts (unexpected privileged processes, file creation as root, privilege-escalation logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry process (or parent Java process) spawning shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /bin/zsh) with arguments; file creation/modification by root originating from Sentry service context; privilege-escalation logs correlated temporally with HTTP access to Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Audit

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for Ivanti Sentry version ≤ [last vulnerable version]. Inspect HTTP Server headers and SSL certificate issuer strings for version strings. Identify all unpatched systems post 2026-06-14 for escalation.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Network Exposure

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt — Sentry Endpoint

suggestion.title: Root Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service Parent

Flag bash, sh, PowerShell, cmd.exe, or reverse-shell executables as children of Sentry JVM/Node process. Alert on process trees indicating post-RCE lateral movement or data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged or Unenrolled Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' mTLS and EPMM/Neurons MDM enrollment provides visibility and control. Requires configuration + enrollment audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query EPMM (Ivanti MDM) or Neurons for MDM agent enrollment logs for Sentry appliances NOT reporting management status or with agent health = 'unenrolled' / 'unmanaged'. Cross-reference with network exposure scan. Unmanaged appliances with external reachability are immediate remediation priority.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' as prerequisite for vulnerability exploitation; pipeline failed to generate asset-exposure hunt, which is canonical for publicly-accessible critical appliances
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry and MobileIron Sentry appliances with external network accessibility via asset inventory correlation, public scanning (SHODAN/Censys), and network flow analysis. Prioritize unmanaged instances and those without mTLS/restricted HTTPS protections mentioned in article.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry service processes for spawned shell commands (bash, sh, /bin/sh, cmd.exe) without preceding authentication audit trail. Alert on process creation from Sentry daemons containing shell metacharacters (pipes, backticks, substitution) in command line, especially execution with elevated UID.

suggestion.title: Root-level Code Execution from Sentry Service Process

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Sentry service daemon and child executes with UID=0 (root) without intervening sudo/su audit event. Flag this pattern as direct RCE exploitation, not legitimate service operation, particularly when paired with unexpected command execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Unpatched Sentry Inventory Against Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active exploitation; pipeline generated no vulnerability-based hunt. Proactive scan-based detection required to close exposure window before federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Nessus/Tenable/Qualys for CVE-2026-10520 detections across all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Cross-reference with asset inventory and patch management. Escalate any remaining unpatched instances post-deadline as imminent breach risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' No application-layer attack detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with unauthenticated request patterns. Cross-reference process execution events for shell spawning from Ivanti service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry service and child runs with uid=0 or exhibits privilege elevation (setuid boundary crossing). Alert on shell interpreters (bash, sh, zsh) spawned from java or Ivanti application processes.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Network Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' as precondition; no network exposure or asset inventory detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry appliances (identified by HTTP headers, certificate CN, banner) with inbound rules from 0.0.0.0/0. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for Ivanti Sentry instances against network firewall policy to identify uncontrolled exposure post-patch deadline (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Vulnerability Scan Correlation

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Presence — Patch Deadline Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with explicit 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' No post-deadline vulnerability persistence detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry instances matching vulnerable version patterns for CVE-2026-10520 are detected in scans dated after 2026-06-14. Correlate with network exposure and lack of mTLS/Neurons enrollment to score criticality.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated POST/GET Request Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. No detection for authentication bypass or unauthenticated exploitation was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry that lack valid authentication headers (Authorization, session cookie, OAuth token) yet trigger application error responses or command output. Flag unauthenticated requests that return shell errors, command output, or file listing artifacts.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects appliances 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—canonical initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry service fingerprints (port 8443, /sentry endpoints, application banners) reachable from the internet. Cross-reference external exposure against internal asset inventory; flag any Sentry instance marked 'unmanaged' or lacking mTLS/HTTPS restrictions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation path. Detect missing or invalid authentication tokens in requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs for HTTP(S) requests without valid session cookies or authentication headers. Flag successful access or 200/302 responses to protected endpoints when no prior authentication occurred.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'—the exploitation mechanism. Detect shell metacharacters and command syntax in HTTP request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;|&$(){}[]<>"'`), command substitution syntax (`$(...)`, backticks), or pipe-chained commands. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses or subsequent system activity from the Sentry process.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article promises 'root-level remote code execution.' Detect child processes created with elevated privileges (UID 0 / SYSTEM) from Sentry-related processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Sentry process trees (parent/child relationships, user context). Alert on any child process spawned from Sentry with effective UID=0 (Linux) or running as SYSTEM (Windows), or unexpected process names (shells, utilities) under Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation grants root privileges; detect sudoers abuse, setuid binaries modified/executed by Sentry, or capability transitions to UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sudo logs for entries run by Sentry service user. Search audit logs for sudoers file modifications, setuid binary execution, or uid/gid transitions from Sentry's user ID to root (UID 0). Alert if these occur during or shortly after unauthenticated HTTP access.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Egress from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may pivot or exfiltrate data. Detect unexpected outbound network connections from Sentry processes outside baseline operational profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Sentry appliance network behavior (allowed destinations, protocols, ports). Alert on unexpected outbound connections from Sentry processes to non-whitelisted external IPs, dynamic DNS, or non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — Unmanaged Appliance Exposure Hunt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks on known management ports, cross-correlated with vulnerability-scanner data and MDM enrollment records. Flag any lacking mTLS certificates or EPMM/Neurons for MDM enrollment markers.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/API traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters, command separators, or encoded payloads indicative of command injection (e.g., semicolons, pipes, backticks, bash -c patterns in query parameters or POST bodies).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — Suspicious Root-Level Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation, unexpected processes with root privileges spawned from the Sentry service account are the execution footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service processes (or the appliance OS kernel) with root/SYSTEM context, especially unexpected shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe), network tools (wget, curl, nc), or privilege-escalation utilities.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — mTLS/EPMM Protection Bypass or Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detect when these mitigations are absent or circumvented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances lacking valid mTLS client certificates or EPMM-issued certificates on inbound connections. Correlate network access logs with MDM enrollment records to flag externally-reachable instances with missing enrollment.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 — Vulnerability Scanner Asset Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends: 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Standard IOC correlation for asset identification and patch-status tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti Sentry appliances flagged as vulnerable for CVE-2026-10520 in scan output with patch-deployment logs. Alert on any unpatched or missing-remediation status beyond the federal due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Public Exposure Hunt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from the internet on default ports (typically 443, 8443). Cross-reference with vulnerability scan data for CVE-2026-10520 presence and confirmation of absence of mTLS/restricted HTTPS mitigations mentioned in article.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Pattern Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs (or upstream WAF/IDS) for requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $(), etc.) in parameters targeting Sentry API/web endpoints. High fidelity indicator of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline must surface detection for attacker activity post-compromise—unusual process spawning or shell commands executed with Sentry service account or root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell processes (bash, sh, /bin/sh) spawned by Sentry daemons or initiated from Sentry contexts. Baseline normal administrative activity; flag deviations. RCE exploitation will manifest as privileged command execution originating from network-accessible Sentry components.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unprotected Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is mitigated by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Identify at-risk Sentry deployments lacking these protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for absence of mTLS certificates, lack of EPMM configuration, or unrestricted HTTPS access. Cross-reference exposed systems from asset hunt; flag those without documented mTLS or Neurons hardening as critical-priority targets for patching.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—foundational attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry (MobileIron Sentry) appliances with external-facing HTTPS listeners (port 443). suggestion.title: Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for command injection syntax: shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks), command separators (&&, ||), redirection operators (>, <), and base64/hex-encoded shell commands. Alert on external/unauthenticated requests containing these patterns.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawn from Sentry Service Context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes created by Ivanti Sentry service principal (e.g., sentry.jar, sentry process, MobileIron services) running as root/SYSTEM when not part of documented patch/upgrade procedures. Flag bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe spawned this way.

suggestion.title: Missing or Disabled mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Controls on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation statement: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—absence of these controls enables attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliances for lack of enforced mTLS client certificate validation on external-facing endpoints. Monitor for configuration changes disabling or weakening certificate pinning. Flag any certificate validation bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP 200 Responses on Sentry Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requirement: 'remote unauthenticated user'—successful exploitation includes successful auth bypass, detectable via access logs showing sensitive endpoints responding without session validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses to Sentry administrative or API endpoints (/admin, /api, /config, /status, /management) from external IP sources without established authentication session or API token in request headers. Baseline legitimate administrative access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner False Negatives

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare vulnerability scanner reports marking Sentry as patched against actual running Sentry version (via banner grab, admin panel, API query). suggestion.title: Suspicious AUR Package Version Jump
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked,' implying rapid version changes or unexpected package updates. Detection needed for packages showing unexpected version increments or unusual source-code diffs.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual login patterns to AUR/Archlinux accounts (geographic anomalies, new devices, off-hours access). suggestion.title: Trojanized Binary Distribution via Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain hijack implies malicious binaries packaged into AUR tarballs. No detection hypothesis generated for identifying compromised package contents (backdoors, shells, miners).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-package installation, monitor for unexpected child processes from package extraction directories or unexpected persistence mechanisms (cron, systemd, init scripts). Hash downloaded AUR tarballs and flag mismatches against upstream repository hashes. Detect unexpected network connections initiated by newly installed package binaries.

suggestion.title: Malicious Build Script Execution (PKGBUILD)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor makepkg or bash execution of PKGBUILD files for suspicious command sequences: curl/wget to attacker infrastructure, chmod +s (privilege escalation), network listeners, shell bindings, or registry/cron modifications. Flag packages where build-time execution diverges from declared package purpose.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Artifact Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes hijacking; detection should cover Git commit spoofing, source-tarball replacement, or checksum mismatches in package metadata—none suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate AUR package manifests (PKGBUILD md5sums, pgp signatures, upstream URLs) against known-good baseline. Alert on signature verification failures, conflicting committer metadata (author email mismatch, unsigned commits), or tarball SHA256 divergence from published checksums.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Access to macOS Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact that tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—baseline detection logic missing. Defenders need to monitor for unauthorized reads/writes to this artifact location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing the Tahoe 26 menu selection artifact outside normal forensic tools. Monitor for copy, exfiltration, or analysis of this artifact by unusual user contexts or processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via macOS Artifact Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Menu selection history across the system (implied by 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system') could reveal user behavior patterns and system state reconnaissance used in lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify non-standard tooling (shell scripts, custom binaries) that enumerate or parse the Tahoe 26 artifact to extract user preference/behavior intelligence for lateral movement planning.

suggestion.title: Budibase workspace-scoped builder used x-budibase-app-id header to bypass builderOrAdmin middleware
suggestion.rationale: Article states middleware 'passes any user who is a builder for the app id in the x-budibase-app-id header' and explicitly allows workspace-scoped builders. This header is the attack trigger — detect workspace-scoped users sending it to invoke global-privilege endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User with workspace-scoped builder role (builder.global=false, builder.apps=[...]) sends HTTP request with x-budibase-app-id header to /api/public/v1/roles/assign. If response is 200/201 and subsequent audit shows builder.global or admin.global flipped to true, flag as successful authorization bypass and privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Budibase request body spread to SDK escalates workspace role to global scope
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'controller spreads the request body into the SDK call, and the SDK grants builder.global=true' — this is a logic flaw where attacker-controlled JSON body fields directly map to privilege escalation. Detect when POST body contains builder.global or admin.global set to true from non-admin source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign includes request body with JSON/form fields builder.global=true or admin.global=true. Source is authenticated but not already a global builder or admin. Response indicates success. Flag as parameter injection / privilege escalation attempt.

suggestion.title: Budibase chained privilege escalation: workspace builder → global builder → global admin
suggestion.rationale: After exploiting the endpoint to gain builder.global=true, attacker can loop and change admin.global=true. Article only describes first escalation; should detect if same user elevates roles twice in quick succession via same endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Same user makes 2+ successful POST requests to /api/public/v1/roles/assign within 5 minutes. First escalates builder.global false→true, second escalates admin.global false→true (or similar role chain). Indicates attacker chaining exploits to reach maximum privilege.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PAM/SSH Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Backdoored Linux Login Software' — implies PAM or SSH modifications to maintain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to /etc/pam.d/, /usr/lib/security/pam_*.so, or /etc/ssh/sshd_config without authorized change control. Detect new PAM module loading, dlopen() calls from sshd/login processes, or SSH configuration reloads outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: LD_PRELOAD Library Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Decade-long persistence ('Hide for Nearly a Decade') suggests advanced evasion via LD_PRELOAD to intercept login calls without modifying core binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable usage in context of ssh, login, or su processes. Monitor for unexpected .so library files with suspicious timestamps in unusual directories. Flag login process spawning with LD_* variables deviating from baseline.

suggestion.title: Credential Interception via Compromised Login Process
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored login software positioned in authentication stack enables password capture from all users attempting login or su.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected read/recv system calls from SSH/login daemons capturing user input. Monitor for unusual library dependencies in sshd/login binaries or unexpected symbol hooks into stdio functions. Alert on sshd spawning shells or exfiltrating data without SSH protocol negotiation.

suggestion.title: SSH Authorized_Keys Persistence via Injected Public Keys
suggestion.rationale: Long-term backdoor requires persistent SSH access; 'nearly a decade' persistence implies SSH key injection across multiple user accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized writes to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for privileged accounts. Monitor for bulk authorized_keys modifications across multiple user homes in short timeframe. Flag insertion of non-standard key formats or keys without corresponding key management workflow.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication Success without PAM Validation
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored login software enables unauthorized authentication; should detect logins bypassing normal PAM challenge-response flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SSH/login authentication with absence of expected PAM prompts, password verification calls, or 2FA validation in audit logs. Flag logins from dormant system accounts with source IPs outside baseline SSH patterns.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Installation for Rootkit Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Decade-long persistence implies kernel-level compromise to survive updates and maintain access across system reboots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insmod, modprobe, or modinfo calls with suspicious naming or unsigned modules. Track sysctl writes disabling LSM/SELinux. Detect unexpected kernel symbol exports or suspicious /proc/modules entries.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume'—the core threat model is mass phishing at scale. Pipeline should detect anomalous email ingestion spikes and suspicious sender patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email volume from external sources exceeding baseline by >3 sigma in rolling 1-hour window. Correlate with low-trust sender reputation, known phishing domains, or spoofed internal addresses. Alert only when distinct recipient count >100 in single batch.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Suspicious Link Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing campaigns often embed obfuscated or newly-registered links. Article context ('AI Phishing') suggests adversaries are automating link generation. Pipeline should detect emails with high-entropy or recently-registered domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing URLs with domain registration age <30 days, suspicious TLD patterns (newly-minted TLDs), or URL shorteners coupled with mismatched display/actual domains. Enrich with reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: Alert Storm / False-Positive Cascade from Phishing Detectors

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor alert queue depth and alert-per-minute rate from email security sensors. Trigger escalation when single phishing rule fires >500 times in 5-minute window with >50% deduplicable (same source, payload hash). Indicate potential tuning failure or evasion variant at scale.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via AI-Generated Phishing Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: AI-assisted phishing often involves synthetic landing pages mimicking legitimate services. Article mentions 'AI Phishing' suggesting adversaries use LLMs to generate convincing fakes. Pipeline should detect post-click behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser navigation to recently-registered domains hosting login-form HTML with form fields (username/password/2FA) shortly after clicking email links flagged as phishing. Correlate with failed login attempts to real services within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Send from Internal User to External Recipients
suggestion.rationale: Compromised internal accounts are often used to amplify phishing reach. Pipeline should flag when legitimate-looking internal accounts suddenly bulk-mail externally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when internal user account sends >100 emails to unique external recipients within 1 hour, with <10% reply rate and identical/near-identical subject lines. Baseline per-user send patterns; exclude distribution lists and mailing-list managers.

suggestion.title: SOC Alert Tuning Failure: Phishing Rules Over-Firing
suggestion.rationale: Article directly addresses analyst overload. Pipeline should detect and recommend tuning for rules triggering at unsustainable rates (e.g., keyword-based phishing rules with high FP rate).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze alert rule performance metrics: for each phishing detection rule, calculate signal-to-noise (confirmed threats / total alerts). Flag rules with <5% true-positive rate as over-tuned. Recommend suppression scopes (exclude marketing emails, newsletters) or threshold adjustments.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: all Ivanti Sentry instances should be identified and version-checked against CVE-2026-10520 patch status. Alert on any instance still running vulnerable version 2 days before federal due date. Correlate with external reachability and auth logs for exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Matches
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry' with 'observed exploited in the wild' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14'—hard deadline requires immediate scanner correlation. Pipeline must extract CVE-2026-10520 as primary IOC and surface to vuln mgmt team.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Ivanti Sentry appliance (product: 'Ivanti Sentry' OR 'MobileIron Sentry') flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 by scanner. Cross-reference asset inventory for external exposure. Prioritize unmanaged instances (no mTLS with EPMM confirmed).

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'—these are hard preconditions for exploitation. Exposure hunting is non-negotiable for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound internet-destined traffic to known Ivanti Sentry management IPs on standard ports (443, 8080, 8443). Correlate with unpatched CVE-2026-10520 status. Flag any external IP source accessing Sentry appliance; verify mTLS + EPMM controls are active.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Patterns in Ivanti Sentry Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'—if Sentry appliance logs HTTP requests, injection attempts (shell metacharacters, command delimiters) should be observable. Pipeline ignored log source analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Ivanti Sentry request logs are centralized, hunt for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (| ; & $ ` $() <() >()), OS path traversal (../ /etc /bin), or common RCE payloads in request parameters or headers. Correlate with unauthenticated requests (no auth token) and anomalous HTTP methods.

suggestion.title: Privileged Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation spawns child processes from service account with root privilege. This is the definitive post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawned from Ivanti Sentry service (running as root) that is suspicious: bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, python, perl, or encoded/obfuscated scripts. Baseline legitimate Sentry subprocesses; flag deviations. High-fidelity signal if process parentage is web service → root service.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS and Access Control Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is mitigated by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM'—infrastructure must verify these controls are active. Pipeline missed configuration compliance hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Ivanti Sentry instances in inventory. For each, confirm: (1) mTLS enabled with EPMM enrollment, OR (2) inbound HTTPS restricted via WAF/firewall ACL (not open to 0.0.0.0/0). Flag any appliance lacking both controls + confirm patch status for CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as the exploitation precondition — SOC must identify which Sentry instances are internet-facing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances; validate patch status for CVE-2026-10520; confirm internet reachability from external IPs and absence of mTLS/restricted access controls.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Detection (Ivanti Sentry)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user' — detection should capture exploitation attempts via malformed HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: backticks, pipes, semicolons, command substitution, variable expansion); correlate with Sentry application error logs.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation, unexpected child processes spawn at elevated privilege level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child process creation originating from Ivanti Sentry service account with System/root privilege; baseline normal child processes and alert on anomalies (system calls, shell spawning, reverse shells).

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Validation: Ivanti Sentry Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — validate security boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Ivanti Sentry appliances are NOT directly accessible from internet-facing networks; confirm mTLS enforcement on EPMM connections and HTTPS access restriction through Neurons for MDM; alert on configuration drift.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Patch Compliance (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and CISA KEV implies active exploitation — patch lag must be detected and escalated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system and vulnerability scanner for unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520; flag for immediate remediation; track deployment status with target completion before 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Web Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit — detection should monitor for authentication bypass or unauthorized access to protected interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative endpoints from external/untrusted IPs without valid authentication; correlate with access control logs and WAF logs for exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AUR PKGBUILD Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked' implying malicious modification of package build files. Pipeline should detect unusual edits to PKGBUILD scripts, build function additions, or pre/post-installation script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PKGBUILD file modifications by unexpected users, additions of suspicious shell commands (curl, wget, base64, bash -c) to build() or post_install() functions, or unexpected dependencies injected into package metadata. Monitor git commit logs in AUR repositories for commits that add exfiltration or persistence logic.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Pacman Package Installation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain hijacking is only dangerous when victims install the compromised packages. Pipeline should detect systems installing affected packages from AUR, especially in bulk or unexpected patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pacman/makepkg commands executing with repositories pointing to AUR, especially for packages known to be compromised. Flag installations of packages that execute unusual post-install scripts (spawning shells, curl, network calls). Correlate multiple systems installing the same AUR packages within short windows.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title suggests '400+ packages hijacked', implying compromise of multiple maintainer accounts or credentials. Pipeline should detect unauthorized account activity, token usage, or API access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AUR user accounts performing unusual actions: commits from new IP addresses, credential reuse patterns, API token creation/usage from unexpected locations, or bulk commits to multiple packages by a single maintainer. Flag sign-in anomalies (unusual times, geographic impossibilities, new devices).

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Script Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious PKGBUILD files typically embed payloads in post_install() functions. Pipeline should detect suspicious execution chains spawned by pacman post-install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by pacman/makepkg post-install functions (child processes of pacman, install scripts, or systemd hooks). Flag execution of shells with obfuscated arguments, network utilities (curl, wget, nc), or encoding/decoding tools. Alert on processes that write to sensitive directories (/usr/bin, /etc, cron directories) during package installation.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Discrepancy Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages may show inconsistencies between declared dependencies, checksums, and actual binaries. Pipeline should detect cryptographic or metadata anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package checksums (SHA256 in .SRCINFO) diverge from actual files in AUR git, when declared dependencies are unused, when package size increases unexpectedly between versions, or when build times spike. Cross-reference against known legitimate versions to identify injected binaries.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration from Compromised Package Installations
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain payloads often exfiltrate system info or credentials. Pipeline should detect network calls to attacker infrastructure from systems running affected packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or network connections to suspicious domains initiated by pacman child processes or by services installed by affected packages. Flag environment variable exfiltration (AWS keys, API tokens) sent over plaintext or to non-standard ports. Correlate domains contacted by post-install scripts against known C2/malware infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detection of MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'new macOS Tahoe 26 artifact discovered' and 'Tracing Digital Intent'—anti-forensics to clear or manipulate this artifact should yield detections, none generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deletion, timestamp modification, or content alteration of macOS Tahoe 26 artifact following suspicious process execution. Alert on access via raw filesystem tools not in baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Enumeration of Tahoe 26 Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates artifact 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—detection for reconnaissance-phase enumeration or inspection by non-system processes should exist, but none generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to macOS Tahoe 26 artifact path where process is not in OS baseline or whitelisted forensics/system tool. Alert on repeated queries to artifact metadata.

suggestion.title: Budibase /api/public/v1/roles/assign POST exploitation (CVE-2026-48150)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerable endpoint: '/api/public/v1/roles/assign is guarded by the builderOrAdmin middleware...The controller then spreads the request body into the SDK call, and the SDK grants builder.global=true'. No use case generated despite explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/public/v1/roles/assign returning 200/201. Baseline legitimate role-assignment volume by workspace/user. Flag POST from unexpected sources or with success rate inconsistent with normal admin activity. High success-rate exploitation shows /api/public/v1/roles/assign abuse by unprivileged builder accounts.

suggestion.title: Budibase CVE-2026-48150 self-issued API key followed by roles escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies temporal attack chain: 'self API key mint then roles/assign within 5 min'. Pipeline missed multi-step detection despite explicit 300-second constraint in article-provided SPL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect same user/source generating new API key (GET /api/global/self/api_key, 200/201) within 300 seconds of calling /api/public/v1/roles/assign (POST, 200/201). Sequential API-key-then-escalation pattern is high-confidence indicator of deliberate exploitation.

suggestion.title: Budibase bulk role-assignment from single source (CVE-2026-48150 mass-promotion)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies volumetric attack: 'bulk role-assign requests from single source' with detection threshold 'count > 3' within 5-minute window. Pipeline missed behavioural detection despite explicit query-ready metric.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sources making >3 POST requests to /api/public/v1/roles/assign returning 200/201 within 5-minute span. Single source hammering roles/assign endpoint indicates mass-privilege-escalation attempt or automated exploitation loop.

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder attempting global scope operation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically targets 'workspace-scoped builders (builder.apps set but builder.global unset)' attempting to assume global privileges. Article establishes that 'both global builders and workspace-scoped builders' pass middleware; detection must flag privilege boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Budibase app logs for /api/public/v1/roles/assign requests where calling user has workspace-scoped builder role (builder.apps populated, builder.global=false). Success = transition from workspace-scope to global-scope, indicating successful privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48150 exploitation signature: builder.global parameter injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the controller then spreads the request body into the SDK call, and the SDK grants builder.global=true'. Attackers inject 'builder.global' in POST body to trigger privilege escalation. This is the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to /api/public/v1/roles/assign where request body contains 'builder.global' parameter, or where response shows caller's builder.global attribute changed from false→true. Parameter injection is the core exploitation technique; presence of this parameter in requests from non-global-builder accounts is exploitation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Impersonating AI Service Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'AI brands as bait'—threat actors lure victims with fake ChatGPT, Claude, or Copilot login prompts to steal credentials. Schema keyword 'Credential theft' confirms this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with AI platform branding (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) in sender display name or logo, combined with account-verification urgency language ('confirm access', 'reactivate', 'suspicious activity'). Monitor for MFA bypass or temporary-password-reset requests. Correlate with web traffic to lookalike domains within 30 minutes of delivery.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Proxy Credential Interception
suggestion.rationale: Schema explicitly tags 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)'—attackers intercept credentials by proxying traffic to legitimate AI service domains. Requires domain spoofing and certificate interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS certificates issued for known AI platform domains (openai.com, anthropic.com, google.com/bard, bing.com/copilot) to unexpected CAs or with suspicious registration timing. Monitor for SSL/TLS interception signatures. Alert on requests to these domains that redirect through intermediate proxies with response-header tampering (cache-control, set-cookie modifications).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted AI Platform Domain Registration and Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via brand impersonation requires attacker-controlled infrastructure. Article discusses 'AI brands as bait'—implies malicious domains mimicking legitimate services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify newly registered domains with ChatGPT/Claude/Copilot typosquats (e.g., 'chatgpt-security-check.com', 'anthropic-ai-verify.com'). Cross-reference registration whois against known bulletproof hosting providers. Flag domains hosting credential-harvesting HTML forms or redirects to legitimate login pages with credential logging middleware.

suggestion.title: Failed Login Spike Correlated with AI Brand Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: After credential theft via phishing, attackers attempt to use harvested credentials. 'Credential theft' keyword confirms follow-on authentication exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of failed login attempts against AI service accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Azure OpenAI) from anomalous IP blocks or geographic locations within 2 hours of suspected phishing email delivery. Correlate with successful logins immediately following password-reset emails. Flag credential-validation patterns (rapid sequential login attempts across multiple accounts from same source IP).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Landing Pages Hosting AI Service Branding
suggestion.rationale: Phishing infrastructure requires hosting fake login pages. Article establishes attackers lure victims via AI brand impersonation to 'steal' credentials (schema keyword).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify web pages hosting HTML login forms with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Microsoft branding but served from attacker-controlled domains. Detect via HTML DOM inspection (logo image src mismatches, credential form POST targets to non-canonical domains). Flag pages with short TTLs, recent domain registration, or ASN registered to hosting providers associated with phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitable...where Sentry appliance is in unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable' and recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite explicit template reference and CISA KEV priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for externally routable Ivanti Sentry appliances across internet-facing subnets. Query vulnerability scanner inventories, shodan/censys results for Ivanti/MobileIron fingerprints. Cross-reference with unmanaged device inventory.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'root-level remote code execution' for 'remote unauthenticated user.' Execution method is explicit but pipeline did not surface Execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTPS interfaces for command-injection payloads (backticks, $(), pipe operators) in request parameters. Alert on root-owned child process spawning from Sentry service runtime.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Configuration Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies unmanaged state as prerequisite risk: 'successfully exploited in cases where...appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Configuration-based hunt absent from pipeline outputs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit MDM/EPMM enrollment status for all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Flag devices with management_status='unmanaged' or enrollment_date=null. Cross-reference with external asset scans to identify critical-path exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—asset exposure is the prerequisite condition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (default ports, service banners) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with network zone assignments and management console state. High-fidelity if appliance lacks expected mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation—authentication bypass is core to attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry admin endpoints without prior authentication session. Flag external IPs accessing /admin, /manage, /api/* lacking valid session tokens.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'OS command injection'—requires payload inspection for command substitution metacharacters targeting Sentry parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, ;, &&, ||, >, <) in Sentry request parameters. Baseline normal patterns; alert on statistically significant deviations in unprotected endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation spawns processes with UID 0; critical post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry hosts, alert on process spawning with UID 0 via unexpected parents (web service daemons, network daemons). Baseline expected admin access; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Patch Compliance Check Against CISA KEV
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal due date 2026-06-14; inventory verification against CVE-2026-10520 is operational necessity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner results for Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched. Cross-reference with network exposure data. Escalate instances both externally reachable and missing patches before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Network Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — prerequisite asset hunt for at-risk infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances with inbound access from untrusted networks via asset inventory, firewall rules, or network scanning. Flag appliances in unmanaged state (verified via EPMM enrollment status or configuration queries) with external port exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Unpatched Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV in-the-wild exploitation with federal patch due 2026-06-14. Vulnerability scanning against baseline required for remediation compliance and risk prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry product instances and correlate version against patched release versions. Flag any endpoint reporting version ≤ vulnerable threshold without compensating controls (mTLS, restricted HTTPS).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection RCE Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability...to achieve root-level remote code execution' — behavioral detection for successful exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, detect unexpected child process spawning from Sentry service process (Java/management threads), especially shell interpreters (sh, bash). Alert on commands with shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $()) or script injection payloads in HTTP request logs preceding process events.

suggestion.title: Sentry Root-Privilege RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation results in 'root-level remote code execution' — detection of privilege escalation from unauthenticated remote context to root is critical indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution events on Sentry appliances where parent process is a low-privilege service but child processes run as root/uid=0. Correlate with HTTP/network access logs from external sources within preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: Sentry Management Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers probe 'externally reachable' endpoints before exploitation attempt. Early detection of reconnaissance phase prevents successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS scanning of Sentry management interface paths (/admin, /api, /status, /console) from external IPs. Flag patterns of endpoint enumeration (multiple 404→200 transitions, parameter fuzzing, version detection requests) within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and specifies vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate network-facing systems running Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry on common appliance ports (443, 8080, 8443). Correlate external reachability with vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-10520. Alert on unauthenticated access to Sentry management interfaces where mTLS/EPMM protections are not enforced.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'OS command injection' enabling 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation. Requires pattern-matching for injection attempts in HTTP request handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP request payloads for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $(), backticks) and command-like substrings in unauthenticated endpoints. Flag oversized parameter values, double-encoding, or JEXL/expression-injection patterns. Correlate with child process spawning from Sentry process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection and Alerting
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and federal patch deadline is 2026-06-14. Scanner detection is the primary compliance signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-10520 detections (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.). Alert with critical priority on any unpatched findings. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm patch status, management enrollment, and external exposure. Escalate to incident response if found on production systems.

suggestion.title: Root-Level RCE Execution from Ivanti Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution.' Requires detection of unexpected system commands and privilege escalation initiated by Sentry processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent = Ivanti Sentry application daemon/java process. Flag spawning of shell interpreters (/bin/sh, bash, cmd.exe) or system administration tools (curl, wget, nc, ssh) from Sentry context. Alert on root/SYSTEM-level execution initiated by application logic.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection and Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Requires asset state inventory and configuration audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry appliances for management enrollment status in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Flag instances without enforced mTLS, not enrolled in management framework, or without recent patch/update activity. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify unmanaged + externally-reachable high-risk instances.

suggestion.title: Known Exploit Activity: CVE-2026-10520 PoC/Commercial Toolkit Usage
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active exploitation in the wild. Industrial exploit kits and PoC code likely available; requires hunting for exploitation indicators and post-breach artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP error cascades (500/502/503) to Ivanti Sentry endpoints indicating fuzzing or exploit crashes. Detect anomalous HTTP patterns: rapid sequential requests to /admin, /api, /config; oversized parameters; requests with shell metacharacters. Correlate with process spawning and new user account creation or SSH key injection artifacts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes the precondition: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — detection of Internet-facing instances is the primary control point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances accessible from untrusted networks via port scanning, certificate inventory, or asset management tools. Prioritize unmanaged appliances lacking standard controls. Correlate with patch status for CVE-2026-10520 to identify exploitable assets.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user' — web application and network logs will contain malicious injection payloads in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry management interface requests for command injection patterns: shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax ($(), backticks), semicolon-delimited commands, or pipe operators in parameter values. Focus on unauthenticated endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Post-Exploitation Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the impact — successful exploitation will manifest as privileged shell session spawning and system command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On affected Sentry appliances, detect unexpected shell interpreter spawning (sh, bash, zsh) from Sentry service context or system commands executed with root privileges. Correlate with external network connections or unauthorized file system modifications.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — unmanaged state is a mandatory precondition for successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM platforms for Ivanti Sentry instances not enrolled or marked as unmanaged. Cross-reference against network exposure scans to identify at-risk instances. Prioritize for immediate remediation or isolation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS/HTTPS Mitigation Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS are protective controls: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — validate these defenses are active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify mTLS enforcement on all Sentry endpoints via certificate validation checks. Monitor for failed client certificate handshakes or unauthenticated HTTP access attempts. Alert on instances with mTLS disabled or Neurons gateway bypassed.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Externally Reachable Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability succeeds 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—immediate inventory need for critical exposed assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (product banners, SSL cert org fields, HTTP fingerprints) listening on external-facing interfaces. Cross-reference asset management system for patch status against CVE-2026-10520 and flag unmanaged/default-config appliances as highest priority.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry HTTP Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'—exploitation attempts will manifest as shell metacharacters or command substitution syntax in HTTP request parameters or POST data targeting the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection payloads: semicolons, pipes, backticks, $(), $(()) in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses (successful injection) or error patterns indicative of code execution.

suggestion.title: Privileged Process Execution from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation spawns commands with root/system privilege from the compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events under root or system privilege originating from Ivanti Sentry service account or process boundaries. Flag unexpected child processes, network utilities (curl, wget, nc), or reverse-shell indicators.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Egress from Ivanti Sentry Appliance Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised RCE-vulnerable appliance may initiate unexpected outbound connections for C2 communication or lateral movement—suspicious network behavior should be correlated with Sentry asset location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry appliances (management, updates, log forwarding); flag new external IPs, non-whitelisted domains, or unusual protocols (e.g., raw sockets, uncommon ports) originating from the appliance.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted Access Control Enforcement Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—defenders should confirm these mitigations are active and detect bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake rejections, invalid client certificates, or connection denials targeting Sentry endpoints from sources lacking valid mTLS credentials or outside restricted IP allowlists. Correlate with post-exploitation network activity to detect mitigation bypass.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry externally network-reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — exposure is the necessary precondition
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (typically TCP 9443 or HTTP) responding from external networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-10520. Alert on assets past federal patch deadline without mTLS/restricted HTTPS mitigations in place.

suggestion.title: OS command injection in Ivanti Sentry HTTP requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'OS command injection...remote unauthenticated' — injection payloads should be detectable in request logs and process spawning
