suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configuration for absence of mTLS enforcement and Neurons gateway deployment. Flag instances accepting unencrypted HTTPS (self-signed, expired, or untrusted certificates) or allowing direct inbound HTTPS without certificate pinning. Non-compliance with secure-baseline = higher risk of exploitation success.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'AI Phishing' as the threat driver. Pipeline should extract detection for AI-crafted phishing emails, which often exhibit reduced grammatical errors, unusual NLP fingerprints, and atypical social-engineering patterns compared to human-authored campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails with sender reputation score below threshold combined with linguistic anomalies (consistent grammar despite varied template structure, unusual phrasings, or atypical urgency language). Correlate high-volume campaigns sharing similar linguistic fingerprints across different sender addresses.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Volume Spike & Alert Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states AI phishing is 'crushing SOCs with alert volume'—pipeline should detect coordinated high-volume phishing pushes that overwhelm Tier 1 analysts through sheer inbound rate rather than evasion techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate inbound phishing detections by campaign signature (e.g., payload hash, sender domain, recipient domain subset) within 1-hour windows. Trigger alert when detection count for a single campaign exceeds organization baseline by >3 standard deviations, indicating coordinated phishing blast.

suggestion.title: Multi-Layer URL Redirection in Phishing Links
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing kits commonly employ URL shorteners and redirect chains to evade static URL filtering. Pipeline should detect and alert on emails containing redirect chains (shortener→intermediary→landing page) as fingerprint of kit-based attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse email URLs for redirect chains exceeding length 2. Flag emails where redirect destination is newly-registered domain (<7 days old) or high-risk IP geolocation. Cross-reference with credential-theft threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing articles routinely describe downstream credential-capture infrastructure. Pipeline should link email delivery detection to abnormal authentication patterns (failed logins, anomalous login locations, or OTP bypass attempts) within 5 minutes of email click events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users who clicked phishing links (from email sandbox/proxy telemetry) with subsequent failed sign-in attempts from unusual geolocations or unusual browser fingerprints within 15 minutes. Alert on attempted OTP reuse or multi-factor authentication bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: SOC Tier 1 Alert Backlog & Fatigue Metric
suggestion.rationale: Article's subtitle explicitly names 'Tier 1 Overload' as the operational impact. Pipeline should generate a composite metric tracking alert queue depth, mean time-to-triage, and escalation rate as a signal of campaign success in degrading SOC response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track rolling 8-hour window: (alerts queued / analysts on shift), mean seconds from alert creation to first action, and percentage of phishing alerts auto-closed without escalation. When queue depth exceeds 50th percentile baseline AND mean triage time increases >25%, escalate remaining phishing alerts and trigger SOC staffing alert.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Sender Reputation Cluster
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing campaigns typically use newly-registered or compromised domains in bulk. Pipeline should detect clusters of emails from senders with below-threshold reputation scores, domain registration dates within previous 30 days, or shared infrastructure (ASN, IP space) arriving in short time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each inbound email, extract sender domain registration age, WHOIS/passive DNS infrastructure, and sender reputation score. Flag emails where >5 senders from newly-registered domains (or from same ASN) arrive within 30 minutes to same organization, indicating infrastructure reuse across phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: PAM Module Replacement and Credential Harvesting

suggestion.title: OpenSSH Trojanization and Credential Logging

Flag suspicious environment variables or runtime hooks in OpenSSH execution flow.

Alert on HTTP POST requests forwarding to fcgiwrap listening on unusual ports. Monitor for fcgiwrap spawning SSH or netcat child processes with parameters derived from HTTP request bodies or headers.

suggestion.title: Process Masquerading as smbd for Unauthorized SOCKS5 Proxy

Monitor network sockets opened by smbd processes; legitimate Samba should match known parent chains and standard port ranges. Detect SOCKS5 traffic signatures on unexpected ports from processes claiming to be smbd.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell with Systemd/Startup Script Persistence

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new or modified systemd service files in /etc/systemd/system/ or /usr/lib/systemd/system/ with ExecStart pointing to unexpected binaries. Alert on GS-Netcat signatures in process names, network connections to hardcoded relay domains, or encrypted tunnel patterns. Flag startup scripts (rc.local, .bashrc, profile.d) with unusual system service entries.

suggestion.title: Custom Binary Launching SSH Sessions via HTTP POST Parameters
suggestion.rationale: 'Installed a custom binary named uptime... The tool established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests.' This bridges the air-gap via HTTP-to-SSH translation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected SSH process spawning from HTTP daemon processes (nginx, lighttpd, httpd) or from unusual parent processes on internet-facing servers. Monitor for child process SSH connections with command-line parameters matching HTTP request body signatures or encoded POST data. Alert on SSH sessions originating from localhost connections initiated by web server processes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Child Spawning from RCE

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on splunkd.exe or splunk spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or other interpreters with suspicious command lines or elevated privilege context. RCE exploitation typically yields immediate shell execution under Splunk's service account.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to Splunk RCE Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'without authentication' — no network-level detection for auth-bypass exploitation attempts generated despite being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/GET requests to Splunk web endpoints (e.g., /en-US/app/*, /services/*, /search/*) from external or untrusted sources that succeed (HTTP 200) without valid authentication tokens, especially with encoded payloads or shell metacharacters in query strings.

suggestion.title: Splunk Version Fingerprinting Probes
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify version to exploit version-specific RCE. Article implies version targeting but no reconnaissance-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated requests to Splunk information endpoints (/services/server/info, /en-US/about) or systematic probes to version-sensitive paths that return version strings in HTTP headers or response bodies, especially from non-browser user agents.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Payload Detection in Splunk Requests
suggestion.rationale: RCE requires sending malicious payloads to vulnerable endpoints. Article describes code execution mechanism but no payload signature detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request bodies and query parameters for shell metacharacters, command separators (|, ;, &, $()), base64/URL-encoded commands, or reverse-shell syntax directed at vulnerable Splunk endpoints, correlated with successful code execution indicators (process creation logs).

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Discovery via Port Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must locate Splunk instances before exploitation. No reconnaissance use case for Splunk port/service discovery generated.

suggestion.title: Session Token / Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically enables bypass of authentication. No detection for anomalous auth patterns or auth-less access to restricted endpoints generated.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise or Unauthorized Package Commit

suggestion.title: Malicious Post-Install Code Execution from Hijacked AUR Packages

suggestion.title: Suspicious PKGBUILD Code Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages must inject or modify code in PKGBUILD or install scripts. No use case for detecting obfuscated code, unusual network calls, post_install hooks, or privilege-escalation patterns in PKGBUILD was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze PKGBUILD diffs for suspicious additions: new curl/wget/nc calls, base64-encoded payloads, obfuscated eval/exec, unexpected post_install() hooks, or exfiltration patterns (keyslogger, netstat, SSH key theft).

suggestion.title: Package Signature or Hash Integrity Verification Failure

suggestion.title: Bulk or Correlated AUR Package Updates from Compromised Source

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Detection via Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article distinguishes exploitable unmanaged instances from protected ones using 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM' — pipeline should hunt for absence of these protective controls in configuration.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry admin interfaces (ports 443, 9443, 8080) accept connections from untrusted/external IP ranges. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unmanaged appliances. Priority escalation if vulnerability scanning confirms CVE-2026-10520 presence.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' This is the exploitation phase requiring detection of crafted payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry for shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, semicolons, pipes) in request parameters, especially to unauthenticated endpoints. Flag POST requests to sensitive Sentry paths (config, admin, command handlers) containing injection syntax.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Ivanti Sentry Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation and notes that 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' prevents exploitation. Detection must identify absence of these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP successful responses (200, 302) to Ivanti Sentry admin endpoints with authentication logs. Alert when HTTP traffic shows successful interaction without prior valid session establishment. Cross-check for mTLS/certificate validation failures.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the achieved impact. Post-exploitation process activity must be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry service account for spawning of unexpected shell processes (sh, bash, ksh, cmd.exe). Alert on process execution with root/SYSTEM privileges following any HTTP command injection signatures. Detect rapid-succession process creation indicating post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Federal patch due date 2026-06-14 creates hard detection deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate compliance report of all Ivanti Sentry instances scanned as vulnerable or unpatched for CVE-2026-10520. Segment by network zone; escalate externally-reachable instances immediately. Track remediation against federal due date.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged status is a pre-exploitation condition enabling attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances without MDM/EPMM enrollment or management agent communication. Flag unmanaged instances in external network zones as critical. Correlate absence of management heartbeats with exposure detection.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Instance Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—asset exposure is the primary initial-access precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound traffic on Ivanti Sentry default ports (443, 8443) from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with device inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Look for public DNS resolutions or cloud asset tags indicating external exposure.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—execution via command injection is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs and HTTP access logs for payloads containing shell metacharacters (pipes, backticks, semicolons, command substitution syntax) in request parameters. Correlate with unexpected process spawning from the Sentry application context.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation via Ivanti Sentry RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'root-level remote code execution'—privilege escalation to root is the outcome of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with UID/GID 0 originating from the Sentry application process tree. Monitor for sudo/setuid transitions from the web application user context. Check for privilege escalation exploitation patterns in system audit logs.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'—management status determines exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM enrollment database and configuration management systems for Ivanti Sentry instances with enrollment_status != 'enrolled' or last_config_check > 30 days. Flag instances without active management policies as exposed.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Across Fleet
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and references asset-exposure hunt template; vulnerability requires patch verification across all Sentry instances by federal due date 2026-06-14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) output against asset inventory to identify Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 detected but unpatched. Trend patch application rate against 2026-06-14 deadline. Flag instances where scan age > 7 days or patch status unknown.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigations include 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM'—monitoring for bypass attempts of these controls is appropriate given active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed mTLS handshakes, certificate validation errors, or HTTP tunneling attempts to Ivanti Sentry interfaces. Alert on traffic attempting to reach Sentry ports via non-standard protocols or with missing client certificates.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'can be successfully exploited...where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—asset exposure is the necessary precondition for all attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for and enumerate Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks. Identify HTTPS endpoints on standard ports (443) using Sentry-specific certificate names or response fingerprints. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner inventory to flag unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10520 is the explicit vulnerability vector. Federal patch due date 2026-06-14 is regulatory deadline driving SOC prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Ivanti Sentry instances for CVE-2026-10520 presence. Flag any appliances with patch gap, missing last-scan date, or divergent patch versions. Compare against deadline to prioritize remediation workflow.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'—exploitation requires shell metacharacters and command sequences in HTTP payloads to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances for payloads containing OS command injection patterns: pipes, semicolons, ampersands, backticks, $() syntax, or newlines in parameters. Flag requests targeting known vulnerable endpoints with shell command sequences (whoami, id, cat, chmod, bash).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation manifests as root-privilege process spawn.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with root/system privileges (uid 0) spawned from or by Ivanti Sentry processes. Flag unexpected child processes, especially system utilities (bash, sh, nc, wget, python, curl) launched with privilege escalation from the Sentry parent.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Outbound Network Activity from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE on externally-facing unmanaged appliance implies risk of lateral movement to internal network—monitor for unexpected external communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry appliances outside normal EPMM/Neurons-for-MDM communication patterns. Alert on DNS queries to internal hosts, SMB attempts to file servers, SSH to administrative systems, or connections to non-Ivanti external IPs.

suggestion.title: Externally Accessible Ivanti Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — direct asset exposure detection required for initial reconnaissance and exploitation surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances listening on external interfaces (typically HTTPS port 8443). Cross-reference firewall allow rules and WAF logs for unauthenticated inbound connections to known Sentry URI paths (/admin, /api). Correlate with vulnerability scanner data to isolate unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — exploitation is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to Ivanti Sentry API endpoints for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: $(, `;`, `|`, `&`, backticks, newline bytes). Flag requests with base64-encoded or URL-encoded shell commands in parameters. Alert on 400/500 responses followed by successful 200 responses (indicator of payload iteration).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation results in arbitrary process spawn with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service running in root/SYSTEM context, spawning unexpected children (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell, curl, wget). Establish baseline of legitimate child processes; any deviation is high-fidelity. Monitor for process execution with source IP from external networks if correlation data available.

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass or Access Control Misconfiguration for Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — missing or misconfigured mitigations enable exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated configuration scan for Ivanti Sentry deployments: verify mTLS is enforced on all externally-facing endpoints, validate certificate pinning, confirm IP whitelisting or VPN requirement. Alert on Sentry instances with certificate validation disabled, mTLS disabled, or bound to 0.0.0.0:8443 without upstream firewall restriction.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Coverage Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet' — scanner coverage and patch status verification is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Ivanti Sentry instances in vulnerability management system for CVE-2026-10520. Verify patch level against vendor bulletin; note firmware version, hotfix status, and deployment date. Flag any instance with CVE-2026-10520 scoring CVSS ≥7.0 or listed in CISA KEV without documented remediation plan and date.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'Sentry appliance in unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable'—immediate inventory and exposure assessment required for CISA KEV (federal SLA: 2026-06-14).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances. Identify those lacking mTLS with EPMM enrollment or HTTPS-only access policies via Neurons for MDM. Cross-reference firewall rules to identify externally reachable instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—must detect injection payloads in HTTP traffic to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for command injection indicators: shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, backtick, ${}), command substitution syntax, or OS command sequences. Differentiate exploitation attempts from legitimate administrative traffic via baseline profiling.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance with External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerable configuration as 'unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable'—detection should verify protective controls (mTLS, HTTPS restriction) are active and flag gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Classify Sentry appliances as managed (EPMM-enrolled) or unmanaged. Verify mTLS client certificate enforcement and HTTPS-only ingress policies. Flag any unmanaged Sentry with internet-routable IP address or external DNS resolution without protective controls.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation 'achieves root-level remote code execution'—post-compromise detection requires monitoring for unexpected root-context process execution on Sentry appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect process spawning from web-server context (Java/Tomcat, nginx) escalating to UID 0. Alert on shell spawning (/bin/sh, /bin/bash) or system utilities (curl, wget, nc, socat) in root context, especially correlated with inbound HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: mTLS Certificate Validation Failure or Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Sentry is protected by 'mTLS with EPMM'—detection should identify failed mTLS handshakes or attempts to access management interfaces without valid client certificates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed TLS/mTLS handshakes to Sentry management endpoints from external sources. Track HTTP (unencrypted) connection attempts to endpoints that mandate HTTPS. Alert on any management interface access attempt without valid client certificate when mTLS is enforced.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Patch Remediation Tracker (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV published 2026-06-11 with federal patch due 2026-06-14 (3-day SLA). Aggressive timeline indicates imminent active exploitation—continuous patch status verification required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform daily version checks on all Ivanti Sentry appliances in fleet against patched build information. Alert immediately on any appliance remaining unpatched after 2026-06-14 federal due date, with escalation priority for externally reachable or unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the entry point for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry on typical ports (8443, 443) from untrusted networks or the internet. Cross-correlate with inventory data to identify appliances without mTLS/EPMM or Neurons for MDM restrictions. Flag any endpoint accessible from external networks.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploited by 'remote unauthenticated user.' Exploitation attempts will contain OS command syntax or shell metacharacters in requests to vulnerable Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application/HTTP logs for command injection patterns (backticks, $(), pipe, semicolon, &&, ||) in request parameters and payloads. Correlate with failed authentication attempts and requests from external sources. Alert on any shell metacharacter combinations in user-controllable inputs.

suggestion.title: Root-level Privilege Escalation from Ivanti Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation results in Sentry process spawning commands with root privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry process (sentry, mobileiron-sentry, or related daemons) spawns shell commands (bash, sh, cmd.exe) with root/SYSTEM privileges, or when child processes of Sentry run with elevated privileges. Compare process parent-child relationships against baseline Sentry behavior.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch due date 2026-06-14. Organizations must validate Ivanti Sentry patch status across fleet. Article implies unpatched/unmanaged appliances are at immediate risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management tools for Ivanti Sentry installations. Extract version numbers and cross-reference against patched releases. Flag any instances below minimum patched version. Correlate unpatched appliances with network exposure (internet-facing, missing mTLS, unmanaged state).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance is in unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' This is the direct precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry management interfaces (TCP 443, 8443) exposed on internet-facing subnets and reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against CMDB for appliances marked 'unmanaged' or without EPMM/Neurons enrollment. Flag any discovered by Shodan/Censys as exploitable window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Access to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit vulnerability. Signals no auth token required for command injection endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP access logs for requests without valid session/authentication tokens reaching API or administrative endpoints. Baseline approved unauthenticated paths, alert on deviations or parameter injection attempts.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability.' Payloads will contain shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, pipes, semicolons, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry with command substitution syntax in parameters: $(…), `…`, |, ;, &, >, <, or newlines. Correlate with process creation from Sentry service spawning unexpected child processes (shells, curl, wget).

suggestion.title: Root-level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow…root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation spawns processes with UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service parent reach UID 0 or run with elevated capabilities. Flag unexpected shells, network utilities (nc, curl, wget), or known exfiltration tools as children of Sentry processes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged / Not Protected by EPMM or Neurons MDM
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence = vulnerability window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry appliances and identify those NOT enrolled in EPMM (mTLS enforcement) or Neurons for MDM (restricted HTTPS). Treat as critical exposure until patched (Federal due date 2026-06-14) or protected.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—the foundational exposure condition for this RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances with inbound internet access on management ports. Cross-reference asset inventory to flag unmanaged instances with external reachability, particularly where mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls are not enforced.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving RCE—direct indicator of pre-auth endpoint exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP responses to Ivanti Sentry management endpoints that occur without preceding authentication. Monitor for POST requests to API or command-execution endpoints originating from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector—should trigger injection-pattern detection on application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, backtick, $()) in Ivanti Sentry request logs and API payloads. Monitor for injection attempts targeting command-execution functions, particularly in pre-auth endpoints.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root on Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—this privilege-escalation impact should be detectable as process execution with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with root/UID-0 on Ivanti Sentry where the parent process is a web service or API handler. Monitor for sudo invocations or setuid abuse originating from application-level code execution.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Once root RCE is achieved, defender should hunt for attacker-controlled activity (reconnaissance, persistence, lateral movement). Article implies active exploitation in the wild, establishing post-breach detection priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry for unusual outbound connections, file-system enumeration, or batch command execution following authentication bypass. Flag execution of reconnaissance tools, persistence mechanisms, or lateral-movement utilities.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and mandates federal remediation by 2026-06-14; asset inventory is the canonical first hunt for any unauthenticated RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry instances in your infrastructure (by product signature or version banner). Flag any instance accessible from the internet without mTLS or HTTPS-only access controls. Cross-reference against patch inventory for CVE-2026-10520 remediation status.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt - Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—need to detect exploitation attempts in flight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Ivanti Sentry API/admin endpoints for command-injection patterns (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(…), command separators). Flag requests containing OS command constructs from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes 'achieve root-level remote code execution'; successful exploitation spawns processes at elevated privilege. Detection at execution time catches live attacks post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal process spawn patterns from the Ivanti Sentry service account. Alert on unexpected root-level child processes spawned from Sentry service context, especially shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) or reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure – CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the canonical asset exposure hunt.
