suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation – HTTP Request Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector. Payloads will contain shell metacharacters in HTTP request parameters to unauthenticated endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, $(), backticks, newlines) or encoded variants in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Flag requests to unauthenticated endpoints with suspicious payload structure.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' on the Sentry host. Post-compromise detection should flag root processes spawned from network-facing services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, alert on shell interpreter processes (bash, sh, dash) or unexpected binaries executing with UID 0 context, spawned from HTTP listener processes or network-initiated pathways. Establish baseline of normal root processes on Sentry and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Patch Status Verification – CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and references federal due date (2026-06-14). Vulnerability management hunt for unpatched systems in fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 detections on Ivanti Sentry instances. Correlate with patch management logs to identify systems past the due date without patches applied. Prioritize instances without mTLS or Neurons for MDM (article notes these provide protection).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Accessible Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—external visibility is the precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliance interfaces (/webui, /api, /admin paths) reachable from untrusted networks. Baseline legitimate external access; flag new or unexpected internet-facing Sentry instances in unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: Command Injection Payloads to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'OS command injection vulnerability'—HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints will contain shell metacharacters attempting to break injection context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $(), etc.) in URL parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Correlate with 200/500 responses containing command output or system error messages.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation 'could allow...root-level remote code execution'—post-RCE detection must monitor for unexpected root processes on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for root process spawning without prior user authentication or shell session. Flag privilege escalation from service accounts to UID 0, or commands executed via cron/at with root context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: CVE-2026-10520 Detection in Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific CVE-2026-10520 with federal patch deadline 2026-06-14; CISA KEV entries require immediate inventory verification regardless of patch status to confirm exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged as CVE-2026-10520. Cross-check product version against known vulnerable releases via HTTP header fingerprinting. Flag any gap between scanner date and 2026-06-14 deadline.

suggestion.title: Appliance Configuration: Unmanaged Sentry State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploitation is explicitly conditioned on appliance 'in an unmanaged state'; mitigations include enrollment in EPMM or Ivanti Neurons for MDM—configuration audit should verify management enrollment status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configuration to verify enrollment in EPMM or Ivanti Neurons for MDM. Flag appliances with HTTPS restrictions disabled, mTLS not enforced, or no active management connection.

suggestion.title: PAM Unix Module Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials.' Nine variants identified. This is the persistence/credential-access pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file modifications to PAM library paths (/lib/security/pam_unix.so, /lib64/security/pam_unix.so). Alert on unexpected file size changes, hash mismatches, timestamp anomalies, or ownership changes. Correlate with syslog/auth.log for authentication event spikes.

suggestion.title: OpenSSH Binary Trojanzation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file integrity for /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp. Alert on hash/size mismatches, unexpected compile timestamps, or modifications outside package manager activity. Cross-check against expected OpenSSH versions.

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Chain to Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'modified... Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server... [whose] Nginx configuration was altered to forward requests to a FastCGI process.' Creates covert command channel into air-gapped environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx config files for proxy_pass directives pointing to internal/RFC1918 IPs. Alert on FastCGI upstream declarations in nginx.conf. Detect HTTP POST requests to non-standard backend ports or unusual request chaining patterns in access logs.

suggestion.title: FastCGI Remote Execution Bridge
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'FastCGI wrapper acted as execution bridge, processing requests and launching a custom binary named uptime. The tool established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor fcgiwrap and php-fpm process spawning with unusual child processes (esp. ssh, nc, or 'uptime'). Alert on SSH connection initiation from fcgiwrap context. Correlate HTTP POST requests to localhost FastCGI ports with subsequent system commands.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Acceptance in Auth Stack
suggestion.rationale: Article: '[malicious PAM modules] accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials.' This produces repeatable authentication success patterns with identical credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated successful logins with identical username-credential pairs across disparate sessions, timestamps, or geographic origins. Alert on authentication success immediately preceding high-privilege command execution. Correlate with PAM modification detection.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Daemon Masquerading as Samba
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling... running as daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.' Enables internal pivot without direct C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for smbd -D processes on non-file-server systems. Alert on unexpected SOCKS5 traffic, Samba processes binding to unusual ports, or smbd running outside standard Samba installation paths. Detect unusual inbound connections on dynamic proxy ports.

suggestion.title: Splunk Web Unauthenticated Code Execution Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'without authentication' — requires detection of HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints (likely /services/*, /en-US/app/*) that succeed (HTTP 200) despite missing or invalid Authorization/session headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk administrative endpoints receiving 200-series responses when Authorization headers are absent, null, or malformed. Correlate repeated failures-then-success patterns (multiple 401s then 200) within 60 seconds from single source.

suggestion.title: Splunk Daemon Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Run Code' — RCE requires spawning child processes (shells, binaries) from Splunk daemon context (splunkd.exe, splunk processes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Splunk child processes; alert on unexpected spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, python, or perl from splunkd or Splunk-related processes. Flag command lines containing network utilities (curl, wget, nc) or encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Unexpected External Network Outbound Connection
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attacker pivots from RCE to C2 or lateral movement — monitor for Splunk-initiated outbound connections to non-whitelisted external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from splunkd.exe/Splunk processes to external IPs outside baseline whitelist, particularly to high ports (>10000), rare geographic locations, or known C2 ASNs. Exclude legitimate Splunk Cloud/enterprise licensing communication.

suggestion.title: Splunk File Persistence: Binary Dropped to Installation Directory
suggestion.rationale: Code execution enables attacker to persist via malware injection into $SPLUNK_HOME or startup app directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification in $SPLUNK_HOME/bin, $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps, /opt/splunk/etc/apps with non-standard extensions (.exe, .sh, .ps1, .pyc) or from unexpected process contexts. Exclude maintenance windows and known deployment/update activity.

suggestion.title: Splunk REST API Call Without Token/Session Validation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE likely exploits authentication bypass in REST API handler — monitor for API calls (typically POST to /services/data/indexes, /services/admin/*, /services/search/jobs) returning success without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track POST/GET requests to Splunk /services/* endpoints that return HTTP 200/201 when X-Auth-Token or Authorization headers are missing or invalid. Baseline legitimate API consumers and flag deviations; correlate with privilege-escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Integrity Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked'—pipeline should detect unexpected package source modifications, mismatched file hashes vs. upstream, or suspicious dependencies injected into build artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AUR package installations where: post-install scripts spawn network utilities or shells, files are written to rc.d/systemd directories, or package checksums deviate from known-good registry without matching upstream commits.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Account Compromise - AUR Maintainer Takeover
suggestion.rationale: 400+ packages hijacked implies maintainer account compromise or repository access. 'Atomic Arch Campaign' indicates coordinated effort—should detect unusual maintainer activity patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AUR for: login anomalies on maintainer accounts, package uploads from non-standard IPs, rapid version bumps without corresponding git history, or uploads of packages previously owned by different maintainers.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Command Execution from Compromised Packages
suggestion.rationale: Campaign nature and scale suggest persistent backdoor delivery. Should detect arbitrary code execution during package installation—'PKGBUILD scripts executing unexpected binaries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package post-install scripts containing curl/wget/nc spawning network processes, shell escapes, privilege escalation attempts, or writes to system-wide startup locations (cron, systemd, etc.).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Infected Package Systems
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack affecting 400+ systems likely results in widespread malware deployment. Critical severity suggests active command-and-control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate systems with recent AUR package installations against C2 signature—outbound connections to non-standard ports, DGA-pattern domains, or beaconing to confirmed malicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Supply-Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Scale of attack (400+ packages) suggests ecosystem-wide infection. Should detect reconnaissance and lateral movement from compromised client systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on systems with compromised AUR packages performing SSH/RDP scanning, network enumeration (whoami, id, arp, hostname), LDAP queries, or mass-credential attempts against internal infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack Campaign Tracking - Atomic Arch Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article names campaign 'Atomic Arch'—pipeline should maintain threat-actor playbook correlations, group indicators by campaign, and track ecosystem-wide impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain campaign-level SIEM dashboards aggregating: affected package names, compromised maintainer accounts, C2 infrastructure, affected user systems, and remediation metrics. Cross-reference against community advisories and mirror integrity checks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to macOS Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes artifact that 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—forensic artifact is a detective's signal and an adversary's persistence footprint. Pipeline missed opportunity to detect access to the artifact location itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file system access, reads, or modifications to macOS Tahoe 26 user menu artifact locations (typically library/caches or forensic-artifact-specific paths). Baseline normal access patterns and alert on out-of-band reads by non-system processes or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Anomalous macOS Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Behavior Change
suggestion.rationale: Artifact 'tracks user menu selections'—abnormal patterns in historical menu activity could indicate lateral movement, privilege escalation, or user-account compromise. Pipeline failed to propose behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of typical user menu selections per user/machine. Alert on statistically significant deviations (new menu items accessed, timing anomalies, rapid sequential selections). Useful for detecting automated lateral-movement discovery or reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Forensic Artifact Timestamp Manipulation on macOS Tahoe 26
suggestion.rationale: Forensic artifacts are attack-surface for anti-forensics. Article introduces new artifact—pipeline should have proposed detection of tampering with its metadata or access timestamps to evade forensic analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for direct writes, deletions, or timestamp modifications to macOS Tahoe 26 menu artifact files. Correlate with tools like touch, SetFile, or low-level file-system calls. Alert on mismatches between file-creation time and system boot time.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires network-layer detection of exposed appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks lacking mTLS/firewall-based access controls. Query firewall/proxy logs for inbound connections to Sentry default ports (443, 8443, 8004) from external IP ranges. Flag appliances in 'unmanaged' state per MDM inventory.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Attack Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection' enabling 'root-level remote code execution.' Article describes injection attack vector but pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&) and command substitution patterns. Correlate with process creation events from Sentry service context spawning shells (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, python, curl with -c flags). Baseline legitimate service process tree and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Root Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level' execution. Detection gap for post-exploitation privilege indicators and unauth API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent process is an HTTP handler/Sentry service and spawned process runs as root/uid=0. Monitor for privilege escalation within Sentry service context (setuid, sudo, direct root spawning). Baseline expected Sentry-spawned processes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Configuration Baseline Drift
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' as exploitation precondition. Requires detection for appliances deviating from hardened config (missing mTLS, exposed interfaces, firewall rules disabled).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliance configs for: (1) mTLS disabled or misconfigured, (2) HTTPS access controls absent/permissive, (3) Unmanaged state flag in MDM, (4) Public routing to admin interfaces. Compare against hardened baseline. Correlate missing mTLS + unmanaged + external routing = exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Suspicious Policy Deployment Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful root RCE on Sentry creates lateral movement risk into managed endpoints. Article describes Sentry's MDM/EPMM function but pipeline missed detection for malicious policy push.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor policy push/deployment events from Ivanti Sentry to endpoints for timing correlation with exploitation windows. Flag policy changes introducing persistence mechanisms, C2 endpoints, or credential theft. Correlate source Sentry appliance patch status (CVE-2026-10520 vulnerable) with downstream endpoint compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Default Credentials / Weak Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article notes unauthenticated access pathway. Detection for credential-based attacks and weak auth on appliance APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry admin APIs for high-frequency failed auth attempts followed by successful admin-level API calls without session tokens. Alert on logins using default/weak credentials (admin/admin, root/root patterns). Flag successful API calls from external IP ranges without corresponding login event.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 as the vulnerability and notes federal patch due date of 2026-06-14. Pipeline generated zero IOC or detection coverage for this actively exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Ivanti Sentry appliances matching CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference patch management logs for unpatched instances after 2026-06-14 deadline. Correlate against asset inventory to identify exposed appliances still at risk of exploitation.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Network Exposure Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only when 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'in an unmanaged state' — conditional risk factors requiring network-layer detection that pipeline completely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTPS and management ports of Ivanti Sentry appliances. Alert on new external network exposure (inbound from untrusted CIDR ranges). Cross-reference against configurations to identify appliances lacking mTLS protection or restricted HTTPS access mentioned as mitigations in the article.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Detection on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism — the actual attack vector. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for command injection payloads (T1059.001) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for command injection syntax (pipes, semicolons, backticks, command substitution, shell metacharacters) in query parameters and POST bodies. Alert on payloads attempting to inject system commands into fields that should be controlled application input.

suggestion.title: Successful Remote Code Execution on Ivanti Sentry (Root Privilege)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — privilege escalation and impact phase signals completely absent from pipeline output despite being central to threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on root-level process execution on Ivanti Sentry appliances following unauthenticated inbound requests. Look for unexpected privilege escalation, sudo/su events with system commands, or root-spawned child processes immediately after web requests from external sources.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance...with its endpoints externally reachable' enables exploitation. Asset exposure is the detection gate before exploitation becomes viable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances on public internet via banner-detection on port 8443 (or SSL/TLS certificate CN matching). Correlate against organization's asset inventory to identify unaccounted externally-reachable instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection must target injection payloads before successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns (backticks, $(), semicolon-delimited commands, pipe operators) in request parameters. Flag requests from unauthenticated sessions with suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation Root Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'could allow...root-level remote code execution.' Detection should trigger on unexpected shell/command execution at root privilege on Sentry appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash/sh/command spawning as root or SYSTEM on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially if parent process is a web service (Tomcat, httpd). Correlate with prior external network access.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability...can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Identifies high-risk deployments before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM enrollment status for all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Flag devices not enrolled or lacking mTLS configuration as critically exploitable per article risk factors.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 and states 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due date 2026-06-14. Must detect unpatched instances across fleet inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 matches on Ivanti Sentry products. Cross-reference with asset registry to identify unpatched instances. Flag any appliances past federal due date without patches applied.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances with public IP addresses, externally routable interfaces, or lacking WAF/mTLS protection mentioned in article. Prioritize unmanaged appliances (those not configured with mTLS via EPMM or restricted HTTPS as article states).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user.' Must detect attack delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP/HTTPS endpoints for unauthenticated requests with command injection metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $()) in parameters. Alert on payloads attempting shell command syntax in request paths or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level RCE Post-Exploitation Detection on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Must detect execution phase after injection succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process creation or command execution spawned by Sentry process running as root/SYSTEM. Look for unusual binaries, network connections, or privilege escalation attempts originating from compromised Sentry appliance.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged vs. Managed Sentry Risk Posture
suggestion.rationale: Article provides risk differentiation: unmanaged appliances are vulnerable, but 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Inventory gap on management status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry appliances for management status: identify any not enrolled in EPMM, lacking mTLS configuration, or without restricted HTTPS access. Unmanaged instances are exploitable; managed instances are protected.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Unauthenticated Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieves 'root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Zero detection UC for identifying exploitation attempts despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests containing shell metacharacters or command injection patterns (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, &&, ||) in request parameters or POST bodies. Filter by external source IPs. Alert on requests to administrative or API endpoints from non-management subnets.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Post-Exploitation Process Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact but no behavioral detection for successful exploitation post-injection. Successful RCE spawns arbitrary processes under root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate Sentry service process activity. Alert on anomalous process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe, PowerShell, wget, curl, netcat) from Sentry service principal or root user. Correlate temporal proximity to inbound exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - At-Risk Appliance Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible.' Identifies clear preconditions; no inventory-based detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset discovery hunt: identify all Ivanti Sentry instances lacking (a) mTLS with EPMM, (b) Neurons for MDM, or (c) restricted HTTPS access. Confirm external reachability via perimeter network scans. Flag as immediately exploitable; prioritize for emergency patching before 2026-06-14 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Abnormal Egress Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful root RCE typically enables callback, lateral movement, or data exfiltration. Article does not describe post-exploitation behavior but threat actor motivation with root access is clear; no UC for C2 or exfil patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry appliances (vendor updates, NTP, DNS only). Alert on unexpected external egress, especially to non-standard ports, P2P addresses, or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate timing with inbound exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - CVE-2026-10520 Patch Status Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with explicit federal remediation deadline. Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14'; no compliance or patch verification UC provided despite regulatory deadline and active exploitation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability scanning systems for unpatched Ivanti Sentry appliances. Flag any unpatched instances found after the federal due date. Post-deadline, correlate unpatched appliances against incident logs; unpatched status + inbound exploitation traffic = probable compromise.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation; requires detection of injection payloads in HTTP parameters targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry interfaces (ports 443, 5000-5001, 8443) for OS command injection metacharacters in parameters: $(command), `command`, |, ;, &&, || in request payloads. Correlate with known vulnerable endpoint patterns (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*, mobile management interfaces) and external source IPs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation: Root Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation manifests as root-owned process spawning from Sentry web service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Linux appliances running Ivanti Sentry, detect child processes spawned with UID 0 (root) from web service parent processes (httpd, nginx, Sentry daemon). Flag first-time-seen system utilities (curl, wget, bash, sh, nc, ncat) invoked at root level from network-accessible service context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Unmanaged Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable' — critical precondition requiring asset inventory hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Ivanti Sentry services listening on internet-facing addresses (ports 443, 5000, 5001, 8443) via netstat/ss or network telemetry. Identify instances not enrolled in EPMM/Neurons MDM (mentioned as mitigating control). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to determine patch status relative to CVE-2026-10520 fixed versions.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Authentication Spike — Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation, attackers probe unmanaged appliances for access points; spikes in failed auth attempts and unusual request patterns precede successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs for sustained elevated request rates from single source IP, unusual User-Agent strings, rapid endpoint enumeration (404 spike), or failed authentication attempts against admin/API paths. Correlate timing with subsequent successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Privilege Escalation: Unexpected Root Process Lineage
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'root-level' achievement; detect anomalous privilege escalation paths distinct from normal service restarts or maintenance operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes gaining root privileges through mechanisms other than expected service restart or sudo rules (e.g., capability-based escalation, exploit-driven escalation). On Sentry appliances, baseline normal root-spawning patterns and alert on deviations, especially if preceded by inbound network requests to web service ports.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable' and affects 'unmanaged state' appliances. Detecting exposed instances is the canonical initial-access hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for externally accessible Ivanti Sentry instances on default ports (8443 typical). Fingerprint via HTTP headers, certificate CN, or known URI patterns (/api/v1/, /system/). Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unmanaged deployments missing mTLS or restricted HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article defines attack vector as 'OS command injection vulnerability'—requires detection of malicious payloads targeting injection points. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API endpoints for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $, >>, <) and common injection patterns in query strings and POST bodies. Flag requests with command substitution syntax or encoded variants targeting known vulnerable parameters.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Code Execution—Sentry Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' achievable via injection. Post-exploitation detection requires process execution monitoring on Sentry hosts, absent from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process execution spawned by Sentry daemons with SYSTEM/root privileges (e.g., bash, sh, cmd.exe child processes from Java/appliance processes). Correlate with HTTP request events to confirm remote trigger.

suggestion.title: Sentry Patch Status / Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS access mitigate exploitation. Detection should include proactive configuration checks to identify at-risk deployments (unmanaged, exposed, no mTLS), not just reactive incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances lacking mTLS, restricted HTTPS ingress, or management enrollment. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against CVE-2026-10520. Flag any unpatched instances in unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: Sentry Authentication Bypass / Unauthenticated Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user'—attack does not require valid credentials. Detection should flag unauthenticated API calls to sensitive Sentry endpoints (command injection targets).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Sentry API endpoints without valid session tokens, client certs, or API keys. Particularly sensitive: requests to parameter/config/system endpoints originating from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Reverse Shell / Outbound Command-and-Control Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved, attacker would establish persistence. Article does not detail post-exploitation, but command-injection RCE typically leads to reverse shell or data exfiltration. Should detect anomalous outbound connections from Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound TCP/UDP connections from Sentry appliance to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially on high-numbered ports. Flag DNS queries for dynamic domains or suspicious FQDN patterns from Sentry host.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection vulnerability'—clear initial-access signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry services for command injection patterns (shell metacharacters: semicolons, pipes, backticks, $(…) substitution) in request payloads. Alert if requests originate from untrusted networks and appliance is marked unmanaged.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly promises 'root-level remote code execution'—privilege escalation to root is the exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts or daemons running as root, especially shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /usr/bin/python) spawning unexpected commands or opening reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Inventory Exposure Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—explicit conditional for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for Ivanti Sentry instances (product name or version from CMDB) flagged as 'unmanaged' or lacking MDM enrollment. Cross-check against network perimeter scans to confirm external reachability; alert on externally-exposed unmanaged instances without mTLS or restricted HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS / Restricted HTTPS Configuration Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—absence of these controls is a finding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configurations for presence of mTLS enforcement and HTTPS access restrictions. Flag instances exposed to external networks lacking these controls as high-risk. Verify certificate pinning and client-certificate requirements are enabled.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance for Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due date 2026-06-14 mandates scan-based remediation tracking; article explicitly references standard asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 across all Ivanti Sentry instances. Alert on unpatched instances with external exposure. Correlate with MDM enrollment state; prioritize remediation for unmanaged appliances by 2026-06-14 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Service Restart or Behavioral Anomaly Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection execution suggests attacker may modify service state, configurations, or spawn child processes inconsistent with baseline behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline behavior for Ivanti Sentry process trees (normal parent-child relationships, spawned interpreters, network connections). Alert on deviations: unexpected child processes, shell spawning, outbound network connections to non-whitelisted IPs, or rapid service restarts after HTTP requests from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'AI Phishing' as the attack vector. No detection logic was generated despite this being the core threat. Requires behavioral indicators: unusual sender reputation history, high-entropy subject lines, mismatched sender domain TLDs, and rapid email volume spikes from new senders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with AI-generated characteristics: novel sender+subject+body combinations, grammatically perfect with subtle anomalies (overuse of filler phrases), or rapid variant generation from lookalike domains. Flag if recipient is in credential-sensitive group (Finance, HR, Executive).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses phishing volume crushing SOCs, implying high-velocity credential theft. No credential-access detection suggested. Typical AI phishing campaigns serve fake login portals or credential forms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to lookalike or newly registered domains mimicking legitimate services (e.g., *.office365-verify.com, *.paypal-secure.io). Correlate with email gateway blocks and user reports to identify phishing landing pages receiving credential submissions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Attachment Execution Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'alert volume' burden; typical phishing campaigns attach malware (Office macros, scripts). Pipeline did not suggest execution-phase detections despite implied breach chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office documents (DOCX, XLSX) opened from email attachment paths executing child processes: WScript.exe, PowerShell, cmd.exe, or LOLBins (mshta.exe, regsvcs.exe). Flag if parent process is WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE and child runs in %TEMP% or %APPDATA%.

suggestion.title: SOC Alert Fatigue Exploitation (Defense Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'alert volume' and 'Tier 1 Overload.' Attackers weaponize phishing floods to overwhelm SOCs and bypass manual review. No detection for this tactical pattern was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous email traffic: spike in rejected/quarantined emails from diverse sender IPs/domains in <24h window, volume exceeding org's baseline by >300%, with subject/body variance suggesting template variation. Correlate with security team alert queue depth to identify potential saturation attacks.

suggestion.title: Link-Based Phishing with Redirect Chains
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing often uses URL shorteners and redirect chains to evade URL filtering. Article does not describe this tactic explicitly but is standard in high-volume campaigns. Pipeline should suggest detection for indirect delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with shortened URLs or multi-hop redirects (bitly, tinyurl, *.bit.do). Monitor proxy for redirect chains exceeding 2 hops before landing on credential-collection or malware-hosting domain. Flag if final domain registered <30 days and shares TLD with legitimate service.

suggestion.title: Bulk Phishing Campaign Indicators (Email Gateway Patterns)
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'alert volume' from phishing—inherently implies bulk distribution. No detection suggested for characteristic mass-mail patterns: SMTP relay abuse, sender spoofing variants, content reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails where: same body/attachment hash sent to >50 recipients in 1h, sender has no prior SMTP history, SPF/DKIM/DMARC fail, and subject includes urgency keywords (verify, confirm, urgent, immediate action). Correlate with external threat feeds for known phishing templates.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — direct asset inventory hunt required. Article itself recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' template application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry instances on public-facing IP ranges (ports 443, 8443). Cross-reference against corporate asset inventory for patch status against CVE-2026-10520 due-date 2026-06-14. Alert on any external Sentry endpoint not confirmed patched.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Pattern — Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Core attack surface requires exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry endpoints for HTTP requests with shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &&, ;) in parameters. Correlate 4xx responses + Sentry process spawning root child processes within 5 seconds to RCE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration State Verification — Unmanaged Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags vulnerability success depends on 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — requires continuous configuration posture assessment.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry web server and API logs for requests containing shell metacharacters (backticks, pipes, semicolons, &&, ||, $(), command substitution) in unauthenticated endpoint parameters, especially management or API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root-Level Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Unexpected uid=0 process spawning or privilege escalation from Sentry service account is post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, alert on processes spawned with UID 0 (root) or privilege escalation from the Sentry service account originating from network requests. Baseline expected root activity (cron jobs, system maintenance).

suggestion.title: Configuration Audit: mTLS and Access Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies protective mitigations: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Compliance check ensures mitigations are not disabled or misconfigured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliance TLS configuration to verify mTLS enforcement with EPMM and restricted HTTPS access are enabled. Flag appliances with permissive TLS, mutual auth disabled, or unrestricted HTTPS listener.

suggestion.title: Linux PAM Module Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials.' Nine distinct variants found, indicating primary persistence and credential access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to /lib*/security/pam_unix.so, /etc/pam.d/ file changes, or runtime modifications to PAM libraries. Correlate with file integrity monitoring violations and unexpected successful authentications using hardcoded credentials.

suggestion.title: Trojanized OpenSSH Component Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions, and stored the collected data locally.' Parallel persistence vector to PAM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ssh/sshd/scp binary hash mismatches or binary replacement events. Alert on creation of local credential logs in unusual paths. Detect SSH process modifications that don't correspond to package manager updates.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component that connected to a hardcoded relay domain, providing encrypted remote shell access.' Achieved persistence via systemd service or startup script.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GS-Netcat process signatures and obfuscated reverse shell patterns. Monitor systemd service files for suspicious reverse shell commands. Alert on processes masquerading as legitimate components that establish outbound C2 connections to relay domains.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as System Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling... ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.' Enables pivot from internet-facing to air-gapped network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SOCKS5 listening ports on internet-facing servers. Alert on processes spoofing 'smbd -D' that actually bind to network sockets. Monitor sustained port forwarding or dynamic proxy creation from compromised internet-facing hosts.

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Chaining to Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server.' Backend Nginx forwards to FastCGI, creating HTTP→SSH bridge into air-gapped network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx.conf for proxy_pass directives to internal FastCGI or SSH endpoints. Alert on HTTP POST requests with SSH-like parameters (hostname, username, command). Detect unusual request forwarding chains between internet-facing and internal Nginx instances.

suggestion.title: FastCGI-Initiated SSH to Internal Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article details the attack vector: 'The FastCGI wrapper acted as an execution bridge, processing requests and launching a custom binary named uptime... established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on fcgiwrap or FastCGI processes spawning SSH/scp binaries. Correlate HTTP POST request content with subsequent SSH connection parameters. Detect SSH connections initiated by web server UIDs (www-data, nginx, etc.).

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempt on Splunk REST/Web API Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes unauthenticated RCE via Splunk endpoint; without article text, assumed exploitation vector is HTTP(S) request to vulnerable endpoint (likely /api/* or /en-US/* paths common in Splunk web interface).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk instances with POST/GET to /api/* or /en-US/* paths containing unusual parameters or command sequences. Flag requests without Authentication headers or valid session tokens to critical Splunk endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is unauthenticated code execution; need detection for spawned processes from splunkd or splunk-web processes indicating successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by splunkd.exe, splunk-web.exe, or python.exe in Splunk context with unexpected command-line arguments (bash, cmd, powershell, curl, wget) or network operations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration Injection or Deployment Client Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Critical unauthenticated RCE likely exploits Splunk config parsing or deployment mechanisms; detection should cover malicious conf file modifications or deployment client reaching unexpected C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to /etc/system/local/* or $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/deployment-client/deploymentclient.conf with unexpected target serverRepositories pointing to attacker C2 or conf files containing embedded commands.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Metadata Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 400+ packages hijacked; implies malicious PKGBUILD modifications or unauthorized metadata changes. No UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to AUR package .git history (commit author/timestamp anomalies, forced pushes from non-maintainer IPs, or batched updates outside normal maintenance windows). Cross-reference with maintainer account logins; flag modifications without corresponding auth events. Alert on package metadata changes preceding new releases.

suggestion.title: Malicious Installation Script Execution Post-AUR Install
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain hijack injects code into PKGBUILD/install scripts; article mentions packages but no detection for script execution phase. 'What the "Atomic Arch" Campaign Means' implies actual payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During pacman -S or yay -S post-installation hooks, detect spawned shell processes with network I/O or file creation outside expected package scope. Flag if /tmp or /var/tmp writes correlate with immediate DNS lookups to non-repo domains or curl/wget to external hosts during package install.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise via Weak Auth or Phishing
suggestion.rationale: 400+ packages compromised suggests either mass maintainer account takeover or single vulnerability. Article likely describes auth mechanism but no UC for detecting account compromise prior to package modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AUR login from new IP geolocation within 24 hours of mass package updates. Flag multiple failed login attempts followed by successful auth from unusual client (e.g., curl vs. web UI). Monitor for new SSH keys added to maintainer accounts without corresponding audit trail or maintainer confirmation email.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Mirror Sync Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 400+ hijacked packages entering distribution; no UC for detecting abnormal sync patterns or mirror-level tampering indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sync operations that introduce packages with mismatched GPG signatures or timestamps predating maintainer commits. Alert if a single sync cycle pushes >100 package updates from non-vetted maintainers or if package size increases anomalously (payloaded binary bloat).

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Network Beaconing to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages likely include persistence or exfiltration payloads; article implies ongoing compromise but no UC for detecting C2 callbacks or data exfil post-install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation (pacman/yay process) with subsequent DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections to non-whitelisted domains. Flag if outbound traffic originates from package-installed paths (/opt, /usr/local/bin, systemd services spawned by package) within 10 minutes of install completion.

suggestion.title: Bulk AUR Package Download/Installation Surge from Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Campaign compromises many packages; detecting mass installation attempts flags either automated testing of exploit or opportunistic infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if a single endpoint installs >5 AUR packages within 30 minutes or if pacman/yay logs show batch installations of packages flagged as compromised in threat intel feeds. Cross-reference against user baseline (non-developers, systems with no history of AUR installs).

suggestion.title: macOS Tahoe 26 Artifact File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact that tracks user menu selections across the operating system.' Any exfiltration requires prior artifact file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file opens or reads of macOS Tahoe 26 artifact locations by non-system processes. Alert on stat(), open(), or mmap() syscalls against artifact paths followed by suspicious process behavior (network egress, archive creation, memory access patterns indicating data staging).

suggestion.title: Tahoe 26 Artifact Deletion or Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Forensic artifact is a 'digital intent' record—attackers will attempt deletion/modification to cover tracks, matching adversarial practice of anti-forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected deletion, truncation, or modification of Tahoe 26 artifact storage locations on macOS. Detect invocations of rm, shred, unlink, or file truncation APIs against known artifact directories. Correlate with shell execution or suspicious process chains.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Data
suggestion.rationale: Artifact's stated function is to track user selections; the collected menu data is the attacker's target for intelligence gathering ('Tracing Digital Intent').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file access to Tahoe 26 artifact with subsequent suspicious network activity. Detect compression (tar, zip, gzip) or encoding of artifact data followed by connections to non-standard ports or known C2 infrastructure. Monitor for data exfiltration to cloud storage or file-sharing services.

suggestion.title: Phishing email impersonating AI vendors with credential CTA
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states AI brands used as social engineering bait. No detection UC for emails spoofing ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other AI platforms requesting verification or urgent action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails claiming to be from major AI vendors with sender domain mismatches or lookalike domains. Trigger on urgency language + credential verification CTA + link to non-canonical domain. Correlate to phishing campaigns targeting specific organization.

suggestion.title: AiTM proxy credential interception and MFA token theft
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly flag 'Adversary-in-the-middle' attacks; article focuses on credential theft via AiTM proxies. No detection UC for real-time token interception or MFA bypass signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed auth + immediate successful auth from different IP (credential replay). Look for MFA completion in <5 seconds post-submission (token reuse). Correlate impossible travel: phishing email open IP + subsequent sign-in from distant geography within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Post-compromise account abuse with stolen credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft is stated attack goal; no UC for detection of compromised account activity patterns post-harvest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-ins with compromised creds: impossible travel, anomalous client apps (legacy auth protocols), suspicious mailbox/file-share access immediately after phishing event, email forwarding rules created post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Lookalike domain registration targeting AI platforms
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via AI brand impersonation requires attacker infrastructure (phishing domains). No IOC extraction of typosquatted AI vendor domains suggests infrastructure not mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domains similar to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, Microsoft AI (Copilot) with edit-distance typos (openai-securelogin.com, claude-verify.net). Alert on user clicks to these domains from phishing emails. High-confidence alert if credential submission detected.

suggestion.title: Suspicious email URL clicks to external credential-submission endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft campaigns involve convincing users to enter passwords on attacker-controlled pages. No UC for phishing link + credential submission detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email URL clicks to non-corporate endpoints followed by suspicious network activity (POST to external login/auth endpoints). Correlate phishing email receipt + link click + subsequent account compromise or MFA alert.

suggestion.title: Forced authentication via malicious redirects or NTLM relay
suggestion.rationale: AiTM campaigns often force credential submission. T1187 (Forced Authentication) is central to AiTM attacks but unmapped by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure within email-forwarding/URL-click session. Look for challenge-response auth to external IPs. Correlate to phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Baseline asset discovery is prerequisite for triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product signatures, DNS patterns, open ports 443/8443) reachable from external networks. Flag appliances without mTLS (EPMM) or Neurons for MDM enrollment indicators. Cross-reference against patch inventory for CVE-2026-10520 remediation status.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Payload delivery is the primary attack vector requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unauthenticated HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (| ; & ` $() backticks), argument separators, or command substitution syntax in request paths, query strings, or POST bodies. Alert on repeated injection attempts from single sources.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these mitigations identifies vulnerable configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query inventory for Sentry appliances lacking mTLS enforcement (certificate validation absence), EPMM agent enrollment, or Neurons for MDM integration. Correlate missing hardening with external network reachability to identify actively exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation indicators must capture process execution privilege escalation and unexpected root-context activity from Sentry services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell spawning (sh, bash, ksh) or reverse-shell payloads with UID=0 originating from Sentry daemon accounts. Flag unexpected network connections (outbound) or file modifications initiated from root-context Sentry processes. Monitor sudoers/privilege escalation logs for Sentry service privilege-climbing attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Reconnaissance Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker reconnaissance phase: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited...where the Sentry appliance is...externally reachable.' Scanning and probing precedes active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass HTTP requests to Sentry management paths (/admin, /ems/, /api/) from external IPs returning 401/403/200 in rapid succession. Alert on port scanning targeting typical Sentry ports (443, 8443, 8080) from single external source. Correlate with Shodan/Censys queries for Ivanti product fingerprints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable only when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must identify exposed unpatched instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network asset inventory against Ivanti Sentry product/version roster. Flag instances externally routable on management ports (443 typical) that lack documented mTLS or restricted HTTPS access. Correlate with patch-status records to isolate unmanaged devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation attempts must be detectable in application/HTTP logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application and web-server logs for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, pipes, semicolons) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Unauthenticated requests exhibiting these patterns should trigger immediate alert.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root-Level RCE Privilege Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise, attacker will execute commands at UID 0. Detection should hunt for shell spawning from Sentry processes with root privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawning (sh, bash, ksh) from Ivanti Sentry service account (typically non-root). If UID/GID reports as 0 in process context, or file modifications occur in /etc, /sys, /root—escalation confirmed.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Match (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the primary IOC, and template instructs 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline extracted no IOCs or hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag assets matching CVE-2026-10520 in any vulnerability scanner output, focusing on Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry). Cross-reference discovered instances against Federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-14. Prioritize any unpatched Sentry appliances exposed to the internet.

suggestion.title: External Exposure: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack prerequisite: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' mTLS and restricted HTTPS negate the vulnerability, so exposure detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances via network reconnaissance (default Sentry service ports, HTTP banner matching Sentry/MobileIron strings, SSL certificate Subject/Issuer patterns). Cross-reference against asset inventory to find appliances NOT protected by mTLS (EPMM) or restricted HTTPS (Neurons for MDM). Unmanaged instances are highest risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is 'OS command injection' allowing 'root-level remote code execution.' Article describes execution technique but pipeline mapped only T1190 and generated no execution-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/REST API requests to Ivanti Sentry for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) in parameter values, URL-encoded variants, and path traversal sequences. Focus on unauthenticated endpoints. Correlate with process execution logs on the appliance to detect post-injection command spawning as root.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution and Privilege Escalation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—this is the impact that requires post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for anomalous process spawning on Ivanti Sentry appliances: shell processes (bash, sh, cmd) launched by Java/Tomcat parent processes, child processes running as root initiated from network-facing services, commands containing shell metacharacters in appliance audit logs, and unexpected privilege escalation events.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' matching CVE-2026-10520 against vulnerability scanner. Pipeline produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Ivanti Sentry instances in vulnerability management system with CVE-2026-10520 exposure. Correlate patch status against federal remediation deadline (2026-06-14). Prioritize unpatched + externally accessible instances as highest-risk.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline missed network-exposure hunting layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry management consoles accessible from untrusted networks (public IPs, non-corporate ranges). Cross-reference externally-facing instances against asset inventory to identify unmanaged appliances lacking mTLS or Neurons MDM restriction.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vulnerability mechanism as 'OS command injection vulnerability.' No behavioral detection mapped despite this being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API/web interfaces for malformed requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, `, $(), backticks) or command-separator patterns in parameters. Alert on systematic probing of known injection endpoints or public PoC payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Unauthorized Root-Level Process Spawning on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states impact as 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed privilege-escalation / impact-phase detection for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect unexpected processes spawned with root UID from Sentry service account, system binary modifications, or outbound network connections from Sentry processes to non-whitelisted destinations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Security Posture: mTLS and Restricted Access Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article documents mitigations: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Pipeline should validate security controls preventing exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Sentry appliances enforce mTLS with EPMM or operate behind Neurons MDM with restricted HTTPS. Flag any appliance in 'unmanaged state' or with open management interfaces on public/untrusted networks as misconfigured and exploitable.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'; federal patch due 2026-06-14 signals active exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated inbound connections to externally accessible Ivanti Sentry instances. Cross-reference asset inventory for Sentry appliances not enrolled in mTLS, EPMM, or Neurons for MDM. Flag unmanaged instances as exploitation-vulnerable.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector leading to RCE; no use case exists to detect injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs and endpoint telemetry for shell metacharacters (pipes, command separators, variable expansion) in HTTP request payloads targeting Sentry endpoints, followed by unexpected child process spawning from Sentry service accounts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution'; privilege escalation to root is the attack outcome and should be detectable post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned with root/SYSTEM privileges under Sentry service context or originating from unauthenticated network listeners. Cross-correlate timing with command-injection detection to flag successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' as the exploitation condition; mitigation explicitly mentions mTLS/EPMM/Neurons enrollment, implying need to detect unenrolled appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/management systems for Ivanti Sentry appliances with no mTLS certificate enrollment, no EPMM integration, and no Neurons for MDM registration. Flag absences as unmanaged exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-10520 as the primary threat ID with federal remediation due 2026-06-14; scanner correlation is foundational for active-exploitation response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner flags for CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry inventory. Any positive match should trigger immediate isolation review and expedited patching, given CISA KEV active-exploitation status.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Asset Inventory & Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry instances exposed on standard ports (443, 8443, 8080) using product-specific signatures (SSL cert subjects, HTTP response banners, /admin path). Correlate asset inventory with vulnerability scanner to identify systems with CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability status. Flag any externally-reachable instances as critical prior to patch due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed detection for injection patterns (pipe, semicolon, backtick, command substitution) in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command-injection metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks, newlines) in query parameters or POST body. Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry API calls first. Alert on obfuscated or encoded variants targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated' access leading to 'root-level' execution. Pipeline failed to propose detection for unexpected privileged process spawning or shell access from the Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect unexpected process creation (bash, sh, perl, python, curl, wget) spawned from the Sentry daemon user with root/UID-0 context. Baseline normal Sentry maintenance tasks. Alert on reverse shells, outbound connections, or filesystem modification by unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: mTLS & HTTPS Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes that mTLS and restricted HTTPS 'make interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—a stated control. Pipeline missed detection for attempts to circumvent these protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed mTLS client certificate validation, TLS renegotiation attempts, or direct-to-IP access bypassing Neurons for MDM proxy. Track non-standard cipher suites or SSL/TLS version mismatches on Sentry ports. Alert on repeated failed certificate validation from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner + Patch Compliance Validation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all Ivanti Sentry instances and cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 patch status. Flag any systems with status 'vulnerable' or 'not assessed' as critical. Priority escalate systems with both vulnerability AND external network exposure. Validate patches installed after 2026-06-14 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 across Ivanti Sentry deployments. Cross-reference scan results with external internet-facing asset data (Shodan, censys). Flag instances not protected by mTLS/EPMM connection or restricted HTTPS access, per article's stated mitigations.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance web logs for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, `, $(), backticks, newlines) in query parameters or POST bodies. suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Process Spawning from Web Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact but pipeline missed process-execution detection from compromised web context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance by Federal Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline missed compliance-based detection for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all Ivanti Sentry deployments affected by CVE-2026-10520. Identify versions running pre-patch baseline per Ivanti advisory. Flag non-compliant systems with patch due-date 2026-06-14 passed, escalating to compliance/audit teams.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Externally Reachable Asset Exposure

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability...remote unauthenticated user' but pipeline generated no exploitation-detection UC. Shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, |, ;) in HTTP request payloads to Sentry endpoints are telltale exploitation attempts.

suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable in 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — this is the primary exposure condition. Asset inventory + network boundary correlation required to identify attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query infrastructure for Ivanti Sentry appliances with public IP bindings (port 8443) and asset management records showing 'unmanaged' status. Cross-reference with network segmentation logs. Baseline expectation: zero externally reachable unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Parameter Injection to Sentry Admin Endpoints

suggestion.title: Root-Privileged Process Spawning Post-Injection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on root-owned process creation (UID=0) spawned from Sentry service accounts or inherited from web application contexts, especially unusual binaries (sh, bash, curl, wget, python) within 1-5 seconds of external SSH/HTTPS connection attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection Match

suggestion.title: Disabled mTLS or Restricted HTTPS Policy Misconfiguration

suggestion.title: Patch Lag Post-Federal Due Date (2026-06-14)

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry External Accessibility
